model_description: Connectome-based predictive modeling, using whole-brain resting-state functional connectivity with 10-fold cross-validation, predicts future problematic social media use scores and identifies contributing neural networks.
title: Connectome-based prediction of problematic use of social media in adolescents: Findings from the ABCD study.
study_design: longitudinal cohort machine learning prediction study

model_family: fused VGG-19, ResNet-50, MobileNet-V2 CNN features with Chi-Square feature selection and SVM classifier
patient_population: children imaged with chest radiography for pneumonia diagnosis (publicly available pneumonia CXR dataset)
clinical_problem: detecting childhood pneumonia on chest radiographs
model_description: Three pretrained CNNs (VGG-19, ResNet-50, MobileNet-V2) extract features from pediatric chest radiographs; a Chi-Square selection step removes redundant features before fusing subsets from the two best-performing networks, which are then classified as pneumonia or normal using a support vector machine.
title: Automatic Childhood Pneumonia Diagnosis Based on Multi-Model Feature Fusion Using Chi-Square Feature Selection.
study_design: retrospective technical development on a public benchmark dataset
headline_result: accuracy 97.59%, recall 98.33%, F1-score 98.19%

patient_population: 236 participants aged 8-18 years (154 with idiopathic scoliosis, 82 healthy controls) from 2 reference hospitals in France and Canada
clinical_problem: screening for idiopathic scoliosis without radiography
model_description: A smartphone application captures video scans of a patient's back and uses AI to estimate the major coronal spinal curve from 3D surface topography, without radiation, to screen for idiopathic scoliosis; results were compared, blinded, against standard radiographic curve measurements.
title: A Preliminary Report: Screening Idiopathic Scoliosis (IS) With a Smartphone Application.
headline_result: sensitivity 100%, specificity 89% for detecting curve >10 degrees

model_family: spatially constrained ICA + ComBat harmonization + support vector machine
patient_population: multi-site rs-fMRI cohort from ABIDE I and II (children/adults with ASD and healthy controls across 11 sites)
clinical_problem: classifying autism spectrum disorder from resting-state fMRI connectivity
model_description: A semi-blind independent component analysis identifies functional brain networks from resting-state fMRI, with ComBat harmonization to correct for scanner/site differences across 11 datasets; a support vector machine then classifies ASD versus healthy controls using features from the default mode, sensorimotor, and visual sensory networks.
title: Multi-Site Classification of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Spatially Constrained ICA on Resting-State fMRI Networks.
study_design: retrospective multi-site machine learning classification study
dataset_size: multi-site rs-fMRI dataset, 11 independent datasets (ABIDE I and II)
headline_result: classification accuracy up to 83.23% (visual sensory network, AUC 87.90%)

patient_population: 21 skeletally immature patients treated for juvenile osteochondritis dissecans of the distal femur, 2002-2017
clinical_problem: monitoring joint space width / cartilage health after treatment for juvenile osteochondritis dissecans of the knee
model_description: IB Lab KOALA, a validated AI-based software, automatically measures joint space width on standardized anteroposterior knee radiographs, used here to compare the affected and contralateral knee and across treatment groups (conservative, drilling, fragment refixation) in juvenile osteochondritis dissecans.
release_evidence: validated AI-based software IB Lab KOALA(TM), Version 2.4
title: Automated Joint Space Width Assessment in Patients Treated for Juvenile Osteochondritis Dissecans of the Distal Femur: A Cross-Sectional Study and Systematic Review of the Literature.
study_design: retrospective cross-sectional feasibility study with systematic review
headline_result: no significant JSW differences between affected/contralateral knee or treatment groups; average JSW >6 mm at median 64-month follow-up

clinical_problem: Real-time diagnosis of fetal congenital heart disease from ultrasound in resource-constrained settings lacking specialized clinicians
model_description: Liquid-Sequencer, a lightweight deep-learning model combining depthwise-separable/squeeze-excitation convolutional feature extraction with a bidirectional Liquid Neural Network sequence module, classifies fetal congenital heart disease from cardiac ultrasound for real-time 'digital twin' diagnostic support.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: Liquid-Sequencer: A Lightweight Liquid Neural Network for Real-Time Fetal Congenital Heart Disease Diagnosis.
headline_result: Strong performance with only 0.30M parameters across 12 datasets (specific accuracy not given in abstract)

body_region: fetal brain (cavum septum pellucidum et vergae, lateral posterior ventricle horn, choroid plexus, cerebellum, cortical plate)
patient_population: 270 3D ultrasound volumes from 141 fetuses, 19-26+6 weeks' gestation, acquired on a different ultrasound vendor than the training data
clinical_problem: automated segmentation of fetal (sub)cortical brain structures on 3D ultrasound for fetal neuroimaging assessment
model_description: Deep learning models automatically segment five fetal (sub)cortical brain structures on 3D ultrasound volumes. The study evaluates these models on a novel dataset acquired with a different ultrasound vendor, using both the Dice similarity coefficient and a new clinician-focused 4-point visual grading framework.
title: Clinical Grading of Artificial Intelligence-Based 3D Fetal Brain Segmentations: A Cross-Vendor Evaluation of Deep Learning in Fetal Neuroimaging.
headline_result: 87.2% of segmentations graded adequate overall; CSPV/ChP/CBM >90.5% adequate; LPVH lowest at 73.9% adequate

patient_population: ABCD study participants with and without ASD, propensity-score matched
clinical_problem: Improving classification of autism spectrum disorder in a community-based adolescent cohort by integrating multimodal brain MRI with physical-health markers (sleep, growth, development)
model_description: Multimodal machine-learning models integrate structural, diffusion, and resting-state functional MRI with physical-health markers (sleep, growth, early development) to classify autism spectrum disorder status in a population-based adolescent cohort.
title: Integrating Multimodal Neuroimaging and Physical-Health Markers for Autism Spectrum Disorder in the ABCD Study.
study_design: cross-sectional cohort study with propensity-matched machine-learning classification
headline_result: AUC-ROC 0.68 (95% CI 0.62-0.73), AUC-PR 0.66 for multimodal model

body_region: brain (multimodal: diffusion tensor imaging, structural MRI, resting-state functional connectivity)
patient_population: children/adolescents with multimodal neuroimaging (DTI, structural MRI, resting-state functional connectivity)
clinical_problem: predicting socioeconomic status / family income from multimodal brain imaging
model_description: Elastic net regression models predict family socioeconomic status, particularly income, from multimodal brain imaging (diffusion tensor imaging, structural MRI, and resting-state functional connectivity), with and without demographic information, to identify which imaging features are most discriminative of SES.
title: Machine learning algorithm reveals neurodevelopmental signatures of combined family income and neighborhood disadvantage in adolescents.
headline_result: AUC 0.75 (test)/0.811 (train) for income without demographics; AUC 0.81 (test)/0.969 (train) distinguishing top vs bottom income deciles

patient_population: infants and children evaluated for developmental dysplasia of the hip (literature review, no single cohort)
clinical_problem: diagnosing developmental dysplasia of the hip using AI-assisted ultrasound and radiography
model_description: A literature review summarizing AI applications (deep learning, CNNs, segmentation networks, 3D convolutional models) for automated landmark detection and measurement of the alpha angle, beta angle, and acetabular index on hip ultrasound and radiographs, for diagnosing developmental dysplasia of the hip.
title: Scaling Early Detection for Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip With Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Imaging.

patient_population: 4,532 first-trimester fetal ultrasound scans (11-14 weeks), 9 medical centers
clinical_problem: Automated detection and classification of key fetal anatomical structures on first-trimester ultrasound to support early fetal anomaly screening
model_description: YOLOv11 and Swin Transformer object-detection models localize nine fetal brain/craniofacial structures on ultrasound; radiomic and deep features from the detected regions are fused and classified by a TabTransformer model into clinically defined anatomical categories.
title: A multi-task deep learning and radiomics framework for fetal anatomical structure detection and classification in ultrasound imaging.
study_design: retrospective multicenter algorithm development and external validation study
headline_result: External test classification accuracy 96.1%, AUC up to 96.89%, sensitivity >95%; detection IoU up to 0.97, F1>=0.94

patient_population: 171 preterm infants (<37 weeks gestation) with cranial ultrasound and 3D T1 brain MRI at 34-46 weeks postmenstrual age, December 2020-August 2024
clinical_problem: predicting neurodevelopmental impairment from brain volume in preterm infants with germinal matrix hemorrhage
model_description: A U-Net-based algorithm automatically segments supratentorial and white matter brain volumes from term-equivalent-age 3D T1 MRI in preterm infants, to test whether reduced volume relative to sex-specific norms is associated with germinal matrix hemorrhage grade and later neurodevelopmental impairment (measured by Bayley-III).
title: Increased risk of neurodevelopmental impairment associated with reduced brain volume at term-equivalent age in preterm infants with germinal matrix hemorrhage.
headline_result: supratentorial volume-PMA slope 19.37 cm3/week control vs 12.37 GMH (P=0.02) vs 11.49 PWML (P=0.04); standardized residuals differed significantly between NDI and non-NDI in GMH group (P<0.001)

patient_population: pregnant women assessed for preterm birth risk across reviewed studies
clinical_problem: predicting spontaneous preterm birth using AI
model_description: A narrative review of AI approaches to predicting spontaneous preterm birth, including electronic-health-record models, deep learning analysis of cervical ultrasound images, cervical texture/radiomics feature extraction, elastography-derived parameters, and multi-omics transformer models, evaluating their methodological quality against TRIPOD and risk-of-bias criteria.
title: Artificial intelligence in preterm birth prediction: a narrative review of current approaches and clinical applicability.
headline_result: AUC range 0.61-0.89 across modalities; 79% of studies at high risk of bias; median TRIPOD adherence 49%

model_family: lightweight deep neural network (CNN), benchmarked against AlexNet, MobileNet, ResNet18, Xception
patient_population: children from the ABIDE and ADHD-200 public datasets
clinical_problem: differentiating autism spectrum disorder from ADHD subtypes (combined, hyperactive/impulsive, inattentive) and neurotypical children
model_description: ADBrainNet is a lightweight deep neural network trained on resting-state fMRI images to classify five groups: ASD, three ADHD subtypes, and neurotypical children. Explainable-AI (LIME) is used to highlight the imaging features driving each classification.
title: ADBrainNet: a deep neural network for Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and Attention Deficit and Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) classification using resting-state fMRI images based on explainable artificial intelligence.
study_design: retrospective machine learning classification study on public datasets
headline_result: mean accuracy 61.87% (+/-5.59%), F1 62.50% (+/-5.78%) on independent external test set, five-fold cross-validation

body_region: fetal anatomy (first-trimester, biometry, anomaly scan planes)
patient_population: 61,959 fetal ultrasound examinations (551,144 images) from 186 sonographers at 34 hospitals in Guizhou Province, China, September 2020-May 2025
clinical_problem: improving fetal ultrasound image quality/standardization in low-resource settings
model_description: An independent, post-examination AI quality-control system scores each fetal ultrasound image 0-100 and classifies it as standard, basic-standard, or non-standard against national plane-acquisition guidelines, to give sonographers feedback and track image-quality trends over time across a multicenter, multi-county rollout.
title: AI-based quality control was associated with improved fetal ultrasound image quality in low-resource settings: a real-world multicenter study from West China.
dataset_size: 61,959 examinations (551,144 images) from 186 sonographers at 34 hospitals
headline_result: full-standard first-trimester scans rose from 39.5% to 82.1%; standard anomaly scans from 16.1% to 53.3% over 36 months (all p<0.0001)

patient_population: 13,865 hand radiographs from the RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Challenge and Roboflow HandBone datasets, ages 0-19 years, tested on 200 hold-out samples
clinical_problem: forensic skeletal age and sex estimation from hand radiographs for disaster victim identification
model_description: A two-stage deep learning system first uses YOLOv8x to detect 17 anatomical keypoints and segment 19 bones on a hand radiograph, then an EfficientNet-B0 stage estimates biological age and sex from these skeletal features, independent of soft tissue, for forensic identification.
title: A two-stage deep learning approach for forensic age and sex determination from hand-wrist radiographs: an anatomical pose estimation and multi-task model.
study_design: retrospective technical development and validation on public datasets
headline_result: age MAE 7.75 months, R2 0.942, ICC 0.993; sex classification accuracy 94% (kappa 0.88)

patient_population: 113 children with medulloblastoma and 74 with pilocytic astrocytoma
clinical_problem: differentiating medulloblastoma from pilocytic astrocytoma preoperatively in children
model_description: A multimodal MRI radiomics model extracts features from DCE-T1WI, T2WI, and ADC sequences and combines them into a radiomics nomogram to distinguish medulloblastoma from pilocytic astrocytoma before surgery in children with posterior fossa tumors.
title: Differentiating medulloblastoma and pilocytic astrocytoma in children based on multimodal MRI radiomics model.
headline_result: combined model AUC 0.999 (primary cohort), 0.994 (validation cohort)

model_family: deep learning / LLM (review of multiple approaches)
patient_population: autistic children (review of literature)
clinical_problem: Support early detection of autism spectrum disorder through integration of multimodal data and generate personalized intervention plans using large language models
model_description: Reviews AI approaches that integrate multimodal data (imaging, audio, video, etc.) for earlier autism detection and use generative LLMs to draft personalized intervention/treatment reports for autistic children.
journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
title: Multimodal data integration for early autism detection and LLM-driven personalized intervention: A review.

patient_population: 37 children with dystonia vs matched healthy controls; brain-age model trained on 2,623 normative scans
clinical_problem: Using a machine-learning brain-age model to identify structural deviations in children with dystonia and predict outcomes after deep brain stimulation surgery
model_description: A machine-learning brain-age model, trained on thousands of normative developmental T1-weighted MRI scans, computes a 'brain-age gap' (predicted minus chronological age) from pre-surgical MRI in children with dystonia, tested as a biomarker of motor severity and deep-brain-stimulation outcome.
journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society
title: The Brain-Age Gap in Pediatric Dystonia: Neuroanatomical Deviations Inform Deep Brain Stimulation Outcomes.
dataset_size: 37 children with dystonia; normative training set n=2,623
headline_result: Greater brain-age gap in dystonia vs controls (P<0.001); associated with worse baseline motor scores and poorer 1-year quality-of-life improvement

patient_population: five tumor populations: adult gliomas, pediatric gliomas, Sub-Saharan African gliomas, intracranial meningiomas, and brain metastases
clinical_problem: generalizable segmentation of brain tumors (including pediatric gliomas) across diverse patient populations
model_description: MTSS-KDNet distills the knowledge of several population-specific teacher segmentation models (including one trained on pediatric gliomas) into a single unified student model, using latent- and output-level supervision, so that one MRI brain tumor segmentation model generalizes across adult, pediatric, and other tumor populations without separate models.
title: Distilling population specific expertise into a unified model for generalizable brain tumor segmentation.
headline_result: average Dice 0.87 (whole tumor), 0.84 (tumor core), 0.77 (enhancing tumor) across all five populations, outperforming population-specific models

patient_population: internal dataset of 52,942 annotated images from 1,940 normal fetal echocardiograms; external testing on 245 normal echocardiograms and 83 abnormal echocardiograms
clinical_problem: automating fetal cardiac function assessment on echocardiography
model_description: A fully automated AI workflow detects and segments fetal cardiac structures on echocardiogram images, performs quality control, then calculates cardiac function parameters, referenced to a dynamic gestational-age Z-score model, replacing labor-intensive manual measurement.
title: Automated interpretation of fetal cardiac function evaluation from the echocardiogram.
dataset_size: 52,942 images from 1,940 normal fetal echocardiograms (internal); 245 normal + 83 abnormal echocardiograms (external)
headline_result: mean Dice similarity coefficient >92%, mean IoU >85% across all test datasets; lower variability than manual or Fetal HQ measurement

patient_population: 180 screening report files (1,097 images), low-risk pregnancies
clinical_problem: Automating identification and image-quality auditing of the fetal left ventricular outflow tract view in routine obstetric ultrasound screening
model_description: A deep-learning pipeline identifies left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) views in obstetric ultrasound screening images and scores 7 predefined image-quality criteria to produce an interpretable 0-7 summary quality score.
journal: Journal of ultrasound in medicine : official journal of the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine
title: AI-Driven Analysis of the Fetal Left Ventricular Outflow Tract: Diagnostic Value and Applications.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and validation study
headline_result: Sensitivity 97.7%, specificity 90.0% for LVOT presence; ICC 0.902 for summary score

patient_population: children undergoing abdominal imaging (literature review)
clinical_problem: reviewing AI applications across pediatric abdominal imaging tasks (detection, classification, functional analysis, severity prediction, segmentation, image-quality optimization, acquisition acceleration)
model_description: A clinically oriented review, organized by organ, of published AI research in pediatric abdominal imaging, covering detection, classification, functional analysis, severity prediction, automated segmentation, image-quality optimization, and acquisition acceleration; it notes that most pediatric AI research so far has focused on musculoskeletal rather than abdominal imaging and that most applications remain confined to the research setting.
title: The role of artificial intelligence in paediatric abdominal imaging.

model_family: EfficientNetB0 and InceptionV3 CNNs (compared to SVM baseline)
patient_population: 150 neonates (75 with ABE, 75 with hyperbilirubinemia without ABE)
clinical_problem: distinguishing acute bilirubin encephalopathy from non-ABE hyperbilirubinemia in neonates
model_description: A computer-aided diagnosis system feeds T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and ADC brain MRI (individually and fused) into convolutional neural networks (EfficientNetB0, InceptionV3) to distinguish neonates with acute bilirubin encephalopathy from those with hyperbilirubinemia but no encephalopathy, whose MRI findings can otherwise look similar.
title: Computer-aided diagnosis of neonatal acute bilirubin encephalopathy with multi-modal MRI images and convolutional neural networks.
headline_result: best model (InceptionV3, fused T1/T2/ADC) accuracy 0.9622, AUC 0.9978, F1 0.9617

patient_population: 511 children with pediatric low-grade glioma and known BRAF status, presurgical MRI, two institutions, January 2009-January 2023
clinical_problem: noninvasively predicting BRAF mutation status (fusion vs V600E vs non-BRAF) in pediatric low-grade glioma to guide targeted therapy
model_description: Radiomics features are extracted from manually segmented tumors on multisequence presurgical MRI (FLAIR, T2WI, contrast-enhanced T1WI, ADC); random forest classifiers combining clinical and radiomics features predict three-class BRAF mutation status (fusion, V600E, non-BRAF) in pediatric low-grade glioma, to help select candidates for molecularly targeted treatment when biopsy is not feasible.
title: Multiclass Radiomics-Based Prediction of BRAF Mutation Status in Pediatric Low-grade Gliomas Using Multisequence MRI.
dataset_size: 511 children (223 BRAF fusion, 105 BRAF V600E, 172 non-BRAF); 180 with all 4 MRI sequences
headline_result: best single sequence FLAIR macro-AUC 0.82; multisequence ensemble/concatenation macro-AUC 0.79

patient_population: 1,321 fetal MRI scans for training/evaluation; 80 additional publicly available fetal MRI scans as an external test set
clinical_problem: estimating gestational age from fetal brain imaging when last menstrual period/ultrasound biometry is unreliable, particularly in late pregnancy
model_description: Deep learning models (transfer-learned ResNet-101, compared against training from scratch and single- vs multi-view input) predict gestational age from multi-view fetal brain MRI; explainability analysis showed the model attends mainly to the lateral ventricles and cerebellum.
title: Deep learning based gestational age estimation from multi-view fetal brain magnetic resonance imaging.
study_design: retrospective model development with external validation
dataset_size: 1,321 fetal MRI scans (internal); 80 public MRI scans (external test set)
headline_result: internal test MAE 4.47 days, R2 0.96; external test MAE 6.57 days vs 9.42 days for biometric regression

model_family: multi-instance learning (deep learning) combined with clinical features
patient_population: 168 hospitalized pediatric patients aged 1-14 years with small bowel obstruction, January 2018-June 2024, multicenter
clinical_problem: distinguishing strangulated from simple small bowel obstruction in children on CT
model_description: A deep learning multi-instance learning (MIL) model analyzes abdominal CT images and is combined with clinical features to discriminate strangulated from simple small bowel obstruction in children; SHAP values explain feature contributions, and the model is tested as decision support for radiologists and surgeons.
title: Interpretable deep learning model for pediatric strangulated small bowel obstruction on CT: A multicenter study.
study_design: retrospective multicenter diagnostic model development and validation
headline_result: combined model AUC 0.87 (95% CI 0.72-1.00) in external test cohort; MIL assistance increased physician AUC by 2-20 percentage points

patient_population: 94 fetuses >=20 weeks' gestation after feticide (63 retrospective training, 28 prospective validation)
clinical_problem: estimating the postmortem interval in fetal death for forensic purposes
model_description: A gradient boosting machine model, built with automated machine learning, predicts the postmortem interval of a fetus from 3D postmortem ultrasound measurements of corneal and ocular volume (cornea-to-eyeball ratio), for forensic use; a web application was built to deploy the model.
release_evidence: A Shiny web application was developed to facilitate clinical implementation (no URL or open-source statement given)
title: Three-Dimensional Postmortem Ultrasound of the Fetal Corneal Volume to Estimate Postmortem Interval.
study_design: single-center model development with prospective validation cohort
headline_result: training R2 0.91 (RMSE 11.49h, MAE 8.45h); validation R2 0.75 (RMSE 18.32h, MAE 14.49h)

patient_population: pediatric emergency brain MRI cases (case series), including leukoencephalopathy in ALL, brain abscess, diffuse axonal injury, posterior circulation infarction, leukostasis syndrome, and posterior fossa tumor with hydrocephalus
clinical_problem: shortening emergency pediatric brain MRI while preserving diagnostic image quality
model_description: Two vendor deep-learning-accelerated MRI protocols, GOBrain (3D volumetric encoding, compressed sensing, DL reconstruction) and Deep Resolve Swift Brain (multi-shot EPI with DL reconstruction), are demonstrated on a series of pediatric emergency brain cases to produce a multi-contrast diagnostic brain MRI in minutes.
release_evidence: GOBrain and Deep Resolve Swift Brain, developed by Siemens Healthineers
title: Insights into Accelerated MRI Protocols for Pediatric Brain Assessment in Emergency Cases.

model_family: random forest (ensemble) and L2-penalized logistic regression radiomics
patient_population: 21 fetal MRIs with prenatal alcohol exposure and 45 without, gestational age matched
clinical_problem: detecting effects of prenatal alcohol exposure on fetal liver development
model_description: Texture-based radiomics features from fetal liver MRI are used to train random forest and L2-penalized logistic regression classifiers to try to discriminate fetuses with prenatal alcohol exposure from those without, alongside manual liver volumetry.
title: Analysis of fetal MRI data reveals no effect on liver maturation following prenatal alcohol exposure.
headline_result: ROC-AUC 0.43 (random forest), 0.40 (logistic regression) - radiomics could not discriminate exposure status; no significant difference in liver volume or signal intensity

patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal MRI (literature review)
clinical_problem: reviewing radiomics applications for fetal brain development assessment, malformation phenotyping, and outcome prediction
model_description: A narrative review of fetal brain MRI radiomics, covering technical foundations (acquisition, segmentation, feature extraction, machine learning models) and clinical applications: brain development phenotyping, Chiari II malformation/edema, isolated ventriculomegaly persistence, and neurodevelopmental outcome prediction.
title: Radiomics in fetal brain MRI: a narrative review.

patient_population: 40 pediatric patients (age 12.16+/-2.56 years) referred for suspected MASLD
clinical_problem: noninvasive quantification of liver fat (MASLD) in obese children
model_description: Two AI approaches -- an XGBoost radiomics model and a deep learning model (Mod-MHDNet) -- use ultrasound radiofrequency data, attenuation parameters, and clinical variables to estimate pediatric liver fat fraction, benchmarked against MRI-PDFF as the reference standard.
title: AI-powered ultrasound radiofrequency analysis for non-invasive pediatric liver fat quantification.
headline_result: R2 = 0.81 (XGBoost) and 0.76 (Mod-MHDNet) vs MRI-PDFF; mean bias <0.4 percentage points

model_family: LASSO-selected ultrasound radiomics + logistic regression nomogram
patient_population: 271 pregnant women with placenta previa from two centers in China (190 training, 81 external validation)
clinical_problem: predicting placenta accreta spectrum in women with placenta previa
model_description: Radiomic features from gray-scale prenatal ultrasound images of the placenta are selected by LASSO and combined with the number of prior cesarean deliveries in a logistic regression nomogram to predict placenta accreta spectrum in women with placenta previa.
title: Nomogram combining ultrasound radiomics and clinical factors for predicting placenta accreta spectrum in patients with placenta previa: a two-center study.
study_design: retrospective two-center model development with external validation
headline_result: clinical-radiomics nomogram AUC 0.859 (training), 0.822 (external validation)

model_family: multivariable logistic regression (planned); machine learning as secondary analysis
patient_population: non-intervened fetuses diagnosed with PA/CS-IVS between 16+0 and 28+6 weeks' gestation, international cohort, retrospective (from 2013) plus prospective validation
clinical_problem: predicting postnatal circulation outcome in fetuses with pulmonary atresia/critical pulmonary stenosis with intact ventricular septum, for counseling and intervention selection
model_description: Study protocol for an international cohort that will use standardized prenatal and postnatal fetal echocardiographic data to build a multivariable logistic-regression prognostic model (with a planned machine-learning secondary analysis) predicting postnatal circulation outcome in fetuses with pulmonary atresia/critical pulmonary stenosis with intact ventricular septum.
title: Development and validation of a prognostic model of postnatal circulation in fetuses with pulmonary atresia or critical pulmonary stenosis with intact ventricular septum: protocol for an observational cohort study with prospective validation.
study_design: protocol for an international observational cohort study with prospective external validation

model_family: automated brain volumetry + machine-learning-style feature selection with logistic regression
body_region: brain (limbic structures: amygdala, hippocampus, nucleus accumbens)
patient_population: 151 late-preterm children (31 with language delay, 120 without), T1-weighted MRI at term-equivalent age
clinical_problem: identifying structural brain correlates of language delay in late-preterm children
model_description: NeuroQuant, an automated volumetry tool, measures limbic and striatal brain structure volumes from term-equivalent-age T1 MRI in late-preterm infants; exploratory feature selection and logistic regression relate these volumes to later receptive and expressive language delay.
title: Limbic structural markers of language delay in late-preterm children by NeuroQuant and machine learning.
headline_result: language delay associated with increased left amygdalar volume and decreased hippocampal volume

model_family: cascaded dual-transfer learning (TEN-S: transfer EfficientNetV2; TY-PS: transfer YOLOv11)
patient_population: 9,142 fetal aortic arch echocardiographic long-axis view images and 58 ultrasound clips from three medical institutions
clinical_problem: screening for ductal-dependent congenital heart disease and differentiating critical subtypes (coarctation of aorta, interrupted aortic arch, transposition of great arteries) on fetal echocardiography
model_description: TLEUDS is a cascaded dual-transfer-learning system for fetal echocardiography: a first module (TEN-S, based on EfficientNetV2) screens for ductal-dependent congenital heart disease, and a second module (TY-PS, based on YOLOv11) further classifies critical subtypes (coarctation of the aorta, interrupted aortic arch, transposition of the great arteries), designed to handle variable image quality across sites.
title: TLEUDS: a cascade Dual-Transfer learning system with quality- and knowledge-enhanced for precise fetal CHD screening.
study_design: retrospective multicenter model development and validation
dataset_size: 9,142 fetal aortic arch images and 58 ultrasound clips from three institutions
headline_result: sensitivity 0.988 (D-CHD overall), 0.941 (CoA), 0.966 (IAA), 0.900 (TGA); specificity 0.988, 0.987, 1.000, 0.956 respectively

patient_population: 150 neonates (dHCP), 133 infants (BCP), 70 infants (in-house) = 353 total
clinical_problem: Reliably quantifying perivascular spaces in the basal ganglia on infant brain MRI to study the glymphatic system, which is challenging in infants
model_description: A deep-learning method using anatomy-informed pseudo-labels jointly segments the basal ganglia (BG) and BG perivascular spaces (PVS) on infant brain MRI across three cohorts with different acquisition protocols.
journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
title: Improved BG-PVS Quantification in Infant Brain MRI Using Anatomy-Informed Pseudo-Labels for Joint BG and PVS Segmentation.
study_design: retrospective multi-cohort technical development and validation study
headline_result: BG Dice 0.91 (dHCP), 0.86-0.89 (external with fine-tuning); PVS quantification agreement r=0.90-0.99, ICC>=0.96

patient_population: pediatric patients (ages 0-17) captured in FDA device labeling; analysis of 952 FDA AI device submissions (Nov 1995-June 2024)
clinical_problem: Characterize the landscape of FDA-regulated AI-enabled medical devices with pediatric indications, including radiology devices
model_description: A cross-sectional analysis of the FDA AI-Enabled Medical Device List characterizing which of 952 marketed AI devices (most in radiology) carry pediatric age-range indications, review times, and clinical trial registration.
release_evidence: FDA's AI-Enabled Medical Device List... Marketing submissions reviewed by the FDA
title: FDA-Regulated AI-Enabled Medical Devices With Pediatric Indications.
study_design: retrospective cross-sectional study of FDA regulatory submissions
dataset_size: 952 FDA AI device submissions; 42 (4.4%) with pediatric age ranges
headline_result: 42/952 (4.4%) devices had pediatric indications; radiology = 75.9% of all devices but only 42.9% of pediatric-labeled devices; pediatric device review time longer (162 vs 134 days, P=.049)

model_family: deep learning (HRNet-based) with pixel intensity data transformation
patient_population: 3,899 full-spine radiographs from 7 hospitals (2 in Hong Kong, 5 in Mainland China), January 2012-August 2024
clinical_problem: automating Cobb angle measurement and severity classification for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis across multiple hospitals
model_description: SpineHRNet+ is a deep learning model that predicts Cobb angle and scoliosis severity from full-spine radiographs; this study adds a real-time pixel-intensity data transformation step to standardize contrast/brightness across scanners and hospitals, improving robustness when applied to radiographs from centers outside the training sites.
title: Scalable and Robust Artificial Intelligence for Spine Alignment Assessment: Multicenter Study Enabled by Real-Time Data Transformation.
study_design: retrospective multicenter model development and external validation
dataset_size: 3,899 radiographs from 7 hospitals (3,034 training/internal validation, 865 external validation)
headline_result: mean Cobb angle prediction error within 4 degrees (SD 3.12 degrees), R2 >0.90 across all centers; sensitivity 90.18%, negative predictive value 93.16% for severity grading

patient_population: 203 consecutive AIS surgical patients
clinical_problem: Using a large language model to recommend surgical fusion levels (upper/lower instrumented vertebrae) for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis surgery, based on structured clinical and radiological (Lenke classification) data
model_description: DeepSeek-R1, a large language model, receives structured clinical and radiological data (including Lenke classification derived from spinal imaging) as text prompts and outputs recommended upper and lower instrumented vertebrae levels for scoliosis fusion surgery.
release_evidence: DeepSeek Reasoning Model R1 (DeepSeek-R1) is a publicly available large language model
title: DeepSeek-R1 performance in fusion planning of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: A preliminary study.
headline_result: Surgically reasonable fusion levels (Likert >=3) in 70.9% of cases (144/203); ICC 0.840 inter-rater agreement

patient_population: pediatric patients (<21 years) across 17 included studies, >10,000 radiographs pooled in meta-analysis
clinical_problem: diagnostic accuracy of AI (CNN) models for detecting fractures on pediatric appendicular radiographs, compared with human readers
model_description: Systematic review and meta-analysis pooling diagnostic accuracy of CNN-based AI models that take plain radiographs as input and output fracture presence/absence, benchmarked against a human-reader reference standard.
title: Convolutional neural networks in paediatric fracture detection: pooled evidence from a systematic review and meta-analysis.
dataset_size: >10,000 radiographs (11 studies in meta-analysis, 17 in review)
headline_result: Pooled sensitivity 0.92, specificity 0.90, diagnostic odds ratio 104.6

patient_population: 774 videos (68,106 images), 3 hospitals (IUGC Grand Challenge dataset)
clinical_problem: Improving deep-learning-based automatic biometry from intrapartum ultrasound video to monitor labor progress where trained sonographers are scarce
model_description: The Intrapartum Ultrasound Grand Challenge (IUGC, with MICCAI 2024) framework integrates standard-plane classification, fetal head-pubic-symphysis segmentation, and biometry measurement; this paper reviews eight teams' submitted deep-learning methods and analyzes their preprocessing, augmentation, architecture and post-processing choices.
release_evidence: "The solutions and the complete dataset are publicly accessible"
title: Beyond benchmarks of IUGC: Rethinking requirements of deep learning method for intrapartum ultrasound biometry from fetal ultrasound videos.

patient_population: 53 pediatric lymphoma patients for training, 30 additional scans for testing
clinical_problem: detecting pediatric lymphoma lesions on whole-body PET/MRI
model_description: A convolutional neural network is trained on annotated whole-body [18F]FDG-PET/MRI scans from pediatric lymphoma patients to detect lesions across five anatomical regions, and its sensitivity, specificity, and reading time are compared with a pediatric radiologist and a radiology resident.
journal: American journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
title: CNN-based detection of pediatric lymphoma on whole body [18F]FDG-PET/MRI.
headline_result: CNN sensitivity 84.6%, specificity 93.7% (vs resident 69.2%/81.5%, vs pediatric radiologist 98.7%/99.5%); median read time 4 min (CNN) vs 8 min (radiologist) vs 15 min (resident)

patient_population: 232 patients with congenital biliary dilatation (116 with ventrally positioned right hepatic artery, 116 controls), single center
clinical_problem: preoperative identification of a ventrally positioned right hepatic artery in children with congenital biliary dilatation, to reduce surgical risk
model_description: A YOLOv12-based model trained on radiologist-selected key arterial-phase CT slices detects a ventrally positioned right hepatic artery, a surgically important anatomic variant, in children with congenital biliary dilatation, and is compared against two radiologists.
title: Deep learning model for automated identification of ventrally positioned right hepatic artery in contrast-enhanced computed tomography of pediatric congenital biliary dilatation: development and clinical application.
study_design: retrospective single-center model development and reader comparison
headline_result: best sub-model (YOLOv12n) recall 0.842, F1 0.914, mAP50 0.989, AUC 0.977; outperformed junior radiologist (AUC 0.737, P<0.001), comparable to senior radiologist (AUC 0.947, P=0.515)

patient_population: bladder and fetal head ultrasound segmentation datasets (not further specified)
clinical_problem: enabling real-time autonomous ultrasound image segmentation (e.g. prenatal fetal biometry, bladder/urinary retention monitoring) on wearable, battery-powered devices
model_description: A custom 28nm chip implements a binarized U-Net with 4-bit skip connections for on-device, real-time medical image segmentation in wearable ultrasound patches, validated on bladder and fetal head segmentation datasets, aiming to preserve accuracy while eliminating external memory and cutting energy use for battery-powered, privacy-preserving deployment.
journal: IEEE transactions on biomedical circuits and systems
title: A 23-µJ-per-Frame All-on-Chip TinyML U-Net Processor for Real-Time Autonomous Image Segmentation in Miniaturized Ultrasound Devices.
headline_result: 13.4 frames per second, 23 microJ per frame on bladder and fetal head segmentation datasets

model_family: self-supervised contrastive learning (dual spatial/temporal contrastive loss)
patient_population: 92 subjects, each with 30-minute extended fetal ultrasound video recordings
clinical_problem: objectively detecting fetal movement from ultrasound video to assess prenatal health
model_description: CURL is a self-supervised contrastive learning framework that learns motion representations from extended obstetric ultrasound video recordings, using a dual spatial-temporal contrastive loss and a task-specific sampling strategy, to detect fetal movement without relying on maternal perception or cardiotocography.
release_evidence: Our code is available at: https://github.com/Mr-TalhaIlyas/CURL/
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: Towards Objective Obstetric Ultrasound Assessment: Contrastive Representation Learning for Fetal Movement Detection.
study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study
headline_result: sensitivity 78.01%, AUROC 81.60%

clinical_problem: Reviewing MRI-based synthetic CT (deep learning) as a radiation-free alternative to conventional CT for orthopaedic bone imaging, with particular relevance in children
model_description: Perspective/review of deep-learning-based synthetic CT generation from MRI sequences (zero echo time, ultrashort echo time, 3D gradient recalled echo) as a radiation-free bone-imaging alternative to CT, with particular relevance to pediatric patients.
journal: The Journal of bone and joint surgery. American volume
title: MRI-Based Synthetic CT Shows Promise as a Radiation-Free Alternative to Conventional CT in Orthopaedics.

body_region: brain (multimodal neurocritical care biosignals including MRI)
patient_population: pediatric and neonatal neurocritical care patients (literature review)
clinical_problem: prognosis, monitoring, and future pediatric applications of multimodal AI in neurocritical care, including neuroimaging-based neuroprognostication
model_description: A review of AI/machine-learning approaches that fuse multimodal neurocritical-care biosignals (hemodynamic waveforms, intracranial pressure, EEG, near-infrared spectroscopy, neuroimaging, and EHR data) for monitoring and prognosis, with examples including MRI-based neuroprognostication in neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, and a discussion of validation and implementation priorities for pediatric translation.
title: Artificial Intelligence in Neurocritical Care : Multimodal Biosignal Analysis for Prognosis, Monitoring, and Future Pediatric Applications.

model_family: multivariate brain-based predictive machine learning models
body_region: brain (cortical thickness, surface area, gray matter volume)
patient_population: Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study participants at baseline (n=8630), 2-year (n=5998), 4-year (n=4844), and 6-year (n=3100) follow-up
clinical_problem: identifying neuroanatomical correlates of impulsivity in youth
model_description: Multivariate brain-based predictive models use regional cortical thickness, surface area, and gray matter volume from structural MRI to predict self-reported impulsivity measures in a large, longitudinal youth cohort, examining consistency across sexes and developmental timepoints.
title: Neuroanatomy reflects individual variability in impulsivity in youth.

patient_population: 103 pediatric patients (median age 11 years), 2011-2024
clinical_problem: Automating tumor segmentation and PET parameter extraction for pediatric glioma [18F]F-DOPA PET scans, replacing time-consuming manual delineation
model_description: A U-Net deep-learning model, fine-tuned via transfer learning from adult glioma datasets, automatically segments pediatric brain tumors on [18F]F-DOPA PET scans and extracts static and dynamic PET parameters (e.g., tumor-to-striatum ratio).
title: U-Net-based transfer learning for automated tumour segmentation enabling fully automated [18F]F-DOPA PET analysis in paediatric gliomas.
dataset_size: 103 pediatric patients (90 for statistical/survival analysis, 32 for dynamic analysis)
headline_result: Dice score 0.82 +/- 0.11; automated indices correlated significantly with tumor grade and survival (p<0.05)

patient_population: 142 pediatric patients (<16 years), 2021-2024
clinical_problem: Comparing image quality and radiation dose between deep-learning and hybrid iterative reconstruction in unenhanced pediatric chest CT
model_description: Deep-learning image reconstruction (DLIR) is compared against hybrid iterative reconstruction (HIR) for unenhanced pediatric chest CT, assessing subjective and objective (noise, attenuation) image quality and radiation dose across age groups.
title: Optimizing pediatric chest CT: superior image quality and lower radiation dose with deep learning reconstruction.
headline_result: Lower image noise with DLIR (e.g., lung 63 vs 81 HU, p=0.017); radiation dose reduced (CTDIvol 1.6 vs 4.3 mGy; effective dose 0.70 vs 2.51 mSv, p<0.001)

patient_population: 1,811 annotated AP/lateral radiographs from a single tertiary pediatric orthopedic center, 2010-2017; tested on 215 independent radiograph pairs
clinical_problem: classifying and triaging pediatric supracondylar humerus fractures (Gartland system) into operative versus non-operative management in the emergency department
model_description: A convolutional neural network trained with transfer learning classifies pediatric elbow radiographs into operative (Gartland IIB, III, flexion type) versus non-operative supracondylar humerus fracture categories, to support emergency-department triage where specialist orthopedic input may not be immediately available.
title: Artificial intelligence-assisted triage of pediatric supracondylar humerus fractures in emergency departments: A single-centre validation study.
headline_result: accuracy 77% (95% CI 71-82%), AUROC 0.84 (95% CI 0.78-0.89); kappa vs surgeon consensus 0.51

patient_population: 125 adolescents aged 12-19 years (48 with major depressive disorder, 36 with bipolar disorder, 41 healthy controls)
clinical_problem: distinguishing adolescent major depressive disorder from bipolar disorder using resting-state fMRI network features
model_description: Input is resting-state fMRI functional network features, including nodal centrality and clustering coefficient from graph-theoretical analysis. A support vector machine trained on these network features distinguishes adolescent major depressive disorder from bipolar disorder, driven mainly by insula and cingulate gyrus features. It is presented as a research classifier, not a validated diagnostic test.
title: Altered brain network topology in adolescents with major depressive disorder and bipolar disorder: A resting-state fMRI graph-theoretical and machine learning study.
dataset_size: 125 adolescents (48 MDD, 36 bipolar disorder, 41 healthy controls)
headline_result: SVM classifier distinguished adolescent MDD from bipolar disorder with 88.24% accuracy (p < 0.001)

clinical_problem: early diagnosis of necrotizing enterocolitis from deep-learning-derived features on neonatal abdominal radiographs
model_description: A letter to the editor discussing the implications and next steps of deep-learning-derived features on neonatal abdominal radiographs for early diagnosis of necrotizing enterocolitis, commenting on a prior study.
title: Letter to the Editor: Deep learning-derived features on neonatal abdominal radiographs-implications and next steps for early NEC diagnosis.

model_family: dual-stream deep learning (EfficientNet + MLP with Feature-wise Linear Modulation)
patient_population: 178 patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis undergoing preoperative standing posteroanterior radiography and pulmonary function testing
clinical_problem: predicting pulmonary function impairment (FVC/FEV1 abnormality) from spinal deformity in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
model_description: A dual-stream deep learning model combines an EfficientNet backbone reading standing spine radiographs with a multilayer perceptron processing structured clinical data, fused via Feature-wise Linear Modulation, to jointly predict abnormal forced vital capacity and FEV1 in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis before surgery.
journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
title: Spinal morphology-based multimodal AI for predicting pulmonary dysfunction in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
study_design: retrospective model development study, five-fold cross-validation
headline_result: macro-AUC 0.827 (FVC AUC 0.814, FEV1 AUC 0.841), outperforming logistic regression on tabular features (macro AUC ~0.71)

patient_population: Indian children and adolescents
clinical_problem: Improving automated bone-age assessment accuracy by modeling segment-specific skeletal maturation instead of assuming uniform maturation across the hand, in Indian children
model_description: digiBONE segments hand radiographs into short-bone, carpal and wrist regions and trains separate convolutional neural networks for each segment plus a full-hand model; segmental predictions are combined into a composite Greulich-Pyle bone-age estimate.
title: digiBONE: an automated tool for segmental Greulich-Pyle bone age assessment of Indian children and adolescents.
headline_result: Mean absolute difference 4.75 months (boys), 4.93 months (girls)

patient_population: 174 pediatric patients with high/low-grade glioma, medulloblastoma, ependymoma and other tumors, single center
clinical_problem: segmenting pediatric brain tumor subregions across heterogeneous tumor types
model_description: A 3D nnU-Net is trained on multi-sequence MRI (T1, T1 post-contrast, T2, FLAIR) to segment four pediatric brain tumor subregions (whole tumor, T2-hyperintensity, enhancing tumor, cystic component), compared against inter-rater variability.
title: Enhancing efficiency in pediatric brain tumor segmentation using a pathologically diverse single-center clinical dataset.
headline_result: Mean Dice 0.85 whole tumor / T2-hyperintensity, 0.75 enhancing tumor, 0.26 cystic component

patient_population: children with suspected or diagnosed neurodevelopmental disorders (literature review)
clinical_problem: early detection and intervention planning for neurodevelopmental disorders (autism, ADHD, genetic/metabolic syndromes, cerebral palsy, developmental delay) using MRI
model_description: A review of pediatric MRI approaches (diffusion imaging, quantitative MRI, resting-state fMRI, spectroscopy) combined with machine learning and integrative genomics for early biomarker-based detection and risk stratification of neurodevelopmental disorders.
title: Neurodevelopmental disorders in children: the role of MRI in early detection and intervention planning.

model_family: deep learning automated segmentation + classification pipeline
patient_population: 2,164 images from institution 1 for training/hold-out testing; external validation at institution 2 (533 radiograph pairs); patients with confirmed LCPD at two tertiary children's hospitals
clinical_problem: staging Legg-Calve-Perthes disease (modified Waldenstrom system) from hip radiographs
model_description: A deep-learning pipeline automatically segments the femoral epiphysis on paired AP and frog-lateral hip radiographs, extracts quantifiable epiphyseal parameters (e.g., sclerosis, epiphyseal area), and classifies modified Waldenstrom stage of Legg-Calve-Perthes disease, evaluated for both early-vs-late staging and full staging.
journal: Journal of the Pediatric Orthopaedic Society of North America
title: Determination of Modified Waldenström Staging in Legg-Calvé-Perthes Disease Using Deep Learning.
study_design: retrospective multicenter model development and external validation
headline_result: hold-out AUROC 0.82 (early vs late); external validation AUROC 0.75; segmentation Dice 0.93

model_family: vision-language model + multimodal large language model with retrieval-augmented generation
patient_population: VinDr-PCXR public pediatric chest radiograph dataset
clinical_problem: generating interpretable, evidence-based diagnoses from pediatric chest radiographs
model_description: A two-stage system: a vision-language model fine-tuned on pediatric data first extracts structured radiological findings from a chest radiograph, then a multimodal large language model combines the image, extracted findings, patient demographics, and retrieved external medical knowledge to generate a final diagnosis, aiming to mirror radiologists' evidence-based reasoning rather than a black-box classification.
title: Evidence-Guided Diagnostic Reasoning for Pediatric Chest Radiology Based on Multimodal Large Language Models.
study_design: retrospective technical development on a public benchmark dataset
headline_result: 90.1% diagnostic accuracy, 70.9% F1-score, 82.5% AUC; up to 13.1% accuracy improvement over baselines

patient_population: children aged 0-18 with brain tumors, across 24 studies published 2010-2025
clinical_problem: classifying pediatric brain tumors and predicting their molecular subtype from imaging
model_description: A systematic review that scores the methodological quality of the field rather than only its accuracy, using the Newcastle-Ottawa scale and the CLAIM checklist. The headline accuracies are high — median AUC 0.91 — and most studies were rated low risk of bias, but only three of 24 validated on an independent cohort. Radiomics still dominates over deep learning here, which reflects how small the available pediatric cohorts are.
title: Artificial intelligence and radiomics for pediatric brain tumor classification and molecular characterization: a systematic review.
headline_result: reported AUCs 0.73-0.98 (median 0.91); 96% used MRI and 88% radiomics-based machine learning; only 12.5% performed external validation

patient_population: 41,625 individuals aged 4-18 years, lateral cephalometric radiographs
clinical_problem: quantifying normal craniofacial growth and sexual dimorphism patterns across childhood and adolescence to guide orthodontic/maxillofacial treatment timing
model_description: An end-to-end deep learning model, trained without manual landmark annotation, learns imaging features on lateral cephalometric radiographs associated with continuous age and sex; Grad-CAM saliency maps and two new indices (Age-related and Sex-related Saliency Index) quantify which craniofacial bone regions drive age- and sex-related appearance changes during growth.
title: Quantification of Craniofacial Growth Pattern Based on Deep Learning.
study_design: retrospective large-scale deep learning development study

patient_population: 301 patients, second-trimester fetal cardiac ultrasound
clinical_problem: Automating extraction of the four-chamber view and cardiac biometric parameters from fetal cardiac ultrasound to screen for congenital heart disease
model_description: YOLOv7 detects the four-chamber view (4CV) in fetal cardiac ultrasound videos; UNet 3+ and SegFormer segment cardiac structures to automatically compute cardiothoracic area ratio, cardiac axis, and cardiac position for congenital heart disease screening.
title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Automated Assessment of the Four-Chamber View in Fetal Cardiac Ultrasound Videos.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development study with clinical comparison
headline_result: AI models achieved screening performance comparable to expert obstetricians (22 obstetricians in comparison study)

patient_population: children <=18 years with cerebral palsy undergoing hip surveillance radiographs, across 6 included studies (over 4,000 radiographs)
clinical_problem: screening for hip dysplasia in children with cerebral palsy using AI-analyzed pelvic radiographs
model_description: A systematic review comparing AI models against expert clinicians for detecting hip dysplasia (by migration percentage) on pelvic radiographs in children with cerebral palsy undergoing routine hip surveillance.
title: Automated Analysis of Pelvic Radiographs for Hip Dysplasia Screening Using Artificial Intelligence in Children with Cerebral Palsy: A Systematic Review.
headline_result: AI sensitivity 70-97.4%, specificity 85-96%, AUC 0.923-0.999 across 6 studies; only one study externally validated

model_family: multitask, view-agnostic transformer-based architecture (expands on PanEcho)
patient_population: internal cohort: 54,727 echocardiograms (3.4 million videos) from Boston Children's Hospital, median age 7.1 years; referral cohort: 3,356 echocardiograms (167,484 videos) from external US and international centers, median age 2.5 years
clinical_problem: automated detection of critical and non-critical congenital heart disease on echocardiography, to extend expert-level interpretation to under-resourced settings
model_description: EchoFocus-CHD is a multitask, view-agnostic deep learning model (built on the PanEcho architecture with an added transformer encoder) that detects 12 critical and 8 noncritical congenital heart lesions, individually and as composites, from full pediatric echocardiogram studies, trained and tested internally then evaluated on an independent US/international referral cohort.
title: Automated Echocardiographic Detection of Congenital Heart Disease Using Artificial Intelligence.
study_design: retrospective multicenter model development with external referral-cohort validation
dataset_size: 54,727 echocardiograms internal (3.4M videos); 3,356 echocardiograms referral cohort (167,484 videos)
headline_result: internal AUROC 0.94 (critical CHD composite), 0.90 (noncritical composite); referral cohort AUROC 0.77 for critical CHD, improving to 0.87 after retraining on all US data

model_family: cross-modal attention transformer with self-supervised contrastive learning + spatiotemporal convolution-LSTM
patient_population: 320 pregnancies (160 with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy), weekly imaging 28-36 weeks' gestation, prospective cohort
clinical_problem: staging fetal lung maturity and individualizing antenatal glucocorticoid dosing
model_description: A physiology-informed multimodal AI framework combines 2D/3D ultrasound, shear-wave elastography, Doppler, and maternal metabolomics, constrained by a placenta-pulmonary coupling model, to unsupervised-stage fetal lung maturity and predict an individualized antenatal glucocorticoid dose and administration window, using a cross-modal attention transformer and a convolution-LSTM dosing branch.
title: Placenta-pulmonary coupling-guided multimodal AI for fetal lung maturity staging and individualized glucocorticoid therapy.
study_design: prospective cohort study with multimodal AI framework development
headline_result: downstream classifier 92.3% accuracy distinguishing early vs late maturity; dosing predicted within +/-0.5 mg of clinical dose, 27% reduction in projected RDS risk vs standard dosing

patient_population: 98 pediatric head CT examinations (0-15 years; 48 hydrocephalus, 50 normal)
clinical_problem: Automated 3D classification of pediatric hydrocephalus from ventricular enlargement on head CT, improving on conventional 2D CT indices
model_description: A multiscale attention 3D convolutional neural network (MSA3DNet) classifies pediatric head CT scans as hydrocephalus versus normal based on 3D ventricular enlargement, benchmarked against a conventional 3D CNN.
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
title: Attention-Driven Deep Learning for Hydrocephalus: Preliminary Benchmarking of Multiscale 3D Attention Against Conventional 3D CNN Models Using Ventricular Enlargement on CT.
headline_result: AUC 0.971 (MSA3DNet) vs 0.952 (conventional 3D CNN); sensitivity 0.958 vs 0.916

patient_population: 151 obstetric sonographers, midwives, gynecologists, and fetal medicine consultants in the Netherlands performing fetal ultrasound
clinical_problem: clinician attitudes toward AI as a diagnostic aid during fetal anomaly ultrasound
model_description: A survey of Dutch obstetric sonographers and gynecologists on their attitudes, expectations, and concerns about AI applications (already used by 62% of respondents, mainly for automated biometry) as a diagnostic aid during fetal anomaly ultrasound scans.
title: Artificial Intelligence as an Add-On Instrument in Fetal Ultrasound; Sonographers' and Obstetricians' Expectations.
headline_result: 62% already use AI (mainly automated biometry); 87% support AI use; 86% want to retain final clinical authority

patient_population: 79 adolescents (10-18 years) with TMJ pain undergoing panoramic radiography and MRI
clinical_problem: diagnosing adolescent temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis using clinical and imaging predictors
model_description: Three decision-tree machine learning models (clinical-only, imaging-only, and combined clinical+imaging) predict temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis in adolescents using panoramic radiograph and MRI findings alongside clinical variables, to identify the strongest diagnostic predictors.
journal: Journal of oral & facial pain and headache
title: Decoding adolescent TMJ osteoarthritis with multimodal machine learning.
study_design: retrospective diagnostic model development study, nested 5-fold cross-validation
headline_result: imaging-only model AUROC 0.719; combined model AUROC 0.657 (sensitivity improved to 0.606); panoramic radiograph finding of TMJ-OA was strongest single predictor (OR 3.93)

body_region: kidney / urinary tract (renal pelvis and calyces)
patient_population: pediatric patients with congenital hydronephrosis undergoing magnetic resonance urography
clinical_problem: reconstructing 3D anatomy of congenital hydronephrosis for diagnosis, prognosis, and urodynamic simulation
model_description: KidMesh is an end-to-end deep neural network that directly reconstructs a 3D mesh of the hydronephrotic renal collecting system from magnetic resonance urography, without requiring manual mesh-level annotations or external post-processing, enabling downstream urodynamic flow simulation.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: KidMesh: Computational Mesh Reconstruction for Pediatric Congenital Hydronephrosis Using Deep Neural Networks.
study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study
headline_result: reconstruction in 0.4s average; 3.7%/0.2% of vertices with error >3.2mm/6.4mm; Dice 0.86 against manual masks

patient_population: Adolescents with knee injuries after skiing
clinical_problem: Diagnosing and classifying knee injuries (meniscus tears, ACL injuries, cartilage injuries) on MRI in adolescents after skiing
model_description: A hybrid deep learning model combining U-Net++ for pixel-level segmentation of injured knee regions with DenseNet121 for classifying the injury type from MRI scans.
title: Magnetic resonance imaging diagnosis of knee injuries after skiing in adolescents under deep learning.
study_design: retrospective model development and internal testing
headline_result: Segmentation Dice 0.89, IoU 0.82; classification accuracy 0.90, F1 0.91, AUC 0.95

patient_population: pediatric musculoskeletal imaging patients (review)
clinical_problem: Summarize current clinical applications, validated commercial AI tools, and limitations of AI in pediatric musculoskeletal imaging (bone age, fractures, scoliosis, hip dysplasia, limb length, bone dysplasia, tumors)
model_description: A narrative review summarizing validated commercial AI tools (bone age, bone health index, appendicular fracture detection, scoliosis measurement, limb length discrepancy, hip dysplasia assessment) and emerging applications (rib/vertebral fracture detection, non-accidental trauma, bone dysplasia, tumor assessment) in pediatric musculoskeletal imaging.
release_evidence: validated AI software for commercial use includes the detection of appendicular fractures, automated measurement of scoliosis, assessment of lower limb length discrepancy, and assessment of developing hip dysplasia
title: Current applications and challenges of artificial intelligence applied to diagnostics in pediatric musculoskeletal imaging.

patient_population: 62 pediatric patients (mean age 7.4 +/- 4.9 years), sedated and awake
clinical_problem: Improving diagnostic image quality of motion-robust, sedation-free single-shot T2-weighted pediatric brain MRI
model_description: A deep learning framework combining compressed sensing and CNNs to reconstruct and enhance single-shot T2-weighted brain MRI, taking undersampled single-shot data as input and producing higher-quality T2-weighted images.
title: Deep learning improves image quality in motion-robust and sedation-free pediatric brain MRI.
headline_result: Higher aCNR (29.9 vs 26.7, p<0.001), aSNR (41.6 vs 38.2, p=0.003), improved sharpness (ERD 0.90mm vs 1.35mm, p<0.001) vs conventional CS reconstruction

model_family: machine learning / deep learning (SVM, ANN, CNN) [review]
patient_population: children with suspected/diagnosed neurodevelopmental disorders (64 studies from an umbrella review, Jan 2015-Aug 2025)
clinical_problem: Synthesize evidence on AI-assisted diagnosis of neurodevelopmental disorders (ASD, ADHD, intellectual disability, communication and learning disorders) in children, largely from neuroimaging data
model_description: An umbrella review of 64 systematic reviews/meta-analyses on machine learning and deep learning models (SVMs, neural networks, CNNs) that take neuroimaging and other data (electrophysiological, clinical, motion/sensor) as input and output a diagnostic classification for autism, ADHD, and related neurodevelopmental disorders.
title: Artificial intelligence support for diagnosis of neurodevelopmental disorders during childhood: an umbrella review.
study_design: umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses
dataset_size: 64 included studies (148 records screened); neuroimaging modality used in 59 studies
headline_result: Diagnostic accuracy ranged 66% (facial/eye movement-based) to 99% (neuroimaging/voice/motion-based); 80% of studies rated critically low methodological quality (AMSTAR-2)

clinical_problem: Estimating skeletal (bone) age from radiographs for growth assessment
model_description: A conceptual dual deep neural network framework integrating anatomical/developmental knowledge, with one network extracting morphological features from public datasets and a second capturing age-related growth patterns; illustrative simulations only, no real-world data collected.
title: Biologically informed dual deep learning for skeletal maturity prediction in pediatrics.
study_design: conceptual perspective with illustrative simulations, no real-world validation

patient_population: Infants (Baby Connectome Project dataset n=154; in-house retrospective dataset n=52)
clinical_problem: Segmenting the lateral ventricles and choroid plexus on infant brain MRI to study cerebrospinal fluid dynamics and neurodevelopment
model_description: A fully automated deep learning segmentation method for joint lateral ventricle and choroid plexus segmentation on T1-weighted infant brain MRI, using an anatomy-aware loss enforcing that the choroid plexus is contained within the ventricles.
title: Automatic lateral ventricle and choroid plexus segmentation method in infant brain MR images.
study_design: retrospective method development and validation on two independent datasets
headline_result: Dice 0.818+/-0.075 (LV) and 0.827+/-0.084 (CP) in BCP dataset; Dice 0.964+/-0.060 (LV) and 0.932+/-0.059 (CP) in in-house dataset

patient_population: 60 children with Tetralogy of Fallot and 61 healthy controls
clinical_problem: Identifying brain structural alterations associated with neurodevelopmental risk in children with Tetralogy of Fallot
model_description: A radiomics-morphometry fusion model combining Pyradiomics and FreeSurfer-derived features from 68 brain regions on 3D T1-weighted MRI, using LASSO feature selection and SVM classification to distinguish children with Tetralogy of Fallot from healthy controls.
title: Quantitative radiomics and morphometry analysis of brain sub-regions reveals neurodevelopmental alterations in children with Tetralogy of Fallot.
headline_result: AUC 0.99 (training), 0.77 (testing)

patient_population: 1740 children under 5 years old undergoing skeletal survey for suspected physical abuse
clinical_problem: Detecting inflicted (non-accidental) fractures on skeletal survey radiographs in suspected physical abuse
model_description: A deep learning-based AI tool (BoneView) retrained to detect inflicted fractures on pediatric skeletal survey radiographs.
release_evidence: commercially available deep learning algorithm (BoneView)
title: Developing an artificial intelligence tool for detecting fractures of child abuse: preliminary findings.
headline_result: Baseline AUC 0.46; after preliminary retraining AUC 0.55, sensitivity 52%, specificity 67%

patient_population: 174 pediatric patients at Seoul Asan Medical Center (2018-2023)
clinical_problem: Automating detection of anatomical features of Tetralogy of Fallot from echocardiograms for screening
model_description: A Detectron2/Mask R-CNN-based deep learning model trained to detect four characteristic anatomical defects of Tetralogy of Fallot in echocardiographic images and videos, for screening in regions lacking pediatric cardiology specialists.
title: Real-time deep learning interpretation of echocardiographic video for automated detection of anatomical features associated with tetralogy of fallot in pediatric patients : a feasibility study.
headline_result: AUC ~1.00, F1 score 96.8%, >97% accuracy

patient_population: 50 infants (20 preterm, 30 full-term) at two sites (Boston, USA and Jimma, Ethiopia)
clinical_problem: Assessing infant body composition (fat and fat-free mass) and nutritional status using ultrasound
model_description: Planned CNN-based machine learning models to predict whole-body composition (fat/fat-free mass) from ultrasound images, as part of a feasibility pilot study establishing the scanning protocol and image database.
title: A machine learning approach to using ultrasound for body composition and nutritional status assessment in newborns: a pilot study protocol.
study_design: pilot study protocol (feasibility); ML models not yet trained/validated on full data

patient_population: 419 children (248 training, 62 testing, 109 external validation)
clinical_problem: Early prediction of refractory Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia in children using clinical, imaging and radiomics features from chest CT
model_description: Radiomics features extracted from chest CT (via PyRadiomics) are combined with clinical and imaging variables in random-forest models to predict which children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia will develop a refractory (treatment-resistant) course.
title: Early identification of refractory Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia in children using CT-based radiomics: a multicenter study.
study_design: retrospective multicenter study with external validation
headline_result: Integrated model AUC 0.811 (95% CI 0.704-0.917) in external validation, vs radiomics-only 0.784 and clinical-imaging-only 0.675

patient_population: Patients <18 years undergoing DXA and chest radiography at two tertiary hospitals
clinical_problem: Predicting bone mineral density (lumbar spine areal BMD) and detecting low BMD in children from chest radiographs
model_description: An AI model combining chest radiograph images with clinical variables (age, sex, height, weight) to predict lumbar spine areal BMD Z scores and detect low BMD, using DXA as the reference standard.
title: Deep Learning-based Bone Mineral Density Prediction Using Pediatric Chest Radiographs: A Multicenter Feasibility Study.
dataset_size: 1464 radiograph-DXA pairs (774 development, 376 internal test, 314 external test)
headline_result: Internal test: r=0.85, AUC 0.92 for low BMD; External test: r=0.76, AUC 0.90

patient_population: 174 pelvic radiographs (139 training, 35 testing)
clinical_problem: Detecting slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE) on pediatric pelvic radiographs
model_description: A two-stage deep learning model: U-Net++ segments the femoral head to define a region of focus, then an attention-guided EfficientNet B1 classifies the radiograph as SCFE or no SCFE, with Grad-CAM for interpretability.
title: Automated Detection of Pediatric Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis: A Deep Learning Approach Using Anatomically Informed Attention Guidance.

model_description: A hybrid ensemble deep learning model trained on air enema fluoroscopic images to objectively predict irreducibility of intussusception, used as a decision-support tool alongside radiologist interpretation.
title: Fluoroscopic image-driven deep learning model for predicting intussusception irreducibility during air enema in children.
study_design: retrospective diagnostic accuracy study with external validation
dataset_size: 1984 cases for development; real-world test (848), external test (110)
headline_result: AUC 0.89 (real-world test), 0.883 (external test); outperformed intermediate radiologist (AUC 0.89 vs 0.804, p<0.001) and comparable to senior radiologist

clinical_problem: Reviewing Doppler ultrasound, 3D vascular indices, and AI integration for placental perfusion assessment and early prediction of preeclampsia
model_description: A PRISMA-guided structured narrative review of 74 studies on Doppler-based placental perfusion, 3D power Doppler vascular indices (VI, FI, VFI), and AI models trained on voxel-level Doppler data and angiogenic biomarkers for early preeclampsia risk prediction.
title: Reimagining Placental Perfusion in Preeclampsia: Integrating Doppler Ultrasound, Three-dimensional Vascular Indices, and Predictive Artificial Intelligence.
headline_result: AI models trained on voxel-level Doppler data and angiogenic biomarkers achieved AUC 0.85-0.91 for early preeclampsia risk (as summarized from reviewed literature)

patient_population: 1,475 patients, fetal cardiac ultrasound 2019-2023
clinical_problem: Early prenatal detection of congenital heart disease from fetal echocardiography, integrating imaging with clinical metadata
model_description: Heartbeat, a multicenter multimodal dataset of fetal cardiac ultrasound images (standard views) and clinical metadata; Heart-ViT, a multimodal transformer integrating imaging features with patient metadata via adaptive layer normalization, was developed for CHD detection, alongside CNN baselines.
release_evidence: The dataset and analytical framework will be made publicly available to support further research
title: Heartbeat: a multimodal dataset of fetal echocardiography and clinical metadata for early detection of congenital heart disease.
study_design: multicenter dataset development and model benchmarking study
headline_result: Heart-ViT: sensitivity 79.17%, specificity 93.18%, AUROC 88.56%, F1 65.63%; 13.22-point F1 improvement over imaging-only baseline

model_family: WEKA ensemble classifiers (computer-aided diagnosis system, CADS)
patient_population: Children, adolescents, and adults with ASD (age-dependent cohorts, dataset size not stated)
age_groups: child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: Computer-aided diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder using resting-state fMRI functional connectivity, with age-specific classification models
model_description: An age-dependent computer-aided diagnosis system (CADS) using frequency-domain functional connectivity (via group-ICA, dual regression, and coherence analysis) from resting-state fMRI, with separate feature selection and classification for children, adolescent, and adult age groups.
title: Diagnostic Classification of Autism Spectrum Disorder in the Frequency Domain Using Resting-State fMRI.
headline_result: Classification accuracy: 95.23% (children), 88.1% (adolescents), 92.8% (adults)

patient_population: Stratified pediatric MRI dataset (size not stated)
clinical_problem: Diagnosing ADHD from pediatric brain MRI using an automated, objective imaging-based classifier
model_description: A biologically informed multi-stream deep learning framework combining a Vision Transformer (ViT) and Enhanced CNN (ECNN), fed raw MRI, phase spectrum transform, and quantile histogram equalization/denoising representations, to classify ADHD from pediatric brain MRI.
title: Hybrid Vi+ECNN framework for advanced ADHD diagnostic accuracy in medical imaging.
headline_result: Accuracy 99.4%, precision 99.3%, recall 99.5%, F1 0.99

patient_population: 680 individuals aged 6-30 years
age_groups: child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: Forensic/legal age estimation and age-threshold classification (12, 14, 16, 18 years) in living children and young adults using pelvic MRI ossification patterns
model_description: Machine learning regression models for continuous age estimation and classification models for legal age-threshold determination (12/14/16/18 years), based on staged ossification patterns of the iliac crest and ischial tuberosity on pelvic MRI.
title: Pelvic MRI-based machine learning models for age estimation and age threshold classification in living children and young adults.
study_design: retrospective study with internal and external validation
headline_result: Age regression MAE 2.957y (internal), 2.252y (external); threshold classification AUCs up to 0.977-0.997

model_family: deep learning multi-task dual-branch segmentation network
