model_family: segmentation pipeline combining an ROI detection network, a foundation model for instance generation, and an instance classifier network, trained with semi-automated annotation and curriculum learning
patient_population: 552 hand X-ray images of children from the public RSNA and Digital Hand Atlas (DHA) datasets, diverse ages and racial backgrounds
clinical_problem: bone segmentation on pediatric hand radiographs to support bone analysis across a wide age range
model_description: PedVision is a segmentation pipeline for pediatric hand X-rays designed to scale across ages without manual annotation. It uses a region-of-interest network to localize relevant areas, a foundation model to generate instance-level predictions, and an instance classifier network to map instances to 19 hand bones grouped into 5 classes, trained via a semi-automated annotation framework and curriculum learning across rounds of increasing model complexity. It was evaluated on 552 hand X-rays from the public RSNA and Digital Hand Atlas datasets against U-Net, DeepLabV3+, and SegFormer baselines.
release_evidence: "The project is open source at github.com/mohofar/PedVision"
title: PedVision: A manual-annotation-free and age scalable segmentation pipeline for bone analysis in hand X-ray images
study_design: retrospective technical development / segmentation benchmark study
dataset_size: 552 hand X-ray images of children (RSNA and Digital Hand Atlas datasets)
headline_result: for pediatric cases (0-7 years): 11.08% Dice improvement over U-Net on RSNA and 7.68% on DHA; 14.43%/14.78% improvement over DeepLabV3+; 8.16%/1.91% improvement over the best SegFormer variant

model_family: review of deep learning segmentation and registration architectures (CNNs, attention mechanisms) for infant brain MRI
patient_population: infants undergoing brain MRI
clinical_problem: segmentation and registration of infant brain MRI to support studying neonatal brain development and diagnosing early brain disease
model_description: This review surveys more than 100 papers on deep learning-based segmentation and registration of infant brain MRI, covering neural network architectures, attention mechanisms, and data processing techniques, and discusses the performance metrics used to evaluate these methods relative to techniques developed for adult brain MRI.
title: A review of deep learning-based segmentation and registration of infant brain MRI

model_family: convolutional neural network with heat-map regression key-point detection and spatial/channel attention
body_region: hand and wrist (radius, ulna, carpal bones)
patient_population: children and infants undergoing hand radiography for skeletal maturity assessment
clinical_problem: Tanner-Whitehouse 3 (TW3) bone age assessment including carpal-bone scoring, for diagnosis of skeletal growth abnormalities
model_description: A two-stage deep learning pipeline first uses a heat-map regression key-point detection network with spatial configuration to locate and segment all 20 TW3 regions of interest on a hand radiograph, then a skeletal-maturity classification network with spatial and channel attention predicts maturity scores and bone age for both the radius-ulna-short-bone (TW3-RUS) and carpal bone (TW3-C) series, extending prior automated methods that could only assess TW3-RUS.
title: A convolutional neural networks with spatial configuration and attention mechanism for Tanner-Whitehouse 3 bone age assessment
study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study
dataset_size: 5,235 left hand radiographs of children of different ages
headline_result: mean absolute error of bone age 0.42 years (TW3-RUS) and 0.44 years (TW3-C)

model_family: 3D multi-view dual encoder-decoder CNN with attention mechanism
patient_population: patients with intractable epilepsy due to focal cortical dysplasia, adults and children
clinical_problem: segmentation of focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) lesions for pre-surgical epilepsy evaluation
model_description: A 3D deep learning model with a multi-view dual encoder-decoder architecture and residual connections segments focal cortical dysplasia lesions on brain MRI. It processes FLAIR MRI volumes together with corresponding cortical thickness maps through two encoders linked by a 3D attention mechanism, and two decoders for dual-task learning using ground-truth-derived distance maps, intended to assist neuroradiologists in presurgical evaluation of epilepsy patients including both children and adults.
title: A dual encoder–decoder multi-task 3D deep learning framework for the segmentation of focal cortical dysplasia lesions
study_design: retrospective technical development / segmentation benchmark study
headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient 4.8% and 2.3% higher than state-of-the-art 2D and 3D FCD segmentation methods, respectively

model_family: self-distillation hybrid-attention network (ResNet50 backbone with Squeeze-and-Excitation and Spatial Transformer attention modules)
patient_population: children undergoing 3-Tesla head MRI
clinical_problem: automatic age estimation from head MRI in children, as a radiation-free alternative to radiographic age estimation
model_description: SDHA is a self-distillation network with Squeeze-and-Excitation and Spatial Transformer attention modules built on a ResNet50 backbone (teacher) with early-exit student branches, trained on 3T head MRI to estimate a child's age without ionizing radiation. Grad-CAM visualization showed the model attends to age-relevant dental, facial, and brain structures. It was compared against manual assessment and conventional CNN methods.
title: Enhanced pediatric age estimation from head MRI via self-distillation hybrid-attention network
study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study
headline_result: SDHA mean absolute error 0.34 years vs manual method 0.44 years; 63.4% MAE reduction vs a non-distilled SENet (MAE 0.93 years); prediction time reduced from 120 s (manual) to 0.11 s per subject

model_family: deep learning pipeline: GAN-based data augmentation, hybrid U-Net segmentation (UDANet) with dilated convolution and decoder attention, IpLU activation
patient_population: adolescents/children with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis undergoing spine X-ray, including presurgical severe cases
clinical_problem: automated Cobb angle measurement for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) severity grading
model_description: SCANet is an end-to-end pipeline for Cobb angle measurement from spine X-rays in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis. It augments training images with geometric transformations and a generative adversarial network, segments the vertebral region with a hybrid U-Net (UDANet) that incorporates dilated convolutions and a decoder attention module, derives a vertebral compression ratio from the segmentation, and computes the Cobb angle from these segmentation coordinates.
title: SCANet: automated Cobb angle measurement using deep learning model in X-ray images for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients
study_design: retrospective technical development / measurement accuracy study
headline_result: 98.65% accuracy in Cobb angle measurement, 2.06% and 4.16% higher than DNN and CNN comparators respectively

model_family: ghost convolution-based YOLOv11 lightweight object detector
patient_population: children undergoing wrist radiography (GRAZPEDWRI-DX public dataset)
clinical_problem: fracture detection on pediatric wrist radiographs
model_description: G-YOLOv11 is a lightweight computer-aided detection system for fractures on pediatric wrist X-rays, built on the YOLOv11 object detector with ghost convolution layers that generate the same feature maps as standard convolution with fewer computations. It was evaluated on the public GRAZPEDWRI-DX pediatric wrist radiograph dataset against the standard YOLOv11l model.
release_evidence: Code and models are available at https://github.com/AbdesselamFerdi/G-YOLOv11
title: Lightweight G-YOLOv11: Advancing efficient fracture detection in pediatric wrist X-rays
study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study
dataset_size: GRAZPEDWRI-DX public pediatric wrist radiograph dataset

model_family: instance segmentation network with a lightweight Vision Transformer (EfficientViT), dilated convolutions, and E-Focal Loss
patient_population: fetuses undergoing standard fetal heart ultrasound views (newly constructed FH-3K dataset)

It combines a lightweight Vision Transformer module (EfficientViT) for long-range feature modeling, dilated convolutions for a wider receptive field, and an E-Focal Loss to address class imbalance, segmenting ten key anatomical structures across five standard fetal heart views. It was developed and benchmarked on the newly constructed FH-3K fetal heart ultrasound dataset.
title: FHSS-Net: A novel instance segmentation network for multi-class fetal heart structures via global context and multi-scale learning
study_design: retrospective technical development / segmentation benchmark study
dataset_size: FH-3K dataset: five standard fetal heart views, ten annotated anatomical structures
headline_result: 93.7% localization accuracy and 92% segmentation accuracy across ten anatomical structures under five-fold cross-validation, outperforming mainstream models

patient_population: 3425 expert-annotated first-trimester fetal CNS ultrasound images (2440 training, 612 test, 373 independent clinical validation)
clinical_problem: first-trimester fetal CNS standard plane and anatomical structure recognition for prenatal screening

It is intended to support earlier, more consistent detection of fetal brain abnormalities on first-trimester ultrasound.
title: FCNSU-NET: Comprehensive recognition of the first trimester fetal CNS ultrasound standard planes and anatomical structures with linear transformer attention
study_design: retrospective technical development with clinical validation
headline_result: mAP@0.5 95.3%, standard-plane classification accuracy 98.53%; on clinical validation set outperformed junior/intermediate physicians and matched senior experts (Kappa 0.90)

model_family: GLCM texture features with LDA, SVM, and shallow neural network classifiers

clinical_problem: fetal brain anomaly classification (arachnoid cyst, Arnold-Chiari malformation, cerebellar hypoplasia, colpocephaly)

title: Fetal brain anomaly identification from ultrasound images using multiclass classifiers
headline_result: LDA best classifier: 100% accuracy for normal, arachnoid cyst, and cerebellar hypoplasia; 89% for Arnold-Chiari malformation; 93% for colpocephaly

model_family: 2.5D deep learning model (ResNet-18 with transfer learning on multiplanar CT reconstructions)
patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing CT for craniofacial trauma
clinical_problem: detection of craniofacial fractures
model_description: Axial, coronal and sagittal CT reconstructions are stacked as a three-channel input to a ResNet-18 convolutional network with transfer learning to flag pediatric craniofacial fractures. The pipeline includes isotropic resampling, bone-window normalization and 384x384 image generation; Grad-CAM highlights the regions driving each prediction, which an independent clinical review confirmed corresponded to fracture-related structures.
title: Automatic Detection of Pediatric Craniofacial Fractures in Computed Tomography Using a 2.5D Deep Learning Model and Grad-CAM
study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study
headline_result: AUC 0.822, AUPRC 0.855; at optimal threshold (t=0.54): sensitivity 0.556, specificity 1.000, F1-score 0.714

clinical_problem: right ventricular functional assessment (fractional area change) in pediatric echocardiography

The best-performing model (FCBFormer architecture) was compared against ground-truth and four expert readers in a blinded evaluation to assess whether it reduces inter-observer variability in RV assessment.
title: Automated right ventricular assessment in pediatric echocardiography via deep learning improves measurement reliability and reduces variability
study_design: retrospective diagnostic accuracy study with reader comparison
headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient 0.926, mean absolute error 5.913% for RVFAC prediction; model-generated segmentation favored over human segmentation in 57.3% of evaluated cases

model_family: review of hybrid LSTM, CNN, transformer and explainable-AI (XAI) models
patient_population: pregnant women in antenatal care, across studies published 2000-2024
clinical_problem: prediction of fetal weight, delivery mode, and fetal gender using antenatal ultrasound and clinical data
model_description: This systematic review evaluates machine learning and deep learning models that combine maternal, fetal, and ultrasound data to predict fetal weight, mode of delivery, and fetal gender. It compares hybrid LSTM, CNN, transformer, and explainable-AI approaches against traditional statistical methods across studies published between 2000 and 2024.
title: Predictive antenatal models: A systematic review of advanced approaches for forecasting fetal weight, delivery mode, and fetal gender

model_family: Lightweight attention-augmented CNN (ResNet-18 backbone with CBAM and Efficient Channel Attention modules)
patient_population: 5,863 pediatric chest X-ray images from the public Kaggle pneumonia dataset
clinical_problem: pneumonia detection on pediatric chest X-ray, for use in low-resource settings with limited radiologist access

Grad-CAM was used to check whether the model attended to radiologist-annotated abnormal regions.
title: AXNet: Attention-enhanced X-ray network for pneumonia detection
study_design: retrospective technical development and evaluation study
headline_result: Test accuracy 93.6%, F1-score 93.1%, AUC 0.964, using only 13.1M parameters and 4.7ms/image inference time; Grad-CAM showed 86.7% alignment with radiologist-annotated abnormalities

model_family: AI decision-support model (architecture not specified) for pneumoperitoneum detection
patient_population: 14 readers (pediatric radiologists, neonatologists, radiology residents) interpreting 125 neonatal radiographs
clinical_problem: detection of pneumoperitoneum (free air) on neonatal radiographs, a time-critical surgical emergency
model_description: This multi-reader multi-center study evaluated how AI assistance for detecting pneumoperitoneum on neonatal radiographs affects clinician verification behavior. Fourteen readers of varying specialty and seniority (pediatric radiologists, neonatologists, radiology residents) interpreted 125 neonatal radiographs across two sessions, under three conditions: unaided, aided by a reliable AI, and aided by an error-injected (unreliable) AI, with outcomes including diagnostic accuracy, deliberation time, and automation bias.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Expertise-Dependent Verification Behaviors in Response to AI Reliability in Neonatal Pneumoperitoneum: A Multi-Reader Multi-Center Study
headline_result: neonatologists overrode 91.6% of AI errors under error-injected AI (OR 4.16 vs unaided baseline, p=0.020); radiology residents accepted incorrect advice from reliable AI in 52.0% of discordant cases vs 20.0% for pediatric radiologists (p=0.016)

model_family: self-supervised transfer learning binary classification models

Manually annotated tumor segmentations were used as input, and per-class probabilities from the three models were combined via a softmax function to compute a multi-class AUC.

title: External validation of self-supervised transfer learning for noninvasive molecular subtyping of pediatric low-grade glioma using T2-weighted MRI
study_design: retrospective external validation diagnostic accuracy study
headline_result: macro-average AUC 0.7671 on the newer dataset, 0.6463 on the older dataset

model_family: Multimodal deep learning fusion (VGG16/ResNet50 transfer learning for imaging and pathology, SVM/Hough transform for circulating tumor cell classification)
patient_population: pediatric patients with distal femur osteosarcoma, using public imaging and genomic datasets (TCIA, TCGA, GEO)
clinical_problem: early diagnosis of pediatric distal femur osteosarcoma
model_description: MRI, CT, histopathology slides and circulating tumor cell (CTC) data are each processed by modality-specific pipelines (CNN transfer learning for imaging and pathology, flow cytometry and machine learning for CTCs) and fused into a single multimodal deep learning model for early diagnosis of pediatric distal femur osteosarcoma, particularly to aid metastasis assessment when imaging alone is inconclusive.
title: Deep learning-based multimodal fusion of imaging, pathology, and CTCs for early diagnosis of pediatric distal femur osteosarcoma
study_design: retrospective technical development and evaluation study
headline_result: Accuracy 92.5%, sensitivity 88.7%, specificity 94.3%, AUC 0.96 on an independent test set; adding CTC data notably improved performance for metastasis assessment when imaging was inconclusive

model_family: Radiomics with LASSO feature selection, combined with MRI findings (Rad-score based classification model)
patient_population: children with posterior fossa brain tumors: 113 medulloblastoma and 31 ependymoma patients
clinical_problem: differentiating medulloblastoma from ependymoma in children
model_description: Radiomic features were extracted from ADC, T2-weighted and DCE-T1-weighted MRI sequences of children with posterior fossa tumors. LASSO regression selected features to build a radiomics score, which was combined with radiologist MRI findings into a nomogram to distinguish medulloblastoma from ependymoma. Diagnostic performance was compared against radiologists using the DeLong test.
title: Multi-parametric MRI-based radiomics to differentiate medulloblastoma from ependymoma in children
headline_result: Combined sequence radiomics model AUC 0.981 (primary cohort) and 0.939 (validation cohort), outperforming radiologists and single-sequence models

model_family: Hybrid deep learning model combining a ResNet-50-based DeepLabV3 network with a UNet3+ architecture (transfer learning)
patient_population: fetal head ultrasound images (public HC18 dataset)
clinical_problem: automated fetal head circumference measurement for monitoring fetal development
model_description: A hybrid DeepLabV3-UNet3+ deep learning model, assisted by transfer learning, segments the fetal head from an ultrasound image; an ellipse is then fitted to the segmentation to compute head circumference automatically, aiming to replace expert-dependent, inconsistent manual measurement.
title: A transfer learning − based DeepLabV3–UNet3+ hybrid model for automated fetal head circumference measurement

model_family: pre-trained deep learning super-resolution model (GAMBAS) for ultra-low-field MRI
patient_population: 64 children aged 3-5 years (from a birth cohort of 180 children: 90 small-for-gestational-age, 90 appropriate-for-gestational-age), scanned with a portable 64mT ultra-low-field MRI system
clinical_problem: brain volume assessment and neurodevelopmental correlation using portable ultra-low-field MRI in small-for-gestational-age vs appropriate-for-gestational-age children

title: Artificial Intelligence methods for ultra-low- field MRI enhancement comparing brain volumes and neurodevelopment scores for small vs appropriate for gestational age children
dataset_size: 64 children aged 3-5 years from a cohort of 180 (90 SGA, 90 AGA); ground-truth comparison subset n=10
headline_result: strong correlation and high concordance between super-resolved and high-field brain volumes for total intracranial volume, white matter, cerebral cortex, basal ganglia and thalamus; correlation between super-resolved volumes and neurodevelopmental (MDAT) z-scores was not statistically significant

patient_population: pediatric pelvic X-ray dataset spanning patients aged 6 months to 16 years
clinical_problem: automated diagnosis of developmental dysplasia of the hip

An attention module highlights key anatomical structures, patient age and gender are embedded into the image features, and extracted anatomical indices are fed into a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network to classify developmental dysplasia of the hip severity.
title: A self-supervised representation-transfer multimodal learning for automated diagnosis of Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip

model_family: graph theory network analysis combined with machine learning on functional brain network features
patient_population: mid-adolescents from low-socioeconomic-status contexts, longitudinal 2-year fMRI cohort (n=65)
clinical_problem: identifying social and psychological predictors of longitudinal functional brain network development in mid-adolescence
model_description: Graph theory measures were computed from a 2-year longitudinal resting-state fMRI dataset of 65 mid-adolescents. Machine learning analysis was used to identify which factors, among parental education, community violence exposure, IQ, and a measured psychological disposition ('transcendent thinking'), best predicted changes in functional brain network organization (segregation, integration, entropy, energy) over the study period.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Intersecting effects of social circumstances and transcendent thinking on mid-adolescents’ longitudinal functional connectome development
headline_result: machine learning identified transcendent thinking and community violence exposure, but not IQ, as the principal predictors of functional brain network change across groups

patient_population: Northwest European and Middle Eastern individuals aged 13-25 years, including asylum seekers, assessed at German clinical sites and reception facilities
clinical_problem: forensic age assessment via distal radial epiphyseal fusion timing (medico-legal age-of-majority determination)

Gradient-boosting machine learning models (LightGBM) were trained on 830 high-quality ultrasound datasets to classify fusion status against reference ages (documented birthdate or Greulich-Pyle bone age), evaluated with leave-one-out cross-validation across sex- and population-specific age thresholds, for forensic determination of whether an individual has reached a legally relevant age threshold.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Distal Radial Epiphyseal Fusion Timing in Northwest Europeans and Middle Eastern Asylum Seekers: An Automated Ultrasound and Machine Learning Approach
dataset_size: 1,061 recordings; 830 high-quality ultrasound datasets analyzed, ages 13-25 years
headline_result: AUC approximately 0.81-1.00 near optimal thresholds; optimal discrimination thresholds ranged 17.0-18.5 years across sex/population groups

model_family: instance segmentation framework with structure-aware overlap metric, Laplacian regularization, and Stable Diffusion/LoRA augmentation
patient_population: fetal brain ultrasound images across five standard planes
clinical_problem: fetal brain anatomical structure segmentation

title: Network-Level Associations in Nonlinear Brain Dynamics Predict Transcendent Thinking in a Diverse Adolescent Sample
study_design: cross-sectional resting-state fMRI study with machine learning prediction of a psychological trait
headline_result: MSE-based network features (particularly spectral energy and Shannon entropy) reliably predicted transcendent thinking, while conventional time-series-based network measures did not; no features predicted IQ.

patient_population: Adolescents with longitudinal structural MRI data
clinical_problem: deriving brain-based markers of adolescent phenotypic (personal, social, neighborhood) variation from structural MRI
model_description: A convolutional neural network was trained on longitudinal structural MRI data to derive latent, low-dimensional brain representations capturing structural variability during adolescence. These learned representations were used to map associations between brain structure and personal, social, and neighborhood conditions.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Latent neural network representations of the brain reflect broad-scale adolescent phenotypic variation
study_design: longitudinal structural MRI study using a convolutional neural network for representation learning

model_family: machine learning model with PCA-derived whole-brain predictors
patient_population: School-aged children, 6.7-10.3 years, in subgroups of 73-97 completing different fMRI tasks
clinical_problem: prediction of children's literacy (reading, verbal, naming) skills from task-based fMRI activation
model_description: Whole-brain activation contrast maps from four task-based fMRI paradigms (a phonological-lexical decision task, audiovisual character learning, and two passive viewing tasks) were reduced with principal component analysis and used in a machine learning model to predict continuous reading, verbal, and naming scores in school-aged children. Active tasks (phonological-lexical decision, character learning) outperformed passive viewing tasks for prediction.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Predicting children's literacy from task-based fMRI: Neural heterogeneity and task-dependent performance
study_design: cross-sectional task-based fMRI study with machine learning prediction of behavioral scores
dataset_size: Subgroups of 73-97 children per fMRI task
headline_result: Highest predictive performance for Reading and Naming scores was with the phonological-lexical decision task, outperforming character-learning and passive viewing tasks.

model_family: multimodal fusion of radiomics and deep learning (Vision Transformer, ResNet, Vision Mamba, Masked Autoencoder, Fixmatch)
patient_population: 81 fetuses with suspected coarctation of the aorta undergoing fetal echocardiography
clinical_problem: prenatal diagnosis of coarctation of the aorta
model_description: Fetal echocardiography images from fetuses with suspected coarctation of the aorta are analyzed with several deep learning architectures (Vision Transformer, ResNet, Vision Mamba, Masked Autoencoder, Fixmatch) and radiomics features, then combined in a multimodal fusion model to output a diagnostic prediction for coarctation of the aorta, compared against a baseline model using standard echocardiographic features alone.
title: Diagnostic value of a fetal echocardiography-based multimodal feature fusion model for fetal coarctation of the aorta
headline_result: Multimodal fusion model AUC 0.906 vs baseline model AUC 0.707 on test set

model_family: vision-language framework (Semantic Injection Module, Dynamic Token Selection, Collaborative Mixture of Experts)
patient_population: pediatric chest radiographs (population not further specified)
clinical_problem: pediatric pneumonia detection
model_description: A vision-language deep learning framework (DSP) takes pediatric chest radiographs and generated radiology-style text captions as input. Three modules fuse image and text semantics, adaptively select informative image tokens, and route fused features through multiple experts to output a pneumonia detection prediction with interpretable, radiology-aligned reasoning.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: DSP: Dynamic Token Selection and Semantic Injection for Pediatric Pneumonia Detection

model_family: radiomics (LASSO feature selection) combined with logistic regression
patient_population: 100 fetuses with congenital pulmonary malformation detected on prenatal ultrasound and confirmed after birth
clinical_problem: predicting postnatal outcome of congenital pulmonary malformation detected prenatally
model_description: Radiomics features were extracted from targeted prenatal grayscale ultrasound images of fetuses with congenital pulmonary malformation and reduced with LASSO regression to a radiomics score. This score was combined with an independent clinical predictor (congenital pulmonary airway malformation volume ratio) in a logistic regression model to predict postnatal outcome.
journal: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
title: Prenatal ultrasound radiomics features combined with clinical indicators for predicting outcomes of fetuses with congenital pulmonary malformation
headline_result: AUC 0.809 (combined model) vs 0.728 (clinical model) and 0.770 (radiomics model) in the test set

model_family: deep learning (unspecified architectures) for feature extraction from fetal brain MRI
patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal brain MRI
clinical_problem: assessing fetal brain development and detecting neurodevelopmental abnormalities
model_description: This review covers AI methods, primarily deep learning, applied to fetal cranial MRI: predicting gestational and brain age, detecting structural abnormalities such as sulcal and ventricular changes, and assisting motion correction and analysis of fetal functional MRI data, with the aim of building AI into clinical decision support for early diagnosis and intervention.
journal: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
title: Progresses in artificial intelligence assisted analysis of fetal brain MRI

patient_population: children in emergency and critical care settings undergoing point-of-care ultrasound
clinical_problem: image acquisition guidance and diagnostic interpretation support in pediatric point-of-care ultrasound
model_description: This review discusses AI-assisted models for point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) in pediatric emergency and critical care, noting that AI can improve image acquisition and augment training, which is particularly useful where ultrasound experts are scarce. It cautions that models trained mainly on adult populations require pediatric-specific validation before use, and that AI should supplement rather than replace ultrasound training and credentialing.
title: Artificial intelligence meets point-of-care ultrasound: implications for pediatric emergency and critical care

patient_population: 70 children under 4 years old undergoing non-contrast chest CT for suspected pulmonary disease (plus a phantom study)
clinical_problem: radiation dose reduction in pediatric chest CT
model_description: A deep learning image reconstruction algorithm (ClearInfinity) is applied to ultra-low-dose 60 kVp chest CT scans in young children, tested at multiple reconstruction weights (40/50/60%) against a conventional 80 kVp adaptive-iterative-reconstruction protocol. Objective noise/signal-to-noise ratio and subjective image quality were compared across dose levels and reconstruction settings in both a phantom and a prospective pediatric cohort.
release_evidence: ClearInfinity (CI), a named deep learning reconstruction product
title: Application value of 60 kVp ultra-low-dose chest CT with deep learning reconstruction in children
dataset_size: 70 children (35 conventional-dose, 35 low-dose) plus phantom study
headline_result: Low-dose group reduced SSDE/CTDIvol/DLP by ~79-80% versus conventional dose, with comparable or better image quality at 50% CI reconstruction weight

model_family: multimodal large language model (dual-stream encoding with weighted attention, fine-tuned MiniCPM-V 2.6)
patient_population: cross-sectional study across seven Chinese provinces; thyroid ultrasound performed in adults, pregnant women, and children
clinical_problem: thyroid ultrasound diagnostic report generation and TI-RADS classification
model_description: A large-language-model-based framework (fine-tuned MiniCPM-V 2.6 with a dual-stream, cross-modally aligned encoder) takes thyroid ultrasound images and generates structured diagnostic reports, including standardized terminology and TI-RADS classification. Performance was measured with text-generation metrics (ROUGE-L, BLEU-4, CIDEr) and expert blind comparison against manually written reports.
title: Thyroid ultrasound diagnostic report generation method based on large language model
study_design: cross-sectional model development and reader evaluation
dataset_size: not stated (multi-province dataset spanning adults, pregnant women, and children)
headline_result: TI-RADS classification accuracy 82.3%; blind-evaluation scores higher than manually written reports (9.55/9.85 vs 9.41/9.52)

model_family: deep learning / machine learning (CNNs and random survival forests most common) applied to kidney ultrasound
patient_population: pediatric patients with CAKUT, most commonly posterior urethral valves (24 studies synthesized)
clinical_problem: predicting progression to chronic kidney disease / end-stage renal disease in children with congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT)
model_description: This systematic review synthesizes 24 studies applying deep learning and machine learning models, most often convolutional neural networks and random survival forests, to kidney ultrasound features such as echogenicity, corticomedullary differentiation, parenchymal area and kidney-to-body-length ratio, to predict progression to chronic kidney disease and end-stage renal disease in children with CAKUT. Most studies lacked external validation and calibration reporting.
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
title: Deep Learning Approaches for Predicting End-Stage Renal Disease in Pediatric Patients with Congenital Anomalies of the Kidney and Urinary Tract (CAKUT): A Systematic Review
headline_result: ensemble models reported AUC 0.85-0.92 for predicting CKD/ESRD progression from kidney ultrasound

patient_population: 1588 annotated fetal abdominal ultrasound images from 169 term pregnancies in a low-resource setting (Uganda)
clinical_problem: screening for severe fetal growth restriction
model_description: A DenseNet-121-based deep learning model classifies 2D fetal abdominal ultrasound images by growth-restriction severity, using abdominal circumference mapped to INTERGROWTH-21st percentiles as a gestational-age-independent proxy label. It is designed as a first-line triage tool for severe fetal growth restriction in low-resource settings lacking reliable dating or Doppler access.
release_evidence: presented as a research framework requiring prospective multi-site validation; no repository or commercial product named
title: Optimizing Screening for Intrauterine Fetal Growth Restriction in Low-Resource Settings Using 2D Ultrasound: A Deep Learning Approach
dataset_size: 1588 fetal abdominal images from 169 term pregnancies
headline_result: 93.7% accuracy, weighted F1-score 0.76, ROC AUC >=0.98 per class on held-out data (3-fold patient-wise cross-validation)

model_family: DenseNet/U-Net hybrid with feature smoothness regularization
patient_population: 167 T2-weighted MRI scans from infants with hydrocephalus
clinical_problem: hydrocephalus brain and CSF volume assessment
model_description: T2-weighted MRI scans from infants with hydrocephalus are automatically segmented into CSF, brain parenchyma, and background by a DenseNet/U-Net hybrid deep learning model with feature-smoothness regularization. The model outputs volumetric measurements of brain and CSF volume for clinical monitoring of hydrocephalus, trained and evaluated on a retrospective single-center cohort split into training/validation/hold-out sets.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Automated Brain and CSF Volume Assessment in Infant Hydrocephalus Using Deep Learning
headline_result: Dice 95.7% (CSF) and 96.4% (brain parenchyma) on hold-out test set, outperforming FSL FAST (85.0%, 77.9%); processing time 0.8 s/scan

patient_population: 932 Gambian children under 15 years undergoing chest radiography for suspected pulmonary tuberculosis
clinical_problem: pulmonary tuberculosis detection
model_description: Digital chest radiographs from children with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis are analyzed by qXR (version 4.2.1, Qure.ai), a paediatric-optimized computer-aided detection algorithm that outputs a probability of TB-consistent abnormality. Performance was assessed against microbiological and clinical reference standards, with Bayesian latent class analysis used to account for imperfect reference standards in children.
release_evidence: qXR-version 4.2.1 (Qure.ai), a paediatric-optimized computer-aided detection (CAD) algorithm
title: Validation of a Paediatric-Optimized Computer-Aided Detection System for Tuberculosis Using Bayesian Latent Class Analysis
headline_result: Against microbiological reference standard: AUROC 0.68, sensitivity 54%, specificity 82%; Bayesian LCA sensitivity 79-89%, specificity 82%

clinical_problem: overview of AI applications across pediatric radiology, for pediatric clinicians
model_description: Narrative review/primer aimed at pediatric clinicians surveying deep learning applications in pediatric imaging: chest radiograph models for pneumonia, tuberculosis and malpositioned tube detection; automated bone age assessment; neuroimaging tools for faster acquisition, lower contrast dose and critical-finding triage; cardiovascular AI for congenital heart disease detection and function assessment; and oncologic tumor characterization and segmentation. Discusses barriers including scarce pediatric datasets and limited prospective validation.
title: Artificial Intelligence in Pediatric Imaging: A Primer for Pediatric Clinicians

model_family: various (convolutional neural networks, hybrid frameworks, 3D video-based, segmentation-driven models)
patient_population: systematic review of 10 studies, 15,868 participants across paediatric, adult, and mixed clinical populations undergoing lung ultrasound
clinical_problem: pneumonia detection
model_description: Systematic review of AI-assisted lung ultrasound interpretation for pneumonia diagnosis. Included studies applied machine learning or deep learning (CNNs, hybrid frameworks, 3D video-based models, segmentation-driven systems) to lung ultrasound images to classify pneumonia versus normal lung, across paediatric and adult populations, and pooled diagnostic performance across ten eligible studies.
title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence for Pneumonia Detection Using Lung Ultrasound Images: A Systematic Review
headline_result: Sensitivity 88-93%, specificity 80-100%, accuracy 86-94.5% across included studies

model_family: 3D-SFCN-UNet deep learning framework for brain age prediction
patient_population: 275 participants from two centers (139 children/adolescents with beta-thalassaemia major, 136 healthy controls), enrolled May 2020-October 2023
clinical_problem: neurodevelopmental alteration and cognitive impairment assessment via brain age gap in beta-thalassaemia major
model_description: A 3D-SFCN-UNet deep learning model was applied to 3D T1-weighted brain MRI to predict brain age and derive a harmonized, corrected brain age gap (BAG) and voxel-level local BAG maps across two centers. Mediation analyses linked haematological indices and regional brain features to cognitive test scores, to evaluate BAG as an imaging biomarker of neurodevelopmental risk in beta-thalassaemia major.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Brain Age Gap as a Neuroimaging Biomarker for Neurodevelopmental Alterations and Cognitive Impairment in Beta-Thalassaemia Major: A Deep Learning-Based Multicentre Study
dataset_size: 275 participants (139 with beta-thalassaemia major, 136 healthy controls)
headline_result: Model achieved brain age prediction MAE 0.74 years (r=0.93) in healthy controls; patients with beta-thalassaemia major had lower corrected brain age gap than controls (-0.645±1.461 vs 0.000±0.954 years; p<0.001), consistent after age-stratification and propensity matching

model_family: Multimodal deep learning framework integrating chest X-ray images, ECG signals, and structured clinical/lab features, with echocardiographic ejection fraction as a physiological supervision anchor
patient_population: two-center inpatient cohort: 5,147 cases (700 myocarditis, 4,447 non-myocarditis) for internal training/validation, plus 529 cases (197 myocarditis, 332 non-myocarditis) from a separate hospital for external validation
clinical_problem: diagnosis and severity grading of pediatric myocarditis
model_description: EF-ConsNET fuses chest X-ray images, ECG signals, and structured laboratory/demographic data to detect pediatric myocarditis and grade its severity (mild vs severe), using echocardiographic ejection fraction during training as a physiological anchor to keep the multimodal representation clinically consistent and to make the model's image attention focus on cardiopulmonary regions. It was designed to remain robust when some input modalities are missing.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: EF-ConsNET: Physiologically Anchored Multimodal Deep Learning for Diagnosis and Severity Grading of Pediatric Myocarditis
study_design: retrospective two-center diagnostic study with external validation
dataset_size: 5,147 cases internal (700 myocarditis); 529 cases external (197 myocarditis)
headline_result: Internal AUROC 0.926 (myocarditis detection) and 0.911 (severity grading); external validation AUROC 0.812 (detection) and 0.765 (severity grading); performance remained above 0.899 AUROC with up to 20% simulated single-modality missingness

model_family: Multivariable logistic regression combining an automated AI-derived chest radiograph consolidation score with clinical and laboratory markers
patient_population: hospitalized children with PCR-confirmed Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia: 503 in the development cohort, 138 in an independent external validation cohort
clinical_problem: predicting macrolide resistance in pediatric Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia at hospital admission
model_description: An AI algorithm automatically quantifies a consolidation score from admission chest radiographs in children with confirmed Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia. This score is combined with routine clinical markers, laboratory findings and PCR cycle threshold values in a logistic regression nomogram to predict macrolide-resistant disease at admission, to guide earlier escalation to second-line therapy.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: AI-Augmented Multimodal Model for Predicting Macrolide Resistance in Pediatric Mycoplasma Pneumonia: An External Validation Study
study_design: multi-institutional retrospective diagnostic study with external validation
headline_result: Adding the AI consolidation score to the clinical model improved internal AUC from 0.819 (95% CI 0.762-0.876) to 0.860 (95% CI 0.812-0.909; P=0.004); external validation AUC 0.726 (95% CI 0.588-0.863)

model_family: YOLOv12-based real-time object detection network, adapted for fetal spinal ultrasound
patient_population: 968 images from 735 fetuses (development) and 221 images from 185 fetuses (external test) at two hospitals
clinical_problem: detecting vertebral abnormalities (hemivertebrae, butterfly vertebrae, block vertebrae) on prenatal spinal ultrasound
model_description: FSU-YOLOv12 is a deep learning object detector adapted from YOLOv12 to detect vertebral abnormalities on fetal spinal ultrasound images, with targeted optimizations to handle small vertebrae, acoustic shadowing, artifacts, and low tissue contrast. It was trained and validated on images from one hospital and independently tested on an external hospital's data, running in real time (149 frames per second) with a lightweight architecture (2.6M parameters).
title: FSU-YOLOv12 for vertebral abnormalities detection in fetal spinal ultrasound
study_design: retrospective multicenter model development with external test set
dataset_size: 968 images from 735 fetuses (development); 221 images from 185 fetuses (external test)
headline_result: mAP(50) 91.9%, mAP(75) 55.9%, mAP 52.3%, precision 94.2%, recall 86.3%, F1 90.1%, 149 fps inference with 2.6M parameters

model_family: YOLOv8 object detector with CMUNeXt encoder module, plus fusion data augmentation
patient_population: 21 children with pancreatoblastoma and 70 children with solid pseudopapillary neoplasm
clinical_problem: detection and classification of pediatric pancreatic tumors (pancreatoblastoma vs solid pseudopapillary neoplasm)
model_description: Abdominal CT images from children with pancreatoblastoma or solid pseudopapillary neoplasm are manually annotated for tumor regions, then an 8-fold data-augmented training set is used to train a modified YOLOv8 object detector (with a CMUNeXt encoder module) to detect tumors and classify them into the two tumor types.
journal: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
title: Deep learning model integrated with data augmentation strategy based on CT for detecting and classifying pediatric pancreatic tumors
headline_result: Best model (post-augmentation YOLOv8-CMUNeXt): precision 92.53%, recall 78.64%, mAP@0.5 86.29%, mAP0.5:0.95 68.45%, accuracy 85.71%/72.86% for the two tumor types

model_family: AI lung-nodule detection algorithm, previously trained on an adult dataset
patient_population: adolescents with osteosarcoma undergoing chest CT (248 CT scans evaluated)
clinical_problem: detecting pulmonary metastases (lung nodules) in adolescents with osteosarcoma
model_description: An existing AI algorithm for lung nodule detection, originally trained on an adult dataset, was applied retrospectively to chest CT scans of adolescents with osteosarcoma to detect pulmonary nodules ≥4 mm (a target finding for metastasis staging), and its accuracy was compared against the reference diagnosis, quantifying false positives and false negatives.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Assessment of the accuracy of lung lesions diagnosis in adolescents with osteosarcoma using artificial intelligence
dataset_size: 248 CT scans of adolescents with osteosarcoma
headline_result: Diagnostic accuracy 0.843 (95% CI 0.794-0.887); false positive rate 2%, false negative rate 13.7%; using the AI algorithm would increase sensitivity from 0.805 to 0.891, an absolute false-negative reduction of 8.6% (relative 44%)

model_family: Fully automated 3D deep learning segmentation framework
patient_population: neonates (term and preterm) imaged with structural T2-weighted MRI at 7T and 3T
clinical_problem: quantitative assessment of neonatal brain white-matter (internal capsule) maturation
model_description: A fully automated 3D deep learning model segments internal capsule subregions and myelin-related signal on structural T2-weighted neonatal MRI, trained on both high-resolution 7T and conventional 3T datasets. Derived volumetric and intensity metrics were modeled against postmenstrual and postnatal age, with normative modeling used to flag individual deviations, particularly in preterm infants.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Automated assessment of neonatal internal capsule maturation on T2-weighted MRI across 7T and 3T
study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study
headline_result: Segmentation accuracy Dice > 0.95 and relative volume difference < 5% across both field strengths; significant postmenstrual-age-related volumetric and intensity changes; normative modeling revealed significant deviations in preterm infants, especially for myelin-related intensity measures

model_family: nnU-Net deep learning segmentation with IBSI-compliant radiomics and L1-penalized logistic regression
patient_population: 9,808 pediatric lumbosacral MRI examinations at a single center; 475 preoperative children surgically treated for tethered cord
clinical_problem: reference distribution of conus medullaris position and radiomic diagnosis of tethered cord syndrome
model_description: Conus medullaris termination levels were extracted from a large archive of pediatric lumbosacral MRI reports to build a normative reference distribution. An nnU-Net deep learning model was separately trained to automatically segment the conus medullaris on axial T2-weighted images, from which IBSI-compliant radiomic features were extracted and tested (with cross-validated logistic regression) for their ability to distinguish children surgically treated for tethered cord from controls.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Conus Medullaris Position in 9,808 Pediatric Lumbosacral MRI Examinations: A Large-Cohort Reference Distribution and the Normally Positioned Conus in Surgically Treated Tethered Cord
study_design: retrospective single-center large-cohort reference-distribution and nested case-control study
headline_result: Conus terminated at L1 in 85.7% and L2 in 14.3% of the reference cohort (n=9,655); low-lying conus (≥L3) in only 0.05%; among 475 children surgically treated for tethered cord, 99.6% had a normally positioned conus; automated segmentation achieved held-out Dice of 0.85; neither conus position nor radiomics distinguished tethered cord from controls

model_family: DenseNet-201 backbone with convolutional block attention module (CBAM) and knowledge distillation, staged/progressive training
patient_population: first-trimester fetuses (12-14 weeks gestation) undergoing fetal echocardiography
clinical_problem: classifying first-trimester fetal echocardiography standard views/planes to support early detection of congenital heart defects
model_description: A three-phase progressive learning framework built on a DenseNet-201 backbone enhanced with a convolutional block attention module and knowledge distillation classifies first-trimester fetal echocardiography standard views/planes, addressing the challenge of underdeveloped cardiac structures and probe-movement variability at this gestational stage. Training proceeds in stages, from clear to deformed to the full image set, to progressively improve generalization on a minority, harder-to-classify view class, with the aim of supporting earlier detection of fetal heart defects.
title: Three-phase learning framework for first-trimester fetal echocardiography plan classification via knowledge distillation and CBAM-enhanced DenseNet
study_design: retrospective technical development and benchmark evaluation
headline_result: 3% and 1% overall accuracy/metric improvement over state-of-the-art baselines; approximately 5% recall and 3% F1 improvement for the minority X-sign view class

model_family: deep neural networks vs. simple demographic models (comparative benchmarking)
patient_population: Youth from a large developmental clinical cohort, evaluated for diverse psychiatric and non-psychiatric phenotypes using EEG and fMRI
clinical_problem: benchmarking AI prediction of psychiatric phenotypes from neuroimaging versus demographic confounds in youth
model_description: Machine learning models, including deep neural networks, were trained on EEG and fMRI data from a large youth developmental cohort to predict psychiatric and non-psychiatric phenotypes. Their performance was compared against simple models using only demographics and recording site; imaging-based models did not outperform the demographic-only models for clinical phenotypes.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: AI-based Psychiatric Prediction in Youth: Neuroimaging Provides Minimal Gains Beyond Confounds
study_design: retrospective benchmarking study of machine learning models on a developmental neuroimaging cohort
headline_result: Simple models using only demographics and recording site matched deep neural network performance using EEG/fMRI data for clinical phenotype prediction.

model_family: ResNet-18 CNN with geometric shape normalization (landmark detection, Procrustes analysis, piecewise affine warping) and Grad-CAM interpretability
patient_population: COVID-19 Radiography Database and a balanced adult-pediatric mixed dataset including pediatric cases from the Kermany dataset
clinical_problem: pneumonia and COVID-19 classification on chest X-ray
model_description: A ResNet-18 landmark detector locates 15 points defining the lung contour on a chest X-ray, which are used to geometrically normalize (warp) the lung region to a standard shape and remove positioning/scale variation. A second ResNet-18 classifier then labels the normalized image as COVID-19, viral pneumonia, or normal. Grad-CAM and a cropping experiment were used to check whether classification relied on true lung pathology versus acquisition artifacts.
title: Accurate Recognition of Pneumonia and COVID-19 by Geometric Shape Normalization of Lung Region Using Automatic Landmark Detection and Piecewise Affine Warping
study_design: retrospective technical development and evaluation study
headline_result: 98.60±0.26% accuracy and 98.00% F1-Macro on the COVID-19 Radiography Database (5-fold cross-validation); geometrically normalized images outperformed non-aligned artifact-masked images, 94.67% vs 94.17%, on the balanced adult-pediatric mixed dataset

model_family: Deep-learning repeated-measures segmentation approach for harmonized multisite MRI
body_region: brain (subcortical structures: amygdala, caudate, hippocampus, pallidum, putamen, thalamus)
patient_population: 44 infants with Down syndrome and 39 control infants without Down syndrome, imaged at 6 and 12 months in a multisite cohort
clinical_problem: characterizing subcortical brain development in infants with Down syndrome
model_description: High-resolution T1- and T2-weighted MRI acquired during natural sleep in infants was harmonized across sites and passed through a deep-learning, repeated-measures segmentation approach to derive total intracranial volume and bilateral subcortical structure volumes. Hierarchical linear modeling was then used to compare longitudinal brain growth between infants with and without Down syndrome.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Variation in infant subcortical brain development from 6 to 12 months in Down syndrome
dataset_size: 44 infants with Down syndrome and 39 control infants
headline_result: Intracranial volume in infants with Down syndrome was 12.6% lower at 6 months and 16.3% lower at 12 months than controls (p<.001); subcortical structure volumes were 6.9-13.1% lower (p≤.003), with slower growth from 6 to 12 months except in the amygdala and putamen

model_family: Two separately trained ResNet-50 CNN classifiers
patient_population: pediatric wrist radiographs (GRAZPEDWRI-DX, n=20,327) and a mixed-age multi-region radiograph dataset (FracAtlas, n=4,083)
clinical_problem: fracture detection generalizability between pediatric and adult radiographs
model_description: Two ResNet-50 fracture classifiers were trained separately, one on a pediatric wrist radiograph dataset and one on a mixed-age multi-region radiograph dataset, then each was tested on the other (opposing) population's data. Grad-CAM was used to visualize what each model relied on.
title: Bidirectional Domain Shift Failure in Radiograph Fracture Classification Across Out-of-Distribution Pediatric and Mixed-Age Multi-Region Data
study_design: retrospective cross-dataset diagnostic accuracy and generalizability study
headline_result: Both models achieved acceptable internal test accuracy (82.2% and 83.7%), but cross-testing on the opposing population caused specificity to collapse to 0% in both directions while sensitivity was artificially inflated to 100%; the FracAtlas-trained model misread normal pediatric growth plates as fractures

patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing CT for chronic rhinosinusitis
clinical_problem: quantitative assessment of chronic rhinosinusitis severity (sinus volume and inflammatory involvement)
model_description: A 3D convolutional neural network was trained to automatically segment the maxillary sinuses on pediatric CT scans, using manually annotated expert segmentations as ground truth, then compute sinus volume and the percentage of the sinus affected by inflammatory changes, giving a quantitative alternative to descriptive CT scoring of chronic rhinosinusitis in children.
title: A machine-learning model for quantitative assessment of maxillary sinus volume and involvement in children based on computed tomography
study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study
dataset_size: 92 CT scans of the paranasal sinuses in pediatric patients
headline_result: mean sensitivity, precision and Dice coefficient near 90%; root-mean-square error 0.4 cm3 for sinus volume and 1.3 percentage points for inflammatory involvement

model_name: GAUGE (GARBH-Ini Ultrasound image-based Gestational age Estimator)
model_family: Multi-task deep learning model with an image-based conformal prediction framework for out-of-distribution rejection
patient_population: 6,579 participants from the GARBH-Ini and WINGS prospective cohorts in North India (development); 1,577 internal test participants; 311 external test participants from a separate ultrasound lab
clinical_problem: gestational age estimation and detection of fetal growth restriction / small-for-gestational-age fetuses in late pregnancy
model_description: A multi-task deep learning model segments the fetal head in an ultrasound image and estimates gestational age directly from image features, rather than relying on standard fetal-size biometry formulas. A conformal-prediction step rejects out-of-distribution images before inference. It was trained on two prospective Indian cohorts and tested on an internal held-out set and an independent external site using a different ultrasound machine.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Accurate Gestational Age Estimation with a Deep Learning Model Using Ultrasound Images to Enhance Detection of Fetal Growth Restriction and Small-For-Gestational-Age Fetuses in Late Pregnancy: A Prospective Cohort Study​
study_design: prospective multi-cohort development and external validation study
dataset_size: 46,926 head ultrasound images from 6,579 participants (development); 1,577 participants internal test set; 311 participants external test set
headline_result: Mean absolute error 3.5 days on internal test set (37.2% lower than Hadlock, 25.4% lower than INTERGROWTH-21st formulas); external test MAE 5.89 days; detected 77.6%, 88.7% and 89.7% of fetal growth restriction cases at 26-28, 30-32 and ≥35 weeks respectively, versus 48.6% (Hadlock) and 64.1% (INTERGROWTH-21st) at ≥35 weeks

model_family: hybrid deep-learning framework: multi-scale joint detection, semi-supervised contrastive language-image pretraining for pseudo-labeling, and LDA/normalization-based global attention
patient_population: 1,000 public RSNA bone age images and 9,577 additional clinical radiographs
clinical_problem: bone age assessment for diagnosing pediatric growth disorders
model_description: A deep-learning bone age assessment pipeline combines a multi-scale joint-detection module for the hand and wrist, semi-supervised contrastive language-image pretraining used to generate pseudo-labels for epiphyseal maturity, and an attention-enhanced classification network, producing a continuous bone age estimate from a hand radiograph. It was validated on the public RSNA bone age dataset plus additional clinical radiographs, improving joint-detection rate over a YOLO baseline.
title: Bone age assessment via joint feature learning, epiphyseal evaluation, and hybrid vision-language modeling
study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study
dataset_size: 1,000 public RSNA bone age images and 9,577 clinical radiographs
headline_result: 99.98% joint-detection rate (4.12% improvement over YOLOv10), 81.8% average classification accuracy, mean absolute error 0.25 years, RMSE 0.29 years

model_family: Machine learning (tabular models combining structured ultrasound descriptors with clinical/lab features)
patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing ultrasound evaluation for suspected acute appendicitis, across 11 included studies (40-780 patients each)
clinical_problem: appendicitis diagnosis and severity stratification on pediatric ultrasound
model_description: Systematic review (PRISMA 2020, PROBAST-AI) of 11 studies applying machine learning to pediatric ultrasound for appendicitis diagnosis and severity stratification, most combining structured ultrasound descriptors with clinical and laboratory features. Reviews internal and the one available cross-site external validation study.
title: Machine Learning Applications in Pediatric Ultrasound for Appendicitis Diagnosis and Severity Stratification: A Systematic Review
headline_result: Internal diagnostic AUROC up to 0.993 (range 0.91-0.96 across tabular models); one external validation study showed diagnostic AUROC decreasing from 0.96 internally to 0.85 externally

model_description: This narrative review (literature from 2021-2026) summarizes AI applications in prenatal medicine. patient_population: pediatric imaging patients generally
clinical_problem: AI applications across pediatric imaging, with bone age assessment and chest radiograph interpretation as the most established use cases
task: detection / diagnosis; measurement / quantification; workflow / non-interpretive
model_description: This narrative review examines why pediatric imaging AI differs from adult radiology AI, citing developmental variability, different disease epidemiology, imaging constraints, and limited pediatric datasets. It finds the most mature applications are in image acquisition, dose reduction and workflow optimization, with bone age assessment and chest radiograph interpretation the most established interpretive/prognostic use cases, while adult-trained models often underperform in children. It calls for pediatric-specific design, shared data infrastructure, federated learning, and age-stratified prospective validation.
journal: Indian Journal of Radiology and Imaging
title: Unique Opportunities and Challenges of Artificial Intelligence in Pediatric Imaging

release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Integrated Brain Connectivity Analysis with fMRI, DTI, and sMRI Powered by Interpretable Graph Neural Networks.
study_design: methods development study using the HCP-Development cohort (preprint)

patient_population: 247 scoliosis patients (2008-2021), frontal/lateral/back images and X-rays
clinical_problem: Automated scoliosis screening and Cobb angle estimation from upright back photographs to reduce unnecessary radiography in adolescents.

title: A New Method for Scoliosis Screening Incorporating Deep Learning With Back Images.
headline_result: Cobb angle measurement accuracy superior to traditional human visual recognition method (specific number not stated)

patient_population: 210 patients (children with cerebral palsy), X-ray scans
clinical_problem: Automated quantification of hip migration percentage from pelvis radiographs to support hip surveillance and severity assessment in children with cerebral palsy.
model_description: Machine learning landmark-detection models (fine-tuned VGG-19 with pre-trained weights) take anterior-posterior pelvis radiographs as input and predict hip landmarks used by a geometric algorithm to automatically calculate migration percentage for hip dysplasia severity assessment.
journal: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
title: An automated framework for pediatric hip surveillance and severity assessment using radiographs.
headline_result: VGG-19 fine-tuned model achieved lowest MSE for landmark detection (specific error value not stated)

model_family: feature-representation drift detection with statistical process control
patient_population: adult and pediatric chest radiographs, and CT images, used as drift scenarios
clinical_problem: knowing when a deployed model is being shown images it was not built for, including adult models being fed pediatric radiographs
model_description: Not a diagnostic model but a guard on one: it detects when an incoming image is out of distribution for the deployed model, and monitors the data stream for gradual drift using statistical process control. One of its three demonstrations is exactly the failure mode a children's hospital should worry about — telling adult chest radiographs from pediatric ones, which it flagged within a day of the shift beginning. Modality- and model-agnostic by design.
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
title: Out-of-Distribution Detection and Radiological Data Monitoring Using Statistical Process Control.
headline_result: sensitivity for out-of-distribution detection 0.980 (CT), 0.984 (chest radiograph modality) and 0.854 (pediatric versus adult chest radiographs); a simulated adult-to-pediatric drift was detected within a day at a low false positive rate

patient_population: children with drug-resistant epilepsy undergoing preoperative diffusion-weighted imaging connectome analysis
clinical_problem: predicting short-term postoperative language improvement in children with drug-resistant epilepsy from preoperative whole-brain diffusion-weighted imaging connectome/tractography
model_description: Uses a deep convolutional neural network to classify white-matter tracts from preoperative whole-brain diffusion-weighted imaging tractography, then applies connectivity markers from resulting language modular networks with machine-learning algorithms to predict short-term postoperative language improvement after epilepsy surgery.
title: Deep Learning-Based Tract Classification of Preoperative DWI Tractography Advances the Prediction of Short-Term Postoperative Language Improvement in Children With Drug-Resistant Epilepsy.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and validation study
headline_result: Best algorithm achieved 96/94/96% accuracy (core/expressive/receptive domains) predicting language improvement on an independent validation cohort

model_family: nnU-Net, evaluated and then retrained or fine-tuned on pediatric data
patient_population: 300 adult and 359 pediatric abdominal CT scans from external datasets
clinical_problem: whether the field's default open organ segmentation model, built on adults, is safe to use on children
model_description: The title is the finding. TotalSegmentator, trained on adults, drops from 0.81 to 0.73 mean Dice on pediatric scans, and the failure concentrates in the small structures — adrenal glands fall to 0.35-0.41 against 0.68-0.69 in adults. The paper then shows both fixes work: a pediatric-only model and an adult model fine-tuned on children each beat it on every organ. This is the cleanest available demonstration of why adult-trained tools need pediatric validation before deployment.
release_evidence: evaluates the openly available TotalSegmentator model
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
title: Children Are Not Small Adults: Addressing Limited Generalizability of an Adult Deep Learning CT Organ Segmentation Model to the Pediatric Population.
study_design: retrospective external evaluation with model retraining
headline_result: mean Dice 0.73 in children versus 0.81 in adults (P < .001); adrenal gland Dice 0.35-0.41 versus 0.68-0.69; pediatric-specific training and fine-tuning both improved every organ, by over 0.2 Dice for the adrenals

model_family: neural network whole-lung and lobar segmentation inside an automated processing pipeline
patient_population: 75 children with cystic fibrosis imaged at 1.5 T
clinical_problem: measuring regional ventilation and perfusion in children with cystic fibrosis without contrast, breath-holds or ionizing radiation
model_description: An end-to-end pipeline that turns free-breathing, contrast-free lung MRI into ventilation and perfusion maps and quantified defect percentages, delivered as a short clinical report. It was feasible in every child attempted, with a six-minute scan and twenty-minute processing. The authors also report how often a human had to correct the segmentation and what difference that made to the numbers, which is the honest way to describe an automated pipeline in clinical use.
title: An automated pipeline for computation and analysis of functional ventilation and perfusion lung MRI with matrix pencil decomposition: TrueLung.
headline_result: feasible in all children, 6 min 20 s mean scan time; automatic whole-lung quantification satisfactory in 88% of patients and lobar quantification in 73%; manual refinement changed relative ventilation and perfusion by 0.7% and 2.0%

model_family: explainable deep learning framework for spatio-temporal coupling (dynamic functional connectivity)
patient_population: children and young adults undergoing resting-state functional imaging
model_description: A deep learning framework jointly models the time-varying coupling between brain regions and their connectivity (dynamic functional connectivity) while providing step-by-step explainability of the results. Applied to resting-state imaging spanning brain development, it captured two distinct patterns of change with age: decreasing connectivity in emotion-regulation regions and increasing connectivity in cognitive regions, with children and young adults showing cyclic fluctuations.
title: An Explainable Unified Framework of Spatio-Temporal Coupling Learning With Application to Dynamic Brain Functional Connectivity Analysis.
headline_result: Identified two distinct developmental functional-connectivity patterns (decreasing emotion-regulation connectivity, increasing cognitive-network connectivity) with age

clinical_problem: segmenting the pubic symphysis and fetal head on intrapartum ultrasound to monitor labor progression

title: PSFHS challenge report: Pubic symphysis and fetal head segmentation from intrapartum ultrasound images.
headline_result: Top-8 challenge algorithms elevated the state-of-the-art in automatic PSFHS segmentation (no single leaderboard metric quoted in abstract)

clinical_problem: Evaluating performance of computer-aided detection systems for lung nodules on standard-dose versus low-dose pediatric chest CT.

title: Editorial Comment: Computer-Aided Detection of Lung Nodules on Low-Dose Pediatric Chest CT-A Cautionary Tale.

model_family: AI classifier (machine learning, architecture not specified in abstract)

clinical_problem: detecting subtle epileptogenic cortical lesions (malformations of cortical development) in children with focal epilepsy and previously negative MRI
model_description: The MELD-FCD AI classifier is applied to a dedicated multi-sequence 3T epilepsy MRI protocol (3D FLAIR, MPRAGE, T2 TSE, MP2RAGE, ASL) to identify pathological findings consistent with focal cortical dysplasia, compared with radiologist scoring of each sequence.
title: Integrating standard epilepsy protocol, ASL-perfusion, MP2RAGE/EDGE and the MELD-FCD classifier in the detection of subtle epileptogenic lesions: a 3 Tesla MRI pilot study.
headline_result: MELD-FCD classifier true positive rate 69.2%; identified one subtle lesion overlooked by neuroradiologists, changing management

clinical_problem: radiologic bone age estimation
model_description: A narrative review describing AI-based algorithms developed for radiologic bone age estimation (object recognition, feature extraction, segmentation) and their reported performance, followed by a Strengths-Weaknesses-Opportunities-Challenges (SWOC) analysis of factors affecting clinical and medicolegal adoption of AI for bone age assessment.
title: Charting the growth through intelligence: A SWOC analysis on AI-assisted radiologic bone age estimation.

clinical_problem: determining the necessity of bronchoscopy for suspected foreign body aspiration on chest radiograph
model_description: Input: PA chest radiographs; output: prediction of whether bronchoscopy is needed (positive/negative for foreign body aspiration), compared against multiple logistic regression.
title: The Impact of Deep Learning on Determining the Necessity of Bronchoscopy in Pediatric Foreign Body Aspiration: Can Negative Bronchoscopy Rates Be Reduced?
dataset_size: 110 PA CXR images (47 FBA patients, 63 controls)
headline_result: CNN sensitivity 94.1%, specificity 97.8%, accuracy 97.3%, F1 0.914

model_family: three commercial bone age programs compared head to head
patient_population: 306 children aged 1-18, stratified by sex and age, at a Central European centre
clinical_problem: which of the bone age products approved for the European market a department should buy
model_description: The comparison the vendors do not run: three commercially available bone age programs on one cohort, against a three-expert Greulich-Pyle ground truth, reporting dropout rates alongside accuracy. All three were reliable across the main age range and differed mainly at the edges of childhood, and the spread between the programs was smaller than the spread between the human readers. Dropout rate varied enormously, from 0% to 20%, which is a practical difference a purchaser would not otherwise see.
release_evidence: three AI-supported programs approved for medical use in Europe: BoneXpert, PANDA and BoneView
title: A critical comparative study of the performance of three AI-assisted programs for bone age determination.
headline_result: root mean squared error 0.62 years (BoneXpert), 0.65 (BoneView) and 0.75 (PANDA), with dropout rates of 2.3%, 20.3% and 0%; variation between AI readers was lower than between human readers (0.54 vs 0.62 years, p < 0.01)

headline_result: RD+CNN image quality 3.6±1.1 vs RD+IR 3.1±0.9 (p<0.001); TD+CNN noise score 2.9±0.6 vs RD+IR 2.7±0.7 (p=0.001)

title: Brain connectomes in youth at risk for serious mental illness: a longitudinal perspective.

title: Spectral Graph Sample Weighting for Interpretable Sub-cohort Analysis in Predictive Models for Neuroimaging.
headline_result: Sample weighting scheme improved interpretability and highlighted sub-cohorts with distinct predictability compared to existing weighting schemes (no single summary accuracy given)

headline_result: face removal accuracy 98%, ear removal accuracy 73%; downstream brain/tumor volume and temporalis metrics correlated with original images (rS > 0.9, all P < .0001)

headline_result: MRI-based measures predicted Bayley scores with higher correlation, more explained variance and smaller error than demographic and laboratory data alone, across cognitive, language and motor domains

title: A neural network to create super-resolution MR from multiple 2D brain scans of pediatric patients.
study_design: retrospective model development and evaluation across multiple datasets

title: Predicting pediatric patient rehabilitation outcomes after spinal deformity surgery with artificial intelligence.
dataset_size: 455 patients at two hospitals, 171 preoperative features
headline_result: area under the ROC curve 0.86, 0.85 and 0.83 for patient-reported outcomes at 6 months, 1 year and 2 years

clinical_problem: Can structural brain MRI distinguish individual adolescents who have experienced abuse or who have internalizing psychopathology?

title: Multiple constraint network classification reveals functional brain networks distinguishing 0-back and 2-back task.

model_family: frame classification network with Bayesian aggregation across the whole video
patient_population: 1,457 recordings of 20-week anomaly scans, comprising 48 million frames
clinical_problem: fetal biometry currently rests on a handful of frames a sonographer chose, and the choice is a source of error
model_description: Inverts how biometry is done. Instead of measuring the image the operator froze, it classifies every frame of the recorded scan, measures wherever the right anatomy is visible, and estimates the true value from that whole population of measurements with a Bayesian model that rejects outliers. The result is not just a number but a credible interval, which no manual measurement provides, and it needs no operator intervention.
title: Whole examination AI estimation of fetal biometrics from 20-week ultrasound scans.
headline_result: human-level performance in estimating fetal biometrics, with well-calibrated credible intervals for the true value

headline_result: ICC 0.892-0.991 vs experienced physicians; mean absolute error 1.16 mm (SVA), 0.22-3.32 degrees (angles)

model_description: A scoping review of 48 papers on neural-network-based methods for fetal heart anatomy classification and segmentation in fetal echocardiography, covering techniques such as attention/saliency, coarse-to-fine refinement, dilated convolution, generative adversarial networks, and spatio-temporal modeling.

model_family: progressive concept bottleneck model with segmentation

Most explainable-AI papers stop at the method; this one tests whether the explanations help.
