patient_population: 39 children with overweight/obesity and 51 children with normal weight, ages 8-12 years, with 1-year follow-up
clinical_problem: predicting future BMI and food-approach behavior in children with obesity from hippocampal effective connectivity
model_description: Resting-state fMRI functional and effective connectivity (via spectral dynamic causal modeling) of the hippocampus are measured in children aged 8-12 with and without excess weight. Linear support vector regression is trained on baseline hippocampal connectivity to predict BMI and food-approach eating behavior measured one year later, identifying altered bidirectional hippocampus-postcentral gyrus connectivity as predictive.
journal: International journal of clinical and health psychology : IJCHP
title: Altered hippocampal effective connectivity predicts BMI and food approach behavior in children with obesity.
headline_result: Altered bidirectional hippocampus-postcentral gyrus effective connectivity predicted BMI and food-approach behavior one year later

patient_population: 3,935 patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (EOS biplanar radiographic system)
clinical_problem: Generating synthetic sagittal spine radiographs from coronal-view radiographs in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis to reduce radiation exposure from biplanar imaging during monitoring
model_description: A GAN model trained on paired coronal and sagittal EOS radiographs generates synthetic sagittal spine images from coronal views alone; synthetic images were compared with real sagittal radiographs for measurement of lumbar lordosis, sacral slope, pelvic incidence, and sagittal vertical axis.
title: Feasibility of generating sagittal radiographs from coronal views using GAN-based deep learning framework in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
study_design: retrospective GAN model development and evaluation against real paired radiographs
headline_result: ICC 0.83-0.88 for synthetic image measurements (vs 0.93-0.99 for real images); correlations between real and synthetic parameters 0.17-0.74; mean absolute errors 7-9 degrees for angular measures and 1.1 cm for sagittal vertical axis; image quality judged insufficient for clinical parameter assessment except for sagittal vertical axis

patient_population: multi-demographic fetal echocardiography dataset and the public CAMUS adult dataset
clinical_problem: estimating cardiac motion for myocardial strain and stroke volume assessment on echocardiography
model_description: An unsupervised deep learning image registration framework, using anatomic shape-encoded and data-driven texture constraints, estimates frame-to-frame cardiac motion on both fetal and adult echocardiography and is benchmarked against optical flow and Elastix.
title: Deep learning image registration for cardiac motion estimation in adult and fetal echocardiography via a focus on anatomic plausibility and texture quality of warped image.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and benchmark comparison
dataset_size: multi-demographic fetal dataset plus public CAMUS adult dataset
headline_result: Outperformed traditional non-deep-learning registration approaches (optical flow, Elastix)

model_family: convolutional neural network (ensemble: EfficientNet, MobileNet, ResNet50, ResNet152, VGG16, Xception)
patient_population: children imaged at Batman Training and Research Hospital
clinical_problem: Can deep learning classify adenoid hypertrophy on X-ray images in children?
model_description: Six ensemble CNN architectures are trained and compared to classify adenoid hypertrophy on masked vs. non-masked pediatric X-ray images, with ResNet50 performing best.
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
title: Automatic Identification of Adenoid Hypertrophy via Ensemble Deep Learning Models Employing X-ray Adenoid Images.
headline_result: ResNet50 100% accuracy on masked images; Xception 65% F1-score

patient_population: Pregnancies complicated by fetal growth restriction
clinical_problem: How AI can improve diagnosis, monitoring and risk stratification of fetal growth restriction
model_description: Narrative review of AI methods (automated fetal biometry, Doppler-index and maternal-characteristic predictive models) used to diagnose and monitor fetal growth restriction and stratify adverse-outcome risk
title: Artificial Intelligence in Fetal Growth Restriction Management: A Narrative Review.

patient_population: 21 typically developing children aged 8 to 17 years
clinical_problem: improving image quality/SNR of arterial spin labeling perfusion MRI to enable measurement of choroid plexus perfusion in children, previously limited by small structure size
model_description: A self-supervised Transformer-based deep-learning model takes noisy multi-delay arterial spin labeling perfusion MRI images (with k-space weighted image averaging as training reference) as input and outputs denoised perfusion images, improving SNR for quantifying choroid plexus and gray-matter perfusion in children.
title: High resolution multi-delay arterial spin labeling with self-supervised deep learning denoising for pediatric choroid plexus perfusion MRI.
study_design: prospective test-retest methodological development study in typically developing children

patient_population: 375 normal inspiratory chest CT scans, ages 0-24 years (screened from 1,160 scans)
clinical_problem: establishing normative pediatric-to-young-adult reference values for airway and pulmonary artery dimensions on chest CT using an automated deep-learning measurement algorithm
model_description: An automated deep-learning-based algorithm takes chest CT scans as input and outputs quantitative measurements of bronchial and pulmonary artery diameters, wall thickness, and lung volume/density, used to derive normative pediatric-to-adult reference ranges.
title: Normative values for lung, bronchial sizes, and bronchus-artery ratios in chest CT scans: from infancy into young adulthood.
study_design: retrospective normative reference-value study using an automated deep-learning CT measurement tool

patient_population: 46 pediatric patients undergoing 3D T1-weighted brain MRI
clinical_problem: shortening pediatric brain MRI acquisition time while maintaining image quality
model_description: A deep-learning-based reconstruction algorithm is applied to accelerated 3D T1-weighted pediatric brain MRI acquisitions, taking undersampled k-space/image data as input and outputting reconstructed images compared with conventional and non-DL accelerated reconstructions.
release_evidence: vendor deep-learning reconstruction algorithm used on a clinical 3T scanner (GE HealthCare SIGNA Premier)
title: Evaluation of Image Quality and Scan Time Efficiency in Accelerated 3D T1-Weighted Pediatric Brain MRI Using Deep Learning-Based Reconstruction.
headline_result: Scan time reduced 29.3-40.7%; DL reconstruction improved aSNR, aCNR and overall image quality vs. conventional acquisition (all P<0.05)

model_family: nnU-Net ensemble trained in two strategies with five-fold cross-validation
patient_population: 4,082 CT images from several databases, including 300 pediatric cases
clinical_problem: having organ masks on a child's CT, which patient-specific dose calculation and any quantitative analysis depend on
model_description: Segments 26 organs on a whole-body CT, trained deliberately across databases with very different acquisition so that it holds up on both children and adults. The comparison that matters is against TotalSegmentator, the field's default open tool, which it outperformed on every mutual organ — TotalSegmentator having been built on adult data.
journal: Physica medica : PM : an international journal devoted to the applications of physics to medicine and biology : official journal of the Italian Association of Biomedical Physics (AIFB)
title: Development and validation of fully automated robust deep learning models for multi-organ segmentation from whole-body CT images.
headline_result: Dice above 0.90 for 17 of 26 organs; outperformed TotalSegmentator on all mutual organs across three test subsets

model_family: various (respiratory sound analysis, automated imaging evaluation, clinical decision support)
patient_population: children and adolescents with lung disease, as discussed across reviewed AI applications
clinical_problem: reviewing AI applications (respiratory sound analysis, automated imaging evaluation, clinical decision support) for diagnosis and treatment of lung disease in children and adolescents
model_description: Review of AI-supported technologies in pediatric pneumology, spanning models for analyzing respiratory sounds, automated evaluation of medical imaging, and clinical decision-support systems, with challenges of adapting AI to pediatric populations.
title: [Artificial intelligence in paediatric pneumology - opportunities and unanswered questions].

patient_population: not stated (letter; no abstract provided)
clinical_problem: direct estimation of fetal biometry measurements from ultrasound video scans (no abstract provided)
model_description: Letter describing direct estimation of fetal biometry measurements from ultrasound video scans using deep learning; no abstract text provided.
journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
title: Direct estimation of fetal biometry measurements from ultrasound video scans through deep learning.

model_family: convolutional neural network (differential CNN, dual CNN)
patient_population: annotated fetal ultrasound datasets, 5th-month gestation
clinical_problem: Can deep learning localize the correct imaging plane and segment the cerebellum on fetal ultrasound to support prenatal prediction of neurodevelopmental disorders?
model_description: Two custom CNN architectures -- a differential CNN for standard-plane localization and a dual CNN for cerebellum segmentation -- process mid-trimester fetal brain ultrasound images.
title: Prenatal Diagnostics Using Deep Learning: A Dual Approach to Plane Localization and Cerebellum Segmentation in Ultrasound Images.
study_design: retrospective model development and validation study
headline_result: 98.6% accuracy (plane localization), Dice 0.956 (cerebellum segmentation)

patient_population: 1340 patients with CM1 and syringomyelia (Park Reeves Syringomyelia Research Consortium registry, pediatric and adult)
clinical_problem: identifying clinically meaningful phenotypic subgroups of Chiari type-1 malformation and syringomyelia using combined clinical and radiological features
model_description: Uses a data-driven feature selection process (Laplacian score) combined with clinician input on clinical and radiological variables (e.g., syrinx size, tonsil position), then applies K-modes clustering to identify three distinct presenting phenotypes of Chiari malformation with syringomyelia.
title: Using Artificial Intelligence to Identify Three Presenting Phenotypes of Chiari Type-1 Malformation and Syringomyelia.

patient_population: 887 female patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, first consulted 2011-2023, single center
clinical_problem: predicting future spinal curve progression in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
model_description: Machine learning regression models, explored via PyCaret, are trained on radiographic and questionnaire data from patients' first two clinic visits to predict future Cobb angles for proximal thoracic, main thoracic and thoracolumbar curves.
journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
title: Machine learning algorithms for predicting future curve using first and second visit data in female adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients.
headline_result: R2 0.73/0.63/0.61 and MAE 2.3/4.0/4.2 degrees for proximal thoracic/main thoracic/thoracolumbar curves

model_family: various machine-learning algorithms (systematic review of 26 studies)
patient_population: very preterm infants (systematic review of 26 studies, January 2018-December 2023)
clinical_problem: Reviewing machine-learning models that predict neurodevelopmental impairment (cognitive, motor, language deficits) in very preterm infants using clinical, neuroimaging, and omics data
model_description: A systematic review of 26 studies applying machine-learning algorithms to clinical and neuroimaging data (and, increasingly, omics data) from very preterm infants to predict later neurodevelopmental impairment.
title: Machine learning techniques for predicting neurodevelopmental impairments in premature infants: a systematic review.

patient_population: patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (dataset size not stated)
clinical_problem: automating vertebral landmark detection and Cobb angle measurement for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis diagnosis
model_description: A deep learning framework (LAD-Net) predicts spine centre and corner landmark points and their offset vectors on spinal X-rays, refined by correction modules, from which Cobb angles and Lenke classification are computed for AIS diagnosis.
journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
title: Adjacent point aided vertebral landmark detection and Cobb angle measurement for automated AIS diagnosis.

patient_population: prospective cohort of fetal abdominal ultrasound images (9 plane classes)
clinical_problem: automatically identifying standard fetal abdominal ultrasound scanning planes (for abdominal circumference measurement) to reduce time required for fetal biometric assessment
model_description: Deep convolutional neural networks (best-performing: MobileNetV3Large and EfficientV2S) take preprocessed fetal ultrasound images as input, after OCR-based removal of on-screen text/artifacts, and classify the image into one of nine fetal abdominal standard-plane/structure categories, aiding automated abdominal circumference measurement.
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
title: Automatic Identification of Fetal Abdominal Planes from Ultrasound Images Based on Deep Learning.
study_design: prospective cohort study with retrospective deep learning model development (ten-fold cross-validation)
headline_result: Best models MobileNetV3Large 79.89% and EfficientV2S 79.19% accuracy

patient_population: 138 neonatal chest radiographs
clinical_problem: Diagnose neonatal respiratory distress syndrome from chest radiographs using radiomics, examining the effect of rib suppression
model_description: Applies rib suppression preprocessing to neonatal chest radiographs, extracts radiomic features from lung regions before and after suppression, and trains machine learning classifiers (e.g., Gradient Boosting Machine) to diagnose neonatal respiratory distress syndrome.
title: Rib suppression-based radiomics for diagnosis of neonatal respiratory distress syndrome in chest X-rays.
study_design: retrospective single-cohort radiomics model development study
headline_result: GBM AUC 0.781 post-rib-suppression vs 0.556 pre-suppression; combined-feature LDA AUC 0.762, LR AUC 0.756

model_family: deep learning radiomics (ResNet50 transfer learning) + logistic regression
patient_population: 323 pediatric patients with pancreaticobiliary maljunction from three centers
clinical_problem: Can a preoperative CT-based model identify children with pancreaticobiliary maljunction who have moderate-to-severe chronic cholangitis, to guide surgical planning?
model_description: A deep learning radiomics nomogram combines ResNet50 transfer-learning features and handcrafted radiomics from contrast-enhanced CT with clinical factors to preoperatively predict cholangitis severity in children with pancreaticobiliary maljunction.
title: Deep learning radiomics nomogram for preoperatively identifying moderate-to-severe chronic cholangitis in children with pancreaticobiliary maljunction: a multicenter study.
study_design: retrospective multicenter model development and external validation study
dataset_size: 323 patients across training, internal validation, and two external test cohorts
headline_result: AUC 0.895-0.916 across internal and external test cohorts

patient_population: not applicable (survey of pediatric radiologists, not patients)
clinical_problem: surveying pediatric radiologists' attitudes toward and current use of AI and teleradiology
model_description: Anonymous online survey of Society for German-speaking Pediatric Radiologists (GPR) and Swiss Society for Pediatric Radiology (SGPR) members on attitudes toward and current use of AI and teleradiology in pediatric radiology.
journal: RoFo : Fortschritte auf dem Gebiete der Rontgenstrahlen und der Nuklearmedizin
title: Artificial Intelligence and Teleradiology in Pediatric Radiology: A Survey by the Society for German-speaking Pediatric Radiologists (GPR) and the Swiss Society for Pediatric Radiology (SGPR).
headline_result: 38.9% fully agreed AI is relevant to pediatric radiology; >80% said bone age determination is well-suited for AI, yet only 31% routinely use such a solution

patient_population: 48 fetuses (24 normal, 24 with congenital heart disease)
clinical_problem: enabling remote second-expert review of fetal cardiac ultrasound to improve detection of congenital heart disease
model_description: AI automatically extracts short video clips of the fetal heart from streamed ultrasound video; these clips, versus manually saved still images, are used by expert clinicians for remote second review to detect cardiac abnormalities.
title: Video Clip Extraction From Fetal Ultrasound Scans Using Artificial Intelligence to Allow Remote Second Expert Review for Congenital Heart Disease.
study_design: retrospective reader study using AI-extracted video clips
headline_result: Second review with AI video clips improved CHD detection sensitivity from 0.792 to 0.975 (vs 0.892 with still images)

model_family: normalizing flow network + shallow harmonizer network
patient_population: Adult and neonatal brain MRI datasets
clinical_problem: Harmonizing brain MRI acquired across different sites/scanners without needing paired data or source-site access, evaluated including neonatal brain segmentation and neonatal brain age estimation
model_description: A normalizing-flow network learns the distribution of a source imaging domain; a shallow harmonizer network is trained (and updated at inference) to make new-site images match that learned source distribution, unsupervised and without needing source-site data at inference, tested on neonatal brain segmentation and brain-age estimation as well as adult brain MRI
release_evidence: The code is available at https://github.com/farzad-bz/Harmonizing-Flows.
title: Harmonizing flows: Leveraging normalizing flows for unsupervised and source-free MRI harmonization.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and cross-domain validation study
headline_result: Superior performance compared with existing harmonization methods (exact metric not given in abstract)

patient_population: infants and children (literature review)
clinical_problem: reviewing AI applications using structural MRI (radiomics) for early diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder in infants and children
model_description: Short review of AI tools applied to structural brain MRI radiomics for early ASD diagnosis, covering cortical parcellation methods and available databases.
title: AI-based non-invasive imaging technologies for early autism spectrum disorder diagnosis: A short review and future directions.

patient_population: 73 children with neuroblastic tumors
clinical_problem: Can ultrasound-based radiomics help distinguish prognostic subsets of pediatric neuroblastic tumors?
model_description: Ultrasound radiomics features are combined with clinical characteristics in machine learning models (extreme gradient boosting selected as best) to differentiate prognostic subsets of pediatric neuroblastic tumors.
title: Ultrasonic-Based Radiomics Signature With Machine Learning for Differentiating Prognostic Subsets of Pediatric Peripheral Neuroblastic Tumors: A Retrospective Study.
headline_result: Validation AUC 0.941 (combined model), 0.918 (radiomics-only model)

model_family: Bayesian optimization of CLAHE contrast enhancement
patient_population: preterm and high-risk neonates undergoing portable chest X-ray
clinical_problem: improving image quality of low-quality portable neonatal chest X-rays to aid lesion classification without increasing radiation dose
model_description: Bayesian optimization automatically selects CLAHE contrast-enhancement hyperparameters for neonatal chest radiographs, improving image quality and downstream deep-learning lesion classification such as transient tachypnea of the newborn.
title: BO-CLAHE enhancing neonatal chest X-ray image quality for improved lesion classification.
headline_result: Improved classification performance for diagnosing transient tachypnea of the newborn

model_family: large language model (Gemma-7B) with a distilled BERT-based model
patient_population: pediatric abdominal X-ray reports from C.S. Mott Children's Hospital (exact n not stated)
clinical_problem: Automatically labeling pediatric abdominal X-ray radiology reports for the presence and subtype (pneumatosis, portal venous gas, free air) of necrotizing enterocolitis, to support NEC research
model_description: AXpert uses a privacy-preserving, instruction-fine-tuned large language model (Gemma-7B) and a distilled BERT-based version to automatically annotate pediatric abdominal X-ray reports for necrotizing enterocolitis presence and subtype (pneumatosis, portal venous gas, free air), trained and deployed locally.
title: AXpert: human expert facilitated privacy-preserving large language models for abdominal X-ray report labeling.
study_design: retrospective model development and evaluation against baseline BERT models
headline_result: Gemma-7B F1 score 0.9 ± 0.015 for detecting NEC-positive samples, a 132% improvement over the BlueBERT baseline

patient_population: 23 adolescents with first-episode, treatment-naive major depressive disorder and 27 matched healthy controls
clinical_problem: differentiating adolescents with first-episode major depressive disorder from healthy controls
model_description: A machine-learning multivariate diagnostic model uses resting-state fMRI graph-theory network topology metrics to classify adolescents with major depressive disorder versus healthy controls.
title: Disorganization of Small-World Functional Brain Networks in First-Episode, Treatment-Naïve Adolescents With Major Depressive Disorder.

patient_population: 640 adolescents and youths screened in three Peruvian youth detention centers
clinical_problem: Can AI-assisted automated reading of chest X-rays help find active tuberculosis cases through active screening in youth detention centers?
model_description: AI software provided automated reading of chest X-rays as part of an active tuberculosis screening algorithm, combined with GeneXpert Ultra molecular testing and clinical evaluation.
journal: Revista peruana de medicina experimental y salud publica
title: Active search for tuberculosis in three youth detention centers in Peru.
headline_result: 8 of 105 GeneXpert tests (8.5%) confirmed TB; screening rate 1250 per 100,000, ten times the general-population rate

patient_population: 1,549 fetal ultrasound images
clinical_problem: Automatically measure the frontomaxillary facial angle on prenatal ultrasound for trisomy 21 screening
model_description: Trains a deep learning network to segment critical facial regions on 2D fetal ultrasound images, then uses a keypoint detection network to locate landmark points and compute the frontomaxillary facial angle automatically.
title: Automatic Measurement of Frontomaxillary Facial Angle in Fetal Ultrasound Images Using Deep Learning.
headline_result: Mean absolute error 2.354 degrees, outperforming typical junior-expert accuracy standards

patient_population: 535 hospitalized children with pleural effusion (167 bacterial, 368 Mycoplasma)
clinical_problem: Distinguishing bacterial pneumonia from Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia as the cause of pleural effusion in children using chest CT
model_description: Radiomics features are manually extracted from non-contrast chest CT regions of pleural effusion, reduced by feature-selection methods (Select K Best, mRMR, LASSO), and input to a logistic regression model that classifies the effusion as bacterial or Mycoplasma pneumoniae-related
title: The value of CT-based radiomics for differentiation of pleural effusions in bacterial pneumonia and Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia in children.
headline_result: AUC 0.942 (training set), 0.917 (test set)

patient_population: 92 patients with pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (from 1,298 records screened)
clinical_problem: Investigate correlation between Lhermitte's sign and AI-based radiological characteristics (upper cervical spinal cord lesions) in pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis
model_description: Uses AI-based radiological analysis of spinal cord MRI to characterize cervical lesions (C1-4) and correlate them with the clinical sign Lhermitte's sign in pediatric-onset MS patients.
journal: Advances in clinical and experimental medicine : official organ Wroclaw Medical University
title: An artificial intelligence model for Lhermitte's sign in patients with pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis: A follow-up study.
headline_result: Upper cervical lesion (C1-4) frequency higher in groups with current/past Lhermitte's sign vs never (p=0.017)

patient_population: fetuses (review, no single cohort)
clinical_problem: using AI and 4D ultrasound to analyze fetal facial expressions as a potential prenatal marker of neurodevelopmental disorders
model_description: A narrative review of AI-assisted analysis of 4D ultrasound fetal facial movements, discussing their potential as diagnostic markers for prenatal neurodevelopmental disorders such as Bell's Palsy and Ramsay Hunt Syndrome.
title: AI and early diagnostics: mapping fetal facial expressions through development, evolution, and 4D ultrasound.

model_family: deep learning radiomics on semi-supervised placental segmentation
patient_population: 420 pregnant women across centres: 140 with preeclampsia (65 with fetal growth restriction) and 280 normotensive
clinical_problem: identifying preeclampsia and, within it, the pregnancies where the fetus is growth restricted
model_description: Segments the placenta automatically on T2-weighted MRI and derives a combined radiomic and deep-learning signature that separates preeclamptic from normotensive pregnancies, and then separates those where the fetus is growth restricted. The discrimination is markedly better for the growth-restricted subgroup than for preeclampsia without restriction, which is the clinically consequential half.
title: Association between deep learning radiomics based on placental MRI and preeclampsia with fetal growth restriction: A multicenter study.
headline_result: AUC 0.84-0.89 across training, test, internal and external validation for preeclampsia; 0.918 for preeclampsia with fetal growth restriction versus normotensive, and 0.742 without restriction; placental segmentation Dice 0.917

patient_population: 758 patients with repaired tetralogy of Fallot at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia; 152 with 2 analyzable CMR scans
clinical_problem: Automate segmentation of cardiac MRI to study right ventricular remodeling and identify imaging traits associated with adverse RV remodeling in repaired tetralogy of Fallot
model_description: Uses the nnU-Net deep learning method to automatically segment left and right ventricular blood pool and myocardium from 2D short-axis cardiac MRI, then computes volumetric remodeling rates to study risk factors for right ventricular deterioration after tetralogy of Fallot repair.
journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
title: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging traits associated with adverse right ventricular remodeling in repaired tetralogy of Fallot: A Single Center Outcomes Using cardiovascular magnetic resonance in Tetralogy of Fallot study.
headline_result: Pulmonic valve replacement patients had significantly lower RV remodeling rates than natural-history patients; baseline LV measures associated with RV remodeling rates

patient_population: adolescents undergoing hand-wrist radiography for bone age assessment (public RSNA dataset and an in-house dataset)
clinical_problem: skeletal maturity / bone age assessment
model_description: Given a hand-wrist radiograph, a U-Net first automatically localizes the regions of interest used in the Tanner-Whitehouse method, then an InceptionResNetV2 network extracts features from both the regions of interest and the whole image to estimate bone age, combining the region-based (TW3) and whole-image (Greulich-Pyle) approaches. It was trained and evaluated on the public RSNA bone age dataset and an in-house dataset.
title: A fully automated U-net based ROIs localization and bone age assessment method.
study_design: technical development with retrospective benchmark validation
dataset_size: public RSNA bone age dataset plus an in-house dataset (exact case counts not stated)
headline_result: Localization precision of 99.1% on the public RSNA dataset; mean absolute error 0.38 years (males) and 0.45 years (females) on RSNA, and 0.41 years (males) and 0.44 years (females) on the in-house dataset.

patient_population: Pregnant women across 17 included studies
clinical_problem: How accurately AI models estimate gestational age from ultrasound compared with the standard reference
model_description: Systematic review and meta-analysis pooling AI models (mainly CNNs) that estimate gestational age from 2D ultrasound images or blind-sweep video against ultrasound-based reference standards
title: Use of artificial intelligence for gestational age estimation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
headline_result: Pooled mean GA error 4.32 days (2D images) and 2.55 days (blind-sweep video)

model_family: longitudinally aware segmentation network with cross-attention between timepoints
patient_population: 297 children in two Children's Oncology Group trials (median age 15.4 and 15.8 years), 200 internal and 97 external
age_groups: child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: deciding from the interim PET whether a child's Hodgkin lymphoma is responding, which determines how much treatment they receive
model_description: Reads the baseline and interim PET together rather than separately, letting features from the first scan inform where to look on the second, which is how a physician actually reads a response study. It then produces the quantities that drive therapy decisions — metabolic tumor volume, total lesion glycolysis, qPET and the change in SUVmax — which correlated strongly with physician measurements. Trained and externally tested on cooperative group trial data.
title: Automatic Quantification of Serial PET/CT Images for Pediatric Hodgkin Lymphoma Using a Longitudinally Aware Segmentation Network.
study_design: retrospective study on clinical trial cohorts with external testing
headline_result: F1 0.61 for detecting residual lymphoma on interim PET, beating all comparators (P < .01); baseline segmentation Dice 0.77; Spearman correlation with physician measurements 0.78-0.96 across the four PET metrics

patient_population: 317 fetuses with ventriculomegaly and 183 typically developing fetuses
clinical_problem: using a fetal brain age prediction model to identify fetuses with ventriculomegaly, its severity, and associated CNS abnormalities on fetal MRI
model_description: Input: multiplanar fetal brain MRI sections; output: a predicted fetal brain age, compared to gestational age (predicted age difference) to identify ventriculomegaly, its severity, and associated CNS abnormalities.
title: Deep Learning-based Brain Age Prediction Using MRI to Identify Fetuses with Cerebral Ventriculomegaly.
dataset_size: 317 fetuses with ventriculomegaly, 183 typically developing fetuses
headline_result: fetuses with VM had significantly larger absolute predicted age difference than typical fetuses (P<.001); severe VM larger than moderate VM (P=.004)

patient_population: 9,024 early adolescents
clinical_problem: improving the reliability of task-fMRI individual-difference measures of cognition and psychopathology in early adolescents
model_description: A machine-learning classifier ('neural signature') is trained on task-based fMRI to distinguish high versus low working-memory load; its prediction captures individual differences and is compared against standard regional brain activation estimates for reliability and association with cognition/psychopathology.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
title: Enhancing task fMRI individual difference research with neural signatures.
headline_result: Signature predictions more reliable and more strongly associated with task performance, cognition and psychopathology than standard regional activation estimates

model_family: deep learning models (various, e.g. ResNet backbone)
patient_population: children aged 0-16 years (pooled across 6 studies)
clinical_problem: diagnostic accuracy of deep learning models for detecting pediatric elbow fractures on radiographs
model_description: Systematic review and meta-analysis of deep learning models (commonly ResNet-backbone CNNs) that classify elbow radiographs as fracture vs. no fracture in children aged 0-16.
journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
title: Impact of deep learning on pediatric elbow fracture detection: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
headline_result: pooled sensitivity 0.93, specificity 0.89, AUC 0.95

patient_population: Pediatric patients (newborns to 6 months) undergoing 3D hip ultrasound for DDH evaluation
clinical_problem: Robustly segmenting bone anatomy from 3D hip ultrasound to automate measurement of developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) metrics
model_description: A 3D extension of the SegFormer transformer architecture, with hierarchically structured encoders producing multi-scale features, segments hip bone anatomy from 3D ultrasound volumes to compute DDH diagnostic metrics more robustly than CNN/ViT baselines
title: SegFormer3D: Improving the Robustness of Deep Learning Model-Based Image Segmentation in Ultrasound Volumes of the Pediatric Hip.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and robustness evaluation study
dataset_size: not stated exactly (clinical pediatric test set)
headline_result: Up to 0.9% improvement in Dice score and up to 3% smaller 95% Hausdorff distance vs. state of the art

body_region: brain (pineal/suprasellar region, intracranial germ cell tumor)
patient_population: 65 pathologically confirmed germinoma patients (adolescents, peak incidence age group; also children)
clinical_problem: Provide a public imaging dataset to support development of AI models to improve diagnostic accuracy for germinoma, avoiding unnecessary surgery
model_description: Releases a public multimodal imaging dataset (T2, FLAIR, T1, contrast-enhanced T1, DWI MRI, and CT) with clinical and radiomic features from 65 pathologically confirmed germinoma cases to support training and validation of future AI diagnostic models.
release_evidence: there are no publicly available imaging datasets for germinoma. This study aimed to create a comprehensive dataset for germinoma...
title: A comprehensive dataset of germinoma on MRI/CT with clinical and radiomic data.

patient_population: 12,611 training, 1,425 validation, 200 test hand/wrist radiographs (RSNA 2017 Pediatric Bone Age Challenge dataset)
clinical_problem: automated pediatric bone age assessment from hand and wrist radiographs to guide orthopedic treatment decisions for growth-related disorders
model_description: A ResNet-50-based deep-learning model takes hand and wrist radiographs as input and outputs a predicted bone age in months, benchmarked against radiologist-determined ages.
title: Enhancing Pediatric Bone Age Assessment Using Artificial Intelligence: Implications for Orthopedic Surgery.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and validation study using a public benchmark dataset
headline_result: RMSE 11.07 months, MAE 8.54 months, R² 0.929

patient_population: image-based flow simulations of fetal and adult hearts (synthetic data, not patient imaging)
clinical_problem: reconstructing detailed 3D blood flow velocity and pressure fields in the cardiac left ventricle from color Doppler echocardiography, tested using fetal and adult heart simulations
model_description: a physics-informed neural network takes sparse, noisy 3D color Doppler velocity data as input and outputs reconstructed 3D flow velocity and pressure fields in the cardiac left ventricle
journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
title: 3D velocity and pressure field reconstruction in the cardiac left ventricle via physics informed neural network from echocardiography guided by 3D color Doppler.

model_family: graph neural networks (simple and residual graph convolutional networks), compared with multi-layer perceptron, random forest, and SVM
patient_population: adult BRIGHT dataset (147 Hodgkin lymphoma survivors, 162 age-matched controls) and pediatric HCP-Development dataset (135 healthy subjects)
clinical_problem: sex classification from pediatric and adult structural brain connectome data
model_description: Structural brain connectome graphs (nodes as brain regions, edges as white matter connection strength) from adult and pediatric datasets are input to graph neural network models (simple and residual graph convolutional networks), compared against a multilayer perceptron, random forest, and support vector machine. Architecture experiments test network depth, pooling, and skip connections, with performance assessed by accuracy, AUC, and adversarial robustness; adult-trained models were also extended to and augmented with pediatric data.
title: Graph Neural Network Learning on the Pediatric Structural Connectome.

model_description: A GAN with a Siamese cyclic encoder-decoder and identity-preservation mechanism learns age- and sex-independent representations from single cross-sectional head CT scans, then synthesizes images predicting how that child's skull will look at other ages.
title: Population-Driven Synthesis of Personalized Cranial Development From Cross-Sectional Pediatric CT Images.
study_design: retrospective model development and longitudinal validation
headline_result: State-of-the-art performance on independent longitudinal dataset (no single number given)

patient_population: 500 fetal ultrasound images from multiple hospitals
clinical_problem: Can a vision transformer classify fetal health status and severity of abnormalities from ultrasound images?
model_description: A Vision Transformer model is trained to classify fetal ultrasound images into health status categories (healthy/mild/moderate/severe) and to score abnormality severity.
title: Fetal Diagnostics using Vision Transformer for Enhanced Health and Severity Prediction in Ultrasound Imaging.
headline_result: 90% classification accuracy, F1 0.87, MAE 0.30

patient_population: infants during the first postnatal year, with brain connectivity data held across multiple hospitals
clinical_problem: predicting infant brain connectivity development trajectories across multiple imaging modalities from a single baseline scan while preserving data privacy across hospitals
model_description: Input: a single baseline brain connectivity graph per modality; output: federated graph neural network forecasting multi-trajectory brain connectivity evolution across hospitals with scarce, incomplete longitudinal data.
release_evidence: Our source code is available at https://github.com/basiralab/FedGmTE-Net-plus
title: Predicting infant brain connectivity with federated multi-trajectory GNNs using scarce data.
headline_result: FedGmTE-Net++ outperformed benchmark methods in brain multi-trajectory prediction from a single baseline graph (no single summary metric stated)

patient_population: 105 head CT scans (6,300 slices), infants
clinical_problem: automated detection of hydrocephalus and ventricular volume estimation in infant head CT
model_description: A VGG16-based CNN combined with an automated segmentation pipeline (windowing, histogram equalization, thresholding) takes infant head CT images as input, segments the cerebral ventricles to estimate ventricular volume, and classifies the scan as hydrocephalus or normal.
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
title: Automated Detection of Hydrocephalus in Pediatric Head Computed Tomography Using VGG 16 CNN Deep Learning Architecture and Based Automated Segmentation Workflow for Ventricular Volume Estimation.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and validation study
headline_result: Mean classification accuracy 90.4% ± 1.2%; segmentation R² 0.94-0.99 vs manual

model_family: machine-learning-based classifier for misaligned slice detection, combined with intersection-based motion estimation
patient_population: fetal MRI (simulated and real data)
clinical_problem: correcting inter-slice motion artifacts in fetal brain MRI to improve 3D reconstruction quality
model_description: Input: orthogonal fetal brain MRI slice stacks; output: motion parameters estimated from intersecting-slice intensity profiles, with a machine-learning classifier flagging misaligned slices for correction.
title: Intersection-based slice motion estimation for fetal brain imaging.
headline_result: very low registration errors on simulated datasets; qualitative improvement over state-of-the-art on real data

model_family: logistic regression (radiomics-based, best of eight ML algorithms compared)
patient_population: 110 FGR cases and 158 healthy controls, 28-37 weeks gestation, two hospital campuses
clinical_problem: predicting fetal growth restriction using placental MRI radiomics combined with clinical factors
model_description: Combines radiomics features extracted from sagittal T2-weighted placental MRI with clinical variables as input to a logistic-regression-based model (best of eight ML algorithms tested), outputting a nomogram-based prediction of fetal growth restriction.
title: A machine learning model based on placental magnetic resonance imaging and clinical factors to predict fetal growth restriction.
study_design: retrospective case-control study with internal and external validation
headline_result: AUC 0.941 training, 0.899 internal test, 0.861 external test

patient_population: 62 patients aged 36-60 months (41 DMD, 21 BMD)
clinical_problem: Can MRI radiomics distinguish early-stage Duchenne from Becker muscular dystrophy in young children?
model_description: Radiomic features extracted from Dixon-sequence MRI (automatically segmented by a deep learning method) are used in machine learning classifiers to distinguish Duchenne from Becker muscular dystrophy in early-stage disease.
title: Machine learning-based radiomics using MRI to differentiate early-stage Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophy in children.
headline_result: ML models: accuracy 81.2-90.6% vs radiologists 69.4%

patient_population: 1014 whole-body FDG-PET/CT images (public, training); validated on pediatric osteosarcoma/neuroblastoma (n=13), pediatric solid tumor (n=14) and adult pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma (n=40) cohorts
clinical_problem: segmenting cancer lesions on whole-body FDG PET/CT regardless of tumor type or site
model_description: A 3D nnU-Net-based deep learning model, trained on a public whole-body FDG-PET/CT dataset, automatically segments cancer lesions agnostic to tumor type or site, and is evaluated on separate pediatric and adult tumor cohorts.
title: Development and validation of pan-cancer lesion segmentation AI-model for whole-body 18F-FDG PET/CT in diverse clinical cohorts.
study_design: retrospective multi-cohort model development and external validation
dataset_size: 1014 whole-body PET/CT (public); 13 osteosarcoma/neuroblastoma, 14 pediatric solid tumor, 40 adult pheochromocytoma cohorts
headline_result: Lesion-level sensitivity/Dice: 97.83%/0.73 (pediatric solid tumor), 40.15%/0.36 (osteosarcoma/neuroblastoma), 78.37%/0.50 (adult pheochromocytoma)

patient_population: pregnant women in Ghana, Kenya, and South Africa (formative qualitative/quantitative study)
clinical_problem: Validating and implementing an AI-based ultrasound tool for gestational age estimation as part of a broader pre-eclampsia risk-screening and prevention program in resource-limited settings
model_description: As part of the formative phase of the PEARLS trial, an artificial-intelligence ultrasound tool for estimating gestational age will be validated and implemented alongside a pre-eclampsia risk-screening algorithm; this protocol paper describes qualitative and quantitative feasibility research (interviews, focus groups, surveys) rather than the AI tool's technical performance.
title: Formative research to optimize pre-eclampsia risk-screening and prevention (PEARLS): study protocol.
study_design: mixed-methods formative research study protocol (trial registration PACTR202403785563823)

patient_population: 35 patients (ages 5-15) for training; validated on 54 children with CP (ages 7-16) and an independent set of 36 children with congenital/acquired brain anatomy distortions (ages 1-17)
clinical_problem: Automatically quantify lesion-free brain volumes in children with unilateral cerebral palsy to relate brain structure to motor and visual outcomes
model_description: Trains deep learning models on T1-weighted and FLAIR MRI, using an automatic label generation workflow, to segment brain structures and lesions and compute lesion-free brain and regional volumes, correlated with lesion extent and motor/visual outcomes.
title: Automatic brain quantification in children with unilateral cerebral palsy.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development with independent external validation cohort
dataset_size: 35 training patients; 54 validation children with CP; independent set of 36 children with brain anatomy distortions
headline_result: Reduced affected-hemisphere volumes correlated with lesion extent (p<0.05); regional (e.g., thalamic) lesion-free volumes linked to motor/visual outcomes (p<0.05)

model_family: YOLOv8n object detection with ResNet18 classification
patient_population: pediatric outpatients aged 2-12 years with respiratory obstruction symptoms
clinical_problem: diagnosing severity of tonsillar and adenoid hypertrophy from lateral nasopharyngeal X-rays in children
model_description: Input: lateral nasopharyngeal X-rays; output: YOLOv8n detection of tonsil/adenoid regions followed by CNN classification of hypertrophy severity.
title: Optimized deep learning model for diagnosing tonsil and adenoid hypertrophy through X-rays.
dataset_size: 819 training/validation images, 484 test images (1,006 collected initially)

patient_population: public dynamic renal scintigraphy database (pediatric)
clinical_problem: Recover image quality in low-dose pediatric renal scintigraphy to allow reduced radiation exposure
model_description: Applies denoising neural networks (DnCNN, UDnCNN, DUDnCNN, AttnGAN) to simulated half-dose (50% counts) pediatric renal scintigraphy images to restore image quality comparable to full-dose acquisitions.
title: Recovering Image Quality in Low-Dose Pediatric Renal Scintigraphy Using Deep Learning.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development study using a public dataset
headline_result: UDnCNN achieved the best balance of SNR and MS-SSIM among four networks; half-dose reconstructed images comparable to full-dose

model_family: random forest and logistic regression on automated MRI volumetry (Infant FreeSurfer)
patient_population: 150 very low birth weight (<1500 g) preterm infants assessed at term-equivalent age MRI and 18-24 months corrected age
clinical_problem: predicting long-term psychomotor and mental developmental outcomes in very-low-birth-weight preterm infants from term-equivalent-age brain MRI volumetry
model_description: Input: automated brain volumetry (Infant FreeSurfer) and diffusion tensor imaging metrics from term-equivalent-age MRI plus clinical data; output: random forest/logistic regression prediction of low Psychomotor and Mental Development Index at 18-24 months.
title: Development and Validation of an MRI-Based Brain Volumetry Model Predicting Poor Psychomotor Outcomes in Preterm Neonates.
study_design: retrospective model development and validation study
headline_result: AUROC 0.9297 (Psychomotor Development Index) and 0.7755 (Mental Development Index) using combined clinical and MRI volumetry model

patient_population: 219 pediatric PBM patients (median age 2.2-3.4 years)
clinical_problem: Can a combined imaging and pathology AI model predict a molecular marker of cancer risk (COX-2) in children with pancreaticobiliary maljunction?
model_description: A deep learning radiopathomics model integrates CT radiomics/deep-learning imaging features with histopathology image features to predict biliary COX-2 expression in children with pancreaticobiliary maljunction.
title: A novel deep learning radiopathomics model for predicting carcinogenesis promotor cyclooxygenase-2 expression in common bile duct in children with pancreaticobiliary maljunction: a multicenter study.
study_design: retrospective multicenter model development and external validation
headline_result: AUC 0.851 (internal test), 0.841 (external test)

patient_population: 461 infants (cross-sectional), 41 infants with longitudinal scans
clinical_problem: Can individual infants be identified from morphological 'fingerprints' of their brain MRI, and do these predict later neurodevelopment?
model_description: A deep learning framework projects 3D cortical morphology (thickness, curvature, sulcal depth) onto 2D maps via quasi-conformal mapping and uses ResNet18 with contrastive learning to identify individual infants from brain MRI and relate morphological patterns to later cognitive/behavioral development.
title: Revealing morphological fingerprints in perinatal brains using quasi-conformal mapping: occurrence and neurodevelopmental implications.
headline_result: Top1 accuracy 85.90%, Top5 accuracy 92.20% for individual identification

patient_population: 1,891 subjects (infants) from two hospitals in Korea
clinical_problem: Automatically evaluate the scan quality of pelvic ultrasound images used to diagnose developmental dysplasia of the hip by scoring five anatomical landmarks
model_description: Uses an ensemble of transfer-learning CNN models to score the quality/visibility of five anatomical landmarks on pelvic ultrasound images for DDH screening, with Grad-CAM verification and an accelerated sequence method for real-time use.
title: Automated scan quality evaluation for DDH using transfer learning: Development of a novel ensemble system.
headline_result: Kappa >=0.6 for all models; AUC 0.89 for classifying standard images; processing time 0.20-0.35 s/image

patient_population: term-born neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy
clinical_problem: segmenting small, diffuse hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy lesions on neonatal brain MRI
model_description: ParadiseNet incorporates global-local learning, progressive uncertainty learning and self-evolution learning modules, inspired by clinical interpretation, to segment small and diffuse HIE lesions on neonatal brain MRI.
title: PARADISE: Personalized and regional adaptation for HIE disease identification and segmentation.
headline_result: Over 4% Dice and 6% NSD improvement for small (<1%) lesions versus U-Net and other general segmentation algorithms

clinical_problem: What multiparametric MRI features and analysis methods can predict cognitive impairment risk in children with brain tumors?
model_description: Review of multiparametric MRI predictors of cognitive impairment in pediatric brain tumors, including discussion of how radiomics and machine learning could integrate complex multifactorial imaging data for cognitive-outcome prediction.
title: Radiological Predictors of Cognitive Impairment in Paediatric Brain Tumours Using Multiparametric Magnetic Resonance Imaging: A Review of Current Practice, Challenges and Future Directions.

patient_population: 81 children diagnosed with medulloblastoma
clinical_problem: predicting prognosis (overall survival) of pediatric medulloblastoma using MRI radiomics combined with clinical features
model_description: Input: radiomics features extracted from T1-weighted MRI tumor regions of interest plus clinical/molecular features; output: risk stratification and survival prediction via a combined clinical-radiomics model.
title: Application of Radiomics in Predicting the Prognosis of Medulloblastoma in Children.
headline_result: clinical-radiomics model C-index 0.860 vs. radiomics-only 0.762 vs. clinical-only 0.806

patient_population: 1682 patients with scoliosis; internal testing set of 87 adolescents (7-16y) and 26 older adults (>=60y)
clinical_problem: Can an automated deep learning tool accurately measure spinal parameters (Cobb angle and others) for scoliosis diagnosis, in both adolescents and older adults?
model_description: A CNN pipeline (coarse segmentation, landmark localization, fine segmentation) automatically measures Cobb angle, T1 tilt, coronal balance, clavicular angle, shoulder height, T5-T12 Cobb angle, and sagittal balance from spinal radiographs.
title: Automated Measurements of Spinal Parameters for Scoliosis Using Deep Learning.
dataset_size: 1682 patients; internal testing 87 adolescents, 26 older adults
headline_result: Adolescent subgroup MAE 0.26-0.51 mm/degree on AP radiographs; Dice >0.90

patient_population: 1,000 pediatric patients referred for head shape concerns (2019-2023); 663 conventional, 337 AI-assisted encounters, propensity matched
clinical_problem: Assess whether AI-generated craniometric analysis changes healthcare resource utilization (radiography ordering, physical therapy, orthotic therapy, specialist follow-up) in neonates evaluated for head shape deformities
model_description: An AI tool generates craniometric measurements and interpretations for neonatal head shape (e.g., distinguishing craniosynostosis from benign deformities), reviewed by providers during clinical encounters; this study compares downstream healthcare resource utilization between AI-reviewed and conventional encounters.
title: Healthcare resource utilization for the management of neonatal head shape deformities: a propensity-matched analysis of AI-assisted and conventional approaches.
study_design: retrospective propensity-matched cohort study of clinical workflow
headline_result: AI review associated with increased orthotic therapy use (31.5% vs 38.6%, p=0.0132); no significant change in radiology ordering rates; all AI craniosynostosis-vs-benign diagnoses congruent with final diagnosis

patient_population: 94 adolescents with MDD and 78 healthy adolescent controls
clinical_problem: Classify adolescents with major depressive disorder from healthy adolescents using whole-brain resting-state functional connectivity as a potential imaging biomarker
model_description: Uses resting-state fMRI functional connectivity between 90 brain regions of interest as input features to a linear support vector machine classifier, which outputs a diagnostic classification of adolescent MDD versus healthy control.
title: Multivariate Classification of Adolescent Major Depressive Disorder Using Whole-brain Functional Connectivity.
dataset_size: 94 adolescents with MDD, 78 healthy adolescent controls
headline_result: Linear SVM classification accuracy 69.18%

patient_population: Children with pediatric low-grade glioma
clinical_problem: Improving both explainability and accuracy of genetic-marker classification for pediatric low-grade glioma, the most common pediatric brain tumor, from MRI
model_description: A multimodal contrastive-learning architecture jointly trains on 3D brain MRI and radiology reports (plus tumor location) to learn MRI representations that are then used to classify pediatric low-grade glioma genetic markers, with attention maps for explainability
title: Multimodal contrastive learning for enhanced explainability in pediatric brain tumor molecular diagnosis.
headline_result: 87.7% classification performance; 31.1% Dice overlap between model attention maps and manual tumor segmentation

patient_population: 500 X-ray images from a pediatric clinic in China
clinical_problem: measuring areal bone mineral density in children from a single hand/forearm X-ray as an alternative to DXA
model_description: Deep learning automatically locates and segments regions of interest and an equivalent step phantom on routine hand/forearm X-rays, then estimates areal bone mineral density after correcting for soft-tissue effects using a fitted calibration curve, compared against DXA.
journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
title: An automatic deep learning-based bone mineral density measurement method using X-ray images of children.
study_design: retrospective method development and validation against DXA
headline_result: Correlation coefficient 0.836 versus DXA-based areal BMD

patient_population: 208 typically developing children and 78 ambulant children with cerebral palsy, ages 5-15
clinical_problem: establishing reference curves for pediatric lower-leg muscle volumes and identifying small-for-age muscles in children with cerebral palsy
model_description: a deep learning model takes MRI of the lower leg as input and outputs automatic segmentation of 10 muscles, used to build quantile-regression reference curves for muscle volume by age
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
title: Childhood muscle growth: Reference curves for lower leg muscle volumes and their clinical application in cerebral palsy.
study_design: cross-sectional reference-curve development study with clinical application
headline_result: 56% of the cerebral palsy cohort had small-for-age total leg muscle volume; 80% had at least one small-for-age muscle

patient_population: 147 infants with cholestasis (112 training, 35 external validation) from 2 sites
clinical_problem: Can MRCP radiomics distinguish biliary atresia from other causes of infant cholestasis when the extrahepatic bile duct cannot be seen on imaging?
model_description: Radiomics features extracted from MRCP images, combined with clinical factors, are used in a K-nearest neighbors-based nomogram to distinguish biliary atresia from cytomegalovirus infection or idiopathic neonatal hepatitis when the extrahepatic biliary tree is not visualized.
title: Identification of Biliary Atresia in Infantile Cholestasis: Integrating Radiomics With MRCP for Unobservable Extrahepatic Biliary Systems.
study_design: retrospective two-site model development and external validation study
headline_result: Nomogram AUC 0.981 (training), 0.913 (external validation)

patient_population: 567 clinical validation cases scanned by 4 radiologists; large multicenter internal training dataset
clinical_problem: automated quality auditing of first-trimester fetal ultrasound standard-plane images to support consistent image quality control and radiologist feedback
model_description: Uses a YOLOv7-based structure detection network plus a multi-branch image-quality regression network to take first-trimester fetal ultrasound images as input and output plane/structure quality scores and standard/non-standard classification, providing feedback to sonographers.
title: Effectiveness and clinical impact of using deep learning for first-trimester fetal ultrasound image quality auditing.
study_design: multicenter deep learning model development and clinical validation study
dataset_size: 567 clinical validation cases + large multicenter internal training set
headline_result: Internal test accuracy/precision/recall/F1 ~0.84-0.91; Cohen's kappa >0.8 vs experts; standard-image rate increased 7.7% (junior radiologists) after feedback

model_family: CNN (U-Net variants: nnU-Net, attention U-Net, 2.5D U-Net; commercial LimbusAI)
body_region: whole body (organs at risk for craniospinal irradiation)
patient_population: 142 pediatric patients for training/validation (St. Jude) plus 16 test scans (McGill)
clinical_problem: comparing deep-learning auto-segmentation approaches (commercial, out-of-the-box, in-house) for delineating organs at risk in pediatric craniospinal irradiation planning
model_description: Compares three deep-learning auto-segmentation approaches — a commercial product (LimbusAI), an out-of-the-box nnU-Net, and in-house U-Net variants (basic, attention, 2.5D) — that take pediatric CT scans as input and output contours of 18 organs at risk for craniospinal irradiation planning.
release_evidence: LimbusAI v1.7 is a commercial auto-segmentation product; nnU-Net is a publicly available open-source segmentation framework used for benchmarking
title: Trade-off of different deep learning-based auto-segmentation approaches for treatment planning of pediatric craniospinal irradiation autocontouring of OARs for pediatric CSI.
study_design: retrospective multi-institutional comparative deep-learning segmentation study
dataset_size: 142 pediatric CT scans (115 train/27 validation, St. Jude) + 16 test (McGill)
headline_result: Model-PMC-UMCU DSC >0.95 for 5/9 OARs; LimbusAI esophagus DSC <0.5 in younger patients

model_family: random forest (best of eight compared machine learning algorithms)
patient_population: women stratified into planned cesarean, emergency cesarean due to CPD-related dystocia, and vaginal delivery groups
clinical_problem: predicting prenatal risk of cephalopelvic disproportion-related dystocia using maternal and fetal (sonographic) parameters
model_description: Input: 21 selected maternal and fetal parameters, including sonographic estimated fetal weight, head circumference, abdominal circumference, biparietal diameter, and femur length; output: random forest prediction of cephalopelvic disproportion-related dystocia risk, deployed as a web-based tool.
journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
title: A machine learning model for prenatal risk prediction of cephalopelvic disproportion-related dystocia: A retrospective study.
headline_result: random forest model AUC 0.824 (training), 0.723 in independent validation

model_family: state space model (visual state space / evidential deep learning)
patient_population: collected fetal echocardiography image dataset
clinical_problem: Can an efficient AI model help sonographers at primary hospitals recognize standard views in fetal echocardiography to improve detection of congenital heart disease?
model_description: An efficient visual state-space model trained with evidential learning classifies eight standard views of fetal echocardiography, aiming to assist sonographers with less experience at primary hospitals.
title: An efficient network with state space model under evidential training for fetal echocardiography standard view recognition.
headline_result: Accuracy 99.32%, F1-score 99.29% for standard-view classification

patient_population: 12,118 training and 2,996 test sagittal knee MR images from children, adolescents, and adults
clinical_problem: Generate synthetic T2*-weighted gradient echo knee MRI images (useful for cartilage, synovial blooming, chondrocalcinosis, and pediatric physis assessment) from routinely acquired fat-suppressed intermediate-weighted images, avoiding an extra sequence
model_description: A CycleGAN model trained on fat-suppressed intermediate-weighted knee MRI images generates synthetic T2*-weighted gradient echo images without requiring an additional acquisition, evaluated for diagnostic interchangeability and image quality.
release_evidence: Code, model and a standalone executable file are provided on github.
title: Generating Synthetic T2*-Weighted Gradient Echo Images of the Knee with an Open-source Deep Learning Model.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and validation study
headline_result: Median NRMSE 0.5, PSNR 17.4, SSIM 0.5; ICC >0.95 for diagnostic interchangeability across findings

patient_population: 189 adolescents: 54 MDD with childhood maltreatment, 45 MDD without, 33 healthy controls with maltreatment, 57 healthy controls without
clinical_problem: Investigate how childhood maltreatment affects neurovascular coupling in adolescent depression and use these imaging features to classify MDD
model_description: Uses multimodal MRI-derived cerebral blood flow, functional connectivity strength, and amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation measures (integrated as neurovascular coupling ratios) as input features to a support vector machine classifier distinguishing adolescents with MDD.
title: Neural effect of childhood maltreatment on neurovascular coupling in adolescent depression.
headline_result: Integration of NVC ratio, CBF, and neuronal activity yielded robust classification performance distinguishing MDD adolescents (no single AUC/accuracy number given)

model_family: deep learning with 2.5D slicing for uncertainty-aware brain age estimation
patient_population: 11 public MRI datasets (N=6,327) spanning children through older adults, with a subgroup analysis in adolescents with ADHD
clinical_problem: estimating brain age with uncertainty quantification from MRI, applied to detect accelerated brain aging in adolescents with ADHD
model_description: Input: 2.5D-sliced structural brain MRI; output: brain age estimate with an accompanying uncertainty score from a spectral-normalized neural Gaussian process, used to detect accelerated brain aging in ADHD.
title: Enhancing brain age estimation under uncertainty: A spectral-normalized neural gaussian process approach utilizing 2.5D slicing.
headline_result: MAE 2.95 years on the main dataset, MAE 3.47 years on independent validation; uncertainty adjustment increased effect size for accelerated brain aging in ADHD adolescents by 38%

patient_population: 167 and 71 fetal datasets for training two networks; evaluated retrospectively in 10 datasets and prospectively in 7 fetal subjects (36-39 weeks gestation)
clinical_problem: Automate real-time planning of phase-contrast flow imaging sequences for fetal cardiovascular MRI to widen access to fetal flow imaging
model_description: Two deep learning networks localize the fetal body and detect cardiac landmarks (descending aorta, spine, umbilical vein) on a coronal whole-uterus MRI scan to automatically plan 2D phase-contrast flow imaging in real time, compared against manual planning.
journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
title: Automatic flow planning for fetal cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development with prospective feasibility evaluation
dataset_size: 167 + 71 fetal training datasets; 10 retrospective + 7 prospective evaluation cases
headline_result: Fetal body localization Dice 0.94+-0.05; cardiac landmark errors 4.3-5.8mm; indexed flow measurements differed by -1.8% (range -14.2% to 14.9%) vs manual planning; successful in 6/7 prospective cases

model_family: logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine (radiomics)
patient_population: 165 children with adenovirus pneumonia (70 with BO, 95 without)
clinical_problem: Can CT radiomics combined with clinical data predict which children with adenovirus pneumonia will develop post-infectious bronchiolitis obliterans?
model_description: Radiomic features from baseline chest CT lesions, combined with clinical parameters, are used in logistic regression, random forest, and SVM models to predict bronchiolitis obliterans after adenovirus pneumonia in children.
title: Computed tomography-based radiomic features combined with clinical parameters for predicting post-infectious bronchiolitis obliterans in children with adenovirus pneumonia: a retrospective study.
headline_result: Testing group AUCs: LR 0.890, RF 0.859, SVM 0.885

model_family: LASSO regression / radiomics-based logistic regression models
patient_population: 433 women with singleton pregnancies (208 PAS, 225 non-PAS; 80 PPH-positive, 353 PPH-negative)
clinical_problem: Predicting placenta accreta spectrum and high postpartum hemorrhage risk before delivery from T2-weighted MRI radiomics
model_description: Radiomic features extracted from T2-weighted MRI are selected via Pearson correlation and LASSO regression and combined with clinical risk factors in nomogram-based clinical-radiomics models predicting placenta accreta spectrum and postpartum hemorrhage risk.
title: Predicting placenta accreta spectrum and high postpartum hemorrhage risk using radiomics from T2-weighted MRI.
study_design: retrospective single-institution model development with internal train/test split
headline_result: clinical-radiomics model AUC 0.918 (training)/0.885 (test) for PAS; AUC 0.918 (training)/0.905 (test) for PPH

patient_population: 21 children, median age 7 years (range 1.5-15.8 years)
clinical_problem: whether deep learning-based denoising reconstruction improves image quality and shortens scan time in pediatric body MRI
model_description: a deep learning denoising reconstruction technique takes radially sampled (PROPELLER) body MRI k-space data as input and outputs a denoised image, compared to conventional reconstruction
title: Deep learning-based denoising image reconstruction of body magnetic resonance imaging in children.
headline_result: SNR/CNR significantly higher with DL reconstruction (P<0.001); scan time per slice reduced from 6.3s to 4.8s (T1) and 5.6s to 4.2s (T2)

model_family: ResNet50-based deep learning combined with radiomics (Pyradiomics) in a nomogram
patient_population: 180 children with pancreaticobiliary maljunction
clinical_problem: noninvasively predicting hepatocyte CK7 status and cholestasis progression in children with pancreaticobiliary maljunction using MRI
model_description: Input: preoperative MRI processed with pretrained ResNet50 and Pyradiomics feature extraction plus clinical features; output: deep learning radiomics nomogram predicting hepatocyte CK7 expression status and cholestasis progression.
title: A magnetic resonance image-based deep learning radiomics nomogram for hepatocyte cytokeratin 7 expression: application to predict cholestasis progression in children with pancreaticobiliary maljunction.
headline_result: deep learning radiomics nomogram AUC 0.95 in validation cohort (deep learning signature AUC 0.92 vs. radiomics signature AUC 0.81)

patient_population: pediatric brain MRIs (883 from a public dataset and 396 from the Preschool MRI dataset) drawn from a 413-image, 56-disorder database
clinical_problem: using deep learning-based brain MRI phenotyping to identify structural brain malformations and their associated rare genetic disorders
model_description: Input: brain MRI encoded via ResNet-50 transfer learning (pretrained for age prediction) into a Clinical Brain Phenotype Space feature vector; output: phenotypic-similarity-based identification of structural brain malformations (e.g., Dandy-Walker malformation) and associated rare disorders.
title: P253 Next-generation phenotyping facilitates the identification of structural brain malformations in rare disorders through computational brain MRI analysis.
study_design: methods development and feasibility study (conference abstract)
dataset_size: 413 brain MRI images across 56 disorders; pediatric subset of 883+396 MRIs
headline_result: Dandy-Walker malformation and Ogden syndrome each formed distinct, separable clusters from controls via leave-one-out cross-validation (no explicit accuracy percentage given)

model_family: commercially available deep learning fracture detection software
patient_population: 1,672 radiographs of children under 18 (median age 10.9 years) from a tertiary pediatric emergency department, in a consecutive real-life cohort and a selected medicolegal cohort
clinical_problem: whether a bought AI tool actually helps the inexperienced physician working nights in a pediatric emergency department
model_description: Two things make this the most useful of the fracture-AI studies for a department. It uses a consecutive real-life cohort rather than a balanced set, and it separately assembles the fractures that generate medicolegal claims, where the tool caught every proximal tibial fracture but only 68% of radial condyle fractures. The reader gain was modest, and in 2% of cases residents talked themselves out of a correct diagnosis because of the AI.
release_evidence: a commercially available, deep learning-based software
title: Real-life benefit of artificial intelligence-based fracture detection in a pediatric emergency department.
study_design: retrospective reader study in a real-life cohort
dataset_size: 1,672 radiographs, three pediatric residents as readers
headline_result: stand-alone sensitivity 92%, specificity 83%; resident accuracy rose from 88% to 90% with AI, and in 2% of cases readers discarded a correct diagnosis after seeing the AI output

patient_population: 46 consecutive pediatric and neonatal chest/abdomen radiograph cases
clinical_problem: Improve image quality of pediatric and neonatal chest and abdominal radiographs via AI-based noise reduction to compensate for image degradation
model_description: Applies Canon's Intelligent NR AI-based noise reduction algorithm to pediatric and neonatal chest/abdominal radiographs, compared against conventional noise reduction and scored by three radiologists using a 4-point visual grading scale.
release_evidence: AI-based noise reduction processing (Intelligent NR, Canon Inc.)
title: Improving image quality on pediatric and neonatal radiography using AI-based compensation for image degradation.
headline_result: Significantly higher image quality scores with AI-based noise reduction vs conventional (p<0.05)

patient_population: 61 pediatric participants ages 6-18: 20 with chronic spinal cord injury, 41 typically developing, single center
clinical_problem: detecting and grading the severity of pediatric spinal cord injury from structural MRI measurements
model_description: Deep convolutional neural networks classify children as having spinal cord injury or being typically developing, and predict ASIA Impairment Scale category, using cross-sectional area and width measurements extracted from T2-weighted MRI at every vertebral level plus age and height.
title: Severity Classification of Pediatric Spinal Cord Injuries Using Structural MRI Measures and Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Analysis across All Vertebral Levels.
headline_result: 96.59% accuracy distinguishing SCI from typically developing; 94.92% accuracy for AIS category classification

patient_population: fetuses (review, no single cohort)
clinical_problem: using AI-enhanced 4D ultrasound to detect fetal anomalies, neurodevelopmental markers and congenital heart defects, linking fetal programming to adult disease risk
model_description: A narrative review synthesizing AI-enhanced 4D ultrasound applications for detecting fetal anomalies, neurodevelopmental markers and congenital heart defects, and discussing links to Barker's Hypothesis of fetal origins of adult disease.
title: Fetal origins of adult disease: transforming prenatal care by integrating Barker's Hypothesis with AI-driven 4D ultrasound.

patient_population: two real-world infant hip ultrasound datasets (DDH)
clinical_problem: Can an AI model accurately detect anatomical landmarks on infant hip ultrasound to support Graf-method DDH diagnosis?
model_description: A topological graph convolutional network guided improved Conformer (TGCN-ICF) detects anatomical landmarks on hip ultrasound images by jointly modeling image features and the spatial relationships among landmarks, supporting Graf-method DDH assessment.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: Topological GCN Guided Improved Conformer for Detection of Hip Landmarks From Ultrasound Images.
study_design: retrospective method development and benchmark comparison
headline_result: Outperformed all compared algorithms (specific metric not given in abstract)

model_family: deep learning with a feature decoupling transformer
patient_population: fetal 3D MRI (proposed benchmark dataset)
clinical_problem: automated landmark detection in the fetal cerebellum on 3D MRI to assess fetal brain development
model_description: Input: 3D fetal brain MRI; output: cerebellum anatomical landmark coordinates from a shared-encoder network with landmark-regression and anatomical pseudo-label segmentation decoders.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: Fetal Cerebellum Landmark Detection Based on 3D MRI: Method and Benchmark.
study_design: methods development study with a new benchmark

model_family: support vector machine (best of random forest, logistic regression, SVM)
patient_population: 802 children with hydronephrosis
clinical_problem: Predicting impaired differential renal function (below 40%) in children with unilateral hydronephrosis from urinary tract ultrasound parameters, to guide surgical decision-making without requiring a renogram
model_description: Machine-learning models (random forest, logistic regression, support vector machine) use urinary tract ultrasound parameters, including renal pelvis diameter, calyx dilation and renal length ratio, plus patient age, to predict differential renal function below 40% in children with unilateral hydronephrosis.
title: Deep Learning Algorithms to Predict Differential Renal Function <40% in Unilateral Hydronephrosis Based on Key Parameters of Urinary Tract Ultrasound.
headline_result: SVM AUROC 0.941, sensitivity 90.32%, specificity 81.03%

model_family: numerical phantom / simulation (not a learned model per se)
patient_population: 78 simulated developing human fetal brains, 20.0-34.8 weeks gestational age
clinical_problem: Can a synthetic fetal brain MRI dataset support development of AI post-processing and segmentation tools when real fetal MRI data are scarce?
model_description: The FaBiAN numerical phantom simulates realistic T2-weighted fetal brain MRI series (594 low-resolution 2D series across 78 simulated fetal brains, healthy and pathological), intended to support development of AI post-processing and segmentation tools.
title: A dataset of synthetic, maturation-informed magnetic resonance images of the human fetal brain.
study_design: synthetic dataset generation and validation study

model_family: machine learning and deep learning models (architectures not specified)
patient_population: pediatric patients with congenital craniofacial anomalies, including prenatal detection through postoperative care
clinical_problem: diagnosis and surgical planning for congenital craniofacial anomalies (craniosynostosis, cleft lip and palate, craniofacial microsomia, microtia)
