title: Machine learning for classification of pediatric bipolar disorder with and without psychotic symptoms based on thalamic subregional structural volume.

model_family: CNN (U-Net++ with ResNet-34 backbone, attention mechanism)
patient_population: large fetal ultrasound image collection (size not specified)
clinical_problem: automated, explainable segmentation of fetal ultrasound images to standardize evaluation of fetal development
model_description: A U-Net++ segmentation model with ResNet-34 backbone and attention mechanisms takes fetal ultrasound images as input and outputs segmentation masks of fetal anatomical structures, with Grad-CAM++ providing explainable visualizations of model decisions.
title: Advancing prenatal healthcare by explainable AI enhanced fetal ultrasound image segmentation using U-Net++ with attention mechanisms.
headline_result: Dice coefficient 97.52%, IoU 95.15%, Hausdorff distance 3.91 mm

patient_population: 207 included publications reviewing obstetric AI models (2019-2024)
clinical_problem: reviewing the current state of AI model development in obstetrics, including ultrasound-based imaging applications and risk-prediction models for pregnancy complications
model_description: Narrative review of 207 obstetric AI publications, describing trends in AI applications including ultrasound imaging analysis and risk prediction for preterm birth, preeclampsia and gestational diabetes.
title: Current State of Artificial Intelligence Model Development in Obstetrics.

model_family: transformer (Vision Transformer) with multi-feature fusion / YOLOv8
patient_population: 1,688 posterior mid-sagittal fetal ultrasound images (occiput-spine angle dataset)
clinical_problem: Improving the accuracy and ease of assessing fetal head flexion (occiput-spine angle) during labor, which is technically difficult for less experienced ultrasound operators.
model_description: OSAM-NET uses YOLOv8 to localize the fetal occiput and spine on ultrasound and a Vision Transformer to extract global image features, fusing the geometric and global information via multi-head self-attention to output a predicted occiput-spine angle for assessing fetal head flexion.
journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
title: OSAM-NET: A multi-feature fusion model for measuring fetal head flexion during labor with transformer multi-head self-attention.
study_design: model development with prospective test-set validation
headline_result: R² improved by nearly 13% over comparison models; intraclass correlation coefficient averaged 0.89 versus ultrasound experts; validated on a prospective test dataset

patient_population: fetuses from five hospital sites in UK and Australia; planned 16,400 retrospective and prospective ultrasound scans (13,000 normal + 1,000 CHD retrospective; 2,000 normal + 400 CHD prospective)
clinical_problem: prenatal detection of congenital heart defects using deep learning-based analysis of fetal echocardiography images and videos, aimed at nonspecialist/low-resource settings
model_description: Input (planned): retrospective and prospective fetal echocardiography still images and 10-second video sweeps; output (planned): classification distinguishing normal fetal hearts from those with congenital heart defects and recognition of specific CHD types, via deep learning/AI models.
release_evidence: study protocol; models to be built, trained and validated; currently 'not accurate enough for practical clinical use'
title: Prenatal detection of congenital heart defects using the deep learning-based image and video analysis: protocol for Clinical Artificial Intelligence in Fetal Echocardiography (CAIFE), an international multicentre multidisciplinary study.
study_design: protocol for a prospective international multicentre multidisciplinary study
dataset_size: planned 16,400 retrospective and prospective ultrasound scans across 5 hospital sites

patient_population: Pediatric patients with posterior fossa tumors, synthesized across six included studies
clinical_problem: Detecting and classifying pediatric posterior fossa astrocytomas using AI-assisted imaging analysis
model_description: Systematic review (PRISMA) of six studies evaluating neural-network-based AI models applied to pediatric brain MRI to detect and classify posterior fossa astrocytomas.
title: Diagnostic Performance of Neural Network-Based Artificial Intelligence in the Detection and Classification of Pediatric Astrocytoma: A Systematic Review.
headline_result: AUROC >0.99, classification accuracy up to 95% (pooled across included studies)

model_family: logistic regression and voting classifier ensemble (radiomics)
patient_population: 67 pediatric patients with peripheral neuroblastic tumors
clinical_problem: Predicting pathological subtype of peripheral neuroblastic tumors non-invasively from 123I-MIBG SPECT/CT imaging, to help guide treatment planning and surgical decisions.
model_description: Radiomic features (1702 extracted) from 123I-MIBG SPECT/CT images are combined with clinical features and fed into a logistic regression model and a four-algorithm voting classifier to predict the pathological subtype of peripheral neuroblastic tumors.
title: Radiomics-based prediction of pathological subtypes in peripheral neuroblastic tumors using 123I-MIBG SPECT/CT imaging: an observational study.
dataset_size: 67 pediatric patients (1702 radiomic features extracted, 7:3 train/validation split)
headline_result: Voting classifier: macro-average AUC 0.968 (training), 0.879 (test); combined clinical+radiomic logistic regression model: macro-average AUC 0.871 (training), 0.836 (test)

model_family: two commercial deep learning fracture detection algorithms
patient_population: 998 emergency musculoskeletal radiographs (585 normal, 413 abnormal) covering adults and children
clinical_problem: choosing between competing commercial fracture detection products, and knowing where both of them fail
model_description: Two marketed products on the same cases, which is the comparison a purchaser needs and vendors do not publish. They performed almost identically and agreed with each other almost perfectly, and performance was similar in adults and children. The shared weakness is the useful finding: subtle abnormalities made up about two-thirds of both algorithms' false negatives but under a fifth of their true positives.
release_evidence: compares two commercial AI algorithms, BoneView and RBfracture
title: Comparative accuracy of two commercial AI algorithms for musculoskeletal trauma detection in emergency radiographs.
headline_result: BoneView sensitivity 0.893 and specificity 0.885; RBfracture 0.872 and 0.892; no significant difference, kappa 0.81; subtle abnormalities were 66-70% of false negatives versus 18-20% of true positives (p < 0.001)

patient_population: 176 hips from 88 anteroposterior pelvic radiographs of children with cerebral palsy
clinical_problem: Automating classification of hip displacement severity (normal/risky/dislocated) in children with cerebral palsy from migration percentage on pelvic radiographs
model_description: A support vector machine classifies hip migration-percentage measurements from anteroposterior pelvic radiographs of children with cerebral palsy into normal, risky, or dislocated categories, compared against manual clinician evaluation
title: Machine learning-assisted classification of hip conditions in pediatric cerebral palsy patients using migration percentage measurements.
study_design: retrospective model development and comparison study
headline_result: Overall accuracy 92.9%, exceeding manual assessment consistency

model_family: deep learning super-resolution (accelerated parallel imaging + simultaneous multislice)
patient_population: 44 children (mean age 15±2 years, range 9-17 years, 24 boys) with painful knee conditions
clinical_problem: diagnostic performance of a fast (<5 min) deep learning super-resolution knee MRI protocol for detecting internal knee derangement in children and adolescents, validated against arthroscopy
model_description: Input: accelerated (sixfold parallel imaging, simultaneous multislice) knee MRI raw data; output: deep learning super-resolution reconstructed images in under 5 minutes, read by radiologists for structural knee abnormalities and compared against arthroscopic findings.
title: Arthroscopy-validated diagnostic performance of sub-5-min deep learning super-resolution 3T knee MRI in children and adolescents.
study_design: retrospective diagnostic accuracy study with arthroscopic reference standard and multi-reader evaluation
headline_result: AUC 0.92 (ACL tears), 0.84 (medial meniscus), 0.82 (lateral meniscus), 1.00 (discoid lateral menisci), 0.98 (MPFL tears), 0.77 (articular cartilage defects); interreader agreement κ≥0.74

patient_population: 92 children with ASD and 52 typically developing preschoolers
clinical_problem: Predicting pragmatic language ability in preschool children with autism spectrum disorder from brain structural connectivity
model_description: NBS-Predict combines network-based statistics with machine learning on diffusion-tensor-imaging-derived structural connectomes to identify dysconnected white matter subnetworks and predict pragmatic language scores in children with ASD.
title: Predicting pragmatic language abilities from brain structural MRI in preschool children with ASD by NBS-Predict.
headline_result: classification accuracy 79.4%; prediction correlation r=0.220

patient_population: Adolescents with major depressive disorder (per the study being commented on)
clinical_problem: Diagnosing major depressive disorder in adolescents using neuroimaging functional-connectivity biomarkers
model_description: Commentary/letter on a study applying support vector machine classification to resting-state fMRI functional connectivity to diagnose major depressive disorder in adolescents.
title: Unveiling the invisible: How cutting-edge neuroimaging transforms adolescent depression diagnosis.
study_design: letter / commentary on a case-control neuroimaging study
headline_result: SVM accuracy 83.91%, sensitivity 79.55%, specificity 88.37%, AUC 0.6765 (per referenced study)

patient_population: Pediatric patients from birth through childhood with hydrocephalus / ventricular abnormalities
clinical_problem: Detecting and monitoring ventricular abnormalities (hydrocephalus) from birth through childhood using imaging biomarkers
model_description: Narrative review of imaging biomarkers (Evans' index, Levene's index, Cella Media index, volumetric/diffusion MRI) and automated/AI-assisted image analysis for diagnosing and monitoring hydrocephalus in children.
title: Imaging biomarkers for detection and longitudinal monitoring of ventricular abnormalities from birth to childhood.

model_description: A brief letter/comment responding to a published review, 'Artificial Intelligence for Neuroimaging in Pediatric Cancer' (Dalboni da Rocha et al., Cancers 2025), discussing that review's coverage of AI applications in pediatric cancer neuroimaging.
title: Comment on Dalboni da Rocha et al. Artificial Intelligence for Neuroimaging in Pediatric Cancer. Cancers 2025, 17, 622.
study_design: letter / commentary on a published review

patient_population: not applicable (reply/letter)
clinical_problem: clarifying segmentation performance metrics discussed in a prior review of AI for neuroimaging in pediatric cancer
model_description: A brief author reply to a reader comment on a prior review, 'Artificial Intelligence for Neuroimaging in Pediatric Cancer,' discussing segmentation performance metrics; contains no new model or data.
title: Reply to Keles et al. Comment on "Dalboni da Rocha et al. Artificial Intelligence for Neuroimaging in Pediatric Cancer. Cancers 2025, 17, 622".

patient_population: pregnant women (scoping review of 5 included studies, 2020-2024)
clinical_problem: reviewing AI's role in predicting and improving adverse pregnancy outcomes, including via ultrasound and continuous monitoring
model_description: A scoping review of 5 studies applying machine learning (e.g., XGBoost, random forest) to predict adverse pregnancy outcomes such as preterm birth, hypertensive disorders and gestational diabetes, discussing ultrasound-based and monitoring applications and ethical issues.
title: Artificial Intelligence's Role in Improving Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes: A Scoping Review and Consideration of Ethical Issues.

patient_population: RSNA bone age X-ray image collection
clinical_problem: Estimating pediatric bone age from hand radiographs using limited labeled data
model_description: AE-BoNet uses an autoencoder for unsupervised pre-training to reconstruct hand radiographs, then a model built on the trained encoder estimates bone age.
title: AE-BoNet: A Deep Learning Method for Pediatric Bone Age Estimation using an Unsupervised Pre-Trained Model.
study_design: retrospective model development using a public dataset
headline_result: MAE 9.3 months on the RSNA dataset

patient_population: Pediatric patients with developmental dysplasia of the hip
clinical_problem: Diagnosing developmental dysplasia of the hip using AI-assisted imaging parameters
model_description: Perspective review of AI applications for measuring hip joint imaging parameters and using predictive modeling to support diagnosis and management of developmental dysplasia of the hip.
title: The role of imaging parameters in the diagnosis of developmental dysplasia of the hip based on artificial intelligence: A perspective.

patient_population: publicly available fetal ultrasound imaging datasets (not a single patient cohort)
clinical_problem: whether publicly available fetal ultrasound image datasets used to train deep-learning prenatal-diagnosis algorithms are demographically and clinically representative
model_description: Audit of publicly available fetal ultrasound datasets used to train deep-learning models, examining demographic representativeness, diversity of clinical conditions, and variability in ultrasound technology across datasets
title: Uncovering ethical biases in publicly available fetal ultrasound datasets.
study_design: bias audit of publicly available fetal ultrasound datasets

model_family: deep learning and traditional machine learning (hyperparameter-tuned)
patient_population: children with pulmonary arterial hypertension
clinical_problem: estimating pulmonary hemodynamics (mean pulmonary arterial pressure and pulmonary vascular resistance) noninvasively, avoiding cardiac catheterization
model_description: Cardiac MRI cine images are input to deep learning and traditional machine-learning models trained to classify severity profiles (low/high/extreme) of mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) and pulmonary vascular resistance index (PVRi), aiming to replace invasive catheterization for hemodynamic assessment.
journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
title: Predicting pulmonary hemodynamics in pediatric pulmonary arterial hypertension using cardiac magnetic resonance imaging and machine learning: an exploratory pilot study.
dataset_size: 40 CMR studies from children with PAH
headline_result: AUC 0.82 (mPAP), AUC 0.73 (PVRi)

patient_population: patients (children and young adults) with drug-resistant epilepsy across 27 reviewed studies
clinical_problem: using AI applied to structural MRI to detect focal cortical dysplasia for presurgical epilepsy planning, particularly in children with drug-resistant epilepsy
model_description: A systematic review of 27 studies applying machine learning and deep learning to structural MRI for detecting focal cortical dysplasia lesions, including MRI-negative cases, to guide epilepsy surgery, particularly in children.
journal: Journal of neuroradiology = Journal de neuroradiologie
title: Recent advances in sMRI and artificial intelligence for presurgical planning in focal cortical dysplasia: A systematic review.
headline_result: AI sensitivity up to 97.1%, specificity up to 84.3%; combined AI-human detection up to 87%

patient_population: Singaporean elderly participants (55-88 years) and children (4-11 years)
clinical_problem: predicting brain age and its rate of change to study links with future executive function across the lifespan
model_description: A previously published deep learning brain-age model, fine-tuned for children, predicts brain age from MRI in Singaporean elderly and pediatric participants; the rate of change in the brain-age gap is related to future executive function.
title: Rate of brain aging associates with future executive function in Asian children and older adults.
headline_result: Model directly generalized to elderly without fine-tuning; fine-tuning was necessary for children; rate of brain-age-gap change significantly associated with future executive function in both groups

model_family: deep learning (challenge-winning segmentation/detection models, various architectures)
patient_population: training data from 3 Public Health Units in Sierra Leone; validation/test from 2 PHUs in Tanzania and a European hospital
clinical_problem: automatically estimating fetal abdominal circumference from operator-agnostic blind-sweep ultrasound in low-resource settings, to enable fetal growth restriction screening without trained sonographers
model_description: Grand challenge (ACOUSLIC-AI) benchmarking AI models that take blind-sweep ultrasound video acquired by novice operators as input and output automatic fetal abdomen frame selection, segmentation, and abdominal circumference measurement.
release_evidence: the three top-performing AI models from the ACOUSLIC-AI challenge are publicly accessible
title: ACOUSLIC-AI challenge report: Fetal abdominal circumference measurement on blind-sweep ultrasound data from low-income countries.
study_design: international AI challenge/benchmark study using multi-country low-resource ultrasound data
headline_result: Top model (A2) limits of agreement for AC measurement comparable to interobserver variability reported in the literature

patient_population: sick infants imaged with a permanent-magnet 1 Tesla scanner in the NICU
clinical_problem: accelerating in-NICU neonatal brain MRI to reduce scan time
model_description: A diffusion probabilistic generative model reconstructs high-quality neonatal brain MR images from undersampled k-space data, trained on low-SNR, low-quantity real-world 1T NICU MRI data using self-supervised denoising and posterior-sample averaging, to shorten scan time while maintaining diagnostic quality.
title: Diffusion probabilistic generative models for accelerated, in-NICU permanent magnet neonatal MRI.
study_design: retrospective technical development with clinical reader study
dataset_size: clinical 1T neonatal MR image dataset (Aspect Imaging and Sha'are Zedek Medical Center); reader study on 1.5x undersampled data
headline_result: reader study suggests images reconstructed at R≈1.5 undersampling are adequate for clinical use

clinical_problem: understanding factors that influence pediatric emergency physicians' trust in AI-augmented point-of-care ultrasound (image acquisition, interpretation, workflow)
model_description: Qualitative interview study (not developing a specific AI model) exploring pediatric emergency physicians' perceptions of and trust in AI-augmented point-of-care ultrasound for image acquisition, interpretation and workflow support.
journal: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open
title: Trust of Artificial Intelligence-Augmented Point-of-Care Ultrasound Among Pediatric Emergency Physicians.
study_design: qualitative semistructured interview study using template analysis

model_family: decision tree / random forest / LightGBM (supervised ML)
patient_population: 70 patients with confirmed ovarian torsion and 73 controls without torsion on ultrasound, 2013-2023, single center
clinical_problem: diagnosing pediatric ovarian torsion using physical examination, sonographic and laboratory findings
model_description: Supervised machine learning models (decision tree, random forest, LightGBM) combine sonographic findings (ovarian size ratio, medialization, follicular ring sign, free pelvic fluid), laboratory inflammatory markers and physical exam findings to classify patients as having ovarian torsion or not.
title: An Innovative Machine Learning-Based Algorithm for Diagnosing Pediatric Ovarian Torsion.
headline_result: Decision tree model: F1 98%, accuracy 98%, specificity 100% (5-fold cross-validation)

model_family: self-supervised temporal deep learning (multistep encoder pretrained on scan-order classification)
patient_population: 715 pediatric patients with low- and high-grade glioma at three institutions
clinical_problem: predicting whether a child's brain tumor (glioma) will recur within one year from a patient's serial surveillance MRI scans
model_description: Self-supervised deep-learning model that encodes a patient's serial postoperative MRI scans (pretrained on predicting correct chronological scan order), then fine-tuned to predict 1-year tumor recurrence from historical surveillance scans
title: Longitudinal Risk Prediction for Pediatric Glioma with Temporal Deep Learning.
study_design: retrospective multi-institutional longitudinal model development and validation
headline_result: AUC 75-89% across datasets; F1 score improved up to 58.5% versus traditional approaches

model_name: MRANet and MLRANet (Multiple [Large] Receptive Attention Network)
patient_population: 203 echocardiographic studies (pediatric patients with suspected incomplete Kawasaki disease vs. pneumonia/other febrile illness)
clinical_problem: Differentiating incomplete Kawasaki disease from pneumonia and other febrile illnesses via echocardiographic detection of coronary artery abnormalities, particularly where pediatric cardiologists are unavailable.
model_description: MRANet and MLRANet use multiple (large) receptive attention layers on echocardiographic images/video to detect coronary artery abnormalities and distinguish incomplete Kawasaki disease from pneumonia, aiming to match expert pediatric cardiologist performance.
title: Expert-level differentiation of incomplete Kawasaki disease and pneumonia from echocardiography via multiple large receptive attention mechanisms.
study_design: retrospective model development and comparison study
headline_result: MLRANet: sensitivity 93.48%, specificity 66.15% for coronary artery abnormality detection, exceeding expert-level performance

patient_population: Infants aged 1 week to 1 year
clinical_problem: Generating high-resolution infant brain MRI from low-resolution scans to reduce long acquisition times that are hard for infants to tolerate.
model_description: An unsupervised single-image super-resolution model, trained using only one low-resolution image plus k-space consistency and self-supervised learning (no paired high-resolution training data required), takes a low-resolution infant brain MRI as input and outputs a higher-resolution reconstruction.
title: Unsupervised single-image super-resolution for infant brain MRI.
study_design: methods development study with quantitative and qualitative image-quality evaluation

patient_population: 189 AIS patients with Lenke 1A and 2A curves enrolled in the MIMO Clinical Trial
clinical_problem: Predicting optimal spinal fusion surgery planning parameters (instrumented vertebrae levels, rod curvature, screw density) for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
model_description: An artificial neural network multi-task learning model uses preoperative clinical and radiographic data to predict spinal fusion surgery planning parameters (upper/lower instrumented vertebrae, rod curvature, screw density), mimicking experienced spine-surgeon decision-making.
title: Neural network-based multi-task learning to assist planning of posterior spinal fusion surgery for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
study_design: retrospective model development with external validation, derived from a randomized clinical trial (MIMO)
headline_result: 82-95% accuracy for UIV, 80-100% for LIV predictions, on external validation

model_family: causal discovery analysis (CDA), a machine learning algorithm
patient_population: 194 healthy adolescent and young adult twin/sibling pairs, aged 14-24 years
clinical_problem: identifying neural and environmental factors causally related to psychosis proneness in youth
model_description: Working-memory fMRI activation is combined with sociodemographic, environmental, cognitive, and self-schema variables (37 variables total) and analyzed with causal discovery analysis, a machine-learning algorithm, to infer directional causal relationships underlying psychosis proneness.
title: Causal Discovery Analysis Reveals Insights into Psychosis Proneness, Brain Function, and Environmental Factors among Young Individuals.
study_design: cross-sectional observational study with causal discovery analysis
dataset_size: 194 adolescent/young adult twin and sibling pairs
headline_result: negative self-schema effect size 0.54; social cohesion/trust effect size -0.18; PPS to DLPFC activation effect size 0.12

patient_population: 2 pediatric patients (9-year-old and 8-year-old females) with cerebral AVM
clinical_problem: Using connectomic mapping to guide surgical planning for pediatric cerebral arteriovenous malformations by visualizing white matter tracts near the lesion.
model_description: A machine learning algorithm generates patient-specific reconstructions of white matter tracts (corticospinal tract, optic radiations) and functional networks (default mode, language) from anatomic and diffusion tensor MRI, overlaid on intraoperative neuronavigation to guide surgical corridor selection and risk assessment.
title: Novel Application of Connectomics to the Surgical Management of Pediatric Arteriovenous Malformations.
headline_result: Both patients had favorable neurologic outcomes at available follow-up

model_family: KNN, gradient boosting machine (GBM), random forest, logistic regression (radiomics ensemble)
patient_population: 247 pediatric patients with posterior fossa tumors (training n=174, validation n=73), mean age 4.88 years
clinical_problem: Predicting which children with posterior fossa tumors will develop cerebellar mutism syndrome after surgery, using presurgical imaging.
model_description: Presurgical MRI is used to extract radiomic and lesion-location (voxel distribution) features, which are combined with clinical variables (gender, tumor location, weight) and fed into KNN, GBM, random forest, and logistic regression models to predict postoperative cerebellar mutism syndrome.
title: Integrating Radiomics and Lesion Mapping for Cerebellar Mutism Syndrome Prediction.
study_design: retrospective model development and validation study
dataset_size: 247 pediatric patients (174 training, 73 validation), Beijing Children's Hospital
headline_result: AUCs of 0.84 (KNN), 0.83 (GBM), 0.81 (RF), and 0.87 (logistic regression)

patient_population: 42 fetuses (third trimester) with fetal congenital heart disease
clinical_problem: Improving image quality and reducing acquisition time for fetal cardiac MRI in prenatal congenital heart disease assessment using deep learning super-resolution.
model_description: A deep learning super-resolution framework (cineDL) reconstructs rapidly-acquired low-resolution fetal cardiac cine MRI into higher-resolution images for diagnostic use.
title: Improving Clinical Utility of Fetal Cine CMR Using Deep Learning Super-Resolution.
study_design: prospective study evaluating deep learning image reconstruction
headline_result: Faster acquisition (134±9.6s vs 252±8.8s, P<0.001); additional pathology found in 5/42 (12%) fetuses

patient_population: 6,065 preadolescents (ABCD study baseline sample)
clinical_problem: predicting preadolescent irritability severity from whole-brain task fMRI during reward anticipation
model_description: Whole-brain fMRI activity acquired during the reward-anticipation period of a monetary incentive delay task in 6,065 preadolescents from the ABCD study is input directly to a 3D convolutional neural network trained to predict parent-reported irritability severity as a continuous score. Regression activation mapping identifies brain regions, including the caudate, amygdala, parahippocampal gyrus, and hippocampus, most predictive of irritability.
title: Deep learning identification of reward-related neural substrates of preadolescent irritability: A novel 3D CNN application for fMRI.
study_design: cross-sectional multi-site cohort study, technical development
headline_result: Mean squared error 1.82; mean absolute error 0.48 ± 1.54 SD predicting irritability severity scores

patient_population: pediatric orthopedic patients across reviewed studies
clinical_problem: comprehensive review of AI applications across pediatric orthopedic subspecialties: spinal deformity classification, hip dysplasia diagnosis, fracture detection, bone age estimation, and limb-length discrepancy

title: Artificial Intelligence in Pediatric Orthopedics: A Comprehensive Review.
headline_result: >90% accuracy achieved by SVM/CNN models for spinal deformity classification and curve prediction (across reviewed studies)

clinical_problem: preoperatively predicting the angiographic classification of venous malformations in children from MRI, avoiding invasive angiography

title: MRI-based radiomics model for the preoperative prediction of classification in children with venous malformations.

title: Perivascular Space Burden in Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder Correlates With Neurodevelopmental Severity.

dataset_size: 30 infants (16 evaluable: 6 meningitis cases, 10 controls); 781 images in stage 2

journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: Bidirectional Prototype-Guided Consistency Constraint for Semi-Supervised Fetal Ultrasound Image Segmentation.
dataset_size: two fetal ultrasound datasets (plus two general medical segmentation datasets for generalization testing)
headline_result: BiPCC outperforms state-of-the-art semi-supervised fetal US segmentation methods (no single metric stated)

clinical_problem: Automated measurement of hip migration percentage and head-shaft angle on pelvic radiographs for hip surveillance in children with cerebral palsy.

title: Fully automated measurement of paediatric cerebral palsy pelvic radiographs with BoneFinder : external validation using a national surveillance database.

clinical_problem: Segmenting and classifying brain tumors, including pediatric low-grade glioma, on MRI using weakly supervised generative AI

clinical_problem: Segmenting pediatric brain tumor subregions on multiparametric MRI to support diagnosis and treatment monitoring

headline_result: Dice 0.852 (TC), 0.876 (WT), 0.764 (ET) with ensemble model after post-processing

journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
title: Automatic diagnosis of autism spectrum disorders in children through resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging with machine vision.

clinical_problem: Predicting risk stratification and prognosis of neuroblastoma in children from contrast-enhanced CT and clinical features

clinical_problem: classifying urinary tract dilation (UTD) severity from renal ultrasound

title: Dual-branch attention fusion network for pneumonia detection.
dataset_size: two publicly available chest x-ray datasets (a pediatric pneumonia dataset, and a multi-source pneumonia/COVID-19/normal dataset)
headline_result: accuracy 97.78% (binary pediatric pneumonia dataset); accuracy 97.20%, AUC 0.997 (multiclass dataset)

patient_population: 233 patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis from three medical centers
clinical_problem: Predicting curve progression risk in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis from radiographic and clinical features

title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Standard Plane Detection in Hip Ultrasound for Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip: A Novel Real-Time Deep Learning Approach.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and validation study

patient_population: 181 public medical imaging datasets surveyed; adult-trained chest radiograph models then tested on children
clinical_problem: whether children are represented at all in the data that medical imaging AI is built on
model_description: A systematic audit rather than a model. It finds children make up just under 1% of the data in 181 public imaging datasets, while most machine learning imaging conference papers build methods on exactly those datasets, and only 17% of FDA-approved medical AI devices carry a pediatric label. It then demonstrates the consequence directly: adult-trained chest radiograph models show significant age bias applied to children, with higher false positive rates in younger ones.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
title: Lack of children in public medical imaging data points to growing age bias in biomedical AI.
headline_result: children are under 1% of data in 181 public imaging datasets; adult-trained chest radiograph models show higher false positive rates in younger children

clinical_problem: placental segmentation for quantitative prenatal imaging analysis

journal: Visual computing for industry, biomedicine, and art
title: Placenta segmentation redefined: review of deep learning integration of magnetic resonance imaging and ultrasound imaging.

journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: 3D Isotropic High-Resolution Fetal Brain MRI Reconstruction From Motion Corrupted Thick Data Based on Physical-Informed Unsupervised Learning.
dataset_size: large-magnitude motion-corrupted simulation data plus clinical fetal MRI data
headline_result: outperforms current state-of-the-art fetal brain reconstruction methods (no single metric given)

patient_population: more than 12,000 expertly annotated ultrasound images across different fetal anatomical planes
clinical_problem: improving interpretation of maternal-fetal ultrasound by integrating detection and segmentation of fetal anatomical structures and detecting anomalies
model_description: Input: fetal ultrasound images across various anatomical planes; output: identification of fetal anatomical structures and detection of anomalies, using a deep learning architecture combining multi-scale CNNs and transformer layers.
title: Fetal-Net: enhancing Maternal-Fetal ultrasound interpretation through Multi-Scale convolutional neural networks and Transformers.
study_design: retrospective model development and internal evaluation
headline_result: anomaly detection precision 96.5%, accuracy 97.5%, recall 97.8%

patient_population: pediatric patients with pediatric-type diffuse low-grade gliomas (review of published literature)
clinical_problem: correlating MRI imaging features (and machine-learning-derived radiogenomic signatures) with molecular subtypes of pediatric-type low-grade gliomas to guide treatment planning and prognostication

title: Illuminating radiogenomic signatures in pediatric-type diffuse gliomas: insights into molecular, clinical, and imaging correlations. Part II: low-grade group.

clinical_problem: identifying high-risk hepatoblastoma per the CHIC risk-stratification system from contrast-enhanced CT to guide treatment

title: Identification of high-risk hepatoblastoma in the CHIC risk stratification system based on enhanced CT radiomics features.

dataset_size: 174 B-mode / 98 Doppler and multimodal image sets, retrospective cohort
headline_result: 5-fold CV accuracy 88.7% (B-mode), 85.1% (Doppler), 90% (multimodal)

clinical_problem: Automating crown-rump length measurement on first-trimester ultrasound for gestational age and growth assessment

clinical_problem: Classifying fetal head orientation (occiput position) during labor from intrapartum ultrasound
model_description: A multi-feature fusion deep learning model (YOLOv8 backbone with attention modules) classifies fetal head orientation (anterior/posterior/transverse occiput) from intrapartum ultrasound video frames of key fetal structures.

title: [A multi-feature fusion-based model for fetal orientation classification from intrapartum ultrasound videos].
headline_result: accuracy 0.984, AUC 0.984, kappa 0.974

clinical_problem: Predicting early pregnancy loss from biometric parameters automatically extracted from first-trimester ultrasound videos
model_description: A two-stage AI model (A3F-net, a modified U-Net) automatically extracts biometric parameters (gestational sac area, yolk sac diameter, crown-rump length, fetal heart rate) from early ultrasound videos, then an ensemble learning model (CatBoost) predicts risk of early pregnancy loss.
title: An AI method to predict pregnancy loss by extracting biological indicators from embryo ultrasound recordings in early pregnancy.
headline_result: CatBoost precision 98.0%, AUC 0.969

patient_population: 947 individuals aged 7-26 years across 8 centers, ADHD-200 dataset
clinical_problem: distinguishing individuals with ADHD from healthy controls and identifying affected brain networks using structural connectivity

headline_result: Accuracy 71.9%, AUC 0.74

patient_population: 82 children who underwent both echocardiography and cardiac MR within 24 hours
clinical_problem: Validating fully automated 3D echocardiography software for right ventricular volume/function quantification in children against cardiac MRI
model_description: Fully automated three-dimensional echocardiography software automatically quantifies right ventricular end-diastolic volume, end-systolic volume, and ejection fraction from echocardiogram images, validated against cardiac MRI in children.

clinical_problem: Improving image quality of pediatric abdominal MRI using deep learning image reconstruction

title: Deep learning reconstruction for improving image quality of pediatric abdomen MRI using a 3D T1 fast spoiled gradient echo acquisition.
headline_result: Image quality scores 3.8-4.6 (DL) vs 3.1-3.9 (non-DL), P<0.001; radiologists preferred DL in 32-37/38 cases

model_family: support vector machine (SVM), object oriented data analysis

clinical_problem: identifying functional connectivity correlates of autism spectrum disorder diagnosis and familial liability in toddlers
model_description: Functional connectivity MRI matrices from 24-month-old infants are analyzed with object-oriented data analysis and classified using a support vector machine to distinguish infants with high familial likelihood and an ASD diagnosis from other groups, alongside network-level connectivity enrichment analyses.

study_design: prospective cohort study, secondary neuroimaging analysis

model_description: Narrative review (Part II of a series) of AI-driven radiomics and machine-learning approaches applied to FDG PET/CT imaging across malignancies (hematologic, genitourinary, melanoma, CNS, and pediatric oncology), covering lesion segmentation, treatment-response prediction, and survival-outcome modeling.
title: Artificial Intelligence for Tumor [18F]FDG PET Imaging: Advancements and Future Trends - Part II.
study_design: narrative review (Part II of a series)

patient_population: Youth from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study
clinical_problem: Predicting future alcohol use (sipping) trajectories in youth from multimodal brain imaging and multilevel risk factors
model_description: Explainable machine learning models combine structural and functional brain MRI features (brain structure and functional connectivity) with individual, family, and environmental factors to prospectively predict early alcohol sipping trajectories in youth from the ABCD Study.
title: Integrating multilevel, multidomain and multimodal neuroimaging factors to predict early alcohol exposure trajectories using explainable AI.

patient_population: 448 subjects aged 4-18 years, 3 centers
clinical_problem: providing reliable, fast automated brain volumetric segmentation and age-specific reference growth charts for healthy children

release_evidence: The morphometric data, growth charts, and code are publicly accessible
title: A FastSurfer Database for Age-Specific Brain Volumes in Healthy Children: A Tool for Quantifying Localized and Global Brain Volume Alterations in Pediatric Patients.

patient_population: 30,121 fetuses across 15 included studies
clinical_problem: How well AI-enabled prenatal ultrasound detects fetal congenital heart defects compared to human sonographers

headline_result: Pooled sensitivity 0.89 and specificity 0.91 for normal vs. abnormal heart classification

clinical_problem: Predicting Mycoplasma pneumoniae co-infection (versus mono-infection) in children with pneumonia using CT-based radiomics to guide treatment.

title: Development and validation of a machine learning model for predicting co-infection of Mycoplasma pneumonia in pediatric patients.

headline_result: AUC 0.951 (LR radiomics model), sensitivity 0.778, specificity 0.875

clinical_problem: Classifying pediatric brain tumor type using combined diffusion MRI and proton MR spectroscopy radiomic features

headline_result: cross-validated accuracy 100% (naive Bayes)

title: Radiomic-based prognostic score for survival risk-stratification in pediatric medulloblastoma tumors: A multi-institutional study.
dataset_size: 119 MRI scans from 3 institutions (42, 47, 30 patients per site)
headline_result: C-indices of 0.7 and 0.63 for risk-group separation when training on Sites 1 and 3 and testing on Site 2 (P = .02, .013)

patient_population: 1250 children with forearm X-rays
clinical_problem: Assisting fracture assessment and treatment decision-making for pediatric forearm fractures, particularly at centers lacking pediatric orthopedic expertise

journal: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
title: Analyzing pediatric forearm X-rays for fracture analysis using machine learning.
headline_result: AUROC 0.81, TPR 0.79, TNR 0.74

clinical_problem: Detecting common chest findings (consolidation, atelectasis, nodule, cardiomegaly, mediastinal widening, pleural effusion, pneumothorax) on pediatric chest radiographs using an AI tool developed for adults
model_description: A commercially available adult chest-radiograph AI tool (Lunit INSIGHT CXR) is applied unmodified to pediatric chest radiographs to detect relevant pathologic findings, comparing performance using adult versus pediatric-optimized output thresholds.

title: Deep learning for pediatric chest x-ray diagnosis: Repurposing a commercial tool developed for adults.
headline_result: AUC 0.94 overall, AUC 0.96 in older children (7-14y)

headline_result: contractile activity detected in 19% of cases; activity increased with advancing gestational age, peaking the week before delivery

model_description: AIDA takes four geometric parameters (Angle of Progression, Head-Symphysis Distance, Midline Angle, Asynclitism Degree) measured on intrapartum ultrasound as input to machine-learning algorithms (Random Forest performed best) and outputs classification of labor dystocia severity class, predicting likelihood of cesarean versus vaginal delivery.
title: Artificial Intelligence Dystocia Algorithm (AIDA) as a Decision Support System in Transverse Fetal Head Position.
study_design: retrospective secondary analysis of a multicenter cohort study

model_family: proprietary AI model (deep learning, retrained across versions)

release_evidence: a proprietary artificial intelligence (AI) model
journal: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians

clinical_problem: Tracking longitudinal tumor growth trajectories in untreated pediatric low-grade gliomas under surveillance using deep-learning volumetrics

model_description: A review of machine learning risk-prediction models for autism spectrum disorder that integrate genetic background, gaze behavior, perinatal factors, brain MRI, and gut microbiome composition.
title: Age of machine learning: new trends in autism spectrum disorder prediction.

clinical_problem: predicting necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) in preterm neonates

title: Ultrasound combined with serological markers for predicting neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis: a machine learning approach.
headline_result: cross-validation AUC 0.97; validation-set AUC 0.88 (sensitivity 0.73, specificity 1.00), outperforming ultrasound-only (AUC 0.73) or serology-only (AUC 0.79) models

clinical_problem: Assessing risk of abnormal early brain development in infants and young children exposed to maternal inflammation, using multi-source deep learning modeling that includes neuroimaging
model_description: Cohort protocol describing a deep-learning artificial intelligence model under development that integrates gene-image-environment-behavior data, including neuroimaging of early brain structure and connectivity, to assess risk of abnormal early brain development.
title: Cohort protocol: risk assessment of maternal inflammation and early brain development in infants and young children based on multi-source data modeling.

patient_population: 24 children with drug refractory focal epilepsy and 35 healthy controls
clinical_problem: Classifying children with MRI-negative drug refractory focal epilepsy using neurovascular coupling imaging biomarkers

title: Altered coupling of cerebral blood perfusion and neuronal activity in children with MRI-negative drug refractory epilepsy.

clinical_problem: Establishing normal reference ranges for first-trimester placental volume using automated deep-learning segmentation of 3D ultrasound

title: Reference charts for first-trimester placental volume derived using OxNNet.

clinical_problem: Automated bone age assessment in Chinese children for growth disorder evaluation

title: Lightweight deep learning system for automated bone age assessment in Chinese children: enhancing clinical efficiency and diagnostic accuracy.

patient_population: 794 patients (603 SickKids, 102 Stanford, 89 CHOP)
clinical_problem: Predicting need for pyeloplasty (surgery) in infants with hydronephrosis from renal ultrasound images

title: Longitudinal image-based prediction of surgical intervention in infants with hydronephrosis using deep learning: Is a single ultrasound enough?
