release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
title: Leveraging fMRI non-stationarity for deep learning classifier training and feature detection to improve schizophrenia diagnosis.
dataset_size: four diagnostic samples (adolescent-onset schizophrenia, adult schizophrenia, major depressive disorder, bipolar disorder), sizes not stated
headline_result: Classification accuracy up to 89.2% (adult schizophrenia); AOS classification examined with convergent regional findings but no separate accuracy given in abstract

patient_population: Pediatric patients with polymicrogyria (numbers not stated)
clinical_problem: Diagnosing polymicrogyria, a subtle cortical malformation, in pediatric patients from brain MRI
model_description: Brain MRI scans, after preprocessing (normalization, CLAHE, bilateral filtering, edge detection), are classified by CNN architectures (ResNet-101 best) to detect polymicrogyria; GradCAM++ used for interpretability.
title: Automated detection of polymicrogyria in pediatric patients using deep learning.
study_design: retrospective model development and preprocessing comparison study
headline_result: ResNet-101 accuracy improved by 10.3 percentage points with preprocessing pipeline

model_family: connectome-based predictive modeling (cross-validated, data-driven machine learning)
patient_population: early adolescents enrolled in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study; exact ages not given
clinical_problem: prediction of cognitive performance from functional connectivity associated with environmental exposome
model_description: Input is resting-state and task fMRI functional connectivity from adolescents in the ABCD Study. A cross-validated, data-driven connectome-based predictive model relates connectivity patterns to an environmental 'exposome' score and to cognitive performance across three domains (general cognition, executive function, learning/memory). Results generalized across data-collection sites and cognitive domains, but this is a research association study, not a diagnostic tool.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
title: Multivariate environmental exposures are reflected in whole-brain functional connectivity and cognition in youth.
dataset_size: n = 6,137-8,391 across models, ABCD Study cohort
headline_result: Cross-validated models: r = 0.34-0.44, p < .001, robust across data-collection sites and cognitive domains (p < 0.0009)

patient_population: not stated (motivated by pediatric and trauma radiation-reduction use case)
clinical_problem: enable AI-based skull segmentation directly from MRI (avoiding CT radiation) for craniomaxillofacial surgical planning, particularly relevant in pediatric and trauma cases
model_description: deep learning models are trained using 186 paired CT-MRI datasets (CT-based segmentation labels transferred to MRI via multimodal registration) to perform automated skull segmentation directly from MRI, avoiding CT radiation exposure
title: Redefining MRI-Based Skull Segmentation Through AI-Driven Multimodal Integration.
study_design: retrospective model development and validation study
headline_result: DSC 0.981 (CT-based segmentation) vs 0.864 (MRI-based segmentation)

patient_population: 8,242 left-hand radiographs from Chinese children
clinical_problem: Assessing bone age and predicting adult height from pediatric hand radiographs to evaluate growth
model_description: Cascaded deep learning framework: Yolact detects and classifies hand bone structures, parallel ResNet-18 subnetworks grade ossification centers in the radius, ulna, and metacarpal/phalangeal bones, a scoring system estimates bone age, and a regression model predicts adult height.
title: Automated Bone Age Assessment and Adult Height Prediction from Pediatric Hand Radiographs via a Cascaded Deep Learning Framework.
headline_result: Pearson r 0.98 (bone age), 0.94 (adult height); MAE 0.25 years bone age, 1.75 cm adult height

patient_population: children who underwent calcaneus stop screw surgery for flexible symptomatic flat foot (124 operated feet)
clinical_problem: measure radiographic angles for pre- and post-surgical assessment of flexible flat foot correction (calcaneus stop screws) in children
model_description: commercial AI software (Bone Metrics AI, Gleamer) automatically measures foot radiographic angles (calcaneus inclination, hallux valgus, 1st-2nd and 1st-5th metatarsal angles, talus-1st metatarsal angle, medial arch angle) on pre- and post-operative X-rays, compared to manual measurements
release_evidence: Bone Metrics AI (Gleamer)
title: Subtalar Arthroereisis with Calcaneus Stop Screws-Can the Angles on Pre- and Post-Surgical X-Ray Images Be Reliably Measured by Artificial Intelligence?
dataset_size: 659 X-rays from 124 operated feet (422 analyzable by AI, 299 met quality criteria)
headline_result: AI measurements comparable to manual for most angles; talus-1st metatarsal angle differed significantly (AI larger by 6.14 deg pre-op, 2.80 deg post-op, P<0.001); medial arch angle smaller by 1.63/0.52 deg (P<=0.013)

patient_population: Public datasets: FETAL_PLANES_DB, HC18, and a large-scale fetal head dataset
clinical_problem: Classifying standard fetal ultrasound planes for prenatal biometric measurement and anomaly detection
model_description: Fetal ultrasound images are input to a hybrid state-space model / vision transformer framework that jointly classifies the standard imaging plane, segments anatomy, and regresses biometric measurements (e.g., head circumference).
title: Hybrid State-Space and Vision Transformer Framework for Fetal Ultrasound Plane Classification in Prenatal Diagnostics.
study_design: retrospective model development and cross-dataset evaluation
dataset_size: FETAL_PLANES_DB, HC18, and a large-scale fetal head dataset (public)
headline_result: 95.8% accuracy on FETAL_PLANES_DB; Dice 95.7%, mean absolute error 2.30 mm for head circumference on HC18

patient_population: 200 pediatric elbow radiographs (100 normal, 100 abnormal) from a tertiary pediatric hospital
clinical_problem: Detecting fractures on pediatric elbow radiographs in the acute emergency setting
model_description: General-purpose multimodal LLM (ChatGPT-4o) is prompted with anonymized pediatric elbow radiographs via a standardized prompt and outputs a fracture vs. no-fracture prediction and fracture site.
release_evidence: ChatGPT-4o, OpenAI's proprietary multimodal model
title: Flexing ChatGPT-4o's Diagnostic Muscle: Detection of Fractures in the Ossifying Pediatric Elbow on Radiographs.
headline_result: Accuracy 85%, sensitivity 87%, specificity 82%, F1 0.85, Cohen's kappa 0.69 vs. ground-truth reports

patient_population: Pediatric neuroblastoma patients; small pediatric imaging dataset used by 9 competing teams
clinical_problem: Automated segmentation of pediatric neuroblastoma on MRI to assist surgical planning
model_description: Multi-modal MRI scans of pediatric neuroblastoma are input to deep-learning segmentation models submitted by 9 teams in a MICCAI 2023 benchmark challenge, outputting tumor segmentations used to build 3D anatomical models for surgical planning.
title: A Community Benchmark for the Automated Segmentation of Pediatric Neuroblastoma on Multi-Modal MRI: Design and Results of the SPPIN Challenge at MICCAI 2023.
dataset_size: small pediatric MRI dataset (9 teams' submissions evaluated)
headline_result: Top team median Dice 0.82 (HD95 7.69 mm, VS 0.91); performance markedly lower on pre-operative scans

model_family: deep transfer learning + radiomics + machine learning classifier
patient_population: 372 pathologically confirmed pediatric appendicitis cases (230 male, 142 female) from three centers
clinical_problem: Differentiating complicated from uncomplicated appendicitis in children using ultrasound and laboratory data
model_description: Combines deep-transfer-learning image features and radiomic features from appendiceal ultrasound images with clinical lab values (WBC, neutrophils, CRP) in a machine learning classifier to distinguish complicated from uncomplicated appendicitis.
title: Retrospective Development of an AI Model Combining Ultrasound and Clinical Data for Pediatric Appendicitis Differentiation.
study_design: Retrospective multi-center model development and validation
headline_result: Combined model AUC 0.940/0.895/0.866/0.783 across cohorts; accuracy 0.862, comparable to senior surgeons and superior to junior surgeons

patient_population: children with ADHD and typically developing children (ADHD-200 database)
clinical_problem: estimate brain functional network small-world topology parameters from resting-state fMRI in children with and without ADHD
model_description: a deep neural network estimates the rewiring-probability parameter of the Watts-Strogatz small-world network model from resting-state fMRI functional connectivity data in children (ADHD-200 database)
title: Inferences on the Watts-Strogatz Model: A Study on Brain Functional Connectivity.
study_design: retrospective methodological study on public dataset
headline_result: mean rewiring probability p = 0.804 +/- 0.003; age (not ADHD diagnosis) was a significant predictor of p (P<0.001)

model_family: deep learning segmentation (TransBTS, MedNeXt, MedicalNet) and CNN classification with segmentation-informed pretraining
patient_population: 455 patients with pediatric low-grade glioma (pLGG) treated 1999-2023 at a children's hospital
clinical_problem: noninvasive pretreatment prediction of BRAF mutation status in pediatric low-grade glioma
model_description: Whole-brain FLAIR MRI is segmented by one of three tested networks (TransBTS, MedNeXt, MedicalNet) and then classified by a deep learning model to predict BRAF status without relying on manual tumor segmentation. A pretraining step embeds segmentation knowledge into the whole-brain classification model to improve accuracy without needing a tumor mask at inference.
title: Segmentation-free pretherapeutic assessment of BRAF-status in pediatric low-grade gliomas.
study_design: retrospective single-center model development and comparison
dataset_size: 455 patients with molecularly characterized pLGG and whole-brain FLAIR MRI
headline_result: AUC 0.741 without segmentation knowledge, improved to 0.772 with segmentation pretraining (vs 0.756 for segmentation-based baseline)

model_family: 2.5D deep learning combining Residual Network and Swin Transformer
patient_population: 309 pediatric patients with pathology-confirmed posterior fossa tumors
clinical_problem: preoperative differentiation of pediatric posterior fossa tumor type (pilocytic astrocytoma, medulloblastoma, ependymoma)
model_description: ResSwinT takes five-sequence MRI (T1WI, T1C, T2WI, FLAIR, ADC) constructed as 2.5D images and outputs a three-way classification among pilocytic astrocytoma, medulloblastoma, and ependymoma. SHAP analysis is used to show which tumor regions drive each prediction.
title: Precise diagnosis of pediatric posterior cranial fossa neoplasms based on 2.5D MRI deep learning.

patient_population: 47 singleton pregnancies at 28-37 weeks of gestation
clinical_problem: characterize fetal facial expression patterns using AI to indirectly infer fetal brain activity
model_description: an original AI model classifies frames of fetal facial expression video into categories (e.g., neutral, mouthing) to quantify duration, transitions, and correlation dimensions, proposed as an indirect proxy for fetal brain activity
title: Characteristics of fetal facial expression changes using artificial intelligence: a pilot study.
dataset_size: 57,208 frames (95.27 minutes) from 47 singleton pregnancies, 28-37 weeks gestation
headline_result: neutral and mouthing expressions had the longest durations (median 71.0 s and 53.3 s)

patient_population: 169 children with epilepsy (96 FCD, 73 DNET)
clinical_problem: preoperatively differentiate focal cortical dysplasia from dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumor in children with epilepsy using MRI radiomics
model_description: radiomics features are extracted from T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and T2-FLAIR MRI, selected via LASSO, and used to build SVM classifiers (individual-sequence and fusion models) to differentiate FCD from DNET preoperatively, compared with radiologists
title: MRI-based radiomics model for differentiating focal cortical dysplasia from dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumor in epileptic children.
headline_result: fusion radiomics model AUC 0.894 (95% CI 0.799-0.968), accuracy 82.0%, superior to junior radiologist and comparable to senior radiologist

patient_population: 270 normal-term pregnancies, 16-40 weeks gestation; pipeline validated on 20 datasets (0.55T and 3T)
clinical_problem: Automated measurement of cervical length and volume on fetal MRI to study cervical remodeling before birth
model_description: 3D T2-weighted motion-corrected fetal MRI is input to a deep learning pipeline that automatically performs multi-layer segmentation of the pregnant cervix and derives biometric measurements (e.g., inlet diameter, length), compared with manual measurement and used to build normative growth curves.
title: Automated cervix biometry, volumetry and normative models for 3D motion-corrected T2-weighted 0.55-3T fetal MRI during 2nd and 3rd trimesters.
dataset_size: 270 normal term cases (16-40 weeks GA); pipeline validated on 20 datasets
headline_result: Automated cervix biometry showed good agreement with manual measurements; inlet diameter and length correlated most strongly with gestational age

model_family: deep learning (cross-modal synthesis model, architecture unspecified)
patient_population: cohorts spanning early development (young children), young adulthood, and elderly age
clinical_problem: synthesize missing T1-weighted or T2-weighted MRI from the other sequence, useful for populations (including young children) who have difficulty completing full MRI protocols
model_description: a deep learning cross-modal synthesis model generates T1-weighted from T2-weighted MRI (and vice versa), incorporating age information across the lifespan, including young children prone to head motion during scanning
journal: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. Annual International Conference
title: Multimodal structural MRI synthesis pipeline across age.
study_design: retrospective methodological development study spanning three age cohorts
headline_result: MSE 0.022-0.024, PSNR 18.96-21.13 across early development/young adulthood/elderly cohorts

patient_population: pediatric bone age X-ray patients (curated expert-validated dataset)
clinical_problem: detect skeletal anomalies and growth disorders in children via bone age X-rays, addressing the rarity of anomalies with self-supervised learning
model_description: self-supervised learning (SSL) pretraining with Vision Transformers extracts features from unlabeled pediatric bone age X-rays; novelty detection techniques then flag rare skeletal anomalies not captured by standard bone-age assessment models
journal: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. Annual International Conference
title: Novelty Detection for Bone Age Anomaly Identification Using Self-Supervised Learning.
study_design: retrospective model development and benchmarking study
headline_result: accuracy 98.2%, AUC 99.8% for SSL-based models, outperforming non-SSL counterparts

patient_population: Infants undergoing hip ultrasound for suspected developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH)
clinical_problem: Diagnosing developmental dysplasia of the hip in infants from B-mode ultrasound images.
model_description: Input: B-mode hip ultrasound images. Output: DDH diagnostic classification, using a symmetry-aware convolution plus Mamba state-space scanning to capture bilateral hip structure.
journal: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. Annual International Conference
title: Hybrid Symmetry Mamba Network for Ultrasound-Based CAD of Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip.
study_design: Retrospective algorithm development and evaluation study.
headline_result: Diagnostic accuracy 89.28% ± 2.32%, outperforming compared CNN/Transformer algorithms.

patient_population: Pediatric patients undergoing hip ultrasound (two datasets, 108 and 200 subjects)
clinical_problem: Assessing the robustness of AI models used for pediatric hip ultrasound scan-adequacy assessment against adversarial image perturbations.
model_description: Input: 2D pediatric hip ultrasound images. Output: scan-adequacy/classification decision from CNN models; adversarial attacks (FGSM, PGD, BIM) tested and adversarial training used to improve robustness.
journal: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. Annual International Conference
title: Impact of Adversarial Attack on Pediatric Hip Ultrasound Deep Learning Models.
headline_result: Accuracy dropped 11-37% under adversarial attack (worst for DenseNet); adversarial training improved accuracy 2-6% on validation dataset.

patient_population: Children with suspected wrist injury imaged with ultrasound in a pediatric emergency setting
clinical_problem: Segmenting bony structures on wrist ultrasound to triage suspected pediatric wrist fractures and reduce need for X-ray.
model_description: Input: wrist ultrasound images, optionally CLAHE-enhanced. Output: segmentation masks of epiphysis, metaphysis, and carpal bone using an nnU-Net-based model.
journal: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. Annual International Conference
title: Automated Wrist Ultrasound Image Bone Enhancement and Segmentation Using Deep Learning.
study_design: Retrospective segmentation model development and evaluation study.
dataset_size: 16,865 training and 3,822 testing images from 74 and 18 subjects
headline_result: Dice score 0.874 with CLAHE preprocessing vs 0.872 without.

patient_population: Patients with Sturge-Weber syndrome (congenital disorder presenting in early childhood)
clinical_problem: Automated detection of leptomeningeal angiomas on brain MRI in children with Sturge-Weber syndrome to speed diagnosis.
model_description: Input: T1-enhanced brain MRI. Output: segmentation/detection of leptomeningeal angiomas via a multi-scale multi-scan Mamba encoder-decoder, pretrained on public BraTS data and fine-tuned on the SWS cohort.
title: Detection of leptomeningeal angiomas in brain MRI of Sturge-Weber syndrome using multi-scale multi-scan Mamba.
study_design: Retrospective model development study with 5-fold cross-validation.
headline_result: Dice score 91.53% (BraTS pretraining set) and 78.67% (SWS test set), outperforming two neurologists.

patient_population: Infants diagnosed with prenatal hydronephrosis
clinical_problem: Predicting congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT) from prenatal/postnatal urinary tract dilation ultrasound findings to guide need for advanced imaging.
model_description: Input: ultrasound urinary-tract-dilation parameters (central/ureteral dilation, AP diameter) and age at first ultrasound. Output: predicted probability of CAKUT diagnosis.
title: Predicting congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT) in prenatal hydronephrosis via machine learning.
study_design: Retrospective cohort study, ML model development.
headline_result: AUC 0.915-0.922 across Random Forest, LightGBM and XGBoost models.

patient_population: Adult and pediatric patients with suspected acute appendicitis (review of 65 studies)
clinical_problem: Reviewing machine learning and deep learning applications for diagnosing acute appendicitis (including differentiating complicated from uncomplicated cases) using clinical, laboratory and imaging (ultrasound/CT) data in adult and pediatric patients.
model_description: Review of 65 studies applying ML (random forest, SVM, logistic regression, XGBoost) and DL (CNNs) models to clinical, laboratory and imaging (ultrasound, CT) data for diagnosing acute appendicitis and differentiating complicated from uncomplicated disease.
title: Artificial intelligence in acute appendicitis: A comprehensive review of machine learning and deep learning applications.
headline_result: ML models sensitivity/specificity >90% in multiple studies; DL outperformed radiologists on US/CT interpretation in some studies

model_family: HRNet + Swin-Transformer deep learning framework with SVD-based curve analysis
patient_population: patients aged 10-18 years with full-spine anteroposterior radiographs for scoliosis
clinical_problem: automated Cobb angle measurement and vertebral wedging assessment for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis severity
model_description: The model takes full-spine anteroposterior radiographs and predicts superior and inferior endplate angles and vertebral midpoints for each vertebra, combining an HRNet/Swin-Transformer backbone with singular value decomposition to compute Cobb angle and a new Vertebral Wedging Index without assuming a predefined curve pattern.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: Accurate Cobb Angle Estimation via SVD-Based Curve Detection and Vertebral Wedging Quantification.
study_design: retrospective model development with dual-rater annotation
dataset_size: 630 full-spine radiographs from patients aged 10-18 years
headline_result: 83.45% diagnostic accuracy, 2.55-degree mean absolute error for Cobb angle

patient_population: Pediatric patients with brain tumors
clinical_problem: Current and emerging imaging approaches, including AI, for diagnosing and classifying pediatric brain tumors
model_description: Narrative review of MRI (structural, diffusion, perfusion, spectroscopy) and PET imaging for pediatric brain tumors, including emerging radiomics and AI methods for tumor classification, segmentation, and recurrence prediction, and privacy-preserving/explainable AI approaches such as federated learning.
title: [Current Imaging Approaches for Pediatric Brain Tumors].

patient_population: Normotensive pregnant women at 22-24 weeks' gestation
clinical_problem: Predicting hypertensive disorders of pregnancy using mid-gestation maternal hemodynamics and Doppler ultrasound placental blood flow measures.
model_description: Input: noninvasive maternal cardiovascular (impedance cardiography) and Doppler ultrasound placental/uteroplacental blood-flow measures. Output: predicted probability of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.
title: Development and validation of a novel prediction model for hypertensive disorders of pregnancy based on maternal cardiovascular function and placental blood flow metrics at 22 to 24 gestational weeks using machine learning.
study_design: Cross-sectional cohort study, ML model development.
headline_result: AUC 0.82 (95% CI 0.65-0.95) on independent test set; sensitivity 70%, specificity 79%.

patient_population: 9 fetal ultrasound images evaluated by 6 Vision LLMs and 3 expert sonographers
clinical_problem: Whether vision-capable large language models can interpret fetal ultrasound images for prenatal care
model_description: Fetal ultrasound images are input to six Vision Large Language Models (via a chatbot platform) with standard vs. tailored prompts; outputs are assessed by expert sonographers on anatomical recognition, biometric potential, image quality, normalcy assessment, and clinical recommendations.
title: Benchmarking Vision LLMs in fetal ultrasound interpretation: a five-point expert evaluation of standard vs. custom prompts.
headline_result: Custom prompts improved performance; best models (Claude Sonnet 3.5, ChatGPT-4o) achieved median scores of 19 and 18 out of 25

patient_population: Female pediatric patients with idiopathic short stature undergoing traditional Chinese medicine treatment, and healthy children controls
clinical_problem: Using AI-assisted bone age assessment methods (Greulich-Pyle, TW3, TW China) to evaluate treatment efficacy in girls with idiopathic short stature.
model_description: Input: left-hand X-rays at baseline and follow-up. Output: AI-assisted bone age estimates via G&P, TW3 and TW-China atlas methods, tracked over 6/9/12-month follow-up to gauge treatment efficacy.
title: The value of AI-assisted multiple bone age assessment methods for evaluating efficacy in idiopathic short stature: A retrospective study of traditional Chinese medicine treatment for girls in China.
dataset_size: 388 healthy children (control) and 190 female ISS patients
headline_result: Bone-age difference on follow-up was significantly higher in the treatment-effective group (P<.01); TW3/TW-China methods detected efficacy as early as 6 months versus 12 months for G&P.

model_family: XGBoost (gradient boosting; best of five ML algorithms compared)
patient_population: Pediatric patients with extrahepatic portal vein obstruction (EHPVO) undergoing shunt surgery
clinical_problem: Preoperative noninvasive prediction of optimal surgical shunt (Rex vs. Warren) in children with extrahepatic portal vein obstruction, using ultrasound and serology instead of invasive portography.
model_description: Input: ultrasound imaging features and serological markers selected via LASSO. Output: predicted probability guiding Rex vs. Warren shunt selection, deployed as an online prediction tool.
title: Preoperative noninvasive prediction of Rex vs. Warren shunt selection in children with extrahepatic portal vein obstruction: a machine learning model based on serology and ultrasound.
study_design: Retrospective diagnostic model development study with internal and external validation.
headline_result: XGBoost AUC 0.90 (95% CI 0.79-0.99) training, 0.75 (95% CI 0.54-0.97) external validation.

patient_population: 953 second- and third-trimester fetuses
clinical_problem: Automated classification of fetal echocardiographic views to support congenital heart disease diagnosis
model_description: Fetal echocardiographic images (8 standard views) are input to CNN architectures (best: ConvNeXt) that output the standard view classification; Grad-CAM used to visualize decision-making.
journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
title: Automated and accurate view classification of fetal echocardiography using convolutional neural networks.
headline_result: ConvNeXt-based model accuracy 97.78%, F1 96.08%

patient_population: Children aged 1-6 years (structural connectome measured at age 1, IQ assessed at ages 4, 6, 8)
clinical_problem: Whether structural brain connectome organization in infancy predicts later cognitive (IQ) outcomes in childhood
model_description: Structural connectome gradients (diffusion-based measures of brain connectivity organization) measured at age 1 are input to machine learning models that predict future intelligence quotient at ages 4, 6, and 8.
title: Structural connectome gradients and their relationship to IQ in childhood.
study_design: prospective longitudinal cohort study with machine learning prediction
headline_result: Mean Spearman correlation >0.25 between predicted and actual IQ

patient_population: Large dataset of pediatric trauma imaging; subset of 1,000 images independently assessed by human raters
clinical_problem: Predicting biological sex from pediatric skeletal radiographs
model_description: Pediatric skeletal radiographs (computed and digital radiography) are input to a family of EfficientNet CNN models (B0-B7) that output a predicted biological sex classification, compared against human raters.
title: Predicting biological sex in pediatric skeleton X-rays using artificial intelligence.
study_design: retrospective model development and comparison to human raters
dataset_size: large pediatric trauma radiograph dataset; 1,000-image subset for human comparison
headline_result: Mean AI accuracy 0.722 (precision 0.731, recall 0.718), surpassing human raters; best in ages 13-18 and pelvic radiographs

model_family: CNN (prior knowledge-guided, with U-Net for brain extraction)
patient_population: Fetuses undergoing MRI during the second and third trimesters
clinical_problem: Estimating fetal brain age from MRI during the second and third trimesters to help optimize pregnancy management and flag abnormal development.
model_description: Input: T2-weighted fetal MRI (axial, sagittal, coronal). Output: predicted fetal brain age in days via an attention-guided CNN, whose attention maps are also combined with the images for a brain-extraction (segmentation) network.
title: A prior knowledge-guided convolutional neural network model for predicting fetal brain age from MRI during second and third trimesters.
dataset_size: 407 T2-weighted MRI studies (2,310 stacks), brain ages 22-39 weeks
headline_result: Mean absolute error 4.62 ± 3.31 days; concordance ρc = 0.977, R2 = 0.953.

body_region: subcortical brain structures (hippocampus, thalamus, caudate, lentiform nucleus)
patient_population: Pediatric participants with autism spectrum disorder and typically developing controls
clinical_problem: Diagnosing autism spectrum disorder in children using radiomics features from routine structural brain MRI.
model_description: Input: radiomics features extracted from manually segmented subcortical structures on T1WI/T2WI MRI. Output: ASD vs. typically-developing classification via a TabTransformer deep-learning model.
title: Leveraging TabTransformer Deep Learning on Conventional MRI Radiomics for Accessible and Interpretable Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder.
study_design: Retrospective case-control diagnostic model development study.
headline_result: AUC 0.900, accuracy 0.834, sensitivity 0.843, specificity 0.823 (combined T1WI+T2WI TabTransformer model).

patient_population: 1,436 transvaginal ultrasound images for development, 189 external images from a different hospital
clinical_problem: Standardizing automated measurement of cervical tissue changes on transvaginal ultrasound to help predict preterm birth
model_description: Transvaginal ultrasound images are input to oriented object-detection models (Oriented RepPoints best among five compared) that localize a standardized oriented cervical canal region for consistent downstream cervical tissue quantification.
title: O-CCR: oriented cervical canal region detection framework toward cervical change assessment in transvaginal ultrasound.
study_design: retrospective model development with external validation
headline_result: Oriented RepPoints achieved average precision 0.981 at IoU 0.5

patient_population: not stated
clinical_problem: Streamlining and standardizing fetal MRI analysis to reduce reliance on subspecialized radiological expertise
model_description: Fetal MRI is input to a web-based AI platform (FetAS) that automates artifact detection, motion correction, segmentation of the fetal body, amniotic fluid and placenta, and classification of fetal/placental position and orientation.
title: Fetal Assessment Suite (FetAS): a web-based platform for automatic fetal MRI analysis using AI.

patient_population: 291 patients (2019-2023), categorized into medical, early surgery, and late surgery groups
clinical_problem: Predicting the need for surgery in necrotizing enterocolitis using abdominal X-ray imaging biomarkers
model_description: Color-channel-transformed radiomics features are extracted from the region of interest on abdominal radiographs and screened with t-tests and LASSO regression to identify imaging biomarkers predicting surgical necessity in necrotizing enterocolitis.
title: New biomarkers to predict the need for surgery of necrotizing enterocolitis: a study based on abdominal X-ray radiomics and machine learning.
headline_result: Three radiomics features (Blue_variance, a_star_variance, L_star_energy) identified as differential markers for surgical necessity (no AUC reported in abstract)

model_family: causal forest algorithm with AI-quantified CT features
patient_population: pediatric MPP patients, derivation cohort n=753, validation cohort n=139, two centers
clinical_problem: identifying which children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia are most likely to benefit from flexible bronchoscopy
model_description: A causal forest model combines clinical, laboratory and AI-quantified CT features (consolidation/atelectasis volume, pneumonia attenuation, consolidation ratio) to estimate each patient's individual treatment effect from flexible bronchoscopy, identifying a subgroup that benefits from the procedure (reduced fever duration) versus one that does not.
release_evidence: an accessible online tool of this model facilitates practical clinical implementation
title: A causal forest model integrating quantitative CT scores to predict benefit from flexible bronchoscopy in pediatric Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia: a two-center retrospective study.
headline_result: fever duration reduced in FB-beneficial subgroup: beta=-1.16 (derivation, p<0.001), beta=-0.68 (validation, p=0.04)

patient_population: 122 preterm infants born <31 weeks gestation without severe neonatal brain injury
clinical_problem: Predicting neurodevelopmental impairment severity at 24 months corrected age in preterm infants without severe brain injury, using resting-state functional MRI connectivity at term-equivalent age.
model_description: Machine learning models take resting-state functional MRI connectivity features (at term-equivalent age) plus neonatal clinical exposures as input and predict severity of neurodevelopmental impairment at 24 months corrected age.
title: Functional connectivity as a prognostic biomarker for neurodevelopmental outcomes in preterm infants without severe brain injury.
study_design: observational cohort study with machine learning outcome prediction
headline_result: Predictive model achieved 82% accuracy

patient_population: Pregnant women undergoing prenatal ultrasound aneuploidy screening (review, no single study population)
clinical_problem: Reviewing AI-enhanced ultrasound predictive models for screening fetal chromosomal numerical abnormalities (aneuploidy).
model_description: Narrative review summarizing AI-based predictive models that combine with ultrasound to screen for fetal chromosomal numerical abnormalities, comparing them to traditional methods and discussing multicenter standardization and interpretability challenges.
title: Application of ultrasound and artificial intelligence in the prediction of fetal chromosomal numerical abnormalities.

model_family: meta-analysis comparing echocardiography, biomarkers, miRNA and AI models
patient_population: childhood cancer survivors treated with anthracyclines (73 studies in qualitative synthesis, 10 in meta-analysis)
clinical_problem: early detection of subclinical anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity in childhood cancer survivors
model_description: Systematic review and meta-analysis pooling the prognostic accuracy of echocardiography (global longitudinal strain), serum biomarkers, microRNAs, and AI-based models for predicting chemotherapy-induced cardiotoxicity in pediatric cancer patients; AI-based models had the highest pooled predictive AUC among the modalities compared.
title: Cardiotoxicity in pediatric oncology: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
headline_result: pooled AUC ~0.80 for AI-based models vs ~0.72 for global longitudinal strain

patient_population: Preschool children with autism spectrum disorder and typically developing controls
clinical_problem: Characterizing corpus-callosum white-matter microstructural alterations in preschool children with autism to inform early diagnosis, using free-water corrected diffusion MRI.
model_description: Input: free-water corrected diffusion MRI. A machine-learning atlas-based approach automatically segments the corpus callosum into seven subregions; diffusion metrics per subregion are then compared between ASD and typically developing children and correlated with symptom severity.
title: Free Water Corrected Diffusion Magnetic Resonance Imaging Reveals Microstructural Alterations in Corpus Callosum Subregions of Preschool Children With Autism.
study_design: Case-control diffusion MRI study using ML-based automated image segmentation.
dataset_size: 61 ASD children (6.03±1.08y) and 62 typically developing controls (6.49±1.45y)
headline_result: CC6 (temporal projections) showed reduced tissue fractional anisotropy (t=-3.251, P<0.01); CC2-5 FAt negatively correlated with autism severity scores (r=-0.36 to -0.52, P<0.01).

model_family: SVM, decision tree, random forest, gradient boosting (comparison)
patient_population: Pediatric patients with drug-resistant epilepsy in Jakarta, Indonesia
clinical_problem: Predicting treatment success (seizure control) in children with drug-resistant epilepsy by integrating clinical data, EEG, and MRI to guide antiepileptic drug selection.
model_description: Input: clinical data, EEG, and modified HARNESS MRI. Output: predicted treatment success/seizure-control classification (protocol; results not yet reported) to support antiepileptic drug decisions.
title: Developing a machine learning model to assist in predicting treatment success in children with drug-resistant epilepsy.
study_design: Prospective/ambispective cohort study protocol for ML model development.

model_family: Support vector machine (best of 11 ML algorithms compared)
patient_population: Children with ovarian space-occupying lesions at two children's hospitals
clinical_problem: Predicting ovarian torsion and secondary ischemic necrosis in children using ultrasound findings and inflammatory markers to guide urgent surgical decisions.
model_description: Input: ultrasound findings (e.g., follicular edema ring sign, pelvic effusion) plus laboratory inflammatory indices. Output: predicted risk of ovarian torsion and ischemic necrosis, with SHAP-based key-factor identification.
title: Construction and validation of a machine learning model integrating ultrasound features and inflammatory markers (OVART-ML) for predicting ovarian torsion and ischemic necrosis risk in children.
dataset_size: 112 children (60 with torsion, 23 with ischemic necrosis)
headline_result: Best (SVM) model AUC 0.911 (95% CI 0.809-1.000), accuracy 0.882, sensitivity 0.900.

patient_population: Pediatric patients with brain tumors (public BraTS-PED 2024 dataset)
clinical_problem: Testing whether adding T1w/T2w ratio maps improves automated deep-learning segmentation of pediatric brain tumor subregions on MRI.
model_description: Input: multiparametric MRI (T1w, T2w, FLAIR, contrast-enhanced T1w), with or without an added T1w/T2w ratio map. Output: nnU-Net segmentation of pediatric brain tumor subregions.
title: Ratio maps of T1w/T2w MRI signal intensity do not improve deep-learning segmentation of pediatric brain tumors.
study_design: Retrospective segmentation ablation study using a public dataset.
headline_result: Adding T1w/T2w ratio or combined maps did not significantly improve Dice scores across tumor subregions.

body_region: white matter regions (25 ROIs, JHU atlas)
patient_population: Individuals in the ABIDE II database (autism spectrum disorder vs. controls)
clinical_problem: Automated detection of autism spectrum disorder from diffusion tensor imaging-derived white matter microstructure measures.
model_description: Input: fractional anisotropy, mean/radial/axial diffusivity from 25 ASD-relevant white-matter regions of interest on DTI. Output: ASD vs. non-ASD classification via a random forest computer-aided-diagnosis system.
title: Autism spectrum disorder detection using diffusion tensor imaging and machine learning.
study_design: Retrospective case-control diagnostic model development study (public dataset) with external test.
headline_result: Best (RF) model: sensitivity 100%, accuracy 95.65%; external test set: 94.73% sensitivity, 97.37% accuracy, 100% precision/specificity.

patient_population: 36 pediatric patients undergoing robot-assisted pyeloplasty
clinical_problem: noninvasively assessing urine flow dynamics after pyeloplasty for hydronephrosis
model_description: input magnetic resonance urography images; output a deep-learning reconstructed 3D mesh model of the upper urinary tract used for computational fluid dynamics simulation of urine flow
title: Novel noninvasive assessment of upper urinary tract urine flow dynamics: a deep learning-driven reconstruction model combined with CFD simulation.

patient_population: 209 participants with anxiety disorder and 232 healthy controls, aged 6-14 at baseline (Brazilian cohort)
clinical_problem: predicting anxiety disorder diagnosis in youth from structural brain MRI
model_description: input FreeSurfer-derived structural brain features; output a random-forest classification of anxiety disorder vs. healthy control
title: Machine learning for anxiety diagnosis using structural MRI does not generalize to unseen data: results from a large developmental cohort.
headline_result: AUC 0.70 on test set but only 0.51 (near chance) on hold-out validation sample

model_family: deep learning segmentation/classification pipeline with LLM explainability module
patient_population: fetuses (publicly available dataset)
clinical_problem: classifying severity of fetal ventriculomegaly from brain MRI
task: segmentation; measurement / quantification; detection / diagnosis; report generation / LLM
model_description: input fetal brain MRI slices; output automated ventricle segmentation, ventricular width measurement, severity classification, and an LLM-generated interpretable explanation
title: AI-Driven Clinical Decision Support System for Automated Ventriculomegaly Classification from Fetal Brain MRI.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development study using a public dataset
headline_result: Dice 89% (2D) and 87.5% (3D) segmentation; classification accuracy 86%, F1 0.84

patient_population: Fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound
clinical_problem: Automated segmentation of the fetal cerebellum on ultrasound to assess fetal development and detect prenatal abnormalities.
model_description: Input: fetal ultrasound images. Output: cerebellum segmentation mask via an attention-enhanced U-Net trained with a multi-stage semi-supervised (pseudo-labeling) strategy to cope with limited annotated data.
title: SS_CASE_UNet: an attention-enhanced semi-supervised framework for fetal cerebellum segmentation in ultrasound images.
headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient 87.65%, accuracy 99.08%, precision 93.49%.

patient_population: Normal Korean children undergoing AP pelvic radiography
clinical_problem: Automated measurement of radiographic parameters (acetabular index, Shenton line, pelvic rotation/tilt) on pediatric pelvic X-rays to assess hip development.
model_description: Input: anteroposterior pelvic radiographs. Output: automated measurement of acetabular index, Shenton line, pelvic rotation index and pelvic tilt index, benchmarked against radiologist measurements across age subgroups.
title: Assessing deep learning accuracy in the measurement of radiographic parameters in pediatric hip X-rays.
study_design: Retrospective model development and validation study.
headline_result: Acetabular index ICC=0.89, MAE=2.07°; pelvic rotation index ICC=0.94; pelvic tilt index ICC=0.97.

patient_population: Full-term neonates diagnosed with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy
clinical_problem: Predicting one-year neurodevelopmental prognosis in term neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy using MRI radiomics combined with clinical data.
model_description: Input: brain MRI radiomics features plus Apgar scores. Output: predicted good vs. poor cognitive/motor prognosis at 12 months.
title: Combined model of radiomics and clinical features for predicting prognosis of term neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy after one year: an exploratory study.
headline_result: Combined clinical+radiomics model AUC 0.952 (training), 0.823 (testing), versus 0.857/0.737 for clinical-only.

model_family: Multimodal large language models (ChatGPT-4.0, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Gemini 2.5 Pro, DeepSeek-R1)
patient_population: Patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis undergoing posterior instrumentation
clinical_problem: Evaluating whether general-purpose multimodal LLMs can reliably perform Lenke classification and fusion-level planning from scoliosis radiographs compared with expert spine surgeons.
model_description: Input: standing AP, lateral and side-bending spine radiographs. Output: LLM-generated Lenke classification and fusion-level (UIV-LIV) recommendation via zero-shot prompting, compared against expert surgeon consensus and test-retest reproducibility.
release_evidence: commercial multimodal LLMs (ChatGPT-4.0, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Gemini 2.5 Pro, DeepSeek-R1) accessed via paid API
title: Reliability of Large Language Model-Based Artificial Intelligence in AIS Assessment: Lenke Classification and Fusion-Level Suggestion.
study_design: Retrospective diagnostic reliability study comparing multimodal LLMs to expert consensus.
headline_result: LLM agreement with expert consensus was chance-level: Lenke classification 1.6-10.2% (κ=0.001-0.036); fusion level 0.8-12.0% (κ=0.003-0.053).

model_family: CatBoost (gradient boosting; best of several ML models compared)
patient_population: Term singleton vaginal deliveries at a single academic hospital over 10 years
clinical_problem: Antepartum prediction of shoulder dystocia at delivery using machine learning that incorporates sonographic estimated fetal weight and maternal factors.
model_description: Input: sonographic estimated fetal weight, maternal BMI and other clinical features. Output: predicted probability of shoulder dystocia at delivery.
title: Antepartum prediction of shoulder dystocia using machine learning.
study_design: Retrospective cohort study, ML model development.
headline_result: CatBoost model AUC 0.83 (95% CI 0.77-0.89); sonographic EFW contributed 55.6% of model decision weight.

patient_population: 213 pregnant women scanned at 8 weeks gestation
clinical_problem: early prediction of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and gestational diabetes from first-trimester ultrasound
model_description: input clinical data plus radiomics and deep-learning features from first-trimester ultrasound; output predicted risk of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and gestational diabetes via a fusion model
title: Development and validation of a multi-modality system combining radiomics and deep learning for predicting mid-pregnancy complications and enabling timely pregnancy care.
headline_result: combined model AUC 0.963 in the independent test cohort

patient_population: Pediatric and adult patients undergoing posterior fossa tumor resection (predominantly pediatric: 67.3% of pooled cohort)
clinical_problem: Comparing predictive tools, including an AI-based model, for the risk of CSF diversion after posterior fossa tumor resection to improve neurosurgical decision-making.
model_description: Systematic review comparing ten predictive models (mostly logistic regression, one AI-based model using intraoperative/postoperative imaging patterns) for predicting need for CSF diversion after posterior fossa tumor resection.
title: Comparison of various predictive tools in predicting risk of cerebrospinal fluid diversion post-resection of posterior fossa tumors: A systematic review.
study_design: Systematic review (PRISMA) of predictive model performance.
headline_result: The AI-based model showed the best performance among reviewed tools, AUC = 0.938.

model_family: linear regression models and random forest
patient_population: 443 adolescents, including clinical and non-clinical individuals (largest sample to date for this analysis)
clinical_problem: predicting adolescent rumination (a depression risk marker) from dynamic resting-state fMRI connectivity
model_description: Input is dynamic (time-varying) resting-state fMRI connectivity from a large adolescent sample. Linear models (including one previously validated in adults) and an exploratory random forest were trained to predict self-reported rumination from default-mode-network and whole-brain dynamic connectivity features. None of the models generalized to an external held-out sample with different rumination levels and scanner protocol, though the random forest showed a nominal association in the training sample.
title: Limited generalizability of dynamic fMRI correlates of adolescent rumination.
study_design: cross-sectional predictive modeling with external generalization test
headline_result: Adult-trained and adolescent-trained connectivity models failed to generalize to an external sample; exploratory random forest showed only a nominal association with rumination in training data

patient_population: 65 premature infants
clinical_problem: estimating body composition (fat mass/fat-free mass) noninvasively to assess malnutrition in newborns
model_description: input ultrasound images from three anatomical sites; output predicted fat mass and fat-free mass, benchmarked against air-displacement plethysmography
journal: IEEE access : practical innovations, open solutions
title: Developing a Deep Learning Approach for Automated Body Composition Prediction in Newborns Using Ultrasound Images.
headline_result: mean absolute percent error 25.3-26.1% for fat mass/fat-free mass prediction

patient_population: Children and adolescents with (or being screened for) pulmonary tuberculosis (review, no single study population)
clinical_problem: Reviewing AI-assisted diagnosis of pediatric pulmonary tuberculosis, including imaging-based approaches, and their limitations.
model_description: Narrative review of AI (deep learning, NLP, computer vision, multimodal fusion) combined with medical imaging, laboratory and pathology data for pediatric pulmonary tuberculosis diagnosis; discusses limitations including scarce pediatric data, limited interpretability, and lack of external validation.
title: Applications and prospects of artificial intelligence in the auxiliary diagnosis of pediatric pulmonary tuberculosis.

model_family: YOLO-based segmentation with radiomics and Random Forest classifier
patient_population: children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis undergoing hip ultrasound (internal and external validation cohorts)
clinical_problem: early diagnosis of hip synovitis in juvenile idiopathic arthritis
model_description: YOLO-JIA automatically segments hip ultrasound images; radiomic features are extracted from the segmented regions and selected via ANOVA/LASSO, then classified by a Random Forest model to identify early hip synovitis in juvenile idiopathic arthritis. The pipeline was deployed locally after internal and external validation.
title: Deep learning and radiomics-based system for early diagnosis of hip synovitis in juvenile idiopathic arthritis.
study_design: retrospective model development with internal and external validation
dataset_size: not stated precisely (internal and external validation sets)
headline_result: YOLO-JIA precision 0.98, recall 1.00, mAP50-95 0.86; Random Forest AUC 0.88 internal, 0.81 external

patient_population: fetuses assessed for growth restriction, small/large-for-gestational-age, and macrosomia
clinical_problem: detection and management of fetal growth restriction and macrosomia
task: detection / diagnosis; measurement / quantification; outcome prediction
model_description: Comprehensive review of AI applications for fetal growth disorders, including automated ultrasound biometry, prediction models combining maternal/fetal biomarkers and Doppler indices, and deep learning applied directly to ultrasound images, noting most evidence is retrospective, small, and lacks external validation.
title: Application of artificial intelligence in diagnosis and management of fetal growth disorders: a comprehensive review.

patient_population: Children with confirmed Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia across three medical centers
clinical_problem: Predicting extrapulmonary organ involvement and recovery duration in children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia using CT radiomics.
model_description: Input: chest CT radiomics features plus clinical laboratory and image features. Output: predicted probability of extrapulmonary organ involvement and estimated recovery duration.
title: Development of a radiomics-based model using computed tomography imaging to assess the incidence of extrapulmonary organ involvement in Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia and to predict recovery times: a multicenter study.
study_design: Retrospective multicenter radiomics model development study.
headline_result: Integrated model AUC 0.94 (95% CI 0.84-0.99), versus 0.73 for radiomics alone and 0.67 for clinical laboratory alone.

model_family: U-Net++ (segmentation) plus Faster R-CNN + HRNet + Attention U-Net (hybrid prototypes)
patient_population: Fetuses undergoing routine obstetric ultrasound (public HC18 dataset plus institutional images)
clinical_problem: Automating fetal biometric measurements (head circumference, abdominal circumference, femur length) from ultrasound to reduce operator-dependent variability in growth assessment.
model_description: Input: 2D obstetric ultrasound images. Output: automated head-circumference measurement (U-Net++ segmentation with convex-hull fitting) and prototype abdominal-circumference (Faster R-CNN+HRNet+Attention U-Net) and femur-length modules.
title: A Modular Deep-Learning Framework for Automated Fetal Biometry: Proof-of-Concept Evaluation of Head, Abdominal, and Femur Measurements.
study_design: Retrospective proof-of-concept model development study using public and institutional datasets.
dataset_size: HC18 public dataset, n=1,334 images (test n=110); additional institutional AC/FL images
headline_result: Head-circumference module: MAE 9.7 mm, accuracy 0.90, sensitivity 0.97; abdominal-circumference prototype: mean difference 5.5±3.1 mm from manual reference.

model_family: deep learning brain segmentation framework using domain randomization
patient_population: infants and young children undergoing brain MRI with diverse, sometimes clinically acquired protocols
clinical_problem: segmenting infant and young child brain MRI to support developmental brain analysis
model_description: BabySeg is a deep learning segmentation model for infant and young-child brain MRI that supports diverse MRI protocols and image types not seen during training, including repeat scans, by training on synthetic images generated through domain randomization; it also flexibly pools features from any number of input scans.
journal: Conference record. Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems & Computers
title: Deep infant brain segmentation from multi-contrast MRI.
headline_result: state-of-the-art performance matching or exceeding existing methods across age cohorts and input configurations, in a fraction of the runtime

model_name: HKD-MGIN (Heat Kernel Diffused Multi-task Graph Isomorphism Network)
model_family: Graph neural network (physics-informed, graph isomorphism network)
patient_population: Adolescents undergoing multi-task functional MRI
clinical_problem: Modeling adolescent brain connectivity dynamics to estimate brain age and identify biomarkers of cognitive maturation.
model_description: Input: multi-task resting/task fMRI functional connectivity. A heat-kernel-diffusion graph isomorphism network estimates brain age and classifies sex, revealing functional circuits linked to cognitive maturation.
journal: Machine learning for computational science and engineering
title: HKD-MGIN: a physics informed graph neural network using heat kernel diffusion for mapping adolescent functional brain connectivity.
headline_result: Brain-age estimation RMSE 1.864±0.157, MAE 1.492±0.139, r=0.816; sex classification accuracy 0.802, AUC 0.834.

patient_population: Pregnant women monitored with low-cost 1D Doppler ultrasound
clinical_problem: Automatically distinguishing fetal heart activity from umbilical cord blood flow in low-cost 1D Doppler ultrasound recordings to improve usability for untrained users in low-resource settings.
model_description: Input: power spectrum (relative energy per 10 Hz interval) of 1D Doppler ultrasound recordings. Output: classification of signal source as fetal heart activity versus umbilical cord blood flow.
title: Classification of the Source of 1D Doppler Ultrasound Activity in Fetal Monitoring.
headline_result: AUC 0.82; accuracy 75% for fetal heart identification and 84% for umbilical cord identification.

patient_population: children whose chest X-rays make up the public Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Centre pneumonia dataset
clinical_problem: pneumonia detection in children
model_description: ConvMixer replaces standard convolutional layers with a mixer that separately processes channel and spatial information, reducing the number of parameters and computations per layer. It was applied to a large, publicly available set of pediatric chest X-rays from Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Centre (via Kaggle) to classify images as normal or pneumonia.
journal: Health Services and Outcomes Research Methodology
title: ConvMixer deep learning model for detection of pneumonia disease using chest X-ray images
dataset_size: large numbers of chest X-ray images, publicly available on Kaggle (Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Centre)
headline_result: Highest accuracy 95.11%, also evaluated for precision, recall, and F1-score

model_family: deep learning models (rod model, 58 mm reference model, head-piece model) for landmark detection and measurement
patient_population: children with early-onset scoliosis treated with magnetically controlled growing rods; 387 radiographs used for model development and 60 radiographs (118 rods) for final testing
clinical_problem: automated measurement of growing rod length in children with early-onset scoliosis treated with magnetically controlled growing rods
model_description: Three deep learning models (rod model, 58 mm reference-marker model, head-piece model) were developed to automatically detect landmarks on posteroanterior spine radiographs and calculate the adjusted length of magnetically controlled growing rods in children with early-onset scoliosis, replacing subjective and time-consuming manual measurement.
journal: Medical and Biological Engineering and Computing
title: Validity of machine learning algorithms for automatically extract growing rod length on radiographs in children with early-onset scoliosis
dataset_size: 387 radiographs for development, 60 radiographs (118 rods) for testing
headline_result: average precision 67.6%/94.8%/86.3% for the three models; mean absolute difference of rod length change 0.98 ± 0.88 mm vs. manual measurement, inter-method correlation coefficient 0.90; average processing time 6.1 seconds per measurement

model_family: signal filtering combined with convolutional neural networks and U-Nets
patient_population: children with cerebral palsy undergoing hip ultrasound, 62 hips (coronal and transverse scans)
clinical_problem: assessment of hip displacement severity (migration percentage) in children with cerebral palsy
model_description: A pipeline combining signal filtering, convolutional neural networks, and U-Nets segments the regions of interest and detects landmarks on hip ultrasound images to automatically compute migration percentage (MP), the standard measure of hip displacement severity in cerebral palsy, as a radiation-free alternative to the conventional X-ray-based measurement.
journal: Medical and Biological Engineering and Computing
title: A fully automated measurement of migration percentage on ultrasound images in children with cerebral palsy
dataset_size: 62 hips (36 used for training with augmentation, 8 for validation, 18 for testing)
headline_result: ICC(2,1) of 0.86 and mean absolute difference of 6.5%+-5.5% between automated ultrasound-based MP and manual X-ray-based MP; automated measurement took an average of 104 seconds per hip

patient_population: infants scanned with paired ultra-low-field and high-field MRI
clinical_problem: super-resolution reconstruction of ultra-low-field MRI to improve paediatric neurodevelopmental imaging in low-resource settings
model_description: A deep learning 'multi-orientation U-Net' takes multiple low-resolution, anisotropic T2-weighted images acquired on an ultra-low-field MRI scanner in orthogonal orientations and reconstructs a single high-resolution isotropic image, aiming to improve MRI accessibility in low- and middle-income countries where high-field scanners are unavailable. It was trained and evaluated on paired ultra-low-field and high-field infant brain MRI data.
title: Ultra-Low-Field Paediatric MRI in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: Super-Resolution Using a Multi-Orientation U-Net
headline_result: improved deep brain structure (caudate) volume estimation versus prior state-of-the-art methods: linear correlation r=0.94 (vs. 0.84), concordance correlation 0.94 (vs. 0.80), mean error 0.05 cm3 (vs. 0.36 cm3)

model_family: multi-task learning with an improved Swin Transformer (spatial and channel reconstruction convolutional Swin block)
patient_population: adolescents with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis undergoing pelvis radiography
clinical_problem: skeletal maturity (Risser stage) assessment for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis evaluation and treatment
model_description: A multi-task deep learning approach extracts the iliac region from pelvis radiographs and forwards it to an improved Swin Transformer to automatically grade Risser stage, a skeletal-maturity measure used in scoliosis evaluation and treatment, aiming to reduce inter- and intra-observer variability seen with manual grading. Grad-CAM visualization was used to interpret model predictions, and code was released on GitHub.
release_evidence: Project address: https://github.com/xyz911015/Risser-stage-assessment
journal: Medical and Biological Engineering and Computing
title: Automatic skeletal maturity grading from pelvis radiographs by deep learning for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
headline_result: Overall accuracy 81.53% for Risser stage assessment, improving on ResNet50 (+5.85%), ResNet101 (+4.6%), Uni-former (+3.6%), Next-ViT (+2.7%), ConvNeXt (+2.25%), and the original Swin Transformer (+1.8%)

model_family: various AI systems for X-ray and sonography support (not individually named)
patient_population: children and adolescents with suspected fractures in pediatric traumatology
clinical_problem: diagnosis and treatment support for fractures in children and adolescents
model_description: This narrative overview reviews the current state of AI applications in pediatric traumatology, covering research and development systems and approved medical products that support X-ray and sonographic fracture diagnosis in children and adolescents. It discusses clinical decision support and raises open questions around traceability, explainability, transparency, and trustworthiness specific to this heterogeneous age group.
title: Children, bones and artificial intelligence: Use of artificial intelligence in pediatric traumatology

model_family: visual state space (VSS) model with evidential training
patient_population: fetal echocardiography images (collected dataset, size not stated in abstract)
clinical_problem: standard view recognition in fetal echocardiography to aid detection of fetal congenital heart disease
model_description: An efficient visual state-space model, trained with an evidential-learning approach, classifies fetal echocardiography images into eight standard anatomical views. It is designed for low computational complexity and fast inference to help sonographers, particularly at primary/resource-limited hospitals, acquire high-quality standard views to improve detection of fetal congenital heart disease.
journal: Medical and Biological Engineering and Computing
title: An efficient network with state space model under evidential training for fetal echocardiography standard view recognition
headline_result: accuracy 99.32%, F1-score 99.29% for classifying 8 standard fetal echocardiography views; lowest FLOPs/parameters/inference time and highest FPS among compared methods

model_family: YOLOv10 object detector with AC-BiFPN multi-scale feature fusion, SimAM attention and WIoU loss
patient_population: children undergoing wrist radiography (GRAZPEDWRI-DX public dataset)
clinical_problem: detection of pediatric wrist fractures on radiographs
model_description: A YOLOv10-based object detector, enhanced with AC-BiFPN for multi-scale feature fusion, a SimAM attention module to emphasize clinically relevant image regions, and a WIoU loss function to reduce both false positives and false negatives, was trained to detect fractures on pediatric wrist radiographs from the public GRAZPEDWRI-DX dataset, intended as a real-time decision-support tool for emergency departments.
journal: Network Modeling Analysis in Health Informatics and Bioinformatics
title: Enhanced diagnosis of pediatric wrist fractures using deep learning
study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study
headline_result: precision 97.4%, recall 95.5%, mAP50 88.5%

model_family: convolutional neural network with ensemble learning
body_region: fetal anatomy (abdomen, brain, femur, thorax, maternal cervix)
patient_population: fetuses undergoing obstetric ultrasound examination
clinical_problem: automatic classification of standard fetal ultrasound planes
model_description: An end-to-end automatic system using convolutional neural networks with ensemble learning classifies fetal ultrasound images into six categories (abdomen, brain, femur, thorax, maternal cervix, other planes), aiming to reduce the time and effort of manual plane identification and improve robustness and accuracy of standard-plane detection.
title: Automatic Detection of Standard Planes in Fetal Ultrasound Images based on Convolutional Neural Networks and Ensemble Learning

model_family: EfficientNet (B0/B1/B2) CNN with SVM and KNN classifiers
patient_population: 947 infants (450 girls, 497 boys) undergoing hip ultrasound, January 2018-September 2021
clinical_problem: diagnosis and Graf classification of developmental dysplasia of the hip
model_description: Hip ultrasound images were classified with EfficientNet convolutional neural networks (B0, B1, B2 variants), without manual image annotation, first into normal (Type 1) versus dysplastic hips, then into four Graf sub-types based on the alpha angle. Support vector machine and k-nearest neighbor classifiers were layered on top of the CNN features to further improve accuracy.
title: Analysis of Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip Using Deep Learning Techniques
headline_result: accuracy 0.9577 (EfficientNetB1) for 2-class classification and 0.8571 (EfficientNetB0) for 4-class classification; with added classifiers, up to 0.99-1.00 (2-class) and 0.97 (4-class)

model_family: 2D convolutional neural network with novel Total Intensity Map input representation
patient_population: Mexican boys aged 7-9 years
clinical_problem: quantification of visceral and subcutaneous abdominal adipose tissue in children for obesity assessment
model_description: A simple 2D CNN takes novel 'Total Intensity Maps' generated from Dixon-based 3T MRI scans and automatically quantifies abdominal subcutaneous (ASAT) and visceral (VAT) adipose tissue in children, compared against the commercial semi-automated AMRA Researcher tool as the reference/gold standard.
title: Automated MRI quantification of pediatric abdominal adipose tissue using convolutional neural networks and novel total intensity maps
dataset_size: Mexican boys aged 7-9 years (sample size not given numerically)
headline_result: High correlation with AMRA Researcher reference (R2=0.98 for ASAT, R2=0.95 for VAT, both P<1e-11); no significant difference in means (ASAT P=0.1765, VAT P=0.7757); reproducibility coefficients 0.32 L (ASAT) and 0.17 L (VAT)

model_family: convolutional neural networks (various, across included studies)
patient_population: children undergoing hand-wrist radiography for bone age assessment, pooled across 33 studies (2019-2024, mostly East Asian in-house cohorts)
clinical_problem: bone age assessment
model_description: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 33 studies applying AI/ML (mostly convolutional neural networks) to estimate bone age from pediatric hand-wrist radiographs, most using radiologist-annotated bone age rather than chronological age as ground truth. Pooled performance across studies reporting mean absolute error (MAE) was synthesized.
title: Artificial Intelligence in Bone Age Assessment of Pediatric Hand-Wrist X-Rays: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Studies from 2019–2024
dataset_size: 33 studies included; mostly in-house hand radiograph datasets from local populations
headline_result: pooled weighted mean absolute error of 7.54 months for bone age estimation across included studies

model_family: InceptionV3 (deep learning CNN, transfer learning), compared against other deep learning models
patient_population: pediatric patients: 1,297 chest radiographs (500 with consolidation, 499 with atelectasis, 298 without opacities)
clinical_problem: differentiating atelectasis from consolidation on pediatric chest radiographs
model_description: A deep learning classification model was trained on 1,297 pediatric chest radiographs labeled as consolidation, atelectasis, or no opacity, to help differentiate types of non-interstitial opacity that can otherwise be difficult to distinguish given the overlapping symptomatology of pediatric respiratory disease. The InceptionV3 architecture performed best among the deep learning models tested, intended to assist radiologists supporting pediatricians in diagnosis.
title: Development of deep learning-based classification models for opacity differentiation in pediatric chest radiography
study_design: retrospective model development and evaluation study
dataset_size: 1,297 chest radiographs (500 consolidation, 499 atelectasis, 298 without opacities)

model_family: deep learning algorithms for detection and segmentation, including multitask and transfer learning
patient_population: fetuses undergoing four-dimensional (4D) ultrasound for fetal facial imaging
clinical_problem: quality assessment and interpretation of 4D fetal facial ultrasound imaging
model_description: Literature review of machine learning and deep learning algorithms applied to four-dimensional fetal facial ultrasound, covering automated detection and segmentation of anatomical structures within the fetal face, scan quality assessment, and multitask/transfer learning strategies developed to address variable convergence rates and limited training data. Does not describe a single named model or quantitative results.
journal: Donald School Journal of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
title: The Capability of Artificial Intelligence Algorithms to Analyze and Interpret Complex Medical Data from Four-dimensional Ultrasound Fetal Facial Imaging: A Literature Review

model_family: deep learning framework with multiscale quality-aware fusion module and clustering-based mix-up (CMX) augmentation
body_region: fetal (general, anatomical structures visualized on prenatal ultrasound)
patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound, evaluated across five public fetal ultrasound image-quality datasets
clinical_problem: automated technical image-quality assessment of fetal ultrasound images
model_description: A deep learning framework automatically scores the technical quality of fetal ultrasound images by fusing multi-scale image features, using a clustering-based mix-up strategy to generate additional training samples, and a custom loss function that directly optimizes for global quality-ranking consistency rather than per-image error alone. It was evaluated on five public fetal ultrasound image-quality datasets.
title: Enhancing fetal ultrasound image quality assessment with multi-scale fusion and clustering-based optimization
headline_result: The framework outperformed other strong competing methods across all five FUIQA datasets tested (specific numeric metrics not given in the abstract)

model_family: compared FCN-8, FCN-32, U-Net, Inception U-Net, and DeepLabv3+ semantic segmentation networks
patient_population: pediatric subjects, from near-skeletally-mature adolescents to younger children, undergoing hand radiography
clinical_problem: semantic segmentation of hand phalanges on pediatric hand radiographs to support growth and skeletal assessment
model_description: Five deep learning segmentation networks (FCN-8, FCN-32, U-Net, Inception U-Net, DeepLabv3+) were trained and compared to segment individual hand phalanges on radiographs, first using near-skeletally-mature subjects, then testing strategies (synthetic scaling-based augmentation and incremental substitution of real pediatric data) to improve generalization to younger pediatric patients whose bone shapes differ due to ongoing growth.
title: Towards growth-accommodating deep learning-based semantic segmentation of pediatric hand phalanges
headline_result: DeepLabv3+ and Inception U-Net performed best on near-skeletally-mature subjects (Mean IoU 0.899 and 0.887); adding 20% real pediatric training data improved Mean IoU by up to 21.1% on pediatric subjects with no adverse effect on near-skeletally-mature performance

model_family: deep learning pipeline (nine models compared) with transfer learning for landmark segmentation and age estimation
patient_population: 742 whole-body CT and 164 pediatric chest-abdomen-pelvis CT scans, ages 1-60 years (437 male, 469 female), with fine-tuning and validation subgroups ages 15-35
clinical_problem: forensic / medico-legal chronological age estimation
model_description: A deep learning pipeline segments the clavicle volume of interest on sternoclavicular joint CT and estimates chronological age, comparing nine deep learning models and using transfer learning fine-tuned on a smaller age group. The model also classifies age thresholds (over 14 and over 18 years) and ossification stage, and its performance was compared with age assessment by a radiologist and two forensic pathologists.
title: Chronological age estimation for medico-legal expertise-based on sternoclavicular joint CT images using a deep neural network
study_design: retrospective model development and validation study
dataset_size: 742 whole-body CT and 164 pediatric chest-abdomen-pelvis CT scans (training); fine-tuning and validation groups of 10 scans each
headline_result: mean absolute error 4.23 ± 4.49 years in cross-validation (3.30 ± 3.58 years after fine-tuning); AUC 0.99 for age classification (>14 and >18 years); accuracy 0.97 for ossification stage classification

model_family: modified U-Net with atrous spatial pyramid pooling and squeeze-and-excitation blocks; YOLOv5 for detection
patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound (public HC18 dataset)
clinical_problem: fetal head circumference measurement on prenatal ultrasound
model_description: The pipeline first detects the fetal head using YOLOv5 with transfer learning, then segments it with SAP-UNet (a modified U-Net incorporating atrous spatial pyramid pooling and squeeze-and-excitation blocks), and finally fits an ellipse to the segmentation to automatically measure head circumference from 2D ultrasound images.
title: Automatic measurement of head circumference in fetal ultrasound images using a squeeze atrous pooling UNet
headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient 98.02%+-0.8, Hausdorff distance 1.20+-0.68 mm, HC difference -0.08+-1.2 mm, HC absolute difference 1.11+-1.3 mm on the HC18 dataset

model_family: various AI/deep learning models (unspecified) for fetal echocardiography image acquisition, measurement and classification
patient_population: fetuses undergoing fetal echocardiography for congenital heart disease screening and diagnosis
clinical_problem: improving detection and diagnosis of congenital heart disease via automated, standardized fetal echocardiography
model_description: Narrative review of AI applications in fetal echocardiography, covering automated image acquisition and optimization, automatic biometric measurement, identification of discrepant values, and diagnosis/classification of congenital heart disease, aiming to standardize examinations, reduce variation in detection rates between regions, and reduce reliance on operator experience. Does not report a single model or quantitative performance figure.
title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence on Fetal Echocardiography

model_family: CNN-transformer hybrid with localized attention mechanisms
body_region: fetal anatomy (maternal-fetal planes, including fetal brain)
