It was trained and evaluated on a real-world clinical ultrasound dataset from multiple practitioners and equipment types, compared against other CNN architectures and a related model (CageVIT).
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Conv-Lamap: A Novel Approach for Maternal-Fetal Ultrasound Analysis Using Convolutional Neural Networks and Transformer
study_design: technical development and comparative evaluation study

model_name: AIM-NT (Automated Identification and Measurement of Nuchal Translucency)
patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound NT assessment, January 2022-October 2023, multicenter
clinical_problem: nuchal translucency plane identification and thickness measurement for prenatal screening
model_description: AIM-NT is a deep learning model that automatically identifies the correct nuchal translucency imaging plane on prenatal ultrasound and measures NT thickness in real time. It was developed and tested on an internal dataset, then evaluated on an external multicenter dataset, with plane identification accuracy, timing, and thickness measurements compared to those of experienced radiologists.
title: Deep Learning Model for Real-Time Nuchal Translucency Assessment at Prenatal US
dataset_size: internal: 3,959 NT images from 3,153 fetuses; external: 267 ultrasound videos from 267 fetuses
headline_result: AUC 0.92 for NT plane identification on internal test set; external accuracy 88.8% (AIM-NT) vs 87.6% (radiologists), P=.69; mean NT measurement difference 0.03 mm, mean absolute error 0.22 mm

model_family: U-Net variant with Zernike Attention, Wavelet Attention, and Morphological Constraint modules
patient_population: fetuses at 18-32 weeks gestation undergoing brain ultrasound
clinical_problem: assessment of fetal brain development via corpus callosum segmentation on prenatal ultrasound
model_description: FB-ZWUNet is an end-to-end deep learning network that automatically segments the corpus callosum on mid-sagittal fetal brain ultrasound images, replacing manual segmentation. It combines a Zernike Attention Module for feature enhancement, a Wavelet Attention Module for feature fusion and reconstruction, and a Morphological Constraint Module for accurate edge and region capture, trained on the FB-CC dataset spanning 18-32 weeks gestation across three ultrasound devices.
title: FB-ZWUNet: A deep learning network for corpus callosum segmentation in fetal brain ultrasound images for prenatal diagnostics
dataset_size: 1,336 annotated fetal brain mid-sagittal ultrasound images (FB-CC dataset)
headline_result: Dice coefficient 0.8743, IoU 0.7813, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in accuracy, stability, and inference speed

model_family: nine machine learning models compared (logistic regression, decision tree, random forest, k-nearest neighbor, SVM, naive Bayes, gradient boosting machine, LightGBM, XGBoost) on MRI radiomics features

clinical_problem: prediction of cerebral palsy risk in infants
model_description: T1- and T2-weighted MRI from infants aged 4 months to 2 years was segmented and 11,190 radiomics features extracted per patient; after feature selection (t-test, LASSO, Z-score normalization), nine machine learning algorithms were trained to predict cerebral palsy risk, with performance compared by ROC analysis and the best model further evaluated with five-fold cross-validation.
journal: Chinese Journal of Anatomy and Clinics
title: Comparison of nine machine learning models based on multi-parameter MRI radiomics for predicting the risk of cerebral palsy in infants
study_design: retrospective single-center case-control diagnostic modeling study
dataset_size: 178 infants (89 cerebral palsy, 89 non-cerebral palsy controls); training set n=142, test set n=36
headline_result: logistic regression model had the best and most stable performance, AUC 0.971 (training) and 0.963 (test), sensitivity/specificity/accuracy approximately 0.93-0.94

patient_population: 45 fetuses imaged with 4D ultrasound across five structured behavioral conditions
clinical_problem: assessment of fetal neuromotor development via facial motor activity
model_description: A commercial AI facial-landmark-tracking engine (Visage|SDK), originally trained on postnatal imagery, was applied to 4D ultrasound video of fetal faces to track facial movements across five conditions (baseline, maternal voice, calming music, stimulating music, recovery). Frame-level tracking success fed into a five-point Fetal Behavioral Arousal Index (FBAI) summarizing facial motor activity intensity and frequency.
release_evidence: a commercial AI engine (Visage|SDK) for facial landmark tracking
journal: Donald School Journal of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
title: Artificial Intelligence-based Characterization of Fetal Facial Motor Activity Patterns Using 4D Ultrasound Imaging
headline_result: Estimated AI frame-level detection success averaged 70.4%; FBAI scores higher during verbal interaction and stimulating music than baseline/calming stimuli (P<0.05); moderate correlation between FBAI and fetal heart rate (r=0.52)

patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound, in the context of commercially marketed AI-enhanced imaging
clinical_problem: diagnostic value and clinical/ethical implications of AI-enhanced ultrasound image rendering
model_description: A narrative integrative review critically evaluates AI-enhanced '8K' fetal ultrasound image rendering, a commercially marketed technology that algorithmically enhances standard 3D ultrasound images for greater visual clarity. The review synthesizes image-quality comparisons between standard 3D ultrasound and AI-enhanced renderings but does not develop a new model itself.
release_evidence: AI-enhanced 8K fetal ultrasound imaging, a rapidly emerging technology marketed as a breakthrough in prenatal diagnostics
journal: Donald School Journal of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
title: 8K Fetal Ultrasound Imaging: Why So Skeptical? A Critical Evaluation of Clinical, Ethical, and Diagnostic Limits
headline_result: No peer-reviewed studies demonstrated enhanced diagnostic accuracy, anomaly detection, or improved perinatal outcomes from AI-enhanced 8K imaging, despite improved perceived visual clarity

model_family: multi-task deep learning model with ShuffleNetV2 backbone, CARAFE feature reassembly, and Coordinate Attention
patient_population: 731 mid-pregnancy women undergoing fetal nasal bone ultrasound
clinical_problem: detection and classification of fetal nasal bone defects (a chromosomal-abnormality marker) on prenatal ultrasound
model_description: FNBUI-NET is a real-time multi-task deep learning model that detects and classifies the fetal nasal bone as normal, dysplastic, or absent on ultrasound images. It integrates a ShuffleNetV2 backbone with a content-aware feature reassembly module and coordinate attention for feature compression, balancing detection speed and accuracy. The authors also built the FNBUI dataset to support this task.
title: FNBUI-NET: A multi-task model for fetal nasal bone ultrasound image defect detection and classification
dataset_size: 1,104 ultrasound images from 731 mid-pregnancy women (FNBUI dataset)
headline_result: mAP@0.5 of 0.985 for nasal bone detection; classification accuracy 0.981, outperforming 18 existing methods

model_family: Vision Transformer (ViT), Data-efficient Image Transformer (DeiT), Vision-LSTM (ViL), Multi-axis Vision Transformer (MaxViT)
patient_population: 200 normal fetuses at 18 to 24+6 weeks gestation undergoing fetal cardiac ultrasound; training set n=140, test set n=60
clinical_problem: classification of standard fetal cardiac ultrasound views
model_description: Four deep learning architectures (ViT, DeiT, ViL, MaxViT) were trained and compared for classifying seven standard fetal cardiac ultrasound views (three-vessel and trachea, apical four-chamber, aortic arch long-axis, bicaval, LVOT, three-vessel, RVOT) in 200 normal fetuses. Gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) heatmaps were used to visualize which image regions (heart and vessels) drove each classification.
journal: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
title: Deep learning models for classifying normal fetal cardiac ultrasound views
study_design: retrospective diagnostic accuracy / model comparison study
headline_result: MaxViT was the best-performing model, with accuracy 98.93%, precision 98.93%, recall 98.95% and F1 score 98.93% for classifying seven standard fetal cardiac views

patient_population: pediatric radiology department patients (general)
clinical_problem: improving pediatric radiology department workflow and image interpretation with AI
model_description: General narrative article on the potential uses of AI across the pediatric radiology workflow, from patient arrival through generation of the radiological report and subsequent follow-up monitoring, with potential to improve examination quality and efficiency, reduce turnaround time to diagnosis, and reduce radiation exposure. Notes that few AI products are currently designed specifically for children, limiting adoption of AI software in pediatric radiology departments. Does not describe a specific model or study.
title: The use of artificial intelligence in the environment of the paediatric radiology department

model_family: automated AI-based brain segmentation technique for regional volumetry
patient_population: 52 children with autism spectrum disorder (DSM-5 diagnosed) and 48 age- and gender-matched typically developing children, single hospital in Qingdao, China, January 2023-April 2024
clinical_problem: characterization of brain structural differences in autism spectrum disorder using automated volumetric segmentation
model_description: 3D T1-weighted 3.0T MRI was obtained from children with autism spectrum disorder and typically developing controls. An automated AI-based brain segmentation technique computed standardized volumes for individual brain structures as a fraction of whole-brain volume, which were compared between groups and correlated with Gesell Developmental Scale scores.
journal: Chinese Journal of Applied Clinical Pediatrics
title: Quantitative analysis of brain volume in children with autism spectrum disorder based on artificial intelligence automatic brain segmentation technology
dataset_size: 52 children with ASD, 48 typically developing controls (100 total)
headline_result: ASD group showed significantly increased volumes in grey matter, orbitofrontal cortex, hippocampus and several other regions and decreased pericalcarine cortex/posterior corpus callosum volume (all P<0.05); right thalamus volume negatively correlated with Gesell adaptation quotient (r=-0.276, P=0.048)

model_family: elastic-net penalized linear regression on MRI radiomic features
patient_population: 160 neonates with gestational age ≥35 weeks and neonatal encephalopathy treated with therapeutic hypothermia at a quaternary neonatal neurocritical care unit, born 2018-2022
clinical_problem: prediction of 18-month neurodevelopmental outcome after perinatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE)
model_description: Radiomic features were extracted from deep-gray matter structures and 2,224 whole-brain image tiles on MRI obtained on postnatal day 4-5 after therapeutic hypothermia in neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy. These features were input to an elastic-net penalized linear regression model, evaluated with 10-fold cross-validation, to predict cognitive, language and motor developmental outcomes at 18 months (Bayley Scales), and predictor weights were mapped back into brain regions.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Neuroprognostication via Spatially-Informed Machine Learning Following Hypoxic-Ischemic Injury
study_design: retrospective single-center cohort study with cross-validated model development
headline_result: mean correlation between predicted and observed 18-month Bayley outcomes 0.947; mean coefficient of determination 0.879 across cognitive, language and motor domains (10-fold cross-validation)

model_family: quantized variational autoencoder with multi-head attention conditioning (3D CNN and transformer), contrastive learning
patient_population: children requiring multi-contrast MRI for cerebral palsy diagnosis, for whom deep, thin-slice acquisition is limited by uncooperative movement
clinical_problem: early diagnosis of cerebral palsy via multi-contrast MRI slice-thickness synthesis
model_description: CaT-MDT takes thick-slice, lower-resolution multi-contrast MRI (e.g. T1, T2, FLAIR) from children, who often cannot tolerate long high-resolution scans, and synthesizes thinner-slice, higher-information images while limiting partial-volume effects. It uses a quantized variational autoencoder with attention conditioned on the desired slice depth and contrastive learning across modalities of the same subject, aiming to retain lesion and biological trait information (age, sex, weight) to support cerebral palsy diagnosis and lesion identification.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Pathognomics and Phenotype Transformation in Depthwise Brain MRI Synthesis for Early Intervention in CP Diagnosis
headline_result: translation quality MAE 0.159, SSIM 0.988, PSNR 63.13; higher cerebral palsy prediction scores at multiple slice-depth translation levels

model_family: machine learning model using structural connectome gradient features
patient_population: children with structural connectome gradients measured by MRI at age 1, followed to assess IQ in early and middle childhood
clinical_problem: prediction of later cognitive ability (IQ) from early brain structural connectivity
model_description: Structural connectome gradients, representing continuous spatial variation in brain structural connectivity, were derived from MRI acquired at age 1. Machine learning was used to predict future intelligence quotient (IQ) in early and middle childhood from these gradient features, testing whether early structural organization relates to later cognitive variability.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Structural Connectome Gradients and Their Relationship to IQ in Early Childhood
study_design: prospective cohort study using machine learning

model_family: image-processing/segmentation pipeline with fast ellipse fitting; segmentation backbones compared included HRNet
patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound exams
clinical_problem: fetal growth assessment via head circumference, biparietal diameter, and occipitofrontal diameter measurement
model_description: The algorithm takes a segmented fetal head ultrasound image, from any of several compared segmentation models, and applies a fast ellipse-fitting method to automatically compute head circumference, head orientation, biparietal diameter, and occipitofrontal diameter. Three segmentation models were compared, with HRNet performing best, to demonstrate the approach's compatibility with different segmentation backbones.
journal: Journal of Engineering and Science in Medical Diagnostics and Therapy
title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Estimation of Fetal Head Circumference With Biparietal and Occipitofrontal Diameters Using Two-Dimensional Ultrasound Images
headline_result: HRNet segmentation backbone achieved the best average Dice score of 0.96 among the three compared models

model_family: three-stage age- and modality-conditioned deep learning generative framework (compared with LGAN, CounterSyn, and a diffusion-based approach)
patient_population: 139 infants from the Baby Connectome Project (mean age ~11-13 months), T1- and T2-weighted MRI
clinical_problem: synthesizing missing longitudinal infant brain MRI time points for developmental modeling
model_description: The framework takes existing longitudinal T1- and T2-weighted infant brain MRI scans and synthesizes missing time points, conditioned on age and modality, modeling volumetric expansion, cortical folding, and myelination. Trained on 119 infants and tested on 20 from the Baby Connectome Project, it also performs tissue segmentation and cortical reconstruction on the synthesized images, intended to support developmental modeling and longitudinal analyses when imaging time points are missing.
title: A Deep Learning Framework for Synthesizing Longitudinal Infant Brain MRI during Early Development
dataset_size: 848 MRI scans from 139 infants (119 training, 20 test)
headline_result: PSNR 25.44-26.93, SSIM 0.87-0.90 for image synthesis (outperforming comparators, P<.001); DSC 0.85 (gray matter) and 0.86 (white matter) for tissue segmentation

model_family: unsupervised deep learning framework using two generative networks (image decomposition) with symmetry, adversarial and uniformity losses
patient_population: MRI datasets from healthy adults, brain tumor patients, infants, and mice (multi-population technical validation)
clinical_problem: correction of MRI intensity bias-field artifact to improve downstream image analysis
model_description: An unsupervised deep learning framework decomposes a 3D brain MRI into a clean image and its bias field using two interacting generative networks, trained with a symmetry-based loss alongside adversarial and uniformity losses, without requiring matched clean/biased training pairs. It was evaluated on MRI from healthy adults, brain tumor patients, infants, and mice, and outperformed traditional and other deep learning bias-field correction methods.
release_evidence: abstract states "the code will be made publicly available" (not yet available at time of publication)
title: Unsupervised Bias Field Correction Via Deep Image Decomposition and Symmetry

model_family: radiomics with LASSO feature selection and a nomogram combining radiomics score and MRI findings
patient_population: 113 children with medulloblastoma and 31 children with ependymoma
clinical_problem: differentiating medulloblastoma from ependymoma in children
model_description: Radiomics features were extracted from ADC, T2WI and DCE-T1WI MRI sequences of children with posterior fossa tumors, and LASSO regression selected features to compute a radiomics score. A nomogram combining the radiomics score with MRI findings was built to differentiate medulloblastoma from ependymoma preoperatively, with single-sequence and combined-sequence models compared.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: ​Multi-Parameter MRI Radiomics Differential Diagnosis of Medulloblastoma and Ependymoma in Children
dataset_size: 113 patients with medulloblastoma, 31 with ependymoma (144 total)
headline_result: combined three-sequence radiomics nomogram achieved AUC 0.981 (primary cohort) and 0.939 (validation cohort); best single-sequence (ADC) model AUC 0.936/0.924

patient_population: 776 subjects from the ADHD-200 Global Competition dataset, collected at three data centers, children being the study focus
clinical_problem: diagnosis of ADHD using brain functional connectivity
model_description: Seed-based correlation was used to extract functional connectivity features from resting-state fMRI focused on default mode network regions relevant to ADHD, and a convolutional neural network was trained to classify children with ADHD versus controls, benchmarked against an SVM and a random forest classifier on the public ADHD-200 dataset.
title: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder identification: FMRI data analyzed with CNN and seed-based approach
study_design: retrospective classification model development using a public dataset
dataset_size: 776 subjects from the ADHD-200 dataset (three data centers)

model_name: FNB-ADS (Fetal Nasal Bone development Automated Diagnostic System)
model_family: cascaded pipeline: YOLOv8 detection, lightweight segmentation network, ResNet34 classification
patient_population: fetuses undergoing early-pregnancy mid-sagittal ultrasound screening
clinical_problem: prenatal screening for chromosomal abnormality via fetal nasal bone development assessment
model_description: FNB-ADS is a cascaded deep learning pipeline for early prenatal fetal nasal bone (FNB) screening: YOLOv8 localizes the FNB region on mid-sagittal ultrasound images, a lightweight network segments the nasal bone, tip, and prenasal skin, and a ResNet34 classifier diagnoses developmental abnormalities. The authors also released a public image and video dataset (FNB-UDV) for this task.
release_evidence: The dataset and code are available at https://github.com/SIGMACX/FNB-AD/tree/FNB-ADS
title: Automatic diagnosis of early pregnancy fetal nasal bone development based on complex mid-sagittal section ultrasound imaging
dataset_size: 1,007 two-dimensional ultrasound images and 12 ultrasound videos (FNB-UDV dataset)
headline_result: Image diagnostic accuracy 92.37% with 0.14 s per-image processing time; video diagnostic accuracy 98.69% with 0.37 s per-frame inference speed

model_family: deep learning segmentation models (TransBTS, MedNeXt, MedicalNet) plus a segmentation-free classifier with segmentation-informed pretraining
patient_population: 455 patients with molecularly-characterized pediatric low-grade glioma treated between 1999 and 2023 at a single tertiary care children's hospital
clinical_problem: non-invasive prediction of BRAF mutation status in pediatric low-grade glioma
model_description: Whole-brain FLAIR MRI from children with low-grade glioma was used to train and compare three medical image segmentation models (TransBTS, MedNeXt, MedicalNet), then a segmentation-free classifier was developed to predict BRAF status directly from the whole-brain FLAIR sequence without relying on any manual or automated segmentation, using a pretraining strategy that embeds segmentation knowledge into the classifier. Performance was compared with a baseline model using manual tumor segmentations as input.

title: Segmentation-Free Pretherapeutic Assessment of BRAF-Status in Pediatric Low-Grade Gliomas
headline_result: MedNeXt segmentation Dice 0.555 (best of three models); segmentation-free classifier AUC 0.741 for BRAF status, improved to 0.772 with segmentation-informed pretraining, not significantly different from the manual-segmentation baseline (0.756, p=0.141)

model_family: deep learning anatomical landmark localization on 3D slice-to-volume reconstructed MRI
patient_population: fetuses at 20-40 weeks gestation undergoing 3D T2-weighted fetal brain MRI; retrospective evaluation on 90 cases, prospective evaluation on 111 cases across varied gestational ages, field strengths and scan parameters; normative centiles from 406 normal controls (19-40 weeks)
clinical_problem: automated fetal brain biometry reporting for prenatal assessment of brain maturation
model_description: Deep learning models localize 13 routinely reported linear fetal brain biometry landmarks on 3D slice-to-volume-reconstructed T2-weighted MRI, automatically computing measurements and growth centiles and generating an html report, removing reliance on manual 2D measurements that are affected by fetal motion and inconsistent plane selection. The fully automated pipeline was evaluated retrospectively and prospectively across a wide range of scanners and gestational ages.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Towards automated fetal brain biometry reporting for 3-dimensional T2-weighted 0.55-3T magnetic resonance imaging at 20-40 weeks gestational age range
study_design: retrospective and prospective technical development and validation study
dataset_size: 90 retrospective cases, 111 prospective cases, 406 normal controls for centile charts
headline_result: more than 98% of landmark placements graded acceptable in prospective evaluation; automated vs. manual measurement difference within 1-3mm; processing time under 5 minutes per case

model_family: attention module combined with existing CNN and transformer-based segmentation models
body_region: whole body (bone scan), chest, and brain across different experiments
patient_population: adolescents undergoing whole-body bone scans, among other imaging cohorts used to validate the general method
clinical_problem: segmentation of lesions in noisy nuclear medicine images and other medical images, leveraging anatomical symmetry
model_description: Deformable Symmetry Attention (DSA) is an attention module that exploits left-right anatomical symmetry to improve automated lesion segmentation on grainy nuclear medicine images. It reflects the image to leverage symmetry, applies deformable registration to correct local anatomical variation, and redistributes attention with learnable Gaussian kernels to address pixel-level noise. It was combined with CNN and transformer segmentation models and tested on several tasks, including lesion segmentation on adolescent whole-body bone scans, 3D MRI brain tumor segmentation, and chest X-ray anatomical segmentation.
title: Deformable symmetry attention for nuclear medicine image segmentation
headline_result: 3.8% to 8.48% Dice improvement segmenting lesions in adolescent whole-body bone scans; 2.88% improvement in 3D MRI brain tumor segmentation; 0.63% to 10.57% improvement in chest X-ray anatomical segmentation

patient_population: children aged 0-6 months undergoing hip ultrasound screening
clinical_problem: screening and diagnosis of developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH)

Reports that AI-assisted ultrasound has better diagnostic accuracy and efficiency than traditional methods, while raising concerns about over-diagnosis and over-treatment; does not describe a single named model or specific quantitative performance metrics.
title: Research progress and controversy of traditional and artificial intelligence-assisted ultrasound in diagnosing DDH in children aged 0-6 months

patient_population: 94 adolescents with depression and 78 age- and gender-matched healthy adolescents, recruited at a single hospital's psychiatric imaging outpatient department
clinical_problem: diagnosis of adolescent depression from brain functional connectivity

title: Brain network connectivity and classification model of adolescent depression based on resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging and machine learning
headline_result: classification accuracy 70.35%, sensitivity 70.21%, specificity 71.80%, AUC 0.724 (95% CI 0.648-0.800) for diagnosing adolescent depression

headline_result: diagnostic accuracy of 90.17%, comparable to fine-tuned CNN approaches reported in the literature

clinical_problem: assessment of renal function and detection of scarring in chronic kidney disease

title: Modern concept of using imaging methods in radionuclide kidney studies in children

title: Deep-learning Segmentation of Pediatric Brain Tumors using Ratio Maps of T1w/T2w MRI Signal Intensity

clinical_problem: low-dose chest CT image quality for congenital heart disease imaging
model_description: This prospective study compared an AI-based iterative reconstruction algorithm (AIIR) with conventional hybrid iterative reconstruction (HIR) for low-dose chest CT in infants with congenital heart disease. Low-dose scans reconstructed with AIIR were compared subjectively and objectively against low-dose HIR images and conventional-dose HIR images. AIIR-reconstructed low-dose images matched the image quality of conventional-dose images while lowering the effective dose.
journal: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
title: Artificial intelligence iterative reconstruction for low-dose chest CT images of infants with congenital heart disease
headline_result: Subjective scores of low-dose AIIR images did not differ from conventional-dose HIR images (most comparisons P>0.05); effective dose fell from 0.85 mSv (conventional) to 0.09 mSv (low-dose).

clinical_problem: spatial registration/localization of 2D fetal cranial ultrasound slices to support standard-plane radiomics analysis of fetal brain development

title: Unsupervised spatial registration of fetal cranial ultrasound slices for radiomics analysis
headline_result: plane angle error 6.870 degrees, Euclidean distance 8.969 voxels, normalized cross-correlation 0.882, structural similarity 0.771

model_family: Spider Wasp Optimization (SWO) feature selection combined with K-Nearest Neighbor classifier, using features from a ResNet50V2 residual learning architecture
patient_population: pediatric patients with brain tumors (brain MRI from King Abdullah Hospital)
clinical_problem: classification of pediatric brain tumor type
model_description: The model classifies pediatric brain tumor type from MRI images. Features are extracted with a ResNet50V2 deep learning architecture, then a Spider Wasp Optimization metaheuristic algorithm selects the most informative features, which are fed into a K-Nearest Neighbor classifier for binary and multiclass tumor classification. It was compared against other deep learning architectures (MobileNetV2, ResNet50V2) and machine learning classifiers (KNN, SVM, Random Forest).
journal: Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine Update
title: A novel deep learning-based spider wasp optimization approach for enhancing brain tumor detection and physical therapy prediction

dataset_size: brain MRI images from King Abdullah Hospital (exact n not stated)

patient_population: paediatric focal epilepsy patients (17 MRI-lesion-positive, 14 MRI-negative; 26 evaluable after exclusions), plus 10 healthy volunteers used for network training
clinical_problem: detection of subtle cortical lesions in pediatric focal epilepsy surgery evaluation
model_description: A 3D U-Net, trained on paired 3T and 7T MRI from 10 healthy volunteers, enhances quantitative R1 relaxation maps acquired at standard 3T field strength to approximate the image quality of ultra-high-field 7T MRI. It was applied to 3T R1 maps from a separate cohort of pediatric focal epilepsy patients scanned at a different site, and radiologists compared lesion visibility and detection on the AI-enhanced maps versus original 3T maps and 3D-FLAIR.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Artificial Intelligence enhanced R1 maps can improve lesion detection in focal epilepsy in children
study_design: retrospective technical development with radiological review
dataset_size: 10 healthy volunteers for training; 17 MRI-positive and 14 MRI-negative pediatric epilepsy patients for application
headline_result: Lesions detected on AI-enhanced R1 maps in 14/15 (93%) MR-positive and 4/11 (36%) MR-negative patients, with superior image quality compared to original 3T R1 maps and 3D-FLAIR

model_family: dual-encoder CNN segmentation network with boundary feature enhancement and channel recalibration modules
patient_population: children with pneumonia undergoing chest CT
clinical_problem: segmentation of pneumonia-infected lung regions on chest CT in children
model_description: A dual-encoder deep learning network segments pneumonia-infected regions on pediatric chest CT. A boundary feature enhancement module uses prior contour labels and multi-directional edge detectors with cross-attention to sharpen lesion boundaries, while a channel recalibration module suppresses background noise, together improving segmentation of small, low-contrast infected regions; the network also generalized to adult COVID-19 CT images.
title: Boundary and channel double calibrated CT segmentation network for pneumonia in children
headline_result: Dice, Jaccard index, sensitivity and Matthews correlation coefficient improved by 2.99%, 4.76%, 2.56% and 3.03% respectively versus the best-performing comparison network on pediatric pneumonia CT

patient_population: adolescents with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS)
clinical_problem: quantifying spinal deformity severity in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
model_description: The uAI DR scoliosis analysis system automatically measures multiple spinal alignment parameters (Cobb angle, coronal balance distance, T1 slope, pelvic tilt, sacral slope, apical vertebral translation, thoracic trunk shift, thoracic kyphosis, sagittal vertical axis) from anteroposterior and lateral spinal radiographs. The study correlated these AI-measured parameters with AIS severity and coronal/sagittal balance status in a large retrospective cohort.
release_evidence: Parameters were measured using the named 'uAI DR scoliosis analysis System' software product.
journal: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
title: Correlations of artificial intelligence measured parameters on anteroposterior and lateral spinal X-ray films with severity of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
headline_result: Cobb angle, coronal balance distance, apical vertebral translation and thoracic trunk shift increased significantly with AIS severity (all P<0.001); T1 slope, apical vertebral translation and thoracic trunk shift were independent predictors of severity.

model_family: MLP-based, Transformer-based, and U-Net/CNN-based deep learning architectures (compared)
patient_population: 488 infant subjects from the developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP) and Baby Connectome Project (BCP)
clinical_problem: estimation of fiber orientation distributions from diffusion MRI to study early brain development, addressing generalizability across scanners and protocols
model_description: Three deep learning architectures (MLP-based, transformer-based, and U-Net/CNN-based) were trained to estimate fiber orientation distribution functions from infant diffusion MRI, and their robustness to domain shifts (scanner/protocol differences, age, number of input gradient directions) was systematically evaluated. Two adaptation strategies, method-of-moments and fine-tuning, were tested to correct inter-site domain shift, with fine-tuning giving the best results.

title: Domain shifts in infant brain diffusion MRI: Quantification and mitigation for fODF estimation
headline_result: U-Net outperformed other models with fewer diffusion gradient directions; performance plateaued from 28-45 input directions across all models; fine-tuning outperformed method-of-moments for correcting inter-site domain shift

title: PW-GAN: Pseudo-Warping Field Guided GAN for Unsupervised Denoising of Fetal Brain MRI Images
dataset_size: not stated precisely (simulated and in vivo data)
headline_result: Outperforms existing unsupervised denoising models and achieves performance on par with several state-of-the-art supervised methods

title: Recognition of normal fetal echocardiogram based on an explainable denosing deep learning model
headline_result: Accuracy 97.1%, precision 97.1%, recall 97.0%, F1-score 97.0% in validation; AUCs of 0.994, 0.928, and 0.932 on three separate test sets

clinical_problem: pneumonia detection on chest X-ray

title: Improving Pneumonia Diagnosis with Radimagenet: A Deep Transfer Learning Approach
dataset_size: not stated precisely (chest X-ray images of children aged 1-5)

model_family: 3D diffusion and symmetrical attention-based frequency-domain adaptive global feature network (DSA-FAGFNet), CNN-based
patient_population: children undergoing head/orbital CT for suspected orbital fracture
clinical_problem: screening for pediatric orbital fractures
model_description: PIOFSF is a deep learning pipeline for screening pediatric orbital fractures on CT: it performs 3D reconstruction, corrects for head tilt so the orbits are symmetrically aligned, localizes the orbits using clustering and a Hough transform, then classifies fracture presence with a 3D network (DSA-FAGFNet) combining diffusion-based orbital position coding, symmetrical attention and frequency-domain feature extraction, aiming to catch subtle fractures that are often missed or misdiagnosed as other conditions in children.
title: PIOFSF: A deep learning-based pediatric inferior orbital fracture screening framework

model_family: AI-assisted bone age assessment (architecture not stated), applied to three established prediction formulas (Bayley-Pinneau, Tanner-Whitehouse 3, China 05)

title: Comparison of three artificial intelligence-assisted bone age assessment methods for predicting adult height in girls
headline_result: TW3 and BP methods overestimated adult height by 2.6+-3.0 cm and 1.7+-3.7 cm; China 05 underestimated by 2.3+-3.5 cm; proportion of predictions within +-5 cm of final height: TW3 80.0%, BP 77.0%, China 05 74.2% (P=0.038)

title: Utilization of artificial intelligence in echocardiographic imaging for congenital heart disease: a narrative review

It was trained on normal-anatomy and congenital diaphragmatic hernia cases across 0.55T, 1.5T and 3T scanners, and used to generate normal fetal lung volumetry growth charts.

study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study
dataset_size: public AASCE challenge dataset plus a private hospital dataset (sizes not stated)

Its output was compared against two expert sonographers using intraclass correlation and Kappa statistics, and its processing speed was compared to manual quality control.
title: Establishment and validation of an artificial intelligence model for ultrasound image quality control in early pregnancy

model_family: hybrid AI model combining view detection and structural segmentation (deep learning)
patient_population: 47 fetuses: 15 anemic (diagnosed via umbilical venous puncture) and 32 normal controls, 2018-2024
clinical_problem: quantitative assessment of fetal cardiac size, morphology and function in fetal anemia
model_description: A hybrid AI model combining four-chamber view detection with structural segmentation extracts a panel of fetal cardiac size, shape, and function measurements (chamber lengths, ventricular diameters, sphericity indices, strain, fractional area change and shortening) and their Z-scores from four-chamber echocardiographic ultrasound videos. It was used to compare anemic and normal fetuses, and its measurement agreement with conventional fetal HQ software was assessed by intraclass correlation.
title: Application of a hybrid artificial intelligence model integrating view detection and structural segmentation in evaluating cardiac function of anemic fetuses

headline_result: AI-based measurements agreed well with conventional fetal HQ technology (ICC 0.788 control, 0.837 anemia); anemic fetuses showed larger right ventricular dimensions, lower ventricular sphericity indices, and reduced LVGLS/LVFAC (P<0.05 to P<0.001)

clinical_problem: nuchal translucency measurement and screening for fetal abnormality

In this study it was used as a training aid: after an initial round of independent NT identification, measurement and diagnosis, two resident sonographers received additional AI-assisted training, then all sonographers performed a second independent round that was compared to a fetal medicine expert's blinded review. The AI model itself was not the subject of an accuracy evaluation here, only its effect on trainee performance.
title: Value of artificial intelligence in assisting ultrasound residents training for the identification，measurement and diagnosis of fetal nuchal translucency thickness
headline_result: AI-assisted training significantly improved NT measurement standardization rate in both resident sonographers (chi2=25.768 and 17.035, both P<0.05) and diagnostic accuracy in one resident (chi2=10.180, P<0.05); traditional lecture-only training produced no significant improvement in the middle-age sonographer

clinical_problem: pediatric brain tumor segmentation and prognosis when MRI sequences are missing from the exam

title: AI-Powered Segmentation and Prognosis with Missing MRI in Pediatric Brain Tumors

clinical_problem: standardized identification of prenatal ultrasound screening planes
model_description: A VMamba-based model was trained to automatically recognize 21 standard prenatal ultrasound screening planes/sections from 2D images. Its classification performance was compared against ResNet-50, Swin-Transformer, ConvNeXtV2, RepViT, and MSPANet, with Grad-CAM heat maps and t-SNE plots used to check whether the model attended to the correct anatomical structures.
journal: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
title: Intelligent recognition of prenatal ultrasound standard sections based on VMamba model
headline_result: VMamba achieved the best performance among compared models: sensitivity 94.54%, specificity 99.72%, accuracy 94.42%, AUC 0.997, F1 0.944.

patient_population: fetuses with prenatally screened ocular malformations and normal controls
clinical_problem: prenatal diagnosis of fetal ocular malformations
model_description: A Swin-Transformer-based model was trained on fetal ophthalmic ultrasound images to distinguish normal fetal eyes from ocular malformations. Its diagnostic performance was compared against MobileNet-V2, ResNet-50, VGG-16 and Vision-Transformer models, with heat maps and confusion-matrix/t-SNE analysis used to assess interpretability.
journal: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
title: Intelligent auxiliary model based on Swin-Transformer for diagnosing fetal ocular malformations
dataset_size: 1,282 ophthalmic ultrasound images of malformed fetal eyes and 526 images of normal fetal eyes (8:1:1 train/validation/test split)
headline_result: The Swin-Transformer model achieved sensitivity 88.31%, specificity 97.37%, AUC 0.990, precision 87.31%, F1 87.71% in the test set, outperforming the four comparison models.

patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing point-of-care ultrasound in emergency and critical care settings
clinical_problem: use of AI to support point-of-care ultrasound in pediatric emergency and critical care
model_description: This review assesses the advantages and limitations of AI-assisted point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) in pediatrics. It reports that AI-assisted models can improve image acquisition and diagnostic accuracy, particularly for less-experienced users, and can augment training in settings with limited ultrasound expertise, while cautioning that most models are trained on adult data and need pediatric-specific validation before use.
title: Artificial intelligence meets point-of-care ultrasound: implications for pediatric emergency and critical care

patient_population: 500 adolescent idiopathic scoliosis individuals (200 training, 300 validation)
clinical_problem: automatically measuring Cobb angle from whole-spine radiographs in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, compared to manual measurement
model_description: A fully automated deep learning framework identifies vertebral boundaries and landmarks on whole-spine radiographs to automatically calculate Cobb angles (proximal thoracic, main thoracic, thoracolumbar/lumbar curves) in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
title: The Comparison of Convolutional Neural Networks and the Manual Measurement of Cobb Angle in Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis.
headline_result: mean absolute error 2.92 degrees (major curve), ICC 0.967, r=0.972; 88.7% within +/-5 degrees

model_family: machine learning (vendor automated software, deep learning-based border detection)
patient_population: 50 normal volunteers (children and young adults)
clinical_problem: Can fully automated machine learning-based echocardiographic analysis reliably measure left ventricular volumes, ejection fraction, and strain in children and young adults compared to manual measurement?
model_description: Takes echocardiographic images as input; AutoLV and AutoSTRAIN (TomTec) software automatically detect endocardial borders and output LV volumes, ejection fraction, and myocardial strain.
release_evidence: AutoLV and AutoSTRAIN (TomTec) were employed for the fully automated LV analysis
title: Machine Learning-Enabled Fully Automated Assessment of Left Ventricular Volume, Ejection Fraction and Strain: Experience in Pediatric and Young Adult Echocardiography.
headline_result: Strong correlation with manual EF (r=0.8373) and GLS (r=0.9766); analysis time significantly shorter with automated methods

model_family: YOLOX-based deep instance segmentation neural network
patient_population: fetal echocardiography (congenital heart disease screening)
clinical_problem: automated localization and segmentation of cardiac anatomical structures in the fetal four-chamber view, to support congenital heart disease diagnosis and growth-parameter measurement
model_description: Input: fetal four-chamber-view ultrasound images; output: instance segmentation of 13 types of cardiac anatomical structures.
journal: IEEE/ACM transactions on computational biology and bioinformatics
title: A YOLOX-Based Deep Instance Segmentation Neural Network for Cardiac Anatomical Structures in Fetal Ultrasound Images.
study_design: methods development and comparison against baseline segmentation methods
headline_result: Outperforms nine competitive baseline methods (no single summary metric reported)

model_family: anatomical landmark detection with automated parameter computation
patient_population: 100 preoperative full spine radiographs of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients
clinical_problem: computing the coronal parameters that classify an adolescent idiopathic scoliosis curve and guide surgical planning
model_description: Detects clavicles, cervical, thoracic and lumbar spine and sacrum and computes T1 tilt, clavicle angle, coronal balance, lumbar modifier and the regional Cobb angles, with no human input, on every image attempted. Agreement with two experienced raters was excellent, and the pattern of which parameters are hardest matched the humans' — proximal thoracic Cobb angle worst, coronal balance and clavicle angle best.
title: Novel AI-Based Algorithm for the Automated Computation of Coronal Parameters in Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis Patients: A Validation Study on 100 Preoperative Full Spine X-Rays.
headline_result: intraclass correlation with human raters 0.78-0.98 across all parameters, computed on 100% of images; mean error 4.7 degrees for proximal thoracic Cobb angle and 0.2 degrees for clavicle angle

model_family: hierarchical (shifted-window) vision transformer for cortical surface meshes
patient_population: neonates (preterm and term) from the Developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP); also tested on adult UK Biobank and MindBoggle datasets
clinical_problem: neonatal brain phenotyping and cortical parcellation from surface MRI data
model_description: A transformer backbone processes cortical surface meshes by applying self-attention within local mesh windows and merging patches hierarchically, producing representations usable for multiple downstream tasks. It was evaluated for predicting neonatal phenotypes from dHCP surface data and, built into a segmentation architecture, for cortical parcellation on adult datasets.
release_evidence: Code and trained models are publicly available at https://github.com/metrics-lab/surface-vision-transformers
title: The Multiscale Surface Vision Transformer.
dataset_size: dHCP neonatal dataset; UK Biobank and MindBoggle datasets for parcellation
headline_result: Outperforms existing surface deep learning methods for neonatal phenotyping prediction; competitive results on cortical parcellation on UK Biobank and MindBoggle

patient_population: 540 pregnant women with suspected placenta accreta spectrum from two institutions (409 training, 103 internal test, 28 external test)
clinical_problem: diagnosing placenta accreta spectrum antenatally from MRI to assist radiologists, especially less experienced ones
model_description: An nnU-Net segments the placenta on T2-weighted MRI, then DenseNet-based classifiers analyze the utero-placental border region and placental position to diagnose placenta accreta spectrum, using histopathology as ground truth.
journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
title: A Deep Learning Pipeline Using Prior Knowledge for Automatic Evaluation of Placenta Accreta Spectrum Disorders With MRI.
study_design: retrospective multi-institution diagnostic model development study
dataset_size: 540 pregnant women (409 training, 103 internal test, 28 external test) from two institutions
headline_result: AUC 0.860 (internal test), 0.897 (external test), exceeding 3 radiologists (AUC 0.737-0.770)

patient_population: 324 pregnant women (mean age 33.3) with suspected placenta accreta spectrum, across two institutions
clinical_problem: Can deep learning radiomics from prenatal MRI improve the diagnosis of placenta accreta spectrum disorders, which is currently unsatisfactory using MRI alone?
model_description: A deep-learning-radiomics model extracts features from T2-weighted pelvic MRI using a pretrained network (MedicalNet) and combines them with a clinical model and radiologists' morphologic assessment to diagnose placenta accreta spectrum.
journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
title: Prenatal Diagnosis of Placenta Accreta Spectrum Disorders: Deep Learning Radiomics of Pelvic MRI.
study_design: retrospective multicenter model development with external validation
dataset_size: 324 pregnant women (170 training, 72 internal validation, 82 external validation)
headline_result: MRI-based deep learning radiomics model AUC 0.880 (training), 0.861 (internal validation), 0.852 (external validation), outperforming the clinical model and MRI morphologic assessment alone

model_family: Deep learning (CNN with learnable atrous spatial pyramid pooling)
patient_population: Fetuses undergoing Doppler ultrasound assessment (collaboration with International Peace Maternity and Child Health Hospital of China)
clinical_problem: Automating fetal middle cerebral artery segmentation and Doppler gate placement to reduce sonographer workload when assessing risk of adverse perinatal outcomes.
model_description: Input: fetal ultrasound Doppler images. Output: automated segmentation of the middle cerebral artery region and detection of the correct Doppler gate position, via a CNN with a learnable atrous spatial pyramid pooling module.
journal: IEEE/ACM transactions on computational biology and bioinformatics
title: MCAS-GP: Deep Learning-Empowered Middle Cerebral Artery Segmentation and Gate Proposition.

patient_population: Children with high-grade glioma across multiple international pediatric neuro-oncology consortia
clinical_problem: Benchmarking automated segmentation algorithms for pediatric brain gliomas via a standardized multi-institutional challenge, to speed development of tools useful for clinical trials and care.
model_description: A community challenge (BraTS-PEDs 2023) providing standardized multiparametric structural MRI training, validation and test data for pediatric brain glioma, to benchmark volumetric segmentation algorithms using shared quantitative performance metrics.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: The Brain Tumor Segmentation (BraTS) Challenge 2023: Focus on Pediatrics (CBTN-CONNECT-DIPGR-ASNR-MICCAI BraTS-PEDs).

model_family: deep keypoint registration network with angle computation
patient_population: 986 neonates aged 0-6 months, with 2,406 images from 921 patients labeled by senior orthopedists
clinical_problem: universal newborn screening for developmental dysplasia of the hip, which ultrasound could deliver if there were enough experienced operators
model_description: Places the five anatomical keypoints that Graf's method requires on a hip ultrasound and derives the alpha and beta angles from them, rather than classifying the image directly. That makes the output auditable against the classification system clinicians already use. The stated motivation is screening capacity: ultrasound is the right test for hip dysplasia, and the shortage of experienced operators is what prevents universal screening.
title: Automatic and human level Graf's type identification for detecting developmental dysplasia of the hip.
dataset_size: 2,406 images from 921 patients, of 986 neonates screened
headline_result: keypoint error about 1 mm, alpha angle correlation 0.89 with ground truth, AUC 0.937 for alpha below 60 degrees and 0.974 for below 50; experts agreed with 96% of inferred images

model_family: two-step U-Net cascade feeding a radiomics classifier
patient_population: children with pediatric low-grade glioma
clinical_problem: predicting BRAF status in pediatric low-grade glioma without the manual tumor outlining that radiomics normally requires
model_description: Removes the manual step that keeps radiomics out of practice: one network locates the tumor on a downsampled image, a second refines the outline on patches, and the automatic segmentation then feeds the genetic-marker classifier. The result worth noting is the comparison against the same radiomics model run on manual segmentations, which it nearly matched — meaning automation cost little accuracy.
journal: Canadian Association of Radiologists journal = Journal l'Association canadienne des radiologistes
title: MRI-Based End-To-End Pediatric Low-Grade Glioma Segmentation and Classification.
headline_result: segmentation Dice 0.795; classification AUC 0.843 (two-class) and 0.730 (three-class) from automatic segmentations versus 0.874 and 0.758 from manual ones

patient_population: 239 children (83 male; 3.6-14.6 years) with pituitary MRI and GnRH stimulation test
clinical_problem: noninvasively determine activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis in peri-puberty children using pituitary MRI radiomics, as an alternative to GnRH stimulation testing
model_description: Radiomics features extracted from sagittal 3D T1-weighted pituitary MRI, selected via LASSO, are used to build a model predicting hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis activation status, compared against conventional pituitary height/volume measurements.
journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
title: MRI Radiomics Features of Adenohypophysis Determine the Activation of Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Gonadal Axis in Peri-Puberty Children.
study_design: retrospective diagnostic radiomics model development and validation
headline_result: AUC 0.81 (95% CI 0.71-0.91) in test set

model_family: support vector machine on T2-weighted radiomic features
patient_population: 135 participants (mean age 15.2 years), 70 with ileal Crohn disease, retrospectively identified and prospectively enrolled
clinical_problem: diagnosing ileal Crohn disease on MR enterography, where reader performance and agreement vary considerably
model_description: Extracts radiomic features from four regions on non-contrast T2-weighted images and classifies ileal Crohn disease, with endoscopy and biopsy as the reference. The comparison against three fellowship-trained pediatric abdominal radiologists is the useful part, as is the finding that the bowel-core region carried nearly all the signal while mesenteric fat and whole-bowel regions performed worse.
title: Machine Learning Diagnosis of Small-Bowel Crohn Disease Using T2-Weighted MRI Radiomic and Clinical Data.
headline_result: best region (bowel core) AUC 0.95 and accuracy 89.6%, against radiologist accuracies of 83.7-88.1% and consensus accuracy 88.1%

patient_population: 20 children (median age 12 years, range 4-18 years) undergoing presurgical epilepsy evaluation
clinical_problem: detecting focal cortical dysplasia lesions on structural MRI to guide electrode placement in children undergoing stereoelectroencephalography for drug-resistant epilepsy
model_description: Machine learning lesion-detection algorithm run on structural MRI to identify putative focal cortical dysplasia clusters, used prospectively to guide additional SEEG electrode placement in children with drug-resistant epilepsy
title: Lesion detection in epilepsy surgery: Lessons from a prospective evaluation of a machine learning algorithm.
study_design: prospective single-arm interventional IDEAL phase 1/2a study
headline_result: algorithm-identified clusters collocated with the seizure-onset zone in 4 of 19 patients; changed resection boundaries in 1 of 19 patients, who was seizure-free at 1 year

patient_population: 2,989 children (adolescents, mean age 13.5 years) from the Generation R cohort
clinical_problem: quantifying subcutaneous and visceral abdominal fat in adolescents noninvasively from MRI to study childhood obesity
model_description: A 2D competitive dense fully convolutional network (2D-CDFNet) automatically segments subcutaneous and visceral adipose tissue on Dixon MRI in adolescents.
release_evidence: The model used (gitlab.com/radiology/msk/genr/abdomen/cdfnet) is publicly available.
title: Automated Deep Learning-Based Segmentation of Abdominal Adipose Tissue on Dixon MRI in Adolescents: A Prospective Population-Based Study.
dataset_size: 2,989 children (62 training, 8 validation, 15 test for segmentation; 504 for visual assessment; 2,820 for correlation analysis)
headline_result: Dice 0.94 (subcutaneous fat), 0.85 (visceral fat); correlation with DEXA fat mass 0.941 (SAT), 0.801 (VAT)

model_family: AI-derived morphological severity score from CT
patient_population: 41 children aged 6-18 with surgically corrected metopic synostosis, tested at a mean age of 10.8 years
clinical_problem: whether how severe a metopic craniosynostosis looks on imaging predicts how the child reads and learns at school age
model_description: Uses an AI-derived quantification of skull morphology severity, rather than a subjective grade, and relates it to neurocognitive testing years after surgery. Greater AI-derived severity was associated with poorer reading comprehension, and older age at surgery with poorer visuomotor integration. The cohort is small, but the design is the interesting one: an automated imaging measurement used as an exposure in a long-term outcome study rather than as a diagnostic output.
title: Morphologic Severity and Age at Surgery Are Associated with School-Age Neurocognitive Outcomes in Metopic Craniosynostosis.
study_design: retrospective cohort with long-term neurocognitive testing
headline_result: greater AI-derived severity was significantly associated with lower reading comprehension and reading composite scores (P = 0.008-0.040)

model_name: AERO (Artificial intelligence Evaluation of Renogram Obstruction)
patient_population: 304 patients (two institutions), median age of diuretic renogram 4 months (IQR 2-7 months)
clinical_problem: predicting risk of renal obstruction to decide whether diuretic renography can be safely deferred in children with hydronephrosis
model_description: takes routine ultrasound findings (kidney length, AP diameter, SFU grade, age, sex) as input and outputs a predicted risk category of obstruction on diuretic renography
release_evidence: deployed in an easy-to-use web application (https://sickkidsurology.shinyapps.io/AERO/)
title: Predicting obstruction risk using common ultrasonography parameters in paediatric hydronephrosis with machine learning.
study_design: retrospective multi-institutional model development with external validation
headline_result: binary AUROC 0.84; external validation AUROC 0.76

patient_population: not stated (editorial/comment, no abstract)
clinical_problem: detection of retinal hemorrhage (a marker of abusive head trauma) on pediatric head CT
model_description: Editorial comment discussing a study on deep learning for detection of retinal hemorrhage on pediatric head CT. No abstract text was provided describing the underlying model or results.
title: Beyond the AJR: Deep Learning Shows Promise in the Detection of Retinal Hemorrhage on Pediatric Head CT.

patient_population: 241 pediatric neuroblastoma patients from two centers
clinical_problem: predicting bone marrow involvement in pediatric neuroblastoma using PET/CT
model_description: Input: 18F-FDG PET/CT radiomics features from tumor and axial skeleton regions plus clinical factors; output: nomogram predicting presence of bone marrow involvement in neuroblastoma.
title: 18F-FDG PET/CT-Based Radiomics Nomogram for Prediction of Bone Marrow Involvement in Pediatric Neuroblastoma: A Two-Center Study.
study_design: retrospective two-center radiomics study with external validation
headline_result: radiomics nomogram AUC 0.932 (training), 0.887 (internal validation), 0.733 (external validation)

patient_population: 64 children with medulloblastoma, Shenzhen Children's Hospital
clinical_problem: Preoperatively predicting short-term recurrence/prognosis risk in pediatric medulloblastoma from multiparametric MRI
model_description: Radiomics features from preoperative multiparametric MRI are selected and combined with clinical variables via an SVM classifier and multivariate logistic regression to build a radiomics nomogram predicting 18-month progression-free survival.
title: Multiparametric MRI-Based Radiomics Signature with Machine Learning for Preoperative Prediction of Prognosis Stratification in Pediatric Medulloblastoma.
headline_result: AUC 0.926 (training)/0.835 (validation) for radiomics nomogram

patient_population: fetal ultrasound standard plane benchmark dataset
clinical_problem: automatically identify standard fetal ultrasound scan planes to reduce operator dependence, optimized for portable low-power ultrasound devices
model_description: Knowledge distillation transfers learned representations from a large teacher deep learning network to a smaller, computationally efficient student network for automatic classification of fetal ultrasound standard planes, suitable for portable ultrasound devices.
title: Knowledge distillation for efficient standard scanplane detection of fetal ultrasound.
study_design: methods development and benchmark evaluation study

model_family: whole-body segmentation network with a quality estimation module
patient_population: 348 fetuses at 19-39 weeks: 249 appropriate for gestational age, 19 with growth restriction, 80 with other abnormalities
clinical_problem: estimating fetal weight, and detecting growth restriction, from MRI rather than ultrasound formulas
model_description: Segments the whole fetal body on MRI and derives an estimated weight, then builds an MRI-based normal growth chart from the normal cases. The evaluation is unusually thorough about the things that decide whether a measurement is usable: repeatability on repeat scans in the same scanner, reproducibility across scanners, and accuracy against actual birth weight. It correctly identified every fetus below the tenth birth-weight centile, and found three referred as normal who were in fact below the third.
title: Deep learning-based segmentation of whole-body fetal MRI and fetal weight estimation: assessing performance, repeatability, and reproducibility.
study_design: retrospective study with repeatability and reproducibility analysis
headline_result: Dice 0.973, repeatability coefficient 4.01%, ICC 0.99; estimated weight differed from birth weight by -0.39% on average; correctly predicted all 18 fetuses below the 10th birth-weight centile

patient_population: children imaged in radiology practice
clinical_problem: the harms AI can cause in a pediatric setting that are not visible from its accuracy figures
model_description: A deliberately sceptical companion to the enthusiastic reviews: it works through AI ethics, bias, limitations and unintended consequences for patients, for society and for the profession, with attention to what is specific about a pediatric population. Worth reading alongside the position statements rather than instead of them.
title: The unintended consequences of artificial intelligence in paediatric radiology.

model_family: machine learning (decision tree regression, among others)
patient_population: Indian population undergoing pelvis/abdomen CT (children through middle-aged adults)
clinical_problem: Estimate chronological age from iliac crest ossification on CT for forensic/legal age determination in children through young adults
model_description: Takes CT-based modified Risser stage scoring of the iliac crest as input to regression and machine learning models (including decision tree regression), outputting an estimated chronological age.
title: Machine learning and regression analysis for age estimation from the iliac crest based on computed tomographic explorations in an Indian population.
headline_result: Decision tree regression: inaccuracy 1.88 years, RMSE 2.28 years, superior to regression models (best compound regression inaccuracy 4.78 years)

patient_population: patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
clinical_problem: automatically measuring the Cobb angle on spine X-rays to assess and classify the severity of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
model_description: CNN-based algorithm that detects and labels thoracic and lumbar vertebrae on X-ray images, then computes the Cobb angle, deformity type, severity grade, and Lenke classification
title: Auto-CA: Automated Cobb Angle Measurement Based on Vertebrae Detection for Assessment of Spinal Curvature Deformity.
headline_result: Cobb angle measurement median difference <5° from ground truth (SMAPE 5.27%); classification accuracy 0.958 (deformity type) and 0.962 (severity), 0.924 for Lenke classification

patient_population: 1,173 participants aged 5-18 years in Mexico
clinical_problem: adult height prediction from bone age assessment
model_description: BoneXpert automatically reads bone age from hand radiographs and its output is fed into adult-height-prediction models, compared against manual bone age readings by two expert radiologists. The study compares BoneXpert-based and manual-reading-based adult height predictions against measured population height.
release_evidence: BoneXpert is referenced with a registered trademark (BoneXpert®) as an existing automated commercial bone age reading method
title: Evaluation of height prediction models: from traditional methods to artificial intelligence.
headline_result: BoneXpert-based adult height prediction had the smallest difference from population mean height for males; manual readings showed up to 43% of interobserver predictions differing by more than 5 cm

model_family: radiomics and deep learning AI models (automated segmentation and prediction)
body_region: neuroblastoma and diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma
patient_population: pediatric oncology patients with neuroblastoma and diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma
clinical_problem: how AI-derived imaging biomarkers and radiomics can noninvasively improve diagnosis and prognosis in pediatric neuroblastoma and diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma
model_description: Review of the PRIMAGE European multi-center project, an open-cloud platform combining MRI, clinical, and molecular data with AI models (automated tumor detection/segmentation, radiomics and deep-feature extraction) to support personalized diagnosis and prognosis for pediatric neuroblastoma and diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma
title: Imaging biomarkers and radiomics in pediatric oncology: a view from the PRIMAGE (PRedictive In silico Multiscale Analytics to support cancer personalized diaGnosis and prognosis, Empowered by imaging biomarkers) project.
study_design: review describing a multi-center AI platform project (PRIMAGE)
headline_result: automated tumor segmentation tool achieved a Dice similarity coefficient of 0.997 on an independent validation dataset

patient_population: not stated (editorial, no abstract)
clinical_problem: differentiating juvenile myoclonic epilepsy from generalized tonic-clonic seizures using MRI radiomics
model_description: Editorial commenting on a study using an MRI-based radiomics approach to differentiate juvenile myoclonic epilepsy from epilepsy with generalized tonic-clonic seizures alone. No abstract text was provided describing the underlying model or results.
journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
title: Editorial for "MRI-Based Radiomics Approach for Differentiating Juvenile Myoclonic Epilepsy From Epilepsy With Generalized Tonic-Clonic Seizures Alone".

patient_population: 11,875 youths (ages 9-10 years at baseline) from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study
clinical_problem: identifying a brain-connectivity-based transdiagnostic dimension linking cognition and psychopathology risk in preadolescents
model_description: Takes resting-state functional MRI connectome data as input and outputs a latent brain-connectivity pattern, identified via canonical correlation analysis, that is associated with cognitive function and psychopathology and is evaluated for its ability to predict future psychiatric diagnosis transitions over 2-year follow-up.
title: Brain Functional Connectome Defines a Transdiagnostic Dimension Shared by Cognitive Function and Psychopathology in Preadolescents.
study_design: prospective multi-site longitudinal cohort study (ABCD) with machine-learning latent-factor analysis
headline_result: 5-fold cross-validation correlation ρ=0.68-0.73 (training set), ρ=0.56-0.58 (test set); heritability h²=74.42%

model_family: support vector machine (with PCA feature selection)
patient_population: 54 children (31 with ASD, 23 controls)
clinical_problem: Testing whether airway branching geometry on chest CT can serve as an imaging biomarker for autism spectrum disorder
model_description: A PCA-based feature-selection and SVM classifier that takes airway branching-angle measurements from chest CT as input and classifies children as ASD versus control.
title: Can lung airway geometry be used to predict autism? A preliminary machine learning-based study.
headline_result: Cross-validation accuracy ~89%, sensitivity 94%, specificity 78%

model_family: deep learning classifier, previously trained at a tertiary center
patient_population: 66 pregnancies with isolated severe congenital heart disease and 42 normal fetuses from a Dutch region, screened in community practice in 2015-2016
clinical_problem: congenital heart defects missed at the routine second-trimester anomaly scan in a low-risk population
model_description: Takes a model developed on tertiary-center images and tests it on stored images from ordinary community screening, which is the transfer that usually breaks. It did not: the model reached 91% sensitivity where the original clinical reading had caught only half the cases, and where three blinded human experts working from the same stored images averaged 55%. Model correctness varied with image quality, which points at where the remaining errors come from.
journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
title: Deep-learning model for prenatal congenital heart disease screening generalizes to community setting and outperforms clinical detection.
headline_result: model sensitivity 91% and specificity 78%, versus 53% sensitivity for the original clinical diagnosis and 55% for blinded human experts on the same stored images

patient_population: 100 patients who underwent vertebral body tethering at a single institution
clinical_problem: measuring interscrew angle to monitor tether integrity and growth modulation after vertebral body tethering surgery for scoliosis
model_description: a U-Net segments vertebral body screws on AP/PA radiographs, then an image-processing algorithm computes the interscrew angle from the segmentation
journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
title: Automated measurements of interscrew angles in vertebral body tethering patients with deep learning.
study_design: single-institution retrospective algorithm development and validation
headline_result: segmentation Dice 0.96; mean absolute interscrew-angle error 0.66 degrees (range 0-2.67 degrees)

patient_population: Fetal four-chamber ultrasound views (patients not further quantified in the abstract), compared against national/local screening programme data
clinical_problem: How does an AI model for detecting hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) on prenatal ultrasound compare to the current national prenatal screening programme's real-world performance?
model_description: A ResNet-based classifier takes four-chamber fetal cardiac ultrasound views as input and outputs a prediction of hypoplastic left heart syndrome, calibrated as either a high-sensitivity or high-specificity model and compared to the current national screening programme's detection performance.
title: Prenatal diagnosis of hypoplastic left heart syndrome on ultrasound using artificial intelligence: How does performance compare to a current screening programme?
study_design: retrospective comparative study of AI model versus real-world national screening programme performance
headline_result: Current screening programme: sensitivity 94.3%, specificity 99.985%; AI model either sensitivity 100%/specificity 94.0% or sensitivity 93.3%/specificity 100% depending on calibration; AI alone performed slightly worse than the screening programme

patient_population: fetuses 18-32 weeks gestation, images from 2017-2018; validated on 836 videos (12,697 images) from four hospitals
clinical_problem: real-time evaluation of fetal ultrasound image quality and completeness of standard anatomical views, to assist inexperienced operators in fetal anomaly screening
model_description: YOLOv3-based deep learning system (PSAIS) with global (anatomic site) and local (structure) feature extraction that evaluates the quality of fetal ultrasound anatomical images in real time, recognizing 19 standard views and indicating existing or missing structures, validated against expert assessment
journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
title: Development and validation of an artificial intelligence assisted prenatal ultrasonography screening system for trainees.
study_design: retrospective multicenter development and external validation study
dataset_size: 134,696 training images; 836 validation videos (12,697 images) from four hospitals
headline_result: internal validation multiclass macro-average AUC 0.943 (95% CI 0.815-1.000); external validation AUC 0.958 (0.864-1.000); micro-average AUC 0.974/0.973; 90.9% accurate labeling of similar-to-standard views

patient_population: 30 children with ASD, 26 matched controls, and their 48 biological parents
clinical_problem: predicting autism spectrum disorder risk in offspring from parental sensory profile
model_description: Sensory fMRI responses to sensory stimuli were measured in children with and without ASD and in their biological parents. A machine learning model trained on the parents' sensory response profile was used to predict the likelihood of autism spectrum disorder in their offspring.
title: A sensory signature of unaffected biological parents predicts the risk of autism in their offspring.
headline_result: Parental sensory profile predicted offspring ASD likelihood with 71.4% accuracy

patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal facial ultrasound screening
clinical_problem: automated detection of fetal facial anatomy on standard ultrasound planes for facial malformation screening
model_description: Input is a 2D fetal facial ultrasound image; a YOLOv5s object detection network localizes and classifies facial anatomical structures on standard facial planes, intended to help physicians automatically screen standard sections during prenatal ultrasound examination.
journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
title: Detection of fetal facial anatomy in standard ultrasonographic sections based on real-time target detection network.
headline_result: Precision 98.3%/98.1% and recall 99.3%/98.2% (single-class structure detection and three-standard-plane structure detection/classification experiments, respectively)

model_family: commercial deep learning fracture and effusion detection
patient_population: 712 children (mean age 7.3 years, range 7 months to 15 years) presenting consecutively to an emergency room with elbow trauma
clinical_problem: elbow trauma in children, where the fracture is often invisible and only a joint effusion betrays it
model_description: An external validation on consecutive real emergency attendances, scored four ways including detection of joint effusion, which is the finding that matters most in a child's elbow because the fracture itself frequently is not visible. Eleven senior radiologists set the reference. The authors end on the number a department should weigh: 8% of the radiographic sets the algorithm called normal came from children who did have a traumatic lesion.
release_evidence: external validation of an AI solution
title: External validation of an artificial intelligence solution for the detection of elbow fractures and joint effusions in children.
headline_result: sensitivity above 89% on all four approaches, highest at 95.0% for lesion detection; specificity 63-77%; 8% of sets ruled out by the algorithm belonged to children with a genuine traumatic lesion

patient_population: 164 patients (127 JME, 37 GTCA), mean age 24.0+/-9.6 years, including adolescents
clinical_problem: Can MRI-based radiomics differentiate juvenile myoclonic epilepsy from epilepsy with generalized tonic-clonic seizures alone, and predict prognosis, when conventional MRI appears normal?
