model_description: Uses simulated pediatric-sized image-quality phantoms across the newborn-to-18-year size range as input to an adult-trained REDCNN deep-learning CT denoiser, evaluating how image quality metrics change relative to adult phantoms.
title: Pediatric evaluations for deep learning CT denoising.
dataset_size: pediatric-sized phantoms spanning newborn to 18 years
headline_result: 60% noise SD reduction in adult phantoms; reduced denoising performance in smaller pediatric phantoms due to FOV-driven noise texture differences

model_family: radiomics with machine learning classifiers (KNN, logistic regression, SVM)
patient_population: 440 pediatric patients with biopsy-proven Henoch-Schonlein purpura nephritis
clinical_problem: Can ultrasound-based radiomics noninvasively classify the histopathological severity (glomerular crescent formation) of Henoch-Schonlein purpura nephritis in children, avoiding biopsy?
model_description: Takes manually drawn regions of interest on renal ultrasound images as input; radiomics features are extracted and fed into machine learning classifiers (KNN, LR, SVM) that output classification of glomerular crescent formation (ISKDC grade group).
title: Ultrasound-Based Radiomics for the Classification of Henoch-Schönlein Purpura Nephritis in Children.
headline_result: Best model (SVM) AUC 0.870, sensitivity 0.706, specificity 0.950 in validation cohort

patient_population: 306 children aged 1-18 (153 boys, 153 girls, 18 per year of life) in a German cohort
clinical_problem: whether a bone age product can be swapped in for an expert reader, not merely correlate with one
model_description: Tests interchangeability rather than agreement, which is the stricter and more decision-relevant question: can the software substitute for one of three blinded expert readers without changing the answer. It could, within the age range the product is declared for. Performance was slightly worse in boys, and the bias was constant across the range rather than drifting at the extremes.
release_evidence: evaluates an AI software with a declared intended-use age range
title: Automated bone age assessment in a German pediatric cohort: agreement between an artificial intelligence software and the manual Greulich and Pyle method.
dataset_size: 306 children, 243 in the declared intended-use subgroup
headline_result: mean difference from the three-expert average 0.39 months, mean absolute difference 6.8 months (6.0 months in the intended-use subgroup); judged interchangeable with expert readers

model_family: hybrid deep learning (U-Net + Bi-LSTM-CNN with metaheuristic optimization)
patient_population: public benchmark datasets HC18 and ORA-data (ultrasound video frames)
clinical_problem: measuring fetal head circumference from ultrasound to monitor fetal growth and health
model_description: Takes fetal ultrasound images/video frames as input, segments the fetal head using a hybrid optimization algorithm and improved U-Net, then estimates head circumference biometry using a hybrid bi-directional LSTM-CNN model.
title: Fetal growth analysis from ultrasound videos based on different biometrics using optimal segmentation and hybrid classifier.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development study using public benchmark datasets

model_family: radiomics machine learning pipeline (FeAture Explorer / PyRadiomics) with logistic regression

clinical_problem: differentiating H3 G34-mutant diffuse hemispheric glioma from IDH-wild-type glioblastoma in adolescents and young adults
model_description: Conventional MRI features (VASARI) and radiomics features extracted with PyRadiomics are used to build a logistic regression / machine-learning pipeline (FeAture Explorer) that differentiates H3 G34-mutant diffuse hemispheric glioma from IDH-wild-type glioblastoma.
title: MRI characteristics of H3 G34-mutant diffuse hemispheric gliomas and possible differentiation from IDH-wild-type glioblastomas in adolescents and young adults.
headline_result: radiomics-based model AUC 0.925 vs. VASARI-feature model AUC 0.843

patient_population: 66 treatment-naive adolescents with MDD and 52 matched healthy controls
clinical_problem: Distinguishing adolescents with treatment-naive major depressive disorder from healthy controls using a novel resting-state fMRI measure of intrinsic neural timescale
model_description: Input: resting-state fMRI intrinsic neural timescale (INT) maps; output: classification distinguishing MDD from healthy controls at the individual level, via multivariate pattern analysis
title: Decreased intrinsic neural timescale in treatment-naïve adolescent depression.
headline_result: INT distinguished MDD from HC using multivariate pattern analysis (specific accuracy not given as a single number)

model_family: 3D residual neural network (multimodal, fusing low-dose CT)
patient_population: 270 pediatric patients undergoing total-body 18F-FDG PET/CT (uEXPLORER scanner)
clinical_problem: reducing pediatric total-body PET/CT scan time (and sedation need) while preserving image quality
model_description: Short-duration PET list-mode data (6-150 s) and low-dose CT images are fused as input to a 3D residual convolutional neural network that outputs a full-length, high-dose-quality PET image, aiming to shorten scan time without sedation-related motion artifacts.
title: Reducing pediatric total-body PET/CT imaging scan time with multimodal artificial intelligence technology.
study_design: retrospective single-center technical development and evaluation
headline_result: 60-second multimodal AI reconstruction produced PET image quality comparable to the full 600-second acquisition

model_family: deep learning pipeline (classifier plus two U-Net 3+ segmentation models)
patient_population: 250 cardiac MRI examinations from 13 institutions in patients with Fontan circulation (congenital heart disease, adults and children); further evaluated on 475 additional unseen examinations
clinical_problem: automated ventricular volume and function quantification in patients with single ventricle (Fontan) physiology on cardiac MRI
model_description: Takes cardiac MRI short-axis cine images as input and outputs automated segmentation of the single ventricle plus volumetric and functional metrics (end-diastolic and end-systolic volume, mass, stroke volume, ejection fraction), using a deep learning pipeline of a cine-stack classifier and two U-Net 3+ segmentation models.
title: A Deep Learning Pipeline for Assessing Ventricular Volumes from a Cardiac MRI Registry of Patients with Single Ventricle Physiology.
study_design: retrospective multicenter registry study with algorithm development and validation
dataset_size: 250 cardiac MRI examinations from 13 institutions (50 held-out test set); 475 additional unseen examinations
headline_result: Dice score 0.91 (EDV) and 0.86 (ESV); ICC>0.97 for ventricular volumes; satisfactory segmentation in 68% of 475 unseen exams, minor adjustments needed in 26%

model_family: XGBoost, random forest, SVM, decision tree (SHAP explainable ML)
patient_population: 90 children diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder
clinical_problem: diagnosing autism severity level using physical fitness and gray matter volume from brain MRI
model_description: Input: physical fitness test results and gray matter volume from brain MRI; output: machine-learning classification of autism severity, with SHAP-based feature explanation.
title: Diagnosing autism severity associated with physical fitness and gray matter volume in children with autism spectrum disorder: Explainable machine learning method.
headline_result: XGB model accuracy 77.9% (95% CI 77.3-78.6%), best of four models

patient_population: pediatric neuroradiology patients (general)
clinical_problem: how AI will influence access to care, workflow, diagnosis, and outcomes in pediatric neuroradiology
task: detection / diagnosis; outcome prediction; report generation / LLM; workflow / non-interpretive
model_description: Narrative review of current and anticipated AI applications in pediatric neuroradiology, spanning access to care, workflow management, abnormality detection/classification, response prediction, prognostication, report generation, and rare-disease pattern recognition.
title: Artificial Intelligence in the Future Landscape of Pediatric Neuroradiology: Opportunities and Challenges.

patient_population: 131 healthy children and young adults (62 male, 69 female; mean age 16.6+/-3.9 years)
age_groups: child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: Establishing normal reference values for global and layer-specific myocardial strain in healthy children and young adults using AI-based cardiac MRI strain analysis
model_description: TrufiStrain deformable-registration research prototype software analyzes cine cardiac MRI to automatically compute global and layer-specific (endocardial-to-epicardial) myocardial strain values (longitudinal, radial, circumferential).
title: Utilizing Artificial Intelligence-Based Deformable Registration for Global and Layer-Specific Cardiac MRI Strain Analysis in Healthy Children and Young Adults.
headline_result: Peak global longitudinal strain -16.0+/-3.0%, radial strain 29.9+/-6.3%, circumferential strain -17.0+/-1.8%

patient_population: 83 Wilms tumor and 33 clear cell sarcoma cases in children
clinical_problem: differentiating Wilms tumor from clear cell sarcoma of the kidney in children using CT radiomics, to guide pre-surgical diagnosis
model_description: Radiomics features extracted from corticomedullary-phase CT images of pediatric renal tumors are combined into a logistic regression model that outputs the probability of Wilms tumor versus clear cell sarcoma of the kidney.
title: CT radiomics to differentiate between Wilms tumor and clear cell sarcoma of the kidney in children.
study_design: retrospective single/primary-cohort study with internal train/test split and cross-validation
headline_result: AUC 0.889 training, 0.792 test set; accuracy 0.864 training, 0.857 test

patient_population: 314 participants with narcolepsy (adolescent and young adult); 204 type 1, 90 type 2, 20 type 1+schizophrenia
clinical_problem: Using machine learning on brain PET imaging to differentiate narcolepsy subtypes (type 1 vs type 2, and with comorbid schizophrenia).

title: The application of machine learning on brain imaging features of different narcolepsy subtypes.
headline_result: Naive Bayes classifier with 3 ROIs achieved accuracy >99%

patient_population: 86 medulloblastomas from 59 male and 27 female pediatric patients
clinical_problem: rapid, non-invasive pre-surgical classification of medulloblastoma molecular subgroup using metabolite profiles measurable by in vivo MR spectroscopy
model_description: Input: tumor metabolite concentrations (10 metabolites quantifiable by in vivo MR spectroscopy); output: predicted medulloblastoma molecular subgroup (WNT, SHH, Group3, Group4), via a support vector machine classifier.
title: Metabolite profiles of medulloblastoma for rapid and non-invasive detection of molecular disease groups.
study_design: retrospective diagnostic model development with cross-validation
dataset_size: 86 medulloblastoma tumor samples (59 male, 27 female patients)
headline_result: tissue-based SVM classifier cross-validated accuracy 89% (100% for WNT); in vivo MRS-adapted classifier accuracy 90% for SHH/Group3/Group4

patient_population: 62 children with autism spectrum disorder and 44 typically developing children
clinical_problem: classifying autism spectrum disorder from white matter microstructure
model_description: Multi-shell diffusion MRI is processed to compute diffusion tensor, diffusion kurtosis, and white matter tract integrity metrics along white matter tracts. The metrics that differed significantly between groups were used to train an XGBoost model to classify children as having autism spectrum disorder or being typically developing, with SHAP values used to rank feature importance.
title: Exploring White Matter Abnormalities in Young Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: Integrating Multi-shell Diffusion Data and Machine Learning Analysis.
dataset_size: 62 children with ASD, 44 typically developing controls
headline_result: XGBoost model demonstrated excellent classification ability distinguishing ASD from typically developing children (exact AUC not given)

patient_population: pregnant patients, second and third trimester
clinical_problem: estimating gestational age from brief ultrasound videos as a quality-control tool to flag substandard fetal biometry measurements
model_description: Input: brief 'fly-to' cineloop ultrasound videos acquired during routine biometry; output: estimated gestational age, used to flag grossly inaccurate (e.g. novice-level) biometry measurements.
journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
title: Deep learning to estimate gestational age from fly-to cineloop videos: A novel approach to ultrasound quality control.
study_design: retrospective model development and validation against expert measurement
headline_result: MAE 3.87±0.07 days (vs 4.80±0.10 days expert biometry); AUC 0.93 for flagging gross errors, sensitivity 81.0%, specificity 89.9%

patient_population: Newborns and infants ("babies") from two cohorts undergoing diffusion MRI
clinical_problem: Investigating domain-shift and generalization challenges of deep-learning models estimating white-matter fiber orientation in newborn and infant brains across scanners and ages.
model_description: Input: diffusion MRI from newborn and infant brains, from different scanners/protocols. Deep-learning models estimate fiber orientation distribution functions; the study evaluates cross-age and cross-site domain shift and mitigation via fine-tuning with a small number of target-domain samples.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: CROSS-AGE AND CROSS-SITE DOMAIN SHIFT IMPACTS ON DEEP LEARNING-BASED WHITE MATTER FIBER ESTIMATION IN NEWBORN AND BABY BRAINS.

patient_population: 173 ultrasound scan videos (98 normal hearts, 75 AVSD) yielding 121,130 four-chamber images; 10 clinicians (fetal cardiologists, trainees, sonographers) tested on 500 images across 4 conditions
clinical_problem: Detecting fetal atrioventricular septal defect (AVSD) on prenatal cardiac ultrasound four-chamber images, and studying how AI advice (with or without confidence/explanation) affects clinician diagnostic accuracy
model_description: Input: fetal four-chamber cardiac ultrasound images; output: binary classification (normal vs. AVSD) with confidence score and Grad-CAM overlay, via a ResNet50 model, studied in human-AI collaboration experiments
journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
title: Interaction between clinicians and artificial intelligence to detect fetal atrioventricular septal defects on ultrasound: how can we optimize collaborative performance?
study_design: retrospective model development with prospective reader study of human-AI collaboration
dataset_size: 121,130 images from 173 videos (98 normal, 75 AVSD); reader study of 500 images, 20,000 classifications from 10 clinicians
headline_result: AI alone accuracy 0.798; clinicians alone 0.844; clinicians with correct AI binary output 0.865 (P<.001); accuracy fell to 0.693 with incorrect AI advice

model_family: deep learning segmentation with Dempster-Shafer theory fallback/fail-safe mechanism
patient_population: 540 manually annotated fetal brain MRIs from 13 centers, including fetuses with various brain abnormalities
clinical_problem: detecting and correcting failures in automated fetal brain MRI segmentation so results are safe to use clinically
model_description: Takes a 3D T2-weighted fetal brain MRI and a backbone AI model's segmentation as input, and outputs a corrected voxel-level brain segmentation with unreliable predictions detected and replaced by a Dempster-Shafer-theory-based fallback.
journal: IEEE transactions on pattern analysis and machine intelligence
title: A Dempster-Shafer Approach to Trustworthy AI With Application to Fetal Brain MRI Segmentation.
study_design: retrospective multi-center algorithm development and validation study
dataset_size: 540 fetal brain 3D T2-weighted MRIs from 13 centers

patient_population: fetuses undergoing echocardiography, across the reviewed literature
clinical_problem: operator dependence in fetal echocardiography, where missing congenital heart disease costs survival
model_description: A systematic review of AI in fetal echocardiography organized by what the model does: image processing, biometry, and disease diagnosis. Its framing is the skill gap — fetal echocardiography depends heavily on operator experience and equipment, and the argument for AI here is bridging that gap between regions rather than outperforming an expert.
journal: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography
title: Advances in the Application of Artificial Intelligence in Fetal Echocardiography.

patient_population: 91 AIS patients who underwent AVBT surgery, Shriners Hospitals for Children Philadelphia
clinical_problem: Predicting short- and mid-term spinal curve correction after anterior vertebral body tethering surgery in adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis.
model_description: A Gradient Boosting Regressor model takes clinical, radiographic and surgical parameters as input and predicts final Cobb angle curve correction after AVBT surgery.
title: Predicting radiographic outcomes of vertebral body tethering in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients using machine learning.
headline_result: Average prediction error 6.3±5.6 degrees; 84% of actual values within 90% prediction interval

model_family: electromagnetic navigation system described as 'based on artificial intelligence' (details not specified)
patient_population: 22 hemifacial microsomia patients aged 3-18 years
clinical_problem: Whether an AI-based electromagnetic surgical navigation system improves osteotomy accuracy during mandibular distraction osteogenesis for hemifacial microsomia in children
model_description: An electromagnetic tracking navigation system, described as artificial-intelligence-based, uses preoperative 3D CT scans and surgical plans to provide real-time guidance during osteotomy for mandibular distraction osteogenesis, compared to traditional (unguided) surgery
title: Efficacy of navigation system-assisted distraction osteogenesis for hemifacial microsomia based on artificial intelligence for 3 to 18 years old: study protocol for a randomized controlled single-blind trial.
headline_result: Study protocol only; no outcome results reported yet

patient_population: 119 depressed/anxious youth at familial risk for bipolar disorder (age 14.9±1.6) and 57 typically developing controls (age 14.8±1.7)
clinical_problem: characterizing brain connectome abnormalities in youth at familial risk for bipolar disorder using task-based fMRI
model_description: Generalized psychophysiological interaction analysis derives task-based fMRI connectome patterns, and machine learning of topological network metrics is used to classify high-risk youth vs. controls.
journal: Journal of child psychology and psychiatry, and allied disciplines
title: Aberrant brain network topology in youth with a familial risk for bipolar disorder: a task-based fMRI connectome study.
headline_result: Case-control classifier cross-validation accuracy 78.4%

model_family: convolutional neural network (segmentation) plus custom measurement code
patient_population: children undergoing standing lower limb radiographs for skeletal pathology assessment
clinical_problem: automated measurement of lower limb alignment (mechanical/anatomic axes) in children
model_description: A CNN segments pediatric weight-bearing lower limb radiographs; custom code then extracts anatomic landmarks from the segmentation to automatically calculate mechanical axis deviation and other alignment angles, compared against manual measurements by orthopaedic fellows.
title: Fully Automated Analysis of the Anatomic and Mechanical Axes From Pediatric Standing Lower Limb Radiographs Using Convolutional Neural Networks.
study_design: retrospective single-center model development compared to manual measurement
headline_result: mechanical axis deviation within mean 2.02 mm; lateral distal femoral angle mean deviation 1.73 degrees; ~2 seconds per radiograph

patient_population: 98 adult and pediatric patients, 137 head and neck CT scans, 8 orientations
clinical_problem: Automatically contour organs at risk for head and neck radiotherapy planning in adult and pediatric patients across multiple positioning orientations
model_description: Takes head and neck CT scans in various patient orientations as input; a commercial deep learning autocontouring model segments 16 organs at risk, compared to manual segmentation.
release_evidence: described as a commercial autocontouring model for head and neck patients
journal: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
title: Validation of a deep-learning segmentation model for adult and pediatric head and neck radiotherapy in different patient positions.
study_design: retrospective validation study across adult and pediatric patients
headline_result: 13/16 OAR autocontours suited for clinical practice in head-first-supine orientations; no significant geometric differences between pediatric and adult autocontours

model_name: TW3 AI bone age assessment system
patient_population: 744 patients aged 1-20 years (378 boys, 366 girls) from 9 children's hospitals
clinical_problem: validating an AI system for Tanner-Whitehouse 3 bone age assessment across multiple children's hospitals
model_description: takes a left-hand radiograph as input and outputs a TW3-method bone age estimate, compared against experienced reviewer consensus
journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
title: Validation of an established TW3 artificial intelligence bone age assessment system: a prospective, multicenter, confirmatory study.

patient_population: 511 echocardiograms in children (229 normal, 282 with rheumatic heart disease)

journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
title: Using Artificial Intelligence for Rheumatic Heart Disease Detection by Echocardiography: Focus on Mitral Regurgitation.
headline_result: RHD detection AUC 0.84, precision 0.78, recall 0.98, F1 0.87; mitral regurgitation feature-based analysis AUC 0.93

model_family: automated bone health index software (existing commercial AI tool)
patient_population: 434 healthy children ages 3-15 (214 European-Caucasian, 220 North African) with normal hand/wrist radiographs
clinical_problem: normative bone mineral content (bone health index) assessment by ethnicity in children
model_description: BoneXpert, a commercial automated software, processes left-hand/wrist radiographs to compute the Bone Health Index (BHI) and its standard-deviation score, which are compared with manually calculated Exton-Smith Index values to establish ethnicity-specific normative ranges.
release_evidence: BoneXpert (R) software
title: Does ethnicity influence bone health index in children? A pilot study.

model_family: CNN ensembles (Cold-start, Warm-start, Shrink-and-Perturb initialization; F-SLSQP and attention-guided fuzzy softmax ensembles)
patient_population: adult and pediatric patients from multiple public chest X-ray datasets
clinical_problem: generalizability of deep learning chest X-ray models across adult and pediatric populations under periodic retraining
model_description: The study compares three ways of initializing deep CNN weights (cold-start, warm-start, shrink-and-perturb) for chest X-ray classification models retrained periodically as new data arrive, evaluating generalization to external adult and pediatric datasets, and proposes new ensembling methods that combine weights from multiple models.
title: Uncovering the effects of model initialization on deep model generalization: A study with adult and pediatric chest X-ray images.
dataset_size: multiple public adult and pediatric CXR datasets
headline_result: ImageNet-pretrained models generalized better; weight-level ensembles showed significantly higher recall (p<0.05)

patient_population: 459 pediatric (0-16 years) and 950 adult (>18 years) CT scans with expert contours
clinical_problem: Whether AI auto-segmentation models trained on adult CT data accurately contour organs on pediatric CT for radiation therapy planning, and how much pediatric training data improves performance
model_description: Input: pelvic/thoracic CT scans; output: automatic organ contours (bladder, spleen, liver, kidney, etc.), via nnU-Net models trained on adult-only, pediatric-only, and combined datasets
journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
title: Deep Learning Auto-Segmentation Network for Pediatric Computed Tomography Data Sets: Can We Extrapolate From Adults?

dataset_size: 459 pediatric and 950 adult CT scans; 290-300 cases per category/organ for training
headline_result: adult-only models: mean DSC <0.5 for bladder/spleen in ages 0-2; combined models achieved mean DSC >0.85 for all organs/age groups

clinical_problem: Reviewing potential AI applications for diagnosing and managing atrial septal defects in children, including automated measurement of cardiac rims on echocardiography for device selection.
model_description: Narrative review discussing potential AI applications in pediatric ASD care, including automated echocardiographic measurement of cardiac rims to guide closure device selection.
title: Can Artificial Intelligence Revolutionize the Diagnosis and Management of the Atrial Septal Defect in Children?

patient_population: pregnant women in a pregnancy cohort with serial fetal lung ultrasound; offspring followed through infancy and to age 5
clinical_problem: predicting risk of early-life respiratory infections and childhood asthma from ultrasound-monitored fetal lung growth
model_description: Input: serially measured fetal lung size on transabdominal ultrasound plus clinical variables; output: predicted risk/number of early-life respiratory infections and risk of early-onset asthma at age 5, using XGBoost regression/classification models.

title: One model, two brains: Automatic fetal brain extraction from MR images of twins.
study_design: Algorithm development and evaluation study (twin fetal MRI).

title: Harsh, unpredictable childhood environments are associated with inferior frontal gyrus connectivity and binge eating tendencies in late adolescents.

dataset_size: 501 late adolescents (376 with attentional-bias task data)

model_name: HR-IQS (fetal Heart Rhythm Intelligent Quantification System)

study_design: multicenter prospective study with deep learning model development (five-fold cross-validation)
headline_result: Significant positive correlation and moderate-to-excellent consistency (ICC) between manual and automated CTI measurements (P<.001)

patient_population: Infants and children; model trained on 3,659 original sonographic images (51,226 derived smartphone photos), tested prospectively on 333 sonographic gallbladder videos from 207 infants
clinical_problem: Can an AI app help radiologists of varying experience diagnose biliary atresia from smartphone photos of gallbladder ultrasound images, especially in settings without expert pediatric radiologists?

release_evidence: described as an 'app' redeveloped for real clinical use, but no code repository or commercial product name stated

title: A Multiplanar Radiomics Model Based on Cranial Ultrasound to Predict the White Matter Injury in Premature Infants and an Analysis of its Correlation With Neurodevelopment.

model_family: deep learning bone age estimation software

headline_result: significantly higher Dice score than five existing tools on the combined dataset; comparable or significantly higher Dice on the NIH (low-resolution) and dHCP (high-resolution) datasets independently

patient_population: in utero fetal brain MRI combined with postmortem 21-week fetal brain histology and microarray gene-expression data
clinical_problem: mapping molecular gene-expression signatures of cortical expansion during human gestation using in utero MRI
model_description: Built with generative AI, the μBrain atlas is a 3D cellular-resolution digital reference combining postmortem 21-week fetal brain serial sections with bulk tissue microarray gene-expression data across 29 cortical regions; it is used to relate molecular signatures to cortical expansion rates measured in utero with MRI.
release_evidence: The μBrain atlas is available from: https://garedaba.github.io/micro-brain/
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
title: Molecular signatures of cortical expansion in the human fetal brain.
study_design: preprint; atlas development and cross-modal analysis
dataset_size: postmortem brain at 21 weeks gestation with microarray data across 29 cortical regions plus in utero MRI cohort

patient_population: 25 fetuses with congenital heart disease, mean gestational age 35 weeks
clinical_problem: improving fetal cardiac MRI image quality for diagnosing congenital heart disease
model_description: A pretrained convolutional neural network denoises Doppler-ultrasound-gated fetal cardiac cine MRI reconstructions to improve image quality and diagnostic confidence for congenital heart disease.
title: Deep learning denoising reconstruction for improved image quality in fetal cardiac cine MRI.
headline_result: higher apparent SNR (13.4 vs 8.3) and CNR (26.6 vs 14.4) vs standard reconstruction; improved contrast and edge definition (P<0.001)

patient_population: fetal ultrasound video datasets and clinical examination cases
clinical_problem: Automatically detecting standard cardiac cycle frames in fetal echocardiography to support congenital heart disease diagnosis
model_description: An object-detector-based network identifies key fetal cardiac anatomical structures and motion phases in ultrasound video frames; a joint probability method localizes the cardiac cycle, and an XGBoost classifier recognizes standard planes.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: HFSCCD: A Hybrid Neural Network for Fetal Standard Cardiac Cycle Detection in Ultrasound Videos.

patient_population: 481 spine radiographs (open-source dataset, train/validation) and 119 spine radiographs from a private dataset (test), pediatric and adolescent scoliosis patients
clinical_problem: Automatically measuring scoliosis Cobb angle on spine radiographs
model_description: Two deep learning Cobb angle assessment models (Seg4Reg, a segmentation-based regression model, and VFLDN, a keypoint-based landmark detection model) automatically measure spinal curvature on radiographs, compared against manual physician measurement.
title: Clinical Application of Automatic Assessment of Scoliosis Cobb Angle Based on Deep Learning.
study_design: Retrospective external validation and clinical application study
dataset_size: 481 spine radiographs (open dataset, train/validation); 119 radiographs (private dataset, test)
headline_result: VFLDN: ICC 0.974, PCC 0.952 vs manual (MAD 2.36 deg); Seg4Reg: ICC 0.809, PCC 0.731 (MAD 6.51 deg)

model_family: nnU-Net (deep learning segmentation) plus SVM classifier
patient_population: fetuses with congenital diaphragmatic hernia (registered clinical trial NCT04609163)
clinical_problem: automatically quantifying fetal lung volume and predicting liver herniation to risk-stratify congenital diaphragmatic hernia
model_description: A publicly available nnU-Net automatically segments fetal lung and liver on MRI; shape features from the segmentation feed a support vector machine classifier that predicts liver herniation in congenital diaphragmatic hernia.
release_evidence: we utilized a publicly available deep learning (DL) segmentation system (nnU-Net)
title: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia: automatic lung and liver MRI segmentation with nnU-Net, reproducibility of pyradiomics features, and a machine learning application for the classification of liver herniation.
study_design: retrospective method development study; registered clinical trial NCT04609163
headline_result: AUC around 0.85 for liver herniation prediction (manual and automatic segmentation-based)

patient_population: RSNA and RHPE public datasets plus a local Han/Tibetan children dataset (825 train, 351 test: 216 Han, 135 Tibetan); external test set of 256 Tibetan children
clinical_problem: Automating bone age assessment for Han and Tibetan children, including in resource-limited high-altitude settings
model_description: EVG-BANet, a deep learning bone age assessment model trained on RSNA and RHPE datasets plus a local Han/Tibetan children dataset, is compared against the open-source BoNet model across multiple test sets including an external all-Tibetan cohort.
title: An artificial intelligence-based bone age assessment model for Han and Tibetan children.
study_design: Retrospective model development with external validation
dataset_size: RSNA (12,611/1,425/200 train/val/test); RHPE (5,491/713/79); local dataset (825 train, 351 test); external Tibetan test set (n=256)
headline_result: MAD 0.52-0.53 years (RHPE, external Tibetan test sets) vs BoNet 0.63-0.66 years; accuracy within 1 year 97.7% local, 89.5% external

patient_population: fetal brain MRI dataset of varying image quality (size not specified numerically)
clinical_problem: joint automated brain extraction and image quality assessment of fetal brain MRI slices to support 3D reconstruction and quantification
model_description: A two-stage dual-task deep-learning framework (with transformer-based feature extraction) takes fetal brain MRI slices as input and jointly outputs a brain extraction (segmentation) mask and an image-quality-assessment score, validated via five-fold cross-validation and cross-dataset testing.
title: A joint brain extraction and image quality assessment framework for fetal brain MRI slices.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development study with five-fold cross-validation and cross-dataset validation

model_family: self-supervised label cross-training on a pretrained medical imaging network
patient_population: 214 children at Dana-Farber/Boston Children's for development and 112 from the Children's Brain Tumor Network for external testing
clinical_problem: determining BRAF mutational status in pediatric low-grade glioma without a biopsy
model_description: A scan-to-prediction pipeline: it segments the tumor on a routine T2 image, then classifies BRAF wild type versus BRAF fusion versus BRAF V600E section by section. The distinction matters because V600E tumors have targeted therapy available. Performance drops from internal to external testing, which the authors report plainly, and they add a center-of-mass metric to check the model is actually attending to the tumor.
title: Noninvasive Molecular Subtyping of Pediatric Low-Grade Glioma with Self-Supervised Transfer Learning.
study_design: retrospective two-cohort study with external validation
dataset_size: 214 children for development, 112 for external testing
headline_result: internal AUC 0.82-0.87 across the three classes, falling to 0.72-0.78 on external testing

patient_population: 1,932 children (1,255 healthy, 292 ASD, 385 VSD) from Beijing Children's Hospital, 2018-2022
clinical_problem: Detecting congenital heart disease (atrial and ventricular septal defects) on pediatric transthoracic echocardiograms across multiple views and modalities to assist less experienced sonographers
model_description: Input: 2D and Doppler transthoracic echocardiogram images across 5 standard views; output: cardiac view classification and prediction of normal vs. ASD vs. VSD status with high-risk region visualization, via a multi-view multi-modal deep learning framework
title: Development and Validation of a Deep-Learning Network for Detecting Congenital Heart Disease from Multi-View Multi-Modal Transthoracic Echocardiograms.
study_design: retrospective model development with cross-center external testing
headline_result: CHD screening AUC 0.996 within-center, 0.990 cross-center; accuracy 0.994/0.993

patient_population: children with functional constipation (n=77), refractory constipation (n=63), or no constipation (n=65)
clinical_problem: early identification of refractory constipation in children
model_description: Standardized colon size ratios measured on barium enema (sigmoid, descending, transverse, rectum, rectosigmoid) were used to train a linear support vector machine that classifies children into functional constipation, refractory constipation, or non-constipation groups, aiming to flag refractory disease earlier.
title: Artificial intelligence-powered early identification of refractory constipation in children.
headline_result: 81% accuracy (95% CI 79.17-83.19%) distinguishing refractory constipation from the other groups

patient_population: Children with pancreaticobiliary maljunction evaluated for acute pancreatitis
clinical_problem: Diagnosing acute pancreatitis in children with pancreaticobiliary maljunction when CT findings are nonobvious, using a radiomics-clinical nomogram.
model_description: Input: pancreatic CT radiomics features plus clinical parameters. Output: nomogram predicting presence of acute pancreatitis in children with nonobvious CT findings.
title: Development of a CT-based radiomics-clinical model to diagnose acute pancreatitis on nonobvious findings on CT in children with pancreaticobiliary maljunction.
study_design: Single-center retrospective radiomics-clinical nomogram development study.
headline_result: Combined radiomics-clinical nomogram AUC 0.938 (training), 0.864 (validation).

patient_population: 5,363 images from 2,551 pregnancies (training/validation); 100 patients prospective validation (192 images)
clinical_problem: Automated quality assessment and view/plane segmentation for fetal echocardiography to support the 18-22 week anomaly scan.
model_description: A deep learning model auto-captures and segments fetal echocardiography images, assigning a quality score that determines segmentation reliability, validated prospectively against clinician review.
title: AI supported fetal echocardiography with quality assessment.
study_design: retrospective model development with prospective clinical validation
dataset_size: 5,363 images from 2,551 pregnancies; prospective validation of 192 images from 100 patients
headline_result: Overall segmentation accuracy 0.91 (SD 0.09); 0.97 for above-average quality images

patient_population: 592 neonates (478 term-born, 114 preterm-born), developing Human Connectome Project
clinical_problem: Estimating post-menstrual age and assessing brain maturity from neonatal brain MRI to help identify preterm-related developmental risk
model_description: A transformer-based multi-modal deep learning model fuses T2-weighted structural MRI and diffusion MRI features via a two-stream dense network and self-attention to estimate post-menstrual age and classify preterm versus term birth, with saliency maps for interpretability.
title: Transformer based multi-modal MRI fusion for prediction of post-menstrual age and neonatal brain development analysis.
headline_result: MAE 0.5 weeks for PMA estimation; 95% accuracy for term/preterm classification

patient_population: multi-institutional pediatric brain MRI data across scan types and age cohorts
clinical_problem: removing non-brain tissue from pediatric brain MRI scans to enable downstream image analysis
model_description: input pediatric brain MRI of varying scan types; output a skull-stripped brain-only image via a model trained on highly variable synthetic images derived from label maps
release_evidence: We distribute our model at https://w3id.org/synthstrip.
title: BOOSTING SKULL-STRIPPING PERFORMANCE FOR PEDIATRIC BRAIN IMAGES.
study_design: methods development study evaluated across multiple pediatric datasets
headline_result: substantially outperforms pediatric baselines across scan types and age cohorts; runtime <1 minute (no single summary metric reported)

model_family: hybrid CNN (classification-regression guidance network + confident-frame detector + segmentation network)
patient_population: fetuses undergoing first-trimester ultrasound
clinical_problem: automating standard-plane selection and crown-rump length measurement from freehand first-trimester ultrasound video
model_description: input freehand first-trimester ultrasound video; output automatically detected standard planes, segmented fetal landmarks, and a crown-rump length/gestational age estimate
title: Automating the Human Action of First-Trimester Biometry Measurement from Real-World Freehand Ultrasound.
headline_result: Pearson r=0.92, R2=0.84 vs. expert CRL measurement; mean absolute error 0.834 weeks for fetal age

model_family: machine learning clustering plus computational hemodynamic model
patient_population: 97 growth-restricted and 111 normally grown singleton fetuses, 24-37 weeks gestation
clinical_problem: characterizing pulmonary vascular reactivity in growth-restricted fetuses using Doppler ultrasound
model_description: Doppler ultrasound waveforms of the pulmonary vessels, taken before and after maternal hyperoxygenation, are classified into clusters by machine learning and fed into a computational model that estimates the ratio of pulmonary vascular resistance before and after oxygenation, distinguishing responsive from non-responsive growth-restricted fetuses.
title: Pulmonary vascular reactivity in growth restricted fetuses using computational modelling and machine learning analysis of fetal Doppler waveforms.
headline_result: cluster A PVR ratio 0.98±0.33 vs cluster B 0.78±0.28, p=0.0156

patient_population: review of studies using the ADHD-200 database and related rs-fMRI cohorts
clinical_problem: reviewing machine-learning approaches for detecting ADHD from resting-state functional MRI in school-age children
model_description: A review of prior studies that use resting-state fMRI functional-network features with machine learning and deep learning methods (network/atlas selection, feature extraction/selection, classification) to detect ADHD.
title: A review of ADHD detection studies with machine learning methods using rsfMRI data.

patient_population: 65 pediatric patients with pathology-confirmed focal cortical dysplasia type II
clinical_problem: detecting and segmenting focal cortical dysplasia lesions on preoperative MRI in children with epilepsy
model_description: Takes a high-resolution 3D T1-MPRAGE brain MRI as input and outputs an automatic voxel-level detection map and segmentation of focal cortical dysplasia lesions, using a 3D full-resolution nnU-Net.
title: Deep learning-based automated lesion segmentation on pediatric focal cortical dysplasia II preoperative MRI: a reliable approach.
study_design: retrospective pilot study with algorithm development and internal validation
headline_result: sensitivity 0.73; mean Dice-Sørensen coefficient 0.57 on the testing dataset

patient_population: 1,425 pediatric hand radiographs (RSNA internal test set), 1,202 (Digital Hand Atlas external test set)
clinical_problem: testing the robustness of an automated bone age assessment algorithm to real-world image variations in pediatric hand radiographs
model_description: The award-winning deep learning bone age model from the 2017 RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Challenge takes pediatric hand radiographs and outputs a predicted bone age; this study computationally stress-tests it against image transformations (rotation, flips, brightness, contrast, inversion, laterality marker, resolution).
title: Evaluating the Robustness of a Deep Learning Bone Age Algorithm to Clinical Image Variation Using Computational Stress Testing.
dataset_size: 1,425 pediatric hand radiographs (RSNA internal test set), 1,202 (Digital Hand Atlas external test set)
headline_result: mean absolute difference 6.8 months (RSNA), 6.9 months (DHA); clinically significant error proportions differed for 57% (19/33) of image transformations

patient_population: Human fetuses aged 17-30 weeks from spontaneous miscarriages and preterm deliveries
clinical_problem: Assessing fetal femur development (ossification center parameters) using AI to aid prenatal detection of skeletal anomalies.
model_description: Input: gestational age and femur length. Output: an MLP (2-3-2-5 architecture) predicts five parameters of the femoral shaft primary ossification center (linear dimensions, cross-sectional areas, volume) derived from CT/digital image analysis.
title: Application of artificial neural networks to evaluate femur development in the human fetus.
headline_result: Correlation between predicted and actual values: R=0.955 (training), 0.942 (validation), 0.953 (testing).

patient_population: Anthropomorphic pediatric (infant) phantom study (not real patients)
clinical_problem: Reducing radiation dose in ECG-gated cardiac CT for infants with congenital heart disease using deep learning image reconstruction while preserving image quality.
model_description: A Deep Learning Image Reconstruction (DLIR) algorithm processes low-dose ECG-gated cardiac CT phantom images and reconstructs images with improved vessel detectability and spatial resolution compared to iterative reconstruction (ASIR-V), enabling dose reduction.
title: Gated cardiac CT in infants: What can we expect from deep learning image reconstruction algorithm?
headline_result: DLIR-H improved detectability 2.4% and discrimination 20.9% vs ASIR-V50; enabled 64% dose reduction

patient_population: pediatric chest X-ray dataset (children, particularly under 5), pretraining on adult chest X-rays then fine-tuning on pediatric pneumonia dataset
clinical_problem: improving diagnosis of pediatric pneumonia (and distinguishing bacterial vs viral) from chest X-rays despite scarce labeled pediatric data
model_description: Input: pediatric chest X-ray images; output: classification of normal vs. pneumonia, and further into bacterial vs. viral pneumonia, using a Masked Autoencoder pretrained (self-supervised) on adult chest X-rays and fine-tuned on a pediatric pneumonia dataset.
title: Enhancing pediatric pneumonia diagnosis through masked autoencoders.
study_design: retrospective model development with self-supervised pretraining and internal evaluation
headline_result: AUC 0.996, accuracy 95.89% (normal vs pneumonia); accuracy 93.86% for 3-class (normal/bacterial/viral)

patient_population: 65 pediatric MS patients (median age 15.5) and 23 age/sex-matched healthy controls
clinical_problem: predicting cognitive impairment in pediatric multiple sclerosis from glymphatic-system MRI markers
model_description: Inputs are MRI-derived diffusion metrics (DTI-ALPS glymphatic index, lesion volume, white matter diffusivity/anisotropy) and IQ; output is a random forest prediction of cognitive impairment status, with feature-importance ranking of MRI predictors.
title: Cognitive Impairment Is Related to Glymphatic System Dysfunction in Pediatric Multiple Sclerosis.
dataset_size: 65 pediatric MS patients and 23 healthy controls
headline_result: out-of-bag AUC 0.762 for predicting cognitive impairment; DTI-ALPS index was the top predictor (relative importance 100%)

model_family: radiomics (various ML classifiers, pooled across studies)
patient_population: 672 patients pooled across 7 studies
clinical_problem: diagnostic accuracy of MRI-based radiomics for prenatal diagnosis of placenta accreta spectrum
model_description: Systematic review and meta-analysis of MRI-based radiomic models for diagnosing placenta accreta spectrum, using histopathology as reference standard; pooled diagnostic performance is reported, not a single model.
journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
title: Accuracy of MRI-Based Radiomics in Diagnosis of Placenta Accreta Spectrum: A PRISMA Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
headline_result: pooled sensitivity 87%, specificity 92%, AUC 0.93, DOR 78%

patient_population: 172 patients with high-risk neuroblastoma reviewed; 87 met inclusion criteria (training/validation 7:3)
clinical_problem: predicting event-free survival after remission induction in high-risk pediatric neuroblastoma from 123I-MIBG SPECT-CT
model_description: Radiomics features extracted from 123I-MIBG SPECT-CT images of the lumbar vertebral bodies are combined with clinical risk factors in a Cox-regression nomogram to predict event-free survival after remission induction.
title: Predicting event-free survival after induction of remission in high-risk pediatric neuroblastoma: combining 123I-MIBG SPECT-CT radiomics and clinical factors.
study_design: retrospective radiomics-nomogram development and validation study
headline_result: Nomogram C-index 0.819 (training), 0.712 (validation); 1-year AUC 0.899/0.748

patient_population: 27 studies of first-trimester pregnancy imaging
clinical_problem: State of AI applications for first-trimester pregnancy ultrasound imaging (segmentation, plane detection, classification)
model_description: Systematic review of 27 studies applying AI (segmentation, standard-plane detection, and image classification models) to first-trimester ultrasound imaging
title: Artificial Intelligence in Imaging in the First Trimester of Pregnancy: A Systematic Review.
headline_result: Only one of 27 studies was externally validated

model_family: adaptive wavelet noise suppression (AWNS) plus supervised machine learning classifier (Naive Bayes)
patient_population: 83/42 children (two cohorts) with ependymoma, medulloblastoma, or pilocytic astrocytoma across four UK centres
clinical_problem: classifying pediatric brain tumor type (ependymoma, medulloblastoma, pilocytic astrocytoma) from proton MR spectroscopy
model_description: Clinical 1H-MR spectroscopy is denoised with adaptive wavelet noise suppression before metabolite concentrations are extracted as features and classified with supervised machine learning (with SMOTE oversampling) to distinguish three pediatric brain tumor types; noise suppression improved classification accuracy.
title: Noise suppression of proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy improves paediatric brain tumour classification.
dataset_size: 83 children (1.5T cohort) and 42 children (3T cohort) from four UK centres
headline_result: classification accuracy improved from 81% to 88% (overall, 1.5T) and 62% to 76% (overall, 3T) after noise suppression

patient_population: Typically developing children undergoing test-retest perfusion MRI
clinical_problem: Improving image quality of pediatric cerebral perfusion MRI (multi-delay arterial spin labeling) to more reliably quantify cerebral blood flow and arterial transit time in children.
model_description: Input: multi-delay arterial spin labeling perfusion MRI images. A Transformer-based deep-learning model, trained using k-space-weighted-image-average denoised references, denoises images to improve SNR and repeatability of cerebral blood flow and arterial transit time maps.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
title: High Resolution Multi-delay Arterial Spin Labeling with Transformer based Denoising for Pediatric Perfusion MRI.
dataset_size: 21 typically developing children aged 8-17 years, test-retest scans

model_family: transfer learning deep learning model (segmentation + image fusion)
patient_population: 1,491 chest radiographs for lung segmentation dataset; 1,021 chest radiographs of preterm infants for BPD prediction dataset
clinical_problem: early prediction of bronchopulmonary dysplasia in preterm infants from chest radiographs
model_description: Input: chest radiographs of preterm infants (as early as ≤24 hours postnatal age); output: automated lung region segmentation (transfer learning) followed by image-fusion-based prediction of bronchopulmonary dysplasia risk, compared against expert diagnostic accuracy.
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
title: Deep Learning Model for Prediction of Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia in Preterm Infants Using Chest Radiographs.
study_design: retrospective model development and internal evaluation
dataset_size: 1,491 CXRs (segmentation) + 1,021 CXRs (BPD prediction) of preterm infants
headline_result: lung segmentation Dice 0.960; BPD prediction model exceeded diagnostic accuracy of experts

patient_population: 4,931 elbow radiographs from patients aged 7 years and older with suspected traumatic distal humerus fracture
clinical_problem: Detecting distal humerus fractures on anteroposterior and lateral elbow radiographs in patients seven years and older, to reduce missed or delayed fracture diagnoses
model_description: Input: AP and lateral elbow radiographs cropped around the capitellum; output: binary classification (fractured vs. normal), via a ResNet18 deep learning model
title: Development of a diagnostic support system for distal humerus fracture using artificial intelligence.
headline_result: accuracy 69.14%, specificity 95.89%, sensitivity 61.49%, AUC 0.787 (vs. 0.580 for senior surgeon reference)

model_family: neural network organ segmentation with a population-averaged atlas
patient_population: 91 normal control fetal 3T MRI datasets across 22-38 weeks gestational age
clinical_problem: volumetry of fetal organs, which is currently done by slice-by-slice manual segmentation of motion-corrupted stacks
model_description: Supplies the two things missing before fetal organ volumetry can be automated: a parcellation protocol defining ten organ regions, which did not previously exist in any standard form, and the first population-averaged T2-weighted atlas of the fetal body. The network trained on that protocol then produced organ growth charts across gestation that behaved as expected, which is the sanity check for a normative tool.
title: Automated body organ segmentation, volumetry and population-averaged atlas for 3D motion-corrected T2-weighted fetal body MRI.
headline_result: robust segmentation across gestational ages, with organ growth charts from 22-38 weeks showing the expected volume increase

model_family: radiomics with machine-learning classifiers (XGBoost, Bernoulli naive Bayes, logistic regression, SVM, linear SVC)
patient_population: 135 children with medulloblastoma or ependymoma from two centers
clinical_problem: distinguishing medulloblastoma from ependymoma in children on brain MRI
model_description: Takes radiomic features extracted from T2-weighted and contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI as input and outputs a machine-learning classification distinguishing medulloblastoma from ependymoma, benchmarked against human expert diagnosis.
title: Multiparametric MRI-Based Interpretable Radiomics Machine Learning Model Differentiates Medulloblastoma and Ependymoma in Children: A Two-Center Study.
study_design: retrospective two-center model development with external validation
headline_result: XGBoost AUC 0.92 on test set and 0.80 on external validation; human expert diagnosis AUC 0.66 (test) and 0.69 (external)

patient_population: Children with polymicrogyria and controls from the Children's Hospital of Eastern Ontario (PPMR dataset)
clinical_problem: Detecting polymicrogyria, a subtle cortical malformation, on pediatric brain MRI
model_description: A center-based deep contrastive metric learning anomaly-detection method flags pediatric brain MRIs likely to show polymicrogyria, intended as a computer-aided screening tool for radiologists; code and a new open pediatric MRI dataset (PPMR) are released publicly.
release_evidence: Our code is available at: https://github.com/RichardChangCA/... ; dataset available at kaggle.com/datasets/lingfengzhang/pediatric-polymicrogyria-mri-dataset
journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
title: A novel center-based deep contrastive metric learning method for the detection of polymicrogyria in pediatric brain MRI.
study_design: Retrospective model development study, first ML application to detect polymicrogyria from MRI
dataset_size: Small, imbalanced pediatric MRI dataset (PPMR; exact N not stated in abstract)
headline_result: 88.07% recall at 71.86% precision

model_family: LASSO feature selection with random forest classifier
patient_population: 422 hospitalized children with community-acquired pneumonia
clinical_problem: diagnostic value of lung ultrasound for community-acquired pneumonia and severity prediction in hospitalized children
model_description: Lung ultrasound signs (consolidation, confluent B-lines, pleural effusion) are selected by LASSO regression and fed into a random forest classifier to diagnose pneumonia (against chest CT) and to predict severe disease in hospitalized children.
journal: Zhonghua er ke za zhi = Chinese journal of pediatrics
title: [The diagnostic value of lung ultrasound in children with community-acquired pneumonia].
dataset_size: 422 children with CAP (110 with chest CT)
headline_result: AUC 0.87 (full variables) / 0.84 (LASSO-selected) for CAP diagnosis; AUC 0.76 for severe CAP using consolidation size/body surface area

model_family: random forest (best of RF, LR, KNN, SVM, MLP)
patient_population: 150 neonates with lung disease (60 NRDS, 30 each pneumonia/meconium aspiration/transient tachypnea) at a maternity and children's hospital
clinical_problem: Objectively diagnosing neonatal respiratory distress syndrome from lung ultrasound, reducing reliance on operator-dependent visual interpretation
model_description: Texture features extracted from lung ultrasound images using PyRadiomics are used to train random forest, logistic regression, KNN, SVM and MLP classifiers to distinguish neonatal respiratory distress syndrome from other neonatal lung diseases
title: Exploring the diagnostic value of ultrasound radiomics for neonatal respiratory distress syndrome.
headline_result: Random forest AUC 0.99, not significantly different from experienced physicians (AUC 0.98, P=0.24) but significantly better than junior physicians (AUC 0.85, P<0.0001)

model_family: machine learning classification model and brain-age prediction model
patient_population: age-matched adolescent females from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) cohort; brain-age model trained on the Philadelphia Neurodevelopmental Cohort
clinical_problem: classifying pubertal status (pre- vs post-menarche) from structural brain MRI and comparing it to brain-age-based markers of neurodevelopment in adolescent girls
model_description: Machine learning model trained on cortical and subcortical structural MRI features to classify pre- versus post-menarche status, compared against a separately trained brain-age prediction model applied to the same data
title: Menarche, pubertal timing and the brain: female-specific patterns of brain maturation beyond age-related development.
study_design: cross-sectional machine learning classification study using cohort MRI data
headline_result: machine learning model achieved moderate but statistically significant accuracy in classifying menarche status

model_family: machine learning fracture detection algorithm used as a reading aid
patient_population: 200 radiographs from patients aged 1 to 95 (mean 40.7 years), half containing at least one fracture, read by four residents of differing experience
clinical_problem: whether AI assistance helps radiology residents find fractures, and what that means for training
model_description: A reader study framed around residency training rather than around the algorithm. Residents gained 19 points of sensitivity with the aid, at essentially no cost in specificity, with the largest gains for the least experienced. The authors raise the training question directly: a tool that lifts a trainee to expert-level detection also removes the errors trainees learn from.
title: AI-Assisted X-ray Fracture Detection in Residency Training: Evaluation in Pediatric and Adult Trauma Patients.
headline_result: resident sensitivity rose from 58% to 77% with AI (p < 0.001) with specificity unchanged; stand-alone AI sensitivity 93% at 77% specificity; interpretation time fell and confidence rose

model_family: graph convolutional network (GCN) with supervised contrastive learning (SCL)
patient_population: ~280 very preterm infants (CINEPS cohort), MRI at term-equivalent age
clinical_problem: early prediction of neurodevelopmental deficits (cognition, language, motor) at 2 years corrected age in very preterm infants using brain structural connectome from MRI at term-equivalent age
model_description: A graph convolutional network trained with supervised contrastive learning takes the brain structural connectome (derived from diffusion MRI at term-equivalent age) as a graph input and outputs predicted risk of neurodevelopmental deficits (cognitive, language, motor) at 2 years corrected age in very preterm infants.
title: Supervised contrastive learning enhances graph convolutional networks for predicting neurodevelopmental deficits in very preterm infants using brain structural connectome.
study_design: prospective single-cohort study with deep learning model development
headline_result: Mean AUCs 0.72-0.75 for predicting three neurodevelopmental deficits

patient_population: 130 patients with 3-foot standing spine radiographs for idiopathic or congenital scoliosis over a 10-year period
clinical_problem: automatic Cobb angle measurement for idiopathic and congenital scoliosis in children and adolescents
model_description: A segmentation-based Augmented U-Net model with non-square kernels automatically measures Cobb angles on 3-foot standing spine radiographs, compared with manual radiologist measurements in idiopathic and congenital scoliosis cohorts.
journal: Canadian Association of Radiologists journal = Journal l'Association canadienne des radiologistes
title: Correlative Assessment of Machine Learning-Based Cobb Angle Measurements and Human-Based Measurements in Adolescent Idiopathic and Congenital Scoliosis.
headline_result: SMAPE 11.82% combined cohort; 13.02% idiopathic, 11.90% congenital

patient_population: fetal freehand 2D ultrasound video sequences from multiple manufacturers
clinical_problem: reconstructing 3D fetal brain volumes from freehand 2D ultrasound sweeps without external tracking, to improve prenatal brain assessment
model_description: ImplicitVol takes a set of untracked 2D freehand fetal brain ultrasound images, predicts their 3D spatial locations, and reconstructs a continuous 3D volumetric representation of the fetal brain.
title: Sensorless volumetric reconstruction of fetal brain freehand ultrasound scans with deep implicit representation.

model_family: machine learning (unspecified algorithms; general linear models + ML)
patient_population: 57 typically developing male and female children who received tDCS
clinical_problem: predicting individual children's behavioral response to transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) from neuroanatomical MRI measures (cortical thickness, surface area), to inform future personalized neuromodulation treatment in neurodevelopmental disorders
model_description: Machine-learning algorithms use structural MRI-derived cortical thickness and surface area measures as input to predict individual children's task-performance response to transcranial direct current stimulation as output.
journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
title: Neuroanatomical Predictors of Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation (tDCS)-Induced Modifications in Neurocognitive Task Performance in Typically Developing Individuals.
study_design: prospective experimental (sham-controlled) study with machine learning model development
headline_result: Highest ML accuracy: 65% of behavioral variance in N-back task performance explained by surface area (DLPFCleft stimulation)

patient_population: ~70,000 pediatric X-ray images collected over 24 years at Asan Medical Center
clinical_problem: building pediatric-specific pretrained radiograph models to improve downstream pediatric radiology AI tasks such as fracture classification and bone age assessment, addressing the mismatch of natural-image pretrained models for grayscale medical images
task: detection / diagnosis; measurement / quantification; foundation model / vision-language
model_description: PedXnets are Inception V3-based models pretrained on ~70,000 pediatric radiographs classified by radiographic view (7, 30, or 68 classes) to serve as domain-specific backbones for transfer learning; validated on downstream tasks of pediatric fracture classification and bone age assessment.
title: Supervised representation learning based on various levels of pediatric radiographic views for transfer learning.
study_design: retrospective single-center pretraining and transfer-learning validation study
dataset_size: ~70,000 pediatric X-ray images (24 years, single center)

patient_population: 560 fetuses between 11 and 13 weeks 6 days gestation, 88 with NT >3.5mm
clinical_problem: Automatically detecting an increased nuchal translucency, a marker of genetic/structural fetal anomalies, on first-trimester ultrasound
model_description: A U-Net convolutional neural network segments the fetus and the nuchal translucency region on standardized mid-sagittal first-trimester ultrasound images, computing an NT:fetus ratio to flag thickened (anomalous) NT
title: Deep-learning computer vision can identify increased nuchal translucency in the first trimester of pregnancy.
headline_result: AUROC 0.96 for detecting thick NT on model segmentation; 94% sensitivity at 91% specificity

model_family: YOLOv5 (detection) and modified DeepLabv3 with an Attentional Multi-scale Feature Fusion (AMFF) module (segmentation)
body_region: fetal heart (three-vessel view: pulmonary artery, aorta, superior vena cava)
patient_population: 511 fetal heart three-vessel-view ultrasound images
clinical_problem: automatically detecting and segmenting the three great vessels on the fetal heart ultrasound three-vessel view to assist prenatal congenital heart disease screening
model_description: Two-stage deep learning framework: YOLOv5 detects and localizes the three vessels on fetal heart ultrasound images, then a modified DeepLabv3 with an attentional multi-scale feature fusion module segments each vessel within the localized region
title: A deep learning framework for identifying and segmenting three vessels in fetal heart ultrasound images.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and internal evaluation
headline_result: Dice coefficients of 85.55%, 89.12%, and 77.54% for pulmonary artery, aorta, and superior vena cava respectively

patient_population: 53 AIS patients, 88 spinal curves
clinical_problem: comparing traditional 2D Cobb angle measurement to automated 3D Cobb angle measurement methods using weight-bearing 3D imaging in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
model_description: Input: weight-bearing 3D spine imaging; output: automated 3D segmentation of the spine and femoral heads using a 3D-UNet deep learning model, from which Cobb angles are automatically calculated by three different 3D geometric methods and compared to manual 2D measurement.
journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
title: From 2D to 3D: automatic measurement of the Cobb angle in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis with the weight-bearing 3D imaging.
headline_result: Plane Projection Method values not significantly different from 2D method; Analytical and Plane Intersecting Methods gave significantly larger estimates

patient_population: 70 individuals, mean age 20.39 years (range 9-26 years)
clinical_problem: improving correspondence between low-field and high-field brain MRI in young people
model_description: T1- and T2-weighted images from a 64mT low-field portable MRI system are processed by SynthSR, a convolutional-neural-network super-resolution method, to produce images with improved correspondence to matched 3T high-field images; performance is compared against a multi-orientation averaging alternative.
title: Bridging the gap: improving correspondence between low-field and high-field magnetic resonance images in young people.
headline_result: SynthSR improved correspondence to high-field images to r=0.85-0.97 for most brain volume measures (vs. r=0.60-0.88 uncorrected); cortical thickness correspondence remained poor (r=0.14)

patient_population: 11,288 children ages 9-10, ABCD Study cohort (baseline)
clinical_problem: Identifying latent brain-behavior dimensions linking gray matter density patterns to psychopathology symptoms in children, using machine learning.
model_description: A sparse partial least squares machine learning framework takes voxelwise structural MRI gray matter density and psychosocial questionnaire data as input and identifies six latent brain-behavior dimensions related to cognition and psychopathology.
journal: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging
title: Voxelwise Multivariate Analysis of Brain-Psychosocial Associations in Adolescents Reveals 6 Latent Dimensions of Cognition and Psychopathology.
headline_result: 6 latent dimensions identified, 4 related to mental health (all p<.03)

model_family: radiomics-based machine learning (feature selection with ANOVA/RFE, multiple classifier pipelines)
patient_population: 82 children with renal tumors at a single pediatric urology department
clinical_problem: preoperative differentiation of Wilms tumor from non-Wilms renal tumors in children using CT
model_description: input CT radiomics texture features extracted from the tumor region of interest; output a machine-learning classification distinguishing Wilms from non-Wilms renal tumors
title: The application of machine learning based on computed tomography images in the identification of renal tumors in children.
headline_result: best internal-validation AUC 0.792 (corticomedullary phase) and 0.655 (nephrogenic phase)

patient_population: A single term infant with perinatal asphyxia (case report)
clinical_problem: Correlating longitudinal brain volumetric changes, measured with 3D machine learning models, with clinical/neurodevelopmental outcome in a case of severe perinatal asphyxia.
model_description: Input: longitudinal 3D brain MRI. Output: ML-based volumetric analysis of basal ganglia, thalamus and cerebellar structures over time in a newborn with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, correlated with clinical neurodevelopmental outcome.
title: Clinical-functional correlation with brain volumetry in severe perinatal asphyxia: a case report.
study_design: Case report with longitudinal 3D volumetric MRI analysis.

patient_population: 31 singleton pregnancies, 28-34 weeks gestation (19 low-risk, 12 high-risk for preterm birth)
clinical_problem: using fetal brain functional connectivity from resting-state fMRI combined with maternal risk factors to improve prediction of preterm birth risk
model_description: A random forest model (MaFra-Neuro) combines the Maternal Frailty Inventory score with fetal brain functional connectivity features derived from resting-state fMRI (estimated using the Greedy Equivalence Search algorithm) as input to predict preterm birth risk, gestational age at birth, and related perinatal outcomes.
title: The maternal-fetal neurodevelopmental groundings of preterm birth risk.

patient_population: 1,109 pediatric chest radiographs, manually labeled by 7 pediatric radiologists
clinical_problem: Automated detection and localization of rib fractures on pediatric chest radiographs to improve sensitivity for identifying non-accidental trauma in children under 3.
model_description: Ensembled CNN object detectors (RetinaNet, YOLOv5) with a dynamic 'avalanche decision' threshold scheme take pediatric chest radiographs as input and detect/localize rib fractures to flag possible non-accidental trauma.
title: High sensitivity methods for automated rib fracture detection in pediatric radiographs.
headline_result: F2 score 0.725±0.012 (best ensembled model) vs expert inter-reader F2 0.732

patient_population: 2,658 participants (ABCD Study), ages 9-10 at baseline; high-risk subgroup with parental history of depression N=625
clinical_problem: Predicting future depression risk in early adolescence using multimodal brain MRI features (structural, diffusion, functional) via machine learning.
model_description: Machine learning models take multimodal neuroimaging features (structural MRI, DTI, task/rest fMRI) as input and predict depression risk at two-year follow-up, validated with leave-one-site-out cross-validation.
title: Predicting depression risk in early adolescence via multimodal brain imaging.
study_design: longitudinal population-based cohort study with machine learning
headline_result: Rest-fMRI functional connectome features showed best classification performance (specific AUC not stated)

patient_population: 299 children from one institution and 23 from a second institution with PLGNTs
clinical_problem: Non-invasively predicting the molecular subtype (BRAF status) of pediatric low-grade neuroepithelial tumors from ADC MRI to guide targeted therapy without biopsy
model_description: Radiomics features extracted from semi-automated tumor segmentation on ADC MRI maps, combined with clinical variables (age, sex, tumor location), train multiclass random forest models to predict KIAA1549-BRAF fusion, BRAF V600E mutation, or non-BRAF molecular status
title: Identification of Multiclass Pediatric Low-Grade Neuroepithelial Tumor Molecular Subtype with ADC MR Imaging and Machine Learning.
headline_result: Combined radiomics + clinical features AUC 0.77 (95% CI 0.75-0.77); per-class AUC up to 0.81 for KIAA1549-BRAF fusion

patient_population: adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis undergoing full-length standing spine radiographs
clinical_problem: adolescent idiopathic scoliosis diagnosis and Cobb angle measurement
model_description: Input is a full-length standing spinal X-ray; the model detects key points and outputs a scoliosis diagnosis/classification and Cobb angle measurement. Trained and tested on 748 retrospectively collected images (602 train/validate, 146 test).
journal: Zhongguo yi liao qi xie za zhi = Chinese journal of medical instrumentation
title: [Application of Deep Learning to Diagnose and Classify Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis].
headline_result: 94.5% diagnostic/classification accuracy; 94.9% of Cobb angle measurements within clinically acceptable range (mean absolute difference 2.1 degrees, r2>=0.9552)

patient_population: 3,247 children undergoing anteroposterior pelvic radiographs
clinical_problem: image quality control of pediatric pelvic radiographs (for DDH assessment)
model_description: Input is an anteroposterior pediatric pelvic radiograph; the model outputs a quality assessment (pelvic tilt and rotation indices) to flag images unsuitable for developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) evaluation. Trained on a random split of the cohort.
journal: Zhongguo yi liao qi xie za zhi = Chinese journal of medical instrumentation
title: [Development and Application of Deep Learning-Based Model for Quality Control of Children Pelvic X-Ray Images].
headline_result: Accuracy 99.4%, AUC 0.993, sensitivity 98.6%, specificity 100.0%

clinical_problem: automated identification of standard imaging planes in fetal ultrasound examinations
model_description: Takes fetal ultrasound images as input and outputs a classification of the standard imaging plane shown, using contrastive pretraining (SimCLR) to reduce the amount of labeled data needed.
title: On the use of contrastive learning for standard-plane classification in fetal ultrasound imaging.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development study comparing training strategies

patient_population: 31 preschool children with ASD and 30 healthy controls
clinical_problem: Assessing diagnostic potential of cortical-cerebellar circuit alterations for autism spectrum disorder in preschool children using multimodal MRI
model_description: Diffusion basis spectrum imaging (DBSI) and 3D structural MRI features from 120 anatomical brain regions are combined using a multi-kernel support vector machine to classify preschool ASD versus healthy controls
title: Cortical-cerebellar circuits changes in preschool ASD children by multimodal MRI.
headline_result: Highest single-model accuracy 86.88% (DBSI_20); combining all three models further improved performance

patient_population: 104 pediatric neuroblastoma patients with pathologic confirmation
clinical_problem: Predicting MYCN copy-number status, a key prognostic marker, in pediatric neuroblastoma from 18F-FDG PET/CT rather than invasive biopsy
model_description: PET/CT radiographic features, PET quantitative parameters and clinical/biological variables are combined via LASSO feature selection and multivariable logistic regression into bio-omics, radiomics and multi-omics models that predict MYCN wild-type vs. gain vs. amplification status
journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
title: 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) imaging of pediatric neuroblastoma: a multi-omics parameters method to predict MYCN copy number category.
headline_result: Multi-omics model AUC 0.83 (95% CI 0.74-0.92) for MYCN wild vs. gain/amplification; AUC 0.95 for gain vs. amplification

model_family: deep learning architectures with data augmentation (literature review plus methodology)
patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound screening
clinical_problem: improving accuracy of detecting Down syndrome on fetal ultrasound
model_description: The paper reviews and proposes advanced deep learning architectures with data augmentation techniques for diagnosing and predicting fetal conditions, including Down syndrome, from ultrasound images, discussing training/validation processes and clinical translation considerations.
title: Advancing fetal ultrasound diagnostics: Innovative methodologies for improved accuracy in detecting down syndrome.

model_family: neural network ("boosted division time attribute extraction"/TAE-PIS)
patient_population: children/fetuses with suspected brain tumor glioblastoma (abstract poorly specifies cohort)
clinical_problem: detection of fetal/pediatric brain tumor (glioblastoma) on MRI
model_description: Input is brain MRI; the method segments and classifies images to recognize glioblastoma, comparing a proposed max/min rationalization and attribute-extraction approach against genetic algorithm, CNN, fuzzy min-max and SVM baselines. The abstract text is unusually garbled and does not clearly describe a real patient cohort or training pipeline.
title: Exploring fetal brain tumor glioblastoma symptom verification with self organizing maps and vulnerability data analysis.
headline_result: Reported accuracy 98.12% (proposed TAE-PIS system)

patient_population: two developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) ultrasound datasets, infants
clinical_problem: automated landmark detection on hip ultrasound to support Graf's method diagnosis of developmental dysplasia of the hip in infants
model_description: Input: B-mode hip ultrasound images; output: detected anatomical landmarks used to compute Graf's method angles for DDH diagnosis.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
