title: Involution Transformer Based U-Net for Landmark Detection in Ultrasound Images for Diagnosis of Infantile DDH.
study_design: methods development and comparison on two DDH ultrasound datasets

patient_population: Fetal cardiac ultrasound dataset (collected dataset, size not specified numerically)
clinical_problem: Automated segmentation of the pulmonary artery, aorta, and superior vena cava in the three-vessel view of fetal cardiac ultrasound to improve detection of congenital heart disease anomalies.
model_description: CoFi-Net, a coarse-fine collaborative deep learning network with two parallel branches, takes fetal cardiac ultrasound three-vessel-view images as input and outputs segmentation of the pulmonary artery, ascending aorta and superior vena cava.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: A Coarse-Fine Collaborative Learning Model for Three Vessel Segmentation in Fetal Cardiac Ultrasound Images.
headline_result: Outperforms state-of-the-art segmentation models (specific metric not stated)

patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing 3D hand ultrasound imaging
clinical_problem: identifying and categorizing individual hand bones for pediatric bone assessment
model_description: Takes 3D ultrasound images of the pediatric hand as input and outputs segmentation masks delineating 38 individual bone structures, using an adaptive multi-dimensional attention deep learning network.
release_evidence: will be globally released as a plugin in the 3D Slicer
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: Adaptive Multi-Dimensional Weighted Network With Category-Aware Contrastive Learning for Fine-Grained Hand Bone Segmentation.
headline_result: Average Dice coefficient of 90.0% across 38 hand bone structures

patient_population: fetuses undergoing morphology ultrasound scan
clinical_problem: autonomous fetal morphology scan (view-plane and organ labeling for congenital anomaly detection)
model_description: Input is real-time fetal ultrasound video; the system first differentiates fetal view planes, then labels and segments internal organs (tested on the fetal abdomen) using a deep learning/clustering merger combined with YOLOv8 segmentation, intended as decision support alongside the sonographer.
journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
title: Autonomous fetal morphology scan: deep learning + clustering merger - the second pair of eyes behind the doctor.
study_design: clinical trial / technical development (registered trial PARADISE, NCT05738954)
dataset_size: not stated (fetal abdomen ultrasound image dataset)
headline_result: System correctly labeled view plane and corresponding organs on real-time ultrasound movies (no numeric performance given)

patient_population: 969 fetal ultrasound images (646 control, 323 kidney anomaly cases)
clinical_problem: Early detection of fetal kidney anomalies (urinary tract dilation, multicystic dysplastic kidney) from prenatal ultrasound
model_description: A CNN classifies prenatal ultrasound images as normal or as one of two kidney anomaly types (unilateral urinary tract dilation, unilateral multicystic dysplastic kidney), with Grad-CAM/HiResCAM visualization used to interpret predictions and misclassifications
title: Deep learning prediction of renal anomalies for prenatal ultrasound diagnosis.
headline_result: Cross-validated AUC 91.28% +/- 0.52%, accuracy 84.03% +/- 0.76%

model_family: radiomics/dosiomics with machine learning feature selection and clustering
patient_population: 48 children (mean age 12±6 years) with metastatic medulloblastoma treated with craniospinal irradiation
clinical_problem: identifying imaging/dose-based biomarkers of radiation-induced neurotoxicity in pediatric metastatic medulloblastoma
model_description: Radiomic features from T1/T2/FLAIR MRI and dosiomic features from the radiotherapy dose distribution are extracted from tumor regions and reduced/selected using machine learning, then used in supervised and unsupervised clustering to stratify pediatric medulloblastoma patients by risk of radiation-induced neurotoxicity.
journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
title: Radiomic- and dosiomic-based clustering development for radio-induced neurotoxicity in pediatric medulloblastoma.
dataset_size: 48 pediatric medulloblastoma patients, 332 extracted features each
headline_result: one-component radiomic signature accuracy 0.73, sensitivity 0.83, specificity 0.64

patient_population: 226 Chilean pediatric patients (68 healthy control, 58 craniopharyngioma, 100 differential sellar/suprasellar tumors)
clinical_problem: Using deep learning to classify pediatric sellar/suprasellar tumors (craniopharyngioma vs differential tumors vs healthy) on MRI to support radiological diagnosis.
model_description: A convolutional deep learning algorithm with explainable AI (XAI) takes T1w and T2w preoperative brain MRI as input and classifies patients into healthy control, craniopharyngioma, or differential sellar/suprasellar tumor categories.
journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
title: Diagnostic support in pediatric craniopharyngioma using deep learning.

patient_population: Over 120 training datasets across field strengths; prospectively tested in 9 fetal subjects at 20-37 weeks gestation
clinical_problem: Fully automatic real-time planning of standard fetal brain MRI imaging planes to widen availability of fetal MRI, especially on low-field 0.55T scanners
model_description: Input: whole-uterus echo planar imaging scan; output: automatic detection of fetal brain landmarks (eyes, cerebellum) used to plan subsequent radiological brain MRI acquisition planes in real time, via a deep learning landmark detection pipeline
title: Fully automated planning for anatomical fetal brain MRI on 0.55T.
dataset_size: over 120 training datasets; prospective test in 9 fetal subjects
headline_result: landmark detection accuracy 4.2±2.6 mm (eyes), 6.5±3.2 mm (cerebellum); planning quality 2.4/3 vs. 2.6/3 manual

patient_population: Children diagnosed with congenital heart disease; dataset of 828 chest X-rays
clinical_problem: Providing a public annotated dataset of pediatric chest radiographs (with congenital heart disease) to support development of deep learning models detecting congenital heart disease from subtle chest X-ray features.
model_description: Dataset release (CHD-CXR) of DICOM chest radiographs with corresponding cardiac ultrasound reports, plus a preliminary deep learning classification model trained on it to detect congenital heart disease.
release_evidence: "we have released a dataset containing 828 DICOM chest x-ray files... publicly available datasets at: https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/congenital-heart-disease"
title: CHD-CXR: a de-identified publicly available dataset of chest x-ray for congenital heart disease.
study_design: dataset release with preliminary model benchmark
headline_result: Preliminary model AUC 0.85

patient_population: developing Human Connectome Project, >700 babies aged 26-45 weeks postconception
clinical_problem: robust automated segmentation of neonatal brain MRI despite variability in contrast, age, and acquisition protocol, for multisite studies
model_description: Input: neonatal T2-weighted (or synthetic) brain MRI of varying contrast; output: brain structure segmentation, trained on synthetic images generated from a few labeled subjects to be contrast-independent.
title: Comprehensive analysis of synthetic learning applied to neonatal brain MRI segmentation.
study_design: methods development and comparison against standard supervised UNet
dataset_size: >700 babies, 26-45 weeks postconception (developing Human Connectome Project)

model_family: ResNet-50 with geometric/color augmentation and preprocessing pipelines
patient_population: 364 premature neonates, 1090 abdominal radiographs
clinical_problem: computer-aided diagnosis of necrotising enterocolitis on neonatal abdominal radiographs
model_description: A ResNet-50-based classifier is trained on abdominal radiographs to perform three-class necrotising enterocolitis classification; the study systematically evaluates geometric and colour-scheme augmentations and proposes two contrast/edge-enhancement preprocessing pipelines to improve accuracy on this limited dataset.
journal: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
title: An investigation into augmentation and preprocessing for optimising X-ray classification in limited datasets: a case study on necrotising enterocolitis.
headline_result: translation augmentation +6.2%; combined preprocessing/augmentation pipelines improved accuracy up to 7.1%

model_family: radiomics + multivariate logistic regression / random forest
patient_population: 32 patients (training, institution A) and 14 patients (external test, institution B), age <=18 years
clinical_problem: Predicting which neuroblastic tumors are high-risk neuroblastoma using MRI radiomics
model_description: Radiomics features (n=930) extracted from manually segmented pre-treatment MRI tumor regions feed multivariate logistic regression and random forest models (10-fold cross-validated) that predict high-risk neuroblastoma status; models were tested on an external institution's cohort.
title: Prediction of High-Risk Neuroblastoma Among Neuroblastic Tumors Using Radiomics Features Derived from Magnetic Resonance Imaging: A Pilot Study.
study_design: Retrospective pilot study with external test set
headline_result: MLR model AUC 0.94 training and test; random forest AUC 0.83 (training CV), 0.91 (test)

patient_population: 193 preterm infants (62 extremely preterm, 131 very-to-late preterm)
clinical_problem: Predicting 2-year neurodevelopmental outcomes in preterm infants from structural and diffusion brain MRI connectivity features
model_description: Volumetric and structural brain network (local connectivity) features from term-equivalent-age MRI and diffusion MRI are input to linear and nonlinear machine learning models that predict Bayley Scales (cognitive, motor, language) scores at 2 years.
title: Predicting 2-year neurodevelopmental outcomes in preterm infants using multimodal structural brain magnetic resonance imaging with local connectivity.
headline_result: variance explained 15-17% for cognitive/motor/language scores

model_family: radiomics feature analysis (pyradiomics feature extraction with feature-importance ranking)
patient_population: 91 fetuses with Chiari II malformation (101 MRI scans), single center
clinical_problem: identifying fetal brain edema in Chiari II malformation on prenatal MRI to help select candidates for fetal surgery
model_description: Multiparametric MRI analysis combining diffusion tensor imaging metrics with radiomics features extracted (via pyradiomics) from manually segmented fetal brain parenchyma, ranking the most discriminative features for distinguishing fetuses with versus without brain edema
title: Multiparametric prenatal imaging characterization of fetal brain edema in Chiari II malformation might help to select candidates for fetal surgery.
headline_result: top 10 radiomics features achieved AUC 0.81 (95% CI 0.71-0.91) for discriminating edema vs non-edema fetuses

patient_population: children younger than 12 years old from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE)
clinical_problem: autism spectrum disorder recognition from functional connectivity
model_description: Regions of interest from resting-state fMRI are treated as nodes of a graph, with wavelet-decomposed BOLD signal features and a functional-connectivity-derived adjacency matrix. A graph attention network with self-attention and node-selection pooling layers classifies scans for autism spectrum disorder while also highlighting the brain regions driving the prediction, improving interpretability over prior deep learning approaches.
title: A novel approach for ASD recognition based on graph attention networks.
headline_result: Superior performance compared to recent similar ASD-classification studies (exact accuracy not given in abstract)

patient_population: 297 patients enrolled in two Children's Oncology Group trials (AHOD1331, AHOD0831)
clinical_problem: quantifying residual disease on interim PET/CT for pediatric Hodgkin lymphoma
model_description: LAS-Net takes paired baseline and interim PET/CT scans and uses longitudinal cross-attention so baseline features inform interim-scan analysis, segmenting lymphoma and detecting residual disease; it also outputs quantitative PET metrics (MTV, TLG, qPET, deltaSUVmax) compared against physician measurements.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Automatic Quantification of Serial PET/CT Images for Pediatric Hodgkin Lymphoma Patients Using a Longitudinally-Aware Segmentation Network.
dataset_size: 297 pediatric Hodgkin lymphoma patients from two COG trials
headline_result: F1 0.606 for interim residual disease detection; Dice 0.772 baseline segmentation; Spearman's rho 0.78-0.96 vs physician measurements

model_family: AI-based automatic segmentation + statistical shape model (PCA)
patient_population: 678 mandibles from CT scans of children and young adults aged 0-22 years
clinical_problem: creating a three-dimensional statistical growth reference model of the mandible spanning birth to young adulthood to aid diagnosis, treatment planning and evaluation of mandibular growth abnormalities
model_description: Input: CT scans of the mandible; output: an automatically (AI-based) segmented 3D mandible shape, registered across subjects to build an open-source statistical shape growth model capturing age-related and sex-related variation.
release_evidence: the first open-source, three-dimensional statistical shape model of the mandible... presented growth model is accessible globally and free-of-charge
title: An open-source, three-dimensional growth model of the mandible.

patient_population: pediatric sarcoma patients (review of 10 studies from a search of 72 papers)
clinical_problem: reviewing the role of radiomics for diagnosis and predictive modeling in pediatric sarcomas (Ewing sarcoma, osteosarcoma)
model_description: Systematic review of 10 radiomics studies in pediatric sarcoma using CT, MRI, PET/CT and PET/MRI, assessed for methodological quality (RQS, METRICS); covers diagnostic and prognostic/treatment-response radiomics applications, no single model detailed.
title: Advancing Pediatric Sarcomas through Radiomics: A Systematic Review and Prospective Assessment Using Radiomics Quality Score (RQS) and Methodological Radiomics Score (METRICS).
study_design: systematic review with methodological quality assessment (RQS/METRICS)

model_family: commercially available vendor deep learning denoising reconstruction algorithm
body_region: knee growth plate (femoral and tibial physis)
patient_population: children undergoing knee DTI at a tertiary pediatric center
clinical_problem: image quality of diffusion tensor imaging of the pediatric growth plate
model_description: A vendor-provided deep learning denoising reconstruction algorithm (75% noise reduction) was applied to knee DTI scans acquired at two spatial resolutions in children, and diffusion tract metrics (count, volume, length, fractional anisotropy) were compared between denoised and non-denoised scans to assess whether denoising preserves or alters quantitative growth-plate diffusion measurements.
release_evidence: the MR vendor-provided a commercially available DL model
title: Impact of Deep Learning Denoising Algorithm on Diffusion Tensor Imaging of the Growth Plate on Different Spatial Resolutions.
dataset_size: prospective study; exact N not stated in abstract
headline_result: Deep learning reconstruction significantly changed several diffusion metrics (e.g., decreased femorotibial FA, p<0.01) versus non-denoised scans at smaller voxel size

patient_population: 195 preoperative MRIs from children with medulloblastoma (n=69) or pilocytic astrocytoma (n=126) across six university hospitals
clinical_problem: Differentiating medulloblastoma from pilocytic astrocytoma, the two most common pediatric brain tumors, preoperatively
model_description: A patch-based 3D-DenseNet deep learning classifier, using automated tumor segmentation and all individually available preoperative MRI sequences, differentiates medulloblastoma from pilocytic astrocytoma and is compared against five human readers of varying experience.
title: Human-Level Differentiation of Medulloblastoma from Pilocytic Astrocytoma: A Real-World Multicenter Pilot Study.
study_design: Retrospective multicenter proof-of-concept diagnostic accuracy study
dataset_size: 195 preoperative MRIs (69 medulloblastoma, 126 pilocytic astrocytoma) from six university hospitals; 64-patient test set
headline_result: AUC 0.986; 62/64 (97%) correct diagnoses in test set; on par with pediatric neuro-oncology experts, better than inexperienced readers (p<0.05)

patient_population: 3508 lateral elbow radiographs, mean age 9.8±1.8 years, children under 18
clinical_problem: pubertal bone age assessment using a single lateral elbow radiograph via olecranon ossification
model_description: A new olecranon-based bone age classification was developed from lateral elbow radiographs and a deep-learning AI model (EfficientDet-b4) was trained to automatically assign olecranon bone age stage, compared against established hand and elbow bone age methods.
title: Olecranon bone age assessment in puberty using a lateral elbow radiograph and a deep-learning model.
study_design: retrospective single-center development with external validation
headline_result: AI model accuracy 0.96, specificity 0.98 internally; external validation accuracy 0.86, specificity 0.91

patient_population: 523 pediatric patients aged 0-21 years, racially diverse
clinical_problem: measuring pediatric lower-extremity length to build updated growth curves
model_description: input standing slot-scanning radiographs; output Mask R-CNN segmentation of the femur and tibia and measured femoral/tibial/total leg length, used to build growth curves
title: Lower Extremity Growth according to AI Automated Femorotibial Length Measurement on Slot-Scanning Radiographs in Pediatric Patients.
study_design: retrospective single-center study with an external test set
headline_result: mean absolute error 0.25/0.27/0.33 cm (femur/tibia/leg); 90% coverage probability 86.7% (AI) vs. 73.4% (Anderson-Green), P<.001

patient_population: 407 adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients and 227 non-scoliosis controls
clinical_problem: Can the Lenke classification of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis be assigned automatically from spinal x-rays, reducing observer-dependent variability in this preoperative evaluation?
model_description: A key-point-based deep learning detector localizes vertebrae on whole-spine x-rays to measure Cobb angle and classify curve type, and a segmentation model identifies lumbar vertebral pedicles to determine the lumbar spine modifier, together producing an automated Lenke classification.
title: Automatic Lenke classification of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis with deep learning.
study_design: retrospective single-center model development and testing
headline_result: Cobb angle measurement ICC 0.925; F1-scores 0.809-0.942 for component classifiers; final Lenke type classifier F1-score 0.885

patient_population: 116 children with hepatoblastoma who received neoadjuvant chemotherapy
clinical_problem: Predicting whether a child's hepatoblastoma will respond to neoadjuvant chemotherapy, using contrast-enhanced CT before treatment
model_description: Radiomics features from pretreatment contrast-enhanced CT are selected and input to a support vector machine radiomics model, combined with a clinical logistic-regression model, to predict RECIST response of hepatoblastoma to neoadjuvant chemotherapy
journal: Journal of cancer research and clinical oncology
title: Predicting response of hepatoblastoma primary lesions to neoadjuvant chemotherapy through contrast-enhanced computed tomography radiomics.
headline_result: Combined clinical-radiomics model AUC 0.874 (training), 0.830 (validation)

model_family: deep learning (SegResNet, DynUNet, SwinUNETR; MONAI framework)
patient_population: 1,731 CT examinations: 483 from three internal pediatric (<=18 years) datasets, 1,248 from three public datasets (pediatric and adult, various pathologies)
clinical_problem: Can deep learning organ segmentation models, well validated in adults, be adapted to accurately segment the liver, spleen and pancreas on pediatric abdominal CT?
model_description: Deep learning segmentation models (three architectures) take abdominal CT as input and output segmentation masks for liver, spleen and pancreas, trained either natively on institutional pediatric data or via transfer learning pretrained on public datasets and fine-tuned on pediatric data; compared against the public TotalSegmentator tool.
release_evidence: 'made available as an open-source MONAI bundle (https://github.com/cchmc-dll/pediatric_abdominal_segmentation_bundle.git)'
title: Deep Learning Models for Abdominal CT Organ Segmentation in Children: Development and Validation in Internal and Heterogeneous Public Datasets.
study_design: retrospective multi-dataset model development and validation study
headline_result: Transfer-learning DynUNet model (best performer) Dice on internal pediatric data: liver 0.965-0.966, spleen 0.937-0.945, pancreas 0.775-0.786; outperformed TotalSegmentator and native training especially on public/adult data

patient_population: 30 preschool-aged children with ASD, 22 typically developing controls
clinical_problem: Diagnosing autism spectrum disorder in preschool children using structural and perfusion (arterial spin labeling) MRI-derived brain network features and machine learning.
model_description: A random vector functional link network machine learning model takes T1-weighted gray matter and ASL-based cerebral blood flow brain network features as input and classifies children as ASD or typical development.
title: Diagnosis for autism spectrum disorder children using T1-based gray matter and arterial spin labeling-based cerebral blood flow network metrics.
headline_result: Classification accuracy 84.91%

model_family: open-access deep learning fracture detection algorithm
patient_population: 240 patients (mean age 11.3 years, range 0-22, 37.9% female) with elbow, hand, humerus, wrist, forearm and clavicle radiographs
clinical_problem: upper extremity fractures missed by residents and pediatricians, who read most of these radiographs first
model_description: An openly accessible model, which is unusual in this literature and is the point: it is available at childfx.com rather than sold. Seven readers across three experience levels read the same cases with and without it. Residents and pediatric residents improved substantially; subspecialist musculoskeletal radiologists did not. With the model, residents reached the same accuracy as unaided subspecialists, and everyone read faster.
release_evidence: an open-source artificial intelligence algorithm at https://www.childfx.com
title: Artificial intelligence improves resident detection of pediatric and young adult upper extremity fractures.
headline_result: radiology resident AUC rose from 0.768 to 0.876 and pediatric resident AUC from 0.706 to 0.844 (both p < 0.001), with no significant gain for subspecialists; residents with AI matched unaided subspecialists (0.863 vs 0.867); reading time fell from 52.1 to 38.9 seconds

patient_population: Infants/toddlers with structural MRI (scarce, class-imbalanced, heterogeneous dataset; longitudinal two-time-point data), exact N not stated
clinical_problem: Early diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder in children under 2 years using structural brain MRI and deep learning, overcoming limitations of behavioral-based diagnosis at young ages.
model_description: A Siamese verification framework with an unsupervised feature compressor and path signature analysis takes longitudinal structural brain MRI as input and diagnoses early autism spectrum disorder, extracting machine-learning-identified brain regions relevant to diagnosis.
title: Early autism diagnosis based on path signature and Siamese unsupervised feature compressor.

patient_population: intrapartum transperineal ultrasound images from laboring patients
clinical_problem: objective assessment of fetal head descent during labor to guide delivery-mode decisions
model_description: Introduces a publicly available, pixel-level annotated dataset of intrapartum transperineal ultrasound images to support development and evaluation of AI models that segment the pubic symphysis and fetal head (PSFHS) for automated fetal head descent assessment.
release_evidence: publicly accessible datasets tailored for PSFHS are notably scarce...this dataset stands as the most expansive and comprehensive resource for PSFHS to date
title: PSFHS: Intrapartum ultrasound image dataset for AI-based segmentation of pubic symphysis and fetal head.
study_design: dataset publication (annotated benchmark dataset for AI segmentation)

patient_population: Newborn and fetal diffusion MRI datasets, external clinical validation datasets, and post-mortem histological validation
clinical_problem: Estimating white matter fiber orientation distribution in newborns and fetuses from limited diffusion MRI measurements, enabling microstructure assessment when only a few measurements are feasible.
model_description: A deep learning model maps as few as six diffusion-weighted MRI measurements to fiber orientation distribution functions, trained against multi-shell high-angular-resolution ground truth, validated across scanners and against histology.
title: Deep learning microstructure estimation of developing brains from diffusion MRI: A newborn and fetal study.
study_design: retrospective methods development with external and histological validation
headline_result: Agreement rate 77.5%/22.2% for 1/2-fiber voxels (3%/5.4% higher than other DL methods); angular error 10/20 degrees (6/5 degrees lower)

model_family: lightweight deep learning segmentation network (distribution-shifting convolutional blocks, tokenized MLP blocks, efficient feature fusion)
patient_population: two intrapartum ultrasound image datasets
clinical_problem: real-time segmentation of the fetal head and pubic symphysis to monitor labor progression on low-power, portable devices
model_description: Takes an intrapartum transperineal ultrasound image as input and outputs real-time segmentation of the fetal head and pubic symphysis, using a lightweight deep learning network (1.86 million parameters) designed to run on low-power portable hardware.
title: RTSeg-net: A lightweight network for real-time segmentation of fetal head and pubic symphysis from intrapartum ultrasound images.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and comparative evaluation study
headline_result: segmentation accuracy comparable to more complex state-of-the-art networks using only 6% of their parameters, running at 31.13 frames per second on a Jetson Nano (7x faster)

model_family: machine learning (AdaBoost, KNN, SVM with SHAP explainability)
patient_population: 144 adolescents (mean age 16.2+/-1.4 years): 81 with early-onset schizophrenia, 63 with early-onset bipolar disorder
clinical_problem: Differentiating early-onset schizophrenia from early-onset bipolar disorder using brain MRI surface morphometry
model_description: Explainable machine learning classifiers (AdaBoost, KNN, SVM) using T1-weighted MRI-derived cortical thickness, gyrification, sulcal depth, fractal dimension, and brain volume features, interpreted via SHAP, differentiate early-onset schizophrenia from early-onset bipolar disorder.
title: The Contribution of Explainable Machine Learning Algorithms Using ROI-based Brain Surface Morphology Parameters in Distinguishing Early-onset Schizophrenia From Bipolar Disorder.
headline_result: AdaBoost accuracy 82.75% (Destrieux atlas, all variables); KNN accuracy 79.31% (Desikan-Killiany-Tourville atlas)

patient_population: 611 infants in the first month of life (174 preterm, 437 term) from the Developing Human Connectome Project
clinical_problem: estimating brain maturity (brain age) from the neonatal connectome
model_description: Resting-state fMRI and diffusion MRI connectomes from newborns are used to train connectome-based predictive models that estimate postmenstrual age. The gap between predicted and actual age (the 'brain age gap') is used as a marker of deviation from normal brain development, and was linked to perinatal exposures and later toddler behavior.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
title: Brain age prediction and deviations from normative trajectories in the neonatal connectome.
headline_result: Structural and functional connectomes accurately predicted postmenstrual age in both term and preterm infants; brain age gap associated with perinatal exposures and toddler outcomes

model_family: deep-learning variational autoencoder (VAE) and PCA for dimensionality reduction
patient_population: 69 CT scans of 2-4-month-old infant heads
clinical_problem: quantifying cranial suture and fontanelle morphology to aid diagnosis of suture-related skull fractures
model_description: CT scans of infant heads are segmented to identify suture/fontanelle semilandmarks, and morphological parameters (length, width, sinuosity, area) are computed; nonlinear/linear PCA and a deep-learning variational autoencoder are compared for dimensionality reduction, then related to global cranial parameters via regression.
title: Quantitative morphological analysis framework of infant cranial sutures and fontanelles based on CT images.
dataset_size: 69 CT scans of infants aged 2-4 months

model_family: lightweight attention denoising convolutional neural network (autoencoder)
body_region: brachial plexus and fetal ultrasound images
patient_population: brachial plexus ultrasound images and fetal ultrasound images
clinical_problem: reducing speckle noise in medical ultrasound images, including fetal ultrasound, to improve diagnostic image quality
model_description: LAD-CNN is a denoising autoencoder that adds lightweight channel-attention and large-kernel attention blocks in its encoder/decoder stages with a skip connection, trained to remove noise from ultrasound images (including fetal ultrasound) while preserving texture detail, evaluated with PSNR and SSIM against other denoising methods.
journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
title: Ultrasound image denoising autoencoder model based on lightweight attention mechanism.
dataset_size: brachial plexus and fetal ultrasound image sets (size not specified)
headline_result: highest PSNR/SSIM among compared models; average PSNR 0.20-0.33 higher than suboptimal model on fetal ultrasound images

model_family: feature pyramid network + Siamese contrastive learning
patient_population: 493 infants imaged with various ultrasound machines
clinical_problem: Improving automated diagnosis of infant hip dysplasia across ultrasound images from different machines and infants, despite limited labeled data
model_description: A semi-supervised method pretrains a Siamese-network feature pyramid on a large set of unlabeled infant hip ultrasound images via contrastive learning, then fine-tunes on a small labeled set to identify anatomical landmarks and recognize standard planes per Graf's method
journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
title: Semi-supervised learning in diagnosis of infant hip dysplasia towards multisource ultrasound images.
headline_result: Mean Dice 0.7873 and Hausdorff distance 5.0102 for landmark identification; standard-plane recognition accuracy 95.4%

patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal CHD screening (review of published literature)
clinical_problem: reviewing AI applications (imaging, genetic diagnosis, risk prediction) for prenatal diagnosis of congenital heart disease
model_description: Review of AI methods for prenatal CHD diagnosis, covering imaging-based detection, genetic diagnosis, and risk prediction, with representative examples for each; discusses current limitations (variability, insufficiency, and independence of data).
title: Applications of artificial intelligence-powered prenatal diagnosis for congenital heart disease.

patient_population: intrapartum ultrasound imaging (patient numbers not stated)
clinical_problem: automatically identifying the pubic symphysis-fetal head standard ultrasound plane during labor to measure the angle of progression, reducing operator dependency
model_description: Input: intrapartum ultrasound images; output: identification of the pubic symphysis-fetal head standard plane to enable subsequent angle-of-progression measurement.
title: PSFHSP-Net: an efficient lightweight network for identifying pubic symphysis-fetal head standard plane from intrapartum ultrasound images.
study_design: model development and comparison against heavyweight and lightweight baselines
headline_result: Accuracy 0.8995, F1 0.9075, recall 0.9191, precision 0.9022, AUC 0.930

model_family: nnU-Net and DeepMedic (3D deep learning segmentation models)
patient_population: 339 pediatric patients (293 internal, 46 external cohort) with a variety of brain tumor subtypes
clinical_problem: automated segmentation of pediatric brain tumors and subregions on MRI for surgical/treatment planning and response assessment
model_description: Input is multiparametric preoperative MRI; output is a 3D segmentation of enhancing tumor, nonenhancing tumor, cystic components and peritumoral edema, comparing two deep learning models (nnU-Net and DeepMedic) trained on pediatric-specific multi-institutional data.
title: Training and Comparison of nnU-Net and DeepMedic Methods for Autosegmentation of Pediatric Brain Tumors.
study_design: retrospective multi-institutional model comparison and external validation study
dataset_size: 339 pediatric patients (293 internal, 46 external) with multiparametric MRI
headline_result: nnU-Net mean Dice 0.9 for whole tumor internally; on external BraTS-PEDs 2023 validation, Dice 0.87 (whole tumor), 0.83 (tumor core), 0.48 (enhancing tumor); nnU-Net significantly outperformed DeepMedic (P<=.01)

patient_population: pediatric patients with appendicitis
clinical_problem: automated grading of pediatric appendicitis severity from free-text operative and ultrasound reports
model_description: letter commenting on an AI/NLP method for labeling free-text operative and ultrasound reports to grade pediatric appendicitis severity (abstract text not available)
title: Comment on: Using Artificial Intelligence to Label Free-Text Operative and Ultrasound Reports for Grading Pediatric Appendicitis.

patient_population: 105 pediatric patients with Wilms' tumor
clinical_problem: automatically segmenting and measuring the volume of Wilms' tumor on CT to guide treatment decisions and reduce inter-radiologist variability
model_description: nnU-Net-based automatic segmentation model that outlines Wilms' tumor on contrast-enhanced CT intravenous-phase images, with volume estimates further refined using the ratio of the tumor's 3D diameters
title: Automated segmentation and volume prediction in pediatric Wilms' tumor CT using nnu-net.
headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient 0.83±0.22, HD95 10.50±8.98 mm; volume percentage difference improved from 21.08%±30.46% to 10.16%±9.70% after optimization

patient_population: 141 normal fetuses, 101 fetuses with ventriculomegaly (68 resolved, 33 stable), 2014-2023
clinical_problem: Predicting postnatal enlarged lateral ventricle outcomes in fetuses with isolated ventriculomegaly from a single prenatal MRI
model_description: Logistic regression models (5-fold cross-validated) using lateral ventricle morphology and cortical/subcortical radiomics features from a single fetal MRI predict postnatal lateral ventricle alterations in fetuses with isolated ventriculomegaly.
title: Machine learning in prenatal MRI predicts postnatal ventricular abnormalities in fetuses with isolated ventriculomegaly.
headline_result: Subcortical-radiomics model distinguishing normal vs ventriculomegaly fetuses: AUC 1/0.992 (train/val); predicting postnatal alteration: AUC 0.822/0.743 (train/val)

patient_population: 114 depressed adolescents (clinical controls, NSSI-only, NSSI+suicide attempt groups)
clinical_problem: Identifying resting-state brain-network alterations that distinguish depressed adolescents with non-suicidal self-injury with and without suicide attempts, to inform risk biomarkers
model_description: Resting-state functional connectivity features are classified with a support vector machine to identify convergent and divergent brain-network alterations distinguishing depressed adolescents with non-suicidal self-injury, with or without suicide attempts, from clinical controls
title: Unveiling convergent and divergent intrinsic brain network alternations in depressed adolescents engaged in non-suicidal self-injurious behaviors with and without suicide attempts.
headline_result: SVM-based classification identified convergent limbic-network alterations across NSSI groups and divergent visual/subcortical alterations in the NSSI+SA group

model_family: graph neural network post-processing of DNN segmentation (U-Net, UNETr, MSGSE-Net backbones)
patient_population: healthy children and children after neonatal arterial ischemic stroke (NAIS)
clinical_problem: segmentation of basal ganglia after early brain lesion (neonatal arterial ischemic stroke)
model_description: Input is brain MRI of healthy children or children after neonatal stroke; a deep neural network (one of three backbones) produces an initial basal ganglia segmentation, which a graph neural network then refines using spatial/class-probability graphs to improve consistency in the presence of lesions.
journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
title: GNN-based structural information to improve DNN-based basal ganglia segmentation in children following early brain lesion.
dataset_size: not stated (small training datasets typical of pediatric/rare pathology)
headline_result: Median Dice improved up to 4%; median Hausdorff distance reduced up to 93% in healthy children (36.45 to 2.57) and up to 91% in NAIS children (40.64 to 3.50)

patient_population: 101 normal pediatric subjects and 46 pediatric subjects with thoracic insufficiency syndrome
clinical_problem: quantifying lung tissue and excursion to assess thoracic insufficiency syndrome via dynamic MRI
model_description: input free-breathing dynamic thoracic MRI; output interactive segmentation of lung tissue and lung excursion using a modified 2D U-Net incorporating shape features
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
title: Interactive Segmentation of Lung Tissue and Lung Excursion in Thoracic Dynamic MRI Based on Shape-guided Convolutional Neural Networks.
study_design: algorithm development and validation study (medRxiv preprint)
dataset_size: 202 dMRI scans from 101 normal subjects; 92 scans from 46 TIS subjects
headline_result: mean Dice 0.96±0.02 (normal), 0.89±0.05 (TIS)

patient_population: 18 pediatric patients with DIPG who underwent reirradiation
clinical_problem: predicting survival after reirradiation for progressive pediatric diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma using MRI features
model_description: Takes radiomic features extracted from FLAIR MRI at tumor progression as input, and produces a Cox proportional-hazards risk score predicting survival after reirradiation.
journal: Strahlentherapie und Onkologie : Organ der Deutschen Rontgengesellschaft ... [et al]
title: Reirradiation for diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma: prognostic radiomic factors at progression.
headline_result: Concordance 0.81 (95% CI 0.75-0.88); tumor sphericity and gray-level heterogeneity associated with longer survival

patient_population: 105 fetal echocardiography images of tetralogy of Fallot and 96 of ventricular septal defect
clinical_problem: differentiating ventricular septal defect from tetralogy of Fallot on fetal echocardiography
model_description: Four CNN architectures (VGG19, ResNet50, NTS-Net, WSDAN) classify fetal echocardiography images as tetralogy of Fallot vs. ventricular septal defect, compared by sensitivity, specificity and AUC.
journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
title: Deep learning-based differentiation of ventricular septal defect from tetralogy of Fallot in fetal echocardiography images.
headline_result: Best model (WSDAN) AUC 0.873

patient_population: 93 participants (79 female, 14 male) with a history of childhood maltreatment
clinical_problem: identifying which type and timing of childhood maltreatment is most associated with altered brain region volumes
model_description: Uses random forest regression on questionnaire-derived childhood maltreatment type and timing to predict volumes of the amygdala, hippocampus, and anterior cingulate cortex from structural MRI.
title: New insights into the effects of type and timing of childhood maltreatment on brain morphometry.
study_design: retrospective cross-sectional neuroimaging association study using random forest regression

body_region: thoraco-abdominal organs (lungs, kidneys, liver, spleen, skin)
patient_population: 189 (near-)normal pediatric subjects undergoing dynamic MRI
clinical_problem: segmenting thoraco-abdominal organs on dynamic MRI to support surgical planning for thoracic insufficiency syndrome and scoliosis
model_description: A two-stage deep-learning pipeline (recognition network then delineation network) auto-segments the lungs, kidneys, liver, spleen and thoraco-abdominal skin on dynamic MRI acquisitions of healthy pediatric subjects at different respiratory phases, intended to support modeling of normal versus deformed thoraco-abdominal anatomy in disorders like thoracic insufficiency syndrome and scoliosis.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
title: Auto-segmentation of thoraco-abdominal organs in pediatric dynamic MRI.
headline_result: average Dice 0.92-0.94 (lungs), 0.82 (kidneys), 0.90 (liver), 0.81 (spleen), 0.93 (skin)

patient_population: not stated (described as the largest dataset to date for fetal head metrics)
clinical_problem: Segmenting the fetal head on ultrasound for prenatal biometric measurement
model_description: FetSAM is a prompt-based deep learning segmentation model for fetal head ultrasound images, using a dual loss (weighted Dice + weighted Lovasz) and benchmarked against U-Net, DeepLabV3, and Segformer.
journal: IEEE open journal of engineering in medicine and biology
title: FetSAM: Advanced Segmentation Techniques for Fetal Head Biometrics in Ultrasound Imagery.
study_design: Retrospective model development and benchmarking study
dataset_size: Largest fetal head ultrasound dataset to date (exact N not stated)
headline_result: Dice 0.90117, Hausdorff distance 1.86484, average surface distance 0.46645

patient_population: children with brain tumors, across response assessment practice
clinical_problem: why two readers measuring the same pediatric brain tumor get different answers, and what AI segmentation would need to fix it
model_description: Works through the specific ambiguities the RAPNO response criteria do not resolve: separating non-enhancing tumor from peritumoral edema, mild from absent enhancement, and the various cystic components, all made worse by non-uniform imaging protocols. The argument for the database is a caution: automated segmentation can only be as consistent as the manual ground truth it learns from, so definitions have to be agreed before the models can help.
title: Towards consistency in pediatric brain tumor measurements: Challenges, solutions, and the role of artificial intelligence-based segmentation.

model_family: quadratic discriminant analysis and bootstrap forest models
patient_population: 242 children aged 18 years and under at a chest-wall deformity clinic
clinical_problem: determining pectus excavatum severity/surgical candidacy without CT radiation using white light body-surface scanning
model_description: input white light surface scan measurements and demographics; output predicted CT Haller Index/Correction Index and surgical-candidacy classification via discriminant analysis and bootstrap forest models
title: Utility of White Light Scanning as an Alternative to Computed Tomography to Evaluate Severity of Pectus Excavatum Deformity.
study_design: retrospective single-center diagnostic study (Level III evidence)
headline_result: AUC 0.91 (Haller Index≥3.25), AUC 0.84 (Correction Index≥28%); test ICC 0.86 (HI), 0.75 (CI)

patient_population: 258 pediatric MPP patients (194 training at institution 1, 64 external test at institution 2)
clinical_problem: Predicting macrolide-resistance-associated gene mutation status in children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia from chest CT
model_description: Radiomics features from semi-automatically segmented pulmonary lesions on chest CT are used in logistic regression and random forest models to predict 23S rRNA gene mutation status (macrolide resistance) in children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia.
title: Chest Computed Tomography Radiomics for Determining Macrolide Resistance-Associated Gene Mutation Status in Children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae Pneumonia: A Two-Center Study.
study_design: Retrospective two-center model development and external validation study
dataset_size: 258 patients (194 training, 64 external test), two institutions
headline_result: Logistic regression AUC 0.868 (train), 0.855 (external test); random forest AUC 0.941 (train), 0.815 (external test)

patient_population: 1,083 fetal four-chamber-view ultrasound images
clinical_problem: automatically segmenting anatomical structures and measuring cardiac axis and cardiothoracic ratio on fetal four-chamber ultrasound views to aid early detection of congenital heart defects
model_description: nnU-NetV2-based deep learning model trained on annotated fetal four-chamber ultrasound images to segment 15 critical anatomical structures and automatically compute cardiac axis and cardiothoracic ratio, compared against sonographers of varying experience
journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
title: Automatic segmentation of 15 critical anatomical labels and measurements of cardiac axis and cardiothoracic ratio in fetal four chambers using nnU-NetV2.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and internal validation
headline_result: mean Dice 87.11%, mean IoU 77.68% for segmentation; ICC 0.83 (cardiac axis) and 0.81 (cardiothoracic ratio) versus experienced sonographers

patient_population: Modeled birth cohort (560-659 births per scenario), Israeli health system data
clinical_problem: Economic evaluation of adding deep-learning-assisted prenatal ultrasound to standard screening (ultrasound plus pulse oximetry) for detecting congenital heart disease.
model_description: A cost-utility model compares standard prenatal ultrasound plus pulse oximetry screening against the same screening augmented with a deep-learning-assisted ultrasound tool for detecting congenital heart disease prenatally.
journal: Cost effectiveness and resource allocation : C/E
title: Cost-utility analysis of prenatal diagnosis of congenital cardiac diseases using deep learning.
headline_result: DL-US sensitivity 95% vs 58.1% standard; cost-effectiveness 1,720 USD per QALY

patient_population: 390 patients (ages 2-81) for training across four datasets; 280 patients (ages 4-90) across six datasets for validation
age_groups: child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: Can a single brain segmentation model work accurately across the full age range from infancy to late adulthood, rather than requiring separate age-specific models?
model_description: A deep learning model trained on T1-weighted MRI across a wide age span segments brain tissues and structures, evaluated for accuracy and scan-rescan/scanner reproducibility against age-specific pediatric and adult tools (childmetrix, FastSurfer, icobrain v5.9).
title: A deep learning model for brain segmentation across pediatric and adult populations.
study_design: retrospective multi-dataset model development and cross-scanner validation
headline_result: Segmentation accuracy comparable to age-specific pediatric and adult models; significantly higher intra- and inter-scanner reproducibility than childmetrix, FastSurfer and icobrain v5.9 (p<0.01)

clinical_problem: Detecting congenital heart defects on fetal ultrasound to improve early detection rates beyond the current ~60%
model_description: Review of deep-learning-based fetal ultrasound image evaluation techniques (preprocessing, localization, segmentation, classification, including CNN-based denoising and CNN/ANN-based segmentation) for detecting congenital heart defects.
title: Investigation on ultrasound images for detection of fetal congenital heart defects.

patient_population: 40 participants (19 with wrist fracture, 21 with sprain), diagnosis confirmed by X-ray
clinical_problem: Detecting wrist fractures in children from infrared thermal imaging as an alternative/adjunct to X-ray
model_description: A 34-layer CNN classifies Fourier-transformed infrared thermal images of pediatric wrists (frequency-domain magnitude spectra) as fractured or non-fractured (sprain).
title: Convolutional Neural Network to Classify Infrared Thermal Images of Fractured Wrists in Pediatrics.
study_design: Retrospective pilot diagnostic model development study
headline_result: Sensitivity 88%, accuracy 76%

model_family: explainable AI / machine learning decision-support system
patient_population: pregnant women in labor undergoing vaginal digital exam and intrapartum ultrasound (sample size not stated)
clinical_problem: predicting dystocic (obstructed) labor and mode of delivery from intrapartum ultrasound measurements of fetal head position
model_description: AIDA, a human-in-the-loop explainable AI algorithm, takes four ultrasound-measured 'geometric parameters' of fetal head position/engagement as input and classifies labor progress into five reference classes predicting delivery outcome (spontaneous vaginal, operative vaginal, or cesarean).
title: Artificial Intelligence, Intrapartum Ultrasound and Dystocic Delivery: AIDA (Artificial Intelligence Dystocia Algorithm), a Promising Helping Decision Support System.

patient_population: children with ALL and normal children (604 brain MRI studies)
clinical_problem: identification of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) marrow involvement from brain MRI

title: Radiomics model and deep learning model based on T1WI image for acute lymphoblastic leukemia identification.
dataset_size: 604 brain MRI studies (ALL and normal children)
headline_result: AUC 0.981 (deep learning) vs 0.962 (radiomics) in the testing cohort; accuracy 0.934/sensitivity 0.870/specificity 0.974 for deep learning model

model_family: radiomics (LASSO feature selection + machine learning classifier)
patient_population: 297 GHD and 300 ISS children (4-12 years) training/validation; external cohort of 49 GHD and 51 ISS
clinical_problem: distinguishing growth hormone deficiency from idiopathic short stature in children using pituitary MRI

title: Pituitary MRI Radiomics Improves Diagnostic Performance of Growth Hormone Deficiency in Children Short Stature: A Multicenter Radiomics Study.
study_design: retrospective multicenter radiomics model development with external validation
dataset_size: 297 GHD + 300 ISS (training/validation); external test 49 GHD + 51 ISS
headline_result: AUC 0.762 (clinical-radiomics) in external testing cohort

clinical_problem: Reviewing how AI (machine learning, NLP, neural networks, computer vision) can be applied throughout pregnancy for early detection, monitoring and risk assessment of feto-maternal health.
model_description: Narrative review describing applications of AI subfields (machine learning, NLP, artificial neural networks, computer vision) across feto-maternal healthcare, including fetal ultrasound analysis for abnormality detection.
title: A Theoretical Exploration of Artificial Intelligence's Impact on Feto-Maternal Health from Conception to Delivery.

patient_population: 94 preschool children aged 3-6 years (53 female, 41 male), China
clinical_problem: Assessing bone age in preschool children and reducing inter/intra-observer variability with AI assistance
model_description: An AI model system assists radiology reviewers performing bone age assessment (TW3 and RUS-CHN methods) on hand radiographs of preschool children; evaluated for its effect on inter- and intra-observer agreement rather than as a standalone diagnostic tool.
title: Artificial intelligence model system for bone age assessment of preschool children.

clinical_problem: Diagnosing autism spectrum disorder in children using cortical myelination abnormalities (T1w/T2w ratio maps) via a convolutional neural network model.

title: T1w/T2w ratio maps identify children with autism spectrum disorder and the relationships between myelin-related changes and symptoms.
headline_result: CNN model demonstrated high diagnostic efficacy for ASD (specific metric not stated)

patient_population: children with cancer undergoing diagnostic imaging
clinical_problem: applying AI to pediatric cancer imaging acquisition, processing, diagnosis, staging and treatment-response monitoring
model_description: Narrative review of current AI applications in pediatric cancer imaging, covering image acquisition, processing, reconstruction, segmentation, diagnosis, staging, and treatment-response monitoring, and the challenges (data scarcity, anatomic diversity, nonstandardized protocols) limiting clinical translation; no single model is developed.
title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence for Pediatric Cancer Imaging.

model_family: recurrent neural network (RNN) with temporal data augmentation
patient_population: pregnant women from the Successive Small-for-Gestational-Age Births study
clinical_problem: predicting fetal macrosomia/large-for-gestational-age from longitudinal ultrasound-derived weight estimates
model_description: input augmented longitudinal sequences of ultrasound-derived estimated fetal weight plus maternal characteristics; output predicted birthweight and macrosomia/LGA classification via an RNN
title: An innovative supervised longitudinal learning procedure of recurrent neural networks with temporal data augmentation: Insights from predicting fetal macrosomia and large-for-gestational age.

patient_population: 408 newborns (408 abdominal X-rays, 11,016 laboratory results)
clinical_problem: Assisting early diagnosis of necrotizing enterocolitis in newborns using abdominal X-ray and laboratory data
model_description: A multimodal model combines initial laboratory test results with abdominal radiograph images to output a diagnosis (NEC vs non-NEC), with Grad-CAM highlighting attended image regions.
title: Development of an artificial intelligence-based multimodal model for assisting in the diagnosis of necrotizing enterocolitis in newborns: a retrospective study.
