model_family: logistic regression, classification tree, and random forest models
patient_population: 64 pediatric osteosarcoma patients suspected of lung metastases on CT, 100 thoracotomies
clinical_problem: predicting pulmonary metastases to qualify children and adolescents with osteosarcoma for thoracotomy
model_description: CT scans of osteosarcoma patients are evaluated for nodule number, size, calcification and location; logistic regression, classification tree and random forest models are built from these CT-derived features to predict which patients truly have pulmonary metastases, aiming to reduce unnecessary thoracotomies.
title: Predictors of pulmonary metastases on chest computed tomography in children and adolescents with osteosarcoma-tips for qualifying patients for thoracotomy.
headline_result: sensitivity 72-92%, positive predictive value 81-90%, accuracy 74-79% across models

patient_population: 981 Mycoplasma pneumonia patients (590 internal: 450 adults/140 children; 391 external test: 121 adults/270 children)
clinical_problem: Distinguishing children from adults with Mycoplasma pneumonia based on clinical, CT imaging, and radiomic features, and quantitatively representing CT imaging signs
model_description: Combined clinical, CT-image, and radiomics (LASSO-selected from 1,904 extracted features) logistic regression models differentiate adult from pediatric Mycoplasma pneumonia cases and provide quantitative radiomic representations of qualitative CT signs.
title: Quantitative radiomics analysis of imaging features in adults and children Mycoplasma pneumonia.
study_design: Retrospective multi-cohort model development and external validation
headline_result: Combined model AUC 0.996 (train), 0.972 (validation), 0.986 (external test)

patient_population: Primary cohort n=101 girls with AIS (followed 6.22+/-0.33 years); secondary cohort n=106 girls with mild AIS
clinical_problem: Predicting risk of scoliosis curve progression in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis based on bone microarchitecture phenotypes
model_description: Unsupervised machine learning (fuzzy C-means clustering) groups girls with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis into three bone microarchitecture phenotypes based on HR-pQCT parameters, which are then tested as predictors of curve-progression risk to surgical threshold.
journal: Journal of bone and mineral research : the official journal of the American Society for Bone and Mineral Research
title: Distinguishing risk of curve progression in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis with bone microarchitecture phenotyping: a 6-year longitudinal study.
study_design: Prospective longitudinal cohort study with unsupervised ML phenotyping
dataset_size: Primary cohort n=101; secondary cohort n=106
headline_result: Phenotype 3: OR 4.88 (95%CI 1.03-28.63) for progression to surgical threshold; secondary cohort OR 5.39 (phenotype 2), 3.67 (phenotype 3) for progression >=6 degrees

patient_population: 59 fetal echocardiography referral cases (retrospective)
clinical_problem: Using a large language model (GPT-4) to determine appropriateness of referral for fetal echocardiography, compared to human specialists, to improve early detection of congenital heart defects.
model_description: GPT-4, a large language model, is given clinical/referral information and outputs a recommendation on whether fetal echocardiography referral is warranted, compared against pediatric cardiologist and gynecologist recommendations.
release_evidence: "OpenAI's GPT-4 (artificial intelligence [AI])"
title: Utilizing ChatGPT to Facilitate Referrals for Fetal Echocardiography.
headline_result: AI-expert agreement approximately 80%

model_family: deep-learning-based synthetic MRI generation for surface-based morphometry
patient_population: 24 patients aged 4-18 years with primary infratentorial tumors and 41 matched healthy controls
clinical_problem: characterizing supratentorial cortical and subcortical morphological changes caused by pediatric infratentorial (posterior fossa) tumors
model_description: Synthetic MPRAGE-like images are generated with deep learning algorithms from T2-axial brain MRI, then used to automatically calculate cortical thickness, surface area, volume, local gyrification index, and subcortical gray matter volumes, comparing pediatric infratentorial tumor patients with healthy controls.
title: Cortical and subcortical structural changes in pediatric patients with infratentorial tumors.
headline_result: cortical thinning in left supramarginal gyrus; volume reduction in several left-hemisphere gyri (P<0.05)

patient_population: 35 pediatric patients, mean age 9.2 years, range 1-17 years
clinical_problem: maintaining image quality/contrast enhancement in children's abdominal CT while reducing iodine contrast dose using AI
model_description: An AI-based contrast-boosting technique reconstructs low-iodine-dose abdominal CT images to increase organ/vessel attenuation and reduce noise, aiming to match standard-dose image quality in children.
title: Low-iodine-dose computed tomography coupled with an artificial intelligence-based contrast-boosting technique in children: a retrospective study on comparison with conventional-iodine-dose computed tomography.
headline_result: contrast-boosted images showed no significant difference in attenuation/CNR/SNR vs standard dose, but lower noise (P=0.002)

model_family: radiomics with logistic regression and quadratic discriminant analysis
patient_population: 66 children (16 DLBCL, 50 HL), 139 lymphoma lesions
clinical_problem: distinguishing diffuse large B-cell lymphoma from Hodgkin's lymphoma in children using enhanced CT
model_description: 2264 radiomics features are extracted from enhanced CT images of pediatric lymphoma lesions, reduced by correlation/mRMR/LASSO, and used to build logistic regression and quadratic discriminant analysis models, with and without the clinical marker LDH, to non-invasively distinguish DLBCL from Hodgkin's lymphoma.
title: Distinguishing diffuse large B-cell lymphoma from Hodgkin's lymphoma in children using an enhanced computed tomography radiomics approach.
headline_result: AUC 0.814-0.845 across radiomics and radiomics+LDH models

patient_population: pediatric chest radiographs (704 unique subjects; 2,800 fracture-present and 2,800 fracture-absent patches)
clinical_problem: rib fracture detection on pediatric chest radiographs
model_description: Input is a patch from a pediatric chest radiograph; a modified cycleGAN (using "near-pair" fracture-present/absent regions from the same subject plus a realism loss term) generates synthetic fracture-present images with known fracture location, which are added to the training set of a YOLOv5 rib-fracture object detector. Output is a bounding box indicating a suspected fracture.
title: Near-pair patch generative adversarial network for data augmentation of focal pathology object detection models.
study_design: retrospective technical development with observer study
dataset_size: 2,800 fracture-present and 2,800 fracture-absent image patches from 704 pediatric chest radiographs
headline_result: Object detector recall 0.57 and F2 0.59 when trained on 500 real + 500 synthetic radiographs, vs. recall 0.49 and F2 0.53 with 500 real radiographs alone; synthetic images rated 2.5/5 vs 4.1/5 (real fracture) on Likert fracture-likelihood scale by 4 pediatric radiologists

patient_population: fetal MRI cohort (size not stated)
clinical_problem: understanding what drives errors in deep-learning-based fetal brain age estimation from MRI, to better identify abnormal brain development
model_description: A convolutional neural network estimates fetal brain age from MRI; this study relates the predicted-age difference to cortical structural features (volume, surface area, curvature, folding depth).
title: The role of cortical structural variance in deep learning-based prediction of fetal brain age.
study_design: retrospective analysis of a deep learning fetal brain age model with regression analysis of cortical features

patient_population: children aged 3 to 14 years; 411 fracture and 190 normal radiograph samples
clinical_problem: automatically diagnosing supracondylar humerus fractures on pediatric elbow radiographs
model_description: Takes radiomics features extracted from manually delineated regions of interest on elbow radiographs as input and outputs a logistic-regression probability of supracondylar humerus fracture.
title: Automatic diagnosis of pediatric supracondylar humerus fractures using radiomics-based machine learning.
headline_result: AUC 0.65 (AP) and 0.72 (lateral) elbow radiographs

patient_population: 28 children with UPJO followed prospectively in the first year of life
clinical_problem: predicting clinically significant outcomes (worsening dilation, UTI, impaired renal function) in infants with ureteropelvic junction obstruction
model_description: Antenatal and postnatal renal ultrasound findings (UTD classification and anteroposterior pelvic diameter, both graded by a blinded pediatric radiologist) are compared using ROC-AUC and Random Forest analysis to predict which infants with UPJO will have a clinically significant event within the first year of life.
title: Predicting clinically significant events in children with ureteropelvic junction obstruction.
headline_result: antenatal APD >15 mm most predictive marker, AUC=0.867

patient_population: 531 preterm and full-term neonates from the Developing Human Connectome Project; validated on an additional cohort from the Gansu Provincial Maternity and Child-care Hospital, plus 47 preterm infants scanned at term-equivalent age
clinical_problem: estimating perinatal brain age / maturity from cortical morphology
model_description: A graph-attention-based network estimates an infant's brain age from cortical folding metrics (mean curvature, sulcal depth), explicitly modeling the relationship between brain hemispheres to capture structural lateralization during early development. It was tested on dHCP neonates and an independent external hospital cohort, and applied to preterm infants scanned at term-equivalent age to detect developmental delay.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: An Attention-Based Hemispheric Relation Inference Network for Perinatal Brain Age Prediction.
study_design: retrospective multi-center technical development and validation
dataset_size: 531 neonates (dHCP); external validation cohort (Gansu); 47 preterm infants at term-equivalent age
headline_result: Mean absolute error 0.53, R² 0.89 for perinatal brain age; predicted age significantly lower than chronological age in preterm infants at term-equivalent age, indicating delayed brain maturation

patient_population: adult brain MRI and fetal MRI time series (sample size not stated)
clinical_problem: correcting/tracking rigid head motion during brain MRI acquisition, including fetal MRI
model_description: Takes successive 3D brain MRI volumes as input (paired with a denoiser to remove noise) and outputs rigid-motion transforms tracking head movement during the scan, tested in adult and fetal MRI.
release_evidence: Our code is available at https://github.com/BBillot/EquiTrack
title: SE(3)-Equivariant and Noise-Invariant 3D Rigid Motion Tracking in Brain MRI.

patient_population: 419 patients (mean age 29 months) with neuroblastic tumors diagnosed 2002-2023 (PRIMAGE project)
clinical_problem: assessing the reproducibility of radiomic features extracted from T2-weighted MRI in children with neuroblastoma, to support their use as imaging biomarkers for personalized diagnosis and prognosis
model_description: Input: T2/T2*-weighted MRI of neuroblastoma tumors, automatically segmented; output: 107 shape, first-order and second-order radiomics features, whose reproducibility under different image-processing and segmentation-mask settings is quantified.
title: Reproducibility Analysis of Radiomic Features on T2-weighted MR Images after Processing and Segmentation Alterations in Neuroblastoma Tumors.
headline_result: without normalization, only 5% of features remained highly reproducible; mask modifications yielded 70% feature stability; shape features CCC>0.90

patient_population: 85 children with gliomas who underwent tumor resection
clinical_problem: Non-invasively predicting whether a pediatric brain glioma is high-grade or low-grade from multiparametric MRI to guide treatment planning
model_description: Radiomics features from multiparametric MRI (contrast T1, T2, FLAIR, DWI, ADC), combined with conventional MRI features and statistically significant clinical features, train AutoGluon automated-ML classifiers to grade pediatric gliomas as high- or low-grade
title: Predicting histological grade in pediatric glioma using multiparametric radiomics and conventional MRI features.
headline_result: Balanced classification accuracy 66.59%; test-set AUC 0.8071

patient_population: 55 typically developing fetuses (gestational weeks 27.4-38.7, mean 32.9)
clinical_problem: automatic cortical surface parcellation of the fetal brain to study neurodevelopmental trajectories
model_description: An attention-gated spherical U-Net takes fetal brain MRI-derived cortical surfaces as input and outputs automatic cortical parcellation, compared with surface-registration-based and prior spherical U-Net methods.
title: Automatic cortical surface parcellation in the fetal brain using attention-gated spherical U-net.
headline_result: Overall Dice coefficient 0.899 ± 0.020, outperforming SPHARM-net and the original spherical U-Net

model_family: Vision Transformer with Federated Self-Supervised Learning
patient_population: pediatric chest X-ray patients (exact cohort size not stated in abstract)
clinical_problem: binary COVID-19 versus non-COVID-19 classification on pediatric chest X-rays
model_description: CAFES pre-trains a Vision Transformer using federated self-supervised learning on adult chest X-ray data across a privacy-preserving federated computing platform, then fine-tunes it to classify pediatric chest X-rays as COVID-19 or non-COVID-19.
journal: Proceedings of SPIE--the International Society for Optical Engineering
title: CAFES: Chest X-ray Analysis using Federated Self-supervised Learning for Pediatric COVID-19 Detection.
headline_result: AUPR 0.952, 0.231 points higher than fully supervised model

patient_population: 136 normal singleton second- and third-trimester fetuses
clinical_problem: Assessing feasibility of automated fetal cardiac functional analysis (2D speckle-tracking echocardiography) for less experienced operators
model_description: FetalHQ, a semi-automated two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography tool, calculates fetal cardiac functional and morphometric parameters (strain, fractional shortening, sphericity index) from ultrasound; compared between beginner and expert operators.
release_evidence: FetalHQ (R), GE Healthcare
title: How automated techniques ease functional assessment of the fetal heart: Applicability of two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography for comprehensive analysis of global and segmental cardiac deformation using fetalHQ®.
headline_result: Excellent inter-operator agreement for morphometry (ED, SI), good agreement for function (endoGLS, FS); Bland-Altman bias -4.24pp/-3.21pp for endoGLS

model_family: hierarchical clustering analysis (unsupervised machine learning) on resting-state functional connectivity
patient_population: 76 infants (resting-state fMRI), 41 further assessed for word reading at school age; 7-year longitudinal cohort
clinical_problem: characterizing how infant brain language network connectivity relates to and predicts later phonological skills and school-age reading ability
model_description: Input: resting-state fMRI functional connectivity in infants; output: a modular infant language network identified via hierarchical clustering, whose inferior frontal module connectivity is used to predict kindergarten phonological skills and later word reading ability.
title: Longitudinal associations between language network characteristics in the infant brain and school-age reading abilities are mediated by early-developing phonological skills.
dataset_size: 76 infants (41 assessed on reading at school age)

model_family: machine learning texture-feature classifier; linear classifier
patient_population: pregnant women with suspected placenta accreta spectrum
clinical_problem: diagnosing placenta accreta spectrum (abnormal placental adherence) noninvasively before delivery using ultrasound
model_description: Machine learning classifiers use texture features extracted from placental ultrasound images to classify placenta accreta spectrum versus normal.
title: Diagnosis of placenta accreta spectrum using ultrasound texture feature fusion and machine learning.
headline_result: test accuracy 87% (linear classifier) and 92% (ML model); 5-fold cross-validation accuracy 88.7% and 83.0%

model_family: convolutional neural network regression (6D pose estimation)
patient_population: fetal brain ultrasound scans (transventricular standard plane acquisition)
clinical_problem: localization/pose estimation of 2D ultrasound planes in 3D fetal brain space, for training and guidance
model_description: Input is a 2D fetal brain ultrasound image; a CNN regression network predicts the six-dimensional pose (translation and rotation) of the imaging plane relative to a normalized fetal brain reference frame, evaluated for accuracy in localizing the transventricular standard plane used for fetal biometry, with data augmentation and larger training sets improving on prior work.
journal: IEEE transactions on medical robotics and bionics
title: Ultrasound Plane Pose Regression: Assessing Generalized Pose Coordinates in the Fetal Brain.
headline_result: Median errors of 2.97 mm (translation) and 6.63 degrees (rotation)

patient_population: 50 pediatric patients (median age 12 years) undergoing clinical brain MRI
clinical_problem: improving image quality of pediatric brain MRI (T2 FLAIR) using AI reconstruction, to reduce scan time and improve diagnostic confidence
model_description: Takes standard clinical T2-weighted FLAIR MRI acquisitions and applies an AI denoising reconstruction algorithm, outputting an image with improved signal-to-noise and contrast-to-noise ratio.
title: Evaluation of T2W FLAIR MR image quality using artificial intelligence image reconstruction techniques in the pediatric brain.
study_design: prospective reader study comparing AI vs standard MRI reconstruction
headline_result: AI reconstruction preferred in 98-99% of cases; gray matter aSNR 30.6 vs 18 (p<0.001)

patient_population: 263 infants diagnosed with NEC (94 surgical, 169 non-surgical), plus 40-case test group
clinical_problem: Can deep learning applied to bedside x-rays help decide whether an infant with necrotizing enterocolitis needs surgery, a decision that currently relies on clinical judgment alone?
model_description: CNN models (ResNet18, DenseNet121, SimpleViT) take bedside anteroposterior chest/abdominal x-rays of infants with NEC as input and predict whether the infant will require surgical intervention, with Grad-CAM used to visualize the image regions driving each prediction.
title: Enhancing surgical decision-making in NEC with ResNet18: a deep learning approach to predict the need for surgery through x-ray image analysis.
study_design: retrospective single-center model development and testing
headline_result: ResNet18 achieved 0.919 accuracy for predicting need for surgery

model_family: hierarchical clustering of resting-state fMRI functional connectivity
patient_population: 76 infants followed longitudinally to kindergarten (41 further assessed for emergent word reading)
clinical_problem: how infant brain language-network connectivity relates to later reading ability
model_description: Input is infant resting-state fMRI; hierarchical clustering is used to identify a modular language network, and functional connectivity of network modules is then related (via mediation models) to later kindergarten phonological skills and word-reading ability. This is a developmental-neuroscience application of unsupervised learning rather than a diagnostic imaging tool.
release_evidence: research/longitudinal cohort study, no software or model release stated
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
title: Longitudinal associations between language network characteristics in the infant brain and school-age reading abilities are mediated by early-developing phonological skills.
headline_result: Inferior frontal module connectivity prospectively correlated with kindergarten phonological skills and emergent word reading (mediation significant, exact stats not given as effect sizes in abstract)

patient_population: 171 UK children and young people (mean age 19, range 6-23 years) surveyed nationally
age_groups: child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: understanding children's and young people's attitudes toward the use of AI in their own medical imaging, including AI for detecting bone fractures on x-ray
model_description: A national UK survey study (not a specific model) of children's and young people's views on the use of AI in their own medical imaging, including AI for detecting bone fractures on x-ray, assessing attitudes toward AI accuracy, speed, and the need for human oversight.
title: "How I would like AI used for my imaging": children and young persons' perspectives.
study_design: national online survey of patient/public perspectives on AI in pediatric radiology
headline_result: 71.3% wanted to know an AI tool's accuracy; 66.1% said accuracy was more important than speed; 64.3% wanted human oversight; 42.7% felt AI would be more accurate than humans at finding bone x-ray problems

patient_population: 81 pediatric patients with peripheral neuroblastic tumors, undergoing contrast-enhanced CT and MRI
clinical_problem: assessing pediatric peripheral neuroblastic tumor cell behavior (pathological subtype and histology group) noninvasively
model_description: Radiomics features are extracted from contrast-enhanced CT and from T1WI/T2WI MRI of segmented neuroblastic tumors, and separate radiomics models compare the ability of CT versus MRI features to distinguish pathological subtype (neuroblastoma vs ganglioneuroblastoma/ganglioneuroma) and INPC histology group.
title: A head-to-head comparison of computed tomography- and magnetic resonance imaging-based radiomics in assessing pediatric peripheral neuroblastic tumor cell behavior.
headline_result: CECT radiomics AUC 0.765-0.870 (subtype) vs MRI radiomics AUC 0.549-0.748

patient_population: 38 children with congenital muscular torticollis
clinical_problem: diagnosing and grading severity of congenital muscular torticollis using MRI texture features
model_description: input T2-weighted muscle texture features (radiomics) from MRI; output a logistic-regression diagnostic model correlated with fatty infiltration and fibrosis on pathology
journal: Journal of orthopaedic surgery and research
title: Muscle texture features on preoperative MRI for diagnosis and assessment of severity of congenital muscular torticollis.
headline_result: AUC 0.828, sensitivity 0.684, specificity 0.868

patient_population: 140 patients aged ≤18 years with brainstem glioma (training n=109, test n=31)
clinical_problem: predicting radiotherapy response in pediatric diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma from MRI
model_description: Quantitative T2 signal intensity metrics, a qualitative heterogeneity grading system, and MRI radiomic features (T2-weighted and T1-enhanced) are combined via multivariate logistic regression to predict partial response to radiotherapy in DIPG.
title: Pediatric diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma radiotherapy response prediction: MRI morphology and T2 intensity-based quantitative analyses.
study_design: retrospective model-development study with training/test split
headline_result: Best predictive model AUC 0.89 (training set), 0.91 (test set)

patient_population: 374 annotated wrist radiographs (345 normal, 29 pathological) from skeletally mature adolescents and adults aged >=16
clinical_problem: Automated detection of perilunate dislocation on anteroposterior wrist radiographs in skeletally mature adolescents and adults.
model_description: Two YOLOv8 deep learning models, one for carpal region detection and one for segmentation between Gilula's arcs, take anteroposterior wrist radiographs as input and classify the wrist as normal or showing perilunate dislocation via ensemble averaging.
title: A deep learning-based algorithm for automatic detection of perilunate dislocation in frontal wrist radiographs.
headline_result: F1-score 0.880 overall (0.928 normal, 0.833 pathological)

patient_population: 270 newborns
clinical_problem: Predicting the presence and severity of pulmonary hypertension in newborns from echocardiography
model_description: A multi-view, spatio-temporal convolutional deep learning model analyzes echocardiogram videos from multiple views (aggregated by majority voting) to classify the presence and severity of pulmonary hypertension, with saliency maps for interpretability.
title: Deep Learning Based Prediction of Pulmonary Hypertension in Newborns Using Echocardiograms.
study_design: retrospective model development study with held-out test set
headline_result: F1 0.84 (severity)/0.92 (binary) on 10-fold cross-validation; 0.63/0.78 on held-out test set

model_family: transformer-based (Swin-UNETR) and UNETR neural network models
patient_population: internal dataset 172 fetuses (519 images, 2018-2022); external dataset 131 fetuses (561 images)
clinical_problem: optimizing automated fetal brain extraction/segmentation from resting-state functional MRI for prenatal neuroimaging research
model_description: Input: fetal resting-state fMRI images; output: automated fetal brain extraction/segmentation mask, produced by transformer-based models (Swin-UNETR, UNETR) compared against convolutional-network reference-standard models across gestational ages and scanner types.
title: Optimizing Performance of Transformer-based Models for Fetal Brain MR Image Segmentation.
study_design: retrospective model development and internal/external cross-validation
dataset_size: internal: 172 fetuses/519 images; external: 131 fetuses/561 images
headline_result: Swin-UNETR mean Dice 0.92, BAHD 0.097; comparable performance to reference models in late-fetal period (>25 weeks), lower in midfetal period (≤25 weeks)

patient_population: 317 neonates with or without risk of cerebral hypoxia-ischemia
clinical_problem: quantification of cerebral venous circulation to assess hypoxic-ischemic risk in neonates
model_description: Input is susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) MRI of the neonatal brain; a deep learning segmentation algorithm automatically detects and quantifies deep medullary veins (number, width, curvature), which are then compared across sex, prematurity, hypoxic-ischemia risk group, and hemorrhage status.
title: Evaluation of Neonatal Cerebral Circulation Under Hypoxic Ischemic Risk Factors Based on Quantitative Analysis of Cerebral Veins with Magnetic Resonance Susceptibility Weighted Imaging.
headline_result: Significant differences in DMV number/width/curvature by sex, prematurity, risk group and hemorrhage status (e.g., width greater in low- vs high-risk group, p<0.01)

patient_population: 2974 pediatric patients
clinical_problem: estimating bone age from hand radiographs
model_description: Takes hand radiographs plus patient sex and chronological age as input and outputs a continuous predicted bone age, combining a CNN image branch with a small clinical-data neural network.
title: Assessment of Bone Age Based on Hand Radiographs Using Regression-Based Multi-Modal Deep Learning.
headline_result: MAE 0.410 years, accuracy 91.1%

patient_population: 564 patients across 6 studies, including 170 (30%) pediatric patients
clinical_problem: AI detection and quantification of injured liver area after trauma, sepsis, or chemotherapy
model_description: Review of six studies applying AI/radiomics to CT (five studies) and FAST ultrasound (one study) to detect and quantify acute liver injury from trauma, sepsis, or chemotherapy, in cohorts combining adult and pediatric patients; most studies reported specificity over 80%.
title: Future Perspectives on Radiomics in Acute Liver Injury and Liver Trauma.
headline_result: 3 of 6 studies reported specificity >80%

patient_population: children with central nervous system tumors, across 63 reviewed articles published 2008-2024
clinical_problem: characterizing, grading and prognosticating childhood central nervous system tumors from imaging
model_description: A review of radiomics and AI in pediatric brain tumors, arguing for quantitative imaging parameters that predict the nature and likely evolution of a lesion rather than relying on what a reader can see. Covers both morphological and functional MRI as feature sources.
title: Radiomics and artificial intelligence applications in pediatric brain tumors.

patient_population: 419 cervical lymph nodes from 146 pediatric patients
clinical_problem: Differentiating benign from malignant, and among four etiologies of, cervical lymphadenopathy in children using MRI radiomics
model_description: Radiomic features (1,218 per lymph node) extracted from T2-weighted MRI, reduced via LASSO, feed support vector machine classifiers to distinguish benign from malignant cervical lymph nodes and to differentiate among four common etiologies (Kikuchi disease, reactive hyperplasia, suppurative lymphadenitis, malignancy).
title: Using T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging-derived radiomics to classify cervical lymphadenopathy in children.
dataset_size: 419 lymph nodes from 146 patients (7:3 train/test split)
headline_result: Benign vs malignant AUC 0.89 (train), 0.80 (test); four-etiology model AUC 0.87-0.97 (train), 0.80-0.96 (test)

patient_population: 4,233 singleton normal fetuses scanned at 11-13+6 weeks gestation
clinical_problem: establishing reference ranges and automating measurement of fetal intracranial markers during the first trimester on ultrasound
model_description: Input: 2D first-trimester ultrasound images of the fetal head; output: automated measurement of 10 key fetal intracranial markers across three standard head planes, compared to manual measurement for accuracy, consistency and speed.
journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
title: A novel artificial intelligence model for measuring fetal intracranial markers during the first trimester based on two-dimensional ultrasound image.
study_design: retrospective model development and validation against manual measurement
headline_result: ICC>0.75, r>0.75 (AI vs manual); average absolute error 0.124-0.178 mm; AI 100% detection rate for abnormal cases; measurement time 0.49s (65x faster than manual)

model_family: autoencoder with reconstruction regularization (vs. MLP and classical ML)
patient_population: 11,534 adolescents aged 9-10 from the ABCD Data Release 3.0
clinical_problem: prediction of fluid intelligence from structural brain MRI in early adolescence
model_description: Input is 604 FreeSurfer-derived structural features from T1-weighted MRI across 148 regions of interest; an autoencoder model with reconstruction regularization outputs a predicted fluid intelligence score, benchmarked against MLP and classical machine learning models, with SHAP used to rank feature importance.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Prediction of Adolescents' Fluid Intelligence Scores based on Deep Learning with Reconstruction Regularization.
study_design: retrospective secondary analysis of ABCD cohort
headline_result: Best model achieved Pearson correlation 0.209 +/- 0.02 and MSE 105.212 +/- 2.53 for predicting fluid intelligence; performance better in female than male adolescents

clinical_problem: whether AI can detect hard-to-identify fetal cardiac anomalies on obstetric ultrasound
model_description: Editorial/comment discussing whether artificial intelligence can detect difficult-to-identify fetal cardiac anomalies on obstetric ultrasound; abstract text not provided, so specific findings are unknown.
journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
title: The Holy Grail of obstetric ultrasound: can artificial intelligence detect hard-to-identify fetal cardiac anomalies?

patient_population: 494 anteroposterior neonatal abdominal radiographs, 214 with necrotizing enterocolitis
clinical_problem: recognizing pneumatosis intestinalis on a neonatal abdominal radiograph, the radiographic call that decides whether necrotizing enterocolitis is diagnosed
model_description: Trained to recognize pneumatosis on neonatal abdominal radiographs and compared directly against senior surgical residents, who are often the ones making this call overnight. It matched every resident individually, and the attention maps confirmed it was looking at the right part of the film. Necrotizing enterocolitis is a diagnosis where hours matter and the radiographic sign is subtle, which is what makes this comparison the relevant one.
title: Artificial Intelligence vs. Doctors: Diagnosing Necrotizing Enterocolitis on Abdominal Radiographs.
study_design: retrospective cohort study with reader comparison
headline_result: AUROC 0.918 and accuracy 87.8%, statistically indistinguishable from each senior surgical resident (median resident AUROC 0.896)

patient_population: 14 children (CT scans) for training/evaluation
clinical_problem: Automating 3D segmentation of Wilms' tumor and affected kidney on CT to enable routine 3D reconstruction without the time cost of manual segmentation
model_description: A CNN U-Net, including a version trained with the 'OV2ASSION' partial-manual-segmentation method, automatically segments Wilms' tumor and neoplastic kidney on pediatric CT scans
journal: Cancer imaging : the official publication of the International Cancer Imaging Society
title: Automation of Wilms' tumor segmentation by artificial intelligence.
headline_result: Fully automatic U-Net Dice 0.69 (tumor)/0.27 (kidney); OV2ASSION method Dice up to 0.97 (tumor)/0.94 (kidney) with partial manual input, cutting expert time by 80%

model_family: deep learning-based attenuation and scatter correction (DL-ASC)
patient_population: 35 sedated pediatric patients under four years old (training), plus 5 non-sedated pediatric patients (validation)
clinical_problem: Enabling sedation-free pediatric PET imaging by using ultra-fast total-body PET scanning with AI-based image correction instead of longer sedated scans
model_description: A deep-learning-based attenuation and scatter correction (DL-ASC) method is applied to ultra-fast (15-second) total-body PET acquisitions in young children, aiming to match standard 300-second sedated-scan image quality without sedation
journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
title: Sedation-free pediatric [18F]FDG imaging on totalbody PET/CT with the assistance of artificial intelligence.
headline_result: No significant differences in qualitative scoring, lesion detectability or SUV between ultra-fast DL-ASC and standard imaging (P=ns)

patient_population: 170 pediatric patients, 510 X-ray images, admitted 2005-2022
clinical_problem: Using a deep learning decision-support algorithm to identify pediatric pneumothorax or pleural effusion on chest X-rays and determine whether tube thoracostomy is warranted.
model_description: XRAInet, a deep learning algorithm, takes pediatric chest radiographs as input and localizes regions of pneumothorax/pleural effusion, classifying whether tube thoracostomy intervention is warranted versus conservative management.
title: XRAInet: AI-based decision support for pneumothorax and pleural effusion management.
headline_result: mAP 0.918; independent test set sensitivity 64.00%, specificity 96.15%

model_family: AI image reconstruction (vendor algorithm, architecture unspecified)
patient_population: 50 pediatric patients (mean age 11.8±3.1 years) undergoing clinical brain MRI
clinical_problem: Improving image quality and reducing scan time for pediatric brain MRI using AI-based image reconstruction at higher acceleration factors.
model_description: An AI reconstruction algorithm processes accelerated (higher compressed-SENSE factor) 3D T1-weighted SPGR brain MRI acquisitions and reconstructs images with improved signal-to-noise and contrast-to-noise ratios compared to standard reconstruction.
title: Evaluation of 3D T1-weighted spoiled gradient echo MR image quality using artificial intelligence image reconstruction techniques in the pediatric brain.
headline_result: AI improved image quality in 94-100% of evaluations at CS=5/8; significantly higher aSNR/aCNR (p<0.001)

patient_population: children with low-grade glioma
clinical_problem: how machine learning can assist grading, typing, segmenting, and predicting genetic status of pediatric low-grade gliomas from MRI
model_description: review of published machine-learning approaches for imaging-based evaluation of pediatric low-grade gliomas, including tumor grading, typing, segmentation, and genetic-status prediction
journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
title: Applications of machine learning to MR imaging of pediatric low-grade gliomas.

patient_population: 58 adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients undergoing posterior spinal fusion (36 surgeon-contoured, 22 pre-contoured rods)
clinical_problem: predicting postoperative sagittal spinal alignment to help plan pre-contoured rods for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis surgery
model_description: Uses a proprietary AI algorithm to predict postoperative sagittal spinal alignment parameters (thoracic kyphosis, PI-LL mismatch, T1 pelvic angle) from preoperative radiographic measurements, compared against actual postoperative radiographs.
title: Pre-contoured patient-specific rods result in superior immediate sagittal plane alignment than surgeon contoured rods in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
headline_result: 95.5% of pre-contoured rod patients met TK goal vs 61.1% surgeon-contoured (P=0.004)

patient_population: 715 pediatric patients with glioma (3,994 scans) from four clinical settings
clinical_problem: predicting future tumor recurrence in pediatric glioma from surveillance brain MRI
model_description: Takes a patient's current and prior longitudinal brain MRI scans as input and outputs a prediction of future tumor recurrence, using a self-supervised spatiotemporal deep learning model (temporal learning).
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
title: Longitudinal risk prediction for pediatric glioma with temporal deep learning.
study_design: retrospective multicenter deep learning model development (preprint)
headline_result: Recurrence prediction performance improved by up to 41% vs traditional approaches

body_region: multiple (neuroradiology, gastrointestinal, genitourinary, musculoskeletal, chest, cardiovascular, breast, multisystem, and pediatric radiology cases)
patient_population: 190 'Diagnosis Please' teaching cases published in Radiology (Jan 2008-Oct 2023), including 12 cases in the pediatric radiology subspecialty
clinical_problem: generate differential diagnoses directly from radiologic images and brief clinical history, compared with subspecialty radiologists, across radiology subspecialties including a pediatric radiology case subset
model_description: GPT-4V and Gemini Pro Vision were given case images plus patient history text (without stated imaging findings) and asked to output three differential diagnoses, repeated at three temperature settings, then compared against diagnoses reached by eight subspecialty-trained radiologists reading the same cases.
release_evidence: GPT-4V and Gemini Pro Vision are named commercial multimodal LLM products (OpenAI, Google)
title: Comparing Diagnostic Accuracy of Radiologists versus GPT-4V and Gemini Pro Vision Using Image Inputs from Diagnosis Please Cases.
study_design: retrospective comparative diagnostic-accuracy study of LLMs vs. radiologists on published teaching cases
dataset_size: 190 cases total, including 12 pediatric radiology cases (no pediatric-specific results reported separately)
headline_result: Overall accuracy: radiologists 61% (115/190) vs. GPT-4V 49% and Gemini Pro Vision 39% at temperature 1; radiologists significantly outperformed Gemini Pro Vision (P<.001) but not significantly different from GPT-4V after correction (P=.02)

patient_population: 414 term neonates from the HEAL trial across 17 institutions
clinical_problem: Predicting 2-year neurodevelopmental outcome (death or impairment) in neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy using multisequence brain MRI and basic clinical variables.
model_description: A deep learning classifier takes T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and diffusion tensor MRI plus sex and gestational age as input to predict death or neurodevelopmental impairment at 2 years.
title: Artificial Intelligence Outcome Prediction in Neonates with Encephalopathy (AI-OPiNE).
study_design: retrospective secondary analysis of multicenter randomized trial data (HEAL trial), with in- and out-of-distribution testing
headline_result: AUC 0.74 in-distribution, 0.77 out-of-distribution; accuracy 63%/78%

patient_population: 184 children from a national brain tumor consortium (median age 7) and 100 from a pediatric cancer center (median age 8), with an independent external test set
clinical_problem: segmenting pediatric brain tumors for volumetric response assessment, when there is not enough pediatric data to train on directly
model_description: The methodological point is training in steps within the domain rather than transferring once from natural images, which is what makes expert-level accuracy reachable on a few hundred pediatric scans. The evaluation is unusually strong: three clinicians rated segmentations blind, and rated the model's higher than each other's, correctly identifying which were machine-made only a quarter of the time.
title: Stepwise Transfer Learning for Expert-level Pediatric Brain Tumor MRI Segmentation in a Limited Data Scenario.
study_design: retrospective multi-cohort study with blinded clinician evaluation
dataset_size: 284 children for development, plus an independent external test set
headline_result: median Dice 0.88 in development and 0.82 on external testing; clinicians rated AI segmentations at median Likert 9 versus 7 for other experts, and judged 80.2% clinically acceptable versus 65.4%

patient_population: fetal ultrasound datasets (NA-4CH private + public FEST dataset)
clinical_problem: classifying fetal four-chamber heart ultrasound images as normal or abnormal to screen for congenital heart disease
model_description: Takes fetal four-chamber-view ultrasound images as input, using semantic-level anatomical knowledge guided by a small number of annotation masks, and outputs a classification of normal versus abnormal heart.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: SKGC: A General Semantic-Level Knowledge Guided Classification Framework for Fetal Congenital Heart Disease.
headline_result: Accuracy 99.68% (NA-4CH) and 95.40% (FEST); improved from 74.68% to 88.14% with only 10 labeled masks

patient_population: 8,735 participants in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study
clinical_problem: predicting neurocognitive measures (general cognitive ability, executive function, learning/memory) from diffusion MRI tractography in children
model_description: TractoSCR, a supervised contrastive regression deep-learning framework, takes white-matter microstructural measures from diffusion MRI fiber-cluster tractography as input and predicts continuous neurocognitive scores, with permutation feature importance identifying predictive fiber clusters.
release_evidence: code available at https://github.com/SlicerDMRI/TractoSCR
title: TractoSCR: a novel supervised contrastive regression framework for prediction of neurocognitive measures using multi-site harmonized diffusion MRI tractography.
study_design: retrospective method-development study using a large multi-site cohort
headline_result: Significantly higher accuracy of neurocognitive score prediction than other state-of-the-art methods (no single number given)

patient_population: 72 patients younger than 18 (12 for suture patency evaluation, 60 for head trauma evaluation)
clinical_problem: Detecting skull fractures and evaluating cranial suture patency without ionizing radiation, using deep-learning pseudo-CT generated from MRI in children
model_description: Automated motion correction is applied to MR imaging, followed by a deep-learning method that generates pseudo-CT images of the pediatric skull from MRI, evaluated for skull fracture detection and cranial suture patency assessment against ground-truth CT.
title: MR Cranial Bone Imaging: Evaluation of Both Motion-Corrected and Automated Deep Learning Pseudo-CT Estimated MR Images.
dataset_size: 72 patients (12 for suture patency, 60 for head trauma)
headline_result: Suture patency: 100% sensitivity/specificity; skull fracture detection: 100% specificity, 90% sensitivity

patient_population: pregnant patients undergoing prenatal fetal membrane imaging
clinical_problem: imaging assessment of fetal membrane abnormalities and their relation to adverse perinatal outcomes
model_description: Review of imaging methods (ultrasound and other modalities) for assessing fetal membrane abnormalities such as thickening and separation, and their relation to adverse perinatal outcomes, with discussion of the future role of artificial intelligence in fetal membrane imaging.
title: Fetal membrane imaging: current and future perspectives-a review.

patient_population: Human Connectome Project (n=1023, young adults) and Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study (n=936, children) twin cohorts
clinical_problem: determining whether patterns of subcortical functional brain connectivity are heritable, using machine learning to discriminate twin pairs
model_description: Uses a machine learning framework applied to subcortico-cortical functional connectivity gradients derived from resting-state fMRI to classify whether twin pairs are monozygotic or dizygotic.
title: Heritability of functional gradients in the human subcortico-cortical connectivity.
headline_result: Classification accuracy 76.2% (P<0.001) distinguishing MZ vs DZ twin pairs

patient_population: premature infants receiving omega-3 supplementation
clinical_problem: rapid identification and grading of hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy severity in newborns via cranial ultrasound
model_description: input cranial ultrasound region-of-interest density measurements (choroid plexus and brain parenchyma); output a 3-class CNN classification of HIE severity (Normal/Moderate/Intensive)
title: Neurosonographic Classification in Premature Infants Receiving Omega-3 Supplementation Using Convolutional Neural Networks.
headline_result: overall accuracy 88.56%, F-measure 88.40%

model_family: AI-derived automated CT lung-lesion quantification combined with clinical logistic regression
patient_population: 126 children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (training, 85 refractory); 54 children (prospective validation, 37 refractory), Children's Hospital of Nanjing Medical University
clinical_problem: early prediction of refractory Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia in children using AI-quantified lung lesion extent on CT plus clinical indicators
model_description: Input: AI-automated quantification of lung lesion volume and CT attenuation (combined into a constant, Log2Phi) plus clinical variables (fever duration, AST, macrolide therapy duration); output: predicted risk of refractory Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia.
title: Model based on the automated AI-driven CT quantification is effective for the diagnosis of refractory Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia.
study_design: retrospective model development with prospective validation cohort
headline_result: Clinical-imaging model AUC 0.897 (training), 0.895 (test)

patient_population: 503 CMR studies from Fontan patients (median age 15y) and 42 age-matched controls, single center, 2005-2011
clinical_problem: Using unsupervised machine learning clustering of CMR-derived ventricular dyssynchrony metrics to identify high-risk phenotypes among patients with Fontan circulation for single-ventricle congenital heart disease.
model_description: Unsupervised K-means clustering machine learning applied to 24 CMR-derived mechanical dyssynchrony metrics (from feature-tracking strain analysis) classifies Fontan patients into distinct phenotypic risk clusters associated with death or heart transplantation.
journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
title: Identifying high-risk Fontan phenotypes using K-means clustering of cardiac magnetic resonance-based dyssynchrony metrics.
study_design: retrospective single-center cohort study with unsupervised machine learning
headline_result: Highest-risk cluster HR 6.4 (95% CI 2.1-19.3) for composite outcome vs lowest-risk cluster

patient_population: 150 adult and 80 fetal brain MRIs (retrospective)
clinical_problem: achieving accurate, efficient fetal brain MRI segmentation based on true physical scan resolution rather than upsampled apparent resolution
model_description: ConvNet segmentation models are evaluated on brain MRI downsampled to its true acquisition (physical) resolution rather than the higher apparent resolution used clinically; for fetal brain MRI, images were downsampled per estimated physical resolution before segmentation and restored via upsampling, showing negligible accuracy loss with much smaller, faster models.
title: Efficient segmentation of fetal brain MRI based on the physical resolution.
headline_result: accuracy reduced by only 0.26-1.8% with downsampling factors of 4/3 to 4; models up to 7x smaller and 10x faster

model_family: twelve machine learning algorithms compared (best: random forest)
patient_population: 32 patients with severe AIS and 31 healthy individuals
clinical_problem: using brain volumetric measurements to predict adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
model_description: Volumetric measurements from 169 brain regions on MRI are used as predictors in twelve machine learning algorithms (random forest performing best) to classify adolescent idiopathic scoliosis versus healthy controls, identifying corticospinal tract and cerebellar volumes as most important.
title: Prediction of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis with machine learning algorithms using brain volumetric measurements.
headline_result: random forest accuracy 0.9083, AUC 0.993, F1 0.970

patient_population: Pediatric radiology literature 2015-2023
clinical_problem: How emerging imaging technologies, including AI/ML, can address the unique challenges of imaging children compared with adults
model_description: Review of emerging pediatric radiology technologies (advanced ultrasound, CT, MRI, nuclear imaging, teleradiology, AI/machine learning, 3D printing, radiomics/radiogenomics) and their roles in addressing pediatric-specific imaging challenges
title: Emerging technologies in pediatric radiology: current developments and future prospects.

patient_population: 29 consecutive patients (mean age 11±5, range 1-17 years) undergoing cardiac MRI
clinical_problem: shortening pediatric cardiac MRI acquisition time for ventricular volumetry
model_description: A deep-learning-accelerated 3-heartbeat cine MRI reconstruction is compared with standard segmented 2D cine bSSFP for biventricular volumetric assessment, evaluated by two readers.
title: Accelerated cardiac magnetic resonance imaging using deep learning for volumetric assessment in children.
headline_result: Scan time reduced from 218.3±44.8 s to 45.5±13.8 s (P<0.001); volumetrics not significantly different except LV mass; ICC >0.9 for most measures

model_family: deep learning (knowledge distillation + contrastive regularization, scribble-supervised segmentation)
patient_population: not stated (fetal MRI dataset used as one of two benchmarks, alongside an adult cardiac MRI dataset)
clinical_problem: Reducing annotation cost for placenta and fetal brain segmentation on fetal MRI using scribble (weak) annotations instead of full pixel-level labels
model_description: ScribSD+ is a scribble-supervised segmentation framework (multi-scale knowledge distillation plus class-wise contrastive regularization) that learns to segment the placenta and fetal brain on fetal MRI (and cardiac structures on adult cardiac MRI) from scribble annotations instead of full pixel-level labels.
journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
title: ScribSD+: Scribble-supervised medical image segmentation based on simultaneous multi-scale knowledge distillation and class-wise contrastive regularization.
study_design: Retrospective methods development and benchmarking study
headline_result: Outperformed five state-of-the-art scribble-supervised segmentation methods (fetal-MRI-specific Dice not given in abstract)

patient_population: pregnant women from the GARBH-Ini (North India) and CMC Vellore (South India) cohorts
clinical_problem: estimating gestational age in the second and third trimesters more accurately than the Hadlock formula in an Indian population
model_description: input three routinely measured second/third-trimester ultrasound biometric parameters; output an estimated gestational age via a genetic-algorithm-optimized polynomial regression model
journal: The Lancet regional health. Southeast Asia
title: Development and external validation of Indian population-specific Garbhini-GA2 model for estimating gestational age in second and third trimesters.
study_design: prospective cohort study with model development and external validation
dataset_size: TEST set n=1,493 (GARBH-Ini); independent VALIDATION set n=948 (CMC Vellore)
headline_result: median gestational-age estimation error reduced more than three-fold vs. the Hadlock formula

model_family: deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR) + MAR algorithm
patient_population: 77 children (3-15 years), 116 pedicle screws evaluated
clinical_problem: Reducing metal-induced beam-hardening artifacts from pedicle screws on post-surgical pediatric low-radiation-dose spine CT, using metal artifact reduction combined with deep learning image reconstruction.
model_description: Deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR) combined with a metal artifact reduction (MAR) algorithm processes low-dose post-surgical pediatric spine CT raw data to reduce beam-hardening artifacts around pedicle screws and improve image quality, compared to iterative reconstruction (ASIR-V).
journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
title: Application of metal artifact reduction algorithm in reducing metal artifacts in post-surgery pediatric low radiation dose spine computed tomography (CT) images.
headline_result: DL-MAR reduced artifact length by 57.4% and artifact index by 65.0% vs standard reconstruction

model_family: DenseNet-121 and EfficientNet-v2-M convolutional neural networks
patient_population: 1,343 infants under 12 months (4,933 skull radiographs)
clinical_problem: postnatal age estimation of infants from skull radiographs
model_description: Input is an anteroposterior or lateral plain skull radiograph of an infant under 12 months; the CNN models output a predicted postnatal age, with gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) used to highlight the cranial sutures and structures driving the prediction.
title: Estimating infant age from skull X-ray images using deep learning.
headline_result: DenseNet-121 corrected accuracy (within +/-1 month) 79.4% (AP) / 84.2% (lateral); EfficientNet-v2-M 79.1% (AP) / 87.3% (lateral)

model_family: deep learning segmentation + machine learning (radiomics feature selection)
patient_population: 69 pediatric DMG patients from 2 centers (53 internal, 16 external cohort)
clinical_problem: Predicting 12-month overall survival in pediatric diffuse midline glioma from diagnostic and post-radiotherapy MRI radiomic features
model_description: Input: multisequence MRI (T1, T1ce, T2, T2 FLAIR) at diagnosis and post-radiotherapy; output: automatic tumor subregion segmentation (deep learning fine-tuned from adult BraTS data) and radiomics-based prediction of 12-month survival
title: Early prognostication of overall survival for pediatric diffuse midline gliomas using MRI radiomics and machine learning: A two-center study.
study_design: retrospective two-center model development with external validation
headline_result: 12-month survival prediction accuracy 77-85% internal, 78-81% external

model_family: YOLOv5 with efficient channel attention (CNN object detector)
patient_population: 632 pregnant women in mid-pregnancy
clinical_problem: Objectively and quickly detecting and classifying fetal cleft lip on prenatal ultrasound
model_description: A modified YOLOv5 model with an efficient channel attention module (Yolov5-ECA) detects the fetal lip region on ultrasound images and classifies it as normal or abnormal (cleft lip)
title: Deep learning based detection and classification of fetal lip in ultrasound images.
headline_result: Detection mAP@0.5 0.920, mAP@0.5:0.95 0.630; classification accuracy 0.925

patient_population: fetal diffusion MRI scans
clinical_problem: improving the accuracy of white matter tract reconstruction (tractography) in the fetal brain from diffusion MRI
model_description: A deep learning model automatically segments fetal brain tissue directly in diffusion MRI space, constraining tractography algorithms to produce more anatomically accurate white matter tract reconstructions.
title: Anatomically constrained tractography of the fetal brain.

model_family: AI-based Greulich & Pyle bone-age software (architecture/vendor not stated)
patient_population: 1,653 children and adolescents aged 3-17 years with hand radiographs after trauma
clinical_problem: whether historical bone-age reference curves still apply to a contemporary Central European pediatric population
model_description: input hand radiographs; output an AI-derived Greulich & Pyle bone age compared with chronological age to build an updated population reference curve
title: Acceleration of skeletal maturation in Central Europe over the last two decades: insights from two cohorts of healthy children.
headline_result: mean absolute error between bone age and chronological age 0.92 years (girls), 0.97 years (boys); significantly different from the historical Rotterdam cohort curve, P<0.001

patient_population: 263 subjects from the National Database for Autism Research, Baby Connectome Project, and cross-site datasets, 6-month-old infants
clinical_problem: infant brain region parcellation to study early brain development
model_description: A two-stage global-to-local pipeline first localizes brain regions of interest using combined transformer/convolution features, then refines boundaries for accurate parcellation of 6-month-old infant brain MRIs.
title: An end-to-end infant brain parcellation pipeline.
study_design: retrospective method-development study using public multi-site infant datasets
headline_result: better Dice-ratio accuracy and robustness than competing methods

patient_population: pediatric scoliosis patients; 7777 AP and 5621 lateral spine radiographs
clinical_problem: automatically classifying pediatric scoliosis spine radiographs (pre-/post-operative, AP/lateral) for large imaging registries
model_description: Takes AP and lateral spine radiographs as input and outputs a classification into one of ten pre-/post-operative categories, using an EfficientNet B6 convolutional neural network, for automated registry data ingestion.
title: Deep learning classification of pediatric spinal radiographs for use in large scale imaging registries.
study_design: retrospective model development and internal validation
headline_result: Test accuracy 1.00 (AP), 1.00 (lateral); precision 0.91-1.00

patient_population: fetal Doppler ultrasound signals from non-stress tests and labor monitoring
clinical_problem: classifying Doppler ultrasound signal type to improve fetal heart rate tracing during monitoring
model_description: A semi-supervised CNN is trained on labeled and unlabeled Doppler ultrasound signal segments (fetal heartbeat, artifact, and two other categories) from cardiotocography monitoring, aiming to classify signal type and improve continuous fetal heart rate tracing beyond the standard autocorrelation algorithm.
title: Extracting fetal heart signals from Doppler using semi-supervised convolutional neural networks.
headline_result: average classification accuracy 80.9%

patient_population: 41 children (20 severe asthma, mean age 10.4y; 21 controls, mean age 11.4y)
clinical_problem: identifying structural airway changes on chest high-resolution CT that distinguish severe asthma from controls in children
model_description: Machine learning models (classification trees, random forests) analyze quantitative chest high-resolution CT airway features (bronchial wall thickness, bronchiectasis scores) to distinguish children with severe asthma from non-asthmatic controls.
title: Machine learning-enhanced HRCT analysis for diagnosis and severity assessment in pediatric asthma.
headline_result: airway wall thickness percentage >=38.6% cutoff gave 95% sensitivity, specificity, and overall accuracy

patient_population: youth and adults aged 7-30 undergoing task-based fMRI during nonsymbolic magnitude processing
age_groups: child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: estimating brain age and its relationship to mathematical performance
model_description: Task-based fMRI connectivity features from the frontoparietal and salience networks during a magnitude-processing task are fed into a Gradient Boosting model to predict chronological (brain) age across ages 7-30. A more mature predicted brain age was associated with better arithmetic performance.
title: Frontoparietal and salience network synchronizations during nonsymbolic magnitude processing predict brain age and mathematical performance in youth.
dataset_size: ages 7-30, independent training and test datasets (N not given)
headline_result: Brain age prediction correlation r=.727, mean absolute error 2.944 years

model_family: DeepLabv3+ (EfficientNet-B0 encoder) segmentation and ConvNeXt-B classification
patient_population: 1,681 supine abdominal radiographs, ages 9-18, from three medical institutions
clinical_problem: automatically grading skeletal maturity (Risser stage) from abdominal radiographs for scoliosis management
model_description: input supine abdominal radiographs; output automatic pelvic-bone segmentation (DeepLabv3+) followed by Risser-stage classification (ConvNeXt-B)
title: Deep learning-based fully automatic Risser stage assessment model using abdominal radiographs.
study_design: retrospective multicenter study with external validation
headline_result: accuracy 0.87/0.75 and AUROC 0.99/0.95 on internal/external test sets

patient_population: adult and pediatric patients with muscular dystrophies undergoing bilateral thigh MRI (23 patients)
clinical_problem: segmentation of thigh muscle and subcutaneous fat in muscular dystrophy for quantitative follow-up
model_description: Input is a T1-weighted out-of-phase thigh MRI; U-Net models automatically segment subcutaneous adipose tissue and either the thigh muscles as a whole (U-Net1) or the three muscular compartments separately (U-Net3), compared against manual radiologist segmentation.
journal: Journal of functional morphology and kinesiology
title: Convolutional Neural Network-Based Automated Segmentation of Skeletal Muscle and Subcutaneous Adipose Tissue on Thigh MRI in Muscular Dystrophy Patients.
headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient: U-Net1 96.8/95.3/95.6% (train/validation/test) for SAT; U-Net3 accuracy 94.1/92.9/93.9%; median DSC 0.95 for SAT segmentation

model_family: convolutional neural network (pneumonia classification), trained on adult data
patient_population: 5,856 pediatric chest X-rays (ages 1-5) for evaluation; 46,947 adult chest X-rays for training
clinical_problem: whether adult-trained CNNs can classify pneumonia on pediatric chest radiographs despite limited pediatric training data
model_description: A pneumonia-classification CNN is trained exclusively on 46,947 curated adult chest X-rays, with thoracic segmentation preprocessing to reduce attention outside the thorax, and then evaluated for its ability to discriminate pneumonia on a separate pediatric chest X-ray dataset without pediatric-specific retraining.
title: CNNs trained with adult data are useful in pediatrics. A pneumonia classification example.
headline_result: pneumonia discrimination AUC 0.95 on adult test set, AUC 0.82 on pediatric dataset

model_family: random forest ensemble of image quality metrics
patient_population: >1600 manually rated fetal brain T2-weighted images from four clinical centers, 13 scanners
clinical_problem: automated image quality assessment/control for fetal brain MRI across multiple clinical centers and scanners
model_description: Input: unprocessed anatomical fetal brain MRI; output: predicted expert-style quality rating, from an ensemble of extracted quality metrics via random forest.
release_evidence: open-source machine-learning framework for automated image quality assessment and quality control
title: FetMRQC: A robust quality control system for multi-centric fetal brain MRI.
dataset_size: >1600 manually rated fetal brain T2-weighted images
headline_result: Predictions generalize well to unseen data across centers (no single summary accuracy reported)

model_family: deep learning fracture detection algorithm trained on adult and pediatric data
patient_population: 600 extremity radiographs from patients under 17 (mean age 8.9 years), balanced positive and negative, grouped by body part
clinical_problem: detecting acute appendicular fractures in children with a tool that was trained on a mixed adult and pediatric population
model_description: Evaluates a fracture algorithm at three levels — per patient, per radiograph and per anatomical location — with follow-up radiographs or second-level imaging as the reference rather than the original report. The per-location analysis is the informative one: of 606 bounding boxes the model drew, 78% were correct and 18% were in the wrong place, so a fracture called at the wrong site is a meaningful fraction of its output.
title: Diagnostic performance of an AI algorithm for the detection of appendicular bone fractures in pediatric patients.
headline_result: per-patient sensitivity 91.3%, specificity 76.7%, accuracy 84%; per-radiograph accuracy 87.2%; of 606 bounding boxes, 77.9% correct and 18.1% incorrectly located

model_family: deep learning with adaptive instance normalization (AdaIN) style transfer
patient_population: children and adolescents undergoing hand radiography (RSNA public dataset, 1-228 months; private dataset, 12-218 months)
clinical_problem: bone age assessment
model_description: Input is a hand radiograph; DASA-net combines age and sex distributions via adaptive instance normalization and style transfer to simulate comparing the hand image with a standard bone atlas, outputting a predicted bone age. Evaluated against BoneXpert, Deeplasia, BoNet and other deep learning methods.
title: Doctor simulator: Delta-Age-Sex-AdaIn enhancing bone age assessment through AdaIn style transfer.
study_design: retrospective model development with external dataset validation
dataset_size: 14,236 hand radiographs (RSNA dataset); 474 hand radiographs (private Zigong dataset, 268 male)
headline_result: Mean absolute deviation 3.52 months on RSNA dataset and 3.82 months on private dataset, outperforming BoneXpert, Deeplasia and BoNet

patient_population: 282 Chinese Han males aged 6.0-21.0 years
age_groups: child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: Forensic bone age assessment (determining whether a person is above or below legal age thresholds of 12/14/16/18) from hand and wrist MRI in Chinese Han males
model_description: A deep learning model extracts and enhances epiphyseal features from hand and wrist MRI to classify subjects into legal age categories (12/14/16/18-year thresholds) and regress a continuous bone age estimate.
title: Forensic bone age assessment of hand and wrist joint MRI images in Chinese han male adolescents based on deep convolutional neural networks.
headline_result: Adult vs minor classification accuracy 91.1%; minor age-threshold classification accuracy 91.1-96.4%; regression MAE 1.24 years

model_family: Random Forest machine learning classifier with SMOTE balancing
patient_population: 34 children (mean age 7.48 years) with posterior fossa tumors (medulloblastoma, pilocytic astrocytoma, ependymoma)
clinical_problem: discriminating pediatric posterior fossa tumor subtype using diffusion kurtosis imaging
model_description: Whole-tumor and region-of-interest diffusion kurtosis imaging metrics are compared for measurement repeatability, then whole-tumor (VOI-based) DKI metrics from a SMOTE-balanced dataset are used to train a Random Forest classifier that discriminates medulloblastoma, pilocytic astrocytoma, and ependymoma.
title: Machine Learning Analysis in Diffusion Kurtosis Imaging for Discriminating Pediatric Posterior Fossa Tumors: A Repeatability and Accuracy Pilot Study.
headline_result: Random Forest classification accuracy 0.928

patient_population: 425 labor-monitoring cases
clinical_problem: distinguishing fetal from maternal heart-rate origin in Doppler-derived CTG monitoring to avoid misinterpreting maternal heart rate as fetal
model_description: input Doppler ultrasound signal segments annotated by a midwife; output a classification of whether the autocorrelation-derived heart rate is of fetal or maternal origin
title: The Approach to Sensing the True Fetal Heart Rate for CTG Monitoring: An Evaluation of Effectiveness of Deep Learning with Doppler Ultrasound Signals.
dataset_size: 425 cases (30,160 fetal and 2,160 maternal data points)
headline_result: AUC 0.98

patient_population: 900 Chinese children and adolescents from 30 centers
clinical_problem: Validating a commercially available AI-powered bone-age analyzer against the Tanner-Whitehouse 3 method in Chinese children and adolescents
model_description: A commercially available AI-powered X-ray bone-age analyzer, using a deep-learning automated bone-age-assessment system, estimates TW3 radius-ulna-short-bone and carpal bone age from hand-wrist radiographs, compared with expert and resident raters
release_evidence: commercially available artificial intelligence (AI)-powered X-ray bone age analyzer
title: Validation of an AI-Powered Automated X-ray Bone Age Analyzer in Chinese Children and Adolescents: A Comparison with the Tanner-Whitehouse 3 Method.
headline_result: TW3-RUS mean absolute error 0.48+/-0.42 years; TW3 carpal MAE 0.48+/-0.65 years, matching or exceeding doctor raters

patient_population: 1,050 patients aged 4-18 years with same-day lateral cephalometric and hand-wrist radiographs
clinical_problem: Comparing whole lateral cephalometric radiographs versus the cervical vertebral region alone for deep-learning bone age estimation in growing children
model_description: Two pretrained CNNs (InceptionResNet-v2, NASNet-Large) are trained to estimate bone age from either the whole lateral cephalometric radiograph or a cropped cervical-vertebrae region of interest, labeled using hand-wrist-radiograph-derived bone age, with Grad-CAM used to visualize model focus
journal: The Journal of clinical pediatric dentistry
title: Comparative analysis of deep-learning-based bone age estimation between whole lateral cephalometric and the cervical vertebral region in children.
headline_result: The whole-cephalogram-trained model outperformed the cervical-vertebrae-ROI-trained model (exact error metrics not given in abstract)

model_family: deep learning model embedded in a low-cost battery-powered ultrasound device
patient_population: 400 individuals with viable single first-trimester pregnancies in Lusaka, Zambia and Chapel Hill, North Carolina
clinical_problem: dating a pregnancy where no trained sonographer and no high-specification machine is available
model_description: The productized form of the blind-sweep gestational age model: the algorithm ships inside a cheap battery-powered probe, and the study puts it in the hands of novice users with no sonography training at all. Ground truth was set by transvaginal crown-rump length in the first trimester, so the comparison is against a fact rather than against another estimate. It met prespecified equivalence to credentialed sonographers doing standard biometry.
release_evidence: incorporated into the software of a low-cost, battery-powered device
title: Diagnostic Accuracy of an Integrated AI Tool to Estimate Gestational Age From Blind Ultrasound Sweeps.
headline_result: mean absolute error 3.2 days for novice users with the AI device versus 3.0 days for credentialed sonographers (difference 0.2 days, within the prespecified 2-day equivalence margin)

model_family: bimodal model combining CNN image features with automatically-generated clinical measurements (aaCM); compared with LightGBM, XGBoost, SVM, single CNN
patient_population: 813 radiographic hip images of infants at risk of DDH (232 unstable, 581 stable), multicenter
clinical_problem: diagnosing hip instability (developmental dysplasia of the hip) in infants at risk

title: Bimodal machine learning model for unstable hips in infants: integration of radiographic images with automatically-generated clinical measurements.
headline_result: aaCM accuracy equal to or higher than specialists; bimodal model outperformed LightGBM, XGBoost, SVM, single CNN

patient_population: 473 patients
clinical_problem: estimating pediatric bone age from left-hand radiographs to reduce inter-observer variability
model_description: input left-hand radiographs; output a predicted bone age via CNN regression
release_evidence: The code of the developed model for predicting the bone age in this study is available publicly on GitHub.
title: Deep learning-based automated bone age estimation for Saudi patients on hand radiograph images: a retrospective study.
headline_result: mean absolute error 2.3 years, median absolute error 2.1 years, MAPE 29%

model_family: three AI algorithms (architecture not specified) trained on disease-specific data
patient_population: 1,612 whole-spine radiographs (1,029 AIS, 583 ASD) for training; 285 for testing (159 AIS, 126 ASD)
clinical_problem: Improving automatic Cobb angle measurement accuracy for both adolescent idiopathic scoliosis and adult spinal deformity by training AI on disease-specific radiograph data

title: Comparison of three artificial intelligence algorithms for automatic cobb angle measurement using teaching data specific to three disease groups.
headline_result: The AIS/ASD-combined-trained AI showed the highest accuracy among the three algorithms (exact MAE/ICC not given in abstract)

model_family: CNN-driven deformable model (learned energy function + explicit deformable surface)
body_region: fetal head; also left ventricle, left atrium, bladder (mixed pediatric/adult tasks)

clinical_problem: 3D anatomical segmentation from limited training data, evaluated in part on fetal head segmentation on ultrasound

journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: Deep-DM: Deep-Driven Deformable Model for 3D Image Segmentation Using Limited Data.
dataset_size: varying numbers of training volumes per task (not specified for fetal head task)
headline_result: Outperformed state-of-the-art deep-learning segmentation methods across all tasks when few training samples were available (no single fetal-head-specific number given)

patient_population: adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis, across 15 reviewed studies
clinical_problem: identifying at the first visit which adolescent scoliosis curves will progress, which determines who gets braced
model_description: A systematic review of the prediction half of scoliosis AI: which radiological and clinical factors have been used to forecast curve progression, and with what models. It reports that machine learning gives higher precision than the traditional progression rules, but that interpretability and data complexity keep it in the research literature; multi-centre work is what would move it.
title: The application of machine learning methods for predicting the progression of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: a systematic review.

patient_population: Pediatric CXR dataset (PhysioNet); population not otherwise detailed
clinical_problem: Diagnosing pediatric thoracic diseases from chest X-rays using models pretrained on adult data (knowledge transfer), given limited pediatric training data
model_description: A three-stage self-supervised and transfer-learning framework fine-tunes transformer (ViT) and CNN models, pretrained on adult chest X-ray datasets (e.g., CheXpert), to diagnose and localize six pediatric thoracic disease categories on a small pediatric chest X-ray dataset.
release_evidence: The source code is available online and the data can be obtained from PhysioNet.
title: Three-Stage Framework for Accurate Pediatric Chest X-ray Diagnosis Using Self-Supervision and Transfer Learning on Small Datasets.
study_design: Retrospective model development and benchmarking study
dataset_size: Pediatric CXR dataset (PhysioNet); size not stated
headline_result: ViT-Base/16 fine-tuned on CheXpert: mean AUC 0.761 (95%CI 0.759-0.763) across 6 disease categories, sensitivity 0.639, specificity 0.683

patient_population: 23 children with early-onset scoliosis surgeries
clinical_problem: measuring implanted growing-rod length noninvasively to guide lengthening in early-onset scoliosis
