title: Automated Method for Growing Rod Length Measurement on Ultrasound Images in Children With Early Onset Scoliosis.
study_design: pilot model development and validation study
headline_result: ICC 0.98; mean absolute difference 0.86±1.0 mm vs. manual measurement

model_family: multimodal large language models (GPT-4, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Claude 3 Opus)
patient_population: 30 medically significant pediatric radiology cases (90 images total)
clinical_problem: interpreting pediatric radiological images and providing a diagnostic impression
task: report generation / LLM; foundation model / vision-language
model_description: Thirty pediatric radiology cases (90 images) with a short clinical history are submitted to three multimodal large language models (GPT-4, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Claude 3 Opus), which generate a diagnostic impression; responses are independently scored for accuracy by a resident and an attending physician.
release_evidence: GPT-4 (OpenAI), Gemini 1.5 Pro (Google) and Claude 3 Opus (Anthropic) are named commercial vendor products
title: Capability of multimodal large language models to interpret pediatric radiological images.
study_design: retrospective diagnostic accuracy evaluation of general-purpose multimodal LLMs
headline_result: correctly diagnosed 27.8% of images (25/90), partially correct 13.3%, incorrect 58.9%

model_name: ADU-GD (Attention Gate Double U-Net with Guided Decoder)
patient_population: not stated (benchmark ultrasound datasets)
clinical_problem: Segmenting and measuring fetal biometric parameters (head circumference, abdominal circumference, femur length, biparietal diameter) from ultrasound
model_description: ADU-GD, an attention-gated double U-Net with a guided decoder, segments fetal anatomical structures on ultrasound and estimates biometric parameters (head circumference, abdominal circumference, femur length, biparietal diameter), benchmarked against numerous other deep-learning segmentation models.
title: Segmentation and Estimation of Fetal Biometric Parameters using an Attention Gate Double U-Net with Guided Decoder Architecture.
study_design: Retrospective model development and benchmarking study
headline_result: MAE 0.99 mm overall; Dice 99.1%; parameter MAE: HC 2.2mm, AC 2.6mm, FL 0.6mm, BPD 1.2mm

patient_population: 2,154 transperineal ultrasound images from term, singleton, cephalic pregnancies across 16 centers
clinical_problem: Automatically identifying fetal head position during the second stage of labor from transperineal ultrasound, to guide delivery management
model_description: Three cascaded ResNet18-based CNNs classify transperineal ultrasound images of the fetal head into occiput anterior/posterior/transverse positions, using transabdominal ultrasound as the ground-truth label
journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
title: A deep learning approach to identify the fetal head position using transperineal ultrasound during labor.
headline_result: Overall accuracy 94.5% (95% CI 92.0-97.0), F1-score 0.92

patient_population: 48 patients with lymphoblastic lymphoma, 61 with Burkitt lymphoma (109 total pediatric patients)
clinical_problem: Using CT radiomics features of the spleen to noninvasively differentiate Burkitt lymphoma from lymphoblastic lymphoma in children.

journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
title: The value of radiomics features of the spleen as surrogates for differentiating subtypes of common pediatric lymphomas.
headline_result: SVM_4 fusion model AUC 0.967 (training), 0.754 (test)

model_family: k-nearest neighbor, SVM, random forest, XGBoost
body_region: fetal (prenatal screening, combined with biochemical markers)
patient_population: 7,076 pregnant women in Northern Vietnam (1,035 with a fetus with Down syndrome)
clinical_problem: Screening for Down syndrome in the first and second trimesters using ultrasound and biochemical testing, especially in resource-limited settings
model_description: Machine learning models (k-nearest neighbor, SVM, random forest, XGBoost) combine ultrasound findings and biochemical test results to predict Down syndrome risk in the first and second trimesters.
title: Applying machine learning in screening for Down Syndrome in both trimesters for diverse healthcare scenarios.
dataset_size: 7,076 pregnant women, single site in Northern Vietnam
headline_result: Trimester 1: XGBoost 94% accuracy, 88% AUC; Trimester 2: SVM 89% accuracy, 84% AUC

patient_population: 28 MRI-negative children (37 SEEG studies) with drug-resistant focal epilepsy
clinical_problem: detecting occult focal cortical dysplasia lesions on structural MRI in children with MRI-negative drug-resistant focal epilepsy
model_description: The MELD deep-learning algorithm analyzes structural brain MRI to detect subtle focal cortical dysplasia lesions not visible on conventional radiological review; applied retrospectively to MRI-negative pediatric epilepsy cases and compared against SEEG and PET findings.
title: The utility of Multicentre Epilepsy Lesion Detection (MELD) algorithm in identifying epileptic activity and predicting seizure freedom in MRI lesion-negative paediatric patients.
headline_result: clusters identified in 14/28 (50%) children; 1 MELD cluster co-localized with resection cavity, associated with Engel 1A outcome

patient_population: 100 women with placenta accreta spectrum (mean age 34.6±3.9), 64 with placenta increta, multi-center 2018-2023
clinical_problem: Antenatal MRI-based radiomic prediction of severe placenta accreta spectrum (placenta increta) to guide delivery planning.
model_description: Radiomic features extracted from T2-weighted antenatal MRI, combined with a clinical variable, are used in a random forest/support vector machine classifier to predict severe (increta) placenta accreta spectrum subtype.
title: Radiomic study of antenatal prediction of severe placenta accreta spectrum from MRI.
study_design: multi-center retrospective radiomics model validation study
headline_result: Clinical-radiomic model AUC 0.713, accuracy 0.695, sensitivity 0.843, specificity 0.447

patient_population: adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis, across 40 reviewed articles
clinical_problem: diagnosing adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, stratifying who will progress, and guiding treatment
task: measurement / quantification; detection / diagnosis; outcome prediction
model_description: Maps what AI has been used for in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: 62.5% of the work is imaging analysis, mostly automatic Cobb angle and vertebral rotation measurement and curve classification, and 37.5% is prediction, mostly of curve progression. The limiting finding is governance rather than accuracy — only 15 of 40 studies offered any clinical implementation guidance, and external validation and model transparency are largely absent.
title: Applications of artificial intelligence for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: mapping the evidence.
dataset_size: 40 articles, 77.5% from the last five years
headline_result: average reported model accuracy 85.4% among the 52.5% of studies that reported it; only 37.5% gave clinical implementation guidance

model_family: neural network algorithm combining demographics, DTI, and graph-theory network metrics
patient_population: 36 first-episode, treatment-naive adolescents with major depressive disorder (mean age 15.8) and 29 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (mean age 15.2)
clinical_problem: diagnosing first-episode major depressive disorder in pubertal children/adolescents from white matter and network changes
model_description: Whole-brain diffusion tensor imaging and graph-theory network topology metrics are combined with demographic data and fed into a neural network model to distinguish first-episode, treatment-naive adolescents with major depressive disorder from healthy controls, identifying white matter and network hub abnormalities linked to symptom severity.
title: Regional brain structural network topology mediates the associations between white matter damage and disease severity in first-episode, Treatment-naïve pubertal children with major depressive disorder.
headline_result: Diagnostic model achieved AUROC 0.88 and F1 score 0.80

patient_population: 336 patients treated for pediatric low-grade glioma (1999-2018)
clinical_problem: non-invasively determining the molecular/genetic status of pediatric low-grade glioma from MRI to guide use of targeted therapy
model_description: Takes T2-FLAIR MRI tumor regions (manually segmented) as input and outputs a prediction of pLGG genetic/molecular status, combining a convolutional neural network with random-forest radiomics features.
title: Beyond hand-crafted features for pretherapeutic molecular status identification of pediatric low-grade gliomas.
headline_result: Mean AUC 0.824 (combined model) vs 0.802 (radiomics) vs 0.764 (CNN)

model_family: random forest classifier atlas-based segmentation with expectation-maximization Markov random field
patient_population: 40 neonatal MR images, gestational age 37-44 weeks
clinical_problem: segmenting gray matter, white matter and CSF on neonatal brain MRI
model_description: A subject-specific atlas is generated using a random forest classifier, then combined with an expectation-maximization Markov random field method to segment gray matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid on neonatal brain MRI, using intensity- and gradient-based features.
title: Subject-specific atlas for automatic brain tissue segmentation of neonatal magnetic resonance images.
headline_result: overall accuracy 94.3%, Dice 0.945 (GM), 0.947 (WM), 0.912 (CSF); up to 4% improvement over comparator methods

patient_population: fetuses undergoing echocardiographic CHD screening (review)
clinical_problem: reviewing AI's role in improving prenatal detection of congenital heart disease via fetal echocardiography
model_description: A review of recent advances in AI applications for fetal echocardiography, including automating/standardizing display of diagnostic cardiac views to improve CHD detection accuracy.
journal: International journal of cardiology. Heart & vasculature
title: Artificial intelligence in fetal echocardiography: Recent advances and future prospects.

model_family: U-Net style architecture with attention mechanism, multi-modality feature learning
patient_population: approximately 72,000 2D fetal brain MRI images (T2-weighted, diffusion-weighted, and functional MRI), including normal and pathological brains from multiple scanners
clinical_problem: automatically extracting (skull-stripping) the fetal brain from heterogeneous fetal MRI sequences as a preprocessing step for fetal brain imaging pipelines
model_description: Deep learning model using U-Net style architecture with attention mechanisms and cross-modality feature learning, trained on a large annotated multi-sequence fetal brain MRI dataset to automatically extract the fetal brain from T2-weighted, diffusion-weighted, and functional MRI
journal: IEEE open journal of engineering in medicine and biology
title: Fetal-BET: Brain Extraction Tool for Fetal MRI.
study_design: retrospective model development with external multi-center test data
headline_result: accurate brain extraction on heterogeneous test data from different scanners, pathological brains, and various gestational stages (no single summary metric stated)

patient_population: children with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (100 training, 60 test radiographs)
clinical_problem: automating kyphotic and lordotic angle measurement on radiographs to diagnose adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
model_description: input lateral spine radiographs; output T1-L5 vertebral segmentation used to automatically compute kyphotic and lordotic angles
title: Using machine learning to automatically measure kyphotic and lordotic angle measurements on radiographs for children with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
study_design: retrospective single-center method development and validation study
headline_result: clinical acceptance rate 98%/75%/97% and ICC 0.91/0.60/0.88 for T1-T12 KA/T5-T12 KA/L1-L5 LA; ~4±2 s per radiograph

clinical_problem: detecting lung consolidations on pediatric lung ultrasound video for pneumonia diagnosis

title: FLUEnT: Transformer for detecting lung consolidations in videos using fused lung ultrasound encodings.
headline_result: mean balanced accuracy 89.3%, outperforming state-of-the-art models by an average of 8 percentage points

patient_population: 78 pediatric medulloblastoma patients (ages 2-18) from three institutions
clinical_problem: Automatically delineating medulloblastoma tumor subcompartments (enhancing tumor, edema, cystic/non-enhancing core) on multiparametric MRI to support radiation therapy planning
model_description: Input: gadolinium-enhanced T1, T2, and FLAIR MRI; output: automatic segmentation of tumor habitat and subcompartments, via nnU-Net models (one pretrained on adult glioma and fine-tuned, one trained directly on medulloblastoma data)
title: nnU-Net-based Segmentation of Tumor Subcompartments in Pediatric Medulloblastoma Using Multiparametric MRI: A Multi-institutional Study.
study_design: retrospective multi-institutional segmentation model development and cross-site evaluation
headline_result: Dice scores for tumor habitat 0.80-0.86 across three test sites

model_family: mask conditional diffusion model (generative deep learning)

clinical_problem: prediction of fetal acidosis at delivery

journal: Studies in health technology and informatics
title: Multimodal Model for Predicting Fetal Acidosis in Delivery Room.
headline_result: AUROC 0.752 on the test dataset

model_description: A PRISMA systematic review of 28 studies (from 621 screened) on AI applications for prenatal detection of congenital heart disease, finding deep learning as the predominant approach and ultrasound and MRI as the main data types used, summarizing the landscape of available data and methods.
journal: Studies in health technology and informatics
title: Data for AI in Congenital Heart Defects: Systematic Review.

title: Separating group- and individual-level brain signatures in the newborn functional connectome: A deep learning approach.
study_design: retrospective methods development using public neonatal and adult rs-fMRI datasets
headline_result: Individual identification accuracy ~45% with VAE vs. ~10-30% with linear models; age prediction r~0.7

patient_population: children and adolescents with wrist trauma radiographs (limited dataset)

dataset_size: limited dataset (exact size not stated in abstract)
headline_result: accuracy 86% (augmented) and 84% (original) test sets; fracture sensitivity 97%

The models successfully predicted these measures in younger children (6-11) with ADHD but not in adolescents (12-16) with ADHD.
title: Identifying developmental changes in functional brain connectivity associated with cognitive functioning in children and adolescents with ADHD.
dataset_size: 373 children/adolescents with ADHD, 106 neurotypical controls, ages 6-16

title: Assessment of deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR) on image quality in pediatric cardiac CT datasets type of manuscript: Original research.

title: Machine learning approach for the prediction of macrosomia.
study_design: retrospective single-center predictive model development study

clinical_problem: Detecting pulmonary consolidation on point-of-care lung ultrasound to diagnose pneumonia in hospitalized children

title: Development and testing of a deep learning algorithm to detect lung consolidation among children with pneumonia using hand-held ultrasound.

clinical_problem: Detecting osteosarcoma on knee X-rays at initial consultation to improve early diagnosis in pediatric and young adult patients

title: High-quality expert annotations enhance artificial intelligence model accuracy for osteosarcoma X-ray diagnosis.

model_description: Input: pediatric limb radiographs; output: detection of acute fractures, evaluated both as a standalone model and as assistive support for emergency physicians.

clinical_problem: general-purpose 3D instance segmentation of blob-like structures, demonstrated (among several non-medical/non-pediatric microscopy and CT applications) on placental cotyledons in human fetal MRI without retraining
model_description: Input: any 3D image containing blob-like star-convex structures, here human fetal MRI; output: 3D instance segmentation, using a network trained solely on domain-randomized synthetic data so it needs no retraining or fine-tuning for new modalities.
release_evidence: Code is available at https://github.com/neel-dey/AnyStar
journal: IEEE Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision. IEEE Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision
title: AnyStar: Domain randomized universal star-convex 3D instance segmentation.
study_design: general-purpose methods development, applied across multiple imaging domains including one fetal MRI application

model_family: deep learning phenotype encoder with domain-adversarial training + growth predictor
patient_population: pediatric patients including those with cranial pathology, imaged with cross-sectional CT and 3D photograms
clinical_problem: prediction of normal and pathologic head shape development for surgical planning
model_description: Input is a cross-sectional head CT or 3D photogram segmentation; a phenotype encoder creates age- and sex-independent patient representations, and a growth predictor generates the predicted head shape at any target age/sex, accounting for pathology, without requiring longitudinal training data. Evaluated against an independent longitudinal dataset.
journal: ... International Symposium on Medical Information Processing and Analysis. International SIPAIM Workshop
title: Personalized phenotype encoding and prediction of pathological head development from cross-sectional images.
study_design: retrospective technical development with independent longitudinal validation
dataset_size: not stated (cross-sectional CT and 3D photogram training set; independent longitudinal test set)
headline_result: Head surface growth prediction error 4.93 +/- 2.29 mm and volumetric error 0.16 +/- 0.11 L in cranial-pathology patients; 4.61 +/- 3.28 mm and 0.27 +/- 0.19 L in normative subjects

patient_population: 407 pediatric and 193 premature-infant chest radiographs
clinical_problem: Segmenting the lungs on chest radiographs of premature and pediatric infants to support diagnosis and severity grading of pulmonary disease
model_description: A two-step deep learning method (UNETR) that first detects the lungs then segments the retro-cardiac lung region on chest x-rays, pretrained on ~31,000 chest x-rays then fine-tuned on pediatric and premature cohorts.
journal: ... International Symposium on Medical Information Processing and Analysis. International SIPAIM Workshop
title: Tiny Lungs, Big Challenges: Pediatric and Premature Lung Segmentation using Deep Learning.
study_design: Retrospective model development and internal evaluation
dataset_size: 407 pediatric images and 193 premature images (fine-tuning); pretrained on ~31,000 chest x-rays
headline_result: Mean Dice 0.960 (pediatric) and 0.946 (premature); mean Hausdorff distance 6.576 and 8.124 pixels

patient_population: Pediatric brain tumor cases from the BraTS 2023 challenge (part of 4,500 total brain tumor cases across all challenge tasks)
clinical_problem: Can automated segmentation of pediatric brain tumors on multi-parametric MRI support quantitative analysis for clinical trials and personalized care?
model_description: Takes multi-parametric MRI as input; an ensemble of nnU-Net and Swin UNETR models with targeted post-processing outputs voxel-wise segmentation of tumor sub-regions (enhancing tumor, tumor core, whole tumor).
journal: Brain tumor segmentation, and cross-modality domain adaptation for medical image segmentation : MICCAI challenges, BraTS 2023 and CrossMoDA 2023, held in conjunction with MICCAI 2023, Vancouver, BC, Canada, October 12 and 8, 2024 : proc...
title: Model Ensemble for Brain Tumor Segmentation in Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
dataset_size: BraTS 2023 pediatric brain tumor (PED) task test cases (part of 4,500 total brain tumor cases across all tasks)
headline_result: Lesion-wise Dice scores for pediatric task (PED): 0.653, 0.809, 0.826 (enhancing tumor, tumor core, whole tumor); ranked 1st in PED task

model_family: deep learning (cycle-consistent multi-task surface reconstruction network)
patient_population: 83 fetal MRI subjects
clinical_problem: Reconstructing the fetal cortical surface from MRI to allow quantitative analysis of normal and abnormal prenatal brain development
model_description: A deep learning model that takes fetal brain MRI volumes as input and outputs reconstructed inner and outer cortical surface meshes, using a cycle-consistent multi-task strategy with stationary velocity fields.
journal: Medical image computing and computer-assisted intervention : MICCAI ... International Conference on Medical Image Computing and Computer-Assisted Intervention
title: Cycle-consistent Learning for Fetal Cortical Surface Reconstruction.
headline_result: Geometric error 0.229 +/- 0.047 mm; 0.023 +/- 0.058% self-intersecting faces

patient_population: 210 infant MRI scans
clinical_problem: Identifying infants who were exposed to drugs prenatally, using brain MRI, to enable earlier intervention
model_description: A deep learning model combining a volumetric network and a cortical-surface network with transformers, taking infant brain MRI as input and classifying whether the infant had prenatal drug exposure.
journal: Medical image computing and computer-assisted intervention : MICCAI ... International Conference on Medical Image Computing and Computer-Assisted Intervention
title: Disentangled Hybrid Transformer for Identification of Infants with Prenatal Drug Exposure.
study_design: Retrospective model development and comparison study

patient_population: adolescents undergoing multi-task fMRI
clinical_problem: characterizing sex-related differences in adolescent brain functional connectivity (neurodevelopment)
model_description: Takes multi-task fMRI-derived brain connectivity graphs as input and outputs a sex classification, with GNNExplainer identifying the sub-networks driving the prediction.
title: Explainable Multimodal Graph Isomorphism Network for Interpreting Sex Differences in Adolescent Neurodevelopment.
study_design: retrospective model-development study for sex classification from multi-task fMRI
headline_result: 81.67% improvement in classification accuracy versus competing models

model_family: artificial intelligence Greulich-Pyle (GP) bone age assessment system (domestically developed)
patient_population: children and adolescents aged 6-15 years undergoing wrist radiography
clinical_problem: bone age assessment using the Greulich-Pyle method
model_description: A domestically developed AI system that applies the Greulich-Pyle atlas method to wrist radiographs was compared against manual GP bone-age assessment by an expert, in a cohort of boys and girls aged 6-15 years, to check whether the AI system's readings agree closely enough with expert readings for clinical use.
journal: Chinese Journal of Tissue Engineering Research
title: Consistency between artificial intelligence and expert Greulich-Pyle atlas method for bone age assessment
dataset_size: 1,322 wrist radiographs from children/adolescents 6-15 years (672 male, 650 female)
headline_result: Mean absolute difference from expert GP assessment was 0.39 years (male) and 0.32 years (female); Pearson correlation r=0.991 (male) and r=0.992 (female); overall Kappa 0.603 (male) and 0.659 (female).

model_family: deep learning landmark detection and segmentation (coordinate-convolution + Polarized Self-Attention feature extraction on a High-Resolution Network)
patient_population: 37 spine radiographs (481 vertebrae) from adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis
clinical_problem: measurement of axial vertebral rotation for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS)
model_description: Spine radiographs are input. An improved feature-extraction module (coordinate convolution plus Polarized Self-Attention) built on a High-Resolution Network outputs vertebral landmark locations and pedicle segmentation, from which an automatic algorithm calculates axial vertebral rotation (AVR), a measurement used in treatment decisions and progression prediction for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
title: Automatic axial vertebral rotation estimation on radiographs for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis by deep learning
dataset_size: 37 spine radiographs, 481 vertebrae, 962 AVR measurements (two observers)
headline_result: mean radial error of landmark detection 2.70mm (2.13mm improvement over baseline); pedicle segmentation Dice 72.45% (4.61% improvement); average AVR measurement error under 5°, within clinical standard

clinical_problem: screening/diagnosis of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) as a non-radiographic alternative to Cobb angle measurement
model_description: Narrative review of non-radiographic AI-based screening approaches for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, proposed as alternatives to radiation-based Cobb angle measurement: three-dimensional spinal ultrasound imaging, camera/sensor-based scoliosis detection systems, combined 2D digital camera plus AI, and computer-vision-based posture analysis systems.
title: Combining artifícial intelligence fór diagnosing adolescent idiopathic scoliosis

patient_population: fetuses undergoing the Kurjak Antenatal Neurodevelopmental Test (KANET) via 4D ultrasound during the third trimester
clinical_problem: early detection of fetal neurological impairment risk via fetal movement analysis (KANET test)
model_description: 3D ultrasound image frames extracted from 4D recordings of fetal movement during the KANET test are input. A custom CNN classifies characteristic fetal neurobehavioral movements (e.g., facial vs hand-to-face movements) to assist early detection of fetal neurological impairment disorders (e.g., cerebral palsy, epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder), with results shown via a graphical interface as each recorded frame is parsed.
journal: Donald School Journal of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
title: Trustworthiness of Four-dimensional Ultrasound and Artificial Intelligence in Improving KANET Test for Detection of Fetuses at Neurorisk
headline_result: overall classification accuracy 93.83%

model_family: two-stage CNN pipeline: YOLOv5-based detection network with polarized self-attention (OSA-YOLOv5), followed by a GRU-UNet segmentation network
patient_population: adolescents undergoing left-hand X-ray, mixed with the RSNA public bone age dataset
clinical_problem: hand bone segmentation to support skeletal bone age assessment
model_description: Left-hand X-ray images are input. OSA-YOLOv5, a detection network enhanced with a coordinate-convolution and Polarized Self-Attention feature-extraction module, first extracts (localizes) the hand bones; GRU-UNet then separates and segments the individual bones, using spatial-sequence modeling. The pipeline is intended as a preprocessing step for automated bone age assessment.
title: Hand bone extraction and segmentation based on a convolutional neural network
dataset_size: 2000 left-hand X-ray images (1000 from adolescents at licensed local hospitals, 1000 from the RSNA public bone age dataset)
headline_result: OSA-YOLOv5 training efficiency 28% higher than the traditional network with higher extraction accuracy; GRU-UNet segmentation accuracy 14.70% higher than UNet

clinical_problem: AI-assisted diagnosis and severity quantification of lung pathology (including pediatric pneumonia) on point-of-care lung ultrasound
model_description: Narrative review of recent deep learning applications in lung point-of-care ultrasound (LUS). Summarizes curated, annotated public datasets and deep learning models developed to detect COVID-19 pneumonia, pulmonary edema, pneumothorax, and pediatric pneumonia, to quantify disease severity, guide image acquisition, and support prognosis/risk stratification; discusses potential to extend LUS AI into limited-resource and prehospital settings.
title: Artificial Intelligence in Lung Ultrasound

patient_population: 75 full-term newborns (gestational age 39.38±1.22 weeks, postnatal age 11.11±6.67 days) with no MRI abnormalities
clinical_problem: postnatal brain regional volume growth and its association with neurobehavioral outcome in term neonates
model_description: 3D T1-weighted neonatal brain MRI is input. VB-Net, a deep learning segmentation model, divides the brain into 87 template-defined regions and computes each region's volume; these volumes are then related to postnatal age and neurobehavioral scores by correlation and regression analysis.
journal: Journal of Xi'an Jiaotong University (Medical Sciences)
title: Postnatal age-related change of brain volume and its association with neurobehavior outcome in term neonates
headline_result: 66.7% of regional brain volumes (58/87) significantly increased with postnatal age (r 0.2-0.7, P<0.05); right occipital lobe gray matter volume grew fastest (slope 100.67) and correlated with behavioral scores (r=0.324, P<0.01)

clinical_problem: bone age assessment practice patterns and adoption of AI-assisted bone age assessment
model_description: Cross-sectional questionnaire survey of 450 radiologists and pediatricians across 162 Chinese medical institutions, on current pediatric bone age assessment practices. Found left-wrist radiography and the ATLAS method predominate, that 98.4% of respondents agreed AI technology should be used to assist bone age assessment, but that only 9.3% of institutions currently use AI-assisted technology.
title: Analysis of the current situation and development trend of bone age assessment of children in China based on questionnaires
dataset_size: 450 valid questionnaires from 162 medical institutions across 26 provinces
headline_result: 98.4% (443/450) of respondents agreed AI should assist bone age assessment, but only 9.3% (15/162) of institutions currently use AI-assisted technology

model_family: geometric/texture feature-based framework (Riemannian geometry descriptors and Haralick texture features) with an Artificial Neural Network classifier
patient_population: 1114 T1-weighted MRI scans from 521 individuals with ASD and 593 controls, age range 6-64 years, divided into three broad age groups
clinical_problem: detection/characterization of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) via structural brain MRI texture analysis
model_description: T1-weighted brain MRI scans are input, from which automatically labeled subcortical and cortical regions have texture features computed using Riemannian geometry descriptors and Haralick texture quantifiers. The most discriminative features are selected and used to train an artificial neural network to classify ASD versus typically developing controls.
title: Automatic characterization of cerebral MRI images for the detection of autism spectrum disorders
dataset_size: 1114 MRI scans (521 ASD, 593 controls), ages 6-64 years

patient_population: pediatric patients admitted between 2005 and 2022 with pneumothorax or pleural effusion
clinical_problem: deciding whether tube thoracostomy is needed for pediatric pneumothorax or pleural effusion
model_description: XRAInet is a deep learning decision-support system trained on chest X-rays to identify pediatric patients with pneumothorax or pleural effusion and to localize the abnormal region, supporting the decision of whether tube thoracostomy intervention is warranted versus conservative management.
title: XRAInet: AI-based decision support for pneumothorax and pleural effusion management
headline_result: XRAInet achieved a mean average precision of 0.918; on an independent test set, sensitivity was 64.00% and specificity was 96.15%.

model_family: commercial deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR) algorithm evaluated against filtered back-projection and ASIR-V, with automatic airway segmentation via VCAR software
patient_population: 52 children undergoing ultra-low-dose chest CT, divided into three age groups (1-2 years, 3-6 years, 7-13 years)
clinical_problem: impact of CT reconstruction algorithm on automatic airway segmentation success and image quality in ultra-low-dose pediatric chest CT
model_description: Ultra-low-dose chest CT raw data are reconstructed with six different algorithms (filtered back-projection, 50%/100% adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction, and low/medium/high-strength deep learning image reconstruction). Automatic airway segmentation software is then applied to each reconstruction, and segmentation success rate plus subjective and quantitative image quality are compared across pediatric age groups and tracheal sizes.
release_evidence: DLIR (deep learning image reconstruction) and VCAR are named, commercially available CT reconstruction/segmentation software
title: Impact of reconstruction algorithms on the success rate and quality of automatic airway segmentation in children under ultra-low-dose chest CT scanning
headline_result: segmentation success rate in the youngest group improved from 7.69% (100% ASIR-V) to 38.64% with DLIR-medium/high (P=0.03); DLIR-high gave the lowest image noise and highest subjective quality score

patient_population: pediatric patients with vesicoureteral reflux, hydronephrosis, or lower urinary tract dysfunction
clinical_problem: AI applications in pediatric urologic imaging (vesicoureteral reflux grading, hydronephrosis, bladder dysfunction)
model_description: This review surveys existing and emerging AI models in pediatric urology, including machine learning and deep learning approaches for grading vesicoureteral reflux, explainable models predicting obstructive hydronephrosis from ultrasound images alone, and ensemble models integrating video urodynamic pressure tracings with fluoroscopic images to characterize bladder dysfunction, while noting persistent problems with generalizability, transparency and reproducibility.
title: Artificial Intelligence Tools in Pediatric Urology: A Comprehensive Assessment of the Landscape and Current Utilization

model_family: radiomics with recursive feature elimination and a random forest classifier
patient_population: 190 patients with suspected juvenile idiopathic arthritis
clinical_problem: diagnosis of active knee arthritis in juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA)
model_description: Blood-pool phase bone scintigraphy images (technetium-99m-methyl diphosphonate) are input, with the region of interest defined as the area between the knee growth plates. Quantitative radiomic features are extracted from original and filtered images, recursive feature elimination selects the most informative features, and a random forest classifier outputs a diagnosis of active JIA-related knee arthritis.
title: Radiomics analysis on blood-pool phase of bone scintigraphy for the diagnosis of Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis
headline_result: AUC 0.89 (95% CI 0.88-0.92) using 14 selected radiomic features (4 original, 10 filtered)

model_family: univariate regression and multivariate machine learning
patient_population: 53 families of children with Noonan syndrome, ages 4-12.9 years (mean 8.48, SD 2.12), 34 female
clinical_problem: predicting child neuroanatomical and neuropsychiatric outcomes in Noonan syndrome (a RASopathy) from parent traits
model_description: Non-carrier parent cognitive and behavioral trait measures are input. Univariate regression and multivariate machine learning models output predicted child cognitive, behavioral, and neuroanatomical outcomes (via structural brain MRI), providing an individualized expected-outcome estimate for children with Noonan syndrome relative to traditional case-control comparisons.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: A familial modeling framework for advancing precision medicine in neuropsychiatric disorders: A study in children with RASopathies
dataset_size: 53 families of children with Noonan syndrome
headline_result: parent cognition (especially visuospatial/motor abilities), depression, anxiety and ADHD symptoms were significantly associated with child neuroanatomical variability, particularly in temporal, parietal, subcortical regions and the amygdala (no single summary statistic given)

model_family: machine learning pipeline (data imputation, feature selection, regression models)
patient_population: 176 control pregnancies and 67 preterm birth cases, using comprehensive multi-modal fetal MRI
clinical_problem: predicting gestational age at birth in the context of preterm birth risk
model_description: Multi-modal morphological and functional fetal MRI features (including cervical length and placental T2* values) are input to a machine learning regression pipeline with data imputation and feature selection. The pipeline outputs a predicted gestational age at birth, which is then classified into term versus preterm categories.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Predicting gestational age at birth in the context of preterm birth from multi-modal fetal MRI
headline_result: R2 0.51, mean absolute error 2.22 weeks; term/preterm classification accuracy 0.88, sensitivity 0.86, specificity 0.89

patient_population: infants scanned with paired ultra-low-field and high-field MRI
clinical_problem: improving image resolution/quality of ultra-low-field MRI for pediatric neurodevelopmental research in low- and middle-income countries
model_description: Multiple low-resolution, anisotropic T2-weighted images acquired in orthogonal orientations on an ultra-low-field MRI scanner are input. A multi-orientation U-Net outputs a high-resolution, isotropic super-resolved T2-weighted reconstruction, trained on paired ultra-low-field and high-field infant MRI data to improve accessibility of MRI for neurodevelopmental research in resource-limited settings.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Ultra-low-field paediatric MRI in low- and middle-income countries: super-resolution using a multi-orientation U-Net
headline_result: caudate volume estimates: linear correlation r=0.94 vs 0.84 for existing methods; concordance correlation 0.94 vs 0.80; mean error 0.05 cm3 vs 0.36 cm3

model_family: radiomics combined with CT features, using logistic regression, SVM, random forest, LDA, and SGD classifiers
patient_population: 153 children with pneumonia (101 mycoplasma, 52 non-mycoplasma)
clinical_problem: distinguishing mycoplasma from non-mycoplasma pneumonia in children
model_description: Chest CT images are input, from which radiomic features and selected qualitative CT features (lobar involvement, bronchial wall thickening, tree-in-bud sign, edge-retraction sign) are extracted. Multiple machine learning classifiers are trained on the combined CT and radiomic features to output a probability of mycoplasma versus non-mycoplasma pneumonia.
journal: Chinese Journal of Interventional Imaging and Therapy
title: Radiomics combined with CT features for distinguishing mycoplasma and non-mycoplasma pneumonia in children
headline_result: best combined CT-radiomics model (SVM) AUC 0.823 in validation (vs CT-only 0.710 and best radiomics-only 0.715, not significant); training-set AUC 0.840, significantly higher than CT-only or radiomics-only (P<0.05)

patient_population: 1370 pediatric patients undergoing elbow X-ray, from multiple healthcare centers
clinical_problem: detection of hidden (occult) pediatric elbow fractures
model_description: Preprocessed (normalized, resized) elbow radiographs are input. A DenseNet-201 convolutional neural network, trained with a 70/30 train-validation split and data augmentation, outputs a classification of whether a pediatric elbow fracture is present, intended to assist diagnosis of fractures that are difficult to detect.
journal: Journal of Radiation Research and Applied Sciences
title: Detection of hidden pediatric elbow fractures in X-ray images based on deep learning
dataset_size: 1370 pediatric patients, X-ray images from multiple healthcare centers
headline_result: accuracy 94.1%, AUC 98.7%, sensitivity 93.2%, specificity 94.8% on the training dataset

patient_population: fetuses imaged with freehand 2D ultrasound sweeps, natively-acquired and volume-sampled video sequences from different ultrasound manufacturers
clinical_problem: 3D reconstruction of fetal brain anatomy from freehand, non-sensor-tracked 2D ultrasound sweeps
model_description: A set of freehand 2D ultrasound images (without external position tracking) is input. ImplicitVol, a deep neural network, predicts each image's location in 3D space, jointly refines these locations, and represents the reconstructed anatomy as a continuous implicit function rather than a discrete voxel grid, producing a 3D fetal brain volume reconstructable to arbitrarily high resolution.
title: Sensorless volumetric reconstruction of fetal brain freehand ultrasound scans with deep implicit representation
headline_result: reconstructions show significantly better visual and semantic quality than existing interpolation-based reconstruction approaches (no single numeric metric given)

model_family: radiomics feature extraction (pyradiomics) with statistical correlation analysis
patient_population: 72 pregnant women: 35 with congenital fetal diaphragmatic hernia, 37 without fetal lung pathology
clinical_problem: assessing fetal lung structural maturity/pathology in congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH)
model_description: Frontal/co-frontal T2-weighted fetal MRI images at the level of the lungs are input, with the lung region of interest manually segmented in 2D and 3D. 107 radiomic features are extracted using pyradiomics, and statistical correlation analysis relates these features to the presence of fetal lung pathology in congenital diaphragmatic hernia, as a potential source of additional diagnostic information on lung structural maturity.
title: Radiomics of fetal magnetic resonance imaging in congenital diaphragmatic hernia
headline_result: 14 significant 2D features and 73 significant 3D features (p<0.05); after removing cross-correlated features, 6 (2D) and 8 (3D) features retained; 20 3D features with correlation coefficient r>0.4 (p<0.05) vs 3 for single-slice

body_region: brain (white matter lesions, cortical and deep gray matter)
patient_population: training: 2934 multiple sclerosis patients (4247 scans) across 592 scanners; external validation: 1001 patients (14,952 scans) from three cohorts, including 161 adolescent patients
clinical_problem: quantifying multiple sclerosis lesion and brain volumes from heterogeneous, single-modality clinical MRI archives
model_description: A single MRI modality/sequence from a clinical brain scan is input (rather than a full multimodal protocol). MindGlide, a deep learning model, outputs volumes of white-matter lesions, cortical gray matter, and deep gray-matter structures, trained on a large multi-scanner multiple sclerosis dataset and externally validated including an adolescent subgroup, to enable analysis of incomplete or heterogeneous clinical archives.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Repurposing Clinical MRI Archives for Multiple Sclerosis Research with a Flexible, Single-Modality Approach: New Insights from Old Scans
study_design: retrospective multi-cohort technical development and external validation
dataset_size: 4247 scans from 2934 patients (training); 14,952 scans from 1001 patients across 3 external validation cohorts (incl. 161 adolescents)
headline_result: MindGlide-derived volumes correlated with EDSS disability (|r| 0.1-0.2, p<0.05) and outperformed an established tool; robustly detected treatment effects (lesion accrual, brain tissue loss) across clinical trials

model_family: statistical and machine learning prediction models
patient_population: fetuses (via prenatal ultrasound) and their offspring followed postnatally with MRI at 6 and 12 months
clinical_problem: early prediction of autism spectrum disorder from prenatal and early postnatal brain imaging
model_description: In a prospective cohort of pregnant women and their offspring, fetal head circumference, corpus callosum thickness and ventricle size were assessed with 3D/4D ultrasound, and postnatal brain structure (amygdala size, frontal cortical volume) was assessed with MRI at 6 and 12 months. Statistical tests and machine learning algorithms were used to evaluate how well these prenatal and postnatal imaging markers predicted later autism spectrum disorder diagnosis.
journal: Journal of Population Therapeutics and Clinical Pharmacology
title: Prediction of Autism Antenatally via Fetal Ultrasound and Postnatally via MRI Studies
headline_result: Prediction accuracy for autism spectrum disorder was 70% using antenatal ultrasound alone, 85% using postnatal MRI alone, and 90% combining both.

model_name: Ex-stGCNN (explainable spatiotemporal connectivity-based Graph Convolutional Neural Network); also an Explainable Convolutional Variational Auto-Encoder
model_family: graph convolutional neural network with SHAP explainability; variational autoencoder
patient_population: 155 participants, age range 3-12 years and adults, watching a short animated film during fMRI
clinical_problem: decoding brain states (Theory of Mind/pain) and predicting individual task performance in early childhood development
model_description: Static and inter-subject functional connectivity matrices, derived from fMRI acquired while participants watched an animated film, are input. Ex-stGCNN, an explainable graph convolutional network, classifies brain states (Theory-of-Mind vs pain), and a separate explainable variational autoencoder predicts an individual's pass/fail/inconsistent performance on a subsequent false-belief task; SHAP is used to identify the most contributing brain regions.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Explainable Deep Learning Framework: Decoding Brain Task and Prediction of Individual Performance in False-Belief Task at Early Childhood Stage
headline_result: brain-state decoding accuracy 94% (inter-subject connectivity) / 85% (static connectivity), 92% average with five-fold cross-validation; false-belief performance prediction accuracy 90%

clinical_problem: AI applications in diagnosis, screening, and surgical treatment of developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH)
model_description: Narrative review of AI applications in DDH: AI combined with X-ray or ultrasound for diagnosis and mass screening, AI-assisted preoperative planning (bone-block position tracking, prosthesis sizing) for periacetabular osteotomy and total hip arthroplasty, and AI-driven 3D navigation/surgical robotics. Concludes that AI-based DDH screening is still in a preliminary stage, with limited work on conservative treatment, postoperative complications, and prognosis prediction.
title: The application progress of artificial intelligence technology in the diagnosis and treatment of developmental dysplasia of the hip

patient_population: pediatric low-grade glioma (pLGG) patients, treatment-naive, in discovery and replication cohorts
clinical_problem: prognostication (immunological profiling, progression-free survival, treatment response) in pediatric low-grade glioma
model_description: Treatment-naive multiparametric MRI, combined with RNA sequencing, is used to build a radiomic signature. The signature predicts immunological cluster membership (derived from XCell enrichment scores), and a combined clinicoradiomic model predicts progression-free survival and correlates with treatment response, to support early risk stratification in pediatric low-grade glioma.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Multiparametric MRI Along with Machine Learning Informs on Molecular Underpinnings, Prognosis, and Treatment Response in Pediatric Low-Grade Glioma
headline_result: radiomic signature balanced accuracy 81.5% (discovery) and 84.4% (replication); progression-free survival concordance index 0.71 and 0.77; clinicoradiomic score correlated with treatment response (p=0.001)

model_family: deep learning-based deformable/rigid slice-to-volume (D/SVR) reconstruction pipeline integrated with the Gadgetron scanner framework
patient_population: 12 prospectively acquired fetal MRI datasets (22-40 weeks gestational age) plus 83 retrospective 0.55T datasets
clinical_problem: real-time, scanner-based 3D reconstruction of motion-corrupted fetal MRI at ultra-low field
model_description: Motion-corrupted 2D T2-weighted single-shot Turbo Spin Echo stacks from a 0.55T low-field MRI scanner are input. An automated deformable/rigid slice-to-volume reconstruction pipeline (SVRTK), integrated into the scanner's Gadgetron workflow, outputs a super-resolved 3D reconstruction of fetal brain and body available on the scanner console during the ongoing scan.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Scanner-based real-time 3D brain+body slice-to-volume reconstruction for T2-weighted 0.55T low field fetal MRI
dataset_size: 12 prospective fetal datasets (22-40 weeks GA); 83 retrospective 0.55T datasets
headline_result: reconstructions available on average 6:42±3:13 minutes after acquisition of the final stack; image quality rated good to acceptable for interpretation; stable reconstruction quality on retrospective testing

clinical_problem: recognition of prenatal structural anomalies on ultrasound
model_description: Systematic clinical-engineering review of AI-based prenatal ultrasound anomaly screening, including multimodal data fusion with circulating biomarkers and explainable AI (XAI) approaches. Proposes a deep-learning-based explanatory framework that would chart anomaly-screening results from ultrasound video and link them to probable structural deformations, to increase clinician trust; no specific trained model's performance is reported.
title: Ultrasound imaging based recognition of prenatal anomalies: a systematic clinical engineering review

model_family: deep learning bone age prediction model
patient_population: children undergoing left-hand radiography, including Han and Tibetan children from plain and highland regions
clinical_problem: bone age assessment in children from different ethnicities and altitudes
model_description: EVG-BANet is a deep learning model that predicts bone age from a left-hand radiograph. It was trained on the public RSNA and RHPE bone-age datasets plus a self-established dataset of Han and Tibetan children from a plain-region and a highland-region hospital, then evaluated on an independent external test set of Tibetan children from a third hospital.
journal: Medical Journal of Peking Union Medical College Hospital
title: Construction and Validation of A Deep Learning-based Bone Age Prediction Model for Children Living in Both Plain and Highland Regions
study_design: retrospective multi-center diagnostic accuracy / external validation study
dataset_size: RSNA dataset (train 12,611/val 1,425/test 200), RHPE dataset (train 5,491/val 713/test 79), self-established dataset (train 825/test 351 from 1,176 children), external test 256 children
headline_result: Mean absolute difference from reference bone age ranged 0.34-0.53 years and accuracy within 1 year ranged 89.45%-97.72% across the RSNA, RHPE, self-established, and external test sets.

patient_population: pediatric patients with primary brain tumors imaged at King Abdullah Specialist Children's Hospital
clinical_problem: detection of primary brain tumors in children
model_description: MRI images of pediatric patients with primary brain tumors (glioma, primitive neuro-ectodermal tumor, pituitary tumor) and normal images were retrieved from the hospital's PACS. Machine learning algorithms, including an artificial neural network, were trained on 70% of the images and tested on the remaining 30% to classify and detect brain tumors.
journal: Journal of Radiation Research and Applied Sciences
title: The role of machine learning in detecting primary brain tumors in Saudi pediatric patients through MRI images
headline_result: The artificial neural network method accurately detected pediatric primary brain tumors, with results reported to match the radiologist's report (no single summary accuracy figure given).

model_name: GAUGE (Garbh-Ini Ultrasound image-based Gestational age Estimator)
model_family: deep learning image-based regression model with a conformal prediction algorithm for distribution-shift detection
patient_population: 2207 pregnant women in the Garbh-Ini cohort, North India, imaged at 18-32 weeks of pregnancy; external test set of 311 participants from a separate ultrasound lab in New Delhi
clinical_problem: estimation of gestational age in the second and third trimesters
model_description: Fetal head ultrasound images (rather than standard fetal biometry measurements) are input. A deep learning model, GAUGE, directly learns image features associated with gestational age and outputs a gestational age estimate; a conformal prediction algorithm flags and rejects images affected by data distribution shift.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published

clinical_problem: predicting postnatal mortality and pulmonary hypertension severity in congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH)

model_family: Optimized Pyramidal Convolution Shuffle Attention Neural Network

It is intended as a non-invasive alternative/adjunct to lumbar puncture for infant meningitis screening.

journal: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
title: Research status and progresses of imaging for musculoskeletal system diseases in children

patient_population: children with osteoarticular (bone and joint) disease
clinical_problem: AI-assisted diagnosis of pediatric bone and joint disease

journal: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
title: Research progresses of artificial intelligence in pediatric osteoarticular imaging

model_family: vision transformer (pretrained on ImageNet, fine-tuned) with age-fusion; convolutional network compared

title: Pediatric brain tumor classification using deep learning on MR-images with age fusion

clinical_problem: landscape of AI applications across pediatric radiology

release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Computer-Aided Reading of Chest Radiographs for Pediatric Tuberculosis: Current Status and Future Directions

model_family: YOLOv8-based segmentation model with post-processing fitting/counting algorithm

title: Artificial Intelligence for the Prenatal Ultrasound Diagnosis of Congenital Heart Disease: A Narrative Review

dataset_size: 657 adolescents, longitudinal with four yearly follow-ups

model_family: multi-task convolutional network jointly classifying placental location and segmenting the placenta, with a multi-view multi-probe acquisition and fusion pipeline
patient_population: fetal ultrasound with annotations from multiple raters, covering anterior and posterior placentas
clinical_problem: segmenting the placenta on fetal ultrasound, where appearance varies widely, image quality makes reference annotations unreliable, and at late gestation the placenta is larger than a single probe's field of view
model_description: Three distinct obstacles are each answered with a different mechanism, which is unusually disciplined. The multi-task design lets a large weakly labelled location dataset improve segmentation trained on little data. Multi-rater annotation variability is measured rather than assumed, and the model is judged against it - reaching human-level agreement. And the field-of-view limit is solved outside the network, by acquiring with three probes and fusing, which is the only way to see a whole late-gestation placenta.
title: Placenta segmentation in ultrasound imaging: Addressing sources of uncertainty and limited field-of-view.
headline_result: Dice 0.86 for anterior and 0.83 for posterior placentas, matching intra- and inter-observer variability, with whole-placenta segmentation from a fused three-probe acquisition

model_family: previously developed deep learning algorithm returning a malignancy likelihood and derived risk level
patient_population: 139 patients 21 years and younger (median age 17.5 years; 119 female) with a thyroid nodule on ultrasound between January 2004 and September 2020, with fine-needle aspiration or surgical pathology as reference
clinical_problem: deciding which thyroid nodules in children need fine-needle aspiration, currently judged by a radiologist's overall impression because the adult risk-stratification system was not built for children
model_description: A three-way comparison that shows the sensitivity-specificity trade being made rather than declaring a winner. Radiologists' gestalt is specific and insensitive (58% / 80%); ACR TI-RADS and the deep learning algorithm are both sensitive but far less specific, and the algorithm's 36% specificity is the lowest of the three. In a population where most nodules are benign and every false positive is a needle in a child's neck, that is the number that governs whether the tool is usable.
title: Thyroid Nodules on Ultrasound in Children and Young Adults: Comparison of Diagnostic Performance of Radiologists' Impressions, ACR TI-RADS, and a Deep Learning Algorithm.
study_design: retrospective diagnostic accuracy study with reader comparison
headline_result: deep learning sensitivity 87.5% with specificity 36.1%, versus ACR TI-RADS 85.1% / 50.6% and radiologists' overall impression 58.3% / 79.9%

patient_population: children undergoing MRI
clinical_problem: long MRI acquisition times in young children, which force sedation or produce non-diagnostic studies
model_description: A practical framework for accelerating pediatric MRI, written from the authors' own deployment experience: parallel imaging, single-shot acquisition, controlled aliasing, compressed sensing and AI-based reconstruction, combined with the right hardware and pulse sequences. The argument is stated in departmental terms — shorter scans mean less sedation, fewer motion artifacts, more throughput.
title: Pediatric magnetic resonance imaging: faster is better.

body_region: vascular malformations (extremity/soft tissue, region not further specified)

model_description: Radiomics features extracted from T1-weighted and fat-saturated T2-weighted MRI, selected via LASSO or Boruta methods, are used to train weighted logistic regression models that classify vascular malformations as fibro-adipose vascular anomaly versus common venous malformation.
title: Radiomics-based machine learning approach in differentiating fibro-adipose vascular anomaly from venous malformation.
study_design: retrospective diagnostic model development with repeated 10-fold cross-validation
dataset_size: 178 patients (41 fibro-adipose vascular anomaly, 137 venous malformation)
headline_result: AUC 97% (sensitivity 94-95%, specificity 87-89%) for the best multi-sequence models

title: Learning the Hidden Signature of Fetal Arch Anatomy: a Three-Dimensional Shape Analysis in Suspected Coarctation of the Aorta.
dataset_size: 112 fetuses with suspected coarctation of the aorta
headline_result: AUC 0.907 for coarctation-of-the-aorta shape risk score classification

patient_population: fetuses undergoing ultrasound, as covered by 153 primary studies published after 2017
clinical_problem: the state of deep learning across the whole of fetal ultrasound
model_description: A survey of 153 papers, sorted into standard-plane detection, anatomical structure analysis and biometry estimation, with the limitations and open problems named for each category and summary tables comparing approaches. It also collects the publicly available datasets and the performance metrics the field uses, and closes on why so little of this work has reached clinical practice.
title: A review on deep-learning algorithms for fetal ultrasound-image analysis.

clinical_problem: automatically measuring fetal volume/weight and indexed blood flow from MRI for clinical use
model_description: a trained neural network takes 3D fetal MRI as input and outputs automatic fetal segmentation used to compute fetal volume/weight and, with phase-contrast MRI, indexed blood flow
title: Automatic Segmentation of the Fetus in 3D Magnetic Resonance Images Using Deep Learning: Accurate and Fast Fetal Volume Quantification for Clinical Use.
headline_result: automatic vs. manual segmentation bias 4.5 +/- 351 mL (0.01% +/- 11%)

clinical_problem: using AI to quantify fluctuation of fetal brain activity via facial expression recognition on 4D ultrasound
model_description: an AI classifier takes 4D ultrasound video of the fetal face as input and outputs confidence scores for seven facial expression categories, analyzed over time

title: Artificial intelligence to understand fluctuation of fetal brain activity by recognizing facial expressions.

clinical_problem: Identify structural brain differences by sex and their changes over a two-year period in adolescents using deep learning on structural MRI

title: Prediction of gender from longitudinal MRI data via deep learning on adolescent data reveals unique patterns associated with brain structure and change over a two-year period.

clinical_problem: characterizing functional-connectivity differences in adolescent social phobia with and without ADHD comorbidity

headline_result: prediction accuracy significantly above chance rates (specific percentage not given)

journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
title: Use of artificial intelligence and deep learning in fetal ultrasound imaging.

clinical_problem: Automatically diagnosing infant developmental dysplasia of the hip from static ultrasound images, with a lightweight design for embedding in ultrasound machines
model_description: Input: static hip ultrasound images; output: alpha/beta angle measurements, femoral head coverage (FHC), percentage of femoral head diameter (PFD), and DDH diagnosis, via a lightweight automatic system (DDHnet) designed for embedding in ultrasound machines

headline_result: Outperforms state-of-the-art deep learning methods on 2D and 2.5D multi-label tasks (no single summary metric reported)

clinical_problem: automatically describing anatomy and modeling operator workflow from first-trimester obstetric ultrasound scans
model_description: Full-length first-trimester ultrasound scan videos are analyzed by a 2D+t (spatio-temporal) convolutional neural network with transfer learning that automatically partitions the video into semantically meaningful segments based on detected fetal anatomy, enabling analysis of operator clinical workflow, skill, and time spent on key tasks such as nuchal translucency measurement.

study_design: retrospective technical development and workflow-analysis study

model_family: neural network trained on structured semiquantitative radiologic reports rather than on binary labels
patient_population: 193 566 radiographs from 45 016 children and adults in the intensive care unit of a university hospital, January 2009 to December 2020, reported by 98 radiologists using a structured template; a 100-radiograph internal test set adjudicated by six radiologists
clinical_problem: reading the supine bedside chest radiograph, one of the most frequently ordered imaging studies in the world, in intensive care units where the person acting on it is often not a radiologist
model_description: Trained on twelve years of structured semiquantitative reports rather than on retrospectively assigned labels, so the network learns graded severity of cardiomegaly, congestion, effusion, opacity and atelectasis as radiologists actually record them. Two results stand out: it agreed with the six-radiologist consensus better than any individual radiologist did, and - the clinically operative finding - when it provided a preliminary reading, intensivists' own reports improved significantly. Nearly 200 000 radiographs including children.
title: Artificial Intelligence for Clinical Interpretation of Bedside Chest Radiographs.
study_design: retrospective model development with a multi-reader study
headline_result: kappa 0.86 against the expert-panel majority versus 0.81-0.84 for individual radiologists; non-radiologist physicians improved from kappa 0.79 unaided to 0.87 when given the network's preliminary reading (P < .001)

clinical_problem: predicting future onset of clinical anxiety in non-anxious adolescents

title: Anxiety onset in adolescents: a machine-learning prediction.
headline_result: AUC 0.68 for prospective prediction of pooled anxiety disorders

headline_result: Dice 0.931 (GM), 0.912 (WM), 0.961 (CSF); ranked first among 30 teams on the iSeg-2019 Grand Challenge validation set

title: Stacked ensemble learning based on deep convolutional neural networks for pediatric pneumonia diagnosis using chest X-ray images.
headline_result: Accuracy 98.3%, precision 99.29%, recall 98.36%, F1 98.83%, AUC 98.24%

clinical_problem: predicting individual differences in response inhibition (cognitive control) from multimodal neuroimaging in children
model_description: Multivariate machine learning models use multimodal region-of-interest neuroimaging features (task fMRI activation, cortical structure, diffusion tensor imaging) to predict individual stop-signal reaction time, a measure of response inhibition, in children.
title: Machine learning approaches linking brain function to behavior in the ABCD STOP task.
study_design: retrospective multi-site cohort machine-learning prediction study (ABCD)
headline_result: stop-signal-task fMRI activation explained 12% of variance in stop-signal reaction time

title: The uncovered biases and errors in clinical determination of bone age by using deep learning models.
headline_result: mean absolute deviation 0.42 years; kappa 0.714 agreement between AI and radiologists

clinical_problem: quantifying complex 3D fetal limb motion in utero from BOLD MRI to assess maternal, placental, and fetal factors affecting fetal movement as a potential biomarker of fetal health and neuromuscular development
model_description: 3D convolutional neural network previously trained to track fetal key points (wrists, elbows, shoulders, ankles, knees, hips) on BOLD MRI time series, used to quantify upper and lower limb kinematics and absolute movement time across gestation and under maternal hyperoxia
title: Cross-Sectional Observational Study of Typical in utero Fetal Movements Using Machine Learning.
dataset_size: 76 fetal MRI scan sets from 52 women
headline_result: significantly longer limb movement duration during maternal hyperoxia; centrifugal increase in movement across limbs; longer upper-extremity movement before 31 gestational weeks and lower-extremity movement after 35 gestational weeks

clinical_problem: Can deep learning automatically and accurately measure fetal intracranial and brain volumes across gestational age to create normative reference standards for detecting abnormal fetal brain volumes?
model_description: Takes 2D fetal brain MRI in axial, coronal, and sagittal planes as input; two sequential 3D U-Nets segment intracranial contents and then brain tissue, outputting volumetric measurements used to build gestational age-based normative reference curves.
title: Development of Gestational Age-Based Fetal Brain and Intracranial Volume Reference Norms Using Deep Learning.
dataset_size: 246 patients (training); 200 additional for norms; 9 pathologic cases for testing
headline_result: Median Dice 0.95 (intracranial), 0.90 (brain); Pearson r=0.996 vs. manual volumes; 8/9 pathologic cases flagged as >2 SD from normative mean

clinical_problem: Automatically classifying fetal movement from continuous fMRI to relate fetal motor behavior to brain network dynamics and postnatal motor outcomes.
model_description: A deep-learning model extracts the fetal brain from 4D fMRI time-series data, from which frame-wise displacement is calculated to classify periods of fetal movement.
title: Fetal behavior during MRI changes with age and relates to network dynamics.

title: Unsupervised machine learning using K-means identifies radiomic subgroups of pediatric low-grade gliomas that correlate with key molecular markers.
study_design: retrospective radiomics/unsupervised machine learning exploratory study
dataset_size: 157 patients with pediatric low-grade glioma; 881 radiomic features extracted
headline_result: three imaging-based subtypes differed in BRAF mutation frequency (p<0.05), age (p<0.05), tumor location (p<0.01) and histology (p<0.0001)

model_family: deep learning-based automated segmentation software (two commercial vendor suites: Medis Suite, SuiteHeart)
patient_population: 80 children (20 each: healthy, LV-CHD, tetralogy of Fallot, univentricular CHD), ages ~8.9-16.4 years

title: A generalizable connectome-based marker of in-scan sustained attention in neurodiverse youth.
study_design: multi-dataset cross-sectional and longitudinal cohort study
headline_result: Successful prediction of in-scan sustained attention performance in the primary sample; the attention network model generalized to predict attention in an independent neurotypical sample

title: A critical role of brain network architecture in a continuum model of autism spectrum disorders spanning from healthy individuals with genetic liability to individuals with ASD.

headline_result: structural connectome predicted polygenic risk for ASD, r=0.30, p<0.0001

model_description: Three AI-assisted bone age assessment methods (Greulich-Pyle, TW3-RUS, RUS-CHN) and three adult height prediction methods (CH05, TW3, Bayley-Pinneau) were compared against actual adult height in Chinese girls with early puberty using left-hand radiographs.
title: Combined assisted bone age assessment and adult height prediction methods in Chinese girls with early puberty: analysis of three artificial intelligence systems.

headline_result: TW3 predicted adult height within +/-5 cm in 92.9% of cases, overestimating by 0.4+/-2.8 cm; CH05 underestimated by 2.9+/-3.6 cm

title: Adolescent functional network connectivity prospectively predicts adult anxiety symptoms related to perceived COVID-19 economic adversity.

headline_result: Subgroup A showed greater increase in anxiety symptoms over time (β=0.138-0.194, p=0.023-0.042) and stronger adversity interaction (β=0.237-0.307, p=0.006-0.021)

patient_population: 6905 adolescents from 18 sites (ABCD Study)
clinical_problem: Predicting a general psychopathology risk factor (p-factor) in adolescents from resting-state functional MRI connectivity, while controlling for scanner-related variability
model_description: A scanner-generalization neural network is trained on resting-state functional connectivity from multi-site fMRI to predict an individual psychopathology (p-factor) score while reducing scanner-related confounding.
title: General psychopathology factor (p-factor) prediction using resting-state functional connectivity and a scanner-generalization neural network.
headline_result: correlation coefficient 0.163 (leave-one-site-out CV) vs. 0.150 (kernel ridge regression baseline)

clinical_problem: noninvasively diagnosing liver fibrosis in children with pancreaticobiliary maljunction to guide preoperative decision-making
model_description: A radiomics-clinical nomogram combining MRI radiomic features from segmented liver parenchyma with clinical factors noninvasively diagnoses liver fibrosis in children with pancreaticobiliary maljunction, validated against histopathology.

title: Development of an MRI-Based Radiomics-Clinical Model to Diagnose Liver Fibrosis Secondary to Pancreaticobiliary Maljunction in Children.
dataset_size: 136 children (111 center A: 74 training/37 internal validation; 25 center B external validation)
headline_result: combined nomogram AUC 0.977 (training), 0.921 (internal validation), 0.878 (external validation)

model_family: deep learning autocontouring + automated treatment planning tool
patient_population: 143 pediatric medulloblastoma CT scans (ages 2-19) for autocontour model training; 6 patients (ages 3-10) tested per planning approach
clinical_problem: Can craniospinal radiotherapy treatment planning for pediatric medulloblastoma be automated, to make this complex, time-consuming plan feasible in resource-constrained (low- and middle-income country) settings?
model_description: A deep learning model generates autocontours of relevant anatomy from pediatric medulloblastoma CT scans, feeding an autoplanning tool that automatically generates 3D-conformal craniospinal irradiation treatment plans, assessed for clinical acceptability by a radiation oncologist.

headline_result: Autocontour Dice similarity coefficient 0.65-0.98; all 18 tested plans scored clinically acceptable as-is or with minor edits; average planning time 3.5 +/- 0.4 minutes

model_family: three models - an image model on standard biometry planes, a video model on fly-to videos, and an ensemble of the two
patient_population: the Fetal Age Machine Learning Initiative cohort of 3842 participants across Chapel Hill, North Carolina and Lusaka, Zambia, with a test set of 404 participants
clinical_problem: estimating gestational age, where derivation from manual head, abdomen and femur measurements is operator dependent and slow
model_description: The novel input is the fly-to video - the five to ten seconds of sweeping that a machine can record automatically before the sonographer freezes the frame, normally discarded. Using it costs the operator nothing and gives the model the search as well as the destination. Two sites on two continents, and the model beat expert-acquired biometry overall and by a wider margin on fetuses predicted to be small, which is where dating errors do the most harm.
title: Development of a Machine Learning Model for Sonographic Assessment of Gestational Age.
headline_result: the ensemble model's mean absolute error was 1.51 days lower than clinical standard biometry (95% CI -1.90 to -1.10 days), with all three models statistically superior to expert-acquired biometry

model_family: multivariate machine learning decoding (within- and between-format)

clinical_problem: decoding cortical representations of numerals and nonsymbolic quantity in children
model_description: Multivariate fMRI adaptation data are combined with within- and between-format machine learning decoding to probe cortical representations of Arabic numerals and approximate nonsymbolic quantity in 89 children aged 5 or 8 years. The decoding approach tests whether the same neural code represents numerals and nonsymbolic quantities, finding a format-independent representation in right parietal cortex only in 5-year-olds.
title: Cortical representations of numbers and nonsymbolic quantities expand and segregate in children from 5 to 8 years of age.
headline_result: Format-independent neural representation of quantity found in right parietal cortex, present only in 5-year-olds

patient_population: 152 (training, Hospital A) + 64 (validation, Hospital B) high-risk PAS patients
clinical_problem: predicting massive intraoperative blood loss in high-risk placenta accreta spectrum before delivery, using prenatal MRI
model_description: Takes radiomics features extracted from sagittal T2-weighted prenatal MRI of the placenta plus clinical features as input, and outputs a nomogram-based prediction of massive intraoperative blood loss during delivery in patients with placenta accreta spectrum.
title: MRI-based radiomics nomogram in patients with high-risk placenta accreta spectrum: can it aid in the prenatal diagnosis of intraoperative blood loss?
study_design: retrospective multicenter radiomics nomogram development study
headline_result: Nomogram AUC 0.866 (training), 0.876 (validation)

model_family: deep learning segmentation trained on noisy multi-atlas labels, with a novel label smoothing procedure and loss function
patient_population: 272 training images covering 19-39 gestational weeks segmented automatically and manually corrected, with 23 manually segmented test images from a separate set of fetuses
clinical_problem: multi-label fetal brain tissue segmentation across gestation, where the transient structures change so fast that a model needs many training images and manual multi-label segmentation of that many 3D volumes is prohibitive
model_description: Trades label quality for label quantity deliberately, then handles the consequence: 272 volumes are segmented by multi-atlas registration with only the large errors fixed by hand, and a smoothing procedure plus a matched loss teaches the network to treat tissue boundaries as uncertain rather than trusting them. Testing on separately, manually segmented fetuses keeps the evaluation clean of the noisy labels. Beat nnU-Net, which is the standard that matters in segmentation.
title: Learning to segment fetal brain tissue from noisy annotations.
dataset_size: 272 training and 23 manually segmented test images
headline_result: average Dice 0.893 for younger and 0.916 for older fetuses on transient structures, significantly more accurate than several state-of-the-art methods including nnU-Net

title: Radiomics based of deep medullary veins on susceptibility-weighted imaging in infants: predicting the severity of brain injury of neonates with perinatal asphyxia.

title: 18F-FDG PET/CT imaging of pediatric peripheral neuroblastic tumor: a combined model to predict the International Neuroblastoma Pathology Classification.

model_family: LASSO feature selection with a machine learning classifier

Blinded external validation against first-trimester-confirmed dates is the right standard and rarely met in this literature.
