model_description: Takes T1/T2/diffusion-weighted MRI-derived injury features (e.g., putamen/globus pallidus injury) plus clinical variables (gestational age, cord pH) as input; a gradient-boosted deep learning model outputs a prediction of adverse motor outcome at 12-24 months.
title: Deep Learning to Optimize Magnetic Resonance Imaging Prediction of Motor Outcomes After Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy.
headline_result: Three-feature DL model: 85% accuracy, AUC 0.75, outperforming logistic regression (AUC 0.69)

patient_population: 8,736 consecutive patients (median age 8 months) at six hospitals; 242 volunteers in a prospective pilot
clinical_problem: diagnosis and severity assessment of ileocolic intussusception in children on ultrasound
model_description: Input: real-time abdominal ultrasound video/images; output: real-time visualization of intussusception lesion signs and classification of disease severity (nonsurgical vs surgical), assisting sonographers of varying experience.
title: A deep-learning pipeline to diagnose pediatric intussusception and assess severity during ultrasound scanning: a multicenter retrospective-prospective study.
headline_result: average-AUC 0.972 (image) and 0.956 (video); junior sonographer+AI AUC 0.966 vs 0.857 without AI (p<0.001), comparable to senior sonographers

patient_population: 1069 ADHD patients (ABCD study) plus independent longitudinal validation cohort of 130 adolescents
clinical_problem: identifying neuroimaging-based ADHD biotypes to guide personalized medication choice in children/adolescents
model_description: Takes resting-state fMRI-derived functional network connectivity as input to a graph convolutional network plus deep clustering algorithm, outputting ADHD neuroimaging biotypes associated with differential response to methylphenidate versus atomoxetine.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Functional Imaging Derived ADHD Biotypes Based on Deep Clustering May Guide Personalized Medication Therapy.
headline_result: Biotype 1 (methylphenidate) showed significantly better recovery than biotype 2 (atomoxetine), p<0.05 FDR corrected

patient_population: 710 patients (0-3 years) for training/internal validation; internal test n=123; external tests n=226 (0-25 months) and n=383 (0-2 months)
clinical_problem: Automatically estimating myelin maturation age from brain MRI in infants and young children to reduce radiologist interpretation time and variability
model_description: Input: brain MRI in children aged 0-3 years; output: predicted myelin maturation age, via an ensemble of 2D and 3D convolutional neural networks trained on radiologist-generated labels
title: Development and Evaluation of Deep Learning Models for Automated Estimation of Myelin Maturation Using Pediatric Brain MRI Scans.
study_design: retrospective model development with external validation
headline_result: MAE 1.77 months (internal test, 2D+3D ensemble); outperformed prior state-of-the-art (MAE 1.22 vs. 2.09 months on external test)

model_family: support vector machine on radiomics features
patient_population: 101 children with cervical suppurative (n=52) or tuberculous (n=49) lymphadenitis
clinical_problem: differentiating suppurative from tuberculous cervical lymphadenitis with nodal necrosis
model_description: Input is contrast-enhanced neck CT of children with cervical lymphadenitis; radiomics features are extracted from segmented lymph nodes after dimension reduction and feature selection, and a support vector machine classifier outputs suppurative vs. tuberculous classification, compared against visual CT feature analysis by radiologists.
title: Observer- and radiomics model-based computed tomography classification of suppurative versus tuberculous lymphadenitis complicated with nodal necrosis of the neck in children.
headline_result: SVM radiomics model: AUC 0.89 (95% CI 0.72-1.00), accuracy 0.88, sensitivity 0.78, specificity 0.90 in the test set

model_family: deep learning (semantic segmentation and landmark localization)
patient_population: 2,372 normal fetuses and 37 with abnormalities (18 trisomy 21, 7 trisomy 18, 12 cleft lip/palate) at 11-13+6 weeks gestation
clinical_problem: Can an AI model automatically measure fetal facial profile markers on first-trimester ultrasound to screen for trisomy 21, trisomy 18, and cleft lip/palate?
model_description: Takes 2D mid-sagittal fetal facial profile ultrasound images as input; a semantic segmentation and landmark localization model outputs automated measurements of facial angle and distance markers used to screen for fetal abnormalities.
title: A novel artificial intelligence model for fetal facial profile marker measurement during the first trimester.
dataset_size: 2,409 fetuses total (1,872 for training; 500 normal + 37 abnormal for testing)
headline_result: FMA AUC 0.904 for trisomy 18; IFA AUC 0.729 for trisomy 18 and 0.686 for trisomy 21

patient_population: 900 routine fetal ultrasound examinations (800 for training, 100 pregnant women 16-38 weeks for prospective test)
clinical_problem: estimating fetal weight directly from ultrasound without performing full standard biometry measurements
model_description: Takes a video scan of the fetal abdomen and gestational age as input and outputs a direct estimate of fetal weight, without requiring standard head/abdomen/femur biometry measurements, using a deep learning model.
journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
title: Deep learning for estimation of fetal weight throughout the pregnancy from fetal abdominal ultrasound.
study_design: retrospective model development with prospectively acquired external test set
dataset_size: 900 ultrasound examinations (800 for training, 100 for prospective external test)
headline_result: mean absolute percentage error 3.75%±2.00% vs. 6 human readers; 2.59%±1.11% vs. 4 expert readers; ICC 0.9761-0.9865

model_name: PAICS (Prenatal Ultrasound Diagnosis Artificial Intelligence Conduct System)
patient_population: 709 fetal neurosonographic images/videos read by 36 sonologists of varying expertise
clinical_problem: detecting fetal intracranial malformations on prenatal neurosonography
model_description: Takes fetal neurosonographic images and videos as input and outputs AI-assisted detection of intracranial malformations, used to assist sonologists concurrently or as a second read, compared to unassisted interpretation.
title: Deep learning system improved detection efficacy of fetal intracranial malformations in a randomized controlled trial.
headline_result: accuracy 73% unassisted vs. 80% concurrent-AI vs. 82% second-read AI (P<0.001); AUC 0.85 to 0.89 to 0.90

model_family: machine learning classifier using T1-weighted and diffusion tensor imaging features
patient_population: IMAGEN dataset adolescents, n=555 (52.61% female), no binge-drinking experience at baseline age 14
clinical_problem: predicting future binge-drinking risk from adolescent brain structure
model_description: A machine learning model uses T1-weighted structural and diffusion tensor MRI features acquired at age 14 to predict future (age 22) binge-drinking behavior; counterbalancing with oversampling tests which psychometric variables explain the prediction.
title: Uncontrolled eating and sensation-seeking partially explain the prediction of future binge drinking from adolescent brain structure.
study_design: prospective longitudinal multi-site cohort machine-learning prediction study (IMAGEN)
headline_result: prediction accuracy above 70%; sensation-seeking and uncontrolled eating each explained ~14% of prediction accuracy

patient_population: pediatric neuro-oncology patients (review)
clinical_problem: integration of radiomic and pathomic AI models to guide precision medicine in pediatric brain tumors
model_description: Narrative review of AI models integrating radiomic (imaging) and pathomic (histologic) data for predictive modeling in pediatric brain tumors, discussing challenges in multi-modal, multi-institutional data aggregation.
title: Radio-pathomic approaches in pediatric neuro-oncology: Opportunities and challenges.

model_family: hybrid convolutional neural network (trained on synthetic data)
patient_population: preterm infants at risk of hypoxic-ischemic brain injury (phantom-based evaluation)
clinical_problem: image reconstruction for near-infrared optical tomography to detect low brain oxygenation in preterm infants
model_description: Input is near-infrared optical tomography (NIROT) measurement data; a hybrid CNN trained on synthetic in-silico data reconstructs tomographic brain images, with generalization tested on phantoms with more varied surface geometry, inclusion shapes and detector arrangements than the training data.
journal: Advances in experimental medicine and biology
title: Image Reconstruction Using Deep Learning for Near-Infrared Optical Tomography: Generalization Assessment.
dataset_size: phantom measurements (synthetic training data, no patient count stated)
headline_result: Substantial gains in reconstruction speed, localization accuracy and image quality even under varied measurement conditions (no single quantitative figure given)

model_family: machine learning (various, including CNN for CT and photograph classification)
patient_population: children with craniosynostosis (reviewed literature)
clinical_problem: How can AI assist in diagnosing craniosynostosis subtypes, planning cranial vault remodeling surgery, and predicting outcomes, potentially reducing the need for CT scanning?
model_description: Narrative review of machine learning models that classify craniosynostosis subtypes from photographs or CT scans, and AI-assisted virtual surgical planning tools for cranial vault remodeling.
title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Diagnosing and Managing Non-syndromic Craniosynostosis: A Comprehensive Review.

model_family: deep segmentation network with machine learning biometry pipeline
patient_population: 268 MRI volumes (5,360 images) from normal fetuses
clinical_problem: automating linear biometric measurements of the fetal brain on MRI
model_description: Fetal brain MRI is segmented by a deep network into cerebrum, cerebellum, and left/right lateral ventricles; the measurement plane is then automatically determined and biometric parameters (biparietal diameter, transverse cerebellar diameter, atrial diameters) are calculated per clinical guidelines and compared to manual measurements.
title: Automatic biometry of fetal brain MRIs using deep and machine learning techniques.
study_design: retrospective single-center technical development and agreement study
headline_result: correlation coefficients: CBPD 0.977, TCD 0.990, LAD 0.817, RAD 0.719

model_family: support vector machine, K-nearest neighbors, ensemble
patient_population: 79 adolescents with suicide risk, 79 matched typically developing adolescents
clinical_problem: identifying structural brain differences that distinguish adolescents at suicide risk from typically developing adolescents
model_description: Machine learning classifiers (SVM, K-nearest neighbors, ensemble) use region-specific cortical/subcortical volumes from structural MRI to classify adolescents as at suicide risk versus typically developing.
title: Machine learning based identification of structural brain alterations underlying suicide risk in adolescents.
headline_result: accuracy 74.79%, sensitivity 75.90%, specificity 74.07%, AUC 87.18% (SVM classifier)

model_family: deep convolutional network fine-tuned by transfer learning
patient_population: fetal ultrasound images from two datasets from different regions, recorded on different machines
clinical_problem: identifying which fetal organ an ultrasound image shows - brain, abdomen, femur, thorax, or the maternal cervix - which depends on fetal position, maternal habitus and technique and needs a trained interpreter
model_description: Standard architecture on a standard task; the design choice worth noting is training across two regional datasets acquired on different machines, which is what the near-perfect test accuracy has to be read against. Accuracy of 99.84% on a five-class organ recognition problem suggests the classes are well separated rather than that the problem is solved clinically - organ recognition is the easy half of what a screening scan requires.
title: Transfer learning for accurate fetal organ classification from ultrasound images: a potential tool for maternal healthcare providers.
dataset_size: two regional datasets, sizes not stated
headline_result: accuracy 99.84%, F1 99.84% and AUC 98.95% on the held-out test set

patient_population: 1,678 radiographs from 866 children (training/validation); 150 radiographs and final height data for 100 adults (test set simulation)
clinical_problem: automatically estimating bone age and predicting final adult height in children using hand radiographs
model_description: A CNN-based deep learning program estimates bone age from hand radiographs and predicts final adult height in Korean children and adolescents.
title: Bone Age Estimation and Prediction of Final Adult Height Using Deep Learning.
study_design: retrospective model development and validation study
headline_result: bone age mean absolute error 0.59 years, RMSE 0.55 years, correlation r=0.99; final height prediction MAE 4.62 cm

patient_population: 41 female pediatric patients (21 adnexal torsion, 20 acute appendicitis), mean age ~10 years
clinical_problem: distinguishing pediatric adnexal torsion from acute appendicitis using clinical presentation and ultrasound findings
model_description: Takes clinical presentation, pain duration, white blood cell counts, and ultrasound findings as input features to a support vector machine classifier, outputting a prediction distinguishing adnexal torsion from acute appendicitis.
title: Enhancing Pediatric Adnexal Torsion Diagnosis: Prediction Method Utilizing Machine Learning Techniques.
headline_result: Predictive accuracy 87-97% across SVM kernel models

model_family: convolutional neural network with convolutional, pooling, batch normalization, dropout and fully connected layers, applied to 2D echo planar samples
patient_population: 22 176 two-dimensional echo planar samples from 126 subjects (56 with autism, 70 controls) from the ABIDE I repository, with 17 740 samples used for training
clinical_problem: early detection of autism spectrum disorder in children, where prompt diagnosis enables targeted intervention
model_description: Reports accuracy above 99% on ABIDE data, far above what other groups obtain from the same repository - and the likely reason is visible in the numbers: 22 176 slice samples come from only 126 subjects, so slices from the same brain can appear in both training and test unless the split is at subject level, which the abstract does not state. Recorded here as a pediatric imaging model, with that caveat attached to the headline figure.
title: Detection of ASD Children through Deep-Learning Application of fMRI.
study_design: retrospective model development on a public dataset
headline_result: reported accuracy 99.39%, recall 98.80%, precision 99.85% and F1 99.32% on ABIDE I

model_family: AI classifier (unspecified type, three models compared)
patient_population: fetuses of women with well-controlled diabetes vs healthy controls
clinical_problem: assess impact of maternal diabetes on fetal subcutaneous fat mass, independent of growth, using 3D ultrasound and AI classification
model_description: Three artificial intelligence classifier models trained on 3D ultrasound-derived fetal subcutaneous fat measurements combined with gestational age, fetal weight, abdominal circumference, and maternal BMI to detect impact of maternal diabetes on fetal fat mass.
title: AI-Enhanced Analysis Reveals Impact of Maternal Diabetes on Subcutaneous Fat Mass in Fetuses without Growth Alterations.
study_design: retrospective/prospective cohort study with AI classifier development and validation
headline_result: detection rate 70% at 10% false positive rate, PPV 82%

model_family: graph convolutional neural network (deep learning) with a custom loss function
patient_population: children longitudinally scanned at 1, 2, 4, and 6 years of age (N=360), compared with adults (N=89)
age_groups: infant; child; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: predicting functional brain connectivity from structural connectivity in early childhood
model_description: A graph convolutional neural network with a novel loss function is trained to predict an individual's functional brain connectivity from their structural (white matter) connectivity, using longitudinal MRI from children scanned at ages 1, 2, 4 and 6 and a comparison adult sample. It improved on existing models at predicting functional connectivity from structural data.
title: Structural and functional connectome relationships in early childhood.
headline_result: Deep learning model improved prediction of individual functional connectivity from structural connectivity compared to existing models

patient_population: not stated (editorial, no abstract)
clinical_problem: development of a Korean-population-specific standard bone age model
model_description: Editorial framing the development of a new Korean standard bone age model as an example paradigm for AI-powered pediatric imaging. No abstract text was provided describing the underlying model or results.
title: Development of a New Korean Standard Bone Age Model: A Paradigm for AI-Powered Pediatric Imaging.

model_family: convolutional neural network trained on chronological age as the label, compared against a commercial Greulich-Pyle-trained model
patient_population: 21 036 hand radiographs of Korean children and adolescents without bone-development-affecting conditions obtained 1998-2019 (median age 9 years), with two external test sets of 343 and 321 healthy Korean children
clinical_problem: whether bone age in a given population should be predicted against the Greulich-Pyle atlas or learned directly from the chronological ages of healthy children in that population
model_description: A direct head-to-head on the question the bone age literature keeps circling: population-specific chronological age labels against the mid-century American atlas, tested at two independent institutions. The locally trained model won on every metric at both sites. That is an argument for retraining rather than importing bone age models, and a caution about deploying an atlas-based commercial product outside the population it encodes - though the comparison is in healthy children, not the children a bone age is usually ordered for.
release_evidence: compared against VUNO Med-BoneAge version 1.1, a commercial Greulich-Pyle-based model
title: Bone Age Assessment Using Artificial Intelligence in Korean Pediatric Population: A Comparison of Deep-Learning Models Trained With Healthy Chronological and Greulich-Pyle Ages as Labels.
study_design: retrospective model development with external validation
dataset_size: 21 036 training radiographs; 664 external test cases at two institutions
headline_result: RMSE 11.2 versus 13.8 months (P = 0.004) and mean absolute error 8.2 versus 10.5 months (P = 0.002) against the commercial Greulich-Pyle model at institution 1, with similar advantages at institution 2

model_family: deep learning (supervised and semi-supervised segmentation networks)
patient_population: 99 patients with various types of congenital heart disease
clinical_problem: Can automated deep learning segmentation of 3D cine cardiac MRI accurately delineate heart chambers and great vessels in patients with congenital heart disease to streamline volumetric analysis?
model_description: Takes 3D cine cardiac MRI as input; supervised and semi-supervised deep learning models output whole-heart segmentation of atria, ventricles, aorta, pulmonary arteries, and venae cavae, used to compute chamber volumes.
title: Automated segmentation of 3D cine cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging.
headline_result: Semi-supervised method Dice 83.23+/-16.76% vs. supervised 77.98+/-19.64% (P<=0.001); volume bias <=5.2 mL vs. <=10.1 mL

patient_population: Adolescent patients with congenital heart disease
clinical_problem: Predicting executive-function outcomes (cognitive flexibility, working memory, inhibition) in adolescents with congenital heart disease from brain MRI/DTI and clinical variables
model_description: Random forest regression models that take clinical, perioperative, diffusion MRI (white-matter tract) and structural MRI volumetric features as input and predict subdomains of executive function (mental flexibility, working memory, inhibition).
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
title: Cerebral Spinal Fluid Volumetrics and Paralimbic Predictors of Executive Dysfunction in Congenital Heart Disease: A Machine Learning Approach Informing Mechanistic Insights.

body_region: fetal (head, abdomen, femur) and amniotic fluid
patient_population: 172,293 Moroccan fetal ultrasound images for training; prospective test on 172 pregnant people at four healthcare centers
clinical_problem: automating fetal biometry and amniotic fluid volume measurement during prenatal ultrasound screening
model_description: Takes fetal ultrasound video clips as input and outputs automated fetal biometry measurements (head, abdomen, femur) and amniotic fluid volume, using deep learning models trained end-to-end.
title: Fetal biometry and amniotic fluid volume assessment end-to-end automation using Deep Learning.
study_design: retrospective model development with prospective multi-center external validation
dataset_size: 172,293 training images; prospective test set of 172 pregnant people (four centers)
headline_result: 95% limits of agreement narrower than reported inter- and intra-observer variability among expert sonographers for all parameters

patient_population: 1009-1111 pediatric CT localizers (training), 116-127 (validation), 203-225 (test); plus adult cohort added to training
clinical_problem: estimating patient body height and weight from CT localizer (scout) images in pediatric patients
model_description: Takes CT localizer (scout) images as input and outputs predicted body height and weight using convolutional neural networks (EfficientNetV2-S, ResNet variants).
title: Determining body height and weight from thoracic and abdominal CT localizers in pediatric and young adult patients using deep learning.
study_design: retrospective single-center model development with temporal validation
headline_result: MAE 5.58 cm (height), 4.25 kg (weight) in independent test cohort

model_family: transformer (Residual Transformer Module with Dynamic Affine Feature Map Transform)
patient_population: 194 patients; 582 2D fetal ultrasound videos acquired less than 24 hours before delivery
clinical_problem: Can automated analysis of fetal ultrasound video combined with clinical data accurately predict birth weight shortly before delivery to guide delivery timing and mode?
model_description: Takes fetal ultrasound video scans (2D+t) and tabular clinical data as input; a transformer-based model outputs a predicted fetal birth weight.
title: BabyNet＋＋: Fetal birth weight prediction using biometry multimodal data acquired less than 24 hours before delivery.
study_design: development and evaluation study on a clinical dataset
headline_result: Prediction accuracy comparable to human experts, outperforming state-of-the-art automatic methods

patient_population: 90 patients ages 0-8 years (592 images)
clinical_problem: Distinguishing high-grade from low-grade hydronephrosis in children using ultrasound
model_description: A radiomic-based algorithm combining computerized texture analysis with a support vector machine classifier is trained on renal ultrasound images to grade hydronephrosis severity as high or low.
title: Pilot study of machine learning in the task of distinguishing high and low-grade pediatric hydronephrosis on ultrasound.
headline_result: AUC 0.86

patient_population: not applicable (review)
clinical_problem: Which deep learning architectures, especially vision and brain transformers, are best suited to diagnosing autism spectrum disorder from MRI, and what biomarkers do they rely on?
model_description: Comprehensive review of brain and vision transformer models (e.g., ViT, Swin, METAFormer, BolT, BrainFormer) applied to MRI-based autism spectrum disorder diagnosis and classification in children, covering CNN- and transformer-based architectures and recommending a systematic transformer-based diagnostic architecture.
title: Do it the transformer way: A comprehensive review of brain and vision transformers for autism spectrum disorder diagnosis and classification.

patient_population: 198 adolescents and young adults with major depressive episode
clinical_problem: predicting treatment response in major depressive episode
model_description: Baseline resting-state functional connectivity from fMRI is fed into a Graph Isomorphism Network, a deep learning model, to predict whether an individual adolescent or young adult with a major depressive episode will respond to treatment. The most discriminating regions were in paralimbic and subcortical brain areas.
title: Predicting treatment response in adolescents and young adults with major depressive episodes from fMRI using graph isomorphism network.
headline_result: Predicted 79.8% of responders and 67.4% of non-responders (overall accuracy 74.24%)

patient_population: 23,876 brain MRIs of healthy subjects ages 4-35, plus validation in children with brain tumors
age_groups: child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: Automated measurement of temporalis muscle thickness (a marker of lean muscle mass) on brain MRI to generate normal growth charts from childhood through adulthood.
model_description: An automated deep learning pipeline measures temporalis muscle thickness (iTMT) on routine brain MRI, generating sex-specific normal growth charts with percentiles across ages 4-35.
title: Automated temporalis muscle quantification and growth charts for children through adulthood.
study_design: retrospective cohort study with automated deep learning pipeline and multi-group validation

patient_population: Children with neuroblastoma (narrative review, no specific cohort)
clinical_problem: Reviewing how radiomics and deep learning can improve diagnosis and prognosis of pediatric neuroblastoma using CT, MRI, and PET imaging
model_description: Narrative review summarizing radiomics feature extraction and deep learning approaches applied to CT, MRI, and PET imaging for neuroblastoma diagnosis and prognosis
title: A narrative review of radiomics and deep learning advances in neuroblastoma: updates and challenges.

patient_population: adolescents from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study (N=3760, minimum age 12) and the NCANDA adolescent cohort (N=540)
clinical_problem: imputing missing structural brain MRI measurements across datasets
model_description: A graph neural network models dependencies between structural MRI regions-of-interest measurements and predicts values missing from one public dataset (ABCD) using a model trained on a related dataset (NCANDA) that shares some of the same measurements. It also accounts for demographic differences such as sex, and the imputed measurements improved downstream sex-classification accuracy.
title: Imputing Brain Measurements Across Data Sets via Graph Neural Networks.
headline_result: 5-fold cross-validation on NCANDA showed imputed scores more accurate than linear regression and other deep learning models; improved sex-classification accuracy when added as features

patient_population: 78 normal pregnancies, gestational ages 15+5 to 38+4 weeks
clinical_problem: Can a combined diffusion-relaxation MRI and unsupervised machine learning pipeline non-invasively characterize distinct placental microenvironments across pregnancy, to develop imaging biomarkers for pregnancy complications?
model_description: Takes combined T2*-diffusion MRI placental scans as input; unsupervised machine learning (InSpect) identifies and maps seven distinct placental microenvironments reflecting oxygenation, microstructure, and microcirculation.
title: Non-invasive mapping of human placenta microenvironments throughout pregnancy with diffusion-relaxation MRI.
study_design: prospective single-center cohort study, methods development
headline_result: Identified seven distinct placental microenvironments with trends across gestation (no single accuracy/AUC reported)

model_family: multiple ML models (LASSO, radial basis function network, multilayer perceptron, gradient-boosted decision tree; LASSO best)
patient_population: 59 Japanese children (27 boys, 32 girls) without prior orthodontic treatment, ages 6-12 at baseline
clinical_problem: predicting longitudinal craniofacial growth from earlier cephalometric radiographs in children, for orthodontic treatment planning
model_description: Input: coordinated skeletal landmark, linear, and angular parameters from lateral cephalometric radiographs (ages 6-12); output: predicted values of the same parameters at age 13.
title: Validation of Machine Learning Models for Craniofacial Growth Prediction.
study_design: retrospective longitudinal model development and validation
headline_result: Best model (LASSO): prediction accuracy up to 97.87% (linear parameters) and 94.45% (angular parameters) at age 13

clinical_problem: Distinguishing MOGAD from other idiopathic inflammatory demyelinating disease in children using multiparameter MRI radiomics
model_description: Radiomics models built from T1WI, T2WI, and FLAIR features of brain demyelinating lesions (individually and combined) to classify pediatric patients as MOGAD versus non-MOGAD, compared against a clinical logistic-regression model.
title: Diagnostic Value of Multiparameter MRI-Based Radiomics in Pediatric Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disorders.

headline_result: Compound radiomics model AUC 0.989 (training), 0.905 (testing)

patient_population: children presenting with wrist trauma (public GRAZPEDWRI-DX pediatric wrist radiograph dataset)
clinical_problem: detecting wrist fractures on trauma radiographs
model_description: Pediatric wrist trauma radiographs go in; a YOLOv8 object-detection model outputs bounding boxes localizing fractures.
title: Fracture detection in pediatric wrist trauma X-ray images using YOLOv8 algorithm.
study_design: retrospective model development using a public dataset, with an accompanying application prototype
dataset_size: GRAZPEDWRI-DX public pediatric wrist radiograph dataset
headline_result: mAP50 0.638, higher than improved YOLOv7 (0.634) and original YOLOv8 (0.636)

model_family: instance segmentation + keypoint detection deep learning pipeline
patient_population: infants undergoing pelvic X-ray for DDH screening
clinical_problem: assessment of acetabular index angle for developmental dysplasia of the hip diagnosis in infants
model_description: Input: pelvic X-ray images of infants; output: automated acetabular index angle measurement via a two-stage instance-segmentation and keypoint-detection pipeline, intended for integration into a mobile application.
title: Assessing Acetabular Index Angle in Infants: A Deep Learning-Based Novel Approach.
headline_result: average pixel error 2.862±2.392; angle error 2.402±1.963 degrees

clinical_problem: Reviewing machine learning methods (classification, detection, segmentation) applied to fetal ultrasound images for anomaly detection.
model_description: Review of recent machine learning approaches for fetal ultrasound anomaly detection, covering classification, object recognition, and segmentation tasks.
title: Enhancing Fetal Anomaly Detection in Ultrasonography Images: A Review of Machine Learning-Based Approaches.

model_family: radiomics with decision tree, logistic regression and support vector machine (nomogram)

clinical_problem: predicting MYCN amplification status in pediatric neuroblastoma noninvasively using 18F-FDG PET/CT
model_description: Input: 18F-FDG PET/CT images plus clinical and radiological features; output: a clinical-radiological-radiomics nomogram predicting MYCN amplification status.
title: Predicting MYCN amplification in paediatric neuroblastoma: development and validation of a 18F-FDG PET/CT-based radiomics signature.
headline_result: Clinical-radiological-radiomics model AUC 0.860 (training), 0.824 (validation)

patient_population: 87 pediatric neuroblastoma patients with genetic testing
clinical_problem: noninvasively predict segmental chromosomal aberrations (1p36, 11q23) in pediatric neuroblastoma using CT radiomics
model_description: Radiomics features extracted from 3-phase contrast CT, selected via LASSO regression, are used to compute a radiomics score predicting segmental chromosomal aberration status (1p36 and 11q23) in pediatric neuroblastoma.
title: Computed Tomography-Based Radiomics Signature for Predicting Segmental Chromosomal Aberrations at 1p36 and 11q23 in Pediatric Neuroblastoma.

headline_result: AUC 0.869 (training), 0.883 (test)

clinical_problem: Preoperatively stratifying risk (low/intermediate/high) in pediatric malignant peripheral neuroblastic tumors from CT
model_description: A radiomics model using LASSO-selected features from manually segmented tumors on preoperative CT to classify tumors into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups, compared to an image-defined risk-factor model.
title: Computed tomography-based radiomics to assess risk stratification in pediatric malignant peripheral neuroblastic tumors.

clinical_problem: bias and generalizability of AI algorithms for pediatric brain tumor classification and prognosis

clinical_problem: prediction of pediatric limb fracture healing time

title: Paediatric orthopaedic expert system.

clinical_problem: Provides annotated fetal head ultrasound images (brain, cavum septum pellucidum, lateral ventricles) as training/validation data to support development of AI algorithms for prenatal biometry
model_description: A public dataset of 3832 annotated fetal head ultrasound images, labeled for brain, cavum septum pellucidum, and lateral ventricle structures, released in 11 annotation formats to support computer vision algorithm development.
release_evidence: assembled under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International license... available in 11 universally accepted formats
title: Large-scale annotation dataset for fetal head biometry in ultrasound images.
headline_result: inter-rater ICC 0.859-0.889, Jaccard similarity 0.855-0.857

patient_population: Public pediatric chest X-ray dataset from Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Centre
clinical_problem: Can a CNN-XGBoost model accurately classify chest X-rays as viral or bacterial pneumonia to assist interpretation regardless of radiologist experience?

title: Automated segmentation of standard scanning planes to measure biometric parameters in foetal ultrasound images–a survey

clinical_problem: improving image quality / reducing radiation dose for pediatric brain CT

headline_result: SVM classification on skeletonized HARDI measures produced satisfactory accuracy, especially for fiber-directionality parameters (no single summary number reported)

title: Progresses of CT image iterative reconstruction technique based on deep learning and applications in pediatric CT

clinical_problem: reducing scan time/radiotracer dose for pediatric 18F-FDG PET/CT while preserving image quality

title: Extracting low-dose (18)F-FDG PET/CT images with list mode based on deep learning reconstruction in children

headline_result: no significant differences in subjective quality score, TBR, CNR, CV, SUVmax, or SUVmean between standard 120s and DL-reconstructed 20s images (all P>0.05)

clinical_problem: assessment of neonatal respiratory status and need for respiratory support using lung ultrasound
model_description: Lung ultrasound scans obtained at defined early time points in newborns with respiratory distress were processed to extract regions of interest and used to train a neural network to interpret lung ultrasound and generate an AI-based score analogous to an established neonatal lung ultrasound score (nLUS). release_evidence: described as a research model with no stated public release
title: The future of neonatal lung ultrasound: Validation of an artificial intelligence model for interpreting lung scans. A multicentre prospective diagnostic study

model_family: hierarchical Bayesian regression normative model with transfer learning

dataset_size: reference model N=40,435 (all ages); transfer cohort N=5,985 children aged 6-17, three waves, two scanners

headline_result: Mean absolute error of 4.09 months on the RSNA bone age dataset

title: SACNet: A Multiscale Diffeomorphic Convolutional Registration Network with Prior Neuroanatomical Constraints for Flexible Susceptibility Artifact Correction in Echo Planar Imaging
headline_result: State-of-the-art correction performance, effectively eliminating susceptibility-artifact-related multicenter effects compared with existing correction methods

Validation on three independent sites held the AUC, which most prediction studies in this literature cannot show.

patient_population: not specified; the review is written for a pediatric radiology readership
clinical_problem: whether radiology AI actually improves efficiency, dose, accuracy and outcomes
model_description: A review, not a model. It names six clinical objectives AI is meant to serve — faster workflow, shorter reading time, less dose and contrast, earlier detection, better accuracy, more personalized diagnostics — and grades the published evidence for each against a hierarchical model of efficacy. Its conclusion is that the market is still maturing and very little is known about what AI contributes in practice, which is the argument for real-world monitoring before procurement.
title: How does artificial intelligence in radiology improve efficiency and health outcomes?

model_description: Fetal resting-state fMRI grew faster than the tooling to process it, and brain masking is where that gap bites - the brain moves unpredictably between volumes, so a single mask never holds. Rather than publishing a network alone, the authors wire it into the surrounding preprocessing steps and explain each adaptation, and release code and data openly. Two held-out test sets from different scanners and populations is a stronger generalization claim than the field usually makes.
release_evidence: openly shared code and data, presented as an advance toward a fully comprehensive open-source workflow

model_description: A ResNet-50 deep convolutional neural network trained on chest radiographs from the Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Center is tested on an internal holdout set and on an external NIH ChestXray14 dataset to detect pneumonia; class-activation-mapping heatmaps assess whether the model relies on clinically relevant features.
title: Limited generalizability of deep learning algorithm for pediatric pneumonia classification on external data.
study_design: retrospective diagnostic accuracy study with internal and external test sets
dataset_size: 5,232 training images; 624 internal test images; 383 external test images
headline_result: AUC 0.95 on internal test set vs. 0.54 on external test set (p<0.0001)

model_family: AI-enabled tools automating image acquisition, biometric measurement and report production during a live scan
patient_population: 23 subjects, each having both a standard and an AI-assisted scan, with a sonographer feedback survey
clinical_problem: the mid-trimester anomaly scan itself - whether separating freehand scanning from image capture, measurement and reporting frees the sonographer to look for malformations
model_description: An end-to-end automation pilot rather than a single model, and the endpoint is the scan rather than an accuracy metric. Seven and a half minutes saved per scan with no clinically significant difference in biometry, and the sonographers reported that removing repetitive tasks let them concentrate on interpretation - which is the mechanism by which this would improve anomaly detection, if it does. The honest limitation is stated: plane detection saved a satisfactory view in 93% of cases for four core views but only 73% for the full thirteen, against 98% manually.
title: Exploring a new paradigm for the fetal anomaly ultrasound scan: Artificial intelligence in real time.
headline_result: 7.62 minutes (34.7%) saved per scan (p < 0.0001) with no clinically significant biometric differences; satisfactory views saved in 93% for four core views and 73% for all thirteen, versus 98% manually

model_family: two convolutional super-resolution networks applied to phase-encoding-undersampled cine acquisitions
patient_population: 28 fetuses at a median gestational week of 36 (IQR 33-38), imaged at 1.5 T with Doppler ultrasound-gated balanced SSFP cine
clinical_problem: fetal cardiac MRI improves diagnosis of congenital heart defects but takes long enough that fetal motion frequently ruins it
model_description: Attacks motion by shortening the acquisition rather than by correcting afterwards: acquire at a third of the phase-encoding resolution, then restore it. The evaluation is a blinded three-observer quality score against the fully sampled clinical acquisition, with bicubic interpolation and zero-padding as the honest comparators - and both of those degraded significantly at 33% while the networks did not. Three times faster acquisition with no measurable quality cost.
journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
title: Super-Resolution Cine Image Enhancement for Fetal Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
dataset_size: 28 fetuses; 36 training, 3 validation and 67 test cine slices
headline_result: no significant difference in blinded image quality from clinical images down to 33% phase-encoding resolution (three times faster), whereas bicubic interpolation and zero-padding degraded significantly

model_family: MRMR and LASSO-selected radiomics signature across FLAIR, DWI, post-contrast T1 and ADC, combined with a clinical predictor in a nomogram
patient_population: 107 children with midline high-grade glioma who underwent biopsy with preoperative MRI between June 2016 and June 2021, 79 of them H3K27M-mutant, randomly split into training and test sets
clinical_problem: predicting H3K27M mutation status before biopsy in pediatric high-grade midline gliomas, where conventional MRI features are not powerful enough to make the call and the mutation defines prognosis
model_description: A purely pediatric counterpart to the mixed-age midline glioma radiomics work, and stronger for it - 107 children from one institution, four sequences plus ADC maps, and a two-stage feature selection that lands on nine features. Adding one visually assessed feature, ring enhancement, to the radiomic signature is a nice touch: it keeps a radiologist-legible term in the model. Training and test AUCs stay close, which the small mixed-age studies in this area do not manage.
title: MRI-based radiomics signature and clinical factor for predicting H3K27M mutation in pediatric high-grade gliomas located in the midline of the brain.
headline_result: radiomics signature AUC 0.95 training and 0.92 test; the nomogram with ring enhancement 0.95 and 0.90

patient_population: children imaged in radiology practice
clinical_problem: where AI fits in the pediatric radiologist's working day, and what it cannot do
model_description: A review in Pediatric Radiology arguing for augmentation rather than replacement. It sets out what AI does better than a person (measuring size, shape, texture and kinetics; handling high-dimensional data) against what it does worse (it is only as good as its training sample and cannot reason toward a near-optimal solution), and proposes explainable AI and an assistant that frees the radiologist's attention for the generic parts of the job.
title: The augmented radiologist: artificial intelligence in the practice of radiology.

model_family: classical ML (region merging, trainable Weka segmentation)
patient_population: First-trimester fetuses undergoing nuchal translucency scans (normal and increased NT groups)
clinical_problem: Segmenting and classifying first-trimester fetal brain ultrasound images to measure fetal cerebral cortex for earlier detection of brain abnormalities.
model_description: Applies two segmentation methods (Statistical Region Merging and Trainable Weka Segmentation) to fetal brain ultrasound images to measure the fetal cerebral cortex.
journal: Journal of ultrasound in medicine : official journal of the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine
title: Machine Learning Algorithms for Classification of First-Trimester Fetal Brain Ultrasound Images.
headline_result: MAPE 1.71% (SRM); MAPE 1.71% (TWS testing set)

body_region: abdomen, chest (FAST views: cardiac, pleural, upper quadrants, suprapubic)
patient_population: Injured children under 18 years old at two pediatric emergency departments, scanned by 30 different clinicians
clinical_problem: Can a deep learning model automatically and accurately identify which standard view was acquired during pediatric FAST (focused assessment with sonography for trauma), to support quality assurance despite variable clinician expertise?
model_description: A deep learning classifier takes FAST ultrasound video clips or still frames as input and outputs the predicted anatomic view (cardiac, pleural, upper-quadrant abdominal, or suprapubic).
journal: Journal of ultrasound in medicine : official journal of the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine
title: Development and Validation of a Deep Learning Strategy for Automated View Classification of Pediatric Focused Assessment With Sonography for Trauma.
study_design: retrospective cohort analysis, multi-clinician, two pediatric emergency departments
dataset_size: 699 FAST studies: 4,925 video clips and 1,062,612 still frames
headline_result: Overall classification accuracy 97.8% (95% CI 96.0-99.0) for video clips and 93.4% (95% CI 93.3-93.6) for still frames

patient_population: 40 pediatric participants (age 15.3 +/- 1.9 years)
clinical_problem: automatically segmenting pediatric thigh muscles on MRI to study musculoskeletal development
model_description: a two-stage cascaded deep learning model takes 3D MR images of the thigh as input and outputs automatic segmentation of the rectus femoris, vasti muscles, and patella
title: Automatic quadriceps and patellae segmentation of MRI with cascaded U2 -Net and SASSNet deep learning model.
study_design: retrospective single-center algorithm development and validation
headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient 93.7-95.1% across segmented muscles

patient_population: not stated (letter, no abstract)
clinical_problem: performance of AI ultrasound algorithms when applied to pediatric rather than adult patients
model_description: This record is a letter (no abstract) arguing that artificial-intelligence ultrasound algorithms behave differently in pediatric patients than in adults, implying a need for pediatric-specific validation of such algorithms.
journal: Journal of ultrasound in medicine : official journal of the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine
title: Aren't Pediatric Patients Just Little Adults? Artificial Intelligence Ultrasound Algorithms Beg to Differ.

patient_population: 136 paediatric posterior fossa tumours (retrospective)
clinical_problem: classifying/differentiating paediatric posterior fossa tumour types from MRI
model_description: Input: multiregional, multiparametric MRI features (T1, T2, contrast-enhanced T1, FLAIR, diffusion-weighted) of tumour and peritumoural regions; output: tumour-type classification via a support vector machine.
title: Differentiation of paediatric posterior fossa tumours by the multiregional and multiparametric MRI radiomics approach: a study on the selection of optimal multiple sequences and multiregions.
study_design: retrospective radiomics model development and validation
headline_result: Overall AUC 0.977 (validation cohort)

model_family: two-stage machine learning (logistic LASSO cure model + survival model)
patient_population: 543 patients under 18 undergoing pyeloplasty (2008-2020); 232 in the survival model
clinical_problem: Can machine learning predict, using ultrasound and clinical findings, which children will develop recurrent ureteropelvic junction obstruction after pyeloplasty, to enable personalized follow-up?
model_description: A two-stage machine learning model (logistic LASSO for a binary 'cure' classification, followed by a survival model) uses 34 clinical fields, including postoperative ultrasound anteroposterior renal pelvis diameter and anatomical variation, to predict risk and timing of recurrent obstruction after pyeloplasty; deployed as a web calculator.
title: Personalized application of machine learning algorithms to identify pediatric patients at risk for recurrent ureteropelvic junction obstruction after dismembered pyeloplasty.
study_design: retrospective single-center model development with leave-one-out cross-validation
headline_result: Leave-one-out cross-validated AUROC 0.86 and concordance 0.78

model_family: deep learning with unsupervised region localization
patient_population: public RSNA bone age dataset, plus an additional dataset
clinical_problem: Can bone age assessment from hand-wrist x-rays be made more objective and less dependent on individual physician experience, using a deep-learning computer-aided diagnosis method?
model_description: An unsupervised method first localizes informative hand regions, then a pretrained backbone image model with a small prediction head (incorporating gender as an embedded input) estimates bone age from the hand radiograph.
title: A deep learning-based computer-aided diagnosis method of X-ray images for bone age assessment.
study_design: retrospective model development and benchmarking on public and additional datasets
dataset_size: public RSNA bone age dataset plus an additional dataset
headline_result: Mean absolute error 6.2 months on the public RSNA dataset and 5.1 months on the additional dataset (MobileNetV3 backbone)

model_family: 3D multi-label dense U-Net trained on single-site and pooled multi-site data
patient_population: 174 subjects across two sites (38 healthy controls, 136 congenital heart disease patients; 46% female), scanned at 1.5 and 3 T
clinical_problem: segmenting the aorta and pulmonary arteries on 4D flow MRI to measure pulmonary and systemic flow and their ratio in congenital heart disease, which is done by hand and takes an expert
model_description: Asks the question a consortium has to answer before pooling: does training across heterogeneous sites, field strengths and vendors degrade a segmentation network relative to a local one? The answer here is no - Dice and, more importantly, the derived flow measurements Qs, Qp and Qp/Qs were statistically indistinguishable between single-site and multi-site models at both sites. That clears the way for training on pooled data in congenital heart disease, where no single centre has enough cases.
journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
title: Segmentation of the Aorta and Pulmonary Arteries Based on 4D Flow MRI in the Pediatric Setting Using Fully Automated Multi-Site, Multi-Vendor, and Multi-Label Dense U-Net.
headline_result: no significant difference between single-site and multi-site networks in aortic Dice (0.916 vs 0.915 and 0.906 vs 0.904) or in Qs, Qp and Qp/Qs at either site

model_family: k-means clustering over 120 radiomics features from pre-therapeutic chest CT
patient_population: 283 adolescents and adults with cystic fibrosis from a French multicentre real-world prospective study, with pre-therapeutic and one-year follow-up chest CT
clinical_problem: identifying, before treatment starts, which people with cystic fibrosis will respond to lumacaftor-ivacaftor, and measuring the structural lung change the drug produces
model_description: Unsupervised rather than supervised, and that choice carries the argument: the clusters are morphological phenotypes discovered in the pre-treatment CT without reference to who responded, and only afterwards are they checked against response. One of the three clusters contained most of the responders. Alongside this, visual Bhalla scoring quantifies what the drug did to the airways - mucus plugging, wall thickening and consolidation all fell over a year.
title: Using chest computed tomography and unsupervised machine learning for predicting and evaluating response to lumacaftor-ivacaftor in people with cystic fibrosis.
study_design: prospective multicentre observational study with retrospective radiomic analysis
headline_result: Bhalla score fell 1.40 +/- 1.53 points at one year (p<0.001); 54% of one radiomic cluster achieved a >= 5% FEV1 gain versus 32% and 33% in the others (p=0.02)

patient_population: 32 children with Takayasu arteritis, 9.14±4.51 years old
clinical_problem: improving CT angiography image quality (reducing noise while preserving contrast-to-noise ratio) in children with Takayasu arteritis
model_description: Input: raw CT angiography projection data; output: reconstructed images with reduced noise and improved contrast-to-noise ratio, compared against filtered back-projection and iterative reconstruction.
journal: Journal of X-ray science and technology
title: Application of deep learning image reconstruction algorithm to improve image quality in CT angiography of children with Takayasu arteritis.
headline_result: DLIR-high setting: noise 15.58±3.65 HU, aorta CNR 24.02±4.55 (best among all reconstructions); subjective nasal-cavity score 3.53±0.51

patient_population: 2,549 children aged 0-17 (mean 8.5 years) referred from a pediatric emergency room for trauma
clinical_problem: detecting fractures on radiographs of children presenting to the emergency room after trauma
model_description: This is the study a department should read before buying: an independent external validation of a marketed fracture-detection product on a consecutive real-life pediatric emergency cohort, scored three ways (is there a fracture, how many, and are they in the right place) with subgroup analysis by age and by whether the limb was in a cast. Performance was materially worse in children under 5 and in casted limbs, which are exactly the pediatric cases that matter.
release_evidence: external validation of the commercially available Rayvolve algorithm
title: External validation of a commercially available deep learning algorithm for fracture detection in children.
headline_result: sensitivity 95.7%, specificity 91.2%, accuracy 92.6% for detection; sensitivity and negative predictive value significantly lower in children aged 0-4 and in casted limbs

patient_population: children (population of the referenced article, not detailed in this editorial)
clinical_problem: diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder using brain MRI
model_description: This is an editorial comment on a study that used deep-learning algorithms applied to conventional MRI and apparent diffusion coefficient maps to help identify imaging features associated with autism spectrum disorder in children. The editorial itself reports no new data.
title: Editorial comment on "Diagnosing autism spectrum disorder in children using conventional MRI and apparent diffusion coefficient based deep learning algorithms".

patient_population: 20,118 pairs of full-spine radiographs from 15,378 patients (2008-2020), institution-wide
clinical_problem: Characterize 3D spinal shape and global alignment from 2D frontal and lateral radiographs in adult and pediatric spinal deformity patients
model_description: Takes frontal and lateral full-spine radiographs as input; a deep learning algorithm automatically extracts the vertebral midline (C7 to S1) to reconstruct approximate 3D spine shape and derive global alignment parameters.
journal: Journal of orthopaedic research : official publication of the Orthopaedic Research Society
title: Institution-wide shape analysis of 3D spinal curvature and global alignment parameters.
headline_result: Robust performance demonstrated across datasets and patient populations (no single accuracy metric given)

patient_population: training set of 57 radiographs; test set of 103 radiographs with a foreign body and 103 without
clinical_problem: triaging radiographs to detect and classify esophageal button-battery vs. coin foreign bodies in children
model_description: An object detector locates esophageal foreign bodies on radiographs, and an image classifier then classifies the detected object as a button battery or coin.
title: Esophageal discoid foreign body detection and classification using artificial intelligence.
headline_result: Detector 100% sensitive/specific; classifier 100% button batteries and 97.9% coins correctly classified

model_family: deep learning coronary artery segmentation framework
patient_population: 27 KD patients (catheterization/angiography + OCT); 34 KD patients with regressed or persistent coronary aneurysms followed longitudinally
clinical_problem: automated assessment of coronary artery distensibility (stiffness) over time in children with Kawasaki disease, using segmentation of angiographic images
model_description: Input: coronary angiography images; output: automated segmentation of the coronary artery lumen across the cardiac cycle to calculate vessel distensibility, correlated with OCT findings of vessel damage.
title: Deep Learning-Based Approach to Automatically Assess Coronary Distensibility Following Kawasaki Disease.
study_design: retrospective longitudinal cohort study using an automated deep learning segmentation framework
dataset_size: 27 KD patients (angiography+OCT); 34 KD patients followed longitudinally over average 14.5 years
headline_result: distensibility negatively correlated with OCT-graded vessel damage severity; significant increase in wall stiffness at 1 year post-diagnosis

body_region: brain (subcortical and cortical regions of interest)
patient_population: 11,848 children from the ABCD study, mean age 9.92 years
clinical_problem: Examine whether brain regional volumes mediate the relationship between traumatic stress exposure and PTSD symptoms in children
model_description: Takes volumes of 300 subcortical and cortical brain regions of interest from structural MRI as input to an elastic-net machine learning model identifying regions associated with traumatic stress and PTSD symptoms.
title: Associations Between Traumatic Stress, Brain Volumes and Post-traumatic Stress Disorder Symptoms in Children: Data from the ABCD Study.
study_design: retrospective cross-sectional structural equation modeling and machine learning analysis
headline_result: Indirect effects of brain ROI volumes on PTSD symptoms were negligible (r<0.0004)

model_family: convolutional neural network image quality assessment running on an external GPU wired into the scanner network, inside a modified HASTE pulse sequence
patient_population: 10 pregnant mothers, 73 acquisitions of the modified HASTE sequence at 3 T
clinical_problem: fetal motion ruining individual HASTE slices, which today means either accepting a degraded stack or repeating the whole stack
model_description: A closed loop rather than a model: the sequence sends each slice out to a network as it is acquired, gets a quality score back, and at the end of the stack reacquires only the worst slices, with no human in the loop. What makes this notable is that it runs inside the acquisition rather than after it, which is where fetal motion has to be handled if scan time is to be saved rather than spent. Tested live on 10 pregnancies.
title: Automated detection and reacquisition of motion-degraded images in fetal HASTE imaging at 3 T.
headline_result: image quality assessment accuracy 85.2% and AUC 0.899, used in real time to reacquire only the motion-degraded slices instead of the whole stack

model_family: elastic net, random forest, light gradient boosting, and support vector regression
patient_population: Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study baseline cohort, N=4042
clinical_problem: predicting future delayed reward discounting (a marker of substance-use risk) from brain MRI and behavioral data in late childhood
model_description: Input: questionnaire/task variables and MRI-derived brain variables at baseline; output: predicted delayed reward discounting score one year later.
title: One-year predictions of delayed reward discounting in the adolescent brain cognitive development study.
study_design: prospective cohort with machine learning prediction, cross-validated and tested on a held-out sample
headline_result: Questionnaire/task-variable models predicted delayed reward discounting in cross-validation and held-out test set; MRI-derived brain-variable models did not reliably predict it

model_family: recurrent deep neural network for deformable image registration
patient_population: infants during the first year of life
clinical_problem: aligning (registering) longitudinal and cross-sectional infant brain MRI scans despite rapid brain development
model_description: Takes brain tissue segmentation maps from infant brain MRI as input and outputs a deformation field that registers images across time points or subjects, using a recurrently-applied deep neural network with adaptive smoothing and anti-folding constraints.
release_evidence: The implementation of our proposed registration network is available online https://github.com/Barnonewdm/ACTA-Reg-Net.
title: Recurrent Tissue-Aware Network for Deformable Registration of Infant Brain MR Images.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and comparative evaluation study
headline_result: achieves highest registration accuracy among compared state-of-the-art methods while preserving deformation field smoothness

patient_population: children undergoing cardiac MRI (narrative review)
clinical_problem: reviewing how AI can assist interpretation of pediatric cardiovascular MRI
model_description: Narrative review summarizing AI applications in pediatric cardiovascular MRI, drawing on pediatric and adult cardiac MRI and broader radiology experience.
title: The role of artificial intelligence in paediatric cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging.

patient_population: 59 children with hippocampal epilepsy and 70 age/sex-matched controls
clinical_problem: identifying epilepsy in children from diffusion kurtosis imaging of the hippocampus
model_description: An SVM classifier takes hippocampal kurtosis-tensor features derived from diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI) as input and classifies subjects as epilepsy vs. normal control.
title: Identifying epilepsy based on machine-learning technique with diffusion kurtosis tensor.
headline_result: 95.24% classification accuracy

patient_population: 16,297 pregnancies at 18-40 weeks from two tertiary Chinese hospitals for development, a third hospital for external validation, and 166 pregnancies for prospective video testing
clinical_problem: screening for congenital central nervous system malformation on standard neurosonographic planes
model_description: Detects ten distinct intracranial abnormality patterns during the scan itself, not afterwards, using a real-time detection architecture. The evaluation ladder is unusually complete: internal validation, external validation at a third hospital, comparison against sonologists of differing experience, and then a prospective video dataset simulating live scanning. Performance drops from internal to external, as it should, and stays useful.
journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
title: Use of real-time artificial intelligence in detection of abnormal image patterns in standard sonographic reference planes in screening for fetal intracranial malformations.
study_design: retrospective development with external and prospective validation
dataset_size: 43,890 images from 16,297 pregnancies and 169 videos from 166 pregnancies
headline_result: micro-average AUC 0.977 internally and 0.898 on external validation across ten intracranial patterns, with prospective real-time video evaluation

model_family: 3D U-Net ensemble (U-Net++, attention U-Net, U-Net with shape prior)
patient_population: preterm/very low birth weight neonates undergoing 3D cranial ultrasound
clinical_problem: measuring intraventricular hemorrhage and post-hemorrhagic ventricle dilatation in preterm neonates via ventricle segmentation
model_description: Takes a 3D cranial ultrasound image as input and outputs an automated segmentation of the neonatal cerebral lateral ventricles, using an ensemble of three U-Net variant deep learning models combined by mean voting.
title: Automated 3D U-net based segmentation of neonatal cerebral ventricles from 3D ultrasound images.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development with fivefold cross-validation
dataset_size: 190 3D ultrasound images (87 two-ventricle, 103 one-ventricle); 165 held-out test images across cross-validation folds
headline_result: Dice 0.720±0.074 (two-ventricle images); Dice 0.806±0.111 (one-ventricle images); ~5 seconds per image

patient_population: Benchmark dataset of 5,856 chest X-ray images (children stated as more prone to the disease; exact population age not further specified)
clinical_problem: Automatically detecting pneumonia on chest X-rays, a disease that disproportionately affects children, using a lightweight deep learning model suitable for fast deployment
model_description: Input: chest X-ray images; output: binary classification of pneumonia vs. normal, via a lightweight MobileNet-based deep learning architecture
title: A lightweight deep learning architecture for the automatic detection of pneumonia using chest X-ray images.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development on a benchmark dataset
headline_result: combined accuracy 97.09%, specificity 0.96, precision 0.97, recall 0.98, F1 0.97

patient_population: 210 fetal lung ultrasound images (159 normal, 51 with neonatal respiratory morbidity)
clinical_problem: prenatally predicting neonatal respiratory morbidity from fetal lung ultrasound
model_description: radiomics features from the fetal lung region of interest plus gestational age and GDM status are input to an imbalance-aware ensemble classifier that outputs predicted risk of neonatal respiratory morbidity
title: Prenatal prediction of neonatal respiratory morbidity: a radiomics method based on imbalanced few-shot fetal lung ultrasound images.
headline_result: sensitivity 0.82, specificity 0.84, balanced accuracy 0.83, AUC 0.87

model_family: support vector machine on functional connectivity
patient_population: 103 adult and 65 pediatric focal epilepsy patients and 109 controls across four epilepsy centers
clinical_problem: distinguishing focal epilepsy patients from controls and lateralizing seizure onset using resting-state functional connectivity
model_description: Resting-state fMRI whole-brain functional connectivity measures (parcelwise connectivity matrix, mean FC, degree of FC) are input to support vector machine models that classify epilepsy patients versus controls and lateralize the hemisphere of seizure onset, evaluated across four epilepsy centers.
title: Common functional connectivity alterations in focal epilepsies identified by machine learning.
study_design: retrospective multicenter case-control diagnostic accuracy study
dataset_size: 103 adult and 65 pediatric epilepsy patients, 109 controls (four centers)
headline_result: epilepsy-vs-control classification median accuracy 75.6% (AUC 0.83); lateralization median accuracy 64.0% (AUC 0.69)

patient_population: Prepared dataset plus the public HC18-Grand Challenge dataset (fetal head circumference)
clinical_problem: Fast, accurate automatic segmentation of the fetal head and abdominal circumference on ultrasound for biometric measurement on clinical devices
model_description: Input: fetal ultrasound images; output: segmentation masks for head and abdominal circumference measurement, via a lightweight, fast U-Net-based architecture
title: Fast and Accurate U-Net Model for Fetal Ultrasound Image Segmentation.
dataset_size: prepared dataset + public HC18-Grand Challenge dataset
headline_result: Dice 97.62% (head)/95.07% (abdomen) on prepared dataset; Dice 97.45% on public HC18 dataset; 0.47s per image

model_family: 3D Bayesian U-Net with spatial concrete dropout, compared to DenseNet, U-Net, and DenseNet/U-Net ensemble
patient_population: 27 very preterm infants with post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus (41 T2-weighted MRIs)
clinical_problem: monitoring post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus in very preterm infants
model_description: T2-weighted brain MRIs from very preterm infants with post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus are automatically segmented into lateral ventricles, external CSF, white and cortical gray matter, brainstem, and cerebellum using a Bayesian U-Net with 3D spatial concrete dropout, which also produces a voxel-wise uncertainty map. Performance was compared against DenseNet, a standard U-Net, and an ensemble of both, using manual segmentations as ground truth, to support more objective 3D monitoring of ventricle size for treatment decisions.
title: Automatic brain segmentation in preterm infants with post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus using 3D Bayesian U-Net.
study_design: retrospective single-center technical development and validation
headline_result: Bayesian U-Net gave the best lateral-ventricle segmentation (mean Dice 0.948) versus DenseNet (0.814), U-Net (0.944), and ensemble (0.942), with mean uncertainty-estimation AUC 0.949

model_family: hybrid model combining an HRNet landmark detector with rule-based post-processing
patient_population: 1542 consecutive patients with scoliosis at two Hong Kong clinics from December 2019 to November 2020 for development, then prospective validation in a further 337 patients; biplanar EOS radiographs recaptured with smartphones or screenshots
clinical_problem: automatic measurement of spine alignment in scoliosis, where existing auto-analysis is unreliable and where the image a clinician has is often a phone photo or a screenshot rather than the original radiograph
model_description: Two things set it apart. First, it is deliberately trained on degraded images - smartphone photographs and screenshots of radiographs - because that is what gets sent between clinics, and robustness to that is the difference between a research tool and a usable one. Second, rules are layered on the network's landmarks so the output can be explained and checked, rather than emerging from an opaque regression. Prospectively validated on 337 further patients, which is rare in this literature.
title: An artificial intelligence powered platform for auto-analyses of spine alignment irrespective of image quality with prospective validation.
dataset_size: 1542 development patients plus 337 prospective validation patients
headline_result: mean landmark error 2.78 pixels posteroanterior and 5.52 lateral; mean angle error 3.18 degrees coronal and 6.32 degrees sagittal; curve detection sensitivity 95.7% and specificity 88.1%; all predicted alignments strongly correlated with ground truth (R2 > 0.97)

model_family: deep learning detection model for plain radiographs
patient_population: children with head trauma who had both skull radiography and cranial CT: development sets of 149 and 264 from two hospitals, external test set of 95 from a third; cranial CT was the reference standard
clinical_problem: detecting skull fractures on plain radiographs in children with head trauma, the film that is often taken first and read by whoever is on shift
model_description: One of the cleaner pediatric AI evaluations in the literature: multi-center development, a genuinely external test hospital, CT as the reference standard, and a two-session reader study with the crossed design that shows who the tool is for. The answer is the one that keeps recurring in pediatric AI - it significantly helped radiology residents and emergency physicians and did nothing measurable for the pediatric radiologist. That is an argument about staffing and coverage, not about accuracy.
title: Deep Learning-Assisted Diagnosis of Pediatric Skull Fractures on Plain Radiographs.
study_design: retrospective multi-center model development with a crossed reader study
dataset_size: 413 development cases from two hospitals, 95 external test cases from a third
headline_result: AUROC 0.922 internal and 0.870 external; with AI assistance AUROC rose by 0.094 for radiology residents (p = 0.012) and 0.069 for emergency physicians (p = 0.043), but by only 0.008 for the pediatric radiologist (p = 0.850)

patient_population: 129 pediatric digitally reconstructed radiographs used for training data generation
clinical_problem: producing bone-suppressed images from pediatric chest radiographs to improve detection of pulmonary disease, since dual-energy subtraction cannot safely be used in children
model_description: Takes standard pediatric chest radiographs as input and outputs a bone-suppressed image using a cascaded deep-learning model, trained via adult CT-derived digitally reconstructed radiographs adapted to pediatric anatomy with a U-Net.
journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
title: Bone suppression on pediatric chest radiographs via a deep learning-based cascade model.
study_design: retrospective model development and reader evaluation study
headline_result: Radiologist effectiveness score 3.31 ± 0.48 (scale 1-5)

patient_population: 2164 pelvis X-ray images, Chinese Han teenagers aged 11-21 years
clinical_problem: Forensic estimation of bone age in adolescents from pelvis radiographs
model_description: A U-Net segmentation network localizes key pelvic regions on X-ray, which are used to augment the image before three convolutional neural networks (Inception-V3, Inception-ResNet-V2, VGG19) estimate bone age.
title: Forensic bone age estimation of adolescent pelvis X-rays based on two-stage convolutional neural network.
headline_result: RMSE 0.93-1.14 years; MAE 0.67-0.88 years (with segmentation-based augmentation)

model_family: multi-task convolutional network doing spatio-temporal feature extraction and standard plane detection on ultrasound video
patient_population: 50 freehand fetal ultrasound video scans, compared against five experienced sonographers measuring at two time points at least two weeks apart
clinical_problem: fetal biometry - head circumference, biparietal diameter, abdominal circumference, femur length - and the gestational age and weight estimates derived from it, in settings short of sonographers who can interpret fetal ultrasound
model_description: Works from video rather than from a frozen frame, so the model chooses the measuring plane as well as the caliper positions - the part of biometry that actually takes skill. The evaluation is the strongest form available short of a trial: five sonographers measured twice, weeks apart, establishing both intra- and inter-observer variability, and the model's disagreement with each expert fell inside that band. Six minutes of expert time becomes a few seconds.
title: Deep learning fetal ultrasound video model match human observers in biometric measurements.
study_design: retrospective model development with a multi-reader repeatability study
headline_result: automated measurements comparable to five experienced sonographers, with differences within inter- and intra-observer variability and not statistically significant against any individual expert; seconds versus an average of six minutes

patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing abdominal CT (83 low-dose, 42 standard-dose studies)
clinical_problem: reducing noise in low-dose pediatric abdominal CT to approximate standard-dose image quality
model_description: a generative adversarial network trained on unpaired low-dose and standard-dose CT images takes low-dose CT as input and outputs a denoised virtual standard-dose CT image
title: Denoising of pediatric low dose abdominal CT using deep learning based algorithm.

patient_population: 97 radiologists across 18 European countries already using the software, from 282 surveyed
clinical_problem: what actually happens when an AI tool designed to replace the radiologist is installed in a department
model_description: The most useful deployment study in this database, and it contains no images. BoneXpert was built as an AI-replace tool; asked how they actually use it, only 18% of radiologists let it replace them, 60% still review the radiograph themselves to exclude underlying disease, and 40% have never overruled it. Reporting time fell sharply. The authors' conclusion is the general lesson: bone age rating is not the whole of reading a bone age radiograph, so a tool validated for one task cannot autonomously own the examination.
release_evidence: the autonomous AI system for bone age rating (BoneXpert), in clinical use in European departments
title: Autonomous artificial intelligence in pediatric radiology: the use and perception of BoneXpert for bone age assessment.
headline_result: radiologists taking over 2 minutes per rating fell from 86% to 21% after installation; only 18% used it to replace the radiologist, 60% still checked the radiograph themselves, and 40% never overruled it
