model_family: previously validated automated deep learning pipeline that finds the L3 axial slice and segments skeletal muscle
patient_population: 2168 children aged 2.00-18.99 years (1125 female, 1043 male; mean age 12.3 +/- 4.3) who had abdominal CT at Cincinnati Children's Hospital between January 2009 and January 2019, screened to exclude abnormal BMI, medical conditions, medications, support devices and surgery
clinical_problem: there is no pediatric normal range for skeletal muscle area or index at L3, so sarcopenia cannot be diagnosed in children the way it is in adults
model_description: The model is a means to a reference standard: an existing validated pipeline is run over 2168 carefully screened normal children to produce age- and sex-based percentile curves for muscle area and index. Automation is what makes the exclusion criteria affordable - screening 8817 scans down to 2168 by BMI percentile, medication, device and surgery status is only practical if the measurement itself is free. The finding that muscle index correlates only weakly with age and BMI, while raw area correlates strongly, is what makes the normative curves necessary.
title: Defining Normal Ranges of Skeletal Muscle Area and Skeletal Muscle Index in Children on CT Using an Automated Deep Learning Pipeline: Implications for Sarcopenia Diagnosis.
headline_result: age- and sex-based percentile curves for pediatric skeletal muscle area and index at L3; muscle area correlated strongly with weight, height, age and BMI (0.75-0.94) while muscle index correlated only weakly to moderately (0.25-0.57)

model_family: artificial neural network on 105 Pyradiomics features from 3D CT, plus a pretrained 2D CNN on slices; six algorithms compared
patient_population: 65 children with neuroblastoma, primary tumors manually segmented and independently reviewed by a subspecialty-trained pediatric radiologist
clinical_problem: predicting mortality, metastases, differentiation grade, mitosis-karyorrhexis index, MYCN amplification and image-defined risk factors in neuroblastoma non-invasively, when these come from pathology and surgical assessment
model_description: Six outcomes from one set of CT images, including two - MYCN amplification and the mitosis-karyorrhexis index - that currently require tissue and that drive risk group assignment in neuroblastoma. The head-to-head between handcrafted radiomics fed to a neural network and a pretrained CNN on slices is instructive: radiomics won on almost every outcome, which is what tends to happen at 65 patients. Segmentations were checked by a pediatric radiologist rather than left to a trainee.
title: Incorporating Radiomics into Machine Learning Models to Predict Outcomes of Neuroblastoma.
headline_result: the radiomics-based neural network outperformed the other algorithms for every outcome except neuroblastic differentiation grade, where elastic regression was best

model_family: machine learning (SVM and others), parcellation-based feature engineering

title: Performance scaling for structural MRI surface parcellations: a machine learning analysis in the ABCD Study.

title: Study on multiplanar measurements of infant hips with three-dimensional ultrasonography.

dataset_size: two independent neonatal cohorts (exact n not stated)

model_family: deep neural network with a visualized internal representation used as an explainable overlay

model_description: The measured outcome is the examiner's performance, not the model's - which is the right endpoint for a screening aid and a rare one to see reported. The gain scales inversely with experience: residents improved most, fellows next, experts least, exactly the gradient you would want from a tool meant to spread a hard skill. The explainability is not a post-hoc heatmap but a purpose-built representation of the network's internals, offered as the thing that earns clinician trust.
title: Medical Professional Enhancement Using Explainable Artificial Intelligence in Fetal Cardiac Ultrasound Screening.
headline_result: mean AUC rose from 0.966 to 0.975 for experts, 0.829 to 0.890 for fellows and 0.616 to 0.748 for residents

model_family: convolutional neural network trained few-shot, compared against training on many weakly labelled atlas-derived segmentations

clinical_problem: quantifying subcortical brain volume development from 3D fetal ultrasound, which manual segmentation makes impractical because of low soft tissue contrast, speckle and shadowing
model_description: Two contributions worth separating. Methodologically, it settles a practical question - nine careful manual annotations beat many weak atlas-derived labels, reaching close to intra-observer variability - which changes how a group with limited annotation time should spend it. Substantively, applying the result to 278 healthy volumes produced ultrasound-specific second-trimester growth curves for choroid plexus, ventricle horns, cavum septum pellucidum and cerebellum, which is a normative reference that did not previously exist for this modality.
title: Subcortical segmentation of the fetal brain in 3D ultrasound using deep learning.
study_design: retrospective model development and normative study
dataset_size: 9 manually annotated training volumes; 278 volumes for the growth curves
headline_result: segmentation performance close to intra-observer variability from only nine manual annotations, and novel ultrasound-specific second-trimester growth curves for four subcortical structures

title: Ultrasound Lung Image under Artificial Intelligence Algorithm in Diagnosis of Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome.

model_family: radiomics feature selection and machine learning modelling over 1294 features from T1-weighted and contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI, combined into a nomogram
patient_population: 253 consecutive children with medulloblastoma from two hospitals, with a training set and two held-out test sets
clinical_problem: predicting progression-free survival in pediatric medulloblastoma and identifying which children benefit from postoperative radiotherapy

The gain over clinicopathological factors alone is real but modest.
journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
title: Radiomics signature for the prediction of progression-free survival and radiotherapeutic benefits in pediatric medulloblastoma.
headline_result: concordance index 0.711, 0.707 and 0.717 on training and the two test sets; the nomogram reached 0.723 and 0.722 versus 0.665 and 0.677 for clinicopathological factors alone

clinical_problem: whether the failure of structural MRI to separate autism from typical development is biological or technical - that is, whether the batch effect of multi-site data collection is masking a real signal

Harmonizing across sites lifts autism-versus-control discrimination from an AUC of 0.58 - indistinguishable from chance - to 0.67, which is significant but still low. The honest conclusion is both that batch effects were hiding a real signal and that the signal, once uncovered, is small. Age-stratified results (0.62 children, 0.65 adolescents, 0.69 adults) and consistent anatomical patterns per subgroup make it more informative than a single pooled number.
title: Multi-site harmonization of MRI data uncovers machine-learning discrimination capability in barely separable populations: An example from the ABIDE dataset.

model_family: three-dimensional regression convolutional neural network with layer-wise relevance propagation attention maps
patient_population: 518 neonates and infants aged 0-25 months with reported normal myelination scanned at one academic center between January 1995 and June 2019 (mean gestationally corrected age 67 weeks +/- 33), with an external test set from the National Institutes of Health
clinical_problem: judging whether an infant's myelination is appropriate for age, which today means a radiologist visually inspecting T1 and T2 images against remembered milestones and comparing to gestationally corrected age
model_description: Automates an assessment that is already part of every pediatric brain MRI report, rather than inventing a new biomarker - the output is the age the brain looks like, which is exactly what the radiologist is estimating by eye. The attention maps are the convincing part: the network attended to cerebellum, posterior white matter and basal ganglia in the youngest infants and to anterior white matter in the oldest, which is the known caudal-to-rostral, posterior-to-anterior order of myelination. Combining T1 and T2 beat either alone, and it held up on an external NIH set.
title: Deep Learning to Predict Neonatal and Infant Brain Age from Myelination on Brain MRI Scans.
study_design: retrospective model development with external validation
headline_result: mean absolute error 9.8 +/- 2.3 weeks (T1), 9.1 +/- 1.9 (T2) and 7.7 +/- 1.7 (both) internally; 9.1 weeks on the external NIH test set

Almost all of it is deep-learning CT reconstruction, and the reported dose reductions are large. It notes that commercially available models dominate but locally built ones matched them, and that the evidence base is narrow: three modalities, small samples, and most examination types untouched.
release_evidence: commercially available AI models based on deep convolutional networks dominate the reviewed studies
title: Artificial Intelligence for Radiation Dose Optimization in Pediatric Radiology: A Systematic Review.
headline_result: most studies reported 36-70% radiation dose reduction without loss of diagnostic information

title: AI Denoising Improves Image Quality and Radiological Workflows in Pediatric Ultra-Low-Dose Thorax Computed Tomography Scans.

dataset_size: 100 pediatric thorax ultra-low-dose CT scans, 8 readers
headline_result: lowest image noise with PixelShine (34.8±3.27 HU vs. 76.9±9.62 HU for wFBP); highest subjective quality (4 vs. 3); shortest time to diagnosis (2.28±1.56 vs. 2.66±2.31 min), all p<0.001

A useful illustration of a measurement where automation is more reliable than the humans it is scored against.
title: Automated Machine Learning Segmentation and Measurement of Urinary Stones on CT Scan.
headline_result: 100% sensitivity and specificity for detecting individual stones; Dice 0.66 against human reviewers, who agreed with each other at Jaccard 0.17 for total stone volume and 0.33 for the largest stone

model_family: multi-scale residual neural network classifying cortical nodes from laminar surface sampling of multi-modal MRI intensities and diffusion tractography edge strengths
patient_population: children with drug-resistant epilepsy undergoing clinically acquired multi-modal MRI, with an independent validation cohort split into lesional and non-lesional MRI groups
clinical_problem: localizing the seizure onset zone non-invasively in children with drug-resistant epilepsy, especially those whose MRI shows no lesion and who currently need intracranial electrodes to find it
model_description: The output is framed as a marker rather than a verdict - a per-node probability of seizure onset - which is how it can be combined with intracranial EEG rather than competing with it. The finding that justifies the whole exercise is in the non-lesional group, where MRI is by definition unhelpful: adding the marker to interictal intracranial EEG markers improved discrimination between resected epileptogenic and preserved non-epileptogenic sites by up to 15%. title: Multi-Scale Deep Learning of Clinically Acquired Multi-Modal MRI Improves the Localization of Seizure Onset Zone in Children With Drug-Resistant Epilepsy.
study_design: retrospective model development with independent validation
headline_result: Cohen's d of 1.21 between seizure onset and non-onset nodes, balanced accuracy 0.75 in lesional and 0.67 in non-lesional MRI groups, improving intracranial EEG-based discrimination by up to 15% in the non-lesional group

Predicting the final angle within about 5 degrees from plain 2D radiographs makes the output directly comparable to the threshold clinicians brace on.
title: Predicting curve progression for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis using random forest model.

Training and validation performance are close, which is reassuring for a radiomics model of this size.
title: Prediction of Histologic Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy Response in Osteosarcoma Using Pretherapeutic MRI Radiomics.
headline_result: best model AUC 0.95 with 91% sensitivity and 92% specificity in training, and 0.97 / 91% / 92% in validation

model_description: Two deliverables in one paper, and the second is the interesting one. The first is a curated, preprocessed, analysis-ready pediatric diffusion MRI resource in BIDS format, openly released. The second is a way of scaling quality control: a small expert-scored subset plus a much larger set scored by community scientists trains a network that agrees with experts on held-out data, and an interpretability check confirms it keys on features that actually bear on quality. That paradigm - crowdsource the bulk, anchor with experts, learn the rest - transfers to any large pediatric imaging cohort.

model_description: Designed backwards from the deployment constraint rather than from the dataset. The most consequential result is that non-inferiority held when novices performed only two of the six sweep types, which is a statement about how little training the pathway actually requires.

The loss function choice is presented as a clinical trade rather than a technical detail: mean absolute error gives higher bone precision, mean squared error higher recall, and which you want depends on whether a missed or a hallucinated bone edge is worse downstream. Generalizability was tested by training and validating across hospitals, vendors and MRI techniques, and augmenting local data with outside data helped.

headline_result: Light_U-Net outperformed the VGG-16 models on Pearson correlation, error and bone precision/recall, with performance improving when local training data were augmented with data from other hospitals, vendors or MRI techniques

title: Anatomical prior based vertebra modelling for reappearance of human spines
study_design: technical development and phantom/in vivo validation study
headline_result: Cobb angle measurement correlation R2=0.978 (P<0.001) against reference

model_family: convolutional neural network for automated segmentation

clinical_problem: fetal biometry (head circumference / biparietal diameter) for gestational age and growth assessment

Trained on 110 labeled images and tested on 80 ultrasound images, aiming to reduce the operator dependence and time cost of manual measurement.
title: EVALUATION OF FETEL HEAD CIRCUMFRENECE (HC) AND ULTRASOUND IMAGES USING CNN
dataset_size: 110 labeled training images, 80 test ultrasound images
headline_result: 94.31% success rate for HC/BPD measurement; 89.14% accuracy on plane acceptance check

model_family: convolutional neural network (deep learning brain-age prediction)

clinical_problem: linking pubertal development to brain maturation via brain-age prediction

Predicted brain age was related to pubertal stage using linear mixed-effects models to test whether pubertal development is associated with accelerated brain maturation.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Linking brain maturation and puberty during early adolescence using longitudinal brain age prediction in the ABCD cohort

model_family: multimodal MRI combined with machine learning (including brain-age prediction and imaging genetics)
patient_population: children with neurodevelopmental disorders
clinical_problem: understanding normal and atypical brain development in children with neurodevelopmental disorders
model_description: A narrative review of 49 studies (1999-2021) summarizing multimodal structural, anatomical and functional MRI combined with machine learning techniques, including brain-age prediction and imaging genetics, used to map normal and atypical brain development in children. Discusses how these quantitative MRI/ML approaches may provide imaging biomarkers for earlier diagnosis, classification and prognosis of neurodevelopmental disorders.
journal: Chinese Journal of Anatomy and Clinics
title: Research progress of magnetic resonance imaging on brain development and neurodevelopmental disorders in children

patient_population: 102 labeled training images and 70 test ultrasound images

clinical_problem: use of AI and simulation to improve prenatal ultrasound education and training

title: Artificial intelligence and simulation in prenatal medicine—What we can learn from machines

clinical_problem: AI-assisted prenatal ultrasound screening
model_description: This review provides an overview of the current state of development of artificial intelligence, particularly neural networks, for automated analysis of prenatal diagnostic ultrasound images, and summarizes which AI technologies are already used in prenatal diagnosis.
title: Value of AI in prenatal sonographic screening

clinical_problem: improving MRI spatial resolution without longer scan times, tested for generalizability across populations including newborns
model_description: Super Resolution Generative Adversarial Networks (SRGANs) were trained on T1-weighted MRI from three cohorts (older adults, newborns, and brain tumor patients) to upsample image resolution, and tested for generalizability when applied across cohorts and when trained on a combined multi-cohort dataset, using synthetic and anatomical quality metrics.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Towards robust and generalizable super-resolution generative adversarial networks for magnetic resonance neuroimaging: a cross-population approach
headline_result: no artifacts were introduced when SRGANs were applied across cohorts or trained on a combined dataset; high image quality and anatomical fidelity were maintained

model_family: attention-based multiple-instance learning convolutional neural network
patient_population: children (RSNA 2017 pediatric bone age dataset)
clinical_problem: bone age assessment for endocrine, genetic and growth disorders
model_description: Takes a whole hand radiograph, cropped into small patches, as input. A feature extraction network computes patch features, and an attention mechanism ranks and aggregates the patches by importance (multiple-instance learning) without requiring manual region-of-interest annotation; the aggregated image features are combined with sex to predict bone age, and the attention weights produce an interpretable heatmap of the regions used. Validated on the Radiological Society of North America 2017 pediatric bone age dataset.
title: Attention-based multiple-instance learning for Pediatric bone age assessment with efficient and interpretable
headline_result: Mean absolute error of 4.17 months

model_family: deep learning CNNs (GoogLeNet, VGG16_bn, VGG19_bn, ResNet18/34/50)
patient_population: 31 children with primary ciliary dyskinesia and 30 age-matched children with otitis media with effusion
clinical_problem: differentiating primary ciliary dyskinesia-related otitis media from simple otitis media with effusion
model_description: Takes temporal bone CT images from children as input and classifies them as primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD)-related otitis media versus simple otitis media with effusion. Several deep learning architectures (GoogLeNet, VGG16_bn, VGG19_bn, ResNet18/34/50) were trained on retrospective CT data and compared, with GoogLeNet performing best, intended to help screen for PCD, a cause of otitis media that is easy to miss clinically.
title: Temporal bone CT-based deep learning models for differential diagnosis of primary ciliary dyskinesia related otitis media and simple otitis media with effusion
dataset_size: 31 children with PCD, 30 age-matched children with OME
headline_result: GoogLeNet model accuracy of 0.99 for PCD screening

model_family: convolutional neural network with dropout in the convolutional layers (custom architecture)
patient_population: pediatric patients aged 1-5 years from Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Center (public dataset)
clinical_problem: detecting pneumonia on chest radiographs
model_description: A convolutional neural network using dropout within its convolutional layers was trained and tested on 5,856 labeled pediatric anterior-posterior chest radiographs (a public dataset originally from Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Center, ages 1-5) to automatically detect pneumonia.
title: Detection of pneumonia using convolutional neural networks and deep learning
study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study
headline_result: 97.2% accuracy, 97.3% recall, 97.4% precision, AUC 0.982, competitive with current state-of-the-art solutions

clinical_problem: fetal brain segmentation, classifying pathological vs neurotypical brain, and estimating gestational age from fetal brain MRI
model_description: MTSE U-Net is a multi-tasking single-encoder U-Net that, from an already-extracted fetal brain MRI, simultaneously segments the brain into seven structures (intracranial/extra-axial CSF spaces, gray matter, white matter, ventricles, cerebellum, deep gray matter, brainstem and spinal cord), classifies the brain as pathological or neurotypical, and predicts gestational age, all with a single shared model.
journal: Network Modeling Analysis in Health Informatics and Bioinformatics
title: MTSE U-Net: an architecture for segmentation, and prediction of fetal brain and gestational age from MRI of brain
headline_result: Jaccard similarity 77% and Dice score 82% for segmentation; 89% accuracy for pathological/neurotypical classification; mean absolute error 0.83 weeks for gestational age prediction

clinical_problem: AI-assisted detection of fetal brain and cardiovascular abnormalities on fetal MRI
model_description: This review summarizes advances in applying artificial intelligence to fetal brain and cardiac MRI, an area with far fewer published studies than AI applied to fetal ultrasound, and discusses how AI tools may assist clinicians and parents in decision-making around central nervous system and cardiovascular abnormalities.
title: Artificial intelligence applications of fetal brain and cardiac MRI

patient_population: infants with clinical suspicion of DDH, mean age 87 days (range 4-267 days), at two tertiary pediatric hospitals (Edmonton, Canada and Melbourne, Australia)
clinical_problem: developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) detection and classification
model_description: Analyzes 3D ultrasound of the infant hip and automatically calculates two standard DDH indices (alpha angle and femoral head coverage) without user input, classifying each hip as normal or dysplastic. The commercial, FDA-cleared algorithm, trained on data from one site, was tested retrospectively on hips from that site and an independent site it had not seen before, and compared against conventional clinical diagnosis made from concurrent 2D ultrasound.
release_evidence: a commercial FDA-cleared AI algorithm
title: Automated diagnosis of hip dysplasia from 3D ultrasound using artificial intelligence: A two-center multi-year study
dataset_size: 2,492 hips from 1,563 patients (1,294 hips Edmonton, 1,198 hips Melbourne)
headline_result: Sensitivity 0.90 for dysplasia; correctly categorized 90% (148/165) of dysplastic hips and 86% (2,006/2,327) of other hips; kappa = 0.79 agreement with clinical diagnosis

model_family: 3D convolutional neural network (U-Net) within a BIDS-App Snakemake workflow
patient_population: 159 fetuses (1,103 volumes) from open-access data for training/testing; 19 fetuses (82 scans, over 2,300 volumes) from a local cohort for generalizability testing
clinical_problem: automated brain masking/segmentation for fetal functional MRI analysis

It was trained and tested on open-access fetal fMRI data from 159 fetuses and further validated for generalizability on a separate local cohort of 19 fetuses.
release_evidence: The tool is freely available and can be applied to any BIDS dataset containing fetal bold sequences.
title: An automated BIDS-App for brain segmentation of human fetal functional MRI data
study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study
dataset_size: 159 fetuses / 1,103 volumes (training/testing); 19 fetuses / 82 scans / >2,300 volumes (generalizability testing)
headline_result: Dice metrics consistently ≥0.74 across both datasets compared to manual segmentation

model_family: convolutional neural network (CNN) approaches for image segmentation
patient_population: fetuses in the second and third trimester of pregnancy
clinical_problem: evaluating fetal brain development in the second and third trimester via MRI

journal: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
title: Research progresses of convolutional neural network for exploring fetal brain development patterns during the second and third trimester of pregnancy

model_family: linear mixed-effect models for regional brain-size analysis; support vector machine for outcome prediction
patient_population: 166 autistic and 109 typically developing toddlers (intake mean age 2.5 years); replicated in 38 autistic and 37 typically developing toddlers
clinical_problem: characterizing early brain structural alterations in autism and predicting later language outcome

A support vector machine model then tested whether adding these early brain-size measures to intake clinical and behavioral data improved prediction of language outcome at ages 3-4.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Language and Social Regions Are Affected in Toddlers with Autism and Predict Later Language Outcome
dataset_size: 166 autistic and 109 typically developing toddlers (discovery); 38 autistic and 37 typically developing toddlers (replication)
headline_result: adding early regional brain-size measures to the SVM model improved accuracy for predicting later language outcome beyond intake clinical and demographic variables (no single accuracy figure given)

model_family: low-light image enhancement stacked with a dense convolutional network (DenseNet) classifier
patient_population: fetuses undergoing fetal echocardiography (460 ultrasound images used to develop the enhancement model)
clinical_problem: detection of fetal heart defects on fetal echocardiography
model_description: FetalNet first enhances low-light, low-contrast fetal echocardiography ultrasound images, then feeds the enhanced images into a dense convolutional network classifier to predict the presence of a fetal heart defect. Developed and evaluated using 460 ultrasound images, with enhancement quality measured by peak signal-to-noise ratio, structural similarity and mean squared error, and detection performance measured on unseen data.
title: FetalNet: Low-light fetal echocardiography enhancement and dense convolutional network classifier for improving heart defect prediction
headline_result: Image enhancement: PSNR 30.85 dB, SSIM 0.96, MSE 18.16; FHD prediction rate improved ~25% in accuracy/sensitivity/specificity, 100% predictive negative on unseen data

model_family: gray-scale ultrasound radiomics with LASSO feature selection and logistic regression
patient_population: 252 lesions from 143 children with subcutaneous hemangioma and 70 children with KHE
clinical_problem: differentiating subcutaneous hemangioma from Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma (KHE)
model_description: Extracts gray-scale ultrasound radiomics features from 252 lesions in 213 children with subcutaneous hemangioma or Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma, selects 22 stable features with LASSO, and builds logistic-regression radiomics models (alone and combined with clinical data) to differentiate the two entities, which require different management.
journal: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
title: Gray-scale ultrasound-based radiomics for differential diagnosis of subcutaneous hemangioma and Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma
dataset_size: 252 lesions from 213 children (143 with hemangioma, 70 with KHE); 176 training / 76 validation
headline_result: Combined clinical-radiomics model AUC 0.90 (95% CI 0.88-0.92) in the validation set, higher than the radiomics-only model (AUC 0.85)

patient_population: patients with atrial septal defect, a congenital heart disease often asymptomatic through childhood/youth
clinical_problem: detection of atrial septal defect, a congenital heart disease
model_description: A review discussing atrial septal defect, a congenital heart disease often asymptomatic through youth, and surveying deep learning algorithms applied across the imaging and diagnostic modalities used to identify it, including echocardiography, chest radiography, MRI and CT, summarizing the strengths and limitations of each approach.
title: A review on the impact of deep learning in the identification of atrial septal defect and a comparative study on the algorithms employed in the imaging modalities

model_family: machine learning classifier on diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) white matter features
body_region: brain (auditory and cognitive white matter pathways)
patient_population: young cochlear implant candidates compared with matched normal-hearing children (exact N not stated)
clinical_problem: predicting speech perception improvement after cochlear implantation in children
model_description: Pre-surgical diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) was compared between pediatric cochlear implant (CI) candidates and normal-hearing children to identify affected cortical regions. A machine learning model then used non-imaging and DTI-derived white matter features (whole-brain, affected, and unaffected regions) to predict whether a child would have high or low improvement in speech perception 6 months after implantation.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Machine Learning-Enabled Prediction of Speech Perception Improvement Based on Diffusion Tensor Imaging of Young Cochlear Implant Candidates
headline_result: prediction using unaffected white matter regions: accuracy 0.86, sensitivity 0.91, specificity 0.80; whole-brain white matter similar (0.85/0.91/0.80), both better than affected regions (0.72/0.74/0.70) and non-imaging features alone (0.67/0.55/0.78)

model_family: deep learning-based automated cerebellar parcellation (segmentation) applied to structural MRI, with diffusion tensor imaging analysis
patient_population: 598 children and adolescents with (n=314) or without (n=284) moderate-severe TBI, mean age 14.0±3.1 years, pooled from 12 datasets (ENIGMA Pediatric msTBI working group)
clinical_problem: quantifying secondary cerebellar volume changes after pediatric moderate-severe traumatic brain injury and their relation to executive function
model_description: A deep learning-based automated parcellation method was applied to structural MRI to measure total cerebellar volume and 17 subregion volumes in 598 children and adolescents with and without moderate-severe traumatic brain injury, pooled across 12 multi-site datasets. Cerebellar volumes were related to executive function scores and, in a longitudinal subsample, to early diffusion tensor imaging white matter measures, to characterize secondary cerebellar changes after pediatric brain injury.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Multimodal Analysis of Secondary Cerebellar Alterations after Pediatric Traumatic Brain Injury
study_design: retrospective multi-site cross-sectional and longitudinal imaging study
dataset_size: 598 children and adolescents (314 msTBI, 284 non-TBI) from 12 pooled datasets; longitudinal subsample n=80
headline_result: smaller total cerebellar volume in msTBI (Cohen's d=-0.37), most pronounced in posterior lobe/vermis regions (d=-0.22 to -0.43); smaller cerebellar volume associated with more parent-reported executive function problems

model_family: vendor deep learning reconstruction (DLR) compared with ASIR-V iterative reconstruction
patient_population: 51 children with craniocerebral trauma and intracerebral hemorrhage undergoing low-dose brain CT
clinical_problem: reducing radiation dose in pediatric craniocerebral trauma CT while maintaining diagnostic image quality
model_description: Low-dose brain CT data from 51 children with traumatic intracerebral hemorrhage were reconstructed at two slice thicknesses with three levels of adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction (ASIR-V) and three levels of deep learning reconstruction (DLR: low, middle, high). Objective image-quality metrics and subjective 5-point scores were compared across reconstruction methods to identify the best approach for low-dose pediatric head CT.
title: A study on application of deep learning reconstruction in low‑dose brain CT in children with craniocerebral trauma
headline_result: 1.25 mm DLR-high images had higher SNR/CNR than 100% ASIR-V (P<0.05); DLR-middle and DLR-high subjective scores exceeded all ASIR-V levels, meeting diagnostic quality thresholds that thin-slice ASIR-V did not

model_family: 3D convolutional neural network ensemble (Bayesian-optimized, K-fold cross-validated)
patient_population: 168 annotated 3D ultrasound scans for model development; applied to N=9,795 ultrasounds from 1,763 participants at 20- and 30-week gestational age
clinical_problem: measuring fetal intracranial volume to study prenatal brain growth and sex differences
model_description: A 3D convolutional neural network ensemble was trained on 168 annotated 3D fetal ultrasound scans, using data augmentation, K-fold cross-validation, and Bayesian optimization, to automatically segment fetal intracranial volume (ICV). The trained model was applied to a large independent longitudinal cohort (9,795 ultrasounds, 1,763 participants at 20 and 30 weeks gestation) to measure ICV and study sex differences in fetal brain growth.
release_evidence: preprint, not yet published
title: Automated segmentation of fetal intracranial volume in 3D ultrasound using deep learning: identifying sex differences in prenatal brain development
dataset_size: 168 annotated 3D ultrasound scans for training; 9,795 ultrasounds from 1,763 participants for the applied study
headline_result: boys had significantly larger ICV at 20 weeks (B=2.83, p=1.4e-13) and 30 weeks (B=12.01, p=2.0e-28), with more pronounced ICV growth than girls (t=-4.395, p=1.3e-5)

patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound
clinical_problem: prenatal diagnostic ultrasound: fetal CNS examination, fetal cardiac anatomy assessment, quantification of cardiac function
model_description: A review describing how AI-assisted automated segmentation of 2D and 3D ultrasound images is being integrated into prenatal diagnostic workflow, assisting targeted examination of the fetal central nervous system and cardiac anatomy and the quantification of cardiac functional parameters, and discussing requirements for clinical implementation including trained staff.
title: Artificial intelligence in prenatal medicine

model_family: unsupervised machine learning (k-means clustering) on chest CT radiomics features
patient_population: 283 adolescents and adults with cystic fibrosis from a French multi-center prospective study, with baseline and 1-year follow-up chest CT
clinical_problem: predicting and evaluating treatment response to lumacaftor-ivacaftor in cystic fibrosis using lung CT phenotypes
model_description: In 283 adolescents and adults with cystic fibrosis starting lumacaftor-ivacaftor therapy, chest CT before and after 1 year of treatment was visually scored with a modified Bhalla score, and 120 radiomics features from pre-treatment CT were used in unsupervised k-means clustering to identify morphological lung-disease phenotypes. The resulting clusters were tested for association with lung function (FEV1) improvement on treatment.
title: Using chest computed tomography and unsupervised machine learning for predicting and evaluating response to lumacaftor-ivacaftor in people with cystic fibrosis
headline_result: Bhalla score decreased significantly after 1 year (-1.40±1.53 points, P<0.001); cluster C patients more likely to have ≥5% FEV1 improvement than other clusters (54% vs 32% and 33%, P=0.02)

model_family: iterative transformer modelling multiple stacks of MR slices as a sequence, trained on synthetically transformed data, alternating volume estimation with transformation updates
patient_population: synthetic data for training and evaluation, with real-world fetal MRI for demonstration
clinical_problem: volumetric reconstruction of the fetal brain from multiple stacks of motion-corrupted slices, which is highly sensitive to how the slice-to-volume transformations are initialized
model_description: Treats the stacks as a sequence and lets attention decide which slices inform which - so a slice whose own content is ambiguous can be placed using its neighbours, which is the situation that defeats pairwise registration under severe motion. Alternating between estimating the underlying volume and updating the transformations means the two problems bootstrap each other rather than one being solved first. Training on synthetic transformations sidesteps the absence of ground-truth motion in real data.
title: SVoRT: Iterative Transformer for Slice-to-Volume Registration in Fetal Brain MRI
headline_result: lower registration error and better reconstruction quality than existing state-of-the-art methods on synthetic data, with improved 3D reconstruction under severe fetal motion on real MRI

patient_population: the population covered by FDA-cleared AI/ML-enabled medical devices, with pediatric representation as one axis of analysis
clinical_problem: what has actually been cleared for use, through which pathway, and for whom
model_description: An analysis of every FDA-cleared AI/ML-enabled device by clearance pathway, timeline, specialty, decision type and recall history. Radiology dominates, approvals surged from 2018, and most went through 510(k) on substantial equivalence, which means no new clinical trial. Two gaps are named that bear directly on children: pediatric-focused devices and trials are underrepresented, and trials are geographically concentrated in the United States.
release_evidence: analysis of FDA-cleared commercial medical devices
title: FDA approved Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AI/ML)-Enabled Medical Devices: An updated landscape
dataset_size: the full FDA AI/ML-enabled device list
headline_result: a significant surge in approvals since 2018 with clear radiology dominance, reliance on the 510(k) pathway, and underrepresentation of pediatric-focused devices and trials

model_family: 94 radiomic features with K-best and sequential forward selection feeding a support vector machine with instance balancing, benchmarked against several deep segmentation architectures
patient_population: 60 axial MRI and 3D ultrasound images from pathological and clinical cases
clinical_problem: segmenting the uterus, placenta, umbilical cord, fetal lungs and fetal brain on fetal MRI and 3D ultrasound, for detection of fetal disorders and computer-assisted surgical planning
model_description: Takes radiomics, normally a classification tool, and uses it for segmentation - selecting about ten features per anatomical structure and classifying voxels with a balanced support vector machine. The practical output is a recipe pairing those features with particular architectures per modality (DeepLabV3+ or BiSeNet for MRI, PSPNet or Tiramisu for 3D ultrasound), and the fact that different networks win on different modalities is itself worth noting. Five distinct maternal and fetal structures across two modalities.
title: Assessment of Radiomics and Deep Learning for the Segmentation of Fetal and Maternal Anatomy in Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Ultrasound.
headline_result: combining ten selected radiomic features per anatomy with DeepLabV3+ or BiSeNet for MRI and PSPNet or Tiramisu for 3D ultrasound gave the best segmentation performance and robustness

body_region: brain (anterior cingulate cortex, ventrolateral prefrontal cortex)
patient_population: 38 youth (19 converters, 19 non-converters)
clinical_problem: Predicting which at-risk youth offspring of bipolar parents will develop their first mood episode using baseline brain metabolite levels
model_description: A support vector machine with a linear kernel classifies youth bipolar offspring as future mood-episode converters or non-converters based on baseline proton MR spectroscopy metabolite levels (choline, myo-inositol, phosphocreatine+creatine) from the anterior cingulate and ventrolateral prefrontal cortex.
title: Individual prediction of symptomatic converters in youth offspring of bipolar parents using proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy.
study_design: retrospective longitudinal case-control model development study
headline_result: classification accuracy up to 79.0% (left VLPFC combined metabolites)

model_family: radiomics with three feature selection methods and four classifiers compared
patient_population: 51 children (24 ependymoma, 27 medulloblastoma)
clinical_problem: telling ependymoma from medulloblastoma in a child, when the two look alike in age, location and symptoms
model_description: Extracts radiomic features from contrast-enhanced T1 and apparent diffusion coefficient maps of semi-automatically segmented tumors and classifies which of the two common posterior fossa tumors it is. Twelve combinations of feature selection and classifier were compared, which is the honest way to do this on 51 patients; the authors note explicitly that no single combination is best for every dataset.
title: Differentiation Between Ependymoma and Medulloblastoma in Children with Radiomics Approach.
headline_result: best model (logistic feature selection with random forest) reached AUC 0.91 (95% CI 0.787-0.968)

model_family: standard machine learning model over 430 high-throughput radiomic features per fetal lung image
patient_population: 548 fetal lung ultrasound images at the four-chamber view from 548 women delivering July 2018 to August 2019 at one hospital: 108 gestational diabetes, 71 pre-eclampsia, 25 both, 344 normal; imaged between 28 and 41 weeks
clinical_problem: whether fetal lung texture on ultrasound differs in pregnancies complicated by gestational diabetes or pre-eclampsia - conditions that raise the risk of neonatal respiratory complications - and whether that difference is separable from the texture change of normal maturation
model_description: Texture in the fetal lung changes with maturation, so any disease signal has to be separated from gestational age - and the study builds both models to check exactly that, finding the disease model far stronger than the age model. That is the right control. The clinical destination named by the authors is prediction of neonatal respiratory complications, which this does not yet do; what it establishes is that the ultrasound carries a signal distinguishing these pregnancies.
journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
title: Application of ultrasound-based radiomics technology in fetal-lung-texture analysis in pregnancies complicated by gestational diabetes and/or pre-eclampsia.
headline_result: AUC 0.95-0.99 with independent test set sensitivity 74.5-91.3%, specificity 75.7-88.4% and accuracy 80.6-86.4% for distinguishing gestational diabetes and pre-eclampsia pregnancies from normal

model_family: LASSO feature selection with logistic regression, presented as an individualized nomogram
patient_population: 624 stored midsagittal fetal profile images at 11+0 to 13+6 weeks in singleton pregnancies: 302 trisomy 21 and 322 euploid, split into training (400) and validation (224) sets with a 60-image retest set
clinical_problem: first-trimester screening for trisomy 21, where nuchal translucency plus maternal age is the standard combination and leaves substantial room for improvement
model_description: Uses twelve measured facial markers rather than the single nuchal translucency, and LASSO keeps eight - prenasal thickness ratio, facial profile line, three facial angles and the prefrontal skin distance among them. All are quantities a sonographer measures on the same stored midsagittal image, so no new acquisition is required. It beat the standard nuchal-translucency-plus-maternal-age model decisively (0.979 versus a substantially lower AUC, P < 0.001), and the nomogram makes the output a patient-specific probability rather than a screen-positive flag.
journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
title: Application of an individualized nomogram in first-trimester screening for trisomy 21.
headline_result: AUC 0.983 training, 0.979 validation and 0.997 retest, significantly higher than the nuchal translucency plus maternal age model (P < 0.001)

patient_population: not applicable (review)

title: Artificial intelligence and radiomics in pediatric molecular imaging.

model_family: commercial AI-based automated 3D fetal brain measurement tool
patient_population: 143 women at routine anatomical survey between 18+0 and 22+6 weeks, each scanned consecutively by both a sonographer and a physician
clinical_problem: obtaining the five standard fetal intracranial measurements - biparietal diameter, head circumference, transcerebellar diameter, cisterna magna and posterior horn of the lateral ventricle - from one sweep instead of five manual planes

The interesting number is not the agreement but the acquisition success - about 70% of patients yielded all five measurements on the first attempt and 4-5% never did, which is the practical yield a department would plan around.
release_evidence: SonoCNS Fetal Brain, an artificial intelligence-based tool on a commercial ultrasound system
journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
title: Accuracy of automated three-dimensional ultrasound imaging technique for fetal head biometry.

title: Reliability of Sonography-based Volume Computer Aided Diagnosis in the Normal Fetal Heart.
study_design: prospective reader-reliability study of automated volume computer-aided diagnosis software
headline_result: Success rate per diagnostic plane 90.6-99.6%; inter-observer kappa 0.439-0.933; intra-observer kappa 0.602-0.903

model_family: linear discriminant analysis (with Boruta feature selection)
patient_population: 239 infants with aortic coarctation undergoing thorax CTA and echocardiography
clinical_problem: classifying severity of aortic coarctation in infants from CT angiography anatomic measurements
model_description: Uses anatomic measurements (aortic diameters, cross-sectional areas) extracted from CT angiography as input, selected by the Boruta algorithm, to classify coarctation severity via linear discriminant analysis and assess re-coarctation risk via Cox regression.
title: Evaluating the severity of aortic coarctation in infants using anatomic features measured on CTA.
headline_result: Accuracy 88.6% (non-PDA) and 90.2% (PDA) for classifying CoA severity

model_family: artificial neural network for whole-lung segmentation on matrix pencil decomposition MRI
patient_population: 10 healthy children and 25 children with cystic fibrosis undergoing matrix pencil decomposition MRI
clinical_problem: whole-lung segmentation for free-breathing functional lung MRI in children, which is done by hand and whose variability propagates directly into the ventilation and perfusion numbers that the technique exists to produce
model_description: The design is a measurement study, not a segmentation contest: the same lungs were segmented by a physician twice, by a technician, and by the network, and the question is how much the ventilation and perfusion outcomes move. The finding is that two humans differ systematically from each other while one human differs from themselves only by noise - and that the network sits at the same distance from the physician as the technician does. So the argument for automation here is consistency in longitudinal studies, not speed.
title: The impact of segmentation on whole-lung functional MRI quantification: Repeatability and reproducibility from multiple human observers and an artificial neural network.
headline_result: Dice 0.89 +/- 0.03 between the network and the physician versus 0.88 +/- 0.02 between two human observers, with intraclass correlation above 0.98 for all comparisons

patient_population: 144 very preterm children and 33 full-term controls at age 7 years
clinical_problem: Whether diffusion MRI white-matter tract structure related to memory and emotion differs in very preterm children and can classify/predict outcomes
model_description: Diffusion MRI tractography measures (diffusivities, neurite density/orientation dispersion, fractional anisotropy) from five white-matter tracts are fed into support vector classification models to distinguish very preterm from full-term children, and support vector regression to predict memory/emotional outcomes
title: White matter tracts related to memory and emotion in very preterm children.
study_design: prospective cohort study with case-control MRI analysis
headline_result: SVM tract-based models significantly classified preterm vs. full-term children; SVM regression did not significantly predict memory/emotional outcomes

patient_population: children imaged in radiology practice
clinical_problem: which parts of the pediatric imaging pathway AI could plausibly improve
model_description: Walks the pediatric patient pathway and asks, at each step, where AI has been shown feasible and where it has not, borrowing from the adult literature to propose targets. Its opening observation is the important one for this database: cancer screening AI has had enormous attention while children's imaging has been neglected, which is a statement about where development effort has gone rather than where the clinical need is.
title: Artificial intelligence in paediatric radiology: Future opportunities.

clinical_problem: Automated segmentation of fetal kidney volume and vascularity from 3D ultrasound to assess fetal renal development/wellbeing
model_description: Fully convolutional neural networks fuse 3D B-Mode and power Doppler ultrasound volumes using multi-parametric input fusion to automatically segment the fetal kidney.
release_evidence: This work and available source code provides a framework to increase the parameter space...
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: Multi-Parametric Fusion of 3D Power Doppler Ultrasound for Fetal Kidney Segmentation Using Fully Convolutional Neural Networks.
headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient 0.81, Hausdorff distance 8.96 mm (best fusion strategy); ICC 0.93

patient_population: 712 youth with a lifetime major depressive episode and 712 typically developing youth matched on age/sex (Philadelphia Neurodevelopmental Cohort); neuroimaging subset MDD n=368, TD n=200
clinical_problem: identifying neurocognitive subtypes of depression in youth and their neural activation signatures
model_description: Input is neurocognitive test performance (accuracy and speed) and, in a subset, n-back working-memory task fMRI activation; a semi-supervised machine learning algorithm delineates neurocognitive subtypes of depressed youth and relates them to fMRI activation patterns.
journal: Neuropsychopharmacology : official publication of the American College of Neuropsychopharmacology
title: Neurocognitive and functional heterogeneity in depressed youth.
study_design: cross-sectional cohort study with semi-supervised machine learning subtyping
dataset_size: 712 youth with MDD and 712 typically developing youth; fMRI subset 368 MDD, 200 TD
headline_result: three distinct neurocognitive subtypes identified, differing in fMRI activation profiles during a working-memory task

model_family: deep learning noise reduction applied to virtual monoenergetic dual-energy reconstructions
patient_population: 29 pediatric patients aged 2-19 years, each with a prior standard single-energy CT for comparison
clinical_problem: reducing both radiation dose and iodinated contrast load in children undergoing abdominal CT
model_description: Combines two dose-sparing ideas that are usually studied separately: dual-energy acquisition with reduced iodine concentration, and deep-learning denoising of the resulting low-energy virtual monoenergetic images. Each alone increases noise; together they held image quality while cutting radiation by about 20% and iodine by 14%. Contrast load matters independently of dose in children with repeated imaging or impaired renal function.
title: Noise reduction approach in pediatric abdominal CT combining deep learning and dual-energy technique.
headline_result: overall and diagnostic image quality maintained against standard single-energy CT, with 19.6% lower dose index and 14.3% lower total iodine administration

model_family: deep learning tract segmentation (TractSeg) plus fixel-based analysis
patient_population: 50 right-handed medication-naive children with ADHD and 56 non-ADHD controls, ages 9-11
clinical_problem: Do children with ADHD and fine motor difficulties show measurable differences in corticospinal tract microstructure on diffusion MRI, using an automated deep-learning tract-delineation approach?
model_description: A semi-automated deep-learning tool (TractSeg) delineates the corticospinal tract bilaterally on high-angular-resolution diffusion MRI, from which fixel-based metrics (fibre density, cross-section) are extracted and compared between children with and without ADHD.
title: Understanding motor difficulties in children with ADHD: A fixel-based analysis of the corticospinal tract.
study_design: prospective single-center case-control diffusion MRI study using an automated deep-learning segmentation tool
headline_result: Children with ADHD showed significantly lower diffusion (fixel-based) metrics bilaterally in the corticospinal tract versus controls, but no significant correlation with fine motor task performance

model_family: multi-voxel pattern analysis with linear support vector machine
patient_population: 146 adolescents (66 with internet gaming disorder, 80 healthy controls), discovery cohort; 28 adolescents (14/14), independent validation cohort
clinical_problem: identifying internet gaming disorder in adolescents using resting-state functional connectivity
model_description: Input: seed-based resting-state functional connectivity patterns of the ventral tegmental area and substantia nigra; output: classification of internet gaming disorder vs. healthy control.
title: Identification of internet gaming disorder individuals based on ventral tegmental area resting-state functional connectivity.
study_design: case-control classification study with independent validation cohort
headline_result: Discovery cohort: mean accuracy 86.1%, AUC 0.91; independent validation: accuracy 78.5%, sensitivity 71.4%, specificity 85.8%

patient_population: 273 subjects with known or suspected chronic liver disease (178 internal cross-validation, 95 external validation)
clinical_problem: classifying severity of liver stiffness (chronic liver disease) in children and young adults without MR elastography
model_description: DeepLiverNet, a deep transfer learning model, takes T2-weighted MRI images plus clinical/demographic data as input and classifies liver stiffness as no/mild vs. moderate/severe, referenced against MR elastography.
title: DeepLiverNet: a deep transfer learning model for classifying liver stiffness using clinical and T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging data in children and young adults.
study_design: retrospective model development with internal cross-validation and external validation
headline_result: Internal AuROC 0.86, accuracy 88.0%; external validation AuROC 0.79, accuracy 80.0%

model_family: region-proposal CNN for head localization followed by a regression CNN trained on distance fields
patient_population: the public HC18 Challenge dataset: 999 training and 335 test images
clinical_problem: head circumference measurement on fetal ultrasound and the intra- and inter-operator variability that makes serial growth assessment noisy
model_description: Argues, correctly, that head circumference is an edge-delineation problem and that segmenting the whole head is a detour - so the second network regresses the contour directly, trained against distance fields rather than a binary mask. Being evaluated on the public HC18 challenge set makes the comparison with the segmentation-based literature a fair one, and the regression approach came out ahead.
journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
title: A regression framework to head-circumference delineation from US fetal images.
study_design: retrospective model development on a public benchmark
headline_result: mean absolute difference 1.90 +/- 1.76 mm and Dice 97.75 +/- 1.32%, exceeding published approaches on the same challenge data

patient_population: individual- and group-level diffusion MRI data, including a dataset of children with ADHD
clinical_problem: reducing motion-related bias in diffusion MRI parameter estimation, tested in part on a pediatric ADHD dataset
model_description: A hierarchical convolutional neural network estimates diffusion kurtosis/tensor parameters from motion-corrupted diffusion MRI after data rejection, aiming to minimize residual motion-level-dependent bias compared with conventional correction methods.
title: Deep learning-based method for reducing residual motion effects in diffusion parameter estimation.
headline_result: H-CNN minimally sensitive to motion effects even with 70-90% of data rejected; ameliorated spurious group differences in a pediatric ADHD dataset

patient_population: children undergoing bone age assessment
clinical_problem: bone age assessment in pediatric endocrinology, sixty years after the atlases were published
model_description: An endocrinology-side overview of how bone age is measured now. It covers the Greulich-Pyle and Tanner-Whitehouse atlases, the automated programs that have been validated against them (which are precise, remove inter- and intra-rater variability and cut reading time), and the radiation-free alternatives using ultrasound or MRI that are the least-developed part of this field.
journal: Journal of clinical research in pediatric endocrinology
title: Traditional and New Methods of Bone Age Assessment-An Overview.

patient_population: 43 adolescents age 11-16 with mild traumatic brain injury or orthopedic injury
clinical_problem: predicting post-concussion symptom recovery at one week after mild traumatic brain injury using imaging
model_description: A Genetic Fuzzy Trees AI system uses volumetric MRI and diffusion tensor imaging inputs to classify adolescents as recovered or not recovered from concussion symptoms at one week post-injury.
title: Predicting Post-Concussion Symptom Recovery in Adolescents Using a Novel Artificial Intelligence.
headline_result: 100% training / 62% validation accuracy; sensitivity 59%, specificity 65%

model_family: radiomics signature combined with clinical factors in a nomogram
patient_population: 78 children with neuroblastoma (55 training, 23 test)
clinical_problem: predicting MYCN amplification in neuroblastoma, which determines risk group and therapy
model_description: A second, independent CT radiomics attempt at MYCN status in neuroblastoma, on a smaller cohort than the other in this database. It reports that both pre- and post-contrast phases contribute, and that adding clinical factors to the radiomics signature clearly beats a clinical model alone. Two independent groups reaching similar conclusions on this question is worth more than either result on its own.
title: Radiogenomics of neuroblastoma in pediatric patients: CT-based radiomics signature in predicting MYCN amplification.
headline_result: combined clinical-radiomics nomogram AUC 0.95 in training and 0.91 in testing, against 0.82 and 0.70 for the clinical model alone

model_family: CNN with joint spatial, channel and scale attention
body_region: placenta and fetal brain (and skin lesions, non-radiologic)
patient_population: fetuses imaged with MRI; a second application uses dermoscopic skin lesion images
clinical_problem: segmenting the placenta and fetal brain on fetal MRI
model_description: Takes a fetal MRI slice and returns a segmentation of the placenta or fetal brain, using three kinds of attention so the network weighs the right location, the right feature channels and the right scale at once. The attention maps can be displayed, which is the paper's explainability claim. It is about fifteen times smaller than a comparable state-of-the-art segmentation network.
release_evidence: our code is available at https://github.com/HiLab-git/CA-Net
title: CA-Net: Comprehensive Attention Convolutional Neural Networks for Explainable Medical Image Segmentation.
headline_result: Dice improved over U-Net from 84.79% to 87.08% for the placenta and 93.20% to 95.88% for the fetal brain

patient_population: fetal ultrasound datasets (domains defined by shadow artifacts and by acquisition device)
clinical_problem: Can a fetal ultrasound classifier generalize to unseen classes and different scanner domains without large amounts of newly labeled data?
model_description: MIDNet learns generalizable categorical image features (disentangled from domain-specific features like scanner or artifact type) using semi-supervised learning, to classify fetal ultrasound images into categories not seen during training.
title: Mutual Information-Based Disentangled Neural Networks for Classifying Unseen Categories in Different Domains: Application to Fetal Ultrasound Imaging.
headline_result: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods for classification of unseen categories in a target domain with sparsely labeled data (no single summary number given)

model_family: dilated convolutional neural network combined with a relation network
patient_population: 51 children with focal epilepsy undergoing preoperative diffusion-weighted imaging connectome analysis before epilepsy surgery
clinical_problem: predicting preoperative language impairment and postoperative seizure outcome in children undergoing epilepsy surgery
model_description: Preoperative diffusion-weighted imaging is used to build whole-brain structural connectomes. A 'dilated CNN + RN' model (a dilated convolutional network combined with a relation network) reasons about sparsely distributed axonal-connection dependencies to predict expressive and receptive language-impairment scores and to classify postoperative seizure outcome (freedom vs. recurrence) in children with focal epilepsy. Gradient-based activation maps highlight the brain regions driving each prediction.
title: Deep Relational Reasoning for the Prediction of Language Impairment and Postoperative Seizure Outcome Using Preoperative DWI Connectome Data of Children With Focal Epilepsy.
study_design: retrospective single-center technical development and validation
headline_result: average improvement of 90.2% and 97.3% in predicting expressive and receptive language scores, and 2.2% and 4% improvement in classifying seizure freedom and recurrence, versus other state-of-the-art algorithms

model_family: similarity network fusion across imaging and behavioral measures
patient_population: 176 children aged 6-16 with autism, ADHD or OCD from the POND network, all scanned on the same 3T scanner
clinical_problem: whether the diagnostic boundaries between autism, ADHD and OCD correspond to anything in the brain
model_description: Fuses cortical thickness, subcortical volume, white matter anisotropy and behavioral measures into a single similarity structure, then finds groups that cut across the three diagnoses. The four resulting transdiagnostic groups differed in everyday adaptive functioning, which the DSM categories did not capture as well. Scanning all children on one scanner removes the usual site confound.
journal: Neuropsychopharmacology : official publication of the American College of Neuropsychopharmacology
title: Integration of brain and behavior measures for identification of data-driven groups cutting across children with ASD, ADHD, or OCD.
headline_result: four transdiagnostic groups driven mainly by cortical thickness in socio-emotional and attention networks plus inattention symptoms; groups remained stable across resampling and differed significantly in adaptive functioning

patient_population: 362 youth with childhood ADHD followed for an average of 4.8 years, plus a never-affected comparison group
clinical_problem: predicting whether childhood ADHD symptoms will worsen, stay stable, or improve over time
model_description: Takes polygenic risk scores, baseline cognitive testing, and diffusion/volumetric brain MRI features as input and outputs a machine-learning classification of future ADHD symptom trajectory (worsening, stable, or improving) versus never-affected.
title: Predicting the course of ADHD symptoms through the integration of childhood genomic, neural, and cognitive features.
study_design: prospective longitudinal cohort study with machine-learning classification, trained and tested on independent groups
headline_result: AUC >0.79 for classifying never-affected vs. worsening/stable/improving symptom groups

patient_population: children undergoing clinical CT (19 patients, mean age 11 years)
clinical_problem: keeping diagnostic image quality on pediatric CT while cutting radiation dose
model_description: Reconstructs the CT image from the raw projection data with a trained network in place of filtered back projection or iterative reconstruction, removing noise without the waxy texture model-based iterative reconstruction introduces. Assessed both by a mathematical observer model across object sizes and contrasts and by three pediatric radiologists scoring edge definition, noise and conspicuity of low-contrast structures.
release_evidence: the abstract does not say whether the algorithm is a vendor product or research software
title: Improving Image Quality and Reducing Radiation Dose for Pediatric CT by Using Deep Learning Reconstruction.
study_design: retrospective single-center image-quality study with reader assessment
headline_result: object detectability improved 51% over filtered back projection, 18% over statistical iterative and 11% over model-based iterative reconstruction; radiologists preferred it (7.0 vs 6.2, 6.2 and 4.6); 52% greater dose reduction than statistical iterative reconstruction

model_family: support vector machine with recursive feature elimination on FreeSurfer cortical measures
patient_population: 66 adolescents and young adults with major depressive disorder
clinical_problem: separating adolescents with depression who have attempted suicide from those with ideation only
model_description: Takes structural MRI cortical thickness and volume measures and classifies whether a depressed adolescent has attempted suicide or has ideation without attempt. The top-ranked features were orbitofrontal and cingulate thickness. The clinical framing is risk stratification for prevention, though the design is cross-sectional so it separates groups rather than predicting a future attempt.
title: Identification of suicidality in adolescent major depressive disorder patients using sMRI: A machine learning approach.
headline_result: 78.6% cross-validated balanced accuracy (sensitivity 73.2%, specificity 84.0%, positive predictive value 88.2%)

patient_population: 40 infant hip examinations
clinical_problem: measuring developmental dysplasia of the hip reproducibly from ultrasound
model_description: Automated 3D ultrasound bone segmentation, using a random forest classifier and rotation/intensity-invariant filters, computes dysplasia metrics for the hip automatically.
title: 3-D Ultrasound Imaging Reliability of Measuring Dysplasia Metrics in Infants.
study_design: retrospective method development and reliability study
headline_result: ~70% reduction in variability of key 3D vs 2D dysplasia metrics

patient_population: 200 children with obstructive hydrocephalus from four pediatric hospitals plus 199 controls, with external testing at a fifth hospital
clinical_problem: tracking ventricular size objectively over time in children with hydrocephalus, which currently drives shunt decisions by eye
model_description: Takes a T2-weighted MRI and returns the ventricles outlined and their volume in about a second and a half. Built deliberately for clinical use rather than research: trained across four pediatric hospitals, tested at a fifth, and benchmarked against FreeSurfer, which it beat on both accuracy and speed. Serial volumes rather than subjective impression are what would change hydrocephalus management.
title: Artificial intelligence for automatic cerebral ventricle segmentation and volume calculation: a clinical tool for the evaluation of pediatric hydrocephalus.
study_design: retrospective multicenter study with external validation
dataset_size: 399 children across four hospitals, plus an external dataset from a fifth
headline_result: Dice 0.901 overall (0.946 in hydrocephalus), 0.926 on external data from a fifth hospital, more accurate than FreeSurfer at 1.48 seconds per scan

model_family: 3D patch-based U-net networks, one per modality
patient_population: 80 children with neuroblastoma or Wilms tumour
clinical_problem: choosing between proton and photon radiotherapy for a child, which currently requires planning both
model_description: Predicts what the proton and the photon dose distribution would look like for a specific child's anatomy, without running either planning process. Two radiation oncologists then chose a modality from the predicted organ-at-risk dose difference and reached the same decision as from the fully planned distributions in 18 of 20 patients. The intended use is explicit: to identify the better technique where proton planning expertise or capacity is not available.
journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
title: Deep learning prediction of proton and photon dose distributions for paediatric abdominal tumours.
study_design: retrospective single-center technical validation with clinician assessment
dataset_size: 80 children (60 for training with 5-fold cross-validation, 20 for inference)
headline_result: dose-volume histogram differences within 6% of planned distributions; identical modality selection in 18 of 20 patients

model_family: CNN with longitudinal pooling layer and consistency regularization
patient_population: ADNI (N=404, Alzheimer's), an alcohol use disorder dataset (N=274 controls + 329 AUD), and 255 youths from NCANDA (National Consortium on Alcohol and NeuroDevelopment in Adolescence)
clinical_problem: Can a machine learning model track gradual, longitudinal disease progression from repeated brain MRI scans more consistently (avoiding clinically implausible classification changes across visits) than standard CNN+RNN approaches?
model_description: A CNN architecture with a novel longitudinal pooling layer combines features across a subject's repeated MRI visits and enforces classification consistency across visits, evaluated on Alzheimer's, alcohol use disorder, and adolescent (NCANDA) longitudinal MRI classification tasks.
release_evidence: 'The code is available at https://github.com/ouyangjiahong/longitudinal-pooling'
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: Longitudinal Pooling & Consistency Regularization to Model Disease Progression From MRIs.
headline_result: Superior to other widely used longitudinal classification approaches across all three datasets (no single pediatric-specific accuracy number given)

model_family: shared response modeling (machine learning functional alignment)
patient_population: children ages 3-12 years watching a movie during fMRI; exact N not stated
clinical_problem: evaluating maturity and localization of adult-like brain functions in children using task fMRI functional alignment
model_description: A machine learning method called shared response modeling learns a lower-dimensional feature space from adult fMRI activity recorded while watching a movie. These learned features are translated into each child's individual anatomical brain space (ages 3-12) and used to reconstruct predicted activity, which is correlated with the child's actual fMRI activity to quantify the maturity and localization of adult-like brain functions across childhood.
title: Emergence and organization of adult brain function throughout child development.
study_design: cross-sectional developmental fMRI study, technical development
headline_result: Reconstructed activity correlated reliably with children's actual fMRI activity throughout cortex; correlation strength in precuneus, inferior frontal gyrus, and lateral occipital cortex predicted chronological age

patient_population: 48 images selected from 91 transabdominal fetal ultrasound scans, mean gestational age 26 weeks
clinical_problem: automatically extracting standard diagnostic fetal head imaging planes (transventricular, transcerebellar) from 3D ultrasound volumes
model_description: Takes 3D fetal head ultrasound volumes as input and automatically extracts standard 2D diagnostic planes (transventricular and transcerebellar) as output, compared against manually and operator-selected planes.
title: Towards automated extraction of 2D standard fetal head planes from 3D ultrasound acquisitions: A clinical evaluation and quality assessment comparison.
study_design: retrospective clinical evaluation study with observer image-quality review
headline_result: 67% of transventricular and 45-55% of transcerebellar planes rated adequate quality; no significant difference between 3D methods

model_family: convolutional neural network on cropped unilateral hip joint images
patient_population: 2601 hip AP radiographs yielding 5076 cropped unilateral hip joint images, split 80/10/10, labeled normal or DDH by three radiologists
clinical_problem: detecting developmental dysplasia of the hip on anteroposterior pelvic radiographs, the study most often available outside a pediatric centre and the one most often read by someone without pediatric training
model_description: The comparison is stratified by reader experience, and the result is the one that recurs across pediatric AI: the algorithm was statistically indistinguishable from the radiologist with pediatric experience and clearly better than the one without. Reporting the precision-recall curve alongside the ROC is the right choice for a screening problem with few positives, and it is where the gap between the model (0.973) and the weakest reader (0.618) is starkest.
title: Diagnostic Performance of a New Convolutional Neural Network Algorithm for Detecting Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip on Anteroposterior Radiographs.
study_design: retrospective model development with reader comparison
headline_result: ROC AUC 0.988 and PRC AUC 0.973 for the algorithm versus 0.988-0.919 and 0.618-0.958 for radiologists; sensitivity 98.0%, specificity 98.1%, NPV 99.8%; no significant difference from the pediatric-experienced radiologist (p = 0.180) but significantly better than the inexperienced one (p < 0.001)

clinical_problem: differentiating adolescents with major depressive disorder from healthy controls using brain connectivity
model_description: Input is static and dynamic functional connectivity features derived from resting-state fMRI across 85 brain regions; output is a support-vector-machine classification of adolescent MDD versus healthy control.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: Classification of Adolescent Major Depressive Disorder Via Static and Dynamic Connectivity.
headline_result: classification accuracy 0.82, sensitivity 0.84, specificity 0.79 (leave-one-out cross-validation)

clinical_problem: Identifying hippocampal subfield volume and connectivity features that discriminate traumatized children with PTSD from those without, using an automated segmentation and machine learning approach
model_description: Input: automated hippocampal subfield segmentation from structural MRI and subfield-centered functional connectivity; output: PTSD vs. non-PTSD classification, via random forest classifiers using discriminative subfield features
title: Hippocampal subfield alterations in pediatric patients with post-traumatic stress disorder.

clinical_problem: Reducing acquisition (scan) time for pediatric 99mTc-DMSA renal SPECT imaging while maintaining diagnostic accuracy for detecting kidney abnormalities
model_description: Input: half-acquisition-time SPECT raw data; output: reconstructed full-acquisition-time-quality SPECT images, via a deep learning reconstruction model
title: Reducing scan time of paediatric 99mTc-DMSA SPECT via deep learning.
headline_result: accuracy 91.7%, sensitivity 83.3%, specificity 100% for detecting affected kidneys

model_family: fully convolutional network with deep attentive modules, mixed kernel convolutions, deep supervision and residual connections
patient_population: reconstructed fetal brain MRI of fetuses scanned at 16 to 39 weeks gestation (mean 28.6 +/- 5.3)
clinical_problem: segmenting the fetal cortical plate, the measurement that quantitative studies of cortical folding and brain maturation depend on and that is otherwise refined by hand
model_description: A segmentation network built around the specific difficulty of this structure: the cortical plate is thin relative to the resolution of reconstructed fetal MRI, partial volume is severe, and its shape changes continuously across the second and third trimesters. Attention modules with mixed kernel sizes are the response. Under a minute per brain, which is what makes population-scale studies of cortical folding practical.
title: A Deep Attentive Convolutional Neural Network for Automatic Cortical Plate Segmentation in Fetal MRI.
study_design: retrospective model development with expert evaluation
headline_result: average Dice 0.87, Hausdorff distance 0.96 mm and symmetric surface difference 0.28 mm, outperforming several state-of-the-art deep models and a multi-atlas method

model_family: self-supervised attention CNN (Part Extracting and Age Recognition Network)
patient_population: children undergoing hand radiography for bone age assessment (public RSNA 2017 dataset)
clinical_problem: bone age assessment
model_description: A self-supervised model (PEAR-Net) discovers discriminative hand regions without needing precise bounding-box annotations, using only image-level weak labels. A Part Extracting agent automatically finds informative regions of interest, and an Age Recognition agent uses them to estimate bone age; the two agents reinforce each other during joint training. Evaluated on the public RSNA 2017 Pediatric Bone Age dataset.
release_evidence: Project is available at http://imcc.ustc.edu.cn/project/ssambaa/
title: Self-Supervised Attention Mechanism for Pediatric Bone Age Assessment With Efficient Weak Annotation.
headline_result: state-of-the-art performance with mean absolute error of 3.99 months
