clinical_problem: Optimizing DCE-MRI acquisition and using perfusion parameters to help diagnose temporomandibular joint involvement in children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis
model_description: A methodological optimization of dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (motion correction, sampling rate, pharmacokinetic modeling) of the temporomandibular joint, followed by unsupervised k-means stratification and supervised random forest classification of left-right TMJ perfusion differences to assess diagnostic value against structural imaging.
title: Effects of motion correction, sampling rate and parametric modelling in dynamic contrast enhanced MRI of the temporomandibular joint in children affected with juvenile idiopathic arthritis.

clinical_problem: Automated diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder in children using task-based fMRI responses to a speech task.

title: A robust DWT-CNN-based CAD system for early diagnosis of autism using task-based fMRI.
headline_result: 80% classification accuracy, sensitivity 84%, specificity 76%

title: Automatic brain extraction from 3D fetal MR image with deep learning-based multi-step framework.

clinical_problem: review of 3D ultrasound techniques for examining fetal brain views, including central nervous system malformations, with discussion of emerging AI applications
model_description: Narrative review describing 3D ultrasound acquisition and analysis techniques for fetal brain examination, including discussion of emerging artificial intelligence and deep machine learning applications for quantitative assessment of fetal cortical development.
title: Brain views that benefit from three-dimensional ultrasound.

clinical_problem: Can an object detection AI model identify rickets on pediatric wrist radiographs using a small dataset and modest computing resources?
model_description: Takes pediatric wrist radiographs as input; an object detection model outputs a labeled bounding box identifying rickets-related metaphyseal changes vs. normal.

headline_result: Overall accuracy 86%; sensitivity 80%/specificity 95% for rickets, sensitivity 89%/specificity 90% for normal

patient_population: 63 pediatric patients with refractory epilepsy and 259 pediatric healthy controls
clinical_problem: classifying pediatric epilepsy patients from healthy controls using resting-state fMRI
model_description: a CNN takes resting-state fMRI latency (BOLD signal delay) maps as input and outputs a binary classification of epilepsy vs. healthy control
title: Convolutional Neural Networks for Pediatric Refractory Epilepsy Classification Using Resting-State Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
headline_result: accuracy 74%, sensitivity 85%, specificity 71%, AUC 0.86 on held-out test data

model_family: symmetricity-driven pair-of-cube Siamese convolutional neural network over 386 symmetry features
patient_population: 201 pediatric patients with temporal lobe epilepsy and 24 age-matched controls who underwent 18F-FDG PET-CT
clinical_problem: localizing the epileptic focus on 18F-FDG PET in children with temporal lobe epilepsy, where the focus may be either hypo- or hyper-metabolic with no clear boundary and misdiagnosis is common
model_description: The architecture encodes the way a nuclear medicine physician actually reads these studies - by comparing the two hemispheres - as a Siamese network over paired cubes, and then reports the metabolic abnormality of the predicted focus as an asymmetry index. Comparison is against the three things it would replace: visual assessment, SPM, and a divergence-based logistic regression. Dice around 0.5 sounds modest until read against expert visual assessment at 0.31 to 0.44 on the same cases.
journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
title: A deep learning framework for 18F-FDG PET imaging diagnosis in pediatric patients with temporal lobe epilepsy.
headline_result: Dice 0.51 for focus localization versus 0.24 for SPM (P < 0.01) and 0.31-0.44 for visual assessment; classification AUC 0.93 versus 0.72 for logistic regression

patient_population: 152 serial 3D ultrasound scans from 10 preterm infants with post-hemorrhagic ventricular dilatation (mean birth weight 1233 g, mean GA 28.1 weeks)
clinical_problem: measuring ventricular volume in preterm infants with post-hemorrhagic ventricular dilatation
model_description: A 2D convolutional neural network takes 3D cranial ultrasound volumes as input and outputs automatic segmentation of brain ventricles, from which ventricular volume is calculated.
title: Automatic segmentation of ventricular volume by 3D ultrasonography in post haemorrhagic ventricular dilatation among preterm infants.
dataset_size: 152 3D ultrasound scans from 10 preterm infants; 230 manually segmented ventricles (108 training, 122 validation)
headline_result: ICC 0.944 (0.874-0.971) vs. manual segmentation; Dice 0.8 ± 0.01

patient_population: 211 NF1-related scoliosis patients (131 dystrophic, 80 nondystrophic), plus 100 congenital scoliosis, 100 adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients, and 114 normal controls
clinical_problem: distinguishing dystrophic from nondystrophic scoliosis in neurofibromatosis type 1 and classifying scoliosis subtypes to assist surgical diagnosis
model_description: Input: whole-spine AP and lateral x-ray images; output: classification of scoliosis type (dystrophic vs nondystrophic NF1-S, or scoliosis subtype) using a bilinear-like feature comparison between the two views.
title: Classification of neurofibromatosis-related dystrophic or nondystrophic scoliosis based on image features using Bilateral CNN.
study_design: retrospective model development with cross-validation and comparison to surgeons
dataset_size: 211 NF1-S patients (131 dystrophic, 80 nondystrophic); 100 congenital scoliosis; 100 AIS; 114 normal controls
headline_result: 80.36% accuracy for NF1 classification (vs 61.90-76.19% for other DLAs; 77.5%/65.0% for senior/junior surgeons); 87.92% accuracy for primary classification

model_family: deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) + fully connected neural network (FCNN) classifier
patient_population: 960 samples (children) in KBD-endemic areas of Tibet, 2017-2018 (219 KBD positive, 741 negative)
clinical_problem: automated screening for Kashin-Beck disease (an endemic bone disease causing short stature) from hand X-rays in children in rural areas with limited access to orthopedists
model_description: Input: hand X-ray images; output: binary classification of Kashin-Beck disease vs. normal, combining global (whole hand shape) and local (metaphysis texture/edge) deep features fused for classification.
journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
title: Kashin-Beck disease diagnosis based on deep learning from hand X-ray images.
study_design: retrospective model development and internal evaluation
headline_result: accuracy 98.5%, sensitivity 97.6% (multi-feature fusion method)

model_family: multiclass convolutional neural network (dual-pathway hybrid model with transfer learning)
body_region: placenta, amniotic fluid and fetus (early pregnancy)

clinical_problem: automated volumetric segmentation of the placenta for early pregnancy screening to predict adverse pregnancy outcomes
model_description: Input is a 3D ultrasound volume from early pregnancy; output is a multiclass segmentation of the placenta, amniotic fluid and fetus, using a dual-pathway CNN with transfer learning to enable population-based screening based on placental volume.
journal: IEEE transactions on ultrasonics, ferroelectrics, and frequency control
title: Fully Automated 3-D Ultrasound Segmentation of the Placenta, Amniotic Fluid, and Fetus for Early Pregnancy Assessment.
dataset_size: 2,093 placental volumes plus 300 additional annotated volumes
headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient 0.84 and average Hausdorff distance 0.38 mm for placental segmentation

patient_population: 69 youths (mean age 14.55 years) with varying irritability across DMDD, ADHD, anxiety disorder, and control groups
clinical_problem: predicting irritability severity in youth from task fMRI functional connectivity during frustration
model_description: Functional connectivity measured during a frustrating cognitive-flexibility fMRI task is input to connectome-based predictive modeling, a machine learning approach with 10-fold cross-validation. The model predicts child- and parent-reported irritability scores across a transdiagnostic sample of 69 youths, identifying predictive networks spanning motor-sensory, subcortical, salience, frontoparietal, and medial frontal regions.
journal: Neuropsychopharmacology : official publication of the American College of Neuropsychopharmacology
title: Functional connectivity during frustration: a preliminary study of predictive modeling of irritability in youth.
headline_result: Connectivity during frustration predicted child-reported irritability (rho = 0.24, RMSE = 2.02, p = 0.03, permutation testing)

model_family: V-Net with attention gates, deep supervision and a multi-scale loss
patient_population: fetuses across trimesters in the public HC18 challenge dataset (355 test images)
clinical_problem: measuring head circumference from a fetal ultrasound image automatically
model_description: Segments the fetal skull on a 2D ultrasound image, then fits an ellipse to it and reports head circumference. Attention gates and deep supervision are what lift it above plain U-Net and V-Net on this task, which is hard because the appearance of the fetal head changes markedly between trimesters. Benchmarked on a public challenge, so the numbers are directly comparable with other entries.
release_evidence: the code of DAG V-Net will be made available publicly on https://github.com/xiaojinmao-code/
title: Fetal Ultrasound Image Segmentation for Automatic Head Circumference Biometry Using Deeply Supervised Attention-Gated V-Net.
study_design: technical development on a public benchmark
dataset_size: HC18 challenge training set with augmentation; 355 test images
headline_result: Dice 97.93%, head circumference absolute difference 1.77 ± 1.69 mm, Hausdorff distance 1.29 ± 0.79 mm; fifth place in the HC18 challenge

model_family: 30 competing deep-learning segmentation methods, 8 reviewed in detail
patient_population: 6-month-old infants; training from UNC, testing from UNC/UMN, Stanford and Emory with different protocols and scanners
clinical_problem: segmenting 6-month infant brain MRI, and whether any method survives being moved to another site's scanner
model_description: A challenge report rather than a single model. Thirty teams segmented 6-month infant brain MRI into white matter, gray matter and CSF, at the age when the two tissues are nearly isointense and conventional tools fail. The design deliberately puts the test data at different institutions from the training data, and the conclusion is the useful one: multi-site consistency remains unsolved, so a model that works on one scanner should not be assumed to work on another.
title: Multi-Site Infant Brain Segmentation Algorithms: The iSeg-2019 Challenge.
headline_result: top methods reviewed across whole brain, regions of interest and gyral landmarks; multi-site consistency identified as still an open issue

model_family: U-net variant combining atrous convolution, multi-scale side-input layers and side-output layers, inside a hierarchical pipeline
patient_population: antenatal ultrasound examinations, sizes not stated
clinical_problem: measuring the amniotic fluid index, which informs fetal development, well-being and perinatal prognosis and whose accuracy varies greatly with the sonographer's experience
model_description: The paper is unusually clear about why this is hard - reverberation artifact, regions that mimic fluid, floating matter, pockets of arbitrary shape, and boundaries that are simply missing from the image - and the architecture answers each with multi-scale context and side supervision. The pipeline follows the clinician's anatomical approach rather than segmenting blind. Claimed as the first automated amniotic fluid index measurement.
title: Automated ultrasound assessment of amniotic fluid index using deep learning.
headline_result: Dice 0.877 +/- 0.086 for amniotic fluid segmentation, with mean absolute error 2.666 +/- 2.986 and mean relative error 0.018 +/- 0.023 for the amniotic fluid index

model_family: deep neural network classification models on structural MRI
patient_population: children and adults with ADHD and controls, drawn from ENIGMA-ADHD consortium samples
clinical_problem: whether the structural brain signature of ADHD in children is the same one seen in adults, tested by asking a model trained on one age group to classify the other
model_description: A study that uses classification accuracy as a hypothesis test rather than as a product claim. The interesting result is the cross-age transfer: a model trained only on adults still separated children with ADHD from controls, which is evidence that the anatomy the network keys on is continuous from childhood into adulthood. Prediction was stronger in children than adults, consistent with the ENIGMA effect sizes.
title: Evidence for similar structural brain anomalies in youth and adult attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a machine learning analysis.
headline_result: structural MRI significantly separated ADHD from control in both children and adults, and the adult-trained model significantly predicted ADHD in the child sample

model_family: convolutional neural network taking paired ultra-low-dose PET and MRI input
patient_population: 33 children and young adults aged 3-30 with lymphoma undergoing whole-body FDG PET/MRI
age_groups: child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: cutting the radiation burden of repeated staging PET scans in children with cancer
model_description: Takes a simulated 6.25% dose PET scan together with the MRI acquired at the same time and outputs an image that behaves like a standard-dose PET. What makes this credible is that it checks the quantitative measure clinicians act on: SUVmax, which noise inflates at ultra-low dose, was restored to standard-dose values, and reader confidence agreed with the standard scans far better than with the low-dose ones.
journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
title: Artificial intelligence enables whole-body positron emission tomography scans with minimal radiation exposure.
study_design: retrospective single-center study with reader assessment
dataset_size: 33 children and young adults with lymphoma
headline_result: reader agreement with standard clinical scans kappa 0.942 for AI-reconstructed images versus 0.650 for 6.25% dose images; SUVmax restored to standard-dose values

clinical_problem: Non-invasive assessment of fetal lung maturity to predict risk of neonatal respiratory distress syndrome
model_description: Review describing quantusFLM, a quantitative ultrasound texture analysis combined with machine learning that assesses fetal lung images (4-chamber view) uploaded via a web application to non-invasively predict fetal lung maturity.
release_evidence: quantitative ultrasound fetal lung maturity (quantusFLM) assessment... Images obtained are then uploaded via a web page application and these are analyzed remotely
journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
title: Fetal lung maturity assessment: A historic perspective and Non - invasive assessment using an automatic quantitative ultrasound analysis (a potentially useful clinical tool).

model_family: multitask scheme of three convolutional networks - feature extraction, class prediction and region proposal
patient_population: fetal head, abdominal and heart standard-plane images
clinical_problem: quality control of 2D fetal sonographic standard planes, the labor-intensive check that biometry and anomaly diagnosis depend on and that currently needs a professional sonographer
model_description: Operationalizes the criterion sonographers actually apply - every essential anatomical structure present, complete and clearly bounded - by having the network identify each structure, judge whether it meets standard, and say where it is. Quality control rather than measurement, which is the step upstream of everything else and the one most automation skips. Under a second per image.
title: Automatic quality assessment for 2D fetal sonographic standard plane based on multitask learning.
headline_result: quality assessment of a fetal sonographic image in under a second, with segmentation and diagnosis competitive with state-of-the-art methods

model_family: convolutional neural network on three-dimensional depth sensor images of the back
patient_population: 160 subjects suspected to have adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, from a consecutive prospectively collected series at five scoliosis centers in Japan
clinical_problem: screening for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis without radiation, by predicting the Cobb angle from a surface scan rather than from a radiograph
model_description: Existing scoliosis screening methods - forward bend test, scoliometer - detect asymmetry but predict the Cobb angle poorly, and that is the specific gap this fills: a depth sensor plus a network that outputs a number on the same scale clinicians decide with. The reported accuracy is framed at the two thresholds that matter, 10 degrees for calling it scoliosis and 20 degrees for considering a brace, which is more useful than a bare correlation. Five centers and ten repeats of five-fold cross-validation.
journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
title: An algorithm for using deep learning convolutional neural networks with three dimensional depth sensor imaging in scoliosis detection.
study_design: retrospective analysis of a prospectively collected multicenter series
headline_result: correlation 0.91 with the actual Cobb angle, mean absolute error 4.0 degrees and RMSE 5.4 degrees; 94% accuracy at the 10-degree threshold and 89% at 20 degrees

patient_population: singleton fetuses of outpatient pregnant women, 19-38 weeks gestation
clinical_problem: classifying fetal facial expressions on ultrasound as a marker of fetal brain development
model_description: Ultrasound images of fetal faces are labeled into seven expression categories (eye blinking, mouthing, no expression, scowling, smiling, tongue expulsion, yawning); a deep-learning AI classifier trained on these images outputs a facial-expression category and confidence score.
title: Recognition of facial expression of fetuses by artificial intelligence (AI).
dataset_size: images from fetuses across five retained expression categories (e.g. 147 mouthing images, 320 no-expression images)
headline_result: overall test-set accuracy 0.985

model_family: deep learning temporal video segmentation followed by automated workflow description
patient_population: full-length routine second-trimester fetal ultrasound scans, over 200 hours of recordings
clinical_problem: characterizing how sonographers actually perform a routine anomaly scan, so that scanning skill, scan time and machine interfaces can be studied at scale
model_description: Not a diagnostic model at all, and that is the point - it treats the scan itself as the object of study. The network temporally segments a full-length recording into semantically meaningful segments, turning an unwatchable archive of 200 hours into a structured description of operator behavior. The stated uses are training sonographers, optimizing scan times and designing better machine interfaces, which is the non-interpretive side of imaging AI that pediatric and fetal services rarely have data on.
title: Knowledge representation and learning of operator clinical workflow from full-length routine fetal ultrasound scan videos.
dataset_size: more than 200 hours of full-length routine scan video
headline_result: first fully-automatic framework to describe operator clinical workflow from full-length routine second-trimester scan video

patient_population: 385 children (300 Tibetan, 85 Han immigrant), ages 4-18
clinical_problem: assessing bone age in children living at high altitude (Tibet) using an AI system developed on a different population
model_description: A previously reported fully-automated AI bone-age system, trained on Han Chinese children from southern China, takes left-hand radiographs as input and outputs an estimated Greulich-Pyle bone age, compared with expert consensus reads.
title: Performance of an artificial intelligence system for bone age assessment in Tibet.
study_design: retrospective external-population validation of an existing AI bone-age system
headline_result: Accuracy within 1 year: 84.67% (Tibetan), 89.41% (Han); MAD 0.65 and 0.56 years respectively

patient_population: 115 pediatric patients with low-grade gliomas from two children's hospitals (training cohort mean age 9.4 years, external validation cohort mean age 8.37 years)
clinical_problem: pretherapeutic differentiation of BRAF-mutated versus BRAF-fused pediatric low-grade gliomas
model_description: Radiomics features extracted from FLAIR MRI tumor segmentations go in; a random forest model outputs predicted BRAF fusion or BRAF V600E mutation status.
title: Radiomics of Pediatric Low-Grade Gliomas: Toward a Pretherapeutic Differentiation of BRAF-Mutated and BRAF-Fused Tumors.
study_design: bi-institutional retrospective radiomics study with external validation
dataset_size: 115 pediatric patients with low-grade glioma (94 training, 21 external validation)
headline_result: AUC 0.75 internal 4-fold cross-validation, AUC 0.85 external validation

patient_population: 188 children ages 0-15 (128 male, 60 female), prospective cohort
clinical_problem: identifying sex-related structural and connectivity differences in the developing brain of children
model_description: a multi-kernel SVM takes combined structural MRI and diffusion tensor imaging ROI features as input and outputs a male/female classification
title: Multimodal Image Analysis of Sexual Dimorphism in Developing Childhood Brain.
headline_result: sex classification accuracy 72%

patient_population: pediatric patients with high-grade brain tumors (sample size not stated in abstract)
clinical_problem: differentiating pediatric high-grade brain tumor histology (tumor cellularity, necrosis, hemorrhage) noninvasively
model_description: A deep neural network takes diffusion basis spectrum imaging (DBSI)-derived diffusion metrics as input classifiers and outputs classification of tumor histology components (normal white matter, dense/less-dense tumor, infiltrating edge, necrosis, hemorrhage).
title: Diffusion histology imaging differentiates distinct pediatric brain tumor histology.
headline_result: Overall classification accuracy 85.8%; AUC 0.950-0.991 across tumor histology classes

model_family: CNN (2D/3D fully convolutional network with CPPN)
patient_population: 21 preterm neonates (25 3D ultrasound volumes), mean 35.8±1.6 gestational weeks
clinical_problem: Automated 3D segmentation of cerebral ventricles in preterm neonates to monitor ventriculomegaly/hydrocephalus risk
model_description: 2D and 3D fully convolutional neural networks, enhanced with a Compositional Pattern Producing Network to encode ventricle location, segment the cerebral ventricular system on 3D ultrasound of preterm neonates.
title: Automatic segmentation and location learning of neonatal cerebral ventricles in 3D ultrasound data combining CNN and CPPN.
headline_result: Dice 0.893 (dilated ventricles, 2D FCN)/0.886 (3D FCN); volume error 0.36-0.45 cm3

patient_population: 93 normal subjects (484 ROIs), 39 NAFLD subjects (260 ROIs); external validation cohort of 42 children
clinical_problem: Differentiating pediatric nonalcoholic fatty liver disease from healthy liver on ultrasound using texture-based machine learning classification.
model_description: Texture features extracted from regions of interest on hepatic ultrasound images are used to train an ensembled machine learning model (SVM, neural network, XGBoost) to classify liver images as NAFLD or normal.
title: Digital image analysis of ultrasound images using machine learning to diagnose pediatric nonalcoholic fatty liver disease.
study_design: cross-sectional study with external validation cohort
dataset_size: 132 subjects total (93 normal, 39 NAFLD) plus a 42-child external validation cohort
headline_result: Ensembled ML model superior to intensity-based indices in external validation of 211 ROIs from 42 children

clinical_problem: predicting newborn body mass index using prenatal ultrasound measurements and maternal/delivery information
model_description: Machine learning models (random forest, linear regression, neural networks) use serial prenatal ultrasound biometry (biparietal diameter, abdominal circumference, estimated fetal weight) plus maternal and delivery information to predict newborn BMI.
title: Prediction of newborn's body mass index using nationwide multicenter ultrasound data: a machine-learning study.
dataset_size: 3,159 obstetric patients and newborns (nationwide multicenter, Korea)
headline_result: linear regression MSE 2.0744, random forest MSE 2.1610 (best performing models)

patient_population: 13,506 pediatric CT reports; also tested on 1,000 adult CT and 1,000 adult X-ray reports
clinical_problem: Can NLP models classify Norwegian pediatric CT radiology reports as containing abnormal findings versus normal, for quality assurance purposes?
model_description: Takes free-text Norwegian radiology reports as input; CNN, bi-LSTM, and SVM models output a binary classification of whether the report describes abnormal findings.
journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
title: Neural classification of Norwegian radiology reports: using NLP to detect findings in CT-scans of children.
dataset_size: 13,506 pediatric CT reports (plus 1,000 adult CT and 1,000 adult X-ray reports for generalization testing)
headline_result: CNN best on children's CT: AUC 0.981, F1 0.930

model_name: CNI-TLC challenge (Connectomics in NeuroImaging Transfer Learning Challenge)
patient_population: 240 subjects (120 neurotypical, 120 ADHD) for training in a pre-adolescent cohort; 100 subjects (50 neurotypical, 25 ADHD, 25 ASD with ADHD) for testing
clinical_problem: Can machine learning models trained to diagnose ADHD from resting-state fMRI connectomics generalize (transfer) to a related condition, autism spectrum disorder with ADHD comorbidity?
model_description: A public challenge (held with MICCAI 2019) invited standardized, containerized machine-learning models that take resting-state fMRI connectome data as input and classify subjects as ADHD-positive or -negative, then tests transfer of the best model to ASD classification.
release_evidence: submissions were 'standardized...containerized Docker images through ChRIS, an open-source image analysis platform'; the challenge dataset was kept publicly available, but no code URL is given for the winning model
title: Neuropsychiatric disease classification using functional connectomics - results of the connectomics in neuroimaging transfer learning challenge.
headline_result: One participant outperformed all others in both ADHD and ASD classification (no single AUC given); authors note further improvements are needed for clinical translation

model_family: convolutional network with a learned pairwise attention module, trained self-supervised by inverting a slice-sampling process
patient_population: 2D slices sampled from 3D fetal brain volumes at 18-22 weeks gestational age, then real 2D transthalamic plane images and freehand scan video
clinical_problem: locating where a 2D fetal neurosonography image sits in 3D atlas space, the alignment step that standard plane finding and any 3D interpretation depend on
model_description: The annotation problem is dissolved rather than solved: instead of labeling each 2D scan with its 3D position, slices are sampled from volumes and the network is trained to invert the sampling, so supervision is free. It takes a set of images rather than one and learns which pairs to weight, so accuracy improves as more images from the same scan are given - useful, since a real examination produces a stream, not a single frame. It transfers to real standard-plane images and to freehand video.
title: Learning to map 2D ultrasound images into 3D space with minimal human annotation.
dataset_size: 3D fetal brain volumes at 18-22 weeks, plus real 2D images and freehand video
headline_result: outperforms the baseline by up to 23% on Euclidean distance, plane angle and normalized cross correlation as the number of input images grows, and matches human annotation on real transthalamic plane images

patient_population: Pediatric X-ray images (test sets of 200 and 4,221 images) across 21 body regions
clinical_problem: Can an automated method correctly align and orient pediatric X-ray images across many body regions to standardize archived studies and support downstream computer-aided diagnosis tools?
model_description: Takes pediatric X-ray images as input; a PCA-based alignment stage plus a VGG16 CNN orientation-classification stage outputs correctly aligned and oriented radiographs for standardized archiving and downstream CAD use.
release_evidence: The Python source code of the best performing implementation of XAOM is publicly available at https://github.com/fhrzic/XAOM.
title: XAOM: A method for automatic alignment and orientation of radiographs for computer-aided medical diagnosis.
headline_result: PCA alignment mean error 1.65 degrees; VGG16 orientation accuracy 0.993

patient_population: children younger than 2 years of age (count not stated)
clinical_problem: Estimating brain age from MRI in children younger than 2 years to help assess early brain development, including myelination delay
model_description: A deep learning AI model trained on a single T1- and T2-weighted MRI slice per subject estimates brain age in children under 2 years old, and flags subjects with myelination delay as having a younger-than-expected estimated brain age.
title: Age estimates from brain magnetic resonance images of children younger than two years of age using deep learning.
headline_result: mean absolute error 8.2 weeks (1.9 months)

clinical_problem: diagnosing pneumonia (and distinguishing bacterial from viral) in children from chest radiographs
model_description: Statistical and deep-learning-derived global features are extracted from chest radiographs and combined for classification by a RandomForest classifier, outputting a three-class label (normal, bacterial pneumonia, viral pneumonia).
title: A Pneumonia Diagnosis Scheme Based on Hybrid Features Extracted from Chest Radiographs Using an Ensemble Learning Algorithm.
study_design: retrospective model-development study on a public dataset
dataset_size: not stated (widely used relabeled chest radiograph dataset)
headline_result: 86.30% classification accuracy, 86.03% F-score

clinical_problem: 3D myocardial segmentation for surgical planning in congenital heart defects
model_description: An adversarial-learning (GAN discriminator-guided) deep-learning model automatically segments the myocardium on cardiovascular MRI to build patient-specific 3D heart models for congenital heart defect surgical planning.
title: A Myocardial Segmentation Method Based on Adversarial Learning.

patient_population: 37 children (mean age 11.8 +/- 3.1 years) with drug-resistant focal epilepsy
clinical_problem: predicting expressive and receptive language function in children with focal epilepsy from diffusion tractography
model_description: a CNN takes the diffusion tractography connectome (streamline connectivity matrix) as input and outputs predicted expressive and receptive language scores
title: Prediction of baseline expressive and receptive language function in children with focal epilepsy using diffusion tractography-based deep learning network.
headline_result: predicted vs. actual scores: r=0.82 (expressive) and r=0.75 (receptive), MAE 7.77/7.40

model_family: image processing and machine learning cranial shape classification software
patient_population: 351 acceptable image sets from open-source (n = 40) and retrospectively collected newborn top-down cranial images with or without facial views (n = 339), collected April 2008 to February 2020, compared against blinded craniofacial specialists
clinical_problem: screening newborns for nonsyndromic craniosynostosis remotely, so that the diagnosis is not missed for want of access to a craniofacial specialist, an optical scanner or a CT
model_description: Explicitly positioned as a substitute for CT-based and optical-scanner craniometrics in the screening step - which in this condition means avoiding a head CT in an infant. Two things are validated separately: the categorical call against blinded specialists, which was strong, and agreement with optical craniometry, which was excellent for cephalic index but only moderate for cranial vault asymmetry. The stated destination is a phone app usable in primary care or by telemedicine.
title: Image processing and machine learning for telehealth craniosynostosis screening in newborns.
headline_result: accuracy 93.3% (95% CI 86.8-98.8), sensitivity 92.0%, specificity 94.3%; intraclass correlation with optical craniometry 0.95 for cephalic index and 0.67 for cranial vault asymmetry index

patient_population: 60 children (30 Pierre Robin sequence, 30 controls)
clinical_problem: Detecting brain developmental differences in children with Pierre Robin sequence using diffusion MRI (ADC) features
model_description: Machine learning models (SVM, logistic regression, AdaBoost) trained on LASSO-selected apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) MRI features to distinguish children with Pierre Robin sequence from controls.
title: Machine Learning Models on ADC Features to Assess Brain Changes of Children With Pierre Robin Sequence.
study_design: Retrospective single-center model development and validation study
headline_result: SVM AUC 0.99 (training), 0.85 (testing)

model_family: CNN feature extractors (e.g. VGG19) combined with classifiers (kNN, Naive Bayes, Random Forest, MLP, SVM)

clinical_problem: detecting pneumonia on chest radiographs in children
model_description: Input: chest X-ray images; output: binary classification (pneumonia vs. normal) using CNN-extracted features (best: VGG19) classified by an SVM with RBF kernel, deployed in a real-time IoT system.
title: A new approach for the detection of pneumonia in children using CXR images based on an real-time IoT system.
study_design: retrospective model development and internal evaluation
headline_result: Accuracy 96.47%, F1 96.46%, Precision 96.46% (VGG19+SVM-RBF)

model_family: 1906 radiomic features from T1- and T2-weighted white matter, reduced by minimum redundancy maximum relevance, with eightfold cross-validation
patient_population: 46 prospectively enrolled preterm neonates (median gestational age 29 weeks, 26 male) scanned at median 37 weeks corrected age, assessed at 12 months corrected age; 13 of 46 had poor outcome
clinical_problem: predicting poor psychomotor development in preterm neonates from the term-equivalent brain MRI they already receive
model_description: The headline finding is what the radiomics saw that the radiologists did not: 45 of 46 neonates had no significant white matter injury on visual assessment, yet texture analysis of that apparently normal white matter predicted psychomotor outcome at an AUC of 0.925. Adding gestational age or diffusion parameters did not improve it. Forty-six neonates with 13 events is small and the model is cross-validated rather than externally tested, so the effect size should be treated as provisional - but the premise, that the injury is subvisual, is the interesting claim.
title: Brain MRI radiomics analysis may predict poor psychomotor outcome in preterm neonates.
headline_result: AUC 0.925 from T1-weighted, 0.834 from T2-weighted and 0.902 from both, with sensitivity 84.6% and specificity 78.8%, despite 45 of 46 scans showing no significant white matter injury on visual assessment

patient_population: European community cohort: resilient n=18, enduring users n=193, controls n=460, self-reported use at ages 14, 16, 19
clinical_problem: identifying brain structural correlates of resilience to polysubstance use in adolescents
model_description: a random-forest model takes personality traits and regional grey-matter volume/fractional-anisotropy features as input and outputs individual-level prediction of resilience to polysubstance use
journal: European neuropsychopharmacology : the journal of the European College of Neuropsychopharmacology
title: Neuroimaging evidence for structural correlates in adolescents resilient to polysubstance use: A five-year follow-up study.
study_design: prospective five-year longitudinal cohort study with machine learning prediction
dataset_size: 671 adolescents total (18 resilient, 193 enduring users, 460 controls)

model_family: end-to-end unsupervised spherical convolutional network learning deformation fields, with scaling-and-squaring diffeomorphic layers and three orthogonal Spherical U-Nets
patient_population: two datasets covering adult and infant multimodal cortical features
clinical_problem: cortical surface registration, the prerequisite for any surface-based analysis and for establishing longitudinal correspondence in a brain that is changing shape
model_description: Infant cortical surfaces are the hard case for registration because the cortex folds rapidly between scans, so longitudinal correspondence is exactly what fails. Learning the deformation directly on the sphere - with a topology-preserving diffeomorphic construction and three orthogonal U-Nets to handle polar distortion - keeps the guarantee that conventional methods provide while cutting the time from a minute to ten seconds, which is what makes large infant cohorts processable.
title: S3Reg: Superfast Spherical Surface Registration Based on Deep Learning.
headline_result: superior or comparable performance to state-of-the-art registration methods while reducing registration time from about 1 minute to 10 seconds

model_family: Random Forest (nonlinear) and linear modeling of MRI features
patient_population: 42 critically ill children with TBI, prospectively recruited from 5 Canadian pediatric ICUs
clinical_problem: predicting long-term neurological function or death after traumatic brain injury in critically ill children
model_description: Random Forest modeling identifies which subacute-phase MRI features (herniation, diffuse axonal injury location, contusion) most predict long-term global neurological outcome or death after pediatric TBI, combined with an MRI composite score in linear outcome models.
title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging Findings Are Associated with Long-Term Global Neurological Function or Death after Traumatic Brain Injury in Critically Ill Children.
headline_result: an MRI composite score significantly improved prediction of favorable vs. unfavorable long-term outcome

patient_population: 80 pregnant women (fetal spleens imaged), Mid-Pregnancy (19-23wk) vs End-Pregnancy (37-41wk)
clinical_problem: Quantifying fetal splenic echogenicity change across gestation as a marker of extramedullary hematopoiesis
model_description: A clustering-segmentation pipeline applied to fetal spleen ultrasound images that derives two new radiomic parameters (Dark Ratio and Light Ratio) reflecting splenic echogenicity, used to track hematopoiesis across gestation.
title: A novel ultrasound-based approach to investigate extramedullary haematopoiesis in foetal spleen.
headline_result: Dark Ratio differed significantly between mid- and end-pregnancy (0.0631 vs 0.0483, P=0.014)

clinical_problem: Classify and localize ADHD-related brain regions in children using structural MRI
model_description: Takes 3D MRI volumes sliced into orthogonal 2D slices as input vectors; a random forest classifier trained per slice position/direction, with predictions intersected across three directions to classify ADHD and localize discriminative brain regions.
title: Localization and Diagnosis of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder.
headline_result: More accurate identification of ADHD than comparison methods; a new suspected region identified (exact figures not given)

model_family: deep neural network tissue segmentation inside a cortical surface reconstruction pipeline, with edge-gradient CSF/GM boundary detection and sulcal skeletonization
patient_population: three independent datasets comprising 736 pre-term and 97 term neonates
clinical_problem: measuring cortical thickness in neonates, where small brains, large partial volume effects and sulci too narrow to show CSF defeat surface extraction methods built for adults
model_description: Notable for working from T1 alone, since the established neonatal pipelines assume T2 and many clinical or research protocols have only T1. The validation is unusually complete: qualitative rating of every surface, landmark displacement below one voxel, three sites, and a biological sanity check - measured thickness rose from 1.3 mm at 28 weeks to 1.8 mm at term, with cingulate growing fastest. A direct comparison against the T2-based dHCP pipeline is reported as inconclusive rather than spun. Publicly available through CBRAIN.
release_evidence: NEOCIVET 2.0 has been open to the public through CBRAIN, a web-based platform for processing brain imaging data
title: Robust Cortical Thickness Morphometry of Neonatal Brain and Systematic Evaluation Using Multi-Site MRI Datasets.
study_design: retrospective methods development with multi-site evaluation
headline_result: 86.9% of reconstructed surfaces rated accurate across three sites, with mean landmark displacement 0.532 +/- 0.035 mm - less than a voxel

model_family: extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) over 651 radiomic features per MRI sequence, with feature selection
patient_population: 109 patients from three academic centers, 60 of them pediatric (55%); 50 H3K27M-mutant and 59 wild-type
clinical_problem: predicting H3K27M mutation status in midline gliomas non-invasively, a molecular marker with prognostic weight that conventional MRI features do not distinguish
model_description: A radiogenomics model for a tumor - diffuse midline glioma - where tissue is often not obtainable and the mutation defines the entity. The motivation is stated as a negative result from the prior literature: enhancement, necrosis and edema rates vary and none separates mutant from wild-type, so the signal, if there is one, is in texture rather than in anything a radiologist reports. Multi-institutional, majority pediatric, but a single random split of 109 patients and test performance below training, so the estimate is fragile.
title: Machine Learning-Based Multiparametric Magnetic Resonance Imaging Radiomics for Prediction of H3K27M Mutation in Midline Gliomas.
headline_result: AUC 0.791 training and 0.737 test; test accuracy 72.7%, precision 76.5%, recall 72.2%, F1 74.3%

model_family: ensemble learner over preoperative radiographic, clinical and surgical parameters
patient_population: 371 adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients who underwent posterior spinal fusion with two-year follow-up, multicenter, with prospectively collected radiographic, clinical and surgical data
clinical_problem: predicting the three-dimensional spinal alignment two years after posterior spinal fusion for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, when current surgical guidelines are based on a two-dimensional classification of the curve
model_description: The design separates what the patient brings from what the surgeon chooses, and quantifies each: preoperative factors alone predicted the outcome cluster at 64%, rising to 75% when the surgical decisions were added. Among the surgical predictors, the identity of the operating surgeon was itself important - and the paper says for which preoperative ranges that mattered, which is a candid and unusual thing to report. Aimed at setting expectations before surgery rather than at automating a measurement.
title: Machine Learning Predicts the 3D Outcomes of Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis Surgery Using Patient-Surgeon Specific Parameters.
headline_result: 75% accuracy predicting three clusters of 3D surgical outcome using preoperative plus surgical factors, falling to 64% with preoperative factors alone

patient_population: 9 children with cerebral palsy (age 8-15) and 12 healthy controls (age 9-16)
clinical_problem: differentiating spastic muscles in cerebral palsy from healthy muscle using MRI fat fraction and texture analysis
model_description: Input: multi-echo Dixon MRI fat-fraction images of calf muscles with radiomics texture features; output: combined radiomics and fat-fraction model distinguishing cerebral-palsy-affected muscle from healthy muscle.
title: Combination of Quantitative MRI Fat Fraction and Texture Analysis to Evaluate Spastic Muscles of Children With Cerebral Palsy.
headline_result: combined model AUC 0.95/0.93/0.83 for the three muscles, better than radiomics or fat-fraction alone

model_family: deep learning on clinical features, extended with a fine-tuned BERT natural language processing model over radiology report text
patient_population: 1312 children from a level 1 pediatric trauma centre registry, January 2010 to January 2020, of whom 737 (56.2%) were abused; matched non-abusive trauma controls
clinical_problem: recognizing child physical abuse, which is difficult, usually needs a multidisciplinary assessment, and is subject to bias in who gets investigated
model_description: The design isolates what the imaging adds: Model 1 uses demographics, vital signs and laboratory values, and Model 2 adds the text of head CT, brain MRI and skeletal survey reports through BERT. Adding the reports lifted accuracy from 86% to 93% and positive predictive value to 96%, which quantifies how much of the abuse signal lives in the radiologist's words. The authors note most individual features correlated weakly with abuse, so the model is finding combinations rather than any single red flag. Intended to run live in the record and prompt the clinician.
title: Using deep learning and natural language processing models to detect child physical abuse.
headline_result: accuracy 86.3% and AUC 0.86 for the clinical model versus 93.4% and AUC 0.94 for the NLP model adding radiology report text, with PPV rising from 88.7% to 95.9%

patient_population: 47 individuals with autism and 37 typically developing controls from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ages not stated in abstract)
clinical_problem: relating brain connectome organization to autism symptom severity
model_description: Structural connectome and microcircuit simulation features derived from MRI go in; supervised machine learning outputs an association with Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule symptom severity scores.
title: Differences in subcortico-cortical interactions identified from connectome and microcircuit models in autism.
study_design: case-control connectome study with supervised machine learning
dataset_size: 47 individuals with autism, 37 typically developing controls
headline_result: macroscale connectome perturbations significantly associated with ADOS symptom severity scores

patient_population: Planned: 100 children with Rolandic epilepsy (50 on anti-epileptic drugs, 50 drug-naive) and 100 healthy children, 5 Chinese hospitals
clinical_problem: Predicting brain age from functional connectivity MRI in children with Rolandic epilepsy to characterize accelerated brain aging
model_description: Planned connectome-based predictive modeling (CPM), a machine-learning approach using whole-brain functional connectivity MRI ('neural fingerprints'), to predict brain age in children with Rolandic epilepsy versus healthy controls.
title: Connectome-based prediction of brain age in Rolandic epilepsy: a protocol for a multicenter cross-sectional study.
study_design: Study protocol for a multicenter cross-sectional study (model not yet developed/reported)
dataset_size: 200 children planned (100 with Rolandic epilepsy, 100 controls)

model_family: deep learning regression on T2-weighted fetal brain MRI
patient_population: 184 T2-weighted fetal MRI acquisitions from 184 fetuses (mean gestational age 29.4 weeks) scanned January 2014 to June 2019, split 126 training, 29 validation and 29 test; reference standard from last menstruation and first-trimester ultrasound
clinical_problem: estimating gestational age after the first trimester, where ultrasound dating loses accuracy as pregnancy advances and some pregnancies were never dated early
model_description: The comparator is the right one - biparietal diameter measured on the same MRI - and the useful number is not the correlation but the spread: the model's upper limit of agreement was 2.45 weeks against 5.62 weeks for biparietal diameter, so the worst-case error is less than half. Both methods drifted with advancing gestation, which is the expected behaviour and worth knowing. Twenty-nine test cases is small.
title: Deep learning model for predicting gestational age after the first trimester using fetal MRI.
headline_result: concordance correlation 0.964 for the model versus 0.920 for biparietal diameter, with upper limit of agreement 2.45 weeks versus 5.62 weeks

model_family: deep transfer learning (VGG19, DenseNet121, Xception, ResNet50)
patient_population: children aged 1-5 years
clinical_problem: detecting pneumonia on pediatric chest radiographs
model_description: Pediatric chest X-rays are classified as pneumonia or normal by four pretrained convolutional neural networks (VGG19, DenseNet121, Xception, ResNet50) fine-tuned via transfer learning; performance is compared across models using accuracy, sensitivity, precision, AUC and F1 score.
title: Automated detection of pneumonia cases using deep transfer learning with paediatric chest X-ray images.
study_design: retrospective diagnostic accuracy comparison of transfer-learning models
headline_result: best model DenseNet121: 86.8% accuracy, AUC 0.86; Xception/DenseNet121 F1 >89%

model_family: cross-validated elastic-net regression on multimodal imaging features
patient_population: children aged 9-10 in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study
clinical_problem: identifying which 9-10 year olds will gain weight pathologically over the following year
model_description: Uses structural, diffusion, resting-state and task-based MRI to model current body mass index and, separately, to predict pathological weight gain a year later. Structural features generalized to held-out data and predicted future pathological gain; functional and reward-task measures did not. The practical reading is that the cheap, routinely acquired structural sequence carried the signal and the elaborate functional paradigms did not.
title: Multimodal brain predictors of current weight and weight gain in children enrolled in the ABCD study ®.
headline_result: structural features explained 27% of held-out variance in body mass index and predicted pathological weight gain with area under the curve 0.83 in both training and test sets

patient_population: 504 full-length lower-extremity radiographs from 359 patients ≤21 years old with limb-length discrepancy indication
clinical_problem: Automatically localizing anatomical landmarks on full-length lower-extremity radiographs to measure limb-length discrepancy in children and young adults
model_description: Input: full-length bilateral lower-extremity AP radiographs; output: localized anatomical landmarks (femoral heads, condyles, tibial plafonds) via heatmap regression CNN, used to compute bone lengths and limb-length discrepancy
title: Anatomical landmark localization via convolutional neural networks for limb-length discrepancy measurements.
headline_result: mean absolute error for LLD prediction 0.36 cm

patient_population: not stated (editorial, no abstract)

model_description: This record is an editorial (no abstract) discussing artificial-intelligence approaches to predicting gestational age from fetal MRI as a practical clinical solution to an unsolved problem.
title: Fetal MRI-based artificial intelligence in gestational age prediction--a practical solution to an unsolved problem?

patient_population: 84 children with medulloblastoma (60 training, 24 internal validation, 40 external validation)
clinical_problem: predicting preoperative cerebrospinal fluid dissemination in children with medulloblastoma from MRI, to improve on imperfect MRI/CSF cytology
model_description: A combined clinical-MRI radiomics model uses features from preoperative contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI plus clinical characteristics to predict CSF dissemination in children with medulloblastoma before surgery.
title: Clinical-MRI radiomics enables the prediction of preoperative cerebral spinal fluid dissemination in children with medulloblastoma.
dataset_size: 84 children (60 training, 24 internal validation, 40 external validation)
headline_result: combined model AUC 0.89 (training), 0.87 (internal validation), 0.73 (external validation)

clinical_problem: Automatically assessing image quality of reconstructed 3D fetal brain MRI to reduce the need for time-consuming manual visual inspection.

journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
title: Image Quality Assessment of Fetal Brain MRI Using Multi-Instance Deep Learning Methods.
study_design: retrospective methods development and validation study
headline_result: Best model (MI-CB-DLM with gestational age): accuracy 0.86, AUC 0.93

patient_population: 18 adolescents with conduct disorder, 18 typically developing controls
clinical_problem: Distinguishing adolescents with conduct disorder from typically developing controls using dynamic resting-state brain activity patterns.

title: Altered dynamic regional homogeneity in patients with conduct disorder.
headline_result: 75% classification accuracy (p<0.001), sensitivity 61%, specificity 89%

clinical_problem: How can AI tools assist in the prediction, identification, and investigation of child abuse in pediatric radiology practice?
model_description: Narrative review discussing potential and emerging roles of AI tools in identifying and investigating findings of child abuse on pediatric imaging.
title: Artificial intelligence in child abuse imaging.

model_family: context-aware convolutional neural network (CA-CNN, U-Net based with transfer learning)
patient_population: 67 pediatric subjects with confirmed orbital abscess from infectious orbital cellulitis
clinical_problem: detecting and segmenting orbital abscess in pediatric infectious orbital cellulitis on CT
model_description: Takes an orbital CT scan as input and outputs automatic detection and segmentation of orbital abscess, using a context-aware convolutional neural network with transfer learning from a pretrained CT lung-segmentation model.
title: Automated delineation of orbital abscess depicted on CT scan using deep learning.
headline_result: Dice coefficient 0.78±0.12, Jaccard index 0.65±0.13, Hausdorff distance 1.94±1.21 mm; no false positives

patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing paired CT and chest X-ray (13 test subjects)
clinical_problem: detecting early bronchiectasis on chest X-ray in children (versus CT gold standard)
model_description: An ANN algorithm quantitatively analyzes chest X-ray regions to detect features of bronchiectasis (airway dilation) that correlate with CT findings in children with suspected non-CF bronchiectasis.
title: Could automated analysis of chest X-rays detect early bronchiectasis in children?
headline_result: AUC 0.71-0.86 across feature classes (normal, severe bronchiectasis, mild airway dilation, other abnormalities)

patient_population: North Indian pregnancy cohort (GARBH-Ini study)
clinical_problem: Estimate first-trimester gestational age from ultrasound crown-rump length in an Indian population to improve preterm birth classification
model_description: Takes ultrasound-measured crown-rump length as input; machine learning feature selection identified CRL as the key parameter among candidate clinical/socioeconomic covariates, yielding a population-specific nonlinear gestational age estimation formula.
title: Comparison of first trimester dating methods for gestational age estimation and their implication on preterm birth classification in a North Indian cohort.
headline_result: Equivalent performance to published formulae (limits of agreement -0.46 to 0.96 weeks); highest sensitivity and accuracy for preterm birth classification among compared formulae

patient_population: 23 size-matched pediatric patients per scanner (46 total), age 2-18 years
clinical_problem: reducing radiation dose in pediatric lung CT while maintaining image quality using newer scanner technology and deep learning reconstruction
model_description: A 256-slice multidetector CT scanner using axial wide-cone acquisition and deep learning image reconstruction is compared to a standard 64-slice helical multidetector CT for pediatric lung CT, assessing radiation dose and image quality.
title: Ultra-low-dose lung multidetector computed tomography in children - Approaching 0.2 millisievert.
dataset_size: 23 pediatric patients per scanner (46 total), age 2-18 years
headline_result: effective dose reduced to 0.23+/-0.11 mSv (MDCT2) vs 1.13+/-0.58 mSv (MDCT1), p<0.001; subjective image quality not significantly different

model_family: deep learning classification and segmentation pipeline
patient_population: obstetric ultrasound images from an expert-sonographer-annotated database
clinical_problem: Can fetal gestational age be estimated fully automatically from low-cost obstetric ultrasound, to help establish gestational age without skilled sonographers in low- and middle-income countries?
model_description: An automated pipeline classifies, segments, and measures several fetal structures (biparietal diameter, head circumference, crown-rump length, abdominal circumference, femur length) from ultrasound images, then estimates gestational age using the Hadlock equation on the automated measurements.
journal: Proceedings of SPIE--the International Society for Optical Engineering
title: An automated framework for image classification and segmentation of fetal ultrasound images for gestational age estimation.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and internal testing
dataset_size: not stated (large database of annotated obstetric US images)
headline_result: 93% classification accuracy; mean IoU 0.91 for segmentation; mean measurement error 1.89 cm; 1.4-day mean gestational age error versus expert sonographer estimate

patient_population: 88 patients with histologically confirmed hepatoblastoma (mean age 2.28 +/- 2.72 years), from two institutions
clinical_problem: Can CT radiomics, before surgery, predict event-free survival in children with hepatoblastoma, to help inform treatment planning?
model_description: A radiomics signature, extracted from pretreatment portal-venous-phase CT and combined via LASSO Cox regression with clinicopathologic risk factors, produces a nomogram predicting event-free survival after hepatoblastoma treatment.
title: Preoperative Assessment for Event-Free Survival With Hepatoblastoma in Pediatric Patients by Developing a CT-Based Radiomics Model.
study_design: retrospective two-institution radiomics model development with external validation
headline_result: Combined radiomics-clinicopathologic nomogram C-index 0.88 (95% CI 0.829-0.933), improved over the clinicopathologic model alone (C-index 0.81 vs 0.85 reported for radiomics vs clinical)

model_family: paired U-Net models for level localization and muscle segmentation
patient_population: 370 patients sampled uniformly from 0 to 18 years and across both sexes
clinical_problem: measuring skeletal muscle mass on CT, a marker of nutritional status and sarcopenia, which requires finding the L3 level and outlining muscle by hand
model_description: Two problems in one pipeline: locating the L3 vertebral level on the sagittal reformat, then segmenting muscle on the corresponding axial slice. Sampling uniformly across ages from birth to 18 is the design choice that makes it pediatric rather than adult-with-children-included, since body habitus changes completely over that range. Level localization landed within the slice thickness.
title: Automated Segmentation of Abdominal Skeletal Muscle on Pediatric CT Scans Using Deep Learning.
headline_result: L3 localization error 3.23 ± 2.61 mm, within the reconstructed slice thickness; muscle segmentation Dice 0.93 ± 0.03

model_family: dilated CNN combined with relational network (dilated CNN + RN)
patient_population: 31 young children with persistent language concerns (mean age 4.25+/-2.38 years)
clinical_problem: Can deep learning analysis of diffusion tractography connectome data, combined with psychometric data, predict expressive and receptive language scores in young children with persistent language concerns?
model_description: Takes diffusion tensor imaging-derived structural connectome features and psychometric data as input; a dilated CNN combined with a relational network outputs predicted expressive and receptive language scores.
title: Deep reasoning neural network analysis to predict language deficits from psychometry-driven DWI connectome of young children with persistent language concerns.
headline_result: Pearson R 1.00 (expressive), 0.99 (receptive) between predicted and actual scores; MAE 0.28 for both

clinical_problem: assessing how prematurity affects brain functional connectivity, activity, and structure at term-equivalent age
model_description: a multivariate machine learning framework takes resting-state fMRI connectivity/activity measures and regional brain volumes as input to assess sensitivity to the effect of gestational age at birth
title: Distinct effects of prematurity on MRI metrics of brain functional connectivity, activity, and structure: Univariate and multivariate analyses.
study_design: neuroimaging cohort study with univariate and multivariate (machine learning) analysis

clinical_problem: Can voxel-wise uncertainty quantification improve the reliability of automated deep learning segmentation used to assess developmental dysplasia of the hip on 3D ultrasound?
model_description: Takes 3D hip ultrasound screening scans as input; a Bayesian 3D U-Net trained with a voxel-wise uncertainty-aware loss outputs segmentation of the ilium and acetabulum along with per-voxel confidence estimates.
journal: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
title: Leveraging voxel-wise segmentation uncertainty to improve reliability in assessment of paediatric dysplasia of the hip.
headline_result: Dice score for ilium/acetabulum segmentation improved by 5% with the proposed uncertainty loss vs. standard cross-entropy loss

patient_population: 29,288 connectomes from six databases (1,555 with autism), mean age 30.72, range 0.42-78.00 years
clinical_problem: Can single-subject structural MRI similarity matrices classify individuals with autism more accurately than functional connectivity, across a wide age range?
model_description: Symmetric similarity matrices derived from regional grey-matter-volume histograms on T1-weighted MRI are fed into a CNN to classify participants as having autism or not, compared against functional-connectivity-based and univariate grey-matter-volume classifiers.
title: Single-participant structural similarity matrices lead to greater accuracy in classification of participants than function in autism in MRI.
headline_result: Structural similarity AUROC 0.7298 (69.71% accuracy); functional connectivity AUROC 0.6964; combined AUROC 0.7354

model_family: LASSO Cox regression on wavelet-filtered radiomic features
patient_population: 177 treatment-naive children with diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma from an international cohort, split into training and independent testing sets
clinical_problem: prognostication in diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma, a uniformly fatal childhood tumor that is rarely biopsied
model_description: Predicts overall survival from texture features of the routine T1-post-contrast and T2 images at diagnosis, before any treatment. It beats a clinical-only model built from age and sex, and holds up in an independent test set, though the concordance drops from 0.70 to 0.59 when it does. For a tumor where biopsy is often avoided and MRI is the only longitudinal measure, an objective imaging prognostic is worth having even at that accuracy.
title: MRI-based radiomics for prognosis of pediatric diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma: an international study.
headline_result: concordance 0.68 for radiomics versus 0.57 for clinical variables alone in training; 0.59 in the independent testing dataset (P = .02)

model_family: ensemble of neural networks with segmentation models
patient_population: fetuses at 18 to 24 weeks undergoing screening ultrasound or echocardiography
clinical_problem: prenatal detection of complex congenital heart disease on screening ultrasound
model_description: Takes a whole fetal ultrasound survey, picks out the five recommended cardiac views, and classifies the heart as normal or complex congenital heart disease, while separate segmentation models compute standard cardiothoracic measurements. It addresses a specific failure of practice: the five screening views can detect 90% of complex disease, but real-world sensitivity is nearer 30%. Performance held up on outside-hospital and lower-quality images.
title: An ensemble of neural networks provides expert-level prenatal detection of complex congenital heart disease.
dataset_size: 107,823 training images from 1,326 echocardiograms and screening ultrasounds; internal test set of 4,108 fetal surveys and over 4.4 million images
headline_result: AUC 0.99, sensitivity 95%, specificity 96%, negative predictive value 100%; sensitivity comparable to clinicians

clinical_problem: correcting cone-beam CT images for accurate adaptive proton-therapy dose calculation in children and young adults
model_description: Pretreatment abdominal/pelvic cone-beam CT images, with body width normalized to reduce size-variation effects, are input to a cycle-consistent generative adversarial network that outputs corrected CT-equivalent images for proton dose recalculation, compared against same-day repeat planning CT.
journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
title: Training a deep neural network coping with diversities in abdominal and pelvic images of children and young adults for CBCT-based adaptive proton therapy.

dataset_size: 64 children and young adults (1-23 years); 14 held-out test patients
headline_result: mean absolute HU error 47±7 HU (combined model) vs. 51±8 HU (site-specific models); gamma passing rate 98.5±1.9%; proton range within ±3mm for 91.2±11.5% of beamlets

clinical_problem: Segment reproductive organs (uterus, prostate) on pediatric abdominal CT for pre-operative planning and radiation dose estimation, addressing scarce training data
model_description: Takes pediatric abdominal CT volumes as input; a segmentation network with a built-in auxiliary classifier GAN conditionally generates additional synthetic features during training to improve segmentation of the uterus and prostate.
journal: Proceedings of SPIE--the International Society for Optical Engineering
title: Enhancing Reproductive Organ Segmentation in Pediatric CT via Adversarial Learning.
headline_result: Prostate DSC 0.929, uterus DSC 0.724 (4-fold cross-validation)

model_family: random forest, gradient boosting and logistic regression compared
patient_population: 430 children and adolescents aged 0-18 with suspected appendicitis
clinical_problem: three separate decisions in suspected pediatric appendicitis: is it appendicitis, does it need surgery, and is it complicated
model_description: Combines history, examination, laboratory values and abdominal ultrasound findings to predict diagnosis, management and severity at once, which no earlier model had done. The authors also identified small subsets of 6 to 18 predictors that performed as well as all 38, and deployed the result as a free online tool. Severity, the target that would justify antibiotics instead of surgery, remains the weakest of the three.
release_evidence: deployed as an open access easy-to-use online tool (the Appendicitis Prediction Tool)
title: Using Machine Learning to Predict the Diagnosis, Management and Severity of Pediatric Appendicitis.
headline_result: area under the precision-recall curve 0.94 for diagnosis, 0.92 for management and 0.70 for severity

patient_population: in-house prenatal ultrasound dataset and a public cephalometric x-ray landmark dataset
clinical_problem: Can anatomical landmarks be detected automatically and accurately across different medical imaging tasks, without needing to hand-tune the target precision for each landmark?
model_description: A reinforcement-learning framework dynamically searches for the optimal objective metric for regressing heatmaps during training of a landmark-detection neural network, avoiding hand-crafted, task-specific precision settings; applied to both prenatal ultrasound and cephalometric x-ray landmark detection.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: Learn Fine-Grained Adaptive Loss for Multiple Anatomical Landmark Detection in Medical Images.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development on two landmark-detection datasets
dataset_size: not stated (in-house prenatal US dataset; public cephalometric x-ray dataset)
headline_result: Improved localization accuracy and training stability versus existing heatmap-regression approaches (no single summary metric reported)

patient_population: 167 children with Rolandic epilepsy and 107 typically developing children
clinical_problem: Is Rolandic epilepsy associated with delayed brain development, measurable as an increased 'brain age gap' on MRI?
model_description: A 3D-CNN brain-age prediction model, trained on 1,155 typically developing children's structural MRIs, estimates a 'brain age' from a patient's structural MRI; the difference from chronological age (brain-predicted age difference) is used as a biomarker of developmental delay.
title: Delayed brain development of Rolandic epilepsy profiled by deep learning-based neuroanatomic imaging.
dataset_size: 1,155 MRIs for training (open-source datasets); 167 RE patients + 107 controls for application
headline_result: Children with Rolandic epilepsy showed a 0.45-year brain age delay compared to typically developing children

patient_population: Iranian children's hand radiographs (test set); trained on the University of Southern California hand atlas
clinical_problem: automatic bone age assessment for growth-disorder screening
model_description: Computer-vision feature extraction (HOG, LBP, SIFT) from hand/wrist radiographs feeds an SVM classifier that automatically assesses bone age, validated on an independent Iranian pediatric radiograph cohort.

title: Bone Age Assessment of Iranian Children in an Automatic Manner.
headline_result: accuracy 90% (female), 71.42% (male); MAE 0.16 years (female), 0.42 years (male)

model_family: unsupervised deep image prior with a learned temporal manifold
patient_population: fetuses in retrospective and real fetal cardiac MRI datasets
clinical_problem: reconstructing a moving fetal heart from sparsely sampled dynamic MRI without cardiac gating
model_description: Reconstructs a dynamic MRI series by fitting a network to that one patient's measurements, with no prior training and no other data. For fetal cardiac imaging this matters because there is no reliable heartbeat signal to gate on, and this method needs none: a low-dimensional manifold encodes the temporal variation and a convolutional network generates the image series consistent with the acquired k-space.
title: Time-Dependent Deep Image Prior for Dynamic MRI.
headline_result: outperformed state-of-the-art methods quantitatively and qualitatively on retrospective and real fetal cardiac datasets

model_family: machine learning classification comparing behavioral, cognitive and neuroimaging predictors
patient_population: 162 young children ages 4-7 (mean age 5.55, 82.6% Hispanic/Latino)
clinical_problem: evaluating whether adding neuroimaging and neurocognitive assessments improves machine-learning-based ADHD diagnosis in young children beyond behavior ratings
model_description: Inputs are parent/teacher behavior ratings, behavioral executive-function measures, and neuroimaging (cortical anatomy) measures; machine learning models compare the predictive value of each input type for classifying ADHD versus typically developing children.
title: Is there any incremental benefit to conducting neuroimaging and neurocognitive assessments in the diagnosis of ADHD in young children? A machine learning investigation.
study_design: cross-sectional single-center machine learning classification study
headline_result: teacher ratings of executive function were the most predictive of ADHD; neuroimaging measures of cortical anatomy added little incremental predictive value

model_family: U-net for brain extraction, followed by super-resolution reconstruction and iterative linear and nonlinear registration for atlas building
patient_population: fetal brain MRI between 23 and 36 weeks of gestation in a Chinese population
clinical_problem: quantitative analysis of fetal brain MRI, held back both by the lack of automated preprocessing and by the absence of normative templates - particularly for non-Western populations
model_description: Two deliverables: an automated pipeline that takes clinically acquired fetal MRI through extraction and super-resolution reconstruction, and the normative product that pipeline makes possible - a 4D spatiotemporal atlas of the fetal brain across mid-to-late gestation. The population specificity is the point, since existing fetal templates are built from other populations and normative comparison against the wrong reference is worse than none.
title: Mapping fetal brain development based on automated segmentation and 4D brain atlasing.
headline_result: average accuracy 97% for automated fetal brain extraction, supporting a 4D atlas quantifying morphological development between 23 and 36 weeks

clinical_problem: Can an AI-based ultrasound technique automatically recognize standard fetal planes and obtain biometric measurements to improve workflow efficiency during prenatal scanning?
model_description: Takes live prenatal ultrasound video as input; the Smart Fetus AI technique automatically recognizes standard fetal planes (thalami, abdomen, femur) and outputs biometric measurements (biparietal diameter, head circumference, abdominal circumference, femur length).
title: A Prenatal Ultrasound Scanning Approach: One-Touch Technique in Second and Third Trimesters.

patient_population: not stated (editorial, no abstract)

model_family: neural network trained on 3D ultrasound sweeps, benchmarked against three human readers
patient_population: 30 children presenting to an emergency department with unilateral wrist injury, scanned on both the injured and uninjured limb, giving 55 wrists; radiographs of the symptomatic limb as comparison
clinical_problem: ruling out wrist fracture in children at the bedside, so that the many children without a fracture are not sent for radiographs
model_description: Two novelties stacked: three-dimensional ultrasound instead of a handheld 2D view, and automated interpretation of the sweep rather than a clinician reading it. Scanning both limbs gives every child their own control, which is how a pediatric emergency clinician would actually judge a subtle cortical break. Framed correctly as a rule-out tool - the sensitivity is what matters and both readers and network reached 1.0 - though on 30 children and 36 test images.
title: Diagnostic Accuracy of 3D Ultrasound and Artificial Intelligence for Detection of Pediatric Wrist Injuries.
headline_result: human readers combined sensitivity 1.00 and specificity 0.90; AI detected all fractures in the 36-image test set (sensitivity 1.0) and was indistinguishable from human interpretation

clinical_problem: Reviewing deep learning techniques applied to pediatric brain tumor imaging (diagnosis, classification, segmentation) and associated challenges.

patient_population: 112 120 frontal chest radiographs from NIH ChestX-ray14 covering ages 1 to 95, with separate pediatric-only models, and external testing on 662 radiographs from China

Splitting children at 11 years works well (0.96), which suggests the radiograph carries a maturational signal. External validation on a Chinese population held up.
title: Radiology "forensics": determination of age and sex from chest radiographs using deep learning.

A vendor algorithm evaluated in clinical practice rather than a research model.
