model_description: Regional homogeneity and Granger causality analysis derive connectivity features from resting-state fMRI, which feed a discriminant classification model to distinguish adolescent-onset schizophrenia patients from healthy controls.
title: Abnormal causal connectivity of left superior temporal gyrus in drug-naïve first- episode adolescent-onset schizophrenia: A resting-state fMRI study.
headline_result: discriminant model accuracy 94.9%

patient_population: 150 adolescents (67 MDD, 47 SCZ, 34 healthy controls)
clinical_problem: Distinguishing major depressive disorder from schizophrenia in adolescents using cortical thickness from structural MRI
model_description: A support vector machine classifier trained on regional cortical thickness measurements from structural MRI, using leave-one-out cross-validation, distinguishes adolescents with major depressive disorder, schizophrenia, and healthy controls.
title: Cortical thickness distinguishes between major depression and schizophrenia in adolescents.
headline_result: accuracy 79.21% (MDD vs HC), 69.88% (SCZ vs HC), 62.93% (MDD vs SCZ)

model_family: supervised classifiers - support vector machines, neural networks, random forest, logistic regression, naive Bayes and k-nearest neighbour
patient_population: 828 children admitted with traumatic brain injury to a trauma center in southern Thailand between January 2009 and July 2020, all of whom had a brain CT; median age 72 months
clinical_problem: predicting functional outcome after pediatric traumatic brain injury, from the vital signs, Glasgow coma scale and intracranial injury characteristics available on admission
model_description: A prognostic model built on the features a trauma team already has, including the characteristics of the intracranial injuries read off the CT - a head CT was an inclusion requirement. Outcome is the King's Outcome Scale for Childhood Head Injury dichotomized into favourable and unfavourable, which keeps the target clinically legible. Six algorithms are compared on the same 70/30 split rather than one being tuned and reported.
journal: Chinese journal of traumatology = Zhonghua chuang shang za zhi
title: Application of machine learning to predict the outcome of pediatric traumatic brain injury.
headline_result: machine learning models trained on admission clinical and CT injury characteristics predicted dichotomized functional outcome in the held-out 30%

patient_population: 250 children with lung consolidation on initial CT, 116 of whom developed necrotizing pneumonia
clinical_problem: early recognition of necrotizing pneumonia in children from initial non-contrast chest CT
model_description: radiomics features from manually segmented lesions on initial non-contrast chest CT are input to KNN, SVM and logistic regression models that output a prediction of subsequent necrotizing pneumonia
title: Early recognition of necrotizing pneumonia in children based on non-contrast-enhanced computed tomography radiomics signatures.
headline_result: logistic regression AUC 0.82 (training), 0.76 (validation)

model_family: 253 MRI radiomic features per subject with gray-level co-occurrence and run-length texture analysis and a preliminary prediction model
patient_population: 38 children with medulloblastoma from two hospitals with frozen tissue, imaging and clinical data; subgroups assigned from the expression of 22 signature genes
clinical_problem: identifying the four molecular subgroups of medulloblastoma - WNT, SHH, Group 3 and Group 4 - from imaging, since the subgroups carry very different prognoses and are otherwise established from tumor tissue
model_description: Radiogenomics anchored on real molecular ground truth - subgroups were assigned from gene expression in frozen tissue, not from surrogate immunohistochemistry - which is what makes the imaging correlate meaningful. Eight texture features separated the four groups, and one run-length feature also tracked survival independently. Thirty-eight children across four groups is very thin, and the authors label the prediction model preliminary.
title: Magnetic resonance radiomics features and prognosticators in different molecular subtypes of pediatric Medulloblastoma.
headline_result: AUC 0.82, 0.72 and 0.78 for predicting WNT, Group 3 and Group 4; a short-run low gray-level emphasis feature was associated with shorter survival (p = 0.04)

body_region: pelvis, humeral heads, femoral heads (iliac crests)
patient_population: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients (EOS radiographs)
clinical_problem: Can a machine learning approach automate Risser sign skeletal maturity grading from EOS radiographs to reduce inter-observer variability in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis management?
model_description: Takes regions of interest (humeral heads, femoral heads, pelvis/iliac crests) from EOS radiographs as input; a ResNet101 CNN extracts image features, and an SVM classifier outputs the Risser sign skeletal maturity grade.
title: Automatic bone maturity grading from EOS radiographs in Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis.
headline_result: Overall accuracy 84% (iliac crests), 78% (humeral heads), 80% (femoral heads)

patient_population: 73 children with cerebral palsy
clinical_problem: Segmenting brain CT lesions in children with cerebral palsy to assist diagnosis and guide rehabilitation treatment
model_description: A deep learning hybrid segmentation network (HSN) that segments brain CT images of children with cerebral palsy to identify the lesion area and assist treatment/rehabilitation planning, compared against other CNN segmentation methods.
title: Value of Rehabilitation Training for Children with Cerebral Palsy Diagnosed and Analyzed by Computed Tomography Imaging Information Features under Deep Learning.
study_design: Randomized controlled trial (AI-assisted vs. standard care) with deep-learning segmentation
headline_result: HSN had the highest Dice score among compared models (exact value not stated in abstract)

model_family: resting-state dynamic causal modeling-based support vector machine (rs-DCM-SVM)
patient_population: discovery cohort: 76 children with Rolandic epilepsy and 76 normal controls; replication cohort: 59 children with Rolandic epilepsy and 60 normal controls
clinical_problem: diagnosing drug-naive Rolandic epilepsy from resting-state brain network imbalance
model_description: Resting-state fMRI functional connectivity across seven canonical neural networks is analyzed with dynamic causal modeling, and an SVM classifier trained on these excitatory/inhibitory-imbalance features distinguishes children with Rolandic epilepsy from normal controls.
title: Brain network excitatory/inhibitory imbalance is a biomarker for drug-naive Rolandic epilepsy: A radiomics strategy.
study_design: multicenter case-control diagnostic accuracy study with discovery and replication cohorts
headline_result: accuracy 88.2% (AUC .92) discovery cohort; 81.5% (AUC .83) replication cohort

model_family: CNN (transfer learning: Inception ResNet v2, MobileNetV2)
patient_population: 122 radiographs (57 training, 10 validation, 55 testing)
clinical_problem: Automatically measuring hip migration percentage on pelvis radiographs to assess hip displacement in children with cerebral palsy.
model_description: Two fine-tuned CNNs (Inception ResNet v2, then MobileNetV2) detect landmark locations on pelvis radiographs to automatically calculate hip migration percentage.
title: Assessment of hip displacement in children with cerebral palsy using machine learning approach.
study_design: retrospective methods development and validation study
headline_result: Mean absolute difference 4.5+/-4.3%, ICC 0.91; sensitivity/specificity 87.8%/93.4% (30% MP threshold)

model_family: random forest and other machine learning approaches (5 compared)
patient_population: 2,949 mother-newborn pairs, multicenter retrospective study
clinical_problem: predicting newborn weight-for-height indicators from prenatal ultrasound biometry
model_description: Machine learning models, including random forest, use ultrasonographic fetal biometry (estimated fetal weight, abdominal circumference, biparietal diameter) and maternal/delivery data to predict newborn weight-for-height indicators.
title: Predictors of Newborn's Weight for Height: A Machine Learning Study Using Nationwide Multicenter Ultrasound Data.

patient_population: children including those with cystic fibrosis, adults with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease from a lung cancer screening trial, and the public EXACT'09 dataset
clinical_problem: extracting the airway tree from chest CT, which quantitative assessment of cystic fibrosis lung disease depends on
model_description: Segments the airway tree from a chest CT in a single pass over large 3D patches, often the whole lungs at once, which keeps the method simple and fast. Validated deliberately across three very different datasets, one of them pediatric cystic fibrosis, to show it does not depend on the disease or acquisition it was tuned on. Generalization across datasets is the claim, not just accuracy on one.
title: Automatic airway segmentation from computed tomography using robust and efficient 3-D convolutional neural networks.
dataset_size: three datasets including a pediatric cystic fibrosis cohort and the public EXACT'09 set
headline_result: highly complete airway trees with few false positives across all three datasets; second highest sensitivity among methods reporting good specificity on EXACT'09

patient_population: 162 children <2 years with Tetralogy of Fallot undergoing surgical repair
clinical_problem: Identifying risk factors, including pre-operative echocardiographic right ventricular function, for post-operative complications after Tetralogy of Fallot repair in children.
model_description: Gradient-boosted machine learning models use patient, operative, and echocardiographic variables (including pre-operative RV strain and fractional area change) to identify predictors of post-operative cardiac complications.
title: Identifying Risk Factors for Complicated Post-operative Course in Tetralogy of Fallot Using a Machine Learning Approach.
headline_result: 26.5% had at least one post-operative complication; cardiopulmonary bypass duration was the highest-ranked predictor

patient_population: 993 neurotypical control MRI exams and 269 moyamoya disease patient MRI exams
clinical_problem: characterizing abnormal cortical development in moyamoya disease using structural MRI and a machine learning predictive model
model_description: takes regional cortical thickness (average and variability) from structural T1 MRI as input and outputs a machine learning-based classification distinguishing moyamoya disease from controls
journal: International journal of developmental neuroscience : the official journal of the International Society for Developmental Neuroscience
title: Cortical thickness in clinical moyamoya disease: A magnetic resonance imaging study.
study_design: retrospective cross-sectional neuroimaging study with machine learning analysis

model_family: support vector machine on graph-theoretical degree centrality maps, leave-one-out cross-validated
patient_population: 35 children with childhood absence epilepsy scanned before and after a mean 46 weeks of antiepileptic drug treatment, and 35 age- and sex-matched healthy controls
clinical_problem: predicting which children with childhood absence epilepsy will respond to antiepileptic drugs, so that non-responders are not left on an ineffective medication for months
model_description: Treatment response prediction from resting-state imaging in a well-defined childhood epilepsy syndrome, with the rare addition of a post-treatment scan showing that the baseline abnormalities renormalize with successful therapy - which supports the claim that the measure is tracking the disease rather than a trait. The regions driving classification, principally the thalamus, match the thalamocortical mechanism of absence seizures.
journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
title: Graph-theory based degree centrality combined with machine learning algorithms can predict response to treatment with antiepileptic medications in children with epilepsy.
dataset_size: 35 patients and 35 matched controls, each scanned twice
headline_result: 84.22% accuracy separating drug responders from non-responders (sensitivity 78.76%, specificity 89.65%, AUC 0.96), with the thalamus contributing most

model_family: sequential machine learning classifier (logistic regression, neural network)
patient_population: 274 medulloblastoma, 156 pilocytic astrocytoma, 97 ependymoma (multinational cohort)
clinical_problem: Distinguishing pediatric posterior fossa tumor types (pilocytic astrocytoma, medulloblastoma, ependymoma) on MRI to aid diagnosis and surgical planning.
model_description: A 2-step sequential machine-learning classifier first distinguishes pilocytic astrocytoma from other tumors using T2/T1 radiomics features (logistic regression), then distinguishes medulloblastoma from ependymoma (neural network) using MRI Image Biomarker Standardization Initiative features.
title: Machine Assist for Pediatric Posterior Fossa Tumor Diagnosis: A Multinational Study.
dataset_size: 527 patients (274 medulloblastoma, 156 pilocytic astrocytoma, 97 ependymoma), multinational
headline_result: F1 scores: 0.8809 (PA vs non-PA), 0.9189 (MB vs EP), 0.9179 combined

model_family: automated analysis of fetal brain morphology on the standard transthalamic axial plane
patient_population: 1394 patients for development; evaluation on 3065 scans from 1992 patients (1761 second trimester, 1298 third trimester) with gestational age known from first-trimester crown-rump length
clinical_problem: dating a pregnancy in the second and third trimesters where first-trimester crown-rump length was never obtained, which is the norm in settings with late booking or infrequent antenatal care
model_description: Reads brain maturation - sulcation and structural appearance - rather than measuring size, which is why it degrades less than biometry as pregnancy advances and why it holds up in growth-restricted fetuses whose size no longer tracks age. The gains are exactly where biometry is weakest: third trimester and small-for-gestational-age fetuses. Combining the model with biometry beat either alone, which suggests brain maturation and body size carry partly independent information.
journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
title: Analysis of maturation features in fetal brain ultrasound via artificial intelligence for the estimation of gestational age.
dataset_size: 1394 development patients; 3065 evaluation scans from 1992 patients
headline_result: 95% CI of dating error 11.0 days for AI plus biometry versus 12.9 days for the best biometry formula; in the third trimester 14.3 versus 17 days, and in small-for-gestational-age fetuses 14.8 versus 18.5 days

patient_population: 63 patients with epilepsy and 259 healthy controls undergoing preoperative rs-fMRI
clinical_problem: detecting pediatric epilepsy from resting-state functional MRI
model_description: Machine learning classifiers (XGBoost, SVM, random forest) take PCA-derived features of resting-state fMRI latency z-score maps as input and classify subjects as epilepsy vs. healthy control.
title: A comparison of machine learning classifiers for pediatric epilepsy using resting-state functional MRI latency data.
headline_result: Best model (XGBoost): test AUC 0.79, accuracy 74%, specificity 73%, sensitivity 77%

model_family: ensemble of eight machine learning models over cervical vertebrae morphometric ratios plus age and sex
patient_population: 499 paired hand-wrist radiographs and lateral cephalograms from 455 orthodontic patients aged 6-18 years, collected at two university hospitals and a paediatric dental clinic
clinical_problem: estimating hand-wrist skeletal maturation stage from the lateral cephalogram already taken for orthodontics, so that treatment timing can be judged without a second radiograph of the hand
model_description: Radiation arithmetic rather than accuracy chasing: the growth information is inferred from a film the patient is already getting, which removes the hand-wrist radiograph from the pathway entirely. Features are explicit and interpretable - width-height, width-perpendicular-height and concavity ratios from 13 cervical vertebra landmarks - and adding chronological age and sex improved prediction, which is worth noting since those are free.
title: Prediction of hand-wrist maturation stages based on cervical vertebrae images using artificial intelligence.
headline_result: mean absolute error 0.90 Fishman stages (round MAE 0.87, RMSE 1.20) under five-fold cross-validation

patient_population: children with generalized anxiety, separation anxiety, and/or social phobia (n=22) compared with matched controls (n=23)
clinical_problem: distinguishing children with anxiety disorders from non-anxious controls using neural responses to emotional faces
model_description: fMRI responses while viewing angry versus fearful faces are measured, and an AdaBoost machine-learning classifier is trained on regional brain activity to distinguish anxious from non-anxious children, with the right temporal pole emerging as the most discriminative region. Conducted as part of a longitudinal clinical trial.
title: Predicting pediatric anxiety from the temporal pole using neural responses to emotional faces.
headline_result: right temporal pole distinguished anxious from control children with 81% classification accuracy

patient_population: obstetric ultrasound operators performing fetal heart and brain scans (not patients directly)
clinical_problem: characterizing sonographer skill level during obstetric fetal heart and brain ultrasound scanning using multimodal sensor data (a workflow/training task, not patient diagnosis)
model_description: takes scan video, eye-tracking gaze, and pupillometry data as input and outputs a classification of operator skill level for the heart and brain scanning tasks
journal: Proceedings. IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging
title: Multi-Modal Learning from Video, Eye Tracking, and Pupillometry for Operator Skill Characterization in Clinical Fetal Ultrasound.
headline_result: best model accuracy 82.4% (brain task), 76.4% (heart task)

patient_population: patients with hippocampal sclerosis and healthy controls; validated in an internal adult MRI-negative TLE cohort (n=22) and a pediatric MRI-negative TLE cohort (n=20) from another center
clinical_problem: lateralizing the seizure focus in MRI-negative temporal lobe epilepsy using radiomic features of the hippocampus and surrounding brain
model_description: Input: radiomics features (e.g. texture) extracted from hippocampal and extrahippocampal brain MRI regions; output: a model score identifying which side is affected in MRI-negative temporal lobe epilepsy.
title: Extrahippocampal Radiomics Analysis Can Potentially Identify Laterality in Patients With MRI-Negative Temporal Lobe Epilepsy.
study_design: retrospective radiomics model development with internal and external (including pediatric) validation
dataset_size: 36 hippocampal sclerosis patients, 50 healthy controls; internal validation n=22 adults; external pediatric validation n=20
headline_result: AUC 0.99 (hippocampus, training) and 0.97 (extrahippocampal, training); external validation AUC 0.92 (extrahippocampal) vs 0.69 (hippocampus)

model_family: convolutional neural network trained on synthesized fetal-like diffusion data
patient_population: fetal brain scans, with high-quality scans of prematurely-born newborns used to generate training data; 100 fetal test scans for accuracy, 20 for precision and expert review
clinical_problem: estimating diffusion parameters from fetal DW-MRI, where fetal motion and low SNR defeat standard fitting
model_description: The contribution is the training data, not the network. Reliable fetal diffusion ground truth does not exist, so the authors estimate accurate parameter maps from high-quality newborn scans and then degrade them to match the fetal measurement scheme and noise distribution - manufacturing a fetal training set out of neonatal data. This is a reusable pattern for any pediatric imaging problem where the population of interest cannot be imaged well enough to label.
title: Deep learning-based parameter estimation in fetal diffusion-weighted MRI.
study_design: retrospective methods development with expert reader assessment
dataset_size: 100 fetal scans for accuracy, 20 for precision, 20 for expert quality assessment
headline_result: significantly lower reconstruction error (n=100, p<0.001) and higher precision (n=20, p<0.001) than standard estimation, with better expert-rated quality in 11 regions of interest

patient_population: fetal ultrasound images (sample size not stated in abstract)
clinical_problem: screening for congenital anomalies of the fetal heart and lungs on ultrasound
model_description: A multi-scale U-Net-style model with skip connections and additive attention gates takes fetal ultrasound images as input and simultaneously segments fetal heart and lung regions.
title: Simultaneous Segmentation of Fetal Hearts and Lungs for Medical Ultrasound Images via an Efficient Multi-scale Model Integrated With Attention Mechanism.
headline_result: Outperformed existing deep-learning segmentation methods (no single metric quoted in abstract)

model_family: hybrid CNN (GoogleNet, MobileNetV2, DenseNet201 features + mRMR feature selection)
patient_population: Pediatric patients diagnosed with VUR between 2016 and 2021: 236 normal and 992 VUR images
clinical_problem: Can vesicoureteral reflux be automatically diagnosed and graded from voiding cystourethrography images in children, supporting evaluation of children with recurrent urinary tract infections?
model_description: A hybrid deep learning model extracts and concatenates features from three pretrained CNNs (GoogLeNet, MobileNetV2, DenseNet201), selects the most relevant features using minimum-redundancy-maximum-relevance, and classifies voiding cystourethrography images into six classes (normal or VUR grade 1-5).
journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
title: Diagnosis and grading of vesicoureteral reflux on voiding cystourethrography images in children using a deep hybrid model.
study_design: retrospective single-center model development and testing
headline_result: Highest accuracy 96.9% with the proposed hybrid model

patient_population: 27 pediatric arrhythmic patients (study group), 27 matched controls
clinical_problem: Reducing contrast medium and radiation dose in pediatric coronary CT angiography using deep learning image reconstruction while maintaining image quality.
model_description: A deep learning image-reconstruction algorithm processes low-dose, low-contrast coronary CT angiography scans acquired at 70 kVp with a shortened contrast-injection protocol, compared to standard-dose scans reconstructed with iterative reconstruction.
journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
title: Performance evaluation of using shorter contrast injection and 70 kVp with deep learning image reconstruction for reduced contrast medium dose and radiation dose in coronary CT angiography for children: a pilot study.
headline_result: Contrast dose reduced 53% to 15.07+/-3.68 mL; radiation dose reduced 36% to 0.57+/-0.31 mSv; similar image quality scores

patient_population: 115 first-trimester ultrasound videos (29,250 training, 7,290 validation, 9,126 test frames)
clinical_problem: predict sonographer visual gaze on individual frames of first-trimester fetal ultrasound to identify important spatio-temporal scanning patterns
model_description: Encoder-decoder convolutional neural network with skip connections predicts per-frame sonographer visual gaze/saliency on first-trimester fetal ultrasound video frames, using automated stochastic data augmentation policy search.
journal: Medical image understanding and analysis : 25th Annual Conference, MIUA 2021, Oxford, United Kingdom, July 12-14, 2021, Proceedings. Medical Image Understanding and Analysis (Conference) (25th : 2021 : Online)
title: First Trimester Gaze Pattern Estimation Using Stochastic Augmentation Policy Search for Single Frame Saliency Prediction.
study_design: retrospective methods development and evaluation study

model_family: NLP + supervised ML (SVM, neural network, naive Bayes, decision tree, random forest, AdaBoost, KNN)
patient_population: 17,337 radiographs from infants under 6 months of age with an upper extremity PICC
clinical_problem: Can machine learning automatically extract and classify the anatomical position of a peripherally inserted central catheter tip from radiology reports in infants, to flag noncentral catheter placement for clinicians?
model_description: Takes free-text radiology report descriptions of PICC line tip location as input; NLP and supervised machine learning classifiers (best: SVM and neural network) output the catheter tip's anatomical location (central vs. noncentral, or one of 12 categories).
title: Machine Learning for Detection of Correct Peripherally Inserted Central Catheter Tip Position from Radiology Reports in Infants.
headline_result: Up to 98% accuracy for binary central/noncentral classification; up to 95% for 12-category classification

model_family: CNN with continuous wavelet transform, local and global classification (computer-aided diagnosis framework)
patient_population: 50 toddlers with autism spectrum disorder and 50 typically developing toddlers undergoing task-based fMRI during a speech-response task
clinical_problem: autism spectrum disorder diagnosis
model_description: Task-based fMRI collected during a speech-response task in toddlers is processed with region-of-interest selection, spatial clustering, and continuous-wavelet-transform feature extraction, then classified with a CNN-based computer-aided diagnosis framework. The system produces both local (per brain region) and fused global autism diagnosis, plus a brain map indicating region-wise severity to support personalized diagnosis and treatment planning.
title: A CNN Deep Local and Global ASD Classification Approach with Continuous Wavelet Transform Using Task-Based FMRI.
study_design: retrospective diagnostic accuracy study, technical development
headline_result: local-region diagnosis accuracy 71-80%; fused global diagnosis accuracy 86%, sensitivity 82%, specificity 92%

patient_population: infants with deformational plagiocephaly
clinical_problem: detecting and monitoring deformational plagiocephaly severity in infants from smartphone photographs instead of anthropometry or CT
model_description: a deep learning classification network takes smartphone camera photos of an infant's head as input and outputs a plagiocephaly classification, deployed via a mobile app for home monitoring
title: Automatic detection and monitoring of abnormal skull shape in children with deformational plagiocephaly using deep learning.
study_design: algorithm development and mobile app deployment study
headline_result: classification accuracy 99.01%

clinical_problem: Can deep learning analysis of diffusion MRI-derived white matter structural connectivity detect juvenile myoclonic epilepsy as a biomarker?
model_description: Takes white matter structural connectivity derived from diffusion MRI (Q-ball imaging, NODDI) as input; a transfer-learned deep convolutional neural network (Inception_resnet_v2) outputs classification of JME vs. normal control.
title: White matter structural connectivity as a biomarker for detecting juvenile myoclonic epilepsy by transferred deep convolutional neural networks with varying transfer rates.
headline_result: Best JME detection accuracy 92.2% with Inception_resnet_v2 at 16% transfer rate

patient_population: 62 children: 33 healthy infants, 22 with bronchiolitis, 7 with bacterial pneumonia
clinical_problem: diagnosis of bronchiolitis and bacterial pneumonia in children using lung ultrasound
model_description: Input: lung ultrasound images/clips; output: classification of healthy vs bronchiolitis vs bacterial pneumonia using deep CNNs, with Grad-CAM visualization of diagnostic LUS artifacts.
title: Classification of Lung Disease in Children by Using Lung Ultrasound Images and Deep Convolutional Neural Network.
dataset_size: 13,962 images from 62 children (33 healthy, 22 bronchiolitis, 7 pneumonia)
headline_result: Inception-ResNet-v2 accuracy 97.75% (healthy vs bronchiolitis); Inception-v3 accuracy 91.5% (three-class)

patient_population: pregnancies across gestation
clinical_problem: the repetitive parts of obstetric ultrasound: positioning, structure identification, gestational age, and real-time quality assurance
task: detection / diagnosis; measurement / quantification; workflow / non-interpretive
model_description: A review that frames AI in obstetric ultrasound around repetition rather than diagnosis: the tasks worth automating are the ones done identically many times per scan. It also makes a point rarely stated in this literature, that realizing any of it depends on interdisciplinary communication between the people building the models and the sonographers who would use them.
title: Artificial Intelligence in Obstetric Ultrasound: An Update and Future Applications.

model_family: random forest / SVM / ANN (ensemble of classifiers)
body_region: hand and wrist (finger, hand, ankle joints)
patient_population: 400 adolescents with Kashin-Beck disease and 400 without
clinical_problem: Distinguishing which clinical and hand/wrist radiographic features best diagnose Kashin-Beck disease, an endemic osteochondropathy, in adolescents
model_description: Combines manually extracted clinical exam findings with radiographic changes on hand X-rays (26 candidate features) as input to random forest, ANN, SVM and linear regression classifiers, with several feature-selection methods, to output a KBD diagnosis
title: Identifying discriminative features for diagnosis of Kashin-Beck disease among adolescents.
headline_result: Best 10-feature subset gave high sensitivity, specificity, accuracy and AUC across classifiers (exact values not given in abstract)

model_family: six 2D, 3D and hybrid deep learning models compared, with Dice and cross-entropy loss variants
patient_population: T1-weighted lower leg MRI of 20 children, six of them with cerebral palsy, with 11 muscles and two bones manually segmented
clinical_problem: segmenting individual lower leg muscles and bones to study how cerebral palsy affects muscle growth, work that currently requires manual segmentation of every scan
model_description: Three findings that transfer beyond this application: the hybrid model matched the inter-rater agreement of human segmenters, so the ceiling has been reached; near-optimal performance came from only 11 training scans, which is the number a small pediatric study can realistically produce; and Dice loss beat cross-entropy consistently. Performance held up on the cerebral palsy scans, only slightly below the typically developing ones, which is the generalization that matters for the intended use.
title: Deep learning methods for automatic segmentation of lower leg muscles and bones from MRI scans of children with and without cerebral palsy.
dataset_size: 20 children (6 with cerebral palsy), 13 labels per scan
headline_result: Dice 0.90, average symmetric surface distance 0.5 mm and volume error 2.6 cm3, matching inter-rater manual performance (0.89, 0.6 mm, 3.3 cm3)

model_family: Bayesian survival analysis followed by unsupervised clustering and a neural network classifier over perfusion and diffusion imaging features
patient_population: 69 children with biopsy-confirmed brain tumors, all with perfusion and diffusion weighted imaging at diagnosis, recruited across multiple sites
clinical_problem: finding survival biomarkers for pediatric brain tumors, which is hard because each individual tumor type is rare - so the study looks for imaging phenotypes that cut across diagnoses
model_description: Sidesteps the small-numbers problem in pediatric neuro-oncology by clustering on imaging rather than modelling each histology separately - the resulting two groups differ in survival across tumor types, and the difference held within high-grade tumors specifically. The practical recommendation is concrete and unusual: perfusion imaging drove the separation and should be prioritized in pediatric brain tumor protocols, where it is often omitted.
title: Combining multi-site magnetic resonance imaging with machine learning predicts survival in pediatric brain tumors.
headline_result: two imaging-defined sub-groups with different survival (p < 0.01), classified by a neural network with 98% accuracy, and a marked survival difference within high-grade tumors (p = 0.029)

patient_population: infants in the first year of life with longitudinal MRI (sample size not stated)
clinical_problem: imputing missing longitudinal MRI scans in infants to complete developmental trajectory studies
model_description: A 3D multi-contrast perceptual adversarial network (MPGAN) takes an infant's T1w/T2w MRI at one time point as input and predicts/imputes the structural MRI appearance at a different developmental time point using voxel-wise and perceptual losses.
title: Longitudinal Prediction of Infant MR Images With Multi-Contrast Perceptual Adversarial Learning.
headline_result: Imputed images improved downstream regression and classification task performance (no single accuracy figure reported)

patient_population: children diagnosed with developmental dyslexia and typical readers (sample size not stated)
clinical_problem: classifying developmental dyslexia from functional MRI and visualizing the brain regions driving classification
model_description: A convolutional neural network classifies subjects as dyslexic or typical readers from functional brain imaging features, with network-visualization techniques used to generate interpretable maps of discriminative brain regions.
title: Visual Explanation for Identification of the Brain Bases for Developmental Dyslexia on fMRI Data.
study_design: retrospective classification study with model-interpretability analysis
headline_result: 94.8% classification accuracy for developmental dyslexia

patient_population: 2,133 children with diarrhea
clinical_problem: Enhancing intestinal ultrasound images and combining with stool data to monitor and provide early warning of norovirus infection trends in young children
model_description: A wavelet-transform-based AI algorithm used for noise reduction/data mining of children's intestinal ultrasound images and stool specimen data, feeding an epidemiological early-warning model for norovirus infection trends.
title: Wavelet Transform Artificial Intelligence Algorithm-Based Data Mining Technology for Norovirus Monitoring and Early Warning.
study_design: Retrospective observational study with AI-based image processing
headline_result: Positive norovirus detection rate 59% among children with diarrhea; noise-reduced ultrasound images were clearer

model_family: Boruta feature selection with multiple kernel learning fusing structural MRI, functional MRI and diffusion tensor features, classified by a support vector machine
patient_population: comorbidity-free children with ADHD and covariable-matched healthy children aged 9-10 from the Adolescent Brain and Cognitive Development (ABCD) study
clinical_problem: diagnosing ADHD in early adolescence, where current criteria rest on behavior analysis that is subjective and inconsistent especially in children
model_description: Fusion at the kernel level rather than by concatenating features, which is the point of the paper - it is compared directly against early feature fusion and against each modality alone, and wins. The cohort design is unusually clean for this literature: comorbidity-free cases, covariable-matched controls, a narrow 9-10 age band, drawn from ABCD. The resulting AUC of 0.698 is the sober number that clean design produces, and it is a useful calibration against the higher figures reported on less controlled samples.
title: Multimodal MR Images-Based Diagnosis of Early Adolescent Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Using Multiple Kernel Learning.
study_design: retrospective model development on a public cohort
dataset_size: ABCD subjects aged 9-10, size not stated in the abstract
headline_result: AUC 0.698 and accuracy 64.3%, significantly better than early feature fusion or any single modality

patient_population: children undergoing CT for a range of clinical indications
clinical_problem: getting diagnostic image quality out of low-dose CT in the population where dose matters most
model_description: A RadioGraphics review of deep-learning CT reconstruction for children: how the engines are trained on paired low-dose and high-dose data to tell true attenuation from noise, how the resulting images look and behave differently from filtered back projection and iterative reconstruction, and what dose reduction is achievable in practice. Written for a department deciding whether to adopt what is already a purchasable scanner option.
release_evidence: deep learning-based reconstruction has been introduced to overcome the limitations of the FBP and IR approaches and is currently available clinically
journal: Radiographics : a review publication of the Radiological Society of North America, Inc
title: Deep Learning-based Reconstruction for Lower-Dose Pediatric CT: Technical Principles, Image Characteristics, and Clinical Implementations.

patient_population: Adolescents with 3D vertebral models (source imaging modality and n not stated)
clinical_problem: Automatically measuring axial vertebral rotation, an indicator of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis severity, from 3D vertebral models
model_description: A point-cloud segmentation neural network (Multi-Input PointNet with attention) that segments vertebral endplates in 3D vertebral models and an algorithm that locates the spinous process tip, to automatically compute axial vertebral rotation angle.
title: Automatic measurement of axial vertebral rotation in 3D vertebral models.
study_design: Retrospective algorithm development and validation study
headline_result: Correlation coefficient 0.986 between automatic and manual AVR measurements

patient_population: 319 fetuses (four-chamber view echocardiography images)
clinical_problem: Automated segmentation of all four fetal cardiac chambers on echocardiography to assist diagnosis of fetal heart disease.

The separate 52-patient cross-platform cohort on standard radiographs is the part that makes it portable beyond an EOS centre.
title: Application of deep learning upon spinal radiographs to predict progression in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis at first clinic visit.

headline_result: Individual-level prediction accuracy 76% (pFWE=0.02), 87% sensitivity, 65% specificity, AUC 0.82, using a superior temporal gyrus-centered network

study_design: retrospective analysis of a public multi-site dataset
headline_result: balanced accuracy up to 99% (5-fold cross-validation)

clinical_problem: Can improved loss functions for deep learning multi-class classifiers more reliably distinguish normal chest x-rays from bacterial and viral pneumonia in children, given that abnormalities are often imbalanced across classes?

title: Evaluation of Glucocorticoid Therapy in Asthma Children with Small Airway Obstruction Based on CT Features of Deep Learning.
study_design: retrospective randomized comparison of treatment groups; NOTE: this publication has been retracted
headline_result: Segmentation algorithm accuracy 81%

clinical_problem: role of AI in improving prenatal ultrasound screening efficiency and diagnostic accuracy
model_description: Narrative review summarizing applications of artificial intelligence to prenatal ultrasound, including automated image quality control, standardized fetal biometric measurement, and diagnostic decision support for anomaly screening.
title: Artificial Intelligence in Prenatal Ultrasound Diagnosis.

patient_population: children with ADHD (literature review)
clinical_problem: diagnosing ADHD in children from MRI-derived functional brain connectivity, as an alternative to subjective clinical assessment
model_description: Review of machine-learning methods that use MRI-derived functional brain connectivity features as input to classify children as having ADHD versus not, comparing feature-extraction and classification techniques.
title: Machine Learning Techniques for the Diagnosis of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder from Magnetic Resonance Imaging: A Concise Review.

headline_result: best model: accuracy 0.771, AUC 0.697 (test set)

clinical_problem: Early detection of osteosarcoma, a bone cancer more common in children than adults, and its lung metastases from CT-derived images
model_description: CT images converted to common file formats (BMP/JPG/PNG) are classified as osteosarcoma-positive or -negative by three pretrained CNNs (VGG-16, ResNet-50, MobileNet-V2)
title: Effectiveness of Learning Systems from Common Image File Types to Detect Osteosarcoma Based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) Models.
headline_result: VGG-16 was the most robust model across image formats; PNG was the preferred format (exact accuracy/F1 not given in abstract)

study_design: retrospective single-center model development and internal testing
headline_result: F1 scores >=0.90 for a majority of the 23 standard views

title: Report of clinical bone age assessment using deep learning for an Asian population in Taiwan.
headline_result: accuracy within 1 year: 95.3%; MAE 0.33y (male), 0.25y (female)

clinical_problem: Characterizing coupled structural and microstructural brain development trajectories in youth from longitudinal multi-modal MRI

title: Longitudinal Correlation Analysis for Decoding Multi-modal Brain Development.
study_design: retrospective longitudinal multimodal neuroimaging methods study (MICCAI)
dataset_size: 679 youths, longitudinal T1 and diffusion MRI

model_family: three-stage pipeline: Mask R-CNN pelvic bone segmentation, HRNet landmark localization, then measurement and classification
patient_population: 1265 pediatric pelvic radiographs for training and 133 from two other medical institutions for validation, with three orthopedic surgeons as comparators
clinical_problem: measuring and classifying developmental dysplasia of the hip on pediatric pelvic radiographs, where the acetabular index and centre-edge angle are drawn by hand and observers disagree
model_description: The decomposition matches how the measurement is actually made - find the ilium, pubis, ischium and femoral heads, then place the landmarks, then compute the angles - which makes each stage checkable. The result that matters clinically is not accuracy but variance: intraclass consistency across surgeons was 0.79-0.98 while the model's was 1.00, because a deterministic model measuring the same film twice cannot disagree with itself. It also matched an intermediate surgeon on Tonnis and IHDI grading, in less time.
title: A Deep-Learning Aided Diagnostic System in Assessing Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip on Pediatric Pelvic Radiographs.
study_design: retrospective model development with external validation and observer comparison
headline_result: Tonnis and IHDI classification accuracy 0.86-0.95 for both hips; no statistically significant difference from surgeons on the numeric indices; intraclass consistency 1.00 for the model versus 0.79-0.98 among surgeons, and significantly faster

patient_population: fetal ultrasound scans (sonographer eye-tracking data)
clinical_problem: identifying which standard scanning task a sonographer is performing during fetal ultrasound, to help standardize image-plane acquisition
model_description: Uses normalized eye-tracking scanpath data recorded from sonographers during fetal ultrasound scans as input and classifies which scanning task/imaging plane is being performed as output.
journal: Simplifying medical ultrasound : second international workshop, ASMUS 2021 : held in conjunction with MICCAI 2021, Strasbourg, France, September 27, 2021 : proceedings. ASMUS (Workshop) (2nd : 2021 : Online)
title: Towards Scale and Position Invariant Task Classification using Normalised Visual Scanpaths in Clinical Fetal Ultrasound.
study_design: retrospective method development study using eye-tracking data
headline_result: F1-score 84%

model_family: Transformer-VLAD deep neural network (self-supervised contrastive learning)
patient_population: obstetric ultrasound scanning (patient numbers not stated)
clinical_problem: guiding sonographer probe movement toward standard anatomical views during obstetric ultrasound, to assist less experienced operators
model_description: Input: real-time ultrasound images during obstetric scanning; output: nearest-landmark descriptor match against a virtual 3D fetal model, visualised as real-time probe-movement guidance cues for the operator.
journal: Medical image computing and computer-assisted intervention : MICCAI ... International Conference on Medical Image Computing and Computer-Assisted Intervention
title: Visual-Assisted Probe Movement Guidance for Obstetric Ultrasound Scanning using Landmark Retrieval.

clinical_problem: assessing lung parenchymal characteristics/aeration in thoracic insufficiency syndrome before and after surgery
model_description: Deep-learning-based segmentation of dynamic MRI extracts lung parenchymal intensity properties to compare lung aeration before/after thoracic insufficiency syndrome surgery and versus healthy children.
journal: Proceedings of SPIE--the International Society for Optical Engineering
title: Lung parenchymal characterization via thoracic dynamic MRI in normal children and pediatric patients with TIS.
dataset_size: 22 scans from 11 TIS patients plus 23 scans from healthy children

clinical_problem: Accurately segmenting brain tissue types on pediatric brain MRI affected by motion/Gibbs artifacts across multiple imaging sites

journal: Machine learning in medical imaging. MLMI (Workshop)
title: Multi-Scale Self-Supervised Learning for Multi-Site Pediatric Brain MR Image Segmentation with Motion/Gibbs Artifacts.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development / benchmark study (MLMI workshop)

patient_population: neonatal brain MRI from multiple sites, including a grand-challenge segmentation dataset (sample size not stated)
clinical_problem: segmenting white matter, gray matter and CSF on neonatal brain MRI acquired at different sites/scanners
model_description: A CycleGAN harmonizes cross-site/cross-scanner neonatal brain MR images into the training-image domain (also reducing motion artifacts), after which a densely-connected U-Net segments white matter, gray matter and CSF.
title: Harmonized neonatal brain MR image segmentation model for cross-site datasets.
headline_result: Better segmentation performance than existing methods on cross-site data and a grand-challenge dataset (no single metric reported in abstract)

patient_population: Pediatric chest x-rays from seven low- and middle-income countries
clinical_problem: Standardizing interpretation of pediatric chest radiographs across epidemiological pneumonia studies to reduce inter/intra-reader variability, per WHO classification
model_description: Convolutional neural networks trained to classify pediatric chest radiographs into five WHO standardized categories, comparing models trained on aggregate consensus labels versus models that predict and then aggregate each individual reader's annotation.
title: Using Machine Learning Methods Incorporating Individual Reader Annotations to Classify Paediatric Chest Radiographs in Epidemiological Studies.
study_design: Retrospective multi-country model development and evaluation study
headline_result: Multi-class accuracy 61% (with individual reader annotations) vs 59% (aggregate only); country accuracy range 45-71%

patient_population: in utero fetal MRI (simulated and real data)
clinical_problem: improving spatial and temporal resolution of dynamic fetal MRI, which is degraded by fetal motion and limited by fast-imaging trade-offs
model_description: Input: low-resolution interleaved dynamic fetal MRI slices; output: super-resolved image series, trained self-supervised on simulated low/high-resolution pairs generated from the acquired data itself.
journal: Medical image computing and computer-assisted intervention : MICCAI ... International Conference on Medical Image Computing and Computer-Assisted Intervention
title: STRESS: Super-Resolution for Dynamic Fetal MRI using Self-Supervised Learning.
study_design: methods development, evaluated on simulated and in utero fetal MRI data

clinical_problem: Overview of AI/machine learning techniques and their current and potential applications in pediatric neuroradiology practice
model_description: Review article defining common AI/machine-vision techniques and surveying their current and potential applications, along with unique adoption challenges, in the subspecialty of pediatric neuroradiology.
title: Current Perspectives of Artificial Intelligence in Pediatric Neuroradiology: An Overview.

patient_population: fetuses undergoing fetal echocardiography for congenital heart disease screening
clinical_problem: prenatal diagnosis of congenital heart disease by fetal echocardiography
task: detection / diagnosis; outcome prediction; measurement / quantification
model_description: This review discusses potential uses of artificial intelligence in fetal cardiology, including improving prenatal detection rates of congenital heart disease on fetal echocardiography, providing more individualized prognosis, and automatically quantifying cardiac function metrics. It notes most existing evidence is retrospective, with few prospective trials, and raises ethical and governance concerns that must be addressed before wider adoption.
title: Artificial intelligence, fetal echocardiography, and congenital heart disease

model_family: deep learning (TW3-C-RUS based bone age assessment system)
patient_population: 80 children aged 5-12 years, hand-wrist radiographs
clinical_problem: bone age assessment to assist junior pediatric radiologists
model_description: A deep-learning bone-age assessment (BAA) system evaluates metacarpal and phalangeal maturity on hand-wrist radiographs using the TW3-C-RUS standard. It was compared against a junior pediatric radiologist reading alone and the same radiologist assisted by the system, referenced against a senior radiologist's assessment aided by BAA. With BAA assistance, the junior radiologist's error and reading time both improved.
journal: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
title: Clinical application of artificial intelligence bone age measurement system based on deep learning
headline_result: System RMSE 0.62 years, MAE 0.47 years; with BAA assistance junior radiologist RMSE improved from 0.71 to 0.27 years and MAE from 0.90 to 0.38 years; mean reading time shortened from 4 min 40 s to 2 min 15 s

patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound (and some 3D ultrasound/MRI) weight estimation
clinical_problem: estimation of fetal weight (EFW) for evaluating fetal growth and pregnancy outcome
model_description: This review summarizes methods for estimating fetal weight from maternal and fetal ultrasound parameters, from traditional formulas (e.g., Hadlock) to 3D ultrasound and MRI volumetric measurement, and notes that a big-data neural-network-based prediction model shows a better coincidence rate than traditional ultrasonic estimation. No specific model, dataset, or performance metric is given.
journal: Journal of Shanghai Jiaotong University (Medical Science)
title: Advances in estimating fetal weight by maternal and fetal ultrasound variables

patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound screening
clinical_problem: prenatal ultrasound screening assistance
model_description: This review describes assistance systems used in prenatal ultrasound, from simple reference curves to newer systems built on artificial intelligence. It argues that AI-based assistance has the potential to change how sonographic fetal examinations are performed, improving efficacy, efficiency, and quality of the exam, though no specific model or trial is described.
title: Current and future assistance systems in prenatal medical imaging

model_family: 3D mixed-scale asymmetric convolutional segmentation network, applied to five canonical CNN backbones
patient_population: 23 six-month-old infants (iSeg-2019 dataset), T1- and T2-weighted brain MRI
clinical_problem: infant brain tissue segmentation (gray matter, white matter, cerebrospinal fluid) for study of early brain development
model_description: 3D-MASNet replaces the standard convolutional layer in existing brain-segmentation networks with a mixed-scale block of asymmetric convolution kernels during training, then equivalently converts it back to the original network architecture for inference. Applied to T1- and T2-weighted MRI from 23 six-month-old infants, it segments the brain into gray matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid, improving five existing CNN segmentation models and ranking first among 30 teams on the iSeg-2019 Grand Challenge validation set.
release_evidence: preprint (bioRxiv); no repository or product mentioned
title: 3D-MASNet: 3D Mixed-scale Asymmetric Convolutional Segmentation Network for 6-month-old Infant Brain MR Images
headline_result: Dice coefficient 0.931 (GM), 0.912 (WM), 0.961 (CSF); ranked first among 30 teams on iSeg-2019 Grand Challenge validation set

model_family: XGBoost, SVM, and Random Forest classifiers
patient_population: 63 patients with epilepsy and 259 healthy controls; preoperative resting-state functional MRI
clinical_problem: detection of epilepsy from brain imaging
model_description: The model uses features derived from resting-state functional MRI hemodynamic 'latency' maps (via principal component analysis of latency z-scores across 36 brain seed regions) as inputs to machine-learning classifiers (XGBoost, SVM, Random Forest) to distinguish patients with epilepsy from healthy controls. It was trained and tested on preoperative rs-fMRI from 63 epilepsy patients and 259 controls, intended as an adjunctive diagnostic tool for pediatric epilepsy.
title: A comparison of machine learning classifiers for pediatric epilepsy using resting-state functional MRI latency data
dataset_size: 63 patients with epilepsy and 259 healthy controls
headline_result: Best model (XGBoost) test AUC 0.79, accuracy 74%, specificity 73%, sensitivity 77%

clinical_problem: assessing inferior vena cava collapse to guide intravenous fluid resuscitation in dehydrated children
model_description: A VGG-16-based deep learning model, run inside a Long Short-Term Memory architecture, analyzes real-time point-of-care ultrasound video of the inferior vena cava to classify complete versus incomplete IVC collapse in children being evaluated for intravenous fluid resuscitation. Trained and tested on 184 previously acquired, de-identified pediatric emergency department ultrasound videos (166 for training/validation, 18 held out for testing), and compared against two blinded point-of-care ultrasound experts.
title: Deep learning algorithm performance compared to experts in visual evaluation of interior vena cava collapse on ultrasound to determine intravenous fluid need in dehydration management
dataset_size: 184 patient IVC ultrasound videos (166 training/validation, 18 held-out test)
headline_result: Substantial agreement with the PEM POCUS attending (Cohen's kappa 0.78, 95% CI 0.49-1.0) and with the PEM resident (kappa 0.66, 95% CI 0.31-1.0) on held-out test videos

patient_population: fetuses; patients undergoing obstetric and gynecologic ultrasound
clinical_problem: AI applications in obstetric and gynecologic ultrasound, including fetal biometry, ovarian tumor malignancy assessment, and fetal CNS/cardiac evaluation

journal: Donald School Journal of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
title: Artificial intelligence and obstetric ultrasound

patient_population: fetuses in the latter half of pregnancy
clinical_problem: objective assessment of fetal facial expressions as a marker of fetal brain function and neurodevelopment
model_description: A review discussing how artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning, can enable objective, automated recognition of fetal facial expressions on four-dimensional ultrasound, moving beyond prior subjective visual assessment, as a potential window into fetal brain function and neurobehavioral development.
journal: Donald School Journal of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
title: Recognition of fetal facial expressions using artificial intelligence deep learning

model_family: previously reported AI bone-age system (deep learning-based, implementing TW3 and TW-China05 methods)
patient_population: 305 Tibetan children (209 boys, 96 girls) aged 4-18 years, left-hand radiographs
clinical_problem: bone age assessment method comparison in Tibetan children
model_description: A previously reported AI bone-age system was used to apply the TW3 (RUS and Carpal) and TW-China05 methods to left-hand radiographs, and its results were compared against manual Greulich-Pyle assessment by two experienced reviewers in 305 Tibetan children aged 4-18. The Greulich-Pyle atlas correlated most strongly with chronological age (r=0.961) among the methods tested, with the AI-implemented TW3-RUS method second (r=0.941).

model_family: 3D deep convolutional neural network built on U-Net with dense connections and residual skip-connections
patient_population: IBSR18 dataset (diverse age groups) and iSeg-2017 multi-modality challenge dataset (MRI scans of infants)
clinical_problem: brain tissue segmentation (white matter, gray matter, cerebrospinal fluid)
model_description: A compact 3D deep convolutional network built on the U-Net architecture, using densely connected convolutional layers and residual skip-connections, to segment brain MRI into white matter, gray matter and cerebrospinal fluid while using far fewer parameters (40-98% fewer) than comparable deep-learning architectures. Trained with cross-entropy, Dice, and combined loss functions and evaluated on the IBSR18 dataset and the iSeg-2017 infant brain segmentation challenge dataset, intended to support study of brain structure/development, detection of abnormal tissue, diagnosis, and surgical guidance.
release_evidence: Code is available at: https://github.com/basnetr/U-DenseResNet
title: A deep dense residual network with reduced parameters for volumetric brain tissue segmentation from MR images
headline_result: Best performance on the IBSR18 test set and competitive performance on the iSeg-2017 infant challenge dataset, while reducing parameters by 40-98% versus comparable architectures

model_family: machine learning with opportunistic stacking across multimodal MRI
patient_population: approximately 11,000 children from the ABCD cohort, followed over 2 years during early adolescence
clinical_problem: prediction of childhood cognitive ability from multimodal brain MRI (task fMRI, resting-state fMRI, structural MRI, DTI)
model_description: Multimodal MRI (task-based fMRI from three tasks, resting-state fMRI, structural MRI, and DTI) from the ABCD cohort was combined using a machine-learning model with 'opportunistic stacking' to handle missing data. The model predicted cognitive ability scores, explaining about 20% of variance, remained stable across two years, and generalized across sites; predictions partially mediated associations with socio-demographic, psychological, and genetic factors.
release_evidence: no code, weights, or product release stated
title: Longitudinally stable, brain-based predictive models mediate the relationships between childhood cognition and socio-demographic, psychological and genetic factors
headline_result: Brain-based model explained ~20% of variance in childhood cognition, stable across 2 years and generalizable across sites.

model_family: ensemble of deep convolutional neural networks
patient_population: premature infants near term (n=107), imaged with quiet-breathing MRI, with and without bronchopulmonary dysplasia
clinical_problem: quantification of neonatal lung disease / bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) severity
model_description: The model segments premature infant lungs on quiet-breathing MRI using an ensemble of deep convolutional neural networks, then reconstructs a 3D lung model and derives descriptors of volume, shape, surface, and signal intensity. It was trained and validated in 107 near-term premature infants against manual annotation, reaching a volumetric Dice score of 0.908 (0.880 in an independent validation cohort). The resulting MRI-derived lung descriptors were used to separate infants with and without bronchopulmonary dysplasia and to grade BPD severity, without radiation exposure.

title: Automated MRI Lung Segmentation and 3D Morphological Features for Quantification of Neonatal Lung Disease
headline_result: Volumetric Dice score 0.908 (independent cohort 0.880); AUC 0.92 for BPD vs no BPD, AUC 0.84 mild vs severe BPD, AUC 0.75 for severity prediction

patient_population: 1,769 children with community-acquired pneumonia, grouped by causative pathogen (virus, bacteria, mycoplasma)
clinical_problem: community-acquired pneumonia pathogen classification (viral vs bacterial vs mycoplasma)
model_description: The model takes chest X-rays from children with community-acquired pneumonia and classifies either the whole-lung image or a lesion region-of-interest to predict the likely causative pathogen (virus, bacteria, or mycoplasma pneumoniae). It was trained and tested on a 7:1:2 split of 1,769 pneumonia cases using a convolutional neural network, comparing a full-lung model against a model restricted to the lesion area. It is intended to help distinguish pathogen type from chest radiograph appearance alone.
journal: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
title: Chest X-ray model based on convolution neural network in diagnosis of children community acquired pneumonia caused by different pathogens
headline_result: Full lung model AUC 0.798 and local model AUC 0.819 for mycoplasma pneumonia (best-performing category); overall accuracy 61.85% (full lung) and 58.04%/63.77%/54.05% variants across models

title: Multi-sequence clinical-radiomic model predicts molecular subgroups of pediatric medulloblastoma
headline_result: Combined clinical-radiomic model AUC 0.944 for WNT and 0.819 for SHH subgroup in the testing cohort (radiomics-only model AUC 0.519 for Group3, 0.705 for Group4)

model_family: 3D CNN-based localization and landmark-guided pose estimation with deformable slice-to-volume registration (DSVR)

clinical_problem: reconstructing high-resolution 3D fetal thorax MRI from motion-corrupted scans to support diagnosis of congenital heart and body anomalies

Evaluated on fetal MRI datasets spanning 21-36 weeks' gestational age and simulated motion, including assessment of vascular structure definition.
