model_family: 2D holistically nested network with multi-feature architecture, in single-plane and three-cardinal-plane variants
patient_population: 93 subjects including actively growing adolescents; 86 femurs and 90 patellae with manual outer cortex models, nine-fold cross-validation
clinical_problem: segmenting the patella and distal femoral cortex on MRI, the manual step that has held back study of how 3D bone morphology relates to knee osteoarthritis and pain - and of how the joint develops in adolescence
model_description: Holistically nested edge detection is well matched to the actual difficulty here - the boundary between cortical bone and the neighbouring joint structures is often indistinct - and the sub-millimetre errors bear that out. The pediatric result is the one worth recording: segmentation accuracy was unaffected by the presence of open growth plates, which is exactly where adult-trained bone segmentation usually breaks. Single-plane input beat the three-plane variant, which is a useful and slightly counter-intuitive practical finding.
title: Fully automated patellofemoral MRI segmentation using holistically nested networks: Implications for evaluating patellofemoral osteoarthritis, pain, injury, pathology, and adolescent development.
headline_result: average absolute surface error 0.33 mm for both bones, Dice 97% femur and 94% patella, with no effect from active growth plates or pathology

model_family: deep representation learning (ensemble space learning and marginal shape deep learning)
patient_population: 668 chest radiographs from patients aged 3 months to 89 years
clinical_problem: segmenting lung fields (including the retro-cardiac region) from chest radiographs across pediatric and adult cohorts for computer-aided diagnosis and lung capacity estimation
model_description: Input: chest radiographs from a wide age range; output: lung field segmentation mask including the retro-cardiac region, using deep representation learning to accommodate large pediatric-to-adult shape variation.
title: A Generic Approach to Lung Field Segmentation From Chest Radiographs Using Deep Space and Shape Learning.
study_design: retrospective segmentation model development and evaluation
headline_result: Mean Dice similarity coefficient 0.96 ± 0.03

model_family: multivariate classification on whole-brain functional connectivity
patient_population: 202 children and adults with Tourette syndrome and control subjects
clinical_problem: whether Tourette syndrome has an imaging signature, and whether it is the same signature in children as in adults
model_description: Classifies Tourette syndrome from functional connectivity separately in children and in adults, then asks whether either classifier transfers to the other age group. It does not, which is the finding: the connections that distinguish the disorder are age-specific. For anyone building pediatric models from adult data, this is a clean demonstration of why that assumption fails in a developmental disorder.
title: Atypical Functional Connectivity in Tourette Syndrome Differs Between Children and Adults.
headline_result: successful classification in children and adults separately, with no generalization across age groups

patient_population: 60 adolescents with conduct disorder and 60 age/sex-matched healthy controls, all male
clinical_problem: classifying conduct disorder in adolescents from structural brain MRI
model_description: A 3D AlexNet CNN takes structural MRI as input and classifies adolescents as having conduct disorder vs. healthy, with saliency maps highlighting discriminative brain regions.
title: Three dimensional convolutional neural network-based classification of conduct disorder with structural MRI.
study_design: retrospective case-control classification study with 5-fold cross-validation
headline_result: Accuracy 0.85, AUC 0.86 (vs. SVM AUC 0.78, p=0.046)

model_family: machine-learning pipeline on clinical and sonographic biometry features
patient_population: 686 singleton vaginal deliveries in Israel for derivation and 2,584 in California for validation, with 131 and 31 cases of shoulder dystocia
clinical_problem: predicting shoulder dystocia, so that Cesarean delivery for suspected macrosomia is offered to the right pregnancies
model_description: Uses sonographic fetal biometry, adjusted for gestational age at delivery, together with obstetric history to predict shoulder dystocia, and validates on a cohort from a different country and health system. It beat the current paradigm of estimated fetal weight plus maternal diabetes. Adjusted estimated fetal weight and abdominal circumference were the strongest imaging contributors, which is a check that the model is using the anatomy one would expect.
journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
title: Development and validation of a machine-learning model for prediction of shoulder dystocia.
headline_result: AUC 0.793 versus 0.745 for adjusted estimated fetal weight combined with diabetes (P = 1e-16)

model_family: adversarial one-class classification combined with video transfer learning (deep learning, GAN-based)
patient_population: fetuses undergoing echocardiographic screening for congenital heart disease
clinical_problem: screening for fetal congenital heart disease on echocardiography
model_description: Four-chamber-view fetal echocardiogram video slices go in; the DGACNN model (one-class anomaly detection plus a GAN-based classifier) outputs recognition of fetal congenital heart disease.
title: Fetal Congenital Heart Disease Echocardiogram Screening Based on DGACNN: Adversarial One-Class Classification Combined with Video Transfer Learning.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development study compared against expert cardiologists
headline_result: 84-85% recognition accuracy, outperforming expert cardiologists (84% in test) and other state-of-the-art networks by 1%-20%

model_family: three-network pipeline: basic CNN, deeper multi-task CNN, and an aggregated residual visual block detector
patient_population: fetuses undergoing cardiac screening ultrasound
clinical_problem: deciding whether a fetal cardiac four-chamber view is adequate to diagnose from
model_description: Scores the quality of a fetal four-chamber view in three steps: is this actually a four-chamber plane, are the gain and zoom right, and are the key anatomical structures visible. The three outputs combine into one quantitative score. It runs at 101 frames per second, which is fast enough to give the sonographer feedback while the probe is still on the abdomen.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: A Generic Quality Control Framework for Fetal Ultrasound Cardiac Four-Chamber Planes.
dataset_size: an institutional fetal ultrasound dataset; size not stated
headline_result: mean average precision 93.52% at 101 frames per second

model_family: voxel-based morphometry with support vector machine
patient_population: 22 children with hydrocephalus (12 progressive, 10 chronic compensated) and 30 age-matched healthy controls
clinical_problem: differentiating progressive from chronic compensated hydrocephalus in children using structural MRI
model_description: An SVM classifier applied to voxel-based-morphometry gray-matter-volume features from T1-weighted MRI differentiates progressive from chronic compensated hydrocephalus, and both from healthy controls.
title: Detection of differentiated changes in gray matter in children with progressive hydrocephalus and chronic compensated hydrocephalus using voxel-based morphometry and machine learning.
headline_result: accuracy 88.46% (hydrocephalus vs. controls); 77.27% (progressive vs. chronic compensated)

model_family: HYDRA (semisupervised machine learning, heterogeneity through discriminative analysis)
patient_population: 1141 youths with internalizing symptoms, structural (and secondary functional/diffusion) MRI
clinical_problem: identifying neurobiological subtypes of internalizing symptoms (anxiety/depression) in youth
model_description: Structural MRI volume and cortical thickness data go in; a semisupervised machine-learning method (HYDRA) outputs discrete neurobiological subtypes of internalizing psychopathology.
title: Neurostructural Heterogeneity in Youths With Internalizing Symptoms.
study_design: cross-sectional cohort study with semisupervised machine-learning subtyping
headline_result: 2 stable subtypes identified (adjusted Rand index 0.66, permutation-based FDR p<.001)

model_family: two-stage CNN localization and segmentation plus outlier-robust super-resolution
patient_population: fetuses with normal brains and with varying ventriculomegaly associated with open spina bifida
clinical_problem: producing a usable high-resolution fetal brain volume from motion-corrupted stacks, including brains malformed by open spina bifida
model_description: A four-stage pipeline that takes the motion-corrupted 2D slice stacks of a fetal brain MRI and returns a high-resolution volume in standard anatomical space with no user input. One network finds the brain, a second segments it finely, then a super-resolution step reconstructs the volume. It removes the manual brain-masking step that has kept fetal volume reconstruction out of routine practice.
title: An automated framework for localization, segmentation and super-resolution reconstruction of fetal brain MRI.
headline_result: each stage outperformed state-of-the-art methods on segmentation and reconstruction, including expert-reader quality assessment

model_family: logistic ridge regression, SVM, J48 decision tree
patient_population: 83 ADHD subjects (training cohort), 36 ADHD subjects (independent validation cohort), in an 8-week open-label methylphenidate trial
clinical_problem: Can pre-treatment features, including brain structural connectivity, predict which children with ADHD will develop sleep problems after starting methylphenidate?
model_description: Machine learning classifiers combine demographic, clinical, neuropsychological, genetic and structural brain connectivity (frontostriatal circuit) features, added stepwise, to predict whether a child with ADHD will develop sleep problems after starting methylphenidate.
title: Prediction of sleep side effects following methylphenidate treatment in ADHD youth.
study_design: prospective open-label trial with machine-learning outcome prediction and independent validation
headline_result: Best model (logistic ridge regression, full feature set including structural connectivity) achieved 95.5% accuracy (AUC 0.99) in training; 86.1% accuracy (AUC 0.92) in independent validation

model_family: problem-based CNN architecture with transfer learning and custom preprocessing
patient_population: children in the pediatric chest X-ray dataset, with a separate dataset used to test generalization
clinical_problem: detecting consolidation on a child's chest radiograph
model_description: Argues that networks designed to win on ImageNet are the wrong shape for radiographs, and designs an architecture around the problem instead, with preprocessing chosen to preserve the information that consolidation lives in. It checks its own reasoning with an occlusion test showing which region drove each decision, and tests generalization on a second dataset rather than a held-out split of the same one.
journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
title: Deep learning, reusable and problem-based architectures for detection of consolidation on chest X-ray images.
dataset_size: the pediatric chest X-ray dataset plus an external validation dataset
headline_result: 94.67% accuracy for consolidation detection, above the previously published architectures on the same dataset

model_family: dual-input CNN merging two ResNet branches
patient_population: children undergoing elbow radiography; 1,266 AP and lateral pairs for development, 258 for temporal testing and 95 from a second hospital
clinical_problem: detecting supracondylar fracture of the humerus in children on conventional radiographs
model_description: Reads the anteroposterior and lateral elbow radiographs together, as a radiologist does, by merging two networks rather than judging each view alone. Tested twice on data the model had never seen: a later year at the same hospital and a different hospital entirely. Its errors are asymmetric in a clinically useful direction, with very high negative predictive value and lower specificity, meaning it over-calls rather than misses.
title: Using a Dual-Input Convolutional Neural Network for Automated Detection of Pediatric Supracondylar Fracture on Conventional Radiography.
study_design: retrospective development with temporal and geographic external validation and reader study
dataset_size: 1,266 radiograph pairs for development; 258 temporal and 95 geographic external test pairs
headline_result: AUC 0.985 (temporal) and 0.992 (geographic) external test sets, comparable to human readers; geographic sensitivity 100%, specificity 86.1%, negative predictive value 100%

patient_population: training: 79 FASD (5.7-18.9y) and 81 controls (5.8-18.5y); testing: 67 FASD (6.0-19.6y) and 74 controls (5.2-19.5y), from two independent datasets
clinical_problem: identifying children and adolescents with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder from regional brain volumes
model_description: 87 regional brain volumes extracted from 3D T1-weighted MRI using FreeSurfer are input to a support vector machine that classifies children/adolescents as having fetal alcohol spectrum disorder or being a healthy control; separate models are also built by sex.
title: Multivariate models of brain volume for identification of children and adolescents with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder.
study_design: retrospective multicenter case-control diagnostic accuracy study with independent test dataset
dataset_size: training: 79 FASD + 81 controls; testing: 67 FASD + 74 controls (independent dataset)
headline_result: test accuracy 77%, sensitivity 64%, specificity 88%

patient_population: 71 Lenke 1 adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients with 2-year follow-up
clinical_problem: Predicting optimal versus suboptimal spontaneous lumbar curve correction after selective thoracic fusion in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis using radiographic parameters.
model_description: Radiographic spinal parameters (Cobb angles, kyphosis, rotation, translation) are used as input to a decision tree model that predicts optimal versus suboptimal spontaneous lumbar curve correction after surgery.
journal: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie
title: Defining criteria for optimal lumbar curve correction following the selective thoracic fusion surgery in Lenke 1 adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: developing a decision tree.
headline_result: Prediction accuracy 82% (95% CI 0.73-0.94)

modality: x-ray / radiography; CT; MRI; nuclear / PET
patient_population: adults and children in the reviewed literature
clinical_problem: where deep learning stands for musculoskeletal lesion detection, progression and prediction, including pediatric bone age
task: detection / diagnosis; measurement / quantification; outcome prediction
model_description: A review that sorts musculoskeletal deep learning by modality and by how close each application is to the clinic. Its judgment is that pediatric bone age and fracture detection on radiographs perform well enough to be nearly ready for practice, while CT and especially MRI applications remain harder because the abnormality has to be tracked across slices and contrasts. It closes by insisting on prospective multi-institution evaluation before deployment.
journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
title: Deep Learning for Lesion Detection, Progression, and Prediction of Musculoskeletal Disease.

model_family: ensemble of semi-dense 3D fully convolutional networks
patient_population: 6-month-old infants in the public MICCAI iSEG-2017 challenge data
clinical_problem: segmenting the 6-month infant brain, where gray and white matter are nearly isointense
model_description: An ensemble of networks segmenting infant brain tissue from paired T1 and T2 images. The useful property is that where the ensemble members disagree, the segmentation is usually wrong, so the disagreement map tells a human where to look and correct. The architecture uses an order of magnitude fewer parameters than a 3D U-Net, which matters for anyone deploying this on ordinary hardware.
journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
title: Deep CNN ensembles and suggestive annotations for infant brain MRI segmentation.
study_design: technical development on a public challenge
headline_result: ranked first or second on most metrics among 21 teams; ensemble disagreement highly correlated with segmentation error

model_family: hybrid wavelet filter bank + fuzzy SVM
patient_population: Newborn infants (<28 days old), T1- and T2-weighted MRI
clinical_problem: Segmenting newborn brain MRI into tissue types (white matter, gray matter) to assess brain growth, when similar tissue intensities make segmentation difficult
model_description: A hybrid atlas-free hierarchical graph-based segmentation method using wavelet filter banks for feature extraction and a fuzzy support vector machine for tissue classification, taking multimodal T1/T2 newborn brain MRI as input and producing tissue segmentation maps.
title: A novel hybrid atlas-free hierarchical graph-based segmentation of newborn brain MRI using wavelet filter banks.
study_design: Retrospective algorithm development and validation study
headline_result: Segmentation precision 90%, sensitivity 98%

model_family: deep learning segmentation of orbital fat used as an intensity reference tissue
patient_population: 1018 scans from 256 participants in a study of pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis, at 1.5 and 3 T
clinical_problem: comparing conventional MRI intensities across scans years apart, where normalizing to brain tissue is circular in a disease that changes the brain - so a reference tissue outside the disease process is needed
model_description: The reasoning is the contribution: in multiple sclerosis both white and gray matter are affected, so normalizing to brain tissue removes the biological change you are trying to measure. Orbital fat is always in a head T1, is unaffected by the disease, and is tedious to outline - which makes it a good automation target. Machine segmentations agreed with the adjudicating expert better than other experts did, and calibrated intensities tracked semi-quantitative magnetization transfer ratio better than the standard normalization algorithm. Half a second per scan.
title: Deep learning segmentation of orbital fat to calibrate conventional MRI for longitudinal studies.
headline_result: machine segmentations agreed with the adjudicating expert better than other expert humans did, and calibration agreed with magnetization transfer ratio imaging better than the WhiteStripe normalization algorithm, at 0.5 s per scan

patient_population: 5 adults and 2 pediatric subjects undergoing brain MR fingerprinting
clinical_problem: rapid, high-resolution brain tissue (T1/T2) quantification via MR fingerprinting
model_description: Input is submillimeter-resolution MR fingerprinting acquisition data; output is quantitative T1 and T2 tissue maps, produced by a deep learning model that replaces standard template matching, tested on adult and pediatric subjects.
title: Submillimeter MR fingerprinting using deep learning-based tissue quantification.
study_design: prospective technical development and feasibility study
headline_result: high-quality 0.8 mm in-plane T1/T2 mapping achieved in 7.5 seconds per slice, a 5-fold acceleration versus standard methods

model_family: separate convolutional networks trained on whole-hand radiographs and on cropped index-finger images
patient_population: the public RSNA pediatric bone age challenge dataset: 12 611 training and 200 test radiographs, with the index finger cropped to create a parallel dataset; three pediatric radiologists also read both versions
clinical_problem: whether the whole hand is needed for bone age, or whether a single digit carries enough of the maturational signal
model_description: A clean ablation with a practical payoff. The network lost almost nothing when restricted to the index finger (5.1 versus 4.7 months), while radiologists reading the same cropped images degraded badly (8.0 months) - so the information is there and humans are not extracting it. The authors turn that into advice a radiologist can act on immediately: use the second digit as the starting point of the search pattern. It also raises the question of how little of an image these models actually need.
title: Bone age determination using only the index finger: a novel approach using a convolutional neural network compared with human radiologists.
study_design: retrospective model development with reader comparison
headline_result: mean absolute difference 5.1 months for the index-finger network versus 4.7 months for the whole-hand network (P = 0.14), against 8.0 months for radiologists reading the same index-finger radiographs (P < 0.0001)

model_family: convolutional neural network on automatically segmented image patches, with speckle-reduction-based data augmentation using an optimized Bayesian non-local means filter
patient_population: neonatal hip ultrasound images captured in Graf's standard plane, divided into normal, mild dysplasia and severe dysplasia
clinical_problem: classifying neonatal hips by Graf's method, the most reproducible ultrasound system for developmental dysplasia of the hip and still highly dependent on the skill of both the sonographer and the evaluator
model_description: The novelty is in the augmentation rather than the architecture: instead of geometric transforms, the training set is expanded with speckle-reduced variants produced by an optimized Bayesian non-local means filter, which teaches the network what is anatomy and what is ultrasound noise. The gain is large and cleanly attributed - accuracy rose from 92.29% to 97.70% from that change alone. A transferable idea for any ultrasound classification problem with limited data.
title: Deep Convolutional Neural Network-Based Automatic Classification of Neonatal Hip Ultrasound Images: A Novel Data Augmentation Approach with Speckle Noise Reduction.
headline_result: accuracy 97.70% with speckle-reduction augmentation, up from 92.29% without it

model_family: random forest, logistic regression, decision trees (classical ML on radiographic measurements)
patient_population: 141 knees (age 7-16) with complete discoid lateral meniscus and 141 age/sex-matched normal knees
clinical_problem: predicting the presence of complete discoid lateral meniscus from knee radiograph measurements
model_description: Input: radiographic measurements of the knee (lateral joint space, fibular head height, tibial spine height, etc.); output: prediction of presence of complete discoid lateral meniscus.
journal: Journal of orthopaedic research : official publication of the Orthopaedic Research Society
title: Predictive validity of radiographic signs of complete discoid lateral meniscus in children using machine learning techniques.
study_design: retrospective diagnostic accuracy / prediction model study
dataset_size: 141 knees with discoid meniscus + 141 matched normal knees
headline_result: Random forest model: AUC 0.909, sensitivity 86.5%, specificity 82.2%

patient_population: 170 physically healthy adolescents followed longitudinally (7th-12th grade)
clinical_problem: Do baseline structural brain MRI features and substance-use onset predict later academic achievement in adolescents, potentially identifying imaging biomarkers of vulnerability related to substance use?
model_description: A machine learning approach uses 336 baseline structural MRI-derived brain metrics (regional thickness, area, volume) together with academic and substance-use history to identify features predicting 11th/12th-grade GPA and to distinguish drinkers from non-drinkers.
title: Substance use initiation and the prediction of subsequent academic achievement.
study_design: longitudinal cohort study with machine-learning feature selection
headline_result: 16 of 336 baseline MRI features distinguished average-performing drinkers from non-drinkers; no single accuracy/AUC given

model_family: deep-learning segmentation, classification and localization models
patient_population: images from 10,251 normal and 2,529 abnormal pregnancies, with abnormality confirmed by neonatal ultrasound, follow-up or autopsy
clinical_problem: recognizing an abnormal fetal brain on standard axial screening planes
model_description: Takes a standard axial fetal brain ultrasound image, segments the skull outline, classifies the brain as normal or abnormal, and overlays a heat map indicating where the abnormality is. Trained on a large hospital archive with outcomes confirmed after birth rather than by the reporting sonographer, and split at case rather than image level, which is the methodologically careful choice.
journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
title: Using deep-learning algorithms to classify fetal brain ultrasound images as normal or abnormal.
dataset_size: 15,372 normal and 14,047 abnormal images from 12,780 pregnancies
headline_result: classification accuracy 96.3%, sensitivity 96.9%, specificity 95.9%, AUC 0.989; lesions localized precisely in 61.6% of abnormal images and closely in a further 24.6%

patient_population: fetuses undergoing echocardiography
clinical_problem: assessing fetal cardiac structure and function when the heart is small, moving, and often scanned by someone without fetal echocardiography training
model_description: A short review for fetal cardiologists of where machine learning can help: improving the acquired image, extracting measurements and segmentations automatically, and supporting the prenatal diagnosis of cardiac remodeling and structural abnormality. Written as an orientation to the technology rather than an evaluation of specific models.
title: Machine Learning in Fetal Cardiology: What to Expect.

model_family: pixel-level texture classification on multi-scale Gaussian derivative features
patient_population: 858 interpretable pediatric chest radiographs, 39% with primary-endpoint pneumonia by radiologist consensus
clinical_problem: identifying WHO-defined primary-endpoint pneumonia on a child's chest radiograph, the definition used in vaccine efficacy and epidemiological studies
model_description: Targets a specific and consequential definition rather than pneumonia in general: the WHO primary-endpoint criterion is what vaccine trials are scored against, and it depends on three radiologists agreeing. Automating it would make large epidemiological studies tractable and remove reader variability from vaccine efficacy estimates. Three radiologists independently set the reference, and the harder task of separating primary-endpoint pneumonia from other infiltrate is reported separately.
title: Computer-aided diagnosis for World Health Organization-defined chest radiograph primary-endpoint pneumonia in children.
headline_result: AUC 0.850 against radiologist consensus (sensitivity 76%, specificity 80%); AUC 0.810 separating primary-endpoint pneumonia from other infiltrate

model_family: four-stage framework: transfer learning, deep feature extraction, feature reduction and classification, with feature fusion across pretrained networks
patient_population: embryonic MRI images across various gestational ages
clinical_problem: detecting embryonic neurodevelopmental disorders on prenatal MRI, where up to three in a thousand pregnancies carry a brain defect and earlier detection changes counseling
model_description: The argument is against the handcrafted-feature pipelines that preceded it: enhancement, segmentation and feature engineering each introduce choices, and a deep network learns from the raw image instead. Feature fusion across several pretrained backbones stands in for the training data that prenatal MRI cohorts do not have. Comparison is against prior work on embryonic images rather than a held-out external set, so the performance claim is relative.
title: Deep Learning Techniques for Automatic Detection of Embryonic Neurodevelopmental Disorders.
headline_result: identified embryonic neurodevelopmental disorders from MRI across a range of gestational ages, performing competitively with prior work on embryonic images

model_family: CNN-based pipeline for transcerebellar plane detection, transcerebellar diameter measurement and gestational age estimation
patient_population: conventional ultrasound data simulating the point-of-care task, with a first application to clinical video from a low-cost probe
clinical_problem: dating a pregnancy at the point of care in low- and middle-income countries, where the two barriers are the steep learning curve for scanning and the lack of affordable portable devices
model_description: Chooses the transcerebellar diameter rather than head circumference deliberately - it is a single linear measurement on one plane, which is what a short sweep from an inexperienced operator can realistically yield. The whole framework is specified around the hardware it would run on: a wireless probe, a phone or tablet, and on-device processing. Proof of concept, with the transfer to real low-cost probe video presented as the next step rather than as an achieved result.
title: Toward point-of-care ultrasound estimation of fetal gestational age from the trans-cerebellar diameter using CNN-based ultrasound image analysis.
headline_result: proof-of-concept accuracy for automatic transcerebellar plane detection, diameter measurement and gestational age estimation, with a first application to low-cost probe video

patient_population: two twin datasets (adult, pediatric) and two repeat-scan datasets (adult, pediatric)
clinical_problem: using individual brain functional connectivity patterns to study genetic influences on network organization across development
model_description: Input is resting-state functional connectivity MRI; support vector machine classifiers trained on one scan session are used to identify the same individual, or a co-twin, from an independent scan, to study how classification accuracy varies with genetic relatedness.
title: Functional Connectivity Fingerprints at Rest Are Similar across Youths and Adults and Vary with Genetic Similarity.
headline_result: 100% accuracy identifying individuals from a repeat scan; classifier accuracy decreased with decreasing genetic relatedness between twins

model_family: transfer-learned convolutional network regressing a continuous value from the chest radiograph
patient_population: 1031 cardiac catheterizations in 657 patients at a tertiary center from January 2005 to April 2019 (median age 3.4 years, IQR 1.2-8.6), with 78 patients / 100 catheterizations held out; mean Fick-derived pulmonary to systemic flow ratio 1.43 (SD 0.95)
clinical_problem: quantifying pulmonary blood flow in congenital heart disease from the chest radiograph, which today is read subjectively and qualitatively and whose gold standard is an invasive catheterization
model_description: Turns a qualitative impression - does the pulmonary vasculature look plethoric - into a number on the same scale as the catheter measurement, with the Fick-derived ratio from a simultaneous catheterization as ground truth. The comparison against three certified pediatric cardiologists reading the same films is what establishes the claim, and the clinically salient operating point (a ratio of 2.0 or more, the shunt magnitude that prompts intervention) is reported separately. A non-invasive stand-in for part of what catheterization is done to answer.
title: Prediction of Pulmonary to Systemic Flow Ratio in Patients With Congenital Heart Disease Using Deep Learning-Based Analysis of Chest Radiographs.
study_design: retrospective observational study with expert comparison
dataset_size: 1031 catheterizations in 657 patients; 100 held out for evaluation
headline_result: prediction of the pulmonary to systemic flow ratio from chest radiographs evaluated by intraclass correlation and Bland-Altman analysis, with the diagnostic concordance rate compared against three certified pediatric cardiologists

model_family: dilated convolutional chain followed by a W-Net refinement stage
patient_population: 895 apical four-chamber views from fetal echocardiography
clinical_problem: outlining the seven key structures of the apical four-chamber view, from which congenital heart disease is judged
model_description: Segments seven anatomical structures in the fetal four-chamber view, contending with speckle, chambers that look alike, and boundaries that simply are not visible in places. A dilated convolution chain localizes the chambers across scales and a second stage sharpens the boundaries. The output is intended as the input to automated cardiac indices rather than as a diagnosis in itself.
journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
title: DW-Net: A cascaded convolutional neural network for apical four-chamber view segmentation in fetal echocardiography.
headline_result: Dice 0.827, pixel accuracy 0.933, AUC 0.990, substantially above established segmentation methods

model_family: machine-learned decision algorithm over discrete sonographic features
patient_population: all pediatric patients treated for surgically confirmed ovarian torsion at a quaternary pediatric hospital over 11 years, with a non-torsed control cohort of girls and young adults presenting to the emergency department between April 2015 and May 2016
clinical_problem: diagnosing ovarian torsion quickly enough in girls with pelvic or abdominal pain, since delay causes irreversible ovarian ischemia and the ultrasound features are not pathognomonic
model_description: Works on the features a radiologist already records rather than on pixels - ovarian volumes, medialized position relative to the mid-uterine line, Doppler signal, peripheral follicles, mass or cyst, free fluid - which makes the resulting algorithm something a reader can follow and argue with at the workstation. Surgical confirmation defines the cases, and the paper also reports how often each individual sonographic sign appears, which is useful on its own. Published in Pediatric Radiology and framed as an aid to the radiologist rather than a replacement.
title: Ovarian torsion: developing a machine-learned algorithm for diagnosis.
dataset_size: 11 years of surgically confirmed torsion cases plus a contemporaneous non-torsed control cohort
headline_result: a machine-learned algorithm over sonographic features to aid radiologists in diagnosing ovarian torsion, with the frequency of each sonographic element quantified

patient_population: 15 analyzed children (of 21 enrolled), average age 5.9 years
clinical_problem: Estimating glomerular filtration rate in children using motion-robust dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI with automated CNN-based kidney/aorta segmentation, compared to nuclear medicine and serum creatinine methods
model_description: In-house software automatically segments kidney parenchyma and aorta on dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI using convolutional neural network techniques, then fits a tracer kinetic model to calculate MRI-based GFR, compared against nuclear medicine 99mTc-DTPA GFR and creatinine-based eGFR.
title: Prospective pediatric study comparing glomerular filtration rate estimates based on motion-robust dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging and serum creatinine (eGFR) to 99mTc DTPA.
headline_result: MR-GFR vs. NM-GFR Pearson r=0.98 (vs. eGFR r=0.73)

model_family: fully automated AI bone age software
patient_population: 514 patients undergoing hand radiography for bone age
clinical_problem: bone age assessment against the Greulich-Pyle standard, in both accuracy and reading time
model_description: Compares a commercial-style automated bone age program against three blinded radiologists applying Greulich-Pyle, with a two-expert consensus as reference. The software was more accurate than the individual readers, not merely comparable, and cut reading time by 87%. Performance did not differ by sex. The design is the useful part: blinded readers, a consensus reference, and time measured alongside accuracy.
release_evidence: described as a novel AI software version; commercial availability not stated in the abstract
title: Artificial intelligence in bone age assessment: accuracy and efficiency of a novel fully automated algorithm compared to the Greulich-Pyle method.
headline_result: mean absolute deviation from reference 0.34 years for the software versus 0.79 years for the readers (p < 0.001); reading time reduced by 87%

model_family: end-to-end deep network (feature extractor, connectivity network, classifier)
patient_population: children in the public ADHD-200 dataset, contributed by several imaging sites
clinical_problem: diagnosing ADHD, which currently rests entirely on behavioral assessment
model_description: Takes preprocessed resting-state fMRI time series and outputs an ADHD diagnosis, learning the functional connectivity representation as part of the network rather than computing it beforehand. Because connectivity is learned end to end, the model can be interrogated for which regions carried the decision; here the frontal lobe dominated. Trained and tested on a public multi-site dataset, so the numbers are directly comparable with prior work.
title: DeepFMRI: End-to-end deep learning for functional connectivity and classification of ADHD using fMRI.
study_design: technical development on a public benchmark
headline_result: 73.1% accuracy at the New York University site (specificity 91.6%, sensitivity 65.5%), above prior state of the art

patient_population: 182 participants aged 12-25 years
clinical_problem: Identifying subfield-specific limbic brain volume changes that differentiate clinical risk stages for mental illness in adolescents and young adults
model_description: A machine-learning classifier trained on subfield-specific hippocampus, amygdala, and thalamus volumes from structural MRI differentiates between clinical risk stages for mental illness in adolescents and young adults.
title: Aberrant limbic brain structures in young individuals at risk for mental illness.
study_design: retrospective cross-sectional case-control study with machine learning classification

patient_population: 99 children with pathology-confirmed posterior fossa tumors (medulloblastoma n=59, ependymoma n=13, pilocytic astrocytoma n=27)
clinical_problem: Differentiating types of pediatric posterior fossa brain tumors (medulloblastoma, ependymoma, pilocytic astrocytoma) using routine MRI
model_description: Wavelet-transformation texture features extracted from ADC MRI images of the whole tumor are fed into a random forest classifier to distinguish three types of pediatric posterior fossa brain tumors.
title: [Classification of the types of pediatric posterior fossa brain tumors based on routine MRI using wavelet transformation analysis of whole tumor].
headline_result: Random forest classifier accuracy 86.8% (validation); sensitivity 100%/94.8%/76.9%, specificity 97.6%/88.0%/98.8% across tumor pairs

patient_population: Data from the Successive Small-for-Gestational-Age-Births study
clinical_problem: Improving prediction of fetal macrosomia and large-for-gestational-age status from prenatal ultrasound biometric measurements.
model_description: Ensemble machine learning methods (voting and stacking) combine 26 empirical fetal weight estimation formulas and statistical models based on prenatal ultrasound measurements to improve prediction of macrosomia and large-for-gestational-age infants.
title: Ensemble Learning to Improve the Prediction of Fetal Macrosomia and Large-for-Gestational Age.
study_design: retrospective cohort study using ensemble learning methods

model_family: fuzzy c-means clustering over ten 3D parameters measured on biplanar radiograph reconstructions
patient_population: patients from a multicenter adolescent idiopathic scoliosis database, all with biplanar radiographs and 3D reconstruction of the entire spine; cluster sizes 11 to 290
clinical_problem: classifying adolescent idiopathic scoliosis in three dimensions, since the classifications surgeons plan from are two-dimensional and do not describe the deformity they are actually operating on
model_description: Unsupervised, and deliberately so - the point is to let the data propose subgroups rather than test an existing scheme. Eleven clusters emerged from ten 3D parameters, and the validation step is the one that matters for a taxonomy: four experienced spine surgeons from the SRS 3D Scoliosis Committee reviewed representative cases and unanimously agreed each cluster was a group current classifications do not name. Whether these subgroups predict surgical outcome is the unanswered question.
title: Towards a new 3D classification for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
headline_result: eleven statistically distinct 3D subgroups, all judged by four spine surgeons to be undefined in current classifications

patient_population: children undergoing MRI
clinical_problem: shortening pediatric MRI enough to reduce or avoid sedation and general anesthesia
model_description: A RadioGraphics review of the commercially available ways to shorten a pediatric MRI (parallel imaging, simultaneous multislice, radial sampling, compressed sensing, automated protocol selection) and the ones still under investigation, including AI-based reconstruction and prospective motion correction. It is the practical counterpart to the model papers: it says which of these a department can buy today.
release_evidence: the reviewed acceleration techniques are described as commercially available products in clinical use
journal: Radiographics : a review publication of the Radiological Society of North America, Inc
title: MRI Techniques to Decrease Imaging Times in Children.

model_family: machine learning classifiers on combined diffusion and perfusion features
patient_population: children with brain tumours imaged at multiple centres
clinical_problem: non-invasive diagnosis of the three common childhood brain tumour types, which is a genuine radiological challenge
model_description: Most quantitative work in this area is single-centre and single-modality; this combines diffusion and perfusion imaging across sites. It also takes features from the whole brain as well as the tumour, and finds both contribute, which is a useful observation for a field that segments the lesion and discards everything else.
title: Distinguishing between paediatric brain tumour types using multi-parametric magnetic resonance imaging and machine learning: A multi-site study.
dataset_size: a multi-centre paediatric brain tumour cohort
headline_result: combining diffusion and perfusion features from tumour and whole brain gave the optimal classifier at over 80% predictive precision

patient_population: 673 patients aged 0 to 116 months (mean 16.5 months) with 2,420 sagittal renal ultrasound images across all five Society for Fetal Urology grades
clinical_problem: grading hydronephrosis severity on renal ultrasound, currently a subjective five-point judgment
model_description: Assigns a Society for Fetal Urology grade to a renal ultrasound image. The reported numbers are refreshingly candid: it places 94% of images correctly or within one grade, but only 51% exactly right on the five-way task, and the clinically decisive distinctions (low versus high grade, and grade II versus III) reach 78% and 71%. The authors frame it as a decision and teaching aid rather than a grader.
title: Using Deep Learning Algorithms to Grade Hydronephrosis Severity: Toward a Clinical Adjunct.
headline_result: 94% of images correct or within one grade on the five-way task (51% exactly correct); 78% accuracy for low versus high grade and 71% for grade II versus III

patient_population: fetal echocardiography video dataset annotated by sonographers
clinical_problem: automated identification of anatomical structures in fetal echocardiography videos, with the ability to add new anatomical classes over time without retraining from scratch
model_description: Input: fetal echocardiography ultrasound video frames; output: classification of anatomical structures/views, using an incremental learning hierarchical network that can add new anatomy classes without forgetting prior ones.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: Hierarchical Class Incremental Learning of Anatomical Structures in Fetal Echocardiography Videos.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and internal validation
headline_result: reduced accuracy depreciation over old tasks from 6.75% to 1.10% (balanced) and 6.95% to 1.89% (imbalanced) with incremental learning

patient_population: premature neonates with post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus (sample size not stated)
clinical_problem: predicting whether post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus in premature neonates will require intervention, from cranial ultrasound
model_description: A deep-learning method (CNN incorporated into a probabilistic-atlas-based loss) segments lateral ventricles on cranial ultrasound to derive ventricular morphological phenotypes, which an SVM classifier then uses with clinical data to predict need for hydrocephalus intervention.
title: Ultrasound-Based Phenotyping of Lateral Ventricles to Predict Hydrocephalus Outcome in Premature Neonates.
headline_result: Segmentation Dice 0.86; outcome prediction accuracy 0.91

model_family: random forest classification + Gaussian mixture model (probabilistic point-cloud registration)
patient_population: 3D ultrasound fetal brain volumes (exact n not stated)
clinical_problem: Automatically registering 3D fetal brain ultrasound volumes affected by acoustic occlusion and noise, to monitor fetal brain growth and support brain-atlas-based segmentation
model_description: A supervised-learning-guided variant of the coherent point drift algorithm uses random-forest classification to weight a point cloud and assign Gaussian mixture model membership probabilities, enabling automatic registration of 3D fetal head ultrasound volumes despite occlusion artifacts and noise.
journal: Computational and mathematical methods in medicine
title: Probabilistic Learning Coherent Point Drift for 3D Ultrasound Fetal Head Registration.
headline_result: target registration error 6.38 ± 3.24 mm; error reduction of 7.4%-60.7% versus comparison algorithms

patient_population: 31 children, longitudinal design (baseline T1, follow-up T2 at 1.5 years)
clinical_problem: Predict current and future math calculation skills in children from fMRI activity during transitive-relation processing
model_description: Takes fMRI activity patterns during a transitive-relations task (intraparietal sulcus) as input to a machine learning model with cross-validation, predicting math calculation skill scores at baseline and 1.5 years later.
title: Neural representations of transitive relations predict current and future math calculation skills in children.
headline_result: IPS activity significantly predicted math calculation skills at both T1 and T2 (exact statistic not given)

model_family: machine learning clustering (unsupervised) on cognitive and cortical morphology data; network-attack simulation on DWI connectome
patient_population: 479 children (299 boys) aged 62-223 months (about 5-18 years), 337 referred for learning-related cognitive problems
clinical_problem: relating brain network organization to childhood learning difficulties and developmental disorders
model_description: Cognitive test scores and cortical morphology/diffusion-weighted connectome data go in; machine learning identifies distinct cognitive and brain profiles and simulates network resilience to loss of connectome hubs.
title: Transdiagnostic Brain Mapping in Developmental Disorders.
study_design: cross-sectional cohort study with machine-learning clustering and connectome simulation
headline_result: distinct cognitive/brain profiles significantly associated with children's learning ability and cognitive impairment (hold-out cross-validation)

patient_population: 95 children with ADHD and 105 healthy controls from the ADHD-200 database
clinical_problem: estimating inattention and impulsivity severity scores in ADHD from resting-state fMRI dynamic connectivity
model_description: Dynamic features of intrinsic connectivity networks from resting-state fMRI, together with head-motion and other measures, are input to support vector regression models. The models estimate individual clinical scores of inattention and impulsivity in children with and without ADHD, with the sensorimotor network most associated with inattention and the executive control network with impulsivity.
title: Estimating individual scores of inattention and impulsivity based on dynamic features of intrinsic connectivity network.
dataset_size: 95 children with ADHD, 105 healthy controls (ADHD-200 database)
headline_result: Estimated scores correlated significantly with inattention (r = 0.4 ± 0.02, p < 0.01) and impulsivity (r = 0.31 ± 0.02, p < 0.01)

model_family: deep convolutional neural network classifying diffusion MRI streamline trajectories, trained against electrical stimulation mapping findings
patient_population: 89 children with focal epilepsy, with electrical stimulation mapping as the reference
clinical_problem: identifying eloquent white matter before epilepsy surgery in children, so that resection margins spare motor, language and vision
model_description: The clinical validation goes well past accuracy. Three things are tested: whether the predicted pathways sit within the 1 cm spatial resolution of electrical stimulation mapping, whether respecting the predicted margins forecasts an absence of postoperative deficit (92% accurate), and whether the volume of language pathway actually removed tracks the postoperative change in language ability (R = 0.7). That last result is the one that turns a tract classifier into surgical evidence - it says the deficit follows the white matter you took, not only the cortex.
title: Novel Deep Learning Network Analysis of Electrical Stimulation Mapping-Driven Diffusion MRI Tractography to Improve Preoperative Evaluation of Pediatric Epilepsy.
study_design: retrospective model development with surgical outcome correlation
headline_result: 98% tract classification accuracy; preserved margins predicted absence of postoperative deficit with 92% accuracy; change in language pathway volume correlated with change in language ability (R = 0.7, p < 0.001)

model_family: convolutional network for spine segmentation on tracked ultrasound
patient_population: trained on eight healthy adult volunteers and tested on eight pediatric patients
clinical_problem: measuring scoliosis without radiographs, which children with scoliosis undergo repeatedly through growth
model_description: Segments the spine on tracked ultrasound and reconstructs a 3D volume from which the scoliosis angle is measured, offering a radiation-free substitute for the serial radiographs that scoliosis follow-up requires. The paper is honest about the adult-to-pediatric transfer: fuzzy segmentation metrics dropped when the network trained on adults was applied to children, and thresholds had to be re-optimized. Measurement error against radiography was nonetheless within 2.2 degrees.
title: Automatic Spine Ultrasound Segmentation for Scoliosis Visualization and Measurement.
dataset_size: eight adult volunteers for training, eight pediatric patients for testing
headline_result: maximum error 2.2 degrees against radiographic scoliosis measurement, with each measurement taking under one minute; segmentation metrics fell when translating from adults to children

model_family: U-Net segmentation with deep active learning, CNN feature extraction (transfer learning), and ensemble regression
patient_population: RSNA pediatric hand radiograph dataset
clinical_problem: automated bone age assessment for skeletal maturity in children
model_description: Takes a hand x-ray as input and outputs a predicted bone age, using a U-Net (trained via deep active learning) to segment the hand, pretrained CNNs to extract features via transfer learning, and ensemble regression models to predict age.
title: Fully Automated Bone Age Assessment on Large-Scale Hand X-Ray Dataset.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development on a public dataset
headline_result: mean discrepancy between predicted and actual bone age of 6.96 months (male) and 7.35 months (female); segmentation Dice score 0.95

model_family: machine learning and multiscale tumour growth simulation on an open cloud platform
patient_population: children with neuroblastoma or diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma across 16 European partner institutions
clinical_problem: phenotyping, treatment allocation and prognosis in neuroblastoma and diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma
model_description: Less a model than an attempt at the infrastructure pediatric AI lacks: a four-year European consortium with two imaging biobanks and three paediatric oncology units, building a cloud decision-support platform on pooled anonymised imaging, clinical, molecular and genetic data for two rare childhood cancers, with external validation at independent centres and results promised to the community. The choice of two rare tumors is deliberate, since these are exactly the diseases no single centre can study alone.
release_evidence: an open cloud-based platform, with final results promised to the scientific community
title: PRIMAGE project: predictive in silico multiscale analytics to support childhood cancer personalised evaluation empowered by imaging biomarkers.
study_design: multicentre observational in silico study protocol
dataset_size: multi-institutional European cohorts for two tumour types

model_family: convolutional neural network scoring the 13 RUS and 7 carpal bones of the Tanner-Whitehouse 3 system
patient_population: 9059 clinical left hand radiographs from PACS between January 2012 and December 2016, split 8005 training / 804 validation / 250 test; the test set was also read by four endocrinologists and two radiologists
clinical_problem: bone age assessment by the Tanner-Whitehouse 3 method, which is more granular than Greulich and Pyle but requires staging twenty individual bones and is correspondingly slow and variable
model_description: Automates the scoring system endocrinologists prefer but rarely use because of its cost in time, and reports agreement bone by bone rather than only in aggregate - which localizes where humans disagree with each other (capitate, hamate, middle and distal phalanges) and where they do not. Six expert readers as the comparator. One and a half seconds per image against many minutes by hand.
journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
title: Diagnostic performance of convolutional neural network-based Tanner-Whitehouse 3 bone age assessment system.
study_design: retrospective model development with multi-reader comparison
headline_result: root mean square 0.50 years against the reviewers' consensus, with accuracy better than the individual reviewers' estimates and image processing in 1.5 +/- 0.2 s

model_family: single-modality and dual-modality 3D convolutional networks retrained for neonatal data
patient_population: 24 pairs of neonatal T1 and T2 data from the Developing Human Connectome Project for retraining, with eight pairs for validation and eight for testing
clinical_problem: segmenting gray matter, white matter and cerebrospinal fluid in the term-equivalent neonatal brain, where the tissue contrast is inverted relative to the older infant brain that existing networks were tuned on
model_description: Takes two networks that won on 6-month infant data and asks whether they transfer to newborns, where the contrast is inverted - a concrete test of how narrow pediatric segmentation models are. Dual-modality HyperDense-Net won, and the ablation is practically useful: single-modality LiviaNET did better on T2 than T1 across every tissue type, which tells a site with only one sequence which to acquire. Training and inference times are reported, which papers rarely do and departments need. The models are being made available through the Canadian Neonatal Brain Platform.
release_evidence: the networks will be continuously retrained and made available through the Canadian Neonatal Brain Platform
title: Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks for Neonatal Brain Image Segmentation.
dataset_size: 40 neonatal T1/T2 pairs from the dHCP public dataset
headline_result: dual-modality HyperDense-Net reached Dice 0.94/0.95/0.92 for the three tissue types versus 0.90/0.90/0.88 for single-modality LiviaNET on T2

model_family: fully automated artificial intelligence system based on the Greulich and Pyle method, developed on Chinese children
patient_population: developed on 8000 bone age radiographs from five medical centres across China, then tested on 745 consecutive children (360 boys, 385 girls) with abnormal growth and development from another tertiary centre in north China between January and October 2018
clinical_problem: bone age assessment in the children it actually gets ordered for - those with abnormal growth and development - rather than in the developmentally normal children most systems are validated on
model_description: The test set is what makes this worth recording: consecutive children with abnormal growth and development, which is the referral population, evaluated at a centre separate from the five that supplied training data. Accuracy within one year was 84.6% overall, and the paper names exactly where it broke down - short stature with bone deformity, severe osteomalacia, and hands where carpals and phalanges mature at different rates. Those are precisely the children a bone age is ordered for.
title: Artificial intelligence system can achieve comparable results to experts for bone age assessment of Chinese children with abnormal growth and development.
dataset_size: 8000 development radiographs from five centres; 745 test cases from a sixth
headline_result: 84.60% accuracy within 1 year against a two-expert consensus reference (89.45% in the 12-18 year group), RMSE 0.76 years, mean absolute difference 0.58 years

model_family: patch-based convolutional neural network on fractional anisotropy maps
patient_population: 77 infants born under 31 weeks gestation, imaged at 29-35 weeks postmenstrual age with motor outcome at 2 years corrected age
clinical_problem: identifying preterm infants headed for neuromotor delay early enough to refer them for intervention
model_description: Predicts abnormal motor outcome at two years from diffusion MRI acquired before term, which is earlier than most preterm prediction work and therefore closer to when intervention could start. Classification is done on image patches and aggregated with a tuned threshold, and heat maps show which brain locations drove the abnormal predictions. Accuracy is moderate and the confidence intervals are wide on 77 infants.
title: Predicting motor outcome in preterm infants from very early brain diffusion MRI using a deep learning convolutional neural network (CNN) model.
dataset_size: 77 very preterm infants (48 normal, 29 abnormal outcome)
headline_result: sensitivity 70%, specificity 74%, AUC 0.72 for abnormal motor outcome at 2 years from MRI acquired at 29-35 weeks postmenstrual age

model_family: multivariate logistic models with leave-one-out cross-validation and exhaustive feature selection over diffusion tensor metrics
patient_population: 102 very-low-birth-weight neonates (birthweight <= 1500 g, gestational age <= 32 weeks) recruited 2010-2011, of whom 92 returned for Bayley-III assessment at 18-22 months adjusted age
clinical_problem: identifying which very-low-birth-weight preterm infants are heading for language delay, early enough to intervene while neuroplasticity is greatest
model_description: Near-term diffusion imaging used as a prognostic instrument rather than a descriptive one. Exhaustive feature selection narrows to three brain regions, which keeps the model small enough to interpret and to replicate. Separate models for composite, expressive and receptive language, with the strongest performance on expressive and receptive - and a side finding that cerebellar asymmetry tracked lower receptive scores. Nearly a third of the cohort scored below 85, so the outcome is common enough for the prediction to matter.
title: Neonatal Brain Microstructure and Machine-Learning-Based Prediction of Early Language Development in Children Born Very Preterm.
headline_result: sensitivity and specificity of 89%/86% for composite, 100%/90% for expressive and 100%/90% for receptive language risk

patient_population: 71 singleton and monochorionic twin pregnancies
clinical_problem: Segment the intrauterine cavity from fetal MRI to plan fetoscopic laser surgery for twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome
model_description: Takes axial, sagittal, and coronal fetal MRI stacks as input; a reinforcement-learning-based capsule network (with nnU-Net feature extraction) detects and segments the intrauterine cavity/womb for surgical planning.
title: Deep Q-CapsNet Reinforcement Learning Framework for Intrauterine Cavity Segmentation in TTTS Fetal Surgery Planning.
study_design: retrospective segmentation model development, compared with 15 state-of-the-art networks
headline_result: Average Dice score above 0.91 across all ablations

model_family: segmentation network followed by geometric calculation
patient_population: 179 children aged 5-19 (mean 12 years) imaged for leg length discrepancy
clinical_problem: measuring leg length discrepancy, a task the paper describes as time consuming but cognitively simple
model_description: Segments the femurs and tibias on a full-length radiograph and computes each bone's length and the discrepancy between sides. The case it makes is not diagnostic accuracy but time: agreement with the radiology report was essentially perfect and the measurement took one second against 96 seconds by hand. This is the shape of the pediatric AI application most likely to pay for itself, an exact, repetitive measurement rather than a judgment call.
title: Deep Learning Measurement of Leg Length Discrepancy in Children Based on Radiographs.
headline_result: correlation 0.99 with radiologist measurements (mean absolute error 0.45 cm for individual bones, 0.51 cm for discrepancy); 1 second versus 96 seconds per study

model_family: radiomics with Kruskal-Wallis feature selection and a support vector machine
patient_population: 135 MRI slices from children with posterior fossa tumors, split into training and validation sets
clinical_problem: telling ependymoma from pilocytic astrocytoma before surgery, two posterior fossa tumors with different management that overlap on conventional MRI
model_description: A conventional radiomics pipeline whose most useful output is the feature ablation: Gabor, texture and wavelet features were compared head to head, and texture features alone matched the full 300-feature set. Small and slice-level rather than patient-level, so the headline accuracy should be read as a feasibility signal rather than a performance estimate.
journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
title: Ependymoma and pilocytic astrocytoma: Differentiation using radiomics approach based on machine learning.
headline_result: accuracy 0.878, sensitivity 0.929, specificity 0.800, AUC 0.865 on the selected feature set, with no significant loss versus the full feature set

patient_population: 796 frontal radiographs of adolescents (84 brace, 325 implant, 387 no treatment), augmented to 2096 images
clinical_problem: automatically detecting scoliosis treatment (brace or implant) present on frontal radiographs
model_description: A CNN followed by discriminant analysis takes postero-anterior spine radiographs as input and outputs a probability of the image containing a brace, spinal implant, or no treatment.
journal: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
title: A convolutional neural network to detect scoliosis treatment in radiographs.
study_design: retrospective model-development study with stratified 10-fold cross-validation
headline_result: 98.3% of radiographs correctly classified (2.0% unclassified); 99.7% of brace radiographs correctly detected

model_family: nonlocal residual neural network + random forest
patient_population: Pediatric T1- and T2-weighted MRI scans
clinical_problem: Automatically flagging poor-quality pediatric MRI slices/volumes in real time to reduce the need for repeat scans
model_description: A nonlocal residual neural network (NR-Net) rates each MRI slice as pass/questionable/fail, refined by semi-supervised learning and iterative self-training; a random forest agglomerates slice ratings into a volume-level quality score
journal: IEEE transactions on image processing : a publication of the IEEE Signal Processing Society
title: Real-Time Quality Assessment of Pediatric MRI via Semi-Supervised Deep Nonlocal Residual Neural Networks.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and validation study
dataset_size: small quality-annotated training set (exact n not stated)
headline_result: Near-perfect accuracy with real-time (millisecond-per-volume) quality assessment

model_family: deep CNN, pretrained on natural images and on adult radiographs
patient_population: adult cohorts for pretraining, then fine-tuned on pediatric patients for the pneumonia task
clinical_problem: flagging abnormal chest radiographs for worklist triage, and pneumonia in children specifically
model_description: Sorts frontal chest radiographs into normal and abnormal so that abnormal studies can be pushed up the worklist. The pediatric relevance is in the transfer step: a model pretrained on adult cohorts and fine-tuned on children reached higher performance for pneumonia than either alone, which is the practical recipe for a children's hospital with a smaller archive.
title: Automated abnormality classification of chest radiographs using deep convolutional neural networks.
dataset_size: about 8,500 images for the pretraining benefit analysis; cohort sizes not stated
headline_result: AUC 0.982 for normal versus abnormal, 0.944 on an external dataset, and 0.985 for normal versus pneumonia after fine-tuning on children

model_family: multi-instance deep learning with mean pooling across multiple images per patient in both sagittal and transverse views
patient_population: 86 children with posterior urethral valves and 71 with mild unilateral hydronephrosis, 3504 sagittal and 2558 transverse images from routine clinical care
clinical_problem: distinguishing posterior urethral valves - which need urgent intervention - from mild unilateral hydronephrosis in children, from the routine ultrasound
model_description: Multi-instance learning is the right match for how renal ultrasound is actually acquired - many images per child, no single one definitive - and the paper quantifies exactly what that buys: pooling lifted the AUC from about 0.80 on single images to 0.96. Combining both planes added a little more. Class activation mapping showed the network attending to anatomically meaningful parts of the kidney, and sensitivity (0.873) trails specificity (0.986), which is the wrong way round for a condition where a miss means renal damage.
title: Multi-instance Deep Learning of Ultrasound Imaging Data for Pattern Classification of Congenital Abnormalities of the Kidney and Urinary Tract in Children.
headline_result: AUC 0.961 +/- 0.026 combining views with mean pooling, versus 0.796 and 0.815 for single sagittal and transverse images; specificity 0.986 and sensitivity 0.873

patient_population: pregnant patients undergoing fetal MRI
clinical_problem: segmenting the uterine cavity and placenta on fetal MRI to help detect abnormalities affecting maternal and fetal health
model_description: 3D fetal MRI, with minimal operator interaction to localize the placenta, is segmented by a fully convolutional neural network into uterine cavity and placenta regions, from which organ volumes are estimated.
journal: Proceedings of SPIE--the International Society for Optical Engineering
title: Segmentation of uterus and placenta in MR images using a fully convolutional neural network.
study_design: retrospective single-center technical development and evaluation study
headline_result: average Dice coefficient 92% (uterine cavity) and 82% (placenta); volume estimation error 2% and 9% respectively

model_family: deep convolutional networks: segmentation of the craniocerebral region, then four-class classification, then class activation mapping for localization
patient_population: real-world clinical fetal brain ultrasound images at the transventricular and transcerebellar standard planes
clinical_problem: prenatal detection of five common fetal brain abnormalities on standard neurosonographic planes, where missed malformations change counseling and management
model_description: A three-stage design that gets weakly-supervised localization for free: the classifier is trained only on image-level labels, and lesions are then localized by class activation mapping rather than by any drawn box. That keeps the annotation burden low, and the numbers show the cost - classification is strong while localization overlap is modest. Positioned as support for junior operators, whose false negatives on fetal brain anomalies are the stated target.
journal: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
title: Computer-aided diagnosis for fetal brain ultrasound images using deep convolutional neural networks.
headline_result: Dice 0.942 for craniocerebral segmentation, average F1 0.96 for classification, average mean IOU 0.497 for lesion localization

patient_population: Fetal ultrasound scans with sonographer eye-gaze tracking
clinical_problem: Automatically discovering anatomical landmarks that sonographers visually attend to during fetal neurosonography, to support image registration
model_description: A CNN is trained to predict sonographer gaze-point (saliency) maps from fetal ultrasound video frames; local maxima of the predicted saliency maps become candidate anatomical landmarks, matched across images via CNN feature clustering
journal: Proceedings. IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging
title: Discovering Salient Anatomical Landmarks by Predicting Human Gaze.
dataset_size: not stated exactly (full-length clinical fetal ultrasound scans)
headline_result: Landmark alignment errors of 4.1%-10.9% of fetal head long-axis length when used for affine registration

model_family: self-supervised network trained to reorder a reshuffled video clip and predict the geometric transformation applied to it
patient_population: unlabelled fetal ultrasound video
clinical_problem: the annotation bottleneck in fetal ultrasound analysis, where expert labels are expensive and scarce and most methods cannot be trained without them
model_description: A pretraining recipe rather than a clinical model, and the pretext tasks are chosen with anatomy in mind: to put a shuffled clip back in order, the network has to know what the sweep is passing over, and to name the geometric transform it has to know the anatomy's orientation. No human annotation is used at any point. Representations transferred to standard plane detection and saliency prediction, which is the argument that what was learned is anatomical rather than incidental.
journal: Proceedings. IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging
title: Self-Supervised Representation Learning for Ultrasound Video.
headline_result: meaningful transferable representations learned without any human annotation, transferring well to standard plane detection and saliency prediction

model_family: deep convolutional encoder-decoders with encoders pre-trained on ImageNet
patient_population: 24 shoulder examinations in children with unilateral obstetrical brachial plexus palsy, evaluated leave-one-out
clinical_problem: segmenting the four rotator cuff muscles on MRI in children with obstetrical brachial plexus palsy, so that muscle volume - and from it force - can be estimated without hours of manual tracing
model_description: A study framed around the two constraints that define pediatric musculoskeletal AI: very little annotated data, and pathological anatomy that looks nothing like the healthy training examples. It answers the transferability question directly by comparing learning schemes, and the winner combines healthy and pathological annotated data with ImageNet pre-training rather than choosing between them. Supraspinatus, the smallest and most atrophied muscle, is where it degrades.
journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
title: Healthy versus pathological learning transferability in shoulder muscle MRI segmentation using deep convolutional encoder-decoders.
headline_result: Dice 82.4% deltoid, 82.0% infraspinatus, 71.0% supraspinatus and 82.8% subscapularis, with surface estimation errors below 83 mm2 except supraspinatus at 134.6 mm2

patient_population: patients under age 16 with CNO treated with pamidronate at a tertiary pediatric hospital
clinical_problem: assessing treatment response on whole-body MRI in chronic nonbacterial osteomyelitis (CNO)
model_description: Pre- and post-pamidronate whole-body MRI segments of the distal femur and proximal tibia are compared by a machine learning algorithm that classifies treatment response (improved, worsened, stable), benchmarked against a panel of pediatric radiologists as ground truth.
title: Artificial intelligence for interpretation of segments of whole body MRI in CNO: pilot study comparing radiologists versus machine learning algorithm.
study_design: retrospective single-center pilot diagnostic accuracy study
headline_result: sensitivity 100% for detecting disease improvement/worsening, but only 33.3% of samples classified correctly overall vs. radiologist ground truth

model_family: CNN with convolutional gated recurrent unit (C-GRU) and a periodicity-aware loss function
patient_population: 25 real ultrasound sequences from third-trimester pregnancy checks, plus 1,000 synthetic sequences
clinical_problem: real-time measurement of fetal aortic vascular diameter from ultrasound
model_description: A neural network combining CNN feature extraction, a convolutional GRU temporal module, and a periodicity-aware loss (CyclicLoss) measures the fetal abdominal aorta diameter in real time from ultrasound video.
title: Real-time diameter of the fetal aorta from ultrasound.
dataset_size: 25 real ultrasound sequences plus 1,000 synthetic sequences
headline_result: MSE 0.09 mm^2 (vs. 0.31 state-of-the-art); relative error 5.3% (vs. 8.1%); 289 frames/sec

model_family: neural network classifier over cortical surface features from structural MRI
patient_population: three cohorts: 34 patients with visible focal cortical dysplasia for training and cross-validation, 20 pediatric healthy controls for specificity, and 34 sEEG patients for the implantation feasibility analysis
clinical_problem: planning stereoelectroencephalography electrode placement in children with drug-resistant epilepsy whose MRI is diagnostically complex, where getting the electrodes to the seizure onset zone is the whole point of the procedure
model_description: Rather than reporting lesion-detection accuracy, the study asks whether the detected lesions land where the seizures actually start, by coregistering electrode contacts with the classifier's predictions and letting clinical neurophysiologists define the onset contacts. Specificity in controls was 100%, which matters more than sensitivity for a tool that would add electrodes. The striking cases are the three patients where sEEG localized nothing and the classifier flagged abnormalities that had not been implanted.
title: Planning stereoelectroencephalography using automated lesion detection: Retrospective feasibility study.
dataset_size: 34 focal cortical dysplasia patients, 20 controls, 34 sEEG patients
headline_result: 74% sensitivity in patients with radiologically defined lesions and 100% specificity in controls; 86% of histopathologically confirmed focal cortical dysplasias detected, with 62% colocalization between classifier output and seizure onset zone contacts

model_family: two-stage system: a detector network localizing ossification areas, then sex- and region-specific regression networks estimating age from each area
patient_population: pediatric hand radiographs, evaluated on the RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Challenge test set
clinical_problem: bone age estimation from the left hand radiograph, which pediatric endocrinologists order routinely and which requires substantial expertise to read
model_description: Deliberately reproduces the Tanner-Whitehouse workflow - find each ossification area, score it, combine - rather than regressing an age from the whole image, and the payoff is interpretability: a radiologist can see which areas drove the estimate and disagree with one of them. The authors make the case explicitly against purely encoder-based architectures, which give a number and no account of it. Competitive on the RSNA challenge test set while remaining explainable, and the detector trains from a small annotated set.
title: Mimicking the radiologists' workflow: Estimating pediatric hand bone age with stacked deep neural networks.
study_design: retrospective model development on a public benchmark
dataset_size: RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Challenge data
headline_result: average error 4.56 months on the RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Challenge test set, with self-explanatory per-area results

patient_population: 131 pediatric neuro-oncology patients (training), 11 healthy adult subjects (evaluation)
clinical_problem: Denoising and suppressing artifacts in arterial spin labeling MRI to improve cerebral blood flow measurement with fewer repetitions.

journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
title: Combined Denoising and Suppression of Transient Artifacts in Arterial Spin Labeling MRI Using Deep Learning.

title: A preliminary study to quantitatively evaluate the development of maturation degree for fetal lung based on transfer learning deep model from ultrasound images.

release_evidence: the dataset is stated to be made publicly available; nothing is said about the models

title: Achieving accurate estimates of fetal gestational age and personalised predictions of fetal growth based on data from an international prospective cohort study: a population-based machine learning study.

title: Deep white matter analysis (DeepWMA): Fast and consistent tractography segmentation.
