model_family: multi-task network with a feature extractor, a bidirectional convolutional LSTM temporal attention module and an auxiliary video classification module, trained with a soft dynamic time warping loss
patient_population: 280 video clips of 3-7 seconds each, one per biometry plane, with simultaneously recorded gaze tracking from an experienced sonographer

Adding time to a previously spatial-only model improved every saliency metric, which says the navigation is a trajectory and not a series of independent glances.
title: Spatio-temporal visual attention modelling of standard biometry plane-finding navigation.
headline_result: best model outperforms the previous spatial model on all static and dynamic saliency metrics, with standard plane detection F1 of 83.7% (abdomen), 89.9% (head) and 81.1% (femur)

The absolute IoU near 0.5 shows how hard this structure is; the contribution is the transferable idea rather than the number.
title: Model-Agnostic Method for Thoracic Wall Segmentation in Fetal Ultrasound Videos.
headline_result: mean IoU rose from 0.448 to 0.493 for U-net and 0.417 to 0.470 for DeepLabv3+ without changing the network structure

model_family: convolutional neural network trained to predict chronological age directly, compared against a Greulich and Pyle-trained deep learning model

clinical_problem: predicting fetal brain age from MRI for developmental analysis and early diagnosis of congenital anomalies, when the fetal brain sits at an arbitrary position and orientation among surrounding organs

And label distribution learning treats the age label as a distribution rather than a point, which both reflects the real uncertainty of gestational dating and helps with a 289-subject sample. Multiple views are aggregated across branches rather than one stack being chosen.
journal: 2020 IEEE 17th International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI)
title: Multi-Branch Deformable Convolutional Neural Network with Label Distribution Learning for Fetal Brain Age Prediction
headline_result: promising fetal brain age prediction on a 289-subject fetal MRI dataset using deformable convolutions, label distribution learning and multi-view aggregation

model_description: Sits between the two families that had failed here and fixes the specific failure of each: regression methods lose landmark ordering and need dense mapping parameters, while segmentation methods produce connected or corrupted vertebra masks. Anchoring on the vertebra center and tracing corners by learned offsets keeps the landmarks ordered by construction, which is what the Cobb angle calculation requires. Code released.
release_evidence: code is available at https://github.com/yijingru/Vertebra-Landmark-Detection
journal: 2020 IEEE 17th International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI)
title: Vertebra-Focused Landmark Detection for Scoliosis Assessment
headline_result: improved Cobb angle measurement and landmark detection on low-contrast and ambiguous X-ray images compared with regression- and segmentation-based methods

clinical_problem: fetal brain segmentation from stacks of motion-corrupted slices still needs human refinement on the difficult slices, and finding which slices those are is itself work
model_description: Accepts that the network will not be good enough on every slice and optimizes the human's time instead - uncertainty computed in a single forward pass points the user at the slices worth correcting, and an interactive level set turns each correction into a refined result. That is a more honest deployment model for fetal MRI than full automation, and it is measured as such: about 30% better efficiency, with the uncertainty shown to correlate with actual mis-segmentation. Code released.
release_evidence: code available at https://github.com/HiLab-git/UGIR
title: Uncertainty-Guided Efficient Interactive Refinement of Fetal Brain Segmentation from Stacks of MRI Slices
headline_result: real-time uncertainty estimation correlating with mis-segmentation, and accurate refinement with about 30% improvement in efficiency by guiding where the user interacts

model_family: VGG16 with a customized multilayer perceptron head, in four training strategies including an ensemble of two preprocessing pipelines
patient_population: chest radiographs from pediatric patients in a public pneumonia dataset
clinical_problem: detecting pneumonia and distinguishing bacterial from viral subforms on children's chest radiographs, particularly when the images are low contrast
model_description: The variable under study is preprocessing rather than architecture, which is the more useful question on a saturated benchmark: cropping to the chest cavity and histogram equalization of the segmented lung each beat the raw image, and ensembling the two beat either. Both the detection task and the harder bacterial-versus-viral call are reported with confidence intervals, and the gap between them (0.97 versus 0.91) is the honest measure of where the difficulty lies.
journal: 2020 42nd Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine & Biology Society (EMBC)
title: Multi-View Ensemble Convolutional Neural Network to Improve Classification of Pneumonia in Low Contrast Chest X-Ray Images
dataset_size: a public pediatric pneumonia chest radiograph dataset
headline_result: ensemble AUC 0.97 (CI 0.96-0.99) for pneumonia versus normal and 0.91 (CI 0.88-0.94) for bacterial versus viral, with every preprocessed variant beating the raw-image baseline

model_family: three CNN architectures (Inception_v3, Inception_v4, Inception_resnet_v2) applied by transfer learning to connectivity matrices from HARDI and NODDI
patient_population: 30 participants: 15 with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy and 15 normal controls
clinical_problem: early detection of juvenile myoclonic epilepsy, which begins in adolescence and where advanced diffusion imaging could serve as a non-invasive biomarker of the subtle white matter change involved
model_description: Uses two advanced diffusion models - high angular resolution imaging and neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging - to build connectivity matrices, then reads them as images with pretrained networks, which is how thirty participants can support a deep model at all. The architecture comparison is the paper's own finding, with residual connections helping. Fifteen patients per group means the 75.2% accuracy is a first indication rather than a result.
journal: 2020 42nd Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine & Biology Society (EMBC)
title: Automated Detection of Juvenile Myoclonic Epilepsy using CNN based Transfer Learning in Diffusion MRI
headline_result: Inception_resnet_v2 detected juvenile myoclonic epilepsy with accuracy 75.2% and AUC 0.839, outperforming Inception_v3 and Inception_v4

model_family: over-complete Ki-Net branch, which projects data onto higher spatial dimensions, augmenting a standard U-Net
patient_population: 2D cranial ultrasound of preterm neonates
clinical_problem: segmenting brain anatomy on 2D ultrasound of preterm neonates, where the structures are small and the boundaries blurred and noisy
model_description: Starts from a diagnosis of where U-Net fails - small structures with blurred noisy boundaries, which is a fair description of neonatal cranial ultrasound - and answers it by adding a branch that projects to higher rather than lower spatial resolution, so fine detail is not discarded in the encoder. Preterm neonatal brain ultrasound is the chosen evaluation task, which makes this one of the few widely cited architecture papers whose benchmark is a pediatric problem. Fewer parameters and faster convergence than the baseline, with code released.
release_evidence: code at https://github.com/jeya-maria-jose/KiU-Net-pytorch
title: KiU-Net: Towards Accurate Segmentation of Biomedical Images Using Over-Complete Representations
headline_result: about 4% improvement in Dice and Jaccard over standard U-Net and 2% over the previous best methods for preterm neonatal brain ultrasound segmentation

model_family: semi-supervised mean teacher model with an additional region-of-interest consistency loss focusing the network on the brain
patient_population: a fetal brain MR dataset with 11 223 labeled and more than 200 000 unlabeled images
clinical_problem: detecting motion-degraded slices during a fetal brain MRI acquisition, so that they can be reacquired rather than discovered as unusable afterwards - and doing it without the time-consuming manual quality annotation such a model normally needs
model_description: The unlabeled-to-labeled ratio is close to twenty to one, which is exactly the shape of real scanner archives, and the ROI consistency term stops the semi-supervised signal from being dominated by the maternal anatomy filling most of the frame. Crucially the authors did not stop at an offline result: the model was implemented on an MR scanner, demonstrating online quality assessment and reacquisition during the scan, which is where a quality model has to live to be useful.
title: Semi-supervised Learning for Fetal Brain MRI Quality Assessment with ROI Consistency
headline_result: about 6% accuracy improvement over supervised learning and better than other semi-supervised methods, with feasibility demonstrated for online quality assessment and reacquisition on an MR scanner

model_family: cross-modal contrastive learning between ultrasound video and sonographer speech, with an affinity-aware self-paced learning scheme
patient_population: multi-modal fetal ultrasound video with the sonographer's narrative speech audio
clinical_problem: learning useful representations from fetal ultrasound without manual annotation, which is expensive and sometimes simply unavailable
model_description: Uses a supervision signal that already exists and is normally discarded: the sonographer talks while scanning, and what they say correlates with what is on screen. Learning that correspondence forces the model to recognize anatomy without a single label. A genuinely clever fit to obstetric ultrasound specifically, where narration is routine. Representations transferred to standard plane detection and eye-gaze prediction.
title: Self-Supervised Contrastive Video-Speech Representation Learning for Ultrasound
headline_result: strong representations learned from paired fetal ultrasound video and sonographer speech without any human annotation, transferring well to standard plane detection and eye-gaze prediction

model_family: reinforcement learning agents trained to summarize video by preserving diagnostically important information
patient_population: fetal ultrasound screening videos
clinical_problem: raw diagnostic video is slow to process, annotate or audit, so most of what is recorded during fetal ultrasound screening is never used
model_description: Aims at an unglamorous but real problem - a screening scan records minutes of video of which seconds are used, and nobody can review the rest. Framing summarization as reinforcement learning lets the reward encode preservation of diagnostic content rather than visual diversity, which is what distinguishes a medical summary from a consumer one. Evaluated against clinical diagnostic standards rather than only against other summarizers.
title: Ultrasound Video Summarization Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
headline_result: superior to alternative video summarization methods while preserving the information required by clinical diagnostic standards on fetal ultrasound screening video

model_family: U-Net with dilated convolution layers after the last encoder and squeeze-and-excitation blocks on the skip connections
patient_population: the HC18 grand challenge dataset of 2D ultrasound images across trimesters
clinical_problem: measuring fetal head circumference across all trimesters, which estimates gestational age, monitors growth and informs prediction of the newborn's state
model_description: An incremental but well-targeted modification of U-Net: dilation widens the receptive field at the bottleneck to see the whole skull, and squeeze-and-excitation on the skip connections reweights which encoder features reach the decoder. Segmenting the skull boundary as well as the skull suits an ellipse measurement. Evaluated on the public HC18 benchmark, so the 2.27 mm head circumference error is comparable across the literature.
journal: 2020 IEEE Conference on Computational Intelligence in Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (CIBCB)
title: Dilated Squeeze-and-Excitation U-Net for Fetal Ultrasound Image Segmentation
headline_result: mean absolute difference 2.27 +/- 3.61 mm in head circumference and mean Dice 97.31 +/- 1.84% for fetal skull segmentation

model_family: multi-task machine learning framework with feature selection on neuroimaging measurements
patient_population: in-house longitudinal infant cohort with neuroimaging from as early as 24 months, cognitive scores measured at age 4
clinical_problem: predicting future cognitive developmental scores in infants from earlier structural brain MRI, with incomplete longitudinal data
model_description: Input is longitudinal structural MRI morphometric measurements from infancy (with missing time points handled by the framework); output is a multi-task machine learning prediction of multiple future cognitive scores at age 4.
title: Multi-task prediction of infant cognitive scores from longitudinal incomplete neuroimaging data.
study_design: prospective longitudinal cohort study with multi-task machine learning
headline_result: root mean square error 0.18 for predicting cognitive scores at age 4 using imaging data from as early as 24 months

patient_population: 1,581 cannabis-naive adolescents aged 14 from the IMAGEN study; outcome group n=365 by age 16
clinical_problem: predicting adolescent risk of future cannabis use initiation from psychosocial, brain and genetic features
model_description: Inputs are psychosocial questionnaire measures, structural brain MRI features and genetic variants measured at age 14; output is a regularized logistic regression prediction of cannabis use initiation by age 16, with sex-specific brain predictors identified.
title: The initiation of cannabis use in adolescence is predicted by sex-specific psychosocial and neurobiological features.

model_family: automatic tissue segmentation with a linear discriminant analysis classifier
patient_population: 84 infants born between 26 and 36 weeks gestation, imaged shortly after birth and again at term-equivalent age, with outcomes at 18-24 months and 5 years
clinical_problem: predicting neurodevelopmental outcome after preterm birth from brain growth in the neonatal period
model_description: Automatically segments serial neonatal T2-weighted MRI into cortical gray matter, unmyelinated white matter, subcortical gray matter, cerebellum and CSF, then asks which volumes and growth rates predict motor and cognitive outcome later. Volumes at birth and term-equivalent age predicted motor outcome at 18-24 months, while volumes and growth rates predicted cognition at 5 years. The sobering finding is that family socioeconomic status was more strongly associated with cognitive outcome than any brain volume.
title: Longitudinal study of neonatal brain tissue volumes in preterm infants and their ability to predict neurodevelopmental outcome.
headline_result: brain tissue volumes contributed to prediction of motor outcome at 18-24 months and cognitive scores at 5 years; socioeconomic status was strongly associated with cognitive outcome while brain volumes were not

model_family: two-stage CNN with geodesic distance transforms and a back-propagatable CRF
patient_population: fetal MRI studies; brain tumor FLAIR MRI is the second test case
clinical_problem: producing clinically usable placental contours on fetal MRI without lengthy manual editing
model_description: One network produces an automatic segmentation, the operator marks where it is wrong, and a second network takes those marks and returns a corrected contour. User clicks are turned into geodesic distance maps and enforced as hard constraints, so a few interactions go a long way. Demonstrated on 2D placenta segmentation from fetal MRI and 3D brain tumor segmentation.
journal: IEEE transactions on pattern analysis and machine intelligence
title: DeepIGeoS: A Deep Interactive Geodesic Framework for Medical Image Segmentation.
headline_result: large improvement over the automatic CNN, with comparable or better accuracy than traditional interactive methods at fewer interventions and less time

model_family: least-squares GAN with a deep residual generator
patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing contrast-enhanced abdominal MRI
clinical_problem: shortening contrast-enhanced MRI in children by reconstructing undersampled data
model_description: Takes an aliased image from undersampled k-space and returns a diagnostic-quality reconstruction in milliseconds. A generative adversarial network learns what real high-quality MR images look like, so the output keeps fine texture instead of the waxy appearance that pixel-wise losses produce. Trained and evaluated on a large contrast-enhanced pediatric MRI dataset with expert radiologist ratings.
title: Deep Generative Adversarial Neural Networks for Compressive Sensing MRI.
dataset_size: a large contrast-enhanced pediatric MR dataset; size not stated
headline_result: expert radiologists rated it higher in fine texture detail than wavelet, dictionary-learning and pixel-wise deep learning reconstructions, at two orders of magnitude faster reconstruction

model_family: 3D fully convolutional network with a multi-directional recurrent refinement network
patient_population: pregnant women undergoing volumetric prenatal ultrasound
clinical_problem: getting reliable biometry out of 3D prenatal ultrasound, which is hard to interpret and therefore little used
model_description: Segments the fetus, gestational sac and placenta simultaneously in a 3D ultrasound volume. A convolutional network makes the initial dense labeling and a recurrent network sweeping in several directions fixes the boundaries, which is where ultrasound segmentation usually fails because contrast is poor and edges are ambiguous. The measurements agreed with experts and were reproducible across scanning variation.
title: Towards Automated Semantic Segmentation in Prenatal Volumetric Ultrasound.
dataset_size: large in-house datasets; sizes not stated
headline_result: superior segmentation performance with decent agreement with expert measurements and high reproducibility against scanning variation

patient_population: 280 age- and sex-matched bone age radiographs from children aged 5 to 18
clinical_problem: whether AI assistance makes pediatric radiologists better at bone age, not whether AI alone beats them
model_description: The model itself is a bone age network the group had already published; the contribution here is the comparison design. Six subspecialty pediatric radiologists read the same 280 cases, then three read them again with the model's estimate in front of them. Every reader improved, and inter-reader variability fell. The conclusion — AI plus radiologist beats either alone — is the argument for deploying these tools as an adjunct rather than a replacement.
title: Artificial intelligence-assisted interpretation of bone age radiographs improves accuracy and decreases variability.
headline_result: AI alone 68.2% accurate versus 63.6% for the six-reader mean; pooled root mean squared error fell from 0.661 to 0.508 years with AI assistance, and every individual reader improved

model_family: regression CNN predicting angle-axis rotation and translation, trained with geodesic loss
patient_population: fetuses scanned in utero across a wide gestational age range, with generalization tested on newborns
clinical_problem: aligning fetal brain images acquired in arbitrary orientations to a standard atlas, the step that motion-robust reconstruction depends on
model_description: Predicts where an arbitrarily oriented fetal brain sits in a canonical space directly from the image, in under 100 milliseconds, replacing an iterative optimization that has a narrow capture range. Trained on T2-weighted fetal scans, it generalized to T1-weighted newborn scans once image contrast was transferred with a conditional GAN, which is a useful demonstration that a model can be moved across contrasts without retraining from scratch.
title: Real-Time Deep Pose Estimation With Geodesic Loss for Image-to-Template Rigid Registration.
headline_result: 3D pose estimation with a wide capture range in under 100 ms, generalizing to newborn scans of a different contrast

patient_population: 60 male patients with conduct disorder and 60 male healthy controls, mean age ~15.3-15.5 years
clinical_problem: Can structural brain MRI patterns distinguish children/adolescents with conduct disorder from healthy controls, as a potential imaging biomarker?
model_description: A support vector machine with searchlight multivoxel pattern analysis classifies gray-matter spatial patterns on structural MRI to distinguish conduct disorder from healthy controls.
title: Multivoxel pattern analysis of structural MRI in children and adolescents with conduct disorder.
headline_result: Classification accuracy up to 83% using grey matter patterns in identified regions

model_family: kernel regression in age with diffeomorphic tensor-to-tensor registration
patient_population: 67 healthy fetuses scanned once each between 21 and 39 weeks gestational age
clinical_problem: having a normative reference for fetal white matter development against which an individual fetus can be compared
model_description: Not a diagnostic model but the normative resource one needs before building any: the first diffusion tensor atlas of the fetal brain built from in utero images, computed by regressing motion-corrected individual tensors against gestational age. It makes group studies and computer-aided diagnosis from fetal diffusion imaging possible, which the authors note had not previously been feasible because individual in utero reconstructions are too noisy.
title: Fetal brain growth portrayed by a spatiotemporal diffusion tensor MRI atlas computed from in utero images.
headline_result: the atlas reproduced the known sequence of limbic, projection and association fiber development between 21 and 39 weeks

patient_population: adolescents through older adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes/obesity; single-center Tellus cohort (90 scans) and multicenter BetaJudo cohort including juvenile diabetes/obesity (20 scans)
clinical_problem: automated segmentation and quantification of visceral and subcutaneous fat
model_description: Multicenter water-fat MRI scans of the abdomen go in; a U-Net or V-Net fully convolutional network outputs segmentations of visceral and subcutaneous adipose tissue for volume quantification.
title: Fully convolutional networks for automated segmentation of abdominal adipose tissue depots in multicenter water-fat MRI.
study_design: retrospective multicenter method-development and validation study
dataset_size: 90 scans (Tellus, cross-validation) plus 20 scans (BetaJudo, external test)
headline_result: U-Net Dice 0.988 (VAT)/0.992 (SAT) internal; 0.970 (VAT)/0.987 (SAT) on external multicenter test data

model_family: artificial neural network over body height and weight, MRI-quantified bone marrow composition intensity and Tanner-Whitehouse 3 skeletal age
patient_population: 79 healthy Hong Kong Chinese adolescents aged 12-17 years scanned on a dedicated skeletal MRI scanner
clinical_problem: assessing chronological age in adolescents without ionizing radiation, and testing whether the Tanner-Whitehouse 3 method transfers to MRI
model_description: Notable for a negative result that motivates the positive one: Tanner-Whitehouse 3 read from MRI systematically underestimated age, significantly so in girls and in older adolescents - the very cases where age assessment is contested. Feeding MRI-quantified bone marrow composition alongside the staging into a neural network removed that bias, and was about ten times more accurate than the staging alone. Seventy-nine adolescents from one ethnic group.
title: Accurate Age Determination for Adolescents Using Magnetic Resonance Imaging of the Hand and Wrist with an Artificial Neural Network-Based Approach.
headline_result: neural network ages agreed with chronological age (p > 0.05) and were about ten-fold more accurate than the Tanner-Whitehouse 3 method applied to MRI alone, which significantly underestimated age in girls and in 15-17 year olds

model_family: regression CNN with an attention module and dynamic attention loss
patient_population: children in two large hand radiograph datasets
clinical_problem: bone age assessment for endocrine, genetic and growth disorders
model_description: Regresses bone age directly from the radiograph, with an attention module that first learns where the growth-relevant regions are and a loss that weights the hard cases more heavily during training. The attention idea addresses the specific failure mode of bone age networks, which is that most of the image is irrelevant and the informative epiphyses are small.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: Regression Convolutional Neural Network for Automated Pediatric Bone Age Assessment From Hand Radiograph.
dataset_size: two large datasets; sizes not stated
headline_result: average discrepancy of 5.2-5.3 months between clinical and automatic bone age on two large datasets

model_family: convolutional neural network segmentation of lumen, wall and background, combined with curved planar reformatting
patient_population: 23 pediatric patients with Crohn disease imaged at 1.5 T with a T1-weighted postcontrast VIBE sequence
clinical_problem: seeing and quantifying disease burden in pediatric Crohn disease on contrast-enhanced small bowel MRI, where following the bowel means scrolling back and forth through a 3D volume
model_description: The segmentation is a means, not the end. Curved planar reformatting straightens the bowel so its whole length is visible at once, and the CNN supplies the lumen and wall boundaries that reformatting needs - together turning a scroll-through into a set of markers. The markers are then tested for what a radiologist would want: whether they separate active from inactive segments and stricturing from non-stricturing, and whether they reproduce. Wall segmentation is more reliable than lumen.
journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
title: Curved planar reformatting and convolutional neural network-based segmentation of the small bowel for visualization and quantitative assessment of pediatric Crohn's disease from MRI.
headline_result: Dice 75 +/- 18% lumen, 81 +/- 8% wall, 97 +/- 2% background; wall thickness at minimum radius (P = 0.0013) and median relative contrast enhancement (P = 0.0033) separated active from non-active segments

patient_population: 76 knee MRI datasets; age estimation proof-of-concept on 145 subjects (14-subject test set)
clinical_problem: Automatically segmenting knee growth-plate structures on MRI to support chronological age estimation in adolescents and young adults lacking legal documentation
model_description: Input: 3D knee MR images; output: automatic segmentation of growth-plate structures used to derive estimated chronological age, via a U-Net-style encoder-decoder CNN
title: Automated segmentation of the knee for age assessment in 3D MR images using convolutional neural networks.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development, proof-of-concept internal validation
dataset_size: 76 MRI datasets (segmentation); 145 subjects for age estimation, 14-subject test set
headline_result: Dice 98%, IoU 96% for segmentation; mean absolute age error 0.48 ± 0.32 years (14-subject test set)

model_family: multivariate pattern analysis over voxel-based morphometry, diffusion tensor and surface features
patient_population: 14 pediatric patients with PANDAS paired with 14 healthy subjects
clinical_problem: whether pediatric autoimmune neuropsychiatric disorder associated with streptococci has a neuroanatomical signature that could serve as a biomarker, in a condition whose very existence as an entity rests on distinguishing it from ordinary early-onset OCD
model_description: The first pattern-analysis study of this early-onset OCD subtype, and its negative results are as informative as the positive one: diffusion metrics and every cortical surface feature showed no group difference, while gray matter did, and only gray matter supported classification. The authors read that as consistent with an immune rather than a developmental origin. Fourteen pairs, so 75% accuracy is a signal that the question is worth pursuing rather than a usable test.
title: Neuroanatomical features and its usefulness in classification of patients with PANDAS.
headline_result: 75% accuracy classifying PANDAS from controls using gray matter features; no significant group differences in diffusion or cortical surface measures

patient_population: preterm newborns
clinical_problem: automated quality control detection of major artifacts (e.g., motion) in neonatal brain MRI datasets
model_description: Input: 2D transverse T2-weighted neonatal brain MRI images, represented by 70 focus/texture/noise/natural-scene-statistics features; output: automated QC Pass/Fail classification.
release_evidence: tested an open source method to detect major artifacts among 2D neonatal MRI via supervised machine learning
title: Supervised machine learning quality control for magnetic resonance artifacts in neonatal data sets.
dataset_size: 1020 two-dimensional T2-weighted MRI images of preterm newborns
headline_result: Best model (RUSBoost): 85% positive predictive value, 75% sensitivity for QC Fail images

model_family: support vector machine on transfer-learned deep features combined with conventional texture features
patient_population: 50 children with congenital abnormalities of the kidney and urinary tract and 50 controls, imaged during routine care
clinical_problem: identifying congenital abnormalities of the kidney and urinary tract on the ultrasound children already receive
model_description: Combines features learned by a pretrained network with hand-computed texture features and shows the combination beats either alone, which is the useful methodological finding on a 100-child dataset where a deep model alone would overfit. Uses images from routine clinical care rather than a curated research acquisition.
title: Computer-aided diagnosis of congenital abnormalities of the kidney and urinary tract in children based on ultrasound imaging data by integrating texture image features and deep transfer learning image features.
headline_result: AUC 0.92, 0.88 and 0.92 for left, right and bilateral abnormal kidney scans, significantly better than either feature set alone (p < 0.001)

model_family: CNN with GloVe embeddings, and a domain-phrase attention hierarchical recurrent network
patient_population: adult and pediatric patients whose thoracic CT reports were collected from four healthcare centers
clinical_problem: extracting whether a CT report says there is a pulmonary embolus, at scale and across institutions
model_description: Reads a free-text thoracic CT report and decides whether it describes a pulmonary embolus. The recurrent model builds up word, sentence and document representations and weights domain-specific phrases through an attention mechanism. The finding that matters for a children's hospital is the transfer: models trained on adult reports classified pediatric reports at the same F1 of 0.99, which is not what happens with image models.
title: Comparative effectiveness of convolutional neural network (CNN) and recurrent neural network (RNN) architectures for radiology text report classification.
dataset_size: over 7,370 thoracic CT reports from four centers
headline_result: F1 0.99 for pulmonary embolus in adults and 0.99 in the pediatric population, beating the rule-based PEFinder on multi-institutional test sets

model_family: deep convolutional neural network with class activation maps
patient_population: 1531 hand radiographs of children and adults aged 5 to 70 years, plus a small exploratory sample of 44 patients with sexual developmental disorders or transgender identity
clinical_problem: whether hand and wrist radiographs carry a sex signal, which bears on bone age assessment (a sex-specific reference) and on forensic identification
model_description: The clearest demonstration in this database of a model doing something people cannot: 95.9% against two radiologists at 58% and 46%, and the radiologists could not find the pattern even when shown the model's heat maps. The exploratory arm is the thoughtful part - in 44 patients with sexual developmental disorders or transgender identity, agreement with phenotypic sex fell to 77.8%, which raises the question of what the model is measuring and complicates any forensic use.
title: Beyond Human Perception: Sexual Dimorphism in Hand and Wrist Radiographs Is Discernible by a Deep Learning Model.
study_design: retrospective model development with reader comparison
headline_result: 95.9% accuracy (kappa 0.92) versus 58% and 46% for two radiologists; agreement with phenotypic sex fell to 77.8% in patients with sexual developmental disorders or transgender identity

patient_population: children whose hand radiographs make up a curated 14,236-image challenge dataset
clinical_problem: skeletal maturity (bone age) assessment
model_description: Not one model but a public competition: RSNA released a curated set of 14,236 pediatric hand radiographs with reference bone ages and invited teams to submit algorithms, scored on mean absolute distance in months. Almost every entry used convolutional neural networks. The paper reports what a coordinated community effort achieved and is the reference point later bone-age papers compare against.
release_evidence: the data set was made available to registered challenge participants; the abstract says nothing about releasing the models
title: The RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Machine Learning Challenge.
headline_result: best five entries achieved mean absolute distance of 4.2 to 4.5 months

model_family: artificial neural network over radiologist-interpreted CT findings
patient_population: 12 902 children from the Pediatric Emergency Care Applied Research Network traumatic brain injury dataset
clinical_problem: ruling in clinically relevant traumatic brain injury in children so that the rest can be discharged on an evidence-based basis rather than admitted for observation
model_description: Built on PECARN, the dataset that produced the clinical decision rule pediatric emergency medicine already uses, and aimed at the same decision - who can safely go home. The inputs are the radiologist's CT findings rather than the pixels, so this is decision support layered on the report rather than image analysis. Sensitivity above 99% is the operating point the problem demands, since the cost of a missed clinically relevant injury is not symmetric with the cost of an observation stay.
title: Using an artificial neural network to predict traumatic brain injury.
study_design: retrospective secondary analysis of a multi-center cohort
headline_result: prediction of clinically relevant traumatic brain injury with greater than 99% sensitivity and AUC 0.99

patient_population: 168 structural connectomes of preterm neonates; 1,013 resting-state functional connectomes from the ABIDE database
clinical_problem: identifying predictive brain connectome subnetworks for developmental outcomes in preterm neonates and for autism classification
model_description: a sparse linear regression model with anatomical and connectivity priors takes a structural or functional connectome as input and outputs a predicted cognitive/neuromotor developmental outcome (preterm cohort) or autism spectrum category (ABIDE cohort) via a learned weighted subnetwork
journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
title: Predictive connectome subnetwork extraction with anatomical and connectivity priors.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and validation study using two cohorts

patient_population: 109 pediatric patients with medulloblastoma from 3 children's hospitals, January 2001 to January 2014
clinical_problem: predicting the molecular subgroup of pediatric medulloblastoma (sonic hedgehog, group 3, group 4) from pre-treatment MRI, without tissue sampling
model_description: 590 radiomic features extracted from MRI tumor segmentations (T1- and T2-weighted) are used with feature selection and cross-validated classifiers to output a predicted molecular subgroup label for each medulloblastoma.
title: MR Imaging-Based Radiomic Signatures of Distinct Molecular Subgroups of Medulloblastoma.
study_design: multi-institutional retrospective radiomics/machine-learning study with cross-cohort validation
dataset_size: 109 pediatric patients (3-cohort multi-institutional dataset), 590 radiomic features
headline_result: AUC 0.79, 0.70, 0.83 (SHH, group 3, group 4) with double 10-fold cross-validation on combined cohort; AUC 0.70-0.73 (SHH) and 0.76-0.80 (group 4) with independent 3-dataset cross-validation

patient_population: 21 adults and 30 children (mean age 7.75 years) undergoing task fMRI
clinical_problem: classifying emotional condition and age group from task fMRI activation during naturalistic emotion processing
model_description: BOLD fMRI activation recorded while children and adults watched movie clips portraying positive, negative, and neutral emotions is used to train multivariate support vector machines. The models classify the emotional condition being viewed and distinguish children from adults within each condition, based on activity in sensory, socio-emotional, and emotion-regulation regions.
title: Neural architecture supporting active emotion processing in children: A multivariate approach.
headline_result: 61.44% accuracy classifying emotional condition across all participants; adults vs. children significantly distinguished within each condition (p < 0.05)

model_family: VGG-inspired detection network followed by a U-net measurement network
patient_population: 183 pregnant women at St. Luke's Hospital, Wolisso, Ethiopia
clinical_problem: estimating gestational age where there is no sonographer, using a sweep protocol any health worker can learn in a day
model_description: Works from sweeps acquired with a fixed protocol that requires no knowledge of ultrasound, and which will usually not contain the standard plane at all. One network finds the frames containing the fetal head, a second measures head circumference in those frames, and gestational age follows from the Hadlock curve. Validated against standard-plane measurements taken by an experienced sonographer on the same women.
title: Automated Fetal Head Detection and Circumference Estimation from Free-Hand Ultrasound Sweeps Using Deep Learning in Resource-Limited Countries.
headline_result: most automatically estimated gestational ages fell within the 2.5th to 97.5th centile interval of the Hadlock curve relative to reference measurements

patient_population: children undergoing hand radiography for bone age assessment (RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Machine Learning Challenge)
clinical_problem: skeletal maturity (bone age) assessment
model_description: An editorial/commentary discussing lessons learned from the RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Machine Learning Challenge, in which competing deep-learning models were benchmarked on pediatric hand radiographs for automated bone age assessment. No abstract text was available; scope inferred from the title alone.
title: What Can We Learn from the RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Machine Learning Challenge?
study_design: editorial / commentary on a machine-learning challenge

patient_population: 328 cognitively normal Chinese children aged 6-12, with two independent validation datasets of 114 and 71 children
clinical_problem: whether a pediatric brain atlas built on one population is valid for children of another
model_description: A set of age-specific brain templates built from Chinese children, made because the widely used NIH pediatric atlases are derived from Caucasian children. The comparison found substantial anatomical differences in frontal and parietal regions, and using the matched atlas gave significantly better tissue segmentation and brain-age prediction in Chinese children. It is a concrete demonstration that population mismatch in a reference dataset degrades downstream results.
release_evidence: released on the NITRC website at https://www.nitrc.org/projects/chn-pd
title: Unbiased age-specific structural brain atlases for Chinese pediatric population.
dataset_size: 328 children for atlas construction; 185 children across two validation datasets
headline_result: significantly higher accuracy than the NIH pediatric atlases for both brain-age prediction and tissue segmentation in Chinese children

patient_population: pediatric cohort with medically intractable epilepsy, MRI-positive and MRI-negative for focal cortical dysplasia
clinical_problem: identifying epileptogenic lesions (focal cortical dysplasia) in children with intractable epilepsy, including MRI-negative cases
model_description: T1-weighted, T2-weighted and FLAIR MRI sequences are processed with morphometric and gray-level co-occurrence texture features, which are input to a 2-step Bayesian classifier that flags candidate epileptogenic lesions, evaluated separately in MRI-positive and MRI-negative epilepsy cases.
title: Identifying lesions in paediatric epilepsy using morphometric and textural analysis of magnetic resonance images.
headline_result: combining all three sequences: 97% subjectwise sensitivity in MRI-positive cases and 70% in MRI-negative cases; 100% healthy-subject rejection

model_family: machine learning models (naive Bayes, random forest, SVM, neural networks)
patient_population: 14 boys with autism spectrum disorder and 33 typically developing boys, aged 8-12 years
clinical_problem: identifying autism spectrum disorder from white matter connectome imaging biomarkers
model_description: Diffusion MRI-derived edge density and tract-based connectome metrics go in; machine-learning classifiers (naive Bayes, random forest, SVM, neural network) output identification of children with autism spectrum disorder.
title: White Matter Connectome Edge Density in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders: Potential Imaging Biomarkers Using Machine-Learning Models.
study_design: case-control diffusion MRI connectome study comparing multiple machine-learning classifiers
dataset_size: 14 boys with ASD, 33 typically developing boys
headline_result: best model (random forest, edge density metrics) accuracy 75.3%, specificity 97.0%, PPV 81.5%

patient_population: adults and children in the reviewed studies, with particular attention to pediatric and deformed-lung cases
clinical_problem: isolating the lungs on a chest radiograph, the step every downstream chest analysis depends on
model_description: A review of lung segmentation on chest radiographs from 2006 to 2017, classifying methods into rule-based, pixel-classification, model-based, hybrid and deep-learning families. Its finding for a children's hospital is a gap: almost all published algorithms are validated on adult posteroanterior films of healthy-looking lungs, while pediatric films are noisier, obstructed by whoever is holding the child, and anatomically different by developmental stage.
journal: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
title: A review on lung boundary detection in chest X-rays.
headline_result: hybrid and deep-learning methods reached inter-observer-level segmentation performance, at the cost of long training and high computational complexity

model_family: deep learning lung delineation feeding quantitative texture analysis
patient_population: 790 fetal lung ultrasound images obtained between 24 and 39 weeks gestation
clinical_problem: predicting neonatal respiratory morbidity from ultrasound instead of amniocentesis
model_description: The successor version of the commercial fetal lung maturity tool, with the manual lung outlining replaced by deep learning. The comparison that makes the paper worth reading is three-way: fully automated, the same texture analysis with manual delineation, and gestational age alone. Automation cost essentially nothing in accuracy (91.5% versus 90.3%) while both beat gestational age alone (75.6%) decisively.
release_evidence: quantusFLM version 3.0, a commercial software tool
title: Evaluation of an improved tool for non-invasive prediction of neonatal respiratory morbidity based on fully automated fetal lung ultrasound analysis.
headline_result: sensitivity 71.0%, specificity 94.7%, accuracy 91.5% fully automated, against 90.3% with manual delineation and 75.6% using gestational age alone

model_family: deep Q-network reinforcement learning agents with multi-scale hierarchical search
body_region: fetal head, adult brain and heart
patient_population: fetuses in a fetal head ultrasound dataset, alongside adult brain and cardiac MRI datasets
clinical_problem: finding anatomical landmarks automatically, the step that biometry and registration depend on
model_description: Rather than scanning the whole image, an agent starts somewhere and learns to walk toward the landmark, treating the 3D scan as an environment to navigate. Searching coarse-to-fine with hierarchical step sizes speeds this up four- to fivefold and copes with the large fields of view and noisy backgrounds where fixed-scale agents fail. Evaluated on fetal head ultrasound among three datasets.
title: Evaluating reinforcement learning agents for anatomical landmark detection.
dataset_size: three medical imaging datasets; sizes not stated
headline_result: surpassed state-of-the-art supervised and reinforcement-learning landmark methods; hierarchical steps sped up search 4-5 times

model_family: attention-gated CNN module for VGG / U-Net
patient_population: fetuses undergoing mid-pregnancy screening ultrasound; the segmentation experiments use adult abdominal CT
clinical_problem: identifying the correct standard views during fetal ultrasound screening
model_description: A drop-in module that makes a standard CNN learn where to look, suppressing irrelevant image regions without a separate organ-localization step. Demonstrated on fetal ultrasound scan-plane detection, where it reduced false positives, and on multi-organ abdominal CT segmentation. It is a general architecture contribution rather than a clinical product.
release_evidence: the source code for the proposed AG models is publicly available
title: Attention gated networks: Learning to leverage salient regions in medical images.
dataset_size: two large 3D CT abdominal datasets plus a fetal ultrasound screening set; sizes not stated
headline_result: consistent improvement in prediction performance over the base architectures across datasets and training sizes

model_family: deep learning classifier on white matter connectomes
patient_population: 75 full-term infants scanned at birth and 37 preterm infants scanned at term-equivalent age
clinical_problem: predicting cognitive ability at age 2 from the brain's wiring at birth
model_description: Builds a white matter connectome from diffusion MRI acquired at birth and classifies whether that child will score above or below the median on cognitive testing at two years, then predicts the individual score. Trained on full-term infants and evaluated separately on preterm infants, which is the transfer that matters clinically. Frontal lobe connections and their links to the rest of the brain carried the classification.
title: White matter connectomes at birth accurately predict cognitive abilities at age 2.
headline_result: 89.5% accuracy in full-term and 83.8% in preterm infants for the 2-year cognitive group; predicted and actual scores correlated at r = 0.98 and 0.96

model_family: two fine-tuned convolutional feature extractors - one on the whole image, one on discriminant cropped regions - whose classification decisions are fused
patient_population: 4074 2-D fetal ultrasound images (3109 training, 965 test)
clinical_problem: labeling which fetal structure a 2D ultrasound image shows, across 14 structures, so that large retrospective archives can be mined for indicators of abnormal development
model_description: The diagnosis of the problem is precise: crops confuse structures that look alike, such as kidney and abdomen, while the whole image lacks the local detail to say which structure is where. Fusing decisions from both, without a prior on where to look, is the contribution, and localization falls out of the same machinery. The high mean accuracy alongside much lower precision and recall reflects 14 unbalanced classes. Its stated purpose is retrospective archive mining rather than live scanning.
title: Decision Fusion-Based Fetal Ultrasound Image Plane Classification Using Convolutional Neural Networks.
headline_result: mean accuracy 97.05%, precision 76.47%, recall 75.41%, Cohen kappa 0.72; 92% mean accuracy on images without scanner overlays

model_family: machine learning classification framework combining multimodal features
patient_population: children/youth with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder and age-matched typically developing controls
clinical_problem: developing a low-cost machine-learning-based screening protocol for fetal alcohol spectrum disorder in children/youth
model_description: Inputs are saccadic eye movement tasks, psychometric tests, and neuroimaging of the corpus callosum; a machine learning framework combines these multimodal measures to classify children/youth with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder, and identifies a reduced low-cost subset (eye movement plus psychometrics) that approaches full-panel performance.
title: Detection of Children/Youth With Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder Through Eye Movement, Psychometric, and Neuroimaging Data.
study_design: prospective case-control multimodal machine learning screening study
headline_result: combination of 4-6 assessments yielded the best FASD-versus-control classification accuracy; a reduced eye-movement-plus-psychometric protocol approached this performance at lower cost

model_family: deep CNN on diffusion tractography streamlines with focal and center losses and a soft attention mechanism
patient_population: streamlines from 70 healthy children and 70 children with focal epilepsy, labeled by functional MRI and electrical stimulation mapping
clinical_problem: identifying eloquent white matter pathways before pediatric epilepsy surgery, so that resection spares motor, language, auditory and visual function
model_description: Aimed at the specific inadequacy of the current tools: electrical stimulation mapping is invasive and maps cortex, fMRI needs task cooperation from a child, and neither shows the fibers connecting eloquent areas. The network classifies individual tractography streamlines, with focal and center losses chosen for an extremely unbalanced label distribution and soft attention for interpretability. Ground truth comes from the invasive standard it would reduce.
release_evidence: the abstract states the implementation will be released at a GitHub repository
title: Objective Detection of Eloquent Axonal Pathways to Minimize Postoperative Deficits in Pediatric Epilepsy Surgery using Diffusion Tractography and Convolutional Neural Networks.
headline_result: 73-100% accuracy for objective detection of functionally important pathways, outperforming existing streamline classification models

model_family: machine learning regression algorithm on normalized brain network metrics
patient_population: 27 patients with epilepsy, ages 8-18 years
clinical_problem: predicting individual IQ from resting-state fMRI brain network architecture in children with epilepsy
model_description: Brain network graph metrics (clustering coefficient, transitivity, modularity, path length, global efficiency) are computed from resting-state fMRI in children with epilepsy under two normalization strategies. A machine learning algorithm uses only these normalized metrics to predict each patient's IQ, with normalization substantially improving prediction accuracy over non-normalized metrics.
title: Normalization enhances brain network features that predict individual intelligence in children with epilepsy.
headline_result: Normalization substantially improved subject-level IQ prediction accuracy versus non-normalized network metrics

model_family: classifier built on resting-state functional connectivity features
patient_population: never-depressed children aged 8-14 with familial risk for major depressive disorder and age-matched controls without familial risk, reassessed by diagnostic interview 3-4 years later
clinical_problem: identifying, before any episode occurs, which children at familial risk for major depression will develop it in adolescence
model_description: A prognostic rather than diagnostic model, and the design carries the weight: imaging at baseline in children who had never been depressed, diagnosis established 3-4 years later, and the classifier built independently of the group differences the paper also reports. Its comparator is the right one - baseline clinical rating scales - and connectivity beat them. A pilot, with the sample size that word implies.
title: Intrinsic Functional Brain Connectivity Predicts Onset of Major Depression Disorder in Adolescence: A Pilot Study.
dataset_size: pilot cohort, size not stated in the abstract
headline_result: classification of converters versus non-converters from baseline connectivity reached high accuracy, sensitivity and specificity, superior to classification from baseline clinical rating scales

model_family: fully convolutional network with a differentiable spatial-to-numerical layer
patient_population: 493 patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, adult deformity and spinal stenosis
clinical_problem: measuring spinal deformity parameters (Cobb angle, kyphosis, lordosis, pelvic incidence) on biplanar radiographs
model_description: Takes biplanar spine radiographs and returns the 78 anatomical landmarks (endplate centers, hip joint centers, S1 endplate margins) from which the standard deformity angles are then computed. It is designed to cope with a wide range of conditions and fields of view. The authors are candid that although the predicted spine shape looks convincing and correlates strongly with ground truth, the standard errors on individual angles are large.
journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
title: Fully automated radiological analysis of spinal disorders and deformities: a deep learning approach.
dataset_size: 493 spines for training, 50 patients for quantitative comparison
headline_result: all parameters strongly correlated with ground truth, but standard errors from 2.7 degrees (pelvic tilt) to 11.5 degrees (L1-L5 lordosis)

patient_population: infants and young children undergoing MRI
clinical_problem: avoiding sedation and general anesthesia for MRI in infants and young children
model_description: A review of every lever available for getting a diagnostic MRI in a small child awake: environment, child life specialists, feed-and-bundle, distraction, noise reduction, and the technical routes to shorter scans, of which artificial intelligence is one. Useful as the framing document for why faster reconstruction matters in a children's hospital, rather than as a source of model performance figures.
journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
title: Techniques for minimizing sedation in pediatric MRI.

patient_population: pediatric patients generally
clinical_problem: overview of future imaging technology trends in pediatric radiology, including AI-based CT dose reduction
model_description: A narrative overview of emerging pediatric radiology imaging technologies, including artificial intelligence for CT dose reduction, new MR techniques to reduce sedation needs, and molecular imaging.
journal: RoFo : Fortschritte auf dem Gebiete der Rontgenstrahlen und der Nuklearmedizin
title: [From Xrays to PET/MR, and then? - Future imaging in pediatric radiology].

patient_population: 394 neonates with MRI-confirmed punctate white matter lesions across 11 Chinese hospitals
clinical_problem: predicting adverse motor outcome in neonates with punctate white matter lesions
model_description: A radiomics model combines MRI-extracted imaging features with clinical/perinatal information to predict adverse motor outcome (Bayley-III / GMFCS) at 24 months corrected age in neonates with punctate white matter lesions.
title: Prediction of adverse motor outcome for neonates with punctate white matter lesions by MRI images using radiomics strategy: protocol for a prospective cohort multicentre study.

model_family: 3D Gabor filters and texture features with a support vector machine and uterus edge-based instance selection, plus a curvature-based corner detector for vessels
patient_population: 44 control and pathological cases: singleton and normal or monochorionic twin pregnancies between 25 and 37 weeks
clinical_problem: quantifying placental anatomy and its peripheral vasculature on fetal MRI, which is needed for diagnosis and for planning fetal surgery and which is ambiguous to interpret by eye
model_description: A classical pipeline that beat six deep networks on the same task - 3D U-Net, V-Net, DeepMedic, Holistic3D Net, HighRes3D Net and Dense V-Net were all implemented for comparison and all lost on placenta localization. With 44 cases, engineered features and a support vector machine with careful instance selection still outperform learned ones, which is a useful counterweight to the assumption that a network is always the right tool in this data regime. Segmenting the peripheral vessels as well as the organ is what makes it relevant to fetal surgical planning.
title: Fully automatic 3D reconstruction of the placenta and its peripheral vasculature in intrauterine fetal MRI.
headline_result: Dice 0.82 +/- 0.02 for placenta and 0.81 +/- 0.08 for its vasculature, outperforming all six convolutional network baselines on placenta localization

model_family: convolutional neural networks with transfer learning and classifier combination, both mixture-of-experts and simple Bayes
patient_population: children aged 5 to 10 years from the ABIDE I and ABIDE II datasets
clinical_problem: diagnosing autism spectrum disorder in young children from resting-state functional MRI, before behavioral symptoms are established enough for interview and observation to settle it
model_description: Two constraints are handled at once: small medical datasets and the need to hold the age window narrow. The age restriction to 5-10 years is a deliberate cost - it shrinks an already small dataset - taken because a diagnostic aid is only useful before the clinical diagnosis is obvious. Combining classifiers and transferring features stand in for the data that does not exist. Accuracy in the low-to-mid 70s is representative of what ABIDE supports, and is a reminder of how far this is from clinical use.
title: Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorders in Young Children Based on Resting-State Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging Data Using Convolutional Neural Networks.
study_design: retrospective model development on public datasets
dataset_size: ABIDE I and ABIDE II subjects aged 5-10
headline_result: ABIDE I accuracy 0.7273, sensitivity 0.712, specificity 0.7348; ABIDE II accuracy 0.700, sensitivity 0.582, specificity 0.804

patient_population: 112 120 chest radiographs from the NIH ChestX-ray14 database, of which 5941 (5%) are pediatric; a second network was trained on the pediatric subset alone (2885 AP, 3056 PA)
clinical_problem: verifying whether a frontal chest radiograph is anteroposterior or posteroanterior, which affects interpretation and which mislabeled metadata routinely gets wrong across facilities
model_description: A quality-control task rather than a diagnostic one, and the pediatric interest is in the ablation: training on the 5% pediatric subset alone, a 95% reduction in data, cost almost nothing (AUC 0.997 versus 1.0, difference not significant). That is a concrete data point for the recurring pediatric worry that adult-scale datasets are needed for anything to work. Aimed at curating large datasets for machine learning and at departmental quality assurance.
title: Deep Learning Method for Automated Classification of Anteroposterior and Posteroanterior Chest Radiographs.
study_design: retrospective model development on a public dataset
headline_result: AUC 1.0 and accuracy 99.6% for the full-dataset network versus AUC 0.997 and accuracy 98% for the pediatric-only network (difference not significant, p = 0.17)

model_family: naive Bayes, random forest, and support vector machine classifiers
patient_population: 39 boys, ages 8-12 years, with and without auditory over-responsivity
clinical_problem: classifying auditory over-responsivity in children from diffusion tensor imaging and connectome edge-density metrics
model_description: Diffusion tensor imaging metrics (fractional anisotropy, mean/radial/axial diffusivity) and derived connectome edge-density maps of white matter tracts are input to naive Bayes, random forest, and support vector machine classifiers. The models were trained and compared to classify boys with versus without auditory over-responsivity, with random forest using edge-density metrics performing best.
title: White Matter Connectome Correlates of Auditory Over-Responsivity: Edge Density Imaging and Machine-Learning Classifiers.
dataset_size: 39 boys, ages 8-12 years (15 with auditory over-responsivity)
headline_result: Left superior longitudinal fasciculus FA gave AUC 0.756 for AOR prediction (p = 0.008); random forest with edge-density metrics had the highest classification accuracy among tested models

model_family: graph convolutional network over spatial and diffusion wave-vector domains, with a multi-scale residual architecture and adversarial learning
patient_population: longitudinal infant brain diffusion MRI
clinical_problem: missing data in longitudinal infant imaging studies, caused by subject dropout and failed scans, which breaks the developmental trajectories those studies exist to measure
model_description: Attacks a problem specific to pediatric longitudinal imaging: infants move, scans fail, families drop out, and a missing timepoint costs a whole trajectory. Building the graph over both space and the diffusion wave-vector domain lets the network use the structure of the acquisition itself, not just the image. Imputing a missing scan is a strong claim that needs careful use downstream, but the alternative - discarding the subject - has its own bias.
title: Longitudinal Prediction of Infant Diffusion MRI Data via Graph Convolutional Adversarial Networks.
headline_result: accurate and robust longitudinal prediction of missing infant brain diffusion MRI data

patient_population: Digital Hand Atlas public bone-age dataset
clinical_problem: Can bone age be estimated automatically and accurately from hand x-rays, using image features tailored to the limited size of typical bone-age training datasets?
model_description: Hand x-ray images are first decomposed into multi-scale, multi-direction representations via non-subsampled contourlet transform, then fed into CNNs (regression and classification variants) that fuse information across scales to predict bone age.
title: A multi-scale data fusion framework for bone age assessment with convolutional neural networks.
study_design: retrospective model development and benchmarking on a public dataset
dataset_size: not stated (Digital Hand Atlas public dataset)
headline_result: Improvement of more than 0.1 years in mean absolute error over corresponding spatial-domain approaches; outperforms several state-of-the-art bone-age methods

patient_population: 198 school-aged children (5-12 years), ABIDE II multi-institutional database
clinical_problem: distinguishing school-aged children with autism spectrum disorder from typically developing children using resting-state fMRI
model_description: Uses full-frequency-band resting-state fMRI features as input to an enhanced stacked auto-encoder deep-learning model that classifies children as having autism spectrum disorder or typically developing.
title: Computer-aided diagnosis of school-aged children with ASD using full frequency bands and enhanced SAE: A multi-institution study.
headline_result: Average accuracy 96.26% (sensitivity 98.03%, specificity 93.62%)

patient_population: sample from the public ADHD-200 dataset (children and adolescents)
clinical_problem: developing an interpretable machine learning model to aid ADHD diagnosis using neuroimaging and phenotypic data
model_description: Input is neuroimaging and phenotypic data from the ADHD-200 collection; output is an ADHD-versus-typically-developing classification produced by a decision tree chosen for its readability, highlighting the limbic system as a relevant predictor.
title: Towards interpretable machine learning models for diagnosis aid: A case study on attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder.
study_design: retrospective public-dataset (ADHD-200) machine learning study emphasizing interpretability

model_family: multiple ML algorithms (naive Bayes, random forest, SVM, neural networks)
patient_population: 44 children with sensory processing disorder and 41 typically developing children, prospectively recruited
clinical_problem: Can diffusion tensor imaging and machine learning identify children with sensory processing disorder based on white matter microstructure and connectivity, as an objective imaging biomarker?
model_description: Diffusion tensor imaging-derived microstructural (FA, MD, RD) and connectivity/connectomic (track density, edge density) metrics are used as input features to several machine learning classifiers to distinguish children with sensory processing disorder from typically developing children.
title: Diffusion tensor tractography in children with sensory processing disorder: Potentials for devising machine learning classifiers.
headline_result: Best model (random forest with tract-based track density) achieved 77.5% accuracy, 73.8% sensitivity, 81.6% specificity

model_family: five ResNet-18 networks pretrained on ImageNet, one per anatomical region, with 30-fold standard augmentation
patient_population: 250 pediatric bone radiographs (50 each of shoulder, elbow, hand, pelvis and knee), plus a separate 100-radiograph test set from a single institution
clinical_problem: knowing which body part a radiograph shows without trusting the metadata, which is what automated hanging protocols and the curation of large training sets both depend on
model_description: A non-interpretive task, and a reminder of how much of radiology AI's near-term value sits there. The finding worth carrying forward is about data economics: 250 radiographs, augmented thirty-fold with standard transforms, produced perfect classification on two separate test sets. Problems this well-posed do not need large datasets. At 33 radiographs per second it is also fast enough to run over an archive, which is the curation use case the authors name.
title: Automated semantic labeling of pediatric musculoskeletal radiographs using deep learning.
study_design: retrospective model development with external validation
dataset_size: 250 training radiographs plus a 100-radiograph external test set
headline_result: ROC AUC of 1 for all five networks on both test sets, classifying at 33 radiographs per second

model_family: CNN landmark detection driving a statistical shape model
patient_population: 68 biplanar radiographs of asymptomatic subjects and adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients
clinical_problem: getting 3D spinal measurements from biplanar radiographs, which currently needs so much manual supervision that it stays out of routine practice
model_description: Fits a realistic statistical shape model of the spine to a pair of biplanar radiographs by having networks find the controlling anatomical landmarks, iteratively and coarse-to-fine. Reconstruction takes under a minute against the semi-automated methods it replaces, and 89% of its measurements fell inside the experts' own confidence intervals. The stated aim is dissemination: 3D measurement exists but nobody has time to do it by hand.
title: Toward Automated 3D Spine Reconstruction from Biplanar Radiographs Using CNN for Statistical Spine Model Fitting.
study_design: retrospective validation against multi-expert ground truth
headline_result: landmark errors 1.6-2.3 mm; absolute error 2.8-4.7 degrees for spinal and 1-2.1 degrees for pelvic parameters; 89% of measurements inside expert confidence intervals

model_family: fully convolutional network embedding a dilated dense network in a U-Net, with residual connections in the second variant
patient_population: infant brain MRI
clinical_problem: segmenting hippocampal subfields in infants, where existing methods are built for adults and fail because of poor tissue contrast and structures that change shape rapidly in early development
model_description: An architecture argument with a specifically infant motivation: dilated dense blocks give multi-scale context while keeping spatial resolution, which is what the hippocampal subfields need since they are small, adjacent and low-contrast in the infant brain. The comparison is against 3D U-Net on the same data, and the gain of 2-2.5 Dice points is modest but consistent across both variants.
title: Dilated Dense U-Net for Infant Hippocampus Subfield Segmentation.
headline_result: average Dice improved by 2.1% (DUnet) and 2.5% (ResDUnet) over classic 3D U-net, outperforming other state-of-the-art methods

model_family: previously trained machine learning classifier (resting-state fMRI network localization)
patient_population: 16 pediatric patients aged 3.1-18.6 years with medically refractory epilepsy undergoing invasive electrographic monitoring
clinical_problem: localizing sensorimotor brain function noninvasively before epilepsy surgery, as an alternative to invasive stimulation mapping
model_description: Resting-state fMRI data from pediatric epilepsy patients are analyzed by a machine learning classifier (previously trained and validated in adults) that localizes sensorimotor resting-state networks; results are compared with direct electrocortical stimulation mapping, the clinical gold standard.
title: A comparison of resting state functional magnetic resonance imaging to invasive electrocortical stimulation for sensorimotor mapping in pediatric patients.
study_design: prospective single-center comparative diagnostic accuracy study
headline_result: comparable functional localization between resting-state fMRI classifier and electrocortical stimulation mapping (no single summary statistic given)

model_family: deep learning pipeline with a plane acceptance check followed by head circumference and biparietal diameter estimation
patient_population: fetal ultrasound images: 102 labeled for training, 70 for validation
clinical_problem: automating head circumference and biparietal diameter on fetal ultrasound, the biometry used to assign gestational age and flag central nervous system pathology
model_description: Biometry with a gatekeeper. The pipeline first decides whether the plane is acceptable and only then measures, which is the right ordering for a measurement that is meaningless off-plane and the part most automated biometry skips. Small dataset, and the reported success rates are plane-level rather than millimetre agreement, so it reads as feasibility.
title: Automatic evaluation of fetal head biometry from ultrasound images using machine learning.
headline_result: 91.43% success for head circumference and 100% for biparietal diameter, with 87.14% accuracy on the plane acceptance check

patient_population: Infant brain MRI (human), also validated on macaque infant MRI
clinical_problem: Correcting topological errors (handles/holes) in reconstructed infant cortical surfaces from brain MRI to enable accurate early brain development studies.
model_description: An anatomically constrained deep learning network iteratively identifies and corrects candidate voxels with topological defects in segmented infant brain MRI to produce topologically accurate cortical surfaces.
title: Topological correction of infant white matter surfaces using anatomically constrained convolutional neural network.
study_design: retrospective methods development study, validated on simulated and real topological errors

patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing body MRA
clinical_problem: correcting off-resonance artifacts to enable faster pediatric body MR angiography
model_description: Short-readout (long scan-time, low-artifact) MRA scans are used as reference and augmented with simulated off-resonance to train a residual CNN (Off-ResNet); applied to faster long-readout 3D-cones scans, the network corrects off-resonance blurring, compared against an autofocus method and radiologist scoring of anatomical features.
title: Deep residual network for off-resonance artifact correction with application to pediatric body MRA with 3D cones.
study_design: prospective single-center technical development and reader-validation study
headline_result: long-readout scans corrected with Off-ResNet were noninferior to short-readout reference scans on radiologist scoring (P<.05); superior RMSE/SSIM/PSNR vs. autofocus (P<.01), with 59.3% shorter scan time

model_family: support vector machine on clinical plus T2-weighted radiomic features
patient_population: 225 children and young adults (mean age 14.1 years) internally and 84 (mean age 13.7) in an external cohort, with known or suspected liver disease
age_groups: child; adolescent; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: estimating liver stiffness without MR elastography, which not every center has
model_description: Classifies liver stiffness above or below 3 kPa from routine T2-weighted images plus clinical data, using elastography as the reference. The point is substitution: if ordinary sequences carry enough signal, centers without elastography could still stratify fibrosis risk. Clinical and radiomic features together beat either alone, and the model held up in an independent external cohort with a modest drop.
title: Machine Learning Prediction of Liver Stiffness Using Clinical and T2-Weighted MRI Radiomic Data.
headline_result: internal AUC 0.84 combining clinical and radiomic features (0.77 clinical, 0.70 radiomic alone); external AUC 0.80 with accuracy 75.0%

model_family: support vector regression (SVR) with PCA dimensionality reduction of HOG/LBP image features
patient_population: adolescents aged 12.0 to <19.0 years (275 male, 225 female), Xinjiang Uygur population, China
clinical_problem: forensic skeletal (bone) age estimation
model_description: The model takes digital radiographs of the knee joint and extracts histogram-of-oriented-gradients (HOG) and local binary pattern (LBP) texture features, reduces their dimensionality with principal component analysis, and regresses skeletal age with a support vector regression model. Separate models were trained and tested for male and female adolescents, intended for forensic bone-age estimation in the age range where hand/wrist growth plates have already fused.
title: Regression Algorithm of Bone Age Estimation of Knee-joint Based on Principal Component Analysis and Support Vector Machine.
study_design: retrospective single-center technical development and validation
dataset_size: 500 subjects (275 male, 225 female) aged 12.0-<19.0 years; 215 male and 180 female used for training, the remainder as an independent test set
headline_result: Accuracy within ±0.8/±1.0 year of true age: 80.67%/89.33% (male), 80.19%/90.45% (female); MAE 0.485-0.486 years, RMSE 0.590-0.606 years

model_family: custom automated computational program (DICOM parsing plus rule-based/NLP report analysis)
patient_population: post-mortem whole-body MRI examinations of fetuses, infants and children at a single pediatric hospital over 5.5 years
clinical_problem: quality audit of post-mortem MRI protocol adherence and diagnostic image quality
model_description: A custom computer program batch-processes DICOM files from whole-body post-mortem MRI examinations to extract imaging sequence parameters, and applies natural language processing to authorized radiology reports to extract the stated diagnostic image quality. It automates a departmental audit of imaging protocol adherence (full vs. abbreviated) and diagnostic quality rather than interpreting the images itself.
title: Automated data extraction and report analysis in computer-aided radiology audit: practice implications from post-mortem paediatric imaging.
study_design: retrospective single-center audit / workflow automation study
dataset_size: 460 whole-body post-mortem MRI examinations over 5.5 years (approximately 80 GB of DICOM data)
headline_result: Automated data-extraction accuracy 96.7% (445/460, 95% CI 94.7-98%); full protocol adherence in 66.3% of cases; 91.9% of studies of diagnostic quality overall

model_family: two sequential CNNs with synthetic intensity-inhomogeneity augmentation
patient_population: fetuses undergoing MRI
clinical_problem: volumetric and morphologic assessment of the fetal brain, which requires tissue-level segmentation
model_description: One network extracts the intracranial volume, a second divides it into seven tissue classes: cerebellum, basal ganglia and thalami, ventricular CSF, white matter, brain stem, cortical gray matter and extracerebral CSF. The trick is in the training: rather than correcting the intensity inhomogeneity that fetal motion causes, artificial gradients are added to clean slices so the network learns to tolerate the artifact, which removes a preprocessing step entirely.
title: Automatic brain tissue segmentation in fetal MRI using convolutional neural networks.
headline_result: average Dice rose from 0.77 to 0.88 and mean surface distance fell from 0.78 mm to 0.37 mm when training data included simulated inhomogeneity

patient_population: pregnant patients undergoing abdominal CT
clinical_problem: estimating fetal (conceptus) radiation dose during maternal CT imaging via automated patient-specific organ segmentation
model_description: Takes an abdominal CT scan of a pregnant patient as input and outputs automated segmentation of six anatomical structures (including the uterus), used to build a patient-specific computational phantom for Monte Carlo estimation of fetal (conceptus) radiation dose.
title: Estimation of the radiation dose in pregnancy: an automated patient-specific model using convolutional neural networks.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and internal validation study
dataset_size: 32 CT exams augmented to 128 datasets (80%/20% train/test)
headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient 0.92-0.98 for internal organs versus manual segmentation; mean uterus absorbed dose 2.9 mGy, organ dose differences -1.55% to 0.28%
