model_family: deep learning segmentation of lung and thorax fields, feeding a downstream pneumonia classifier
patient_population: a clinical pediatric chest radiograph set of 1351 patients, with two adult chest radiograph sets used to test generalizability
clinical_problem: segmenting the lungs and thorax on children's chest radiographs, and whether doing so improves the harder downstream call of bacterial versus viral pneumonia
model_description: Segmentation is treated as a means rather than an end, and the paper measures what it buys: cropping to the lung field raised the AUC for bacterial versus viral pneumonia from 0.815 to 0.879, which is a concrete argument for anatomical preprocessing rather than feeding whole radiographs to a classifier. Generalization runs the unusual direction here, from a pediatric-trained model to adult radiographs, and holds up.
title: Using deep-learning techniques for pulmonary-thoracic segmentations and improvement of pneumonia diagnosis in pediatric chest radiographs.
study_design: retrospective model development with external validation
dataset_size: 1351 pediatric patients plus two adult test sets
headline_result: Jaccard 0.910 and Dice 0.948 for lung segmentation; pneumonia classification AUC rose from 0.815 to 0.879 after lung extraction; Jaccard 0.888-0.903 on the two adult sets

patient_population: 95 very preterm infants (development/internal), 28 preterm infants (external validation)
clinical_problem: identifying diffuse white matter abnormality on T2-weighted MRI in preterm infants
model_description: A deep convolutional neural network classifies individual voxels on T2-weighted MRI image patches as diffuse white matter abnormality or normal white matter in preterm infants.
title: Objective and Automated Detection of Diffuse White Matter Abnormality in Preterm Infants Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks.
study_design: retrospective model development with external validation
headline_result: Dice similarity 0.85-0.99 for DWMA detection

model_family: benchmark of six segmentation methods (classical to deep learning)
patient_population: children with Wilms' tumor
clinical_problem: benchmarking segmentation of Wilms' tumor from multisequence MRI for therapy and treatment planning
model_description: Input: multisequence MRI before and after chemotherapy; output: tumor segmentation, benchmarked across six computer-based methods (classical to deep learning) against a multi-expert consensus ground truth.
title: Benchmarking Wilms' tumor in multisequence MRI data: why does current clinical practice fail? Which popular segmentation algorithms perform well?
study_design: benchmark study comparing algorithmic segmentation to multi-reader consensus
headline_result: Best computer-based methods achieved segmentation quality comparable to human expert annotations

patient_population: children and subadults in the 26 studies reviewed, mostly from the United States and Western Europe
clinical_problem: the state of machine learning for bone age assessment
model_description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 26 bone age studies using machine learning. Its value is in the gaps it names: the field works almost entirely on hand and wrist radiographs and has barely explored radiation-free alternatives such as MRI, few studies address ethnic differences, the samples cluster around the medico-legal age of 18, and socioeconomic influences on skeletal maturation are untouched.
title: Bone age assessment with various machine learning techniques: A systematic literature review and meta-analysis.

model_family: U-Net trained with one-cycle learning rate policy, transfer learning, generalized Dice loss, mixed precision, self-attention and augmentation
patient_population: paediatric patients treated for hydrocephalus; 80 CT images
clinical_problem: measuring cerebrospinal fluid volume on head CT during treatment of pediatric hydrocephalus, which radiologists do by manual segmentation and which is prone to bias and high intraobserver variability
model_description: A demonstration of how far careful training tricks carry a small dataset: eighty CT scans, a standard U-Net, and a stack of well-chosen optimizations reach near human-level Dice. The clinical case is time and consistency rather than accuracy - the volume is already measurable, just expensively and variably - which is the recurring shape of the argument for segmentation tools in pediatric neurosurgery.
title: Automated Ventricular System Segmentation in Paediatric Patients Treated for Hydrocephalus Using Deep Learning Methods.
headline_result: mean Dice 0.917 (SD 0.0352) on cross-validation and 0.9506 on a separate test set

patient_population: fetuses imaged with 2D ultrasound; further experiments use abdominal CT and brain tumor MRI
clinical_problem: getting usable models when few images are labelled, demonstrated on fetal ultrasound scan-plane detection
model_description: A pretraining recipe rather than a clinical model: patches of an unlabelled image are swapped and the network learns to restore the original, which teaches it semantic features without any annotation. The pretrained weights are then fine-tuned for a downstream task. Demonstrated on fetal ultrasound scan-plane detection, abdominal organ localization on CT and brain tumor segmentation on MRI.
title: Self-supervised learning for medical image analysis using image context restoration.
headline_result: improved models in all three downstream tasks; magnitudes not stated in the abstract

patient_population: 56 children with medically intractable epilepsy from 3 institutions (discovery n=38, validation n=18)
clinical_problem: predicting vagus nerve stimulation response in children with drug-resistant epilepsy from structural and functional connectomic profiling
model_description: Diffusion tensor imaging identifies white matter microstructural differences between VNS responders and non-responders, which inform beamforming of resting-state magnetoencephalography functional connectivity. These structural and functional connectomic features are combined in a support vector machine trained to predict VNS response and independently validated in a separate cohort, outperforming a classifier built from clinical covariates alone.
title: Connectomic Profiling Identifies Responders to Vagus Nerve Stimulation.
study_design: retrospective multi-institutional prognostic accuracy study with external validation
headline_result: 89.5% accuracy, AUC 0.93 on 10-fold cross-validation; 83.3% accuracy (85.7% sensitivity, 75.0% specificity) in external validation; superior to clinical covariates alone (AUC 0.57, p < 0.008)

model_family: LASSO-selected radiomic signatures from two anatomical regions, combined with a clinical factor in a predictive nomogram
patient_population: 53 children with clinically confirmed pulmonary tuberculosis and 62 with community-acquired pneumonia, split 3:1 into primary (n=86) and validation (n=29) cohorts
clinical_problem: separating primary progressive pulmonary tuberculosis from community-acquired pneumonia in children on chest CT, a distinction that changes treatment entirely and that experienced radiologists get wrong often enough to matter
model_description: Two separate radiomic signatures rather than one, extracted from the consolidation and from the lymph nodes, which mirrors how the two diseases actually differ and lets the model use nodal texture that no visual score captures. Duration of fever is the only clinical variable added. The comparator that gives the result its weight is a senior radiologist reading the same scans, who scored 0.79 against the nomogram's 0.97 - though on 29 validation patients.
title: Computed tomography-based predictive nomogram for differentiating primary progressive pulmonary tuberculosis from community-acquired pneumonia in children.
headline_result: AUC 0.971 (95% CI 0.912-1) versus 0.791 for a senior radiologist's clinical judgment and 0.832 for the clinical factor alone

model_family: random forests and deep convolutional neural networks on 3D hand MRI, with several image-input simplifications compared
patient_population: 328 hand MR images of children and adolescents; the best method was then adapted to 2D and applied to a public hand radiograph dataset
clinical_problem: estimating age in children and adolescents without ionizing radiation, for both clinical and forensic use
model_description: The MRI answer to bone age. Three problems with radiographic staging are addressed at once - radiation, the absence of MRI-specific staging systems, and examiner subjectivity - by regressing age directly from 3D volumes and skipping staging entirely. The paper is unusually careful about what is being estimated, separating biological age estimation from chronological age approximation, and it validates by porting the method to 2D radiographs where it matches published automatic methods.
title: Automated age estimation from MRI volumes of the hand.
study_design: retrospective model development with external dataset validation
headline_result: mean absolute error 0.37 +/- 0.51 years for biological age in subjects 18 or younger

model_family: deep learning and image processing pipeline: whole-fetus semantic segmentation, plane orientation estimation, biometry localization and limb detection
patient_population: 44 3D ultrasound volumes for development and an independent clinical set of 21 volumes for evaluation
clinical_problem: assessing fetal health at the first trimester scan - viability, gestational age, early anomaly detection - where the fetus looks nothing like it does in the second trimester and almost no automation exists
model_description: Deliberately broad where the literature is narrow: most first-trimester automation targets one anatomy, and this handles segmentation, plane orientation, biometry and limb detection from a single 3D volume. That matters because the first trimester scan asks several questions at once and the fetus is too small for any of them to be easy. Forty-four development volumes is little, and the claim is calibrated accordingly - approaching, not exceeding, expert assessment.
title: Automated 3D ultrasound image analysis for first trimester assessment of fetal health.
dataset_size: 44 development volumes and 21 independent evaluation volumes
headline_result: automated methods approached human expert assessment of a 3D volume on an independent clinical dataset

patient_population: 70 neonates from a local hospital plus 7 infants from the public NeuroBrainS12 dataset
clinical_problem: automatically removing skull/non-brain tissue from neonatal T1-weighted MRI to enable brain structural analysis
model_description: Takes neonatal T1-weighted brain MRI as input and outputs a brain mask (skull-stripped image) using a multi-view pyramid deep-learning network fused across 2D slice views.
title: A multi-view pyramid network for skull stripping on neonatal T1-weighted MRI.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and validation study using local and public neonatal MRI data
headline_result: Dice ratio 95.44-97.33%, sensitivity 93.19-97.02%, specificity 97.52-99.68%

model_family: computer vision and deep learning segmentation and registration of MRI and 3D ultrasound, integrated into a C++/MITK surgical simulation platform
patient_population: pregnancies with twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome, imaged with MRI and 3D ultrasound
clinical_problem: planning minimally invasive fetoscopic laser surgery for twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome, a technically difficult operation with a steep learning curve where untreated cases carry 90% perinatal mortality
model_description: The segmentation is in service of a surgical rehearsal: mother's soft tissue, uterus, umbilical cords, placenta and its vascular tree are segmented and registered automatically, then rendered as an intrauterine environment where the surgeon can simulate the fetoscope view, choose the entry point and practise the laser ablation before the operation. For a procedure this rare and this difficult, rehearsal on the actual patient's anatomy is the intervention. Experienced surgeons rated it highly in a usability study.
journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
title: TTTS-GPS: Patient-specific preoperative planning and simulation platform for twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome fetal surgery.
study_design: software platform development with usability study
headline_result: the first twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome fetal surgery planning and simulation platform, rated highly by experienced surgeons in a comprehensive usability study

model_family: convolutional network trained against gradient vector flow to derive an external force field for active contour models
patient_population: three clinical applications: fetal head in ultrasound, optic disk in fundus images and fluid in retinal OCT
clinical_problem: the sensitivity of gradient vector flow - the standard external force in active contour segmentation - to noise and false edges, which limits where snakes can be used
model_description: A hybrid rather than a replacement: the classical active contour machinery is kept, and only the external force - the part that fails on noisy images - is learned, using the classical force as the training reference. Fetal head ultrasound is one of three evaluation tasks and the noisiest of them, which is where the substitution should matter most. The other two applications are ophthalmic and outside this database's scope.
title: Deriving external forces via convolutional neural networks for biomedical image segmentation.
headline_result: competitive performance against state-of-the-art algorithms across all three segmentation tasks including fetal head ultrasound

model_family: J48 pruned decision tree classifier over diffusion MRI structural connectome attributes, ten-fold cross-validated
patient_population: 30 depressed adolescents treated with three months of cognitive behavioral therapy, with baseline diffusion MRI connectomes and 21 attributes including baseline depression score, age and sex
clinical_problem: which depressed adolescents will improve with cognitive behavioral therapy - a first-line treatment that many do not respond to, with treatment planning currently unguided by biology
model_description: Treatment selection rather than diagnosis, which is the more useful question and the rarer one in this literature. The deliberate choice of a small pruned decision tree over a black box pays off - the final tree has three attributes and puts right thalamus node strength at the centre, a finding then corroborated by a direct correlation with symptom change. Thirty adolescents, so this is a hypothesis with an accuracy attached rather than a validated predictor.
title: Application of machine learning to structural connectome to predict symptom reduction in depressed adolescents with cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT).
headline_result: 83% accuracy predicting depressive symptom reduction after three months of cognitive behavioral therapy, from a three-attribute tree centred on right thalamus node strength

clinical_problem: automatically screening for fetal head abnormalities (microcephaly, dolichocephaly) from ultrasound biometric measures
model_description: an SVM classifier takes morphological and biometric features from fetal head ultrasound as input and outputs a classification of normal vs. abnormal (microcephaly/dolichocephaly) cases
title: Supervised classification approach of biometric measures for automatic fetal defect screening in head ultrasound images.

model_family: multi-task faster region-based CNN with shared convolutional trunk
patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound
clinical_problem: deciding whether a fetal head ultrasound image is good enough to measure from, before anyone measures from it
model_description: Detects the key anatomical structures of the fetal head, checks whether the image magnification is appropriate, and scores the plane against clinical protocol, all from one network with a shared feature trunk and task-specific heads. It returns a verdict in under half a second, which is fast enough to be useful during the scan rather than after it. Prior clinical rules are folded in to hold down false detections.
title: Multi-task learning for quality assessment of fetal head ultrasound images.
dataset_size: an institutional dataset; size not stated
headline_result: quality assessment of an ultrasound plane in under half a second, comparable with state-of-the-art methods

model_family: classical classifiers - diagonal quadratic discriminant analysis, k-nearest neighbour, random forest, naive Bayes and RBF networks - plus bagging and AdaBoost ensembles of them
patient_population: fetuses of widespread gestational ages imaged with brain MRI
clinical_problem: classifying fetal brain abnormalities on MRI before birth, across a wide span of gestational ages rather than at one fixed age
model_description: Pre-deep-learning in method but pointed in framing: most work on early brain abnormality classification had been done on newborns and premature infants, and this pushes the same question back before birth and across gestational ages rather than at a single one. Handcrafted features with a bank of classical classifiers and ensembles compared against their base models; k-nearest neighbour won.
title: Fetal Brain Abnormality Classification from MRI Images of Different Gestational Age.
headline_result: highest accuracy and AUC around 95% using the k-nearest neighbour classifier

model_family: machine-learning classifier on a routine biomarker signature
patient_population: 590 children and adolescents aged 0-17 with suspected appendicitis at a Berlin hospital (473 histologically confirmed, 117 negative)
clinical_problem: deciding whether a child with abdominal pain has appendicitis, and whether it is complicated
model_description: Combines the appendiceal diameter measured on ultrasound with the full blood count and C-reactive protein, all of which are obtained routinely anyway, and returns a diagnosis of appendicitis. The framing is investigator-independent: no expert interpretation is needed. Discrimination of appendicitis from no appendicitis is good; separating complicated from uncomplicated inflammation, the decision that would actually change management toward antibiotics, is not.
title: Diagnosis and classification of pediatric acute appendicitis by artificial intelligence methods: An investigator-independent approach.
dataset_size: 590 patients, with at most 35% used for discovery and training
headline_result: 90% accuracy for appendicitis (93% sensitivity, 67% specificity); only 51% accuracy for identifying complicated inflammation

patient_population: 130 children with cerebral palsy, multicenter cohort in west China (planned)
clinical_problem: predicting individualized response to rehabilitation treatment in children with cerebral palsy using MRI radiomics combined with clinical data

journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
title: Treatment response prediction of rehabilitation program in children with cerebral palsy using radiomics strategy: protocol for a multicenter prospective cohort study in west China.
study_design: study protocol for a multicenter prospective cohort study (radiomics-based treatment-response prediction)

model_family: image analysis + machine learning-based pedicle detector
patient_population: 149 healthy and adolescent idiopathic scoliosis subjects; validation cohort of 11 healthy (age 6-33) and 46 AIS (age 6-16) subjects
clinical_problem: automating measurement of vertebral axial rotation (a scoliosis severity marker) from frontal spine X-rays by automatically locating the pedicles
model_description: Input: frontal spine radiographs; output: automatically detected pedicle landmarks used to calculate vertebral axial rotation (Stokes method), combining image analysis, machine learning and minimal manual input.
journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
title: Vertebral rotation estimation from frontal X-rays using a quasi-automated pedicle detection method.
study_design: retrospective method development and validation against manual annotation
dataset_size: 149 subjects (development); validation set of 11 healthy + 46 AIS subjects
headline_result: pedicle localization precision 84%, mean difference 1.2±1.2 mm; VAR signed difference -0.2±3.4°

model_family: semi-supervised framework pairing supervised CNN feature learning with deep embedded clustering, implemented on a 3D densely connected fully convolutional network
patient_population: isointense-phase infant brain MRI, alongside MNIST and SVHN benchmark classification tasks
clinical_problem: the cost of expert annotation in medical image segmentation, demonstrated on isointense infant brain MRI tissue segmentation, where the labels are especially expensive because white and gray matter look alike at 6-8 months
model_description: A semi-supervised method with a design property that matters more than its accuracy: it needs few hyperparameters, so it does not require the large labeled validation set that most semi-supervised algorithms quietly assume - which defeats the purpose when labels are the scarce resource. Validated on standard benchmarks and then on the isointense infant segmentation problem, where it beat both supervised-only training and pseudo-labelling.
journal: IEEE access : practical innovations, open solutions
title: Semi Supervised Learning with Deep Embedded Clustering for Image Classification and Segmentation.
dataset_size: not stated for the infant MRI task
headline_result: significant improvement over supervised-only training and over pseudo-labelling for isointense infant brain MRI tissue segmentation; 0.46% error on MNIST with 1000 labels and 4.43% on SVHN with 500

model_family: test-time augmentation for CNN segmentation uncertainty
patient_population: fetuses imaged with MRI; brain tumor MRI is used as a second test case
clinical_problem: knowing when to distrust an automated fetal brain segmentation
model_description: A way of putting an uncertainty estimate on a segmentation: the same image is transformed several ways at test time and the spread of the resulting segmentations is treated as image-based uncertainty, formalized as Monte Carlo sampling over an image acquisition model. Applied to fetal brain and brain tumor MRI, it flags overconfident wrong predictions better than dropout-based model uncertainty alone.
title: Aleatoric uncertainty estimation with test-time augmentation for medical image segmentation with convolutional neural networks.
headline_result: better uncertainty estimation than test-time dropout alone, and higher accuracy than single-prediction segmentation

model_family: linear kernel support vector machine with inter-site cross-validation
patient_population: 190 male children ages 6.5-13 (102 with ASD, 88 typically developing) from the ABIDE multi-site public dataset
clinical_problem: distinguishing children with autism spectrum disorder from typically developing children using resting-state functional connectivity, across multiple imaging sites
model_description: Input is resting-state fMRI functional connectivity between brain regions; a linear-kernel SVM classifies children as ASD or typically developing, trained on data from some sites and cross-validated on held-out sites.
title: Evaluation of Altered Functional Connections in Male Children With Autism Spectrum Disorders on Multiple-Site Data Optimized With Machine Learning.
study_design: retrospective multi-site public-dataset case-control classification study
dataset_size: 190 male children (102 with ASD, 88 typically developing)
headline_result: mean classification AUC 0.75+/-0.05; best site combination AUC 0.83

model_family: logistic/linear regression with exhaustive feature selection (statistical learning)
patient_population: 66 VLBW preterm infants imaged near-term; 52/66 completed gait follow-up at 18-22 months
clinical_problem: predicting future gait impairment in toddlers born very-low-birth-weight preterm from near-term brain white-matter microstructure on diffusion tensor imaging
model_description: Input: near-term diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) of 48 bilateral and corpus callosum white-matter regions; output: predicted risk of gait impairment at toddler age, via regression with exhaustive feature selection and leave-one-out cross-validation.
title: Prediction of Gait Impairment in Toddlers Born Preterm From Near-Term Brain Microstructure Assessed With DTI, Using Exhaustive Feature Selection and Cross-Validation.
study_design: prospective cohort study with statistical learning models and leave-one-out cross-validation
headline_result: logistic regression: 93%/79% sensitivity/specificity for gait velocity; up to 100%/100% for single-limb support

clinical_problem: Distinguishing neonatal acute bilirubin encephalopathy from normal myelination using MRI radiomics features.
model_description: Radiomics texture features extracted from T1-weighted MRI regions of interest are fed into multiple machine learning classifiers (decision tree, SVM, etc.) to distinguish ABE from normal myelination.
title: Machine Learning Assisted MRI Characterization for Diagnosis of Neonatal Acute Bilirubin Encephalopathy.
headline_result: Best AUC 0.946 (decision tree)

clinical_problem: screening adolescents for idiopathic scoliosis without radiographs and without unnecessary referrals
model_description: The input is an unclothed photograph of the back, not a radiograph, which is the point: current school screening has such low positive predictive value that it sends many children for radiographs they did not need. The algorithms detect scoliosis, flag curves of 20 degrees or more, and grade severity, with the aim of triaging who actually needs imaging and of following untreated cases without repeated radiation.
title: Development and validation of deep learning algorithms for scoliosis screening using back images.
headline_result: accuracy superior to human specialists for detecting scoliosis, for detecting curves of 20 degrees or more, and for severity grading

patient_population: 343 infant MRI scans, newborns to 48 months old
clinical_problem: Automatically extracting the brain from surrounding tissue (skull stripping) on infant brain MRI, since existing methods are tuned to adult anatomy
model_description: Input: infant brain MRI images; output: skull-stripped brain segmentation mask, via a flattened residual CNN with a boundary loss and an artifact simulator for augmentation
journal: Proceedings. IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging
title: FRNET: FLATTENED RESIDUAL NETWORK FOR INFANT MRI SKULL STRIPPING.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and internal testing

patient_population: infant subjects with risk of ASD, around 24 months of age (NDAR)
clinical_problem: developing an early imaging biomarker for autism spectrum disorder via amygdala/hippocampal subfield volumes in infancy
model_description: A dilated-dense U-Net automatically segments the amygdala and hippocampal subfields from infant brain MRI to enable volumetric analysis linked to autism spectrum disorder risk.
journal: Proceedings. IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging
title: A PRELIMINARY VOLUMETRIC MRI STUDY OF AMYGDALA AND HIPPOCAMPAL SUBFIELDS IN AUTISM DURING INFANCY.

patient_population: 90 neonates
clinical_problem: parcellating the cortical surface of neonatal brain MRI into anatomically meaningful regions
model_description: Spherical convolution, pooling and upsampling operations extend CNNs (U-Net and SegNet architectures) to spherical cortical surface meshes, taking neonatal cortical surface data as input and outputting a parcellation into anatomical regions.
journal: Proceedings. IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging
title: SPHERICAL U-NET FOR INFANT CORTICAL SURFACE PARCELLATION.
headline_result: Outperformed spherical SegNet and a prior patch-wise classification method (no single number reported in abstract)

clinical_problem: automated bone age assessment for young children using the carpal bone region
model_description: a regression CNN takes the carpal bone region of interest from a left-hand wrist radiograph as input and outputs a predicted bone age
title: Skeletal bone age assessments for young children based on regression convolutional neural networks.
headline_result: average discrepancy 2.75 months from clinical assessment; accuracy within 6 months 90.15% (male), within 1 year 99.43%

clinical_problem: Predicting persistent post-concussion symptom recovery in children using structural and functional brain MRI markers of the default mode network.

journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
title: Default mode network anatomy and function is linked to pediatric concussion recovery.
headline_result: AUC 0.86 predicting clinical outcome at follow-up

model_description: Radiomic features extracted from T2-weighted placental MRI, combined with clinical variables, go in; a nomogram model outputs predicted risk of postpartum hemorrhage.

study_design: multicentre retrospective radiomics study with external validation
headline_result: AUC 0.888 training, 0.832 external validation

model_family: two convolutional networks - one selecting the most informative slices of an MRI sequence, one estimating age from them - with GoogLeNet pretrained on ImageNet performing best
patient_population: 402 volunteers aged 14-21 years (221 male, 181 female) imaged with knee MRI
clinical_problem: age assessment in the range where hand bone age saturates and the growth zones close (14-21 years), for clinical use and for legal age estimation where documents are lacking - without ionizing radiation
model_description: Targets the specific age band where hand radiographs stop being informative, using the knee, whose growth plates close later - and does it on MRI, which matters because the legal use of age assessment on undocumented young people cannot ethically justify irradiating them. The result is reported at the threshold that actually gets contested, 18 years, where accuracy was 98.1% for males and 95.0% for females. A first network selecting which slices to use is a sensible answer to sequence-level input.
title: Age Assessment of Youth and Young Adults Using Magnetic Resonance Imaging of the Knee: A Deep Learning Approach.
headline_result: mean absolute error 0.793 years for males aged 14-20.5 and 0.988 years for females aged 14-19.5; 98.1% and 95.0% accuracy classifying minors at the 18-year threshold

clinical_problem: classifying autism spectrum disorder from resting-state fMRI
model_description: ASD-DiagNet takes resting-state fMRI connectivity features and jointly trains an autoencoder with a single-layer-perceptron classifier to distinguish individuals with autism spectrum disorder from healthy controls. A linear-interpolation data-augmentation strategy generates synthetic training examples, and the method was evaluated on the public ABIDE dataset (1,035 subjects, 17 imaging centers). Code and trained model are released publicly.
release_evidence: "The implemented code is available as GPL license on GitHub portal of our lab (https://github.com/pcdslab/ASD-DiagNet)"
title: ASD-DiagNet: A Hybrid Learning Approach for Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using fMRI Data.
study_design: retrospective multi-site classification study using a public dataset
headline_result: Up to 28% increase in classification accuracy over prior state-of-the-art methods, maximum accuracy 82%, and much faster runtime (40 min vs. 7 h)

model_family: convolutional neural network for intracranial volume segmentation

model_description: Deliberately trained and tested across the heterogeneity that usually breaks these tools - three axes of acquisition variation, a 22-week age span, and four different pathologies - and the Dice range of 0.98 to 0.99 across all of it is the claim. That robustness is what makes it usable as a generic preprocessing step rather than a study-specific one, which is how the authors position it.
title: Automatic extraction of the intracranial volume in fetal and neonatal MR scans using convolutional neural networks.
headline_result: Dice 0.98 to 0.99 across neonatal and fetal scans regardless of acquisition parameters or patient pathology

patient_population: 225 fetuses, 16-30 weeks of gestation (planned enrollment)
clinical_problem: Assessing whether automated 3D ultrasound image-recognition software can reduce variability in fetal biometric measurements (head/abdominal circumference, femur length) used to estimate gestational age and monitor fetal growth
model_description: Automated software extracts standard reference planes from 3D ultrasound volumes of the fetal head, abdomen, and femur and computes biometric measurements automatically, to be compared with manual 2D ultrasound measurements for agreement and reproducibility.
title: Optimization of Fetal Biometry With 3D Ultrasound and Image Recognition (EPICEA): protocol for a prospective cross-sectional study.
study_design: prospective cross-sectional study protocol (trial registration NCT03812471)

model_family: YOLOv3-based detector that localizes the right abdomen and classifies it
patient_population: 681 children aged 5 years or under (242 with intussusception) imaged March 2005 to December 2017 for training, and 75 children (25 with intussusception) from January to August 2018 for validation, with ultrasound as the reference standard
clinical_problem: screening for ileocolic intussusception on the abdominal radiograph, which is usually the first imaging a young child with suspected intussusception receives and which is insensitive when read by eye
model_description: Built around a clinical observation rather than a generic classifier: intussusception lives in the right abdomen, so the detector is trained to find that rectangle first and judge it second. The result is the one worth carrying - the algorithm's sensitivity was 0.76 against the radiologists' 0.46 on the same films, with no loss of specificity. Radiographs miss most intussusceptions when read conventionally, which is why the comparison is so lopsided and why a screening aid here has real value.
title: Performance of deep learning-based algorithm for detection of ileocolic intussusception on abdominal radiographs of young children.
study_design: retrospective model development with temporal validation and reader comparison
headline_result: sensitivity 0.76 for the algorithm versus 0.46 for radiologists (p = 0.013), with specificity 0.96 versus 0.92 (p = 0.32)

dataset_size: 87 echocardiography videos (2,216 images) from Shenzhen Children's Hospital

model_family: convolutional network trained to predict sonographer gaze by visual saliency prediction or gaze-point regression, then transferred to standard plane detection
patient_population: a gaze tracking dataset of sonographers performing routine clinical fetal anomaly screening
clinical_problem: learning transferable image representations without manual class labels, which are in any case a simplistic approximation of how a sonographer understands an image
model_description: Argues that class labels throw away most of what an expert knows, and that where they look is a richer and free signal. The evaluation is careful in a way that matters: besides fine-tuning, the authors train a simple softmax on each layer's activations, which measures the representation itself rather than the transfer hyperparameters - and finds the attention-derived features approach a fully supervised baseline at every layer but the last. The largest fine-tuning gain was on the cardiac planes, which are the hardest.
title: Ultrasound Image Representation Learning by Modeling Sonographer Visual Attention
dataset_size: a unique sonographer gaze tracking dataset
headline_result: fine-tuning the saliency predictor beat random initialization by 9.6% F1 overall and 15.3% for the cardiac planes, with layer-wise representations approaching a fully supervised baseline

model_family: convolutional networks with activation and prediction visualization tools
patient_population: pediatric chest radiographs
clinical_problem: pneumonia detection in children's chest radiographs, and the opacity of the models proposed to do it - a bottleneck for screening in the field where poorly interpreted model behaviour would drive decisions

It also makes the point that pediatric pneumonia is poorly studied relative to adult pneumonia, which is the recurring theme of this whole database.
title: Visualizing and explaining deep learning predictions for pneumonia detection in pediatric chest radiographs
headline_result: demonstration that visualizing and explaining CNN activations for pediatric chest radiograph pneumonia detection helps reduce bias, overfitting and generalization error

model_family: residual networks trained with a Discriminant Analysis Loss Function that minimizes within-class and maximizes between-class variance without eigen-decomposition
patient_population: the pediatric pneumonia chest X-ray dataset
clinical_problem: pneumonia classification on pediatric chest radiographs, used here as the medical test bed for a new representation-learning objective

The contribution is computational as much as conceptual - earlier discriminant-analysis losses required eigen-decomposition and matrix inversion, and avoiding both makes the objective usable inside a deep network. Reported to beat the results published with the dataset itself, at 96.63% accuracy with the usual asymmetry between sensitivity (99.2%) and specificity (92.3%).
journal: 2019 53rd Annual Conference on Information Sciences and Systems (CISS)
title: Discriminant Analysis Deep Neural Networks
headline_result: 96.63% accuracy with sensitivity 99.23% and specificity 92.30% on the pediatric pneumonia dataset, better than the results published with the dataset

model_family: comparison of 2D and 2D+t CNNs, LSTM and convolutional LSTM in a multi-stream framework for spatio-temporal video analysis

Short- and long-term temporal contributions are ablated, with the multi-stream combination winning.

title: Spatio-Temporal Partitioning And Description Of Full-Length Routine Fetal Anomaly Ultrasound Scans
headline_result: top-1 accuracy 0.77 and top-3 accuracy 0.94, with automated workflow statistics on unlabelled scans correlating with manually labelled videos at rho = 0.95 (p = 0.0004)

patient_population: the RSNA pediatric bone age dataset
clinical_problem: bone age assessment from hand radiographs, where whole-image models are distracted by everything in the film that is not hand

The attention maps double as visual support for the prediction, which is what makes the output arguable rather than opaque.
journal: 2019 IEEE 16th International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI 2019)
title: Residual Attention Based Network for Hand Bone Age Assessment
dataset_size: the RSNA pediatric bone age dataset
headline_result: superior performance to previous methods on the RSNA pediatric bone age dataset, with attention maps as visual support for each prediction

model_family: flattened residual network with a boundary loss for ambiguous low-contrast regions and an artifact simulator for augmentation
patient_population: 343 subjects from newborn to 48 months
clinical_problem: skull stripping infant brain MRI, where the brain is small and tissue intensities change rapidly through the early months, so methods built for adults fail
model_description: Three responses to three specific failures: a simplified architecture for robustness, a boundary loss aimed exactly at the ambiguous brain/non-brain interface that low contrast produces in infants, and an artifact simulator so the model sees poor-quality images during training rather than meeting them first at deployment. Tested across the whole 0-48 month range and reported to beat the state of the art in every age band, which matters because infant methods often work at one age and not another.
journal: 2019 IEEE 16th International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI 2019)
title: Frnet: Flattened Residual Network for Infant MRI Skull Stripping
headline_result: better than state-of-the-art skull stripping in all age groups across a 343-subject dataset spanning newborns to 48-month-olds

model_family: ensemble of random forest, XGBoost and LightGBM over cubic-spline-fitted characteristics extracted from ultrasound reports
patient_population: 4212 intrapartum recordings
clinical_problem: estimating fetal weight, where ultrasound-based estimation varies between populations, demands strict operating technique from the sonographer and is unavailable in low-resource areas - and where inaccurate estimates cause adverse perinatal outcomes
model_description: Works on ultrasound-derived biometric characteristics across gestation rather than on images, fitting each with a cubic spline so the model sees a trajectory rather than a snapshot - which is what distinguishes it from the biometry formulas it competes with. The proposed intersection-over-union evaluation acknowledges that fetal weight estimation produces a range rather than a point. Positioned partly as a self-monitoring tool for pregnant women, which is a strong claim on this evidence.
journal: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
title: Ensemble Machine Learning for Estimating Fetal Weight at Varying Gestational Age
headline_result: intersection-over-union of 0.64 with the ultrasound-derived weight range, improving estimation accuracy by 12% and reducing mean relative error by 3% compared with the ultrasound method

patient_population: 10,289 skeletal age examinations, 8,909 from one institution's archive and 1,383 from the public Digital Hand Atlas
