model_description: Argues, and demonstrates, that a network designed and trained from scratch for the specific task can beat transfer learning from natural images, given a large enough institutional dataset. Training is split into four cohorts by sex and age band, which reflects how Greulich and Pyle is applied in practice. Testing uses 20 radiographs per one-year age cohort rather than a random split, so performance is visible across the age range instead of averaged over it.
title: MABAL: a Novel Deep-Learning Architecture for Machine-Assisted Bone Age Labeling.
dataset_size: 10,289 training images across four sex and age cohorts
headline_result: reported to outperform existing proposed bone age algorithms; figures not stated in the abstract

model_family: support vector machine classifier on neuroanatomical MRI features
patient_population: 967 healthy youth (Philadelphia Neurodevelopmental Cohort) for training/testing; 682 healthy youth (PING cohort) for independent validation
clinical_problem: predicting sex from neuroanatomical MRI features in youth to characterize sex-related brain differences
model_description: Input is regional cortical thickness and other neuroanatomical MRI features; output is an SVM classification of biological sex, trained on one multi-site youth cohort and independently validated on a second multi-site youth cohort.
title: Neuroanatomical morphometric characterization of sex differences in youth using statistical learning.
study_design: retrospective multi-cohort case-control MRI classification study
dataset_size: 967 youth (PNC, training/testing) plus 682 youth (PING, independent validation)
headline_result: 83% cross-validated accuracy on the PNC cohort; 77% accuracy on the independent PING validation cohort

model_family: random forest (machine learning) on CT/organ-derived features
patient_population: 37 recently treated children, 2-6 years old, with abdominal CT and organ delineations
clinical_problem: automatically finding, from a database of recently treated children, the patient most anatomically similar to a historically treated childhood cancer (Wilms' tumor) patient, to support individualized radiotherapy dose reconstruction
model_description: Input: CT scans and 3D organ delineations (liver, spleen, spinal cord, body contour); output: a predicted similarity ranking between patients, using random-forest models trained on historically recorded anatomical features.
title: On the feasibility of automatically selecting similar patients in highly individualized radiotherapy dose reconstruction for historic data of pediatric cancer survivors.
headline_result: random forest models of external-abdomen/organ-distance similarity achieved pseudo-R2 ≥0.69; most-similar patient correctly retrieved 22% of the time

patient_population: children undergoing chest radiography for suspected pneumonia; the primary cohort is adults with retinal OCT
clinical_problem: pediatric pneumonia on chest radiographs, and bacterial vs viral origin
model_description: A transfer-learning framework that takes a single image and returns a diagnostic label, with an occlusion map highlighting the regions that drove the decision. It was developed on retinal OCT images and then retrained on pediatric chest radiographs to separate normal from pneumonia and bacterial from viral pneumonia. The paper's argument is that a general transfer-learning recipe needs far less labelled data than training from scratch.
title: Identifying Medical Diagnoses and Treatable Diseases by Image-Based Deep Learning.
study_design: retrospective technical development with expert comparison
dataset_size: not stated in the abstract for the chest radiograph cohort
headline_result: performance comparable to human experts on the retinal task; the pediatric chest radiograph result is not quantified in the abstract

patient_population: pediatric craniosynostosis patients (review of published literature)
clinical_problem: reviewing technological advances (including imaging diagnostics and machine learning) for diagnosing and managing craniosynostosis in children
model_description: Systematic review of 21 novel technologies for craniosynostosis management, grouped as diagnostic imaging (n=6), surgical planning (n=4), cranial vault evaluation (n=4), machine learning (n=3), ultrasound pinning (n=3), and near-infrared spectroscopy (n=1); no single model described.
title: The State of Technology in Craniosynostosis.

patient_population: 140 fetal ultrasound volumes, gestational age 26.0 ± 4.4 weeks
clinical_problem: putting 3D fetal neurosonography volumes into a common reference frame despite arbitrary fetal position
model_description: Localizes the fetal brain, segments its structures, and aligns the volume to a reference coordinate system, all from one network with shared features and task-specific outputs. The coordinate system is defined anatomically from the skull boundary, eye sockets and head pose predicted from intracranial structures, which is what makes alignment robust to how the fetus happens to be lying.
title: Fully-automated alignment of 3D fetal brain ultrasound to a canonical reference space using multi-task learning.
headline_result: high brain overlap and low eye localization error on co-alignment, independent of gestational age or head size

patient_population: 43 fetuses with postnatally confirmed congenital aqueductal stenosis and 32 fetuses with ventriculomegaly from other causes
clinical_problem: predicting a postnatal diagnosis of congenital aqueductal stenosis from prenatal MRI findings in fetuses with ventriculomegaly
model_description: Anatomic findings on prenatal MRI (ventricular size, aqueduct findings, corpus callosum appearance) go in; univariate and random forest multivariate analysis output predictors of a postnatal diagnosis of congenital aqueductal stenosis.
title: Congenital Aqueductal Stenosis: Findings at Fetal MRI That Accurately Predict a Postnatal Diagnosis.
study_design: retrospective single-center fetal MRI diagnostic-accuracy study
dataset_size: 43 cases of confirmed congenital aqueductal stenosis, 32 controls with ventriculomegaly from other causes
headline_result: specific MRI findings (enlarged ventricular recesses, aqueduct funneling, abnormal corpus callosum) identified as significant predictors on multivariate random forest analysis

clinical_problem: automatically segmenting key fetal brain structures (corpus callosum, choroid plexus) on ultrasound for standardized biometry
model_description: a region-based descriptor learning approach takes fetal neurosonography images as input and outputs segmentation of the corpus callosum and choroid plexus
title: Learning to segment key clinical anatomical structures in fetal neurosonography informed by a region-based descriptor.

clinical_problem: Editorial commentary on the application and promise of deep learning in pediatric radiology
model_description: Editorial/commentary discussing deep learning applications in pediatric radiology (no abstract available)
title: Deep Learning Lends a Hand to Pediatric Radiology.

patient_population: 472 Uyghur teenagers (245 male, 227 female), aged 13.0-19.0 years
clinical_problem: Automated bone age assessment from left-wrist radiographs in adolescents, for forensic medicine age estimation
model_description: An AlexNet-based deep learning regression model trained on digital left-wrist radiographs to automatically estimate bone age/chronological age in Uyghur adolescents.
title: [Automated Assessment for Bone Age of Left Wrist Joint in Uyghur Teenagers by Deep Learning].
study_design: Retrospective single-center model development and validation study
headline_result: Test-set accuracy within +/-1.0 year: 79.5% (male), 79.4% (female)

model_family: three view-based convolutional networks predicting 2D projections of structures onto anatomical views, plus a 3D CNN skull-stripping tool
patient_population: 3D fetal neurosonography volumes
clinical_problem: locating key brain structures in 3D fetal neurosonography, which is used clinically to detect cerebral abnormalities and assess growth but which requires expertise and is tedious even then
model_description: The design imitates how a sonographer works a volume - looking at three orthogonal views rather than reasoning in 3D - and that choice is also what makes it fit in GPU memory at full resolution. The satisfying result is that the model pinpoints structures in 3D despite each stream only ever being supervised in 2D. Compared head to head with random forest and 3D U-Net baselines, and paired with a skull-stripping network so the pipeline takes a raw volume and needs no human step.
title: VP-Nets : Efficient automatic localization of key brain structures in 3D fetal neurosonography.
headline_result: center deviation 1.8 +/- 1.4 mm, size difference 1.9 +/- 1.5 mm and 3D IoU 63.2 +/- 14.7%, consistently outperforming random forest and 3D U-Net baselines

model_family: deep belief network on combined functional and structural features
patient_population: 185 children aged 5-10 from the ABIDE I and II datasets (116 with autism, 69 controls)
clinical_problem: diagnosing autism spectrum disorder in young children, where early diagnosis changes what intervention is possible
model_description: Combines resting-state functional MRI with gray and white matter measures over anatomically labelled regions and learns a joint representation with a deep belief network, on the argument that earlier work used only shallow hand-computed features. Deliberately restricted to 5-10 year olds because that is where diagnosis matters. The accuracy is modest and the specificity is poor, which the numbers make plain.
title: Combination of rs-fMRI and sMRI Data to Discriminate Autism Spectrum Disorders in Young Children Using Deep Belief Network.
study_design: technical development on a public dataset
headline_result: 65.56% accuracy (sensitivity 84%, specificity 33%, F1 74.76%) by 10-fold cross-validation

model_family: voxel-based morphometry feeding logistic regression, random forest and support vector machine classifiers, five-fold cross-validated
patient_population: 60 adolescents with conduct disorder and 60 age-matched healthy controls
clinical_problem: whether the structural brain alterations reported in conduct disorder are large and consistent enough to identify an individual adolescent, rather than only to differ at group level
model_description: Asks the right follow-up question to a group-difference literature - can these differences classify a person - and answers it with three classifiers that all land in the same range, which is reassuring against one model being overfitted. Eight regions across frontal, parietal, cingulate, cerebellar, lingual and insular areas carry the signal. Accuracy near 80% in 120 adolescents is a group-level effect strong enough to notice but not a diagnostic test, and the authors call the features potential biomarkers rather than a tool.
title: Distinguishing Adolescents With Conduct Disorder From Typically Developing Youngsters Based on Pattern Classification of Brain Structural MRI.
headline_result: accuracy 77.9-80.4%, sensitivity 75.4-87.5%, specificity 73.3-80.4% and AUC 0.76-0.80 across three classifiers

model_family: three-dimensional convolutional neural networks combined with neonatal structural brain segmentation
patient_population: term infants born with congenital heart disease, neonatal MRI, ten-fold cross-validation
clinical_problem: detecting cerebellar dysplasia - a subtle form of brain dysmaturation - in term infants born with congenital heart disease, where no reliable automated diagnostic tool exists and volume alone does not make the diagnosis
model_description: Takes on the two things that usually stop deep learning working on neonatal MRI - small samples and structures that are barely differentiated by signal intensity - by pairing the network with an explicit structural segmentation. The class activation maps then do real scientific work rather than serving as a plausibility check: they localize the discriminating signal to the superior cerebellar surface, posterior lobe and midline vermis, which the authors connect to genetic mechanisms and neurodevelopmental outcome. Code released under the BSD licence.
release_evidence: the code developed for this project is open source, published under the BSD License and designed to be generalizable
title: A computational framework for the detection of subcortical brain dysmaturation in neonatal MRI using 3D Convolutional Neural Networks.
headline_result: classification accuracy 0.985 +/- 0.024 for subtle cerebellar dysplasia in congenital heart disease under ten-fold cross-validation

model_family: joint generalized additive model and machine-learning classifier
patient_population: 705 adolescents from the NCANDA baseline cohort
clinical_problem: identifying brain structural patterns associated with adolescent alcohol misuse while controlling for confounding factors
model_description: Takes macrostructural MRI and microstructural diffusion tensor imaging metrics as input and outputs a classification of high- versus low-drinking adolescents, using a joint machine-learning model that simultaneously removes confounding factors and identifies cohort-specific neuromorphometric patterns.
title: Alcohol use effects on adolescent brain development revealed by simultaneously removing confounding factors, identifying morphometric patterns, and classifying individuals.
study_design: retrospective cross-sectional cohort study with machine-learning classification
headline_result: an eight-brain-region pattern classified high-drinking adolescents more accurately than regions identified by alternative approaches

patient_population: Contrast-enhanced NCAP CT scans from adult and pediatric patients
clinical_problem: Fully automated classification of trunk tissues (lung, fat, muscle, solid organ, blood/bowel contrast, bone) on contrast-enhanced CT, including distinguishing bone from contrast
model_description: A random forest classifier trained on 28 2D and 12 3D image filters plus one spatial feature assigns each CT voxel to one of six tissue classes (lung, fat, muscle, solid organ, blood/bowel contrast, bone)
title: Fully automated tissue classifier for contrast-enhanced CT scans of adult and pediatric patients.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and validation study
dataset_size: 28 training CT scans (4 adult, 3 pediatric) plus 70 additional manually classified images; tested on 21 manually classified slices
headline_result: Dice similarity coefficients ranged 0.90 (bone) to 0.98 (lung) at trained locations

model_family: machine learning (unspecified) combined with a computational hemodynamics model
patient_population: pregnant women 22-34 weeks gestation in a peri-urban settlement near Karachi, Pakistan
clinical_problem: predicting fetuses at increased risk of stillbirth and adverse perinatal outcomes from Doppler ultrasound flow patterns
model_description: Input (planned): Doppler ultrasound waveforms of fetal cardiovascular, cerebral and placental flow combined with maternal clinical data; output (planned): a machine-learning-based prediction of risk for stillbirth and other adverse perinatal outcomes. Study protocol; no results yet reported.
release_evidence: study protocol, prospective cohort just beginning enrollment; no completed model reported
title: Machine learning from fetal flow waveforms to predict adverse perinatal outcomes: a study protocol.

model_family: stacked sparse autoencoder for feature selection with a support vector machine classifier
patient_population: 28 infants born at 23-31 weeks without brain injury, scanned at term-equivalent age; features pretrained on 884 subjects from a public database
clinical_problem: identifying at term-equivalent age which very preterm infants will have cognitive deficits at 2 years
model_description: Learns a compressed representation of the functional connectome without labels, using a large public dataset, then uses that representation to predict 2-year cognitive outcome in a small preterm cohort. The transfer step is the point: neonatal cohorts are too small to train a deep model directly. Frontal lobe and somatosensory regions contributed most. The authors present it explicitly as proof of concept given the sample size.
title: Early prediction of cognitive deficits in very preterm infants using functional connectome data in an artificial neural network framework.
dataset_size: 884 subjects for unsupervised pretraining; 28 very preterm infants for prediction
headline_result: 70.6% accuracy and AUC 0.76 for cognitive deficit at 2 years corrected age

model_family: CNN with image-specific fine tuning inside a bounding-box and scribble pipeline
patient_population: fetuses imaged with MRI; a second application uses brain tumor MRI
clinical_problem: outlining fetal organs on MRI when only some organ classes were annotated for training
model_description: The radiologist draws a bounding box, and optionally scribbles, and the network segments the structure inside it, fine-tuning itself on that specific image before producing the final contour. Because it adapts per image, it can outline organ classes that were never annotated during training. Demonstrated on fetal MRI organs and on brain tumor MRI.
title: Interactive Medical Image Segmentation Using Deep Learning With Image-Specific Fine Tuning.
headline_result: more robust than state-of-the-art CNNs on unseen object classes, with fewer user interactions and less user time than traditional interactive segmentation

model_family: supervised machine-learning brain-age regression on T1-weighted MRI
patient_population: 953 healthy children aged 3-21 for model development; 275 clinically high-risk individuals (39 of whom developed psychosis) and 109 controls aged 12-21 for application
clinical_problem: identifying which clinically high-risk adolescents will convert to psychosis
model_description: A model trained on structural MRI of healthy children to predict chronological age; the gap between that predicted age and the child's real age is then read as a measure of deviant neuroanatomical maturation. Applied to clinically high-risk adolescents, a larger gap was associated with higher risk of developing psychosis, but only in the younger part of the range.
title: Use of Machine Learning to Determine Deviance in Neuroanatomical Maturity Associated With Future Psychosis in Youths at Clinically High Risk.
dataset_size: 953 healthy children for training; 384 subjects for external validation and application
headline_result: clinically high-risk individuals showed a mean 0.64-year gap between predicted and chronological age versus controls (P = .008); greater deviation was associated with psychosis risk (P = .01)

model_family: convolutional network classifying anatomical landmarks, followed by a Hough transform to fit the circumference
patient_population: clinical ultrasound data from 56 pregnant women, with two experts providing acceptance judgments
clinical_problem: automating abdominal circumference measurement, the hardest of the standard fetal biometry parameters because the abdomen has low and non-uniform contrast against its surroundings and an irregular outline
model_description: Built around how the sonographer decides rather than around end-to-end regression: the network is trained to recognize the three landmarks that define an acceptable abdominal plane - stomach bubble, amniotic fluid and umbilical vein - and only then does a Hough transform fit the circle. That keeps the training requirement small and the failures interpretable. The paper names its failure modes plainly, which is unusual: an oversized fetus, absent amniotic fluid, or a distorted abdominal outline.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: Automatic Estimation of Fetal Abdominal Circumference From Ultrasound Images.
study_design: retrospective model development with expert acceptance check
headline_result: agreement of 0.809 and 0.771 with two experts, against 0.905 agreement between the two experts themselves; stable even on images degraded by shadowing

model_family: CNN regression predicting rigid transformations to a learned canonical atlas
patient_population: fetuses at around 20 weeks gestation, including heavily moving cases, plus simulated data
clinical_problem: initializing slice-to-volume registration for fetal MRI, where heavy in-utero motion breaks optimization-based methods
model_description: Predicts where an arbitrarily oriented 2D slice belongs in a canonical 3D atlas space from intensity alone, with no initialization. Conventional registration has a narrow capture range and needs a good starting estimate, which a heavily moving fetus does not provide; this removes that dependency and slots into a full reconstruction and motion compensation pipeline. It runs fast enough for real-time use.
title: 3-D Reconstruction in Canonical Co-Ordinate Space From Arbitrarily Oriented 2-D Images.
dataset_size: simulated MRI plus real fetal MRI data
headline_result: average spatial prediction error 7 mm on simulated data, with qualitatively improved reconstructions for heavily moving fetuses at around 20 weeks

model_family: L1-norm support vector machine, bi-objective optimization
patient_population: school-aged children with and without ADHD
clinical_problem: ADHD diagnosis from fMRI data
model_description: fMRI-derived features from children are input to an L1-norm support vector machine formulated as a bi-objective optimization that trades off margin of separation against empirical classification error, producing a family of candidate classifiers for ADHD diagnosis. The normal boundary intersection method is used to generate the trade-off curve, avoiding manual tuning of the regularization parameter.
title: Classification of ADHD with bi-objective optimization.

model_family: hybrid machine learning method on interregional morphological connectivity features derived from surface-based analysis, leave-one-out cross-validated
patient_population: children with ADHD and controls
clinical_problem: diagnosing ADHD in children from structural imaging, where previous models used regional features and reached limited accuracy
model_description: Changes the feature rather than the classifier: instead of the volume or thickness of each region taken separately, it constructs an individual's interregional morphological connectivity - how regions covary in shape within one brain - and shows that this significantly outperforms regional features on the same data. The identified altered connections involved insula, caudal anterior cingulate, frontal pole and postcentral cortex, and correlated with clinical symptoms, which is the check that keeps the features interpretable rather than merely discriminative.
title: Diagnostic model for attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder based on interregional morphological connectivity.
headline_result: total accuracy 74.65% with sensitivity 75% and specificity 74.29%, significantly better than a model built on regional features

patient_population: patients with pulmonary valve disease / congenital defects (children or adults)
clinical_problem: designing a patient-specific handmade trileaflet valve for pulmonary valve reconstruction in congenital heart disease
model_description: A generalized regression neural network predicts optimal trileaflet valve design parameters (width, length, curvature) from the main pulmonary artery diameter measured on CT pulmonary angiography, for patch-valved conduit reconstruction.
journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
title: Handmade trileaflet valve design and validation for patch-valved conduit reconstruction using generalized regression machine learning model.

patient_population: Pediatric ultrasound kidney images, CAKUT patients vs. normal controls (n not stated)
clinical_problem: Diagnosing congenital abnormalities of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT) in children from ultrasound kidney images using transfer-learning-derived imaging features
model_description: Input: ultrasound kidney images (with gradient and distance-transform feature maps); output: CAKUT vs. normal classification, via transfer-learning features from a pretrained deep CNN (AlexNet) combined with conventional imaging features and SVM classifiers
journal: Proceedings. IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging
title: TRANSFER LEARNING FOR DIAGNOSIS OF CONGENITAL ABNORMALITIES OF THE KIDNEY AND URINARY TRACT IN CHILDREN BASED ON ULTRASOUND IMAGING DATA.

model_family: random forest regression with conditional inference trees
patient_population: 21 children/adolescents with reactive attachment disorder (mean age 12.76) and 22 typically developing controls (mean age 12.95)
clinical_problem: identifying sensitive periods and types of childhood maltreatment associated with structural brain changes in reactive attachment disorder
model_description: Inputs are the type and timing (age) of childhood maltreatment events; a random forest regression with conditional inference trees ranks their relative importance for predicting reduced gray matter volume in the left primary visual cortex measured by voxel-based morphometry MRI.
title: Type and timing of childhood maltreatment and reduced visual cortex volume in children and adolescents with reactive attachment disorder.
study_design: cross-sectional case-control MRI study with random forest analysis
dataset_size: 21 children with reactive attachment disorder, 22 typically developing controls
headline_result: number of maltreatment types was the strongest predictor of visual cortex gray matter reduction; sensitive period identified at ages 5-7

patient_population: 34 pediatric patients with embryonal brain tumor
clinical_problem: using quantitative MRI radiomic features to characterize histology, metastasis risk and recurrence risk in pediatric embryonal brain tumors
model_description: Input: 3D radiomic features from preoperative T1 postcontrast and FLAIR MRI; output: associations/predictions of tumor histology, neuraxis metastasis, and recurrence.
journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
title: Clinical Applications of Quantitative 3-Dimensional MRI Analysis for Pediatric Embryonal Brain Tumors.
headline_result: Increased tumor size and decreased heterogeneity (FLAIR) associated with recurrence, AUC 0.7 for each

patient_population: fetal ultrasound images spanning all trimesters of pregnancy
clinical_problem: automated measurement of fetal head circumference on ultrasound to estimate gestational age and monitor fetal growth
model_description: A random forest classifier trained on Haar-like features locates the fetal skull in 2D ultrasound images; Hough transform, dynamic programming and ellipse fitting then output the fetal head circumference measurement.
title: Automated measurement of fetal head circumference using 2D ultrasound images.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and validation study
headline_result: mean difference from reference gestational age: 0.6±4.3, 0.4±4.7, 2.5±12.4 days (1st/2nd/3rd trimester), comparable to an experienced sonographer (0.8±2.6, -0.0±4.6, 1.9±11.0 days)

model_family: commercial automated plane identification and measurement software
patient_population: 30 fetuses at 17-30 weeks gestation, each with two 3D volumes and a conventional 2D image
clinical_problem: finding the transthalamic plane and measuring biparietal diameter and head circumference from a 3D volume rather than by hand
model_description: Extracts the standard measurement plane out of an acquired 3D volume and measures it, removing the operator's plane selection from the equation. Agreement with two experienced sonographers was good, and the confidence intervals quantify what automation costs: about 4 mm on biparietal diameter and 11 mm on head circumference against manual 2D measurement, which is the number to weigh against the reproducibility gain.
release_evidence: artificial intelligence software (Smartplanes)
title: Artificial intelligence assistance for fetal head biometry: Assessment of automated measurement software.
headline_result: intra- and interobserver ICC above 0.98; 95% confidence intervals 4 mm for biparietal diameter and 11 mm for head circumference between automated 3D and manual 2D measurement

model_family: several convolutional networks and a U-Net chained across three stages, with a Hough transform for the initial circumference fit
patient_population: clinical 2D fetal ultrasound data, validated against clinical measurements
clinical_problem: automating fetal abdominal circumference measurement and, separately, deciding whether the plane is acceptable to measure on at all
model_description: The fuller version of the same group's abdominal circumference work: the landmark classifier and Hough fit are joined by networks that locate the spine and the bone regions to refine the final circumference, and then by a U-Net and classifier that judge whether the image was a valid standard plane. Building the acceptance check into the pipeline is the part that makes it deployable - a measurement returned on the wrong plane is worse than no measurement.
title: Machine-learning-based automatic identification of fetal abdominal circumference from ultrasound images.
headline_result: Dice similarity for abdominal circumference measurement, with 87.10% accuracy on the fetal abdominal standard plane acceptance check

model_family: previously validated machine-learning classifier on CSF volume, brain volume, age and sex
patient_population: 159 children aged 2-4 with autism spectrum disorder (both simplex and multiplex families) and 77 with typical development
clinical_problem: whether extra-axial cerebrospinal fluid volume is an imaging marker of autism beyond infancy
model_description: Applies a classifier previously validated in infants to an independent cohort of 2-4 year olds, using extra-axial CSF volume together with brain volume, age and sex to separate children with autism from typically developing controls. The substantive finding is replication: the CSF excess is present in an independent sample, persists beyond infancy, and is the same in children with and without a family history.
title: Extra-axial cerebrospinal fluid in high-risk and normal-risk children with autism aged 2-4 years: a case-control study.
headline_result: 15.1% more extra-axial CSF in the autism group after adjustment (p = 0.007, Cohen's d 0.39)

model_family: deep convolutional neural networks of varying depth and architecture, some ImageNet-pretrained and some randomly initialized
patient_population: 882 children presenting to the emergency department with upper extremity trauma, 901 lateral elbow radiographs
clinical_problem: detecting traumatic joint effusion on lateral elbow radiographs, the indirect sign that often stands in for an occult pediatric fracture
model_description: A direct test of whether a small pediatric dataset is enough. Fewer than 700 training radiographs, transfer learning from ImageNet, and a hyperparameter search on 115 validation images produced a classifier that reads elbow effusion at roughly 91 percent sensitivity and specificity. The clinical framing matters more than the numbers: effusion is the finding that tells the emergency physician to treat a child as fractured when no fracture line is visible.
title: Detection of Traumatic Pediatric Elbow Joint Effusion Using a Deep Convolutional Neural Network.
headline_result: test-set AUC 0.943, sensitivity 0.909, specificity 0.906

model_family: deep features from three pre-trained convolutional networks combined by majority voting
patient_population: 33 retrospective pullbacks of intracoronary cross-sectional OCT images from pediatric patients with Kawasaki disease
clinical_problem: characterizing the intracoronary tissue changes caused by Kawasaki disease on optical coherence tomography, so that coronary involvement can be classified without expert manual interpretation of every cross-section
model_description: An unusual corner of pediatric imaging AI: intravascular OCT in the coronary arteries of children with Kawasaki disease, where the pathological formations differ from adult atherosclerosis and no reader has seen many of them. Rather than train from scratch on 33 cases, the authors take deep features from three ImageNet-pretrained networks and vote - the standard small-data recipe, applied to a disease that will never have a large dataset.
title: Characterization of coronary artery pathological formations from OCT imaging using deep learning.
headline_result: accuracy, sensitivity and specificity up to 0.99 +/- 0.01 per tissue class with the majority voting scheme

model_family: computer-assisted gray scale analysis with textural features and machine learning, compared against a standardized visual score
patient_population: 75 neonates admitted to the NICU for respiratory distress, with a 600-frame ultrasound dataset; oxygenation ratio and alveolar-arterial gradient as reference standards
clinical_problem: grading neonatal respiratory status from lung ultrasound at the cot side, against oxygenation as the reference, so that point-of-care ultrasound can substitute for blood gas sampling in the NICU
model_description: The comparison is against a trained human reading the same frames, and the humans win - visual scoring correlated better with both oxygenation indices than the texture analysis did, with near-perfect interobserver agreement. That is a useful negative for a literature full of claims in the other direction, and the authors read it correctly, presenting computer-assisted analysis as a route to point-of-care diagnostics rather than as an improvement on the expert eye. Region-of-interest size mattered to the texture result.
title: Visual assessment versus computer-assisted gray scale analysis in the ultrasound evaluation of neonatal respiratory status.
headline_result: visual scoring correlated with oxygenation at r = -0.55 and 0.59 (kappa 0.91 between observers) versus r = -0.35 to -0.42 and 0.46 to 0.58 for gray scale texture analysis

model_family: densely connected convolutional neural network (DenseNet-style CNN)
patient_population: 6- and 12-month-old infants from the Baby Connectome Project (BCP)
clinical_problem: automatic segmentation of infant cerebellar tissue for quantitative brain development studies
model_description: The model takes infant brain MRI as input and produces a tissue-level segmentation of the cerebellum. It is a densely connected convolutional neural network in which every layer receives feature maps from all preceding layers, intended to handle the weak tissue contrast, highly folded structure, and partial volume effects of the infant cerebellum. It was trained and evaluated on 6- and 12-month-old infant MRI from the Baby Connectome Project.
journal: Machine learning in medical imaging. MLMI (Workshop)
title: Automatic Accurate Infant Cerebellar Tissue Segmentation with Densely Connected Convolutional Network.
dataset_size: infant MRI from the Baby Connectome Project (BCP), 6- and 12-month-olds; exact number of scans not stated
headline_result: Superior performance compared with other state-of-the-art infant cerebellum segmentation methods (no specific metric value given)

model_family: CNN + support vector regression (SVR) with multiple kernel learning
patient_population: Two datasets of pediatric hand/wrist radiographs plus race and gender data (ages not fully specified)
clinical_problem: Automatically assessing skeletal bone age from left-hand and wrist X-rays in children, incorporating heterogeneous demographic features
model_description: Input: left-hand/wrist X-ray images plus race and gender; output: estimated bone age, via a CNN for image feature extraction combined with support vector regression using multiple kernel learning to fuse heterogeneous features
title: A Deep Automated Skeletal Bone Age Assessment Model with Heterogeneous Features Learning.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and comparative evaluation
headline_result: improved accuracy over state-of-the-art on two datasets (no single summary number given)

model_family: machine learning regression algorithm using brain network graph metrics
patient_population: 24 children with focal epilepsy, ages 8-18 years
clinical_problem: predicting full-scale IQ from resting-state fMRI brain network metrics in children with epilepsy
model_description: Resting-state fMRI brain network metrics (clustering coefficient, modularity, path length, global efficiency), computed using either Pearson correlation or mutual information to define connectivity, are input to a machine learning algorithm trained to predict full-scale IQ in children with epilepsy. Mutual-information-based network metrics explained more IQ variance than correlation-based metrics.
journal: Computational and mathematical methods in medicine
title: Mutual Information Better Quantifies Brain Network Architecture in Children with Epilepsy.
headline_result: Mutual information network metrics explained 49% (95% CI 46-51%) of IQ variance versus 17% (95% CI 13-19%) for Pearson correlation

patient_population: 52 adolescents with major depressive disorder (37 treated, 15 untreated)
clinical_problem: distinguishing treated from untreated adolescent major depressive disorder using anatomical (DTI) connectivity
model_description: Diffusion tensor imaging anatomical connectivity between brain-region pairs and derived network topology measures are used to train a nonlinear support vector machine. The classifier distinguishes adolescents with major depressive disorder who received treatment from those who did not, using features selected by p-value filtering and minimum-redundancy-maximum-relevance, evaluated with leave-one-out cross-validation.
journal: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. Annual International Conference
title: Classifying Treated vs. Untreated MDD Adolescents from Anatomical Connectivity using Nonlinear SVM.
headline_result: 73% accuracy, 100% specificity, 100% precision (leave-one-out cross-validation)

patient_population: 12,611 radiographs of patients 0-19 years old
clinical_problem: Can bone age be estimated automatically from hand radiographs with improved accuracy by exploiting a deep learning model's sensitivity to image rotations and flips?
model_description: A deep learning network predicts bone age from a hand radiograph; Gaussian process regression combines predictions from multiple rotated/flipped versions of the same image to improve overall accuracy.
journal: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. Annual International Conference

model_description: The most elegant idea in this batch: the parts of the skull missing from an ultrasound volume are missing for a physical reason - the beam struck at a grazing angle, or bone cast a shadow - so the network is given an angle-of-incidence map and a shadow map computed from its own first-pass segmentation and asked to complete what the physics says should be there. The clinical payoff is reported rather than implied: 3D-based cranial deformation assessment reached 100% specificity against 50% for traditional 2D biometrics.
journal: 2018 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI 2018)
title: Deep learning with ultrasound physics for fetal skull segmentation
headline_result: average Dice 0.83 +/- 0.06 for skull segmentation, with cranial deformation assessment reaching 100% specificity versus 50% for traditional 2D biometrics

model_description: Aimed squarely at the pediatric case: traditional 4D segmentation builds a template or assumes the timepoints can be co-registered, which is exactly what a developing brain violates, since appearance changes between scans. Treating time as a sequence to be modelled by an LSTM rather than as a registration problem is the reframing, and the application shown is longitudinal pediatric MRI.
journal: 2018 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI 2018)
title: Fully convolutional structured LSTM networks for joint 4D medical image segmentation
headline_result: the first deep learning framework integrating fully convolutional networks and LSTM end to end for joint 4D segmentation, demonstrated on longitudinal pediatric MRI

title: SonoEyeNet: Standardized fetal ultrasound plane detection informed by eye tracking
headline_result: precision 96.5%, recall 99.0% and F1 97.8% with eye fixation information, against 73.6%, 74.1% and 73.8% without it
