title: Fully Automated Deep Learning System for Bone Age Assessment.
study_design: retrospective single-center development with clinical deployment
headline_result: bone age within 1 year in 90.4% (female) and 94.2% (male) of test radiographs; within 2 years in 98.1% and 99.0%

model_family: random forest classifier with local phase symmetry-based geometric features
patient_population: 693 ultrasound scans from 35 infants
clinical_problem: automated developmental dysplasia of the hip screening: scan adequacy assessment and dysplasia metric extraction from ultrasound
model_description: Input is a 2D hip ultrasound image; the model uses local phase symmetry image features and a random forest classifier to determine whether the image is adequate for diagnosis, then extracts developmental dysplasia of the hip metrics from adequate images.
title: Automatic Evaluation of Scan Adequacy and Dysplasia Metrics in 2-D Ultrasound Images of the Neonatal Hip.
study_design: retrospective single-center technical development and validation study
headline_result: AUC 0.985 for scan adequacy classification versus clinicians; significantly reduced variability in DDH metrics (p<0.05)

model_family: two CNNs (localization network and quality-classification network)
patient_population: fetuses undergoing obstetric ultrasound examination
clinical_problem: automatic quality control of obstetric ultrasound images before biometric measurements are taken from them
model_description: One network finds the fetal abdominal region in the image, a second scores whether the key landmarks (stomach bubble and umbilical vein) are adequately depicted. The output is a quality verdict, not a diagnosis: it is meant to catch a badly acquired or wrongly chosen slice before someone measures from it, which is a common and unmonitored source of biometric error.
title: FUIQA: Fetal Ultrasound Image Quality Assessment With Deep Convolutional Networks.
headline_result: quality assessment comparable to the subjective ratings of three medical doctors

model_family: composite convolutional and recurrent network with multitask learning
patient_population: fetuses in hundreds of obstetric ultrasound videos
clinical_problem: acquiring the correct standard planes during obstetric ultrasound, which currently depends on operator experience
model_description: Identifies several different fetal standard planes from ultrasound video with one general framework, rather than a separate detector per plane as earlier work did. The convolutional part learns appearance within a frame and the recurrent part learns how frames relate over time; multitask learning shares what is common between plane types, which is how it copes with limited training data.
title: Ultrasound Standard Plane Detection Using a Composite Neural Network Framework.
headline_result: better standard-plane detection than plane-specific prior methods; figures not stated in the abstract

model_family: classifiers trained on intrinsic connectivity network features in one cohort and tested in an independent cohort
patient_population: two independent cohorts: UCLA (33 with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome and 33 matched controls) and Syracuse (28 and 28)
clinical_problem: identifying which young people with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome - one of the largest known genetic risk factors for psychosis - are on a psychosis-risk trajectory
model_description: The design is what gives it weight: classifiers trained at UCLA were tested at Syracuse, and three of twelve network-derived classifiers replicated. More importantly, four networks predicted psychosis-risk status within the deletion syndrome group in both cohorts - a within-diagnosis stratification that replicated across sites, which is rare in psychiatric imaging. 22q11.2 deletion syndrome is a defined genetic population, so this is closer to a stratification biomarker than a diagnostic classifier.
title: Intrinsic Connectivity Network-Based Classification and Detection of Psychotic Symptoms in Youth With 22q11.2 Deletions.
study_design: retrospective two-cohort model development and replication
headline_result: the anterior cingulate/precuneus, default mode and posterior default mode classifiers distinguished 22q11.2 deletion syndrome from controls in the replication cohort, and four networks predicted psychosis-risk status within the syndrome in both cohorts

model_family: hierarchical sparse feature selection with an extreme learning machine
patient_population: children in the public ADHD-200 dataset
clinical_problem: separating ADHD inattentive from ADHD combined from typical development on imaging
model_description: Combines structural measures (cortical thickness and its variability, volume, surface area, intensity) with functional connectivity maps, selects the most discriminative features hierarchically, and classifies into three groups rather than two. Multi-class performance is much weaker than binary, which is the honest and clinically relevant part: telling ADHD from typical development is easier than telling the subtypes apart.
title: Multi-modal, Multi-measure, and Multi-class Discrimination of ADHD with Hierarchical Feature Extraction and Extreme Learning Machine Using Structural and Functional Brain MRI.
study_design: technical development on a public dataset
dataset_size: selected subjects from the public ADHD-200 dataset
headline_result: 76.19% accuracy in the three-class setting and 92.86% in the binary setting (both p < 0.0001)

clinical_problem: Automated quality assessment and biometric measurement (biparietal diameter, occipital-frontal diameter, head circumference) of the fetal head on 2D obstetric ultrasound.
model_description: Texton-based segmentation extracts the fetal head region; shape and anatomic features are fed into a random forest classifier to assess image quality and derive fetal head biometry.
title: Automatic image quality assessment and measurement of fetal head in two-dimensional ultrasound image.
study_design: retrospective methods development and validation study
headline_result: Quality assessment precision 95.24%; segmentation accuracy 99.27%

model_family: support vector machine with multiple kernel learning
patient_population: 44 drug-naive Tourette syndrome children and 41 age- and gender-matched healthy children
clinical_problem: classifying pediatric Tourette syndrome from structural connectome topology
model_description: Diffusion MRI probabilistic tractography-derived white-matter network topological features go in; an SVM with multiple kernel learning outputs classification of Tourette syndrome vs. control.
title: Disrupted topological organization of structural networks revealed by probabilistic diffusion tractography in Tourette syndrome children.
study_design: case-control diffusion MRI connectome study with SVM classification
headline_result: classification accuracy 86.47%

patient_population: Children in the multi-institutional PHIS+ clinical repository; 282 reports manually annotated for training/testing
clinical_problem: Automatically determining presence or absence of bacterial pneumonia in children from the text of chest imaging reports, to support large-scale comparative effectiveness research
model_description: Input: free-text pediatric chest diagnostic imaging reports; output: extracted imaging findings and automatic classification of whether the report is consistent with bacterial pneumonia, via an NLP application with machine learning algorithms
title: Enhancing Comparative Effectiveness Research With Automated Pediatric Pneumonia Detection in a Multi-Institutional Clinical Repository: A PHIS+ Pilot Study.
study_design: pilot study, retrospective NLP model development and testing
headline_result: finding extraction sensitivity 0.939, PPV 0.925; report classification sensitivity 0.71, PPV 0.86, specificity 0.962

model_family: support vector machine on automated MRI-derived tissue/morphology descriptors
patient_population: 173 preterm infants imaged at 30 and/or 40 weeks postmenstrual age
clinical_problem: predicting cognitive and motor developmental outcome at 2-3 years in preterm infants from neonatal brain MRI
model_description: Input is automatically computed brain MRI descriptors (tissue volumes and cortical morphology measures); output is an SVM classification of infants likely to have low cognitive or motor outcome at 2-3 years, assessed at 30 and 40 weeks postmenstrual age.
title: Prediction of cognitive and motor outcome of preterm infants based on automatic quantitative descriptors from neonatal MR brain images.
study_design: prospective cohort study with automated MRI-based outcome prediction
dataset_size: 173 patients (86 imaged at 30 weeks PMA, 153 at 40 weeks PMA)
headline_result: AUC 0.78-0.85 for identifying infants with low cognitive/motor outcome, depending on imaging timepoint

patient_population: individuals with autism spectrum disorder, multi-site neuroimaging data (age not stated)
clinical_problem: identifying structural and functional brain characteristics that distinguish individuals with autism spectrum disorder from controls, to support diagnosis and treatment stratification
model_description: A web-based collaborative research platform applying multivariate machine-learning approaches to multi-site structural and functional MRI data to distinguish autism spectrum disorder from controls and identify subgroups for treatment stratification.
release_evidence: platform accessible to the community of researchers working on ASD (https://arianna.pi.infn.it)
title: ARIANNA: A research environment for neuroimaging studies in autism spectrum disorders.
study_design: description of a multi-site machine-learning-based neuroimaging research platform for autism spectrum disorder

model_family: cross-validated machine-learning classifier on functional connectivity features
patient_population: 59 six-month-old infants at high familial risk for autism
clinical_problem: prediction of an autism spectrum disorder diagnosis at 24 months from imaging at 6 months
model_description: Takes resting-state functional connectivity MRI acquired at 6 months of age and returns a prediction of whether that child will receive an autism diagnosis at 24 months. Functional connections were first related to 24-month social, language, motor and repetitive-behavior scores, then used as features in a fully cross-validated classifier.
title: Functional neuroimaging of high-risk 6-month-old infants predicts a diagnosis of autism at 24 months of age.
headline_result: positive predictive value 100% (95% CI 62.9-100), sensitivity 81.8%, specificity 100%

model_family: deep learning shape model (statistical shape model + deep classifiers)
patient_population: 314 normal and abnormal pediatric chest radiographs
clinical_problem: automated segmentation of the lung fields on pediatric chest radiographs
model_description: Input: pediatric chest radiographs; output: lung field segmentation contours, estimated by deep classifiers predicting statistical shape model parameters in marginal eigenspaces (MaShDL).
journal: Proceedings of SPIE--the International Society for Optical Engineering
title: Marginal Shape Deep Learning: Applications to Pediatric Lung Field Segmentation.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and internal evaluation
headline_result: mean Dice similarity coefficient 0.927 (vs 0.888 for classical ASM, p=0.01)

model_family: auto-context CNN (voxelwise multi-plane and U-net variants)
patient_population: public adult benchmark datasets plus reconstructed fetal brain MRI
clinical_problem: extracting the brain from surrounding tissue on MRI, including fetal brains in arbitrary orientations
model_description: Separates brain from non-brain on MRI without registering to an atlas and without assuming anything about image geometry, which is what makes it work on a fetal brain lying in an arbitrary orientation inside the uterus. It feeds its own probability maps back in as context, iteratively, so the network learns the shape and connectedness of the brain rather than only local intensity.
title: Auto-Context Convolutional Neural Network (Auto-Net) for Brain Extraction in Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
dataset_size: two public benchmarks (LPBA40, OASIS) plus a fetal brain MRI set
headline_result: Dice 97.73% and 97.62% on the public adult benchmarks and 95.97% on arbitrarily oriented fetal brains, where competing methods performed poorly

model_family: machine learning (classifier on cortical thickness features)
patient_population: 115 youth from the LAMS study plus 31 healthy comparison youth, mean age ~13 years
clinical_problem: Distinguishing youth with higher versus lower trajectories of manic-like mood/energy dysregulation using cortical thickness patterns from structural MRI
model_description: A machine learning classifier trained on cortical thickness measures (68 anatomical regions) extracted via surface reconstruction from structural MRI, used to distinguish youth with higher versus lower longitudinal trajectories of manic-like mood and energy dysregulation.
title: Using machine learning and surface reconstruction to accurately differentiate different trajectories of mood and energy dysregulation in youth.
study_design: Retrospective longitudinal cohort study with machine-learning classification
dataset_size: 115 LAMS youth (18 higher trajectory, 34 lower trajectory) plus 31 healthy comparisons
headline_result: AUC 0.89, p=0.03 for distinguishing higher vs lower mania trajectory groups

model_family: real-time CNN with weakly supervised localization
patient_population: fetuses undergoing routine mid-pregnancy anomaly screening ultrasound
clinical_problem: finding and labelling the standard views required by the mid-pregnancy anomaly scan
model_description: Watches freehand 2D ultrasound as it is acquired and, in real time, names which of 13 standard fetal views is on screen and draws a box around the relevant anatomy. The localization is learned from image-level labels alone, with no manual boxes. Intended to help less experienced operators acquire and recognize the required views, and to pull the right frames out of stored video afterwards.
title: SonoNet: Real-Time Detection and Localisation of Fetal Standard Scan Planes in Freehand Ultrasound.
study_design: technical development on clinical screening data
dataset_size: images and video from a large set of full clinical anomaly screenings; size not stated
headline_result: F1 0.798 for real-time detection, 90.1% accuracy for retrospective frame retrieval, 77.8% for localization

model_family: natural language processing engine with an inference rules engine
patient_population: pediatric hospital encounters with ultrasound studies performed between July 2015 and March 2016, 3371 hospital encounters
clinical_problem: detection of deep venous thrombosis from radiology reports
model_description: Reveal NLP, a commercial natural language processing tool paired with an inference rules engine, scans radiologists' free-text ultrasound reports to flag studies as positive or negative for deep venous thrombosis. It was first validated on a curated set of reports, then configured to scan all available radiology reports daily as an automated, prospective safety-net screen for hospital-acquired VTE, rather than interpreting the images itself.
release_evidence: validated an NLP tool, Reveal NLP (Health Fidelity Inc, San Mateo, CA)
title: The use of natural language processing on pediatric diagnostic radiology reports in the electronic health record to identify deep venous thrombosis in children.
study_design: prospective single-center diagnostic accuracy / workflow validation
dataset_size: validation set of 144 DVT-positive and 106 negative reports; prospective run on 6373 radiology reports from 3371 hospital encounters
headline_result: Validation set sensitivity 97.2% (95% CI 93-99.2%), specificity 92.5% (95% CI 85.7-96.7%); prospective run sensitivity 82.9% (95% CI 74.8-89.2%), specificity 97.5% (95% CI 96.9-98%)

patient_population: neonates in three groups: term controls, intrauterine growth restriction, and mild isolated ventriculomegaly
clinical_problem: classifying neonatal brain conditions (term controls vs. intrauterine growth restriction vs. ventriculomegaly) from neuroimaging
model_description: a neighborhood-approximation random forest combined with manifold learning takes multiple distance measures derived from neonatal MRI as input and outputs a classification among term, IUGR, and ventriculomegaly groups
title: Learning and combining image neighborhoods using random forests for neonatal brain disease classification.

patient_population: 1 adolescent patient with mixed eating-disorder, depressive, and GI symptoms
clinical_problem: Distinguishing gastrointestinal, depressive, and eating-disorder symptom etiology in a single adolescent patient using functional MRI response to experimental pain
model_description: Supervised machine learning classifies a single patient's functional brain imaging response to an experimental pain paradigm, together with self-report psychological data, to identify which diagnostic phenotype (GI, depressive or eating-disorder) the patient's pattern most closely resembles.
journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
title: The clinical application of fMRI data in a single-patient diagnostic conundrum: Classifying brain response to experimental pain to distinguish between gastrointestinal, depressive and eating disorder symptoms.
study_design: single-patient case report using supervised machine learning classification

patient_population: 74 boys with ADHD and 69 age-matched controls (ADHD-200 Consortium)
clinical_problem: predicting inattention and impulsivity symptom severity in ADHD from resting-state fMRI connectivity
model_description: A LASSO-based predictive model takes intra- and inter-network temporal connectivity features (sample entropy, phase synchronization) from resting-state fMRI as input and predicts continuous inattention and impulsivity symptom scores.
title: Predicting clinical symptoms of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder based on temporal patterns between and within intrinsic connectivity networks.
study_design: retrospective predictive-modeling study using a public multi-site cohort (ADHD-200)
headline_result: Prediction performance r=0.79 (inattention), r=0.48 (impulsivity), both p<10^-8

patient_population: 16 pediatric patients (<21 years) with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage
clinical_problem: Predicting risk of symptomatic cerebral vasospasm after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage in children using an adult-derived neural network model applied to pediatric clinical and radiographic data.
model_description: An artificial neural network trained on adult aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage data is applied to pediatric demographic, clinical, and radiographic variables to output a likelihood score for symptomatic cerebral vasospasm.
journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
title: Predicting symptomatic cerebral vasospasm after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage with an artificial neural network in a pediatric population.
headline_result: ANN correctly predicted all 16 outcomes; mean prediction strength -0.86 (no vasospasm) vs 0.93 (vasospasm case)

patient_population: Children and adults with autism spectrum disorder or ADHD (literature review)
clinical_problem: Identifying brain-imaging-based biomarkers, using machine learning, to aid objective diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder and ADHD in children
model_description: Reviews studies that use structural and functional brain MRI features (e.g., functional connectivity, gray matter volume) as input to machine learning classifiers that output a diagnostic label distinguishing autism spectrum disorder or ADHD from typical development.
title: Progress and roadblocks in the search for brain-based biomarkers of autism and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder.

model_family: deep learning implementing the Greulich-Pyle method
patient_population: 200 patients aged 3-17 undergoing left-hand radiography
clinical_problem: bone age estimation, and whether software assistance makes radiologists faster without making them worse
model_description: Takes a left-hand radiograph and returns a ranked list of candidate Greulich-Pyle bone ages. The study is designed around the assisted workflow rather than the model alone: two radiologists read the same 200 cases with the software and with the atlas, and both concordance with the reference and reading time were measured. This is the question a department actually faces before buying such a tool.
release_evidence: described as a new automatic software system; the abstract does not say whether it is commercially available
title: Computerized Bone Age Estimation Using Deep Learning Based Program: Evaluation of the Accuracy and Efficiency.
headline_result: software alone concordant in 69.5% of cases (r = 0.992 with reference); concordance rose from 63.0% to 72.5% and 49.5% to 57.5% for the two readers, with reading times cut by 18% and 40%

model_family: random forest regression with auto-context model
patient_population: infants scanned longitudinally at 2 weeks, 3, 6, 9 and 12 months
clinical_problem: deformable registration of infant brain MRI acquired at different developmental time points for early brain development studies
model_description: A multioutput random forest regression with an auto-context model learns the evolution of anatomical shape and appearance from longitudinal infant MRI, then predicts deformation fields and appearance changes to register images from two different developmental time points.
title: Learning-based deformable registration for infant MRI by integrating random forest with auto-context model.
headline_result: Higher registration accuracy than nonlearning-based registration methods (no single number reported in abstract)

model_family: three-stage deep learning pipeline (localization, region detection, acoustic pattern verification)
patient_population: a large clinical dataset of 2D mid-gestation fetal images
clinical_problem: checking that a transventricular fetal brain plane meets the clinical standard before biometry is taken from it
model_description: Verifies that an acquired fetal neurosonographic plane actually satisfies the imaging protocol, by locating the brain, finding the regions that should contain named structures, and then learning the acoustic patterns that distinguish a compliant plane from a near-miss. This is quality control against a written clinical standard rather than diagnosis, and the standard is what non-experts find hardest to meet.
title: A Deep Learning Solution for Automatic Fetal Neurosonographic Diagnostic Plane Verification Using Clinical Standard Constraints.
dataset_size: a large real-world clinical dataset; size not stated
headline_result: automatic verification approached human expert assessment

model_family: trained machine-learning algorithm for individual resting-state network identification
patient_population: 20 children aged 1.9-18.4 years undergoing craniotomy, six of whom needed sedation for imaging
clinical_problem: mapping eloquent cortex before craniotomy in children who cannot perform task-based fMRI
model_description: The clinical case for this is unusually clear: task-based functional mapping requires a cooperative patient, and many children are not, whether through age, cognitive deficit or the need for sedation. A trained classifier identifies resting-state networks in the individual child, and the maps are loaded straight into the surgical navigation system. Six of the twenty children were sedated and it still worked, which is the point.
title: Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging for surgical planning in pediatric patients: a preliminary experience.
headline_result: resting-state network maps produced for all 20 patients and uploaded to clinical navigation systems, including in six sedated children

patient_population: 21 children (ages 5-21 years) with medically intractable epilepsy undergoing VNS; independent external cohort of 8 children
clinical_problem: predicting response to vagus nerve stimulation from presurgical resting-state fMRI connectivity in children with intractable epilepsy
model_description: Whole-brain resting-state fMRI connectivity to thalamic regions of interest is measured before vagus nerve stimulation implantation in children with drug-resistant epilepsy. A supervised support vector machine trained on this connectivity classifies patients as responders or non-responders to VNS, and was tested in an independent external cohort. Enhanced thalamic connectivity to the anterior cingulate cortex and left insula was associated with greater treatment benefit.
title: Presurgical thalamocortical connectivity is associated with response to vagus nerve stimulation in children with intractable epilepsy.
study_design: retrospective diagnostic/prognostic accuracy study with external validation
headline_result: 86% accuracy on 10-fold cross-validation; 88% accuracy in an independent external validation cohort of 8 children

model_family: linear support vector machine (feature selection + classification)
patient_population: 64 extremely premature neonates (<29 weeks gestation, <1500g) with IVH
clinical_problem: predicting which premature neonates with intraventricular hemorrhage will need intervention for post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus, using cranial ultrasound
model_description: Input: morphological features of the cerebral ventricles extracted from cranial ultrasound images; output: prediction of need for temporizing intervention for post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus, via SVM-based feature ranking and selection.
journal: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. Annual International Conference
title: Cranial ultrasound-based prediction of post hemorrhagic hydrocephalus outcome in premature neonates with intraventricular hemorrhage.
study_design: retrospective study with SVM-based feature selection and internal evaluation
headline_result: prediction accuracy 84% (vs 76% for linear manual measurement)

patient_population: Clinical fetal ultrasound data (sample size not stated)
clinical_problem: Automatically segmenting the fetal body and amniotic fluid on prenatal ultrasound images
model_description: Input: fetal ultrasound images; output: pixel-wise segmentation of fetal tissue and amniotic fluid, via an encoder-decoder deep learning network fine-tuned from a pretrained model
journal: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. Annual International Conference
title: Automatic fetal body and amniotic fluid segmentation from fetal ultrasound images by encoder-decoder network with inner layers.

model_family: graph theory / structural covariance network analysis
patient_population: Large autism MRI dataset (age- and sex-matched ASD vs. controls)
clinical_problem: Characterizing differences in frontoparietal and default mode brain network organization in children with autism using structural MRI covariance
model_description: A graph-theoretical structural covariance analysis of frontoparietal and default mode network regions derived from structural MRI, comparing network organization between children with autism spectrum disorder and matched controls.
journal: Proceedings. IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging
title: Graph theoretical approaches towards understanding differences in frontoparietal and default mode networks in Autism.
study_design: Retrospective preliminary case-control structural covariance network study

patient_population: 50 fetal echocardiography cases (40 frames each)
clinical_problem: estimating fetal left ventricular volume from 2D echocardiography for quantitative assessment of fetal cardiac function
model_description: Uses 16 distances from the 2D echocardiographic left ventricular border to its center as input to a backpropagation neural network, outputting left ventricular volume and derived stroke volume/ejection fraction.
title: Determination of Fetal Left Ventricular Volume Based on Two-Dimensional Echocardiography.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and validation study
headline_result: Highest ICC and CCC agreement with volume references, compared to area-length, Simpson's, and regression methods

clinical_problem: Accurate tissue segmentation of isointense-phase (~6-month) infant brain MRI, challenging due to low tissue contrast from ongoing myelination
model_description: Local AdapTivE and Sequential Training (LATEST) trains local random-forest classifiers per voxel using neighboring atlas training samples, iteratively refining tissue-probability maps to segment isointense infant brain MRI.
journal: Medical computer vision and Bayesian and graphical models for biomedical imaging : MICCAI 2016 international workshop, MCV and BAMBI, Athens, Greece, October 21, 2016 : revised selected papers
title: LATEST: Local AdapTivE and Sequential Training for Tissue Segmentation of Isointense Infant Brain MR Images.

patient_population: 31 young boys (15 with DMD, 16 age-matched healthy controls)
clinical_problem: Segmenting the lung across the breathing cycle on cine MRI to track respiratory muscle involvement in Duchenne muscular dystrophy
model_description: A holistically nested CNN, trained on one manually segmented frame per subject, performs image-to-image lung segmentation across an entire cine MRI breathing-cycle sequence in axial, sagittal and coronal planes
title: Holistic segmentation of the lung in cine MRI.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and validation study
headline_result: Dice similarity coefficients of roughly 0.9 across sagittal, axial and coronal views (exact figures obscured in abstract formulas)

patient_population: Adult and pediatric cochlear implant recipients
clinical_problem: Automating the initial rough alignment step of image-guided cochlear implant programming by localizing anatomical landmarks on head CT
model_description: A random forest localizes multiple anatomical landmarks on head CT images; a heuristic search then uses these landmarks to estimate an initial point-based registration transform for image-guided cochlear implant programming
title: Localizing landmark sets in head CTs using random forests and a heuristic search algorithm for registration initialization.
headline_result: Automated landmark-based initialization performed equivalently to manual initialization

patient_population: youth football players (non-contact, low-impact and high-impact exposure groups)
clinical_problem: Detecting brain functional-connectivity changes associated with different levels of sub-concussive head-impact exposure in youth football players using resting-state MRI
model_description: Group independent component analysis extracts resting-state brain networks from fMRI, and supervised machine learning classifiers predict whether a youth football player had no, low, or high cumulative head-impact exposure based on network connectivity patterns.
journal: Proceedings. IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging
title: Changes in resting state MRI networks from a single season of football distinguishes controls, low, and high head impact exposure.
study_design: prospective cohort study with machine-learning classification (IEEE ISBI)
headline_result: Classification accuracy up to 78% (10-fold cross-validation)

model_family: deep convolutional neural network (8-layer and 16-layer architectures) with transfer learning
patient_population: fetuses at 20-36 weeks gestational age undergoing routine ultrasound examination
clinical_problem: recognition of standard fetal facial ultrasound planes (axial, coronal, sagittal) during routine obstetric ultrasound
model_description: The model takes 2D fetal ultrasound images as input and classifies whether the image is a standard fetal facial plane (axial, coronal, or sagittal) versus a non-standard image. It was trained using CNNs of varying depth (8-layer and 16-layer), comparing training from scratch against transfer learning from an ImageNet-pretrained network. It is intended to automate recognition of standard fetal facial planes during routine obstetric ultrasound.
title: Fetal facial standard plane recognition via deep convolutional neural networks
dataset_size: 4,849 training images (375 axial, 257 coronal, 405 sagittal, 3,812 non-standard) and 2,418 test images (491 axial, 127 coronal, 174 sagittal, 1,626 non-standard)
headline_result: best recognition accuracy 94.5%, a 3.66% improvement over the authors' previous study; transfer learning improved accuracy by 9.29% and increasing CNN depth from 8 to 16 layers improved accuracy by 3.17%

model_family: regression random forest with importance sampling
patient_population: infants undergoing brain MRI
clinical_problem: anatomical landmark localization on infant brain MRI to support segmentation, registration, and disease prediction
model_description: The model takes infant brain MRI images as input. An importance map highlights informative locations in each scan, training voxels are sampled according to this map to address wide morphological variability among infant brains, and a regression random forest aggregates evidence from the sampled locations to localize anatomical landmarks. It is intended to support downstream tasks such as landmark-based segmentation, image registration, and disease prediction in infant brain imaging.
journal: Journal of Medical Imaging and Health Informatics
title: Accurate anatomical landmark detection based on importance sampling for infant brain MR images
headline_result: significant improvement in landmark detection accuracy compared with traditional methods

model_family: texture analysis with linear and nonlinear discriminant analysis (LDA/NDA) classifiers
body_region: fetal brain (ventricles, thalamus, grey matter, white matter)
patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal brain MRI (1.5T and 3T)
clinical_problem: automated classification of fetal brain anatomical structures on MRI to improve diagnostic imaging interpretation during pregnancy
model_description: The system takes manually selected regions of interest from fetal brain MRI (multiple field strengths, imaging planes, and signal weightings) as input, extracts texture features using the MaZda software customized into a knowledge-based system, and classifies each region into one of four anatomical tissue classes (ventricles, thalamus, grey matter, white matter) using linear and nonlinear discriminant analysis. It is intended as a data-mining tool to assist texture-based classification of fetal brain structures for prenatal imaging screening.
title: Texture analysis of the developing human brain using customization of a knowledge-based system
headline_result: LDA and NDA combined with dimensionality-reduction techniques achieved 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity (95% CI: 99.79-100) for ROI classification

patient_population: fetuses screened by ultrasound in the first and second trimester for Down syndrome markers
clinical_problem: detection of Down syndrome soft-marker features on first- and second-trimester ultrasound
model_description: This review of computer-aided diagnosis algorithms and techniques, covering 50 papers published from 1982 to 2016, examines secondary-observer systems developed to detect Down syndrome soft markers on first- and second-trimester fetal ultrasound, including nasal bone length, nuchal translucency thickness, and naso-frontal angle. It compares sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy across the reported algorithms.
title: A Review on techniques for computer aided diagnosis of soft markers for detection of down syndrome in ultrasound fetal images

model_family: convolutional neural network regressing the rotation and translation of an arbitrary 2D slice into a learned canonical atlas coordinate system
patient_population: simulated MRI brain data with extreme random motion, plus fetal MRI within a full reconstruction and motion compensation pipeline
clinical_problem: the limited capture range of intensity-based 2D/3D registration, which needs a good initialization - precisely what is unavailable when a fetus has moved unpredictably between slices
model_description: Solves the initialization problem rather than the registration problem, which is the correct target: conventional methods work well once close and fail entirely when far, and a learned regression to atlas coordinates puts them close. Milliseconds per slice makes it usable inside an acquisition. The demonstration that matters is on very young fetuses, where the motion is worst and previous reconstruction pipelines simply failed.
title: Predicting Slice-to-Volume Transformation in Presence of Arbitrary Subject Motion
headline_result: average prediction error 7 mm on simulated data with extreme motion, and convincing reconstruction of images of very young fetuses where previous methods fail

model_family: residual convolutional network for context-sensitive upsampling that learns organ-specific appearance
patient_population: 145 fetal scans
clinical_problem: the trade-off in fetal MRI between fast low-resolution acquisition, which the fetus's motion demands, and the detail that diagnosis requires
model_description: Argues against the spatially independent upsampling that was standard - it treats every part of the image the same and so is error prone - and learns instead what particular organs should look like at high resolution. The evaluation goes one step further than image quality: the super-resolved slices are fed into brain volume reconstruction on motion-corrupted data, where the gain is larger (1.73 dB) than on upsampling alone (1.25 dB), showing the benefit compounds through the pipeline.
title: Context-Sensitive Super-Resolution for Fast Fetal Magnetic Resonance Imaging
headline_result: PSNR increased by 1.25 dB over baseline upsampling on under-sampled fetal data, and by 1.73 dB when used for brain volume reconstruction from motion-corrupted captured data

model_family: fully convolutional networks for heart localization and frame-level viewing plane classification, with several architectures compared
patient_population: real-world clinical fetal echocardiography screening images
clinical_problem: the first step of automating fetal echocardiography screening - finding the fetal heart in the image and naming which standard viewing plane it is - which is hard because the heart is small, its structures indistinct and the images full of artefact
model_description: Frames the problem correctly as a prerequisite rather than a diagnosis: congenital heart disease cannot be detected automatically until the heart is located and the plane identified. A 23.5% frame-level classification error on real clinical screening data is a sober number, and the comparison across FCN architectures is what the paper offers to the groups that followed.
journal: 2017 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI 2017)
title: Automated characterization of the fetal heart in ultrasound images using fully convolutional neural networks
headline_result: 23.48% classification error rate for standard viewing plane assignment on real-world clinical fetal ultrasound data

model_family: multi-scale superpixels feeding a deep learning framework to produce a bone probability map, used to guide probabilistic graph search segmentation
patient_population: 2D ultrasound of 50 infant hips
clinical_problem: diagnosing developmental dysplasia of the hip on 2D ultrasound, where the geometric indices are drawn by hand and inter-operator variability is high, and where early detection means a Pavlik harness rather than surgery
model_description: Segments the acetabular bone and then computes the clinical indices from the contour, including a new index of acetabular rounding the authors propose - so the output is in the vocabulary a pediatric orthopedic surgeon already uses. Combining a learned probability map with probabilistic graph search keeps the contour anatomically plausible where the bone signal fades. Fifty infant hips, described as pilot data, with an AUC of 86.2% for normal versus dysplastic.
journal: 2017 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI 2017)
title: Toward automatic diagnosis of hip dysplasia from 2D ultrasound
headline_result: RMS error 1.8 +/- 0.7 mm and Hausdorff distance 2.1 +/- 0.9 mm against manual segmentation, with AUC 86.2% for classifying normal versus dysplastic hips

model_family: customized fully convolutional network embedded in a modified Auto-Context scheme, with summation rather than parallelization at the join
patient_population: two datasets of fetal head and fetal abdomen ultrasound images
clinical_problem: segmenting anatomy on prenatal ultrasound so that biometry can be interpreted efficiently and objectively, against boundaries that are frequently incomplete or ambiguous in the image
model_description: The named difficulty is boundary incompleteness - the fetal skull or abdominal outline simply is not present in parts of the image - and cascading the network through an Auto-Context scheme lets a second pass reason from the first pass's global prediction rather than from local intensity alone. Changing the Auto-Context join from parallelization to summation is a small change credited with a considerable further gain. Evaluated on head and abdomen, the two hardest standard planes.
journal: 2017 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI 2017)
title: Cascaded Fully Convolutional Networks for automatic prenatal ultrasound image segmentation
dataset_size: two datasets of fetal head and abdomen images
headline_result: best segmentation accuracy compared with state-of-the-art methods on fetal head and abdomen ultrasound, bridging severe boundary incompleteness

title: Using Convolutional Neural Networks and Transfer Learning for Bone Age Classification
headline_result: outperformed the state-of-the-art bone age classification methods on a small dataset by fusing region-specific fine-tuned models

model_family: 3D joint segmentation model, spherical harmonic shape analysis of the cortex, gyral distance maps of white matter, and a multi-level deep network for feature fusion and classification
patient_population: ABIDE subjects aged 8-12.8 years, NDAR/Pitt subjects aged 16-51 years, and NDAR/IBIS infants
age_groups: infant; child; mixed pediatric and adult
clinical_problem: diagnosing autism from structural MRI across the lifespan, and specifically whether it can be done early
model_description: Shape rather than intensity or connectivity, with cortical and white matter descriptors fused on the hypothesis - drawn from prior findings - that the two abnormalities are related. Testing on three databases spanning infancy to middle age is unusually broad, and the accuracy gradient tells the real story: 97% in adults, 93% in children, 85% in infants, so the signal weakens exactly where early diagnosis would need it to be strongest.
journal: 2017 IEEE International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP)
title: A new deep-learning approach for early detection of shape variations in autism using structural mri
dataset_size: three databases: ABIDE, NDAR/Pitt and NDAR/IBIS
headline_result: accuracy 93% on ABIDE (8-12.8 years), 97% on NDAR/Pitt (16-51 years) and 85% on the NDAR/IBIS infant database

model_family: fully convolutional network pre-trained on ImageNet, fed stacks of three successive 2D slices as pseudo-colour images, with transfer learning
patient_population: two public datasets covering neonatal and adult brain MRI
clinical_problem: tissue segmentation of brain MRI in neonates and in adults, the basis of any quantitative analysis of brain development or neurological disease
model_description: The trick is cheap and effective: stacking three adjacent slices as the three channels of a colour image lets an ImageNet-pretrained 2D network see some 3D context without the cost of a 3D network, giving segmentation in seconds from a single modality. Claimed as the first method applying transfer learning to both neonatal and adult brain segmentation - and the neonatal half is the harder one, since adult-pretrained assumptions about tissue contrast do not hold.
journal: 2017 IEEE International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP)
title: From neonatal to adult brain MR image segmentation in a few seconds using 3D-like fully convolutional network and transfer learning
headline_result: state-of-the-art results on two public datasets in a few seconds per volume from a single modality

model_family: ensemble of deep networks trained end to end on whole hands and hand regions

clinical_problem: bone age assessment for endocrine and metabolic disorders of child development
model_description: A challenge entry that goes further than winning: by training separately on whole hands and on specific hand regions, it measures which bones actually carry the bone age signal, and evaluates performance separately by skeletal development stage rather than as one average. That per-stage breakdown is what a clinician needs, because accuracy at the extremes of childhood is where these models tend to fail.
title: Pediatric Bone Age Assessment Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
headline_result: outperformed other common bone age methods on the challenge data

model_family: multi-task convolutional network with an anchor mechanism and IoU loss, made recurrent so regional convolutional features are computed over sequential frames
patient_population: a real-world clinical dataset of fetal cardiac screening ultrasound video
clinical_problem: describing what a fetal cardiac screening video actually contains - whether the heart is visible, which viewing plane, and where and how it is oriented - which is what would let a system guide interpretation frame by frame
model_description: Predicts four quantities jointly - visibility, plane, location and orientation - which is closer to what a sonographer knows at each moment than any single classification would be. The recurrent design means each frame's prediction is conditioned on the whole video, so a moment of poor visibility is interpreted in context rather than in isolation. Performance on par with expert annotations on real clinical screening video.
title: Temporal HeartNet: Towards Human-Level Automatic Analysis of Fetal Cardiac Screening Video
headline_result: frame-level joint prediction of fetal heart visibility, viewing plane, location and orientation on par with expert annotations

title: Multivariate classification of autism spectrum disorder using frequency-specific resting-state functional connectivity--A multi-center study.
study_design: Multi-center case-control study with machine learning classification
dataset_size: 240 adolescents (112 ASD, 128 controls) from 6 sites, Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE)
headline_result: SVM classification accuracy of 79.17% (p<0.001) using Slow-4 band functional connectivity

patient_population: First-trimester pregnancies (database size not stated)
clinical_problem: Estimating the risk of trisomy 21 and other chromosomal aneuploidies at 11-13 weeks of gestation using sonographic and biochemical markers
model_description: Input: sonographic markers (e.g., crown-rump length), biochemical markers, and maternal data; output: estimated risk of euploidy, trisomy 21, or other chromosomal aneuploidy, via an artificial neural network
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: First Trimester Noninvasive Prenatal Diagnosis: A Computational Intelligence Approach.

model_family: random-forest feature selection with a nonlinear support vector machine
patient_population: 105 preterm infants scanned at term-equivalent age and 26 healthy term-born neonates
clinical_problem: characterizing how preterm birth has altered functional brain organization by term-equivalent age
model_description: Builds whole-brain functional connectivity networks from neonatal resting-state MRI, selects the small set of connections that actually distinguish preterm from term infants, and classifies each infant from connectivity alone. The discriminative connections clustered in the basal ganglia and between subcortical structures and association cortex, which localizes the disruption rather than only detecting it.
title: Machine-learning to characterise neonatal functional connectivity in the preterm brain.
headline_result: 80% cross-validated classification accuracy from a small set of discriminative connections

clinical_problem: distinguishing children with hypoxic-ischaemic brain injury from unaffected children

title: Quantification of structural changes in the corpus callosumin children with profound hypoxic-ischaemic brain injury.
headline_result: SVM classification accuracy over 95%

model_family: quantitative image analysis producing 131 morphological parameters, with machine learning used to fit safety thresholds
patient_population: 50 consecutive children with hydronephrosis of varying severity who had both 2D sonography and diuretic MAG3 renography
clinical_problem: deciding which children with hydronephrosis actually need a diuretic nuclear renogram, using the ultrasound they have already had
model_description: A triage model rather than a diagnostic one, and the design reflects that: thresholds are fitted at 100 percent sensitivity, so the model is only allowed to rule out. What it buys is concrete and measurable in avoided studies - up to 62 percent of children spared a diuretic renogram, which for this population means avoided radiopharmaceutical, catheterization and sedation. It also beats the two scoring systems urologists actually use, the Society for Fetal Urology grade and the hydronephrosis index.
title: Quantitative Ultrasound for Measuring Obstructive Severity in Children with Hydronephrosis.
headline_result: at 100% sensitivity, specificity 94%, 70% and 74% for the three washout thresholds (AUC 0.98, 0.94, 0.94), significantly better than SFU grade and the hydronephrosis index; up to 62% of diuretic renograms avoidable

model_family: random forests over semiquantitative signal abnormality and atrophy scores across 109 muscles
patient_population: 8 children with LMNA-related dystrophy and 9 with SEPN1-related myopathy, whole-body MRI with 109 muscles scored each
clinical_problem: distinguishing pediatric LMNA-related dystrophy from SEPN1-related myopathy, two congenital myopathies whose clinical overlap makes the genetic workup expensive and slow
model_description: A clean use of machine learning at very small n: with 17 children and 109 scored muscles per child, the data are wide rather than long, and random forests are used to find which muscles carry the discrimination rather than to build a classifier for deployment. The output is a named pattern - an atrophied semimembranosus as the single most informative feature - which is the form a radiologist can actually use at the workstation. Whole-body MRI muscle pattern reading is exactly the kind of expertise that lives in a few centres.
title: Pediatric laminopathies: Whole-body magnetic resonance imaging fingerprint and comparison with Sepn1 myopathy.
headline_result: a selective whole-body MRI pattern for pediatric LMNA-related dystrophy, distinguishable from SEPN1-related myopathy, with atrophied semimembranosus the most relevant discriminating feature

model_family: hybrid system pairing the MedLEE natural language processing engine with statistical machine learning classifiers
patient_population: 2121 CT reports from the PECARN pediatric traumatic brain injury study, manually coded by trained abstractors, split evenly for training and testing
clinical_problem: turning free-text head CT reports into structured traumatic brain injury outcomes, which is otherwise done by trained human abstractors and is the rate-limiting step in large trauma studies
model_description: Report mining rather than image analysis, and an unusually careful instance of it: MedLEE supplies negation, certainty and temporal modifiers so that a mentioned-but-absent finding is not counted, findings are coded against the NINDS common data elements so the output is comparable across studies, and past, future and indication mentions are filtered out. The paper is explicitly a generalization test of a method that had worked for a simple outcome (orbital fracture), applied to a complex one.
journal: Academic emergency medicine : official journal of the Society for Academic Emergency Medicine
title: Automated Outcome Classification of Computed Tomography Imaging Reports for Pediatric Traumatic Brain Injury.
study_design: secondary analysis of a multicenter study
headline_result: validation of automated outcome classification for pediatric traumatic brain injury from free-text head CT reports, extending a hybrid NLP and machine learning system from a simple to a complex outcome

model_family: linear support vector machine on regional white-matter features
patient_population: 28 school-aged children with developmental dyslexia and 33 age-matched controls
clinical_problem: identifying developmental dyslexia from imaging rather than behavioral testing alone
model_description: Takes structural and diffusion MRI, reduces each white-matter region to five measures (volume, fractional anisotropy, mean, axial and radial diffusivity), and classifies a child as dyslexic or not. The features that carried the classification extended well beyond the classical reading network into limbic and motor tracts, which is the paper's substantive claim.
title: Disrupted white matter connectivity underlying developmental dyslexia: A machine learning approach.
headline_result: 83.61% classification accuracy, replicated with a logistic regression classifier

clinical_problem: identify sex-related structural brain differences in young children with autism spectrum disorder using structural MRI, separately from a case-control classification of ASD vs. typical development
model_description: Support vector machine analysis of voxel-based morphometry gray-matter maps from structural brain MRI to classify and compare young children with autism spectrum disorder versus controls, separately for each sex.
title: The effect of gender on the neuroanatomy of children with autism spectrum disorders: a support vector machine case-control study.
study_design: case-control structural MRI study with SVM-based group classification
dataset_size: 152 MRI scans (76 ASD children, 76 matched controls)
headline_result: SVM showed significantly increased gray-matter volume in ASD vs. controls in specific regions (e.g., bilateral superior frontal gyrus); sex-specific regions of difference identified (no single overall accuracy figure given)

clinical_problem: classifying pediatric Tourette syndrome from resting-state brain connectivity
model_description: Resting-state functional connectivity MRI data go in; an SVM classifier outputs group membership (Tourette syndrome vs. control), with a per-individual confidence measure.
title: Multivariate pattern classification of pediatric Tourette syndrome using functional connectivity MRI.
study_design: case-control resting-state fMRI study with SVM classification

clinical_problem: predicting cognitive impairment in survivors of pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia from brain structural connectivity
model_description: Diffusion tensor imaging was used to build whole-brain structural connectomes, analyzed with graph-theoretical measures (small-worldness, clustering coefficient) in young survivors of acute lymphoblastic leukemia versus healthy controls. A random forest model combining connectome and demographic variables was then trained to automatically classify survivors as having cognitive impairment or not.
title: Atypical Structural Connectome Organization and Cognitive Impairment in Young Survivors of Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia.
study_design: case-control diagnostic imaging study with random forest classification
dataset_size: 31 ALL survivors (ages 5-19) and 39 matched healthy controls
headline_result: Random forest classification accuracy 0.89 (p < 0.0001) for cognitive impairment status

patient_population: 663 adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients across 915 visits, reviewed by the Scoliosis Research Society 3D Classification Committee
clinical_problem: classifying three-dimensional spinal deformity in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, which the two-dimensional Lenke system does not capture
model_description: Compresses each patient's 3D spine reconstruction into a learned code and clusters those codes with no assumptions about how many groups there should be or what defines them. Eleven groups emerged, discriminated mainly by curve location, kyphosis and lordosis, and subgroups appeared within existing Lenke types. This is data-driven taxonomy rather than diagnosis, aimed at replacing a classification the field agrees is inadequate.
journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
title: Three-dimensional morphology study of surgical adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patient from encoded geometric models.
headline_result: eleven clusters identified with curve location, kyphosis and lordosis as the discriminating factors, revealing subgroups within existing Lenke types

clinical_problem: Improving the reliability of 2D/3D image registration used for daily patient setup verification in pediatric brain-tumor proton/external beam radiotherapy
model_description: A neural network pattern classifier ('registration quality evaluator') analyzes geometric features of daily orthogonal setup X-ray-to-CT registration solutions to automatically flag failed registrations for rejection and re-attempt
journal: Journal of applied clinical medical physics
title: A neural network-based 2D/3D image registration quality evaluator for pediatric patient setup in external beam radiotherapy.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and randomized controlled evaluation
dataset_size: six pediatric patients, multiple registration trials each
headline_result: Sensitivity 0.865-0.964 and specificity 0.797-0.990 for detecting registration error >1mm; final acceptance ratio 92.4%

model_family: genetic algorithm searching polynomial regression equations

clinical_problem: estimating gestational age in women who first present late in pregnancy with unknown menstrual dates
model_description: Takes routine fetal biometry from a single late ultrasound and returns an estimated gestational age. An automated search over more than 64,000 candidate polynomial equations picked head circumference and femur length as the best pair. The clinical value is in antenatal care where first-trimester dating was never done; the honest limitation, stated by the authors, is that accuracy degrades to worse than two weeks in the third trimester.
release_evidence: the prediction equations are published in full in the abstract

title: Ultrasound-based gestational-age estimation in late pregnancy.
headline_result: gestational age uncertainty of 6-7 days at 14 weeks, 12-14 days at 26 weeks, and more than 14 days in the third trimester

model_family: partitioned statistical shape and appearance model steered by conditional-space deep learning features across multiple MRI sequences
patient_population: MRI sequences from 165 pediatric subjects, evaluated leave-one-out
clinical_problem: segmenting the optic nerves, chiasm and tracts on MRI - thin, long, structurally variable and poorly contrasted against neighbours - including when they are distorted by low-grade glioma
model_description: Built for a structure that defeats generic segmentation and for a population where it matters most - optic pathway glioma is a childhood tumor, and treatment decisions turn on how the pathway is involved. The design pairs a statistical shape model, which enforces that the result still looks like a visual pathway, with learned features that carry it through the low-contrast optic tracts and pathological regions where intensity alone gives out. Partitioning the model regionally is what allows local deformation without losing global plausibility.
title: Deep Learning Guided Partitioned Shape Model for Anterior Visual Pathway Segmentation.
headline_result: mean Dice 0.779 for the whole anterior visual pathway and 0.791 for the optic nerve, significantly better than state-of-the-art methods and as robust as manual segmentation

model_family: sparsity-based atlas selection combined with machine-learning label fusion, for multi-modal input
patient_population: multi-modal brain MRI of 50 newborns
clinical_problem: brain extraction from neonatal MRI - the first step of nearly every neuroimaging pipeline - where methods built and validated on adults have never been shown to hold
model_description: The comparison is unusually thorough: eleven publicly available brain extraction methods run on the same 50 newborns, which establishes not just that ALFA works but how badly the adult-derived alternatives do on neonates. The atlas selection strategy is the contribution - a handful of atlases spread evenly through the data space rather than many similar ones - and because it learns from partially labelled data it scales to large cohorts.
title: Accurate Learning with Few Atlases (ALFA): an algorithm for MRI neonatal brain extraction and comparison with 11 publicly available methods.
headline_result: outperformed all eleven compared publicly available brain extraction methods across modalities on 50 newborns

model_family: convolutional neural network (multi-scale patch and kernel sizes)
patient_population: preterm infants scanned at 30 and 40 weeks postmenstrual age, alongside aging adults (~70y) and young adults (~23y) used as comparison cohorts
clinical_problem: automatic brain tissue segmentation for quantitative MRI analysis
model_description: The model takes a single anatomical MR brain image as input and outputs a multi-class tissue segmentation. It is a convolutional neural network that combines multiple patch sizes and convolution kernel sizes to capture multi-scale voxel information, learning discriminative features from training data rather than relying on hand-crafted ones. It was evaluated across five separate cohorts spanning preterm infants and adults of different ages.
title: Automatic Segmentation of MR Brain Images With a Convolutional Neural Network.
dataset_size: five datasets covering preterm infant MRI (30 and 40 weeks PMA, coronal and axial) and adult/young-adult MRI cohorts; exact per-group counts not stated
headline_result: Average Dice coefficients of 0.87, 0.82, 0.84, 0.86, and 0.91 across the five segmented datasets

patient_population: pregnant patients; fetuses at early (16-32 weeks) and late (36-41 weeks) gestation
clinical_problem: Automatically timing the opening and closing of fetal cardiac valves from Doppler ultrasound to assess fetal cardiac electromechanical function
model_description: K-means clustering groups Doppler ultrasound signal patterns, and a hybrid SVM-HMM model trained per cluster detects the timing of cardiac valve opening/closing events from the high-frequency component of the fetal Doppler ultrasound signal.
journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
title: Model-Based Estimation of Aortic and Mitral Valves Opening and Closing Timings in Developing Human Fetuses.
study_design: retrospective algorithm development and validation study

The method was trained and tested on the ADHD-200 dataset (118 ADHD, 98 controls).
journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
title: Network-based classification of ADHD patients using discriminative subnetwork selection and graph kernel PCA.

dataset_size: 118 ADHD patients and 98 normal controls (ADHD-200 dataset)

patient_population: 50 infants born at 23-29 weeks without moderate or severe brain injury, scanned at term-equivalent age, and 50 term-born controls
clinical_problem: quantifying how much preterm birth has disrupted brain development, as a route to predicting neurodevelopmental outcome
model_description: Takes resting-state functional MRI from a term-equivalent infant and either classifies them as preterm or term born, or estimates their birth gestational age as a continuous measure of how disrupted development has been. The regression output is the interesting one clinically: it gives a per-infant number rather than a group difference, which is what a prediction of individual outcome would need.
title: Prediction of brain maturity in infants using machine-learning algorithms.

clinical_problem: differentiating specific reading comprehension deficit from dyslexia and typical reading using brain structure
model_description: Takes whole-brain gray matter volume maps from structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry) as input and outputs an SVM classification distinguishing reading comprehension deficit, dyslexia, and typically developing readers.
title: Anomalous gray matter patterns in specific reading comprehension deficit are independent of dyslexia.

headline_result: classification accuracy 92.5% (SRCD vs. TD, p<0.001), 88.0% (SRCD vs. DYS, p<0.001), 80.0% (DYS vs. TD, p<0.01)

clinical_problem: estimating fetal weight for small-for-gestational-age fetuses
model_description: A gradient-boosting regression model derives a new formula estimating fetal weight from ultrasound biometric measurements (biparietal diameter, head circumference, abdominal circumference, femur length), fetal sex, and gestational age, tailored to small-for-gestational-age fetuses.
journal: Journal of ultrasound in medicine : official journal of the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine
title: A New Sonographic Weight Estimation Formula for Small-for-Gestational-Age Fetuses.
headline_result: lowest median absolute percentage error among compared weight-estimation formulas

clinical_problem: Differentiating common pediatric cerebellar tumor types (ependymoma, medulloblastoma, astrocytoma) using MRI texture analysis

title: [Utility of texture analysis of magnetic resonance imaging in differential diagnosis of common pediatric cerebellar tumors in children].
headline_result: SVM accuracy: ependymoma vs medulloblastoma 86.15%, ependymoma vs astrocytoma 73.63%, medulloblastoma vs astrocytoma 74.32%

clinical_problem: Estimating missing longitudinal cortical thickness measurements at missing time points in infant brain MRI studies

title: Learning-based subject-specific estimation of dynamic maps of cortical morphology at missing time points in longitudinal infant studies.
dataset_size: 31 healthy infants, up to 5 time points each
headline_result: average estimation error < 0.23 mm

patient_population: cohort of healthy and high-risk fetuses
clinical_problem: Parcellating the fetal cortical surface into anatomically meaningful regions despite the lack of consistent anatomical landmarks across gestation
model_description: A Random Forest learns geometrical mesh-signature features to parcellate the fetal cortical surface, refined with an alpha-expansion graph-cut using the forest's probability maps, producing an unsupervised brain parcellation from fetal MRI surface data.
journal: Proceedings of SPIE--the International Society for Optical Engineering
title: Unsupervised fetal cortical surface parcellation.

patient_population: 41 children with ASD (21M/20F), 40 controls (20M/20F), ages 22-72 months
clinical_problem: Identifying a common pattern of structural brain alterations distinguishing young children with autism spectrum disorder from controls using structural MRI.
model_description: Regional structural features from brain MRI are used to train a one-class support vector machine on the ASD group alone, which then classifies new subjects as ASD or outliers (controls).
title: One-Class Support Vector Machines Identify the Language and Default Mode Regions As Common Patterns of Structural Alterations in Young Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders.
headline_result: AUC 0.74 (male), 0.68 (female); AUC 0.81/0.72 for NVIQ>=70 subgroup

patient_population: fetal, neonatal and pediatric populations imaged with brain MRI (systematic review, not a single cohort)
clinical_problem: Reviewing multivariate pattern-recognition analysis techniques applied to fetal, neonatal and pediatric brain MRI for brain cancer and neurological injury
model_description: Systematic review synthesizing multivariate analysis (pattern-recognition) methods applied to MRI of the developing brain for identifying biomarkers, understanding injury/cancer etiology, and supporting diagnosis and treatment monitoring.
title: Pre-Adult MRI of Brain Cancer and Neurological Injury: Multivariate Analyses.

model_family: surface-mesh fMRI-seeded diffusion tractography pipeline with a machine-learning track classifier
patient_population: 31 children with unilateral cerebral palsy
clinical_problem: running diffusion tractography in brains with major pathology, where automated cortical parcellation fails, manual region drawing is slow and error-prone, and the usual structure-function assumptions break down after cortical reorganisation
model_description: Aimed at exactly the situation pediatric neuroimaging keeps running into: the brain is too abnormal for atlas-based methods and too numerous for hand-drawn regions. Seeding from the child's own functional activation sidesteps the atlas, surface meshes tighten the seed, and a learned track classifier removes the irrelevant pathways that fMRI smoothing drags in. The head-to-head against the standard voxelwise approach is decisive on the metric that matters for a clinical pipeline - how many children could be processed at all.
title: Surface-Based fMRI-Driven Diffusion Tractography in the Presence of Significant Brain Pathology: A Study Linking Structure and Function in Cerebral Palsy.
headline_result: processed 87% of participants versus 65% for the voxelwise approach, with 15 of 20 diffusion-clinical correlations significant (R2 0.43-0.73) versus 2 for voxelwise

model_family: hierarchical extreme learning machine (H-ELM), compared with SVM and basic ELM
patient_population: 159 children from the public ADHD-200 MRI dataset: typically developing, ADHD-inattentive, ADHD-combined

clinical_problem: predicting abnormal neonatal neurobehavior in small-for-gestational-age fetuses from fetal brain MRI texture

title: Automatic quantitative MRI texture analysis in small-for-gestational-age fetuses discriminates abnormal neonatal neurobehavior.

clinical_problem: classifying adolescent idiopathic scoliosis curve types and predicting surgical fusion levels

title: Artificial neural networks assessing adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: comparison with Lenke classification.

patient_population: children with cystic fibrosis from an Australian pediatric CF registry
clinical_problem: Score chest radiograph severity (Shwachman-Kulczycki score) in children with cystic fibrosis
model_description: Texture features (Tamura, LBP, GLCM, Gabor) from chest radiographs input to an SVM classifier to output an automated Shwachman-Kulczycki severity score.

title: Fully automated scoring of chest radiographs in cystic fibrosis.

patient_population: 15 high-functioning adolescents and adults with autism and 15 typically developing controls
clinical_problem: distinguishing individuals with autism from typically developing controls using brain connectivity during a Theory-of-Mind fMRI task, as a potential imaging biomarker
model_description: Effective (causal) connectivity among 18 fMRI regions of interest, computed with a multivariate autoregressive model, combined with DTI fractional anisotropy and assessment scores, is fed into a recursive-cluster-elimination support vector machine that outputs an autism-versus-control group label for each participant.

patient_population: children ages 7-14 referred for auditory processing disorder testing with left ear advantage, versus controls with right ear advantage

patient_population: Cohort of patients with neonatal encephalopathy
clinical_problem: Predicting neurological outcome in neonates with neonatal encephalopathy using brain structural connectivity networks derived from diffusion tractography.

patient_population: children with developmental dyscalculia compared with typically developing control children, performing non-symbolic number comparison and exact calculation tasks during fMRI
clinical_problem: diagnosing developmental dyscalculia from functional brain activation

Fronto-parietal activation patterns from both tasks combined best separated the two groups, though the specific regions of abnormal activation overlapped little across individual dyscalculic children.
title: Diagnosing developmental dyscalculia on the basis of reliable single case FMRI methods: promises and limitations.
study_design: case-control diagnostic imaging study with single-case and multivariate SVM/cluster analysis

clinical_problem: Building an accurate neonatal brain MRI template for spatial normalization, to support development of a template-based computer-aided diagnosis system for neonatal cerebral disorders

title: A neonatal brain MR image template of 1 week newborn.

patient_population: 76 female children (38 with ASD, 38 matched controls), 2-7 years
clinical_problem: distinguish female children with autism spectrum disorder from typically developing controls using structural brain MRI
model_description: Voxel-based morphometry (VBM-DARTEL) combined with support vector machine classification and recursive feature elimination (SVM-RFE) using leave-pair-out cross-validation to identify gray-matter patterns that discriminate female children with ASD from controls.

patient_population: 16 healthy offspring genetically at risk for bipolar disorder (12-17 years) and 16 age/gender-matched low-risk offspring
clinical_problem: identifying adolescents at risk for future mood/psychiatric disorders from brain imaging

title: Pattern recognition and functional neuroimaging help to discriminate healthy adolescents at risk for mood disorders from low risk adolescents.
study_design: longitudinal case-control fMRI study with machine-learning classification
headline_result: 75% classification accuracy (sensitivity 75%, specificity 75%)

patient_population: 98 childhood-onset schizophrenia patients and 99 age-, sex-, and ethnicity-matched healthy controls
clinical_problem: classifying childhood-onset schizophrenia from structural brain MRI
model_description: 74 anatomic brain MRI sub-region volumes go in; a random forest classifier outputs group membership (childhood-onset schizophrenia vs. control) and a probability-of-illness score.
title: Using multivariate machine learning methods and structural MRI to classify childhood onset schizophrenia and healthy controls.
study_design: case-control structural MRI study with random forest classification
headline_result: classification accuracy 73.7%

clinical_problem: Improving estimated fetal weight accuracy specifically for extreme macrosomia (>=4500 g) where standard formulas perform poorly

title: A new formula for optimized weight estimation in extreme fetal macrosomia (≥ 4500 g).
headline_result: New formula had lowest mean absolute percentage error (2.506%) versus existing equations

patient_population: children with ADHD versus typically developing children across 8 research sites (ADHD-200 dataset)
clinical_problem: objectively classifying ADHD versus typically developing children from structural and functional brain MRI, as an aid to subjective clinical diagnosis

clinical_problem: predict an individual's 'brain age' from resting-state functional-connectivity MRI across a lifespan cohort that includes children

model_family: machine learning-based automatic segmentation and classification
patient_population: pediatric population with and without ADHD
clinical_problem: assisting ADHD diagnosis via caudate nucleus volumetric abnormalities

title: Automatic brain caudate nuclei segmentation and classification in diagnostic of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder.

clinical_problem: predicting/classifying ADHD from resting-state brain imaging

title: ADHD-200 Global Competition: diagnosing ADHD using personal characteristic data can outperform resting state fMRI measurements.
study_design: Machine learning competition entry (ADHD-200 Global Competition) comparing clinical/demographic-only versus fMRI-based classifiers
headline_result: 62.52% diagnostic accuracy using personal characteristics alone, the highest of 21 competing teams, outperforming fMRI-based classifiers

patient_population: 55 patients (mixed ages) with brain tumors: astrocytoma, glioblastoma, childhood medulloblastoma, meningioma, metastases
clinical_problem: differentiating types of brain tumors, including pediatric medulloblastoma, on MRI to assist radiologist diagnosis

headline_result: Mean absolute percent error 5.26% +/- 4.14%, mean absolute error 157.91 +/- 119.90 g; outperformed conventional EFW formulas (p<0.05)

clinical_problem: Segmenting airway shapes on chest X-ray to support detection of lymphadenopathy associated with pediatric tuberculosis

title: Interactive segmentation of airways from chest X-ray images using active shape models.

title: Neural systems predicting long-term outcome in dyslexia.

model_family: voxelwise multivariate regression / log-Euclidean full-diffusion-tensor machine learning framework
patient_population: 30 children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder

title: [Application of pulse-coupled neural network combined with genetic algorithm on MR images of hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy].

model_description: Input is 3D and 2D ultrasound biometric measurements (abdominal volume, head circumference, femur volume/length, biparietal diameter); output is an estimated fetal weight formula derived using gradient boosting with component-wise smoothing splines.
